mandarin_meaning: 裝腔作勢並硬撐到底；明明做不到卻不肯認輸、死撐
english_meaning: To put on a show/pretend bravado and stubbornly hold on; to stubbornly refuse to admit defeat or give up despite being unable to continue.
explanation_mandarin: 「戲棚竹，死頂」用來形容有人為了面子或顯得有氣勢而裝腔作勢，明明已經撐不住仍硬要堅持下去、不肯認錯或放棄。
explanation_english: This phrase describes someone who puts on a show or false bravado and stubbornly persists; even when they cannot continue, they insist on carrying on to avoid admitting defeat or losing face.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做唔到就承認啦，唔好戲棚竹，死頂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 m4 dou3 zau6 sing4 jan6 laa3, m4 hou2 hei3 paang4 zuk1, sei2 ding2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做不到就承認吧，別再裝腔作勢、硬撐了。
examples.english_sentence: If you can't do it, admit it—don't put on a show and stubbornly hang on.

mandarin_meaning: 可怜没用／可怜呆笨的人（俚语）
english_meaning: to pity someone who is useless or a gullible fool (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「戥猪石」為粵語口語俚語，通常帶貶義，指對某些無用、笨拙或容易被利用的人表示同情或可憐，語氣常帶不滿或輕蔑。
explanation_english: “戥猪石” is Cantonese slang, usually derogatory. It refers to pitying someone who is useless, naive, or easily taken advantage of; the tone often carries contempt or frustration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日戥豬石，佢根本唔會學嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 dang3 zyu1 sek6, keoi5 gan1 bun2 m4 wui5 hok6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別老是可憐那種沒用的人，他根本不會學東西。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep pitying that useless person; he simply won't learn.

mandarin_meaning: 不是常见的粤语固定词语，可能为罕用或误写。字面上可拆为“戥（同情／怜惜）+ 穿石”。在实际语境中可能是误写或误用，亦有可能被混淆为“滴水穿石”（坚持不懈）或以“戥”表示“可怜／惋惜”。
english_meaning: Not an established Cantonese phrase; likely a rare or mistaken form. Literally reads as 'pity pierce stone' (戥 = pity/sympathize). It may be a miswriting or confusion with phrases like '滴水穿石' (dripping water wears through stone = perseverance) or with the colloquial use of 戥 meaning 'to pity'.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 片語（罕用 / 疑似誤寫）
explanation_mandarin: 此短語並非廣泛收錄的標準粵語詞彙，使用時應小心。若遇到，常見情況是當事人誤用或把幾個字混淆，需根據語境判斷真正含義。
explanation_english: This is not a widely recognized Cantonese lexical item. Use cautiously — it is likely a rare or incorrect form. Context is needed to interpret intent; it may reflect pity/sympathy or be a confusion with more common idioms like '滴水穿石'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我成日聽人講「戥穿石」，但其實好少人知係咩意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing4 jat6 teng1 jan4 gong2 "dang3 cyun1 sek6", daan6 kei4 sat6 hou2 siu2 jan4 zi1 hai6 me1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我常听人说“戥穿石”，但其实很少人知道是什么意思。
examples.english_sentence: I often hear people say '戥穿石', but actually very few people know what it means.

synonyms: 可能為「滴水穿石」的誤寫

mandarin_meaning: 灰溜溜地走/掉头躲避（因尴尬、羞愧或害怕而退缩）
english_meaning: to slink away or hide in shame/embarrassment; to turn away and retreat awkwardly
explanation_mandarin: 形容因為害怕、尷尬或羞愧而轉身躲開或悄悄離開，帶有退縮、灰溜溜的語氣。
explanation_english: Describes turning away to hide or quietly leaving out of embarrassment, shame, or fear; conveys a sense of retreating or slinking off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做錯嘢驚到要死，最後扭頭埋牆走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 co3 je5 geng1 dou3 jiu3 sei2, zeoi3 hau6 nau2 tau4 maai4 coeng4 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做错事害怕得要死，最后灰溜溜地走了。
examples.english_sentence: He messed up and was terrified, and in the end he slunk away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺人面前俾人鬧完，佢就扭頭埋牆走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 jan4 min6 cin4 bei2 jan4 naau6 jyun4, keoi5 zau6 nau2 tau4 maai4 coeng4 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在别人面前被骂完，他就灰溜溜地走了。
examples.english_sentence: After being scolded in front of others, he just slunk away.

mandarin_meaning: 挑衅；故意惹人
english_meaning: to provoke someone; to tease or pick at someone to get a reaction
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，指故意挑釁、惹怒或戲弄別人，常用於非正式語境。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning to deliberately provoke, tease, or rile someone to get a reaction; used in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日扽虾笼，佢已經好嬲喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 dan3 haa1 lung4, keoi5 ji5 ging1 hou2 nau1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要老是挑衅他，他已經很生氣了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep provoking him — he's already very angry.

mandarin_meaning: 擔心、焦慮、心裡不安
english_meaning: to feel anxious or worried; to fret; to be uneasy
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用語，表示心裡不安、擔心或焦慮，常用來形容對某事反覆擔憂。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to feel anxious, worried, or uneasy — often used to describe repeatedly fretting about something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近啲壓力好大，夜晚成日抌心口，瞓唔着。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 di1 aat3 lik6 hou2 daai6, je6 maan5 sing4 jat6 daan2 sam1 hau2, fan3 m4 zoek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近壓力很大，晚上總是擔心得睡不着。
examples.english_sentence: I've been under a lot of pressure lately; I keep worrying at night and can't sleep.

mandarin_meaning: 非常担心、焦虑
english_meaning: to be extremely worried or anxious
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，字面可理解為「捶打心肺」，用來形容對某事非常擔心、焦慮或心神不寧。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning 'pounding the heart and lungs', used to describe being extremely worried, anxious, or distressed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我為嗰件事抌心抌肺，成日諗到頭都痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 wai6 go2 gin6 si6 taam2 sam1 taam2 fui3, sing4 jat6 nam2 dou3 tau4 dou1 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我为那件事非常担心，总是想着想到头都痛。
examples.english_sentence: I'm extremely worried about that matter; I keep thinking about it until my head hurts.

mandarin_meaning: 忍受寒冷而貪戀潇湘（比喻為了向往的事物甘願受苦）
english_meaning: to brave the cold out of longing for Xiaoxiang (figuratively: willing to endure hardship for something alluring)
explanation_mandarin: 此短语並非常見的粤語成語，可能為創作性或地區性用法。可逐字拆解：抵冷 = 忍受寒冷、抗寒；贪潇湘 = 贪戀潇湘（潇湘可指地名或象徵的美景/享受）。合起來可理解為為了貪戀某地或某種享受而願意忍受寒冷，比喻為了向往的事物甘願受苦。
explanation_english: This phrase is not a standard Cantonese idiom and may be a creative or regional expression. Literally: '抵冷' = endure the cold; '贪潇湘' = covet/long for Xiaoxiang (a place or its charms). Together it suggests being willing to suffer cold because of longing for Xiaoxiang — figuratively, willing to endure hardship for something desired.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係抵冷贪潇湘，凍到發抖都唔肯走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 dai2 laang5 taam1 siu1 soeng1, dung3 dou3 faat3 dau2 dou1 m4 hang2 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是忍受寒冷也貪戀潇湘，冷得發抖也不肯離開。
examples.english_sentence: He truly braves the cold for Xiaoxiang — shivering from the cold, he still refuses to leave.

mandarin_meaning: 非常划算；很值
english_meaning: extremely worth it; an excellent bargain
explanation_mandarin: 香港口語俚語，用來誇張地形容某物或某事非常划算、值回票價。字面帶有誇張意味，並非真正與脖子有關。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase used hyperbolically to say something is extremely worth it or a terrific bargain. The reference to "neck" is figurative and not literal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次減價真係抵得颈！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 gam2 gaa3 zan1 hai6 dai2 dak1 geng2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次降价真是非常划算！
examples.english_sentence: This price cut is really a great bargain!

mandarin_meaning: 划算又份量大
english_meaning: good value and generous (large portion/size); cheap but substantial
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口語俚語，通常用來形容食物或商品既價格便宜又份量或尺寸較大，物有所值。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase describing something that is inexpensive (good value) and comes in a large portion or size—i.e., cheap but substantial.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間茶餐廳嘅叉燒飯真係抵食夹大件，份量多又平，大家都推介。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 ge3 caa1 siu1 faan6 zan1 hai6 dai2 sik6 gaap3 daai6 gin6, fan6 loeng6 do1 jau6 peng4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 teoi1 gaai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家茶餐厅的叉烧饭真的划算又份量大，既便宜又实惠，大家都推荐。
examples.english_sentence: The char siu rice at this cha chaan teng is really good value and large — cheap and filling; everyone recommends it.

mandarin_meaning: 挑食；挑剔（尤指對食物）
english_meaning: to be picky/choosy (especially about food)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人對食物或其他事物非常挑剔，只會選擇自己喜歡的。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is picky or choosy, especially about food — they only select things they like.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好拣饮择食，去食飯總係淨係食佢鍾意嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 gaan2 jam2 zaak6 sik6, heoi3 sik6 faan6 zung2 hai6 zing6 hai6 sik6 keoi5 zung1 ji3 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很挑食，去吃飯總是只吃他喜歡的東西。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is very picky about food; when eating out, they always only eat what they like.

mandarin_meaning: 在床上亲热／滚床单（俚语）
english_meaning: to fool around/make out in bed; to have sex (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，形容在床上打情罵俏、親熱或發生性行為，通常口語或帶俗語色彩。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase describing fooling around, making out, or having sex in bed. Informal and colloquial.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋昨晚喺屋企捵床捵席，唔怕人知。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 zok6 maan5 hai2 uk1 kei2 waan2 cong4 waan2 zik6, m4 paa3 jan4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们昨晚在家里滚床单，不怕别人知道。
examples.english_sentence: They were fooling around in bed at home last night and didn't care if anyone knew.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公共地方唔好捵床捵席啦，咁唔雅觀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 zung3 dei6 fong1 m4 hou2 waan2 cong4 waan2 zik6 laa1, gam2 m4 ngaap6 gun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公共场合不要在这里滚床单，这样很不得体。
examples.english_sentence: Don't fool around in public places like this — it's inappropriate.

mandarin_meaning: 有經驗／見識
english_meaning: to have experience; to know what's what
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，字面為「掂過條蔗」，用來形容一個人對某事有實際經驗或見識，能應付相關情況或不需他人指導。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "have handled a sugarcane." It describes someone who has practical experience or knows what's what and can handle a situation without guidance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗咁耐，掂過條蔗，唔使你教。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 gam2 noi6, dim6 gwo3 tiu4 ze3, m4 sai2 nei5 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做了這麼久，有經驗了，不用你教。
examples.english_sentence: He's been doing it for so long; he's experienced and doesn't need you to teach him.

mandarin_meaning: 把人丟棄／把責任推給別人（像丟棄一隻死狗一樣）
english_meaning: to dump/abandon someone or to throw someone under the bus (to discard or blame someone ruthlessly)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面是「掟死狗」，用來形容無情地拋棄某人、把責任或麻煩推給別人，或讓某人承擔全部責任/受罰。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "throw a dead dog." It describes ruthlessly abandoning someone, passing blame/responsibility onto them, or otherwise discarding them—similar to "throwing someone under the bus."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢出事，管理層就即刻掟死狗，話係佢一個人嘅錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 ceot1 si6, gun2 lei5 cang4 zau6 zik1 hak1 deng6 sei2 gau2, waa6 hai6 keoi5 jat1 go3 jan4 ge3 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他出事後，管理層就把責任推給他，說全是他一個人的錯。
examples.english_sentence: When he messed up, management immediately threw him under the bus, saying it was all his fault.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好俾人掟死狗，遇到問題要爭取自己嘅權益。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 deng6 sei2 gau2, jyu6 dou3 man6 tai4 jiu3 zeng1 ceoi2 zi6 gei2 ge3 kyun4 jik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要讓別人把你拋棄，遇到問題要爭取自己的權益。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let people dump you—when problems come up, fight for your own rights.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）分手、結束戀愛關係；有時指大吵或決裂
english_meaning: Cantonese slang for breaking up (ending a romantic relationship); sometimes used for a major falling-out
explanation_mandarin: 「掟煲」是香港廣東話的俚語，字面是「掟（扔）煲」，引申為情侶或伴侶結束關係或發生嚴重爭執而決裂。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term literally meaning "throw the pot." It is used to describe a couple breaking up or having a serious falling-out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋上個月掟煲咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 soeng6 go3 jyut6 dang3 bou1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们上个月分手了。
examples.english_sentence: They broke up last month.

mandarin_meaning: 搅局者；惹事生非、挑拨是非的人
english_meaning: troublemaker; an instigator who stirs up trouble or provokes conflict
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話粗俗俚語，字面意思為「攪屎的棍子」，用來形容喜歡挑事、搬弄是非或在他人之間製造矛盾的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese coarse slang term literally meaning "a stick that stirs shit." It describes someone who deliberately stirs up trouble, provokes conflict, or spreads discord.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個搅屎棍，成日挑事，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 gaau2 si2 gwan3, sing4 jat6 tiu1 si6, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個惹事生非的人，總是挑事，弄得大家不高興。
examples.english_sentence: He's a troublemaker who always stirs things up and makes everyone unhappy.

mandarin_meaning: 惹是生非；挑起争端、搬弄是非
english_meaning: to stir up trouble; to create discord or pick quarrels; to nitpick and cause disputes
explanation_mandarin: 表示故意挑起争端或搬弄是非，常用来形容喜欢找碴、惹麻烦或挑拨他人关系的行为。
explanation_english: Indicates deliberately stirring up disputes or sowing discord; often describes someone who likes to pick faults, cause trouble, or foment quarrels.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日搅是搅非，令公司氣氛好差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gaau2 si6 gaau2 fei1, ling6 gung1 si1 hei3 fan1 hou2 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是惹是生非，讓公司的氣氛很差。
examples.english_sentence: He is always stirring up trouble, making the atmosphere at the company very bad.

mandarin_meaning: 搅风搅雨（捣乱、制造事端、挑拨）
english_meaning: to stir up trouble; to cause disturbances or create mischief
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，指在人群或事務中挑拨、捣乱或制造麻烦，使情况变得混乱或不和谐。
explanation_english: A colloquial phrase meaning to stir up trouble, cause disturbances, or create conflicts and disorder among people or in situations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度搅风搅雨，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 gaau2 fung1 gaau2 jyu5, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在制造事端，弄得大家不开心。
examples.english_sentence: He is always stirring up trouble, making everyone upset.

mandarin_meaning: 搞不定 / 办不成 / 应付不了
english_meaning: can't handle it; unable to get it done; can't manage
explanation_mandarin: 表示无法完成、处理或应付某事，常为口语用法，带有无奈或无能为力的语气。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning one cannot complete, deal with, or manage something; often expresses helplessness or inability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家睇落好複雜，搞唔掂喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 tai2 lok6 hou2 fuk1 zaap6, gaau2 m4 dim6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在看起来很复杂，搞不定了。
examples.english_sentence: It looks really complicated now; I can't handle it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意我一個人搞唔掂，要請人幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dan1 saang1 ji3 ngo5 jat1 go3 jan4 gaau2 m4 dim6, jiu3 ceng2 jan4 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这笔生意我一个人搞不定，需要请人帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: I can't handle this deal by myself; I need to hire someone to help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試太難，我搞唔掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 taai3 naan4, ngo5 gaau2 m4 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次考试太难，我应付不了。
examples.english_sentence: This exam is too difficult; I can't manage it.

mandarin_meaning: 搞定 / 完成 / 处理好
english_meaning: to get something done; to finish; to sort out / take care of
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，表示把某件事處理好或完成、搞定。常用於日常會話，帶有非正式語氣。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to take care of or finish something, to get it done or sorted. Common in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我幫你搞掂啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bong1 nei5 gaau2 dim6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我帮你搞定了。
examples.english_sentence: I'll take care of it for you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲報告已經搞掂晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 bou3 gou3 ji5 ging1 gaau2 dim6 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 报告已经都弄好了。
examples.english_sentence: The reports are all finished.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔使驚，我會幫你搞掂一切。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 sai2 ging1, ngo5 wui5 bong1 nei5 gaau2 dim6 jat1 cai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不用担心，我会帮你处理一切。
examples.english_sentence: Don't worry, I'll handle everything for you.

mandarin_meaning: 胡闹 / 玩闹 / 捣乱
english_meaning: to mess around; to fool around; to cause a minor disturbance or stir for fun
explanation_mandarin: 香港粤语俚语，指不认真地玩闹、捣乱或刻意制造骚动，既可表示无伤大雅的玩闹，也可带有惹麻烦或挑事的含义，通常用于非正式场合。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term meaning to mess around, fool around, or cause a minor stir. It can be playful (doing something for fun) or annoying (provoking trouble or showing off). Used in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日喺度搞搞震，大家要做正經嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 gaau2 gaau2 zan3, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zou6 zing3 ging1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你别老是在这里胡闹，我们要做正经事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep messing around here; we need to do serious work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識搞搞震，冇認真做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 gaau2 gaau2 zan3, mou5 jing6 zan1 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只会胡闹，不认真工作。
examples.english_sentence: He only messes around and doesn't take his work seriously.

mandarin_meaning: 搞笑；滑稽
english_meaning: funny; comical; to joke around
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某事或某人有趣、令人發笑，也可指開玩笑或鬧著玩的行為。可作形容詞或動詞使用，語氣可正式亦可口語化。
explanation_english: Used to describe something or someone as amusing or funny, and can also mean to joke around or act comically. It functions as an adjective or a verb and is common in both formal and colloquial contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套電影好搞笑，我笑到肚痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 din6 jing2 hou2 gaau2 siu3, ngo5 siu3 dou3 tou5 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部电影很搞笑，我笑到肚子痛。
examples.english_sentence: This movie is so funny I laughed until my stomach hurt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度搞笑，唔認真。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 dou6 gaau2 siu3, m4 jing6 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在那儿搞笑，不认真。
examples.english_sentence: He is always joking around there and not being serious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺我面前搞笑，今次好重要。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 ngo5 min6 cin4 gaau2 siu3, gam1 ci3 hou2 zung6 jiu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要在我面前搞笑，这次很重要。
examples.english_sentence: Don't joke around in front of me — this time is important.

mandarin_meaning: 胡说/说谎
english_meaning: to talk nonsense; to lie / to spout rubbish
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，口语用法，表示说胡话、讲大话或胡乱说话，常用于指某人说话不可信或乱讲。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to talk nonsense or tell lies. Used informally to say someone is speaking rubbish or being untruthful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日放葫芦，唔好信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 fong3 wu4 lou4, m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是胡说八道，别相信他。
examples.english_sentence: He is always talking nonsense / lying; don't trust him.

jyutping: gaau3 syu1 sin1 saang1 bun1 uk1, zap1 syu1 (syu1)
mandarin_meaning: （雙關）字面：教书先生搬家，拿著书。引申：因「书/輸」同音，常用來幽默或婉轉地表示某人输了/落败。
english_meaning: A Cantonese pun: literally 'the teacher moves house and carries books', but because 'book' (syu1) is a homophone of 'lose' (syu1), it's a playful way to say someone lost or was defeated.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話利用粵語「書」與「輸」同音的特性，把「執書」（拿書）當作「執輸」（認輸、輸掉）的委婉或幽默說法，常用於比賽或鬥嘴後表示對方落敗。
explanation_english: This phrase plays on the Cantonese homophone between 'book' (syu1) and 'lose' (syu1). '執書' (pick up books) sounds like '執輸' (accept defeat), so it's used humorously or euphemistically to say someone lost.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今場比賽輸咗，教书先生搬屋，执书喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 coeng4 bei2 coi3 syu1 zo2, gaau3 syu1 sin1 saang1 bun1 uk1, zap1 syu1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們這場比賽輸了，真是“教书先生搬家，执书”了。
examples.english_sentence: We lost this match — it's a 'teacher moves house, carries books' moment (i.e. we lost).

mandarin_meaning: 連一文都不值／毫無價值
english_meaning: not worth a damn; worthless; not worth a penny
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語／俚語，用來形容某物或某事完全沒有價值或不值得重視，等同「一文不值」或「毫無價值」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to say something has no value or is not worth anything — equivalent to 'not worth a penny' or 'worthless.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲藉口連斗令都唔值，唔好再聽佢講喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 zek3 hau2 lin4 dau2 ling6 dou1 m4 zik6, m4 hou2 zoi3 teng1 keoi5 gong2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的那些藉口連一文都不值，別再聽他說了。
examples.english_sentence: His excuses aren't worth a penny — don't listen to him anymore.

jyutping: gwai3 ze2 maai6 bou3, jat1 pat1 waan4 jat1 pat1
mandarin_meaning: 以一還一；對等回報，兩清
english_meaning: Tit for tat; to return exactly the same; to settle accounts evenly
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，字面指賣布的桂姐按一匹布還一匹，借指以同樣的方式回報對方或講求對等、兩清。
explanation_english: A colloquial proverb meaning to repay in the same way or to settle things evenly — literally ‘Sister Gwai sells cloth, one bolt returned for one bolt.’ It implies tit for tat or exact reciprocity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁樣對我，我就照佢樣做返，桂姐卖布，一匹还一匹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 joeng6 deoi3 ngo5, ngo5 zau6 ziu3 keoi5 joeng6 zou6 faan1, gwai3 ze2 maai6 bou3, jat1 pat1 waan4 jat1 pat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這樣對我，我就照他的方式回報，桂姐賣布，一匹還一匹。
examples.english_sentence: He treated me like that, so I'll return the favor the same way — tit for tat.

jyutping: gwaang1 long4 syu6, jat1 tiu4 sam1
mandarin_meaning: 团结一致；同心同德
english_meaning: United; of one mind; working together in agreement
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，用來形容一群人彼此團結、意見一致、同心協力。字面提到桄榔樹作比喻，強調「一條心」的團結狀態，屬於口語或地區性用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe a group of people who are united and of one mind, cooperating closely. The phrase uses the image of the tree as a metaphor for solidarity. It is informal and regionally used.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋桄榔樹，一條心，遇到事會互相幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gwaang1 long4 syu6, jat1 tiu4 sam1, jyu6 dou3 si6 wui5 wu6 soeng1 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们团结一致，遇到事情会互相帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: They're united and help each other when problems come up.

jyutping: gun1 coi4 tau4 siu1 paau3 zoeng6, haak3 sei2 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 把人吓得要命／把人吓死了（形容非常可怕或令人震惊）
english_meaning: to scare someone to death; extremely frightening or shocking
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面上把棺材頭上燒鞭炮，形象地表達非常驚嚇或嚇得要命。常用作口語誇張的感嘆，表示某事或某人很嚇人或非常震驚。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally describing lighting firecrackers on a coffin's head — an exaggerated image meaning to frighten someone terribly. Used informally to say something is terrifying or shocking (often as an exclamation).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢突然跳出嚟嚇我，真係棺材头烧炮仗，吓死人！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dat6 jin4 tiu3 ceot1 lei4 haak3 ngo5, zan1 hai6 gun1 coi4 tau4 siu1 paau3 zoeng6, haak3 sei2 jan4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然跳出来吓我，真是把人吓死了！
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly jumped out and scared me — it was terrifying, it nearly scared me to death!

jyutping: gun1 coi4 gwaai2 zoeng6, sei2 ding2
mandarin_meaning: （口語）死撐、死頂，頑固堅持到最後，往往不顧後果或自取滅亡
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to stubbornly persist or dig in one's heels to the bitter end, often despite clear danger or inevitable failure.
explanation_mandarin: 「棺材拐杖，死顶」字面為「拿棺材當拐杖，硬撐到底」，用來形容一個人固執、死撐、不肯退讓，或形容情況已無可挽回仍硬撐。
explanation_english: Literally "coffin cane, die and persist" — the phrase mocks or describes someone who stubbornly refuses to give up, holding on to the point of self-harm or ruin. It's a colloquial/slang way to say someone is digging in their heels.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日棺材拐杖，死頂唔聽人講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gun1 coi4 gwaai2 zoeng6, sei2 ding2 m4 teng1 jan4 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是死撐、死頂，不聽別人勸。
examples.english_sentence: He always digs in his heels and refuses to listen to others.

jyutping: gwaan1 coi4 lou5 syu2, sik6 sei2 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 字面上是「棺材裡的老鼠，吃死人」，用作罵人，形容人極其卑鄙、狠毒，常趁人不幸或從別人的災難中牟利或加害於人。
english_meaning: Literally 'coffin mouse, eats people to death.' A vulgar Cantonese insult for someone extremely despicable or malicious who takes advantage of others' misfortune or harms people.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語/罵人用語，名詞短語
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語帶有強烈貶義，用來形容心狠手辣、見利忘義、會趁人困難時出手或從中得益的人。通常為口語或粗俗用法，不適合正式場合。
explanation_english: A strongly pejorative, colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe a person who is morally vile, exploits others' misfortune, or causes serious harm. It is vulgar and used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係棺材老鼠，食死人，成日等人有難就出嚟搵好處。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 gwaan1 coi4 lou5 syu2, sik6 sei2 jan4, sing4 jat6 dang2 jan4 jau5 naan6 zau6 ceot1 lai4 wan2 hou2 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是棺材老鼠，食死人，成天等人有難就出來謀取好處。
examples.english_sentence: He's really a 'coffin mouse' — despicable and harmful; always waiting for others' misfortune to profit.

jyutping: gun1 coi4 leoi5 min6 san1 sau2, sei2 jiu3 cin2
mandarin_meaning: 形容人極度貪婪或吝嗇，連死了還要錢；可用近義詞「貪得無厭」
english_meaning: Describes someone extremely greedy or miserly — so avaricious they'd still want money even after death.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語 / 口語 (成語式說法)
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用比喻手法，說一個人貪心到極點，連棺材裡面都要伸手拿錢，形容貪婪或吝嗇的程度非常嚴重。
explanation_english: A figurative, colloquial expression describing someone who is excessively greedy or stingy — metaphorically 'reaching into the coffin' to get money, i.e. wanting money even in death.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋為咗嗰筆遺產爭得面目全非，真係棺材里面伸手，死要钱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 wai6 zo2 go2 bat1 wai4 caan2 zing1 dak1 min6 muk6 cyun4 fei1, zan1 hai6 gun1 coi4 leoi5 min6 san1 sau2, sei2 jiu3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们为了那笔遗产争得面目全非，真是棺材里伸手，死也要钱。
examples.english_sentence: They fought mercilessly over the inheritance — truly 'reaching into the coffin', wanting money even after death.

jyutping: gun1 coi4 pou3 baai3 san4, soeng2 jan4 sei2
mandarin_meaning: 在棺材店拜神，等于希望別人死；比喻言行自相矛盾、虛偽或別有用心（希望別人遭禍）。
english_meaning: Literally 'a coffin shop worships gods — wishes people dead.' A Cantonese saying used to describe hypocritical or two-faced behavior, acting with ulterior motives, or seemingly hoping others come to harm.
explanation_mandarin: 此語字面意思是棺材店裡祭拜神佛，等於希望有更多人死亡來增加生意。引申為批評某人言行不一、居心叵測或表面善意實際想別人倒霉。
explanation_english: The literal image is a coffin shop praying to gods as if wishing for more deaths to boost business. It is used metaphorically to criticize people who are insincere, two-faced, or whose actions suggest they secretly want others to suffer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好信佢，佢表面一副好人樣，其實係棺材铺拜神，想人死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5, keoi5 biu2 min6 jat1 fu3 hou2 jan4 joeng6, kei4 sat6 hai6 gun1 coi4 pou3 baai3 san4, soeng2 jan4 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別相信他，他表面一副好人樣，其實是在棺材鋪拜神，想人死。
examples.english_sentence: Don't trust him — he acts like a good person, but he's like 'a coffin shop worshipping gods' who wants people to die (i.e. two-faced or malicious).

jyutping: him3 jan4 cin2 zai3 bat1 si6 coi4
mandarin_meaning: 欠别人的钱不是财富（债务不等于财产）
english_meaning: Owing money to others is not wealth (debt is not an asset)
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语强调欠别人的钱并不算是自己的财产，欠债不是值得炫耀的东西，应该及时还清债务。
explanation_english: This proverb stresses that money you owe others is not your wealth; debt is not something to boast about and should be repaid.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 欠人錢債不是財，遲早要還清。
examples.jyutping_sentence: him3 jan4 cin2 zai3 bat1 si6 coi4, ci4 zou2 jiu3 waan4 cing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 欠别人的钱不是财富，迟早要还清。
examples.english_sentence: Owing someone money is not wealth; sooner or later you have to pay it back.

mandarin_meaning: 不要輕視或挑釁大自然；比喻不要招惹難以控制或有實力的事物／人
english_meaning: Don't provoke the mountain nor the water; figuratively, don't mess with forces (or people) you cannot control — respect nature or powerful/resourced parties.
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俗語，字面意思是「別去欺負山也別去欺負水」，用來提醒人們要敬畏自然或不要挑釁有實力或有背景的人、事、物，否則後果難以預料。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally meaning 'don't bully the mountain, don't bully the water.' It's used to caution people to respect nature or to avoid provoking forces (or people) that are beyond one's control or have strong backing, because the consequences can be serious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂開發山頭，欺山莫欺水，後果可能好嚴重。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 hoi1 faat3 saan1 tau4, hei1 saan1 mok6 hei1 seoi2, hau6 gwo2 ho2 nang4 hou2 jim4 zung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要隨便開發山頭，欺山莫欺水，後果可能很嚴重。
examples.english_sentence: Don't recklessly develop the hillside — don't mess with the mountain and the water; the consequences could be severe.

mandarin_meaning: 镇定从容；不慌不忙
english_meaning: calm and composed; unhurried and relaxed
explanation_mandarin: 形容在紧张或突发情况下仍然镇定从容、不慌不忙的状态或态度。
explanation_english: Describes a state or attitude of remaining calm, composed, and unhurried even in stressful or sudden situations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面對突如其來嘅問題，佢仲氣定神閒，慢慢咁搞掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 deoi3 dat6 jyu4 kei4 loi4 ge3 man6 tai4, keoi5 zung6 hei3 ding6 san4 haan4, maan6 maan6 gam2 gaau2 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面对突如其来的问题，他仍然气定神闲，慢慢地把事情处理好。
examples.english_sentence: Facing the sudden problem, he remained calm and composed and took his time to deal with it.

mandarin_meaning: 氣喘吁吁
english_meaning: out of breath; panting; gasping for breath
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，形容因運動、奔跑或勞累而呼吸急促、氣喘的狀態，也可泛指慌張或慌亂的樣子。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone who is out of breath or panting from exertion; can also be used more loosely to describe being flustered or in a rush.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢跑咗幾陣，已經氣羅氣喘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 paau2 zo2 gei2 zan6, ji5 ging1 hei3 lo4 hei3 cyun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他跑了好一會兒，已經氣喘吁吁了。
examples.english_sentence: He ran for a while and is already out of breath.

mandarin_meaning: 把（事情）弄得一团糟；把一切搞砸
english_meaning: to mess everything up; to screw things up completely; to make a total mess of something
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話俚語，表示把事情弄亂或搞砸，常帶責備、不滿或斥責的語氣，類似「把一切都搞砸了／弄得一團糟」。
explanation_english: A coarse Cantonese slang phrase used to say someone has made a complete mess of things or ruined everything. It often carries blame, frustration, or an admonishing tone, similar to "mess everything up" or "screw it all up."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日咁樣，淨係識滚搅晒啲嘢！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 gam2 joeng6, zing6 hai6 sik1 gwan2 gaau2 saai3 di1 je5!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是這樣，總是把事情搞得一團糟！
examples.english_sentence: You're always like this — you only know how to mess things up!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一到就滚搅晒成個計劃，最後要我哋重新開始。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 dou3 zau6 gwan2 gaau2 saai3 sing4 go3 gai3 waak6, zeoi6 hau6 jiu3 ngo5 dei6 cung4 san1 hoi1 ci2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一來就把整個計劃搞砸，最後要我們重新開始。
examples.english_sentence: He arrived and messed up the whole plan; in the end we had to start over.

jyutping: gwan2 seoi2 m4 hoeng2, hoeng2 seoi2 m4 gwan2
mandarin_meaning: 能干的人不爱夸耀；爱喧哗的人往往没有真本事（能者不言）
english_meaning: Capable people are quiet while those who make a lot of noise often lack real ability (i.e., actions speak louder than words).
explanation_mandarin: 一句粤语俗语，用來形容有真本事的人通常低調、不張揚；反而愛出風頭、誇誇其談的人未必有實際能力。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb meaning that those with real ability tend to be low-key and do not boast, whereas those who are loud often lack substance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好叻但好低調，真係滚水唔响，响水唔滚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 lek1 daan6 hou2 dai1 diu6 zan1 hai6 gwan2 seoi2 m4 hoeng2, hoeng2 seoi2 m4 gwan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很能干但很低调，真是“滚水不响，响水不滚”。
examples.english_sentence: He's very capable but low-key — it's truly a case of 'boiling water doesn't make noise, noisy water doesn't boil' (capable people don't boast).

jyutping: gwan2 seoi2 luk6 zyu1 coeng4, loeng5 tau4 suk1
mandarin_meaning: 见风转舵／两面讨好（不敢明确表态或两边都想讨好的消极态度）
english_meaning: To sit on the fence / play both sides; be noncommittal or try to please both parties and end up retreating on both ends
explanation_mandarin: 字面意为把猪肠放入滚水中会两头收缩，比喻人在关键时刻不敢明确表态或见风转舵、两面讨好，结果两边都退缩、无所作为。
explanation_english: Literally 'boiling water cooks pig intestines, both ends shrink.' Figuratively it describes someone who avoids taking a clear stance, tries to please both sides or changes with the wind, and ultimately withdraws from both ends or achieves nothing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強喺客戶面前滾水渌豬腸，兩頭縮，兩邊都想討好，結果乜都無做成。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 hai2 haak3 wu6 min6 cin4 gwan2 seoi2 luk6 zyu1 coeng4, loeng5 tau4 suk1, loeng5 bin1 dou1 soeng2 tou2 hou2, git3 gwo2 mat1 dou1 mou5 zou6 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强在客户面前见风转舵、两面讨好，结果什么都没做成。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Keung tried to play both sides in front of the client and please everyone, and ended up accomplishing nothing.

mandarin_meaning: 用滚烫的水烫脚；引申为受到严重教训、惨败或尴尬失败
english_meaning: Literally: to scald/soak one's feet in boiling water. Figuratively: to receive a severe lesson, be badly beaten, or suffer humiliation.
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是用滚烫的水烫脚，常用于民间保健或治疗脚痛。口语中有引申义，表示遭受严厉教训、被狠狠打败或非常尴尬的失败，属于粤语口语/俚语用法。
explanation_english: Literally means to scald/soak the feet with boiling water, often for medicinal relief. Colloquially in Cantonese it can be used figuratively to mean receiving a harsh lesson, being soundly beaten, or suffering an embarrassing defeat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆話腳痛，要用滾水淥腳先舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 waa6 goek3 tung3, jiu3 jung6 gwan2 seoi2 luk6 goek3 sin1 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶說腳痛，要用滾水燙腳才舒服。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma says her feet hurt and needs to soak them in hot water to feel better.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好亂講嘢，小心滾水淥腳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lyun6 gong2 je5, siu2 sam1 gwan2 seoi2 luk6 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別亂說話，小心會吃大虧/受教訓。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say random things, or you might get into big trouble (or learn a hard lesson).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 昨晚比賽佢哋畀人滾水淥腳，整場都輸曬，面都冇晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zok6 maan5 bei2 coi3 keoi5 dei6 bei2 jan4 gwan2 seoi2 luk6 goek3, zang2 coeng4 dou1 syu1 saai3, min6 dou1 mou5 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚比賽他們被狠狠打敗，整場都輸光了，丟盡了臉。
examples.english_sentence: They were badly beaten in last night's match; they lost everything and were utterly humiliated.

jyutping: gwan2 jau4 luk6 lou5 syu2, jat1 wok6 suk6
mandarin_meaning: 字面意思是把老鼠放進滾燙的油裡，整個鍋都熟了。比喻一件事或一個人被揭發或出事，牽連到整個團體，大家一起完蛋或一起被處理；也可引申為一次過全部解決或處理。
english_meaning: Literally 'throw a mouse into boiling oil, the whole wok is cooked.' Figuratively: if one person is exposed or a problem arises, the whole group will be implicated or ruined; can also mean doing everything in one go (all resolved/finished at once).
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容某件事一旦被揭發或出錯，會牽連到其他人或整個團隊，導致大家一起受罰或完蛋；在某些語境亦可表示一次過把所有東西處理/解決。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying used to describe a situation where, once one person or matter is exposed, the entire group becomes implicated or ruined; in some contexts it can also mean handling everything all at once.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果呢件事畀人揭發，啲人就會滚油渌老鼠，一镬熟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 ni1 gin6 si6 bei2 jan4 kit3 faat3, di1 jan4 zau6 wui5 gwan2 jau4 luk6 lou5 syu2, jat1 wok6 suk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果這件事被揭發，大家就會一起完蛋。
examples.english_sentence: If this gets exposed, everyone will be implicated/finished.

mandarin_meaning: 非常燙／非常熱（有時視語境也可指很辣）
english_meaning: scorching hot; piping hot; extremely hot (sometimes used for very spicy food depending on context)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，通常用來形容溫度非常高、燙到的狀態（如食物或天氣），視上下文也可用來強調食物很辣。常見於香港日常對話中，帶有強調語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe something extremely hot to the touch or very hot weather; depending on context it can also emphasize that food is very spicy. Common in everyday Hong Kong speech and carries an emphatic tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢碟咖喱滾热辣，食嘅時候小心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dip6 gaa3lei1 gwan2 jit6 laat6, sik6 ge3 si4hau6 siu2sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這盤咖哩非常燙，吃的時候要小心。
examples.english_sentence: This plate of curry is piping hot — be careful when you eat it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日天氣滾热辣，出門記得帶水同遮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 tin1hei3 gwan2 jit6 laat6, ceot1 mun4 gei3 dak1 daai3 seoi2 tung4 ze3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天天氣非常炎熱，出門記得帶水和傘。
examples.english_sentence: The weather today is scorching; remember to take water and an umbrella when you go out.

mandarin_meaning: 紅綠交替閃爍；顏色鮮豔、花哨
english_meaning: to flash red and green; gaudily multicolored; eye-catching (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，原指燈光或裝飾紅綠交替閃爍；引申用來形容外觀顏色鮮豔、花哨、很引人注意。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase originally describing lights or decorations flashing red and green; extended to describe something gaudily colorful or eye-catching.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰條街嘅霓虹燈滾紅滾綠，幾搶眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 tiu4 gaai1 ge3 ngai4 hung4 dang1 gwan2 hung4 gwan2 luk6, gei2 coeng2 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那條街的霓虹燈紅綠交替閃爍，挺搶眼的。
examples.english_sentence: The neon lights on that street flash red and green — they're quite eye-catching.

mandarin_meaning: 怒火中烧；大发脾气
english_meaning: to fly into a rage; to become very angry
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语用语，形容突然非常生气或勃然大怒，往往情绪激动、难以平静。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone suddenly becoming very angry or furious, often with intense emotional reaction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到嗰件事就灯光火着，成個人好激動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 go2 gin6 si6 zau6 dang1 gwong1 fo2 zoek6, sing4 go3 jan4 hou2 gik1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一听到那件事就火冒三丈，整个人很激动。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as he heard about it, he flew into a rage and was very agitated.

mandarin_meaning: 指日常生活中很小、琐碎的东西或开支（如灯油、蜡烛等），引申为琐事或微不足道的事情。
english_meaning: Refers to minor everyday items or small living expenses (e.g. lamp oil, candle wax); figuratively, trivial matters or petty issues.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，原指燈油、火蠟等日常小物，常用來比喻生活中的瑣碎小事或微小開支，亦可用來批評為小事爭執不值得。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression originally naming small household items like lamp oil and candle wax. It's commonly used metaphorically for trivial everyday matters or minor expenses, and to criticise squabbling over petty things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好為咗啲燈油火蜡去爭拗啦，重要嘅係大家開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 wai6 zo2 di1 dang1 jau4 fo2 laap6 heoi3 zing1 au2 laa1, zung6 jiu3 ge3 hai6 daai6 gaa1 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要为一些灯油火蜡的琐事争执，重要的是大家开心。
examples.english_sentence: Don't argue over trivial things like lamp oil and candle wax; what's important is that everyone is happy.

synonyms: 柴米油鹽（指日常小事或開支）

jyutping: dang1 sam1 haau1 zung1, mou5 jam1
mandarin_meaning: 比喻做事徒勞無功、沒有效果或白費力氣
english_meaning: Literally 'beat a bell with the wick, no sound' — an idiom meaning to make futile efforts; to do something that yields no result
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容付出努力但沒有成果，或做法徒勞無功、白費力氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing efforts that produce no result — actions that are futile or pointless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家咁樣做係灯芯敲钟，冇音，淨係浪費時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 gam2 joeng6 zou6 hai6 dang1 sam1 haau1 zung1, mou5 jam1, zing6 hai6 long6 fai3 si4 gaan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你现在这样做是灯芯敲钟，没效果，只是在浪费时间。
examples.english_sentence: What you're doing now is like beating a bell with the wick — no sound; it's pointless and just a waste of time.

mandarin_meaning: 炖冬菇 / 炖香菇 (炖煮冬菇)
english_meaning: to stew shiitake mushrooms
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是用炖的方式烹煮冬菇（即香菇）。主要用於烹飪語境，並非常見的俚語或成語。
explanation_english: Literally 'to stew shiitake mushrooms' — a verb phrase meaning to cook shiitake (donggu/xianggu) by stewing. It's primarily a cooking expression rather than a widely used idiom or slang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽今晚炖咗冬菇雞，成間屋都好香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 gam1 maan5 dun6 zo2 dung1 gu1 gai1, sing4 gaan1 uk1 dou1 hou2 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈今晚炖了冬菇鸡，整个房子都很香。
examples.english_sentence: Mom stewed chicken with shiitake mushrooms tonight; the whole house smells delicious.

mandarin_meaning: 我怎麼知道 / 怎麼會知道
english_meaning: How should I know? / I have no idea
explanation_mandarin: 表示不知道或沒把握的口語用法，常帶有隨意或略帶不耐煩的語氣（粵語裡常說「點唔知」）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning "How should I know?" Used to indicate lack of knowledge or unwillingness to answer, often with a casual or slightly impatient tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你問我佢幾時返？我點唔知呀！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 man6 ngo5 keoi5 gei2 si4 faan1? ngo5 dim2 m4 zi1 aa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你問我他什麼時候回來？我怎麼知道啊！
examples.english_sentence: You ask me when he'll be back? How should I know!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰份報告好唔好，我點唔知，我未睇過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 fan6 bou3 gou3 hou2 m4 hou2, ngo5 dim2 m4 zi1, ngo5 mei6 tai2 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那份報告好不好，我怎麼知道，我還沒看過。
examples.english_sentence: Whether that report is good or not—how would I know? I haven't read it yet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話佢有冇約會？我點唔知啦，問佢自己啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 keoi5 jau5 mou5 joek3 wui6? ngo5 dim2 m4 zi1 laa1, man6 keoi5 zi6 gei2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說他有沒有約會？我怎麼會知道，去問他自己吧。
examples.english_sentence: You say whether he has a date? How would I know—ask him yourself.

mandarin_meaning: 怎麼可能？（表示難以做到或難以置信）
english_meaning: How is that possible? / How could (I/you) possibly...?
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感嘆詞 / 疑問短語（口語）
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示對某事感到難以置信或認為不可能做到，常用作反問或抱怨的語氣詞。
explanation_english: Used to express disbelief or that something is impossible or unlikely; often a rhetorical question or complaint about inability to do something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 咁多功課，我點得呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam2 do1 gung1 fo3, ngo5 dim2 dak1 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這麼多功課，我怎麼(做)得完？
examples.english_sentence: So much homework—how am I supposed to finish it?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢要我而家交錢？點得呀！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jiu3 ngo5 ji4 gaa1 gaau1 cin2? dim2 dak1 aa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他要我現在交錢？怎麼可能！
examples.english_sentence: He wants me to pay right now? No way!

mandarin_meaning: 怎么回事 / 怎么样
english_meaning: What's going on? / What's up? / What's the matter?
explanation_mandarin: 口语粤语用法，用来询问情况、表示惊讶或要求对方解释发生了什么。相当于“怎么回事？”或“怎么了？”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to ask what is happening, to express mild surprise, or to prompt an explanation — equivalent to "What's going on?" or "What's up?"

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你點系呀？發生咩事？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dim2 hai6 aa3? faat3 saang1 me1 si6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你怎么了？发生什么事？
examples.english_sentence: What's wrong with you? What happened?

synonyms: 發生咩事 (faat3 saang1 me1 si6)

mandarin_meaning: 不知道該怎麼說/不知如何是好
english_meaning: Don't know what to say / at a loss for words or how to handle it
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示對某事無語或不知如何處理，意指「不知道該怎麼說才好」或「不知道該怎麼辦」。
explanation_english: Used to express being at a loss for words or unsure how to handle a situation — meaning 'I don't know what to say' or 'I don't know what to do'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講完啲事，我真係唔知點話點好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 jyun4 di1 si6, ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 zi1 dim2 waa6 dim2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說完那些事情，我真的不知道該怎麼說才好。
examples.english_sentence: He finished telling me about those things; I'm really at a loss for how to respond.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家公司咁樣裁員，大家都唔知點話點好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 gung1 si1 gam2 joeng6 coi3 jyun4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zi1 dim2 waa6 dim2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在公司這樣裁員，大家都不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: With the company laying people off like this, everyone doesn't know what to say or do.

mandarin_meaning: 垄断（或独占）市场的生意；在某个市场上独家经营、缺乏竞争的业务。
english_meaning: A monopoly or sole-source business; an operation that exclusively occupies a market with little or no competition.
explanation_mandarin: 指在某個市場上獨佔經營、缺乏競爭對手的生意模式，通常含有壟斷或佔據市場主導地位的意思。
explanation_english: Refers to a business model in which a company exclusively occupies a market with few or no competitors, implying monopoly or market dominance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間公司喺本地市場做緊独市生意，其他對手好難入場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 gung1 si1 hai2 bun2 dei6 si5 coeng4 zou6 gan2 duk6 si5 saang1 ji3, kei4 taa1 deoi3 sau2 hou2 naan4 jap6 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家公司在本地市场做独市生意，其他对手很难进入市场。
examples.english_sentence: This company is operating a monopoly (sole-source) business in the local market, making it hard for other competitors to enter.

mandarin_meaning: 只坚持一种做法或观点，不肯变通
english_meaning: to stick to a single approach or viewpoint; to be inflexible
explanation_mandarin: 指固执地坚持某一种做法或观点，不肯变通或采纳别人的意见，带有批评意味。
explanation_english: An idiom used to criticize someone who insists on one method or viewpoint and refuses to adapt or consider alternatives.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺工作上獨沽一味，唔願意改進，最後被辭退。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gung1 zok3 soeng6 duk6 gu1 jat1 mei6 , m4 jyun6 ji3 goi2 zeon3 , zeoi6 hau6 bei6 ci4 teoi3 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在工作上固守一法，不肯改进，最后被辞退。
examples.english_sentence: He stuck to one way at work, refused to improve, and was eventually fired.

mandarin_meaning: 独自行动、不依赖他人的人；特指性格独立、做事特立独行的人（类似“孤胆英雄”“独行者”）
english_meaning: a lone ranger / maverick; someone who acts alone and doesn't rely on others
explanation_mandarin: “独行侠”用于形容那种喜欢独自行动、独立做决定、不太依从他人意见的人。语气可褒可中性，亦可带有不太合群的意味。
explanation_english: Refers to a person who prefers to act alone and make independent decisions. It often describes a maverick or solitary hero and can be positive or neutral.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個獨行俠，成日自己做決定，唔會理其他人嘅意見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 duk6 hang4 haap6, seng4 jat6 zi6 gei2 zou6 kyut3 ding6, m4 wui5 lei5 kei4 taa1 jan4 ge3 ji3 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是个独行侠，总是自己做决定，不太在意别人的意见。
examples.english_sentence: He's a lone ranger; he always makes decisions on his own and doesn't care much about others' opinions.

mandarin_meaning: 獨自占有好處難以得到豐厚的利益；獨吞不利，與人合作才能發展
english_meaning: You can't prosper by monopolizing everything; hoarding gains for yourself won't bring big benefits—cooperation is needed to grow.
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「一個人獨自吃東西難以變胖」，引申為一個人獨吞好處或資源，難以得到大的利益或發展，強調合作或分享的重要性。
explanation_english: Literally 'if you eat alone you won't get fat.' Figuratively it means monopolizing benefits rarely leads to major gains—emphasizing that sharing or cooperating is necessary for greater success.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好諗住一個人攬晒，獨食難肥，大家合作先至可以做大生意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lam2 zyu6 jat1 go3 jan4 laam2 saai3, duk6 sik6 naan4 fei4, daai6 gaa1 hip6 zok3 sin1 zi3 ho2 ji5 zou6 daai6 saang1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要想着一个人揽下所有，独食难肥，大家合作才能把生意做大。
examples.english_sentence: Don't try to take everything for yourself—you can't prosper by monopolizing; cooperating is how you can grow the business.

jyutping: din6 dang1 saam1 gwaa3 lou5 syu2 soeng1, jat1 gou1 jat1 ngai2
mandarin_meaning: （用来）形容一对人或物高矮、大小不相称，常用以指情侣或搭档一高一矮、外形不协调
english_meaning: Describes a pair (people or things) that are mismatched in height/size — literally 'one tall, one short'; often used about couples or duos that look uneven or ill-matched.
explanation_mandarin: 俗语，字面意为“电灯衫挂老鼠箱，一高一矮”，用来形容两个人或两样东西高矮或大小差别明显、不相称，语气可带戏谑或调侃。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying literally meaning 'one tall, one short.' It describes two people or things with a clear mismatch in height/size; the tone is often teasing or humorous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個好似电灯杉挂老鼠箱，一高一矮，行埋一齊好搞笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 hou2 ci5 din6 dang1 saam1 gwaa3 lou5 syu2 soeng1, jat1 gou1 jat1 ngai2, haang4 maai4 jat1 cai4 hou2 gaau2 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们两个人像电灯杉挂老鼠箱，一高一矮，走在一起很滑稽。
examples.english_sentence: They look mismatched — one tall, one short — walking together looks funny.

jyutping: din6 dang1 daam2, m4 tung1 hei3
mandarin_meaning: （粤语俚语）形容人愚笨、没头脑、反应迟钝
english_meaning: Cantonese slang for someone who is dimwitted or scatterbrained
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚语（贬义），可作名词或形容词
explanation_mandarin: 「电灯胆，唔通气」是香港粤语的口语说法，用来戏谑或责备某人愚笨、反应慢或常忘记事情，语气多为轻蔑或玩笑。
explanation_english: This Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase is used to tease or scold someone as being dull-witted, slow to react, or forgetful. The tone is usually derogatory or joking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做嘢都唔记得，真係电灯胆，唔通气。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zou6 je5 dou1 m4 gei3 dak1, zan1 hai6 din6 dang1 daam2, m4 tung1 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是做事都忘记，真是个笨蛋/没头脑。
examples.english_sentence: He always forgets things — what a dimwit.

mandarin_meaning: （口語/網絡用語）強調肯定、確實
english_meaning: A colloquial emphatic affirmation meaning 'indeed' or 'definitely' (often playful or ironic)
explanation_mandarin: 「的而且确」為非正式的口語/網絡用法，混合了「的确」與「而且」的成分，用來以誇張或戲謔的語氣強調某事確實如此，常見於粵語社群或網絡用語中。
explanation_english: An informal internet/Cantonese expression that blends 的确 (indeed) and 而且 (moreover) to provide an emphatic — sometimes playful or ironic — affirmation that something is certainly true.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好叻，的而且确！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 lek1, dik1 ji4 ce2 kok3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的很厲害，的而且確！
examples.english_sentence: He's really impressive — indeed!

mandarin_meaning: 鼓起勇氣／下定決心
english_meaning: to summon up the courage; to make up one's mind to do something
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示鼓起勇氣或下定決心去做某事，常用於勉勵自己或別人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to summon up courage or resolve to do something. Often used to encourage oneself or others to take action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我終於的起心肝同佢講清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung1 jyu1 dik1 hei2 sam1 gon1 tung4 keoi5 gong2 cing1 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我終於鼓起勇氣跟他說清楚。
examples.english_sentence: I finally summoned the courage to tell him clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 入監/坐牢（俚語）
english_meaning: to be sent to prison / to end up in jail (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，指被送入監獄或坐牢。屬口語、不正式用法，常用於日常會話中形容會被判刑入獄。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning to be sent to prison or end up in jail. It is informal and used colloquially to describe being convicted or incarcerated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果畀人告，你可能要監粗嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 bei2 jan4 gou3, nei5 ho2 nang4 jiu3 gaam1 cou1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果被人告，你可能要入監了。
examples.english_sentence: If you're accused, you might end up in prison.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢因為貪污被揭發，最後真係監粗嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1 wai6 taam1 wu1 bei6 gik1 faat3, zeoi3 hau6 zan1 hai6 gaam1 cou1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他因為貪污被揭發，最後真的入獄了。
examples.english_sentence: He was exposed for corruption and eventually really went to prison.

mandarin_meaning: 唠叨/管閒事/指手畫腳
english_meaning: to nag or meddle; to be bossy and nitpick
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容人對別人的事情不停指手畫腳、嘮叨或過度干預，對細節斤斤計較。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who constantly nags, meddles, or criticizes others, being overly bossy and nitpicky about details.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個上司成日喺度督口督鼻，我做嘢都冇得閒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 soeng5 si1 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 duk1 hau2 duk1 bei6, ngo5 zou6 je5 dou1 mou5 dak1 haan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个上司总是在那儿唠叨、指手画脚，我做事都没空。
examples.english_sentence: That boss is always nagging and meddling; I can't get any work done.

mandarin_meaning: 非標準或罕見詞語，可能為打字錯誤或地方用語；字面逐字拆解為「短」「度」「闊（阔）」「封」，無固定或廣泛接受的含義。
english_meaning: Not a standard or widely recognized Cantonese term; possibly a typo or very local usage. Literally the characters read 'short / degree / wide / seal', with no established meaning.
partOfSpeech_english: non-standard phrase / unknown part of speech
explanation_mandarin: 此詞在常用粵語詞典及語料庫中未見收錄。可能是打字錯誤、拼寫變體或極地方言用語。若單純按字面理解，可分別解作「短」「程度」「闊（寬）」「封（封住/封閉/封號）」，但合起來並無固定含義，需根據語境確認。
explanation_english: This expression is not found in common Cantonese dictionaries or corpora. It may be a typo, a variant spelling, or a very local colloquialism. Literally the characters mean 'short', 'degree', 'wide', and 'seal', but together they have no established meaning — the interpretation would depend entirely on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個「短度阔封」係咪打錯字？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 'dyun2 dou6 fut3 fung1' hai6 mai6 daa2 co3 zi6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个“短度阔封”是不是打错字？
examples.english_sentence: Is '短度阔封' a typo?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺網上見到有人講「短度阔封」，但冇人解釋意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 mong5 soeng6 gin3 dou2 jau5 jan4 gong2 'dyun2 dou6 fut3 fung1', daan6 mou5 jan4 gaai2 sik1 ji3si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在网上看到有人说“短度阔封”，但没人解释意思。
examples.english_sentence: I saw someone use '短度阔封' online, but nobody explained what it means.

cantonese: 端午节先嚟拜山，迟唔迟啲
jyutping: dyun1 ng5 zit3 sin1 lai4 baai3 saan1, ci4 m4 ci4 di1
mandarin_meaning: 端午节才来扫墓/拜山，难道不觉得有点迟吗？（用于责备只在节日才来的人）
english_meaning: Only coming to pay respects at the graves on the Dragon Boat Festival — isn't that a bit late? (used to scold someone who only appears on festival days)
explanation_mandarin: 用于责备或抱怨某人只在节日（如端午节）才来扫墓或看望，暗含不够尽孝或不真诚的意味。属于粤语口语，带讽刺或责备色彩。
explanation_english: Used to reproach or complain that someone only visits graves or family on festival days (e.g. the Dragon Boat Festival), implying a lack of genuine filial duty or sincerity. Colloquial Cantonese with a sardonic tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢平時都冇嚟探阿媽，端午节先嚟拜山，迟唔迟啲？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ping4 si4 dou1 mou5 lai4 taam3 aa3 maa1, dyun1 ng5 zit3 sin1 lai4 baai3 saan1, ci4 m4 ci4 di1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他平时都不来看妈妈，端午节才来扫墓，迟不迟啊？
examples.english_sentence: He normally doesn't visit Mom; he only comes to pay respects at the graves on the Dragon Boat Festival — isn't that a bit late?

cantonese: 端陽有雨是豐年，芒種行雷米滿田
jyutping: dyun1 joeng4 jau5 jyu5 si6 fung1 nin4, mong4 zung2 haang4 leoi4 mai5 mun5 tin4
mandarin_meaning: 端午若遇雨則為豐年；芒種時雷聲響，稻米會豐收。
english_meaning: A farming proverb: rain at the Dragon Boat Festival and thunder during Mangzhong signal a bountiful harvest (especially rice).
explanation_mandarin: 這句農業諺語把傳統節氣的天氣與收成聯繫起來：端午（端陽）有雨代表降水充足，利於作物成長；芒種期間若打雷，通常表示生長條件良好，稻穀可能豐收。反映農民根據節氣與天象預測年成的民間經驗。
explanation_english: A rural proverb linking weather during specific solar terms to harvest outcomes: rain on the Dragon Boat Festival (Duanwu) and thunder during Mangzhong (Grain in Ear) are taken as signs of sufficient water and good growing conditions, predicting a plentiful rice harvest. It reflects folk agricultural knowledge for predicting yields.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿爸成日講：「端陽有雨是豐年，芒種行雷米滿田」，話今年收成應該唔錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baa1 sing4 jat6 gong2: "dyun1 joeng4 jau5 jyu5 si6 fung1 nin4, mong4 zung2 haang4 leoi4 mai5 mun5 tin4", waa6 gam1 nin4 sau1 sing4 jing1 goi1 m4 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 爸爸常說：「端午有雨是豐年，芒種打雷米滿田」，說今年的收成應該不錯。
examples.english_sentence: Dad often says, "If it rains on Dragon Boat Festival it's a good year; if there's thunder during Mangzhong the rice fields will be full," meaning this year's harvest should be good.

mandarin_meaning: 第一时间 / 立即、尽快
english_meaning: at the first opportunity; immediately; as soon as possible
explanation_mandarin: 表示在最短时间内、尽快采取行动或通知，一有情况就马上处理。
explanation_english: Indicates doing something immediately or at the earliest possible moment when something happens; used to express prompt action or notification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我一收到消息，就會第一時間通知你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 sau1 dou3 siu1 sik1, zau6 wui5 dai6 jat1 si4 gaan3 tung1 zi1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我一收到消息，就会在第一时间通知你。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as I receive the news, I'll inform you right away.

jyutping: dai6 jat1 zan6 deoi3 soeng5, mou5 pou2 (常見正寫: 「第一陣對上，冇譜」)
mandarin_meaning: 一开始就没有谱/没有章法，行为没计划、很随意或难以预测
english_meaning: Right from the start there's no plan or sense—chaotic, unpredictable or acting without a script
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口语短语 / 形容词性短语
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，通常用来形容一個人或一件事從一開始就沒安排、沒規矩或表現得很亂，類似「沒譜」、「沒規劃」、「亂來」。書寫上常見變體為「第一陣對上，冇譜」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe someone or something that, right from the outset, has no plan, sense or order—acting unpredictably or recklessly. Often written as the variant "第一陣對上，冇譜" and is similar to saying "there's no plan" or "completely chaotic".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢第一陣對上就冇譜，做嘢成日亂嚟，點信得過？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dai6 jat1 zan6 deoi3 soeng5 zau6 mou5 pou2, zou6 je5 seng4 jat6 lyun6 lai4, dim2 seon3 dak1 gwo3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一开始就没谱，做事总是乱来，怎么能相信？
examples.english_sentence: He was clueless/unreliable from the very start—always doing things messily. How can you trust him?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次個project開波嗰陣，真係第一陣對上冇譜，大家一路摸索一路改。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 go3 project hoi1 bo1 go2 zan6, zan1 hai6 dai6 jat1 zan6 deoi3 soeng5 mou5 pou2, daai6 gaa1 jat1 lou6 mok6 sok3 jat1 lou6 goi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次项目一开始真的很没谱，大家一边摸索一边改。
examples.english_sentence: This project was really unplanned at the start—everyone was feeling their way and making changes as they went.

jyutping: dai6 jat1 coeng1, dai6 ji6 jing1, dai6 saam1 maa5 gaau1 long4
mandarin_meaning: 第一鲳鱼，第二（𱇮）鱼，第三马鲛郎（按序列举鱼类）——一种广东口语的俚语/顺口溜，用来戏谑地按顺序列举事物，常含义为“随便排列、无甚重要性、胡乱数数”
english_meaning: “First the pomfret, second the 𱇮, third the Spanish mackerel” — a Cantonese colloquial rhyme used jokingly to list things in order; implies a trivial/arbitrary ranking or a playful, nonsensical enumeration.
explanation_mandarin: 这是广东话的一个口语顺口溜，字面上列举三种鱼（其中“𱇮”为罕见字/鱼名），常用来戏谑或轻蔑地按顺序列举事物，表示排列是随意或无关紧要的，也可表示说话内容是胡乱拼凑、无实质意义。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial rhyme that literally lists three fish (the middle character 𱇮 is a rare fish name). People use it playfully or ironically to enumerate things in order, often to suggest the ranking is arbitrary, trivial, or that the speaker is spouting nonsense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好散，成日都係『第一鲳，第二𱇮，第三马鲛郎』，講完冇重點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 saan3, sing4 jat6 dou1 hai6 'dai6 jat1 coeng1, dai6 ji6 jing1, dai6 saam1 maa5 gaau1 long4', gong2 jyun4 mou5 zung6 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話很散亂，總是說“第一鲳，第二𱇮，第三马鲛郎”，說完沒重點。
examples.english_sentence: He talks in a scattered way, always saying 'first the pomfret, second the 𱇮, third the Spanish mackerel' — he finishes without a point.

mandarin_meaning: 誰都… / 人都…（表示普遍現象或理所當然的結果）
english_meaning: anyone would… / everybody… (used to state a general or expected reaction)
explanation_mandarin: 「系人都…」是廣東話的口語用法，用來表示一種普遍性或理所當然的反應或結果，相當於普通話的「誰都…」「人都…」。通常用於引出一般性的判斷或感受，語氣偏口語化。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning 'anyone would…' or 'everybody…'. It introduces a generalization or an expected reaction/outcome (equivalent to Mandarin '誰都…' or English 'anyone would…'). Common in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 咁大隻狗一吠，你系人都會驚㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam2 daai6 zek3 gau2 jat1 fai3, nei5 hai6 jan4 dou1 wui5 geng1 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这么大的狗一叫，你誰都會害怕。
examples.english_sentence: If such a big dog barks, anyone would be scared.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新入職做錯嘢好正常，系人都會犯錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 jap6 zik1 zou6 co3 je5 hou2 zing3soeng4, hai6 jan4 dou1 wui5 faan6 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剛入職做錯很正常，誰都會犯錯。
examples.english_sentence: Making mistakes when newly employed is normal; anyone will make mistakes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 天氣咁凍，系人都會覺得冷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tin1 hei3 gam2 dung3, hai6 jan4 dou1 wui5 gok3 dak1 laang5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 天氣這麼冷，誰都會覺得冷。
examples.english_sentence: With weather this cold, anyone would feel cold.

mandarin_meaning: 差不多；大約
english_meaning: more or less; about; roughly
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语短语，用来表示数量、程度或情況上的大概、差不多或不精确的估计，也可表示「大概如此」或「馬馬虎虎、凑合」的意思。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to indicate an approximation or rough estimate of quantity, degree, or situation (i.e., 'more or less', 'about'). It can also mean 'roughly the same' or 'so-so/adequate'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個成績系咁上下，唔使太擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 sing4zik1 hai6 gam2 soeng6 haa6, m4 sai2 taai3 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的成绩差不多，不用太担心。
examples.english_sentence: His grades are about average; don't worry too much.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部手機嘅價錢系咁上下，差唔多五百蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 sau2 gei1 ge3 gaa3 cin4 hai6 gam2 soeng6 haa6, caa1 m4 do1 ng5 baak3 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部手机的价格差不多，大约五百块。
examples.english_sentence: The price of this phone is about right—roughly 500 dollars.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我估佢有二十幾歲，系咁上下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gu2 keoi5 jau5 ji6 sap6 gei2 seoi3, hai6 gam2 soeng6 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我估他二十几岁，差不多就是这样。
examples.english_sentence: I guess he's in his early twenties — more or less.

mandarin_meaning: 有这么严重/重要吗？（表示怀疑或不以为然）
english_meaning: Is it such a big deal? / Is it that serious? (used to question or downplay something)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，常用於反問或表示不以為然，質疑某事是否真的那麼嚴重或重要。可用單獨疑問或接「件事」等詞。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used rhetorically to question or downplay the importance or seriousness of something. Often used with a questioning tone (e.g. '係咁大咩？') or expanded to '係咁大件事？'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你淨係遲到一次，唔好搞到好似世界末日，系咁大咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zing6 hai6 ci4 dou3 jat1 ci3, m4 hou2 gaau2 dou3 hou2 ci5 sai3 gaai3 mut6 jat6, hai6 gam2 daai6 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你只迟到一次，不要搞得好像世界末日，有那么严重/重要吗？
examples.english_sentence: You were only late once — don't act like it's the end of the world. Is it such a big deal?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話考試唔及格，我講唔使咁驚，系咁大？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 haau2 si3 m4 kap6 gaak3, ngo5 gong2 m4 sai2 gam2 geng1, hai6 gam2 daai6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说考试不及格，我说不用那么担心，是这么严重/重要吗？
examples.english_sentence: He said he failed the exam; I said don't be so worried — is it that big of a deal?

mandarin_meaning: 是不是啊？（用于确认或表示怀疑/惊讶）
english_meaning: Isn't it? / Is that so? (used to seek confirmation or express doubt/surprise)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 疑问短语 / 语气助词用法
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语中常用的反问或确认语气词，由“係唔係”（是不是）加上“先”（加强或缓和语气）组成，用来确认信息、表示怀疑或惊讶，类似普通话的“是不是/是不是啊”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese question tag used to seek confirmation or express doubt/surprise. It combines '係唔係' (is or isn't) with '先' which adds emphasis or a softening effect, roughly equivalent to Mandarin '是不是' or English 'isn't it?/is that so?'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話今晚會嚟，系唔系先？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 gam1 maan5 wui5 lai4, hai6 m4 hai6 sin1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说今晚会来，是不是？
examples.english_sentence: He said he's coming tonight — is that right?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講佢辭職喇，系唔系先？
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 keoi5 ci4 zik1 laa3, hai6 m4 hai6 sin1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听说他辞职了，是真的吗？
examples.english_sentence: I heard he resigned — is that true?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋約咗八點見，系唔系先？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 joek3 zo2 baat3 dim2 gin3, hai6 m4 hai6 sin1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们约好八点见，是吧？
examples.english_sentence: We arranged to meet at eight — right?

mandarin_meaning: 就是/是啦/对啦（表示同意、讓步或強調的語氣）
english_meaning: A Cantonese colloquial particle expressing agreement, concession, emphasis, or mild annoyance (similar to 'that's right', 'yeah, right', or 'come on').
explanation_mandarin: 「系啦」是廣東話常用的語氣詞，通常用來表示同意、讓步、強調或帶點不耐煩的回應。根據語氣和語境，可相當於普通話的“就是/是啦/對啦”。
explanation_english: ‘hai6 laa3’ is a common Cantonese discourse particle used to indicate agreement, concession, emphasis, or mild annoyance. Depending on tone and context, it corresponds to Mandarin '就是/是啦' or English phrases like 'that's right', 'yeah, right', or 'alright'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 系啦，我拎咗你本書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai6 laa3, ngo5 ling1 zo2 nei5 bun2 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 是啦，我拿了你的书。
examples.english_sentence: Yes, I took your book.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 系啦，下次我會早啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai6 laa3, haa6 ci3 ngo5 wui5 zou2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 好吧，下次我會早一點。
examples.english_sentence: Alright, I'll be earlier next time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 系啦，你講得啱，唔使再爭啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai6 laa3, nei5 gong2 dak1 aam1, m4 sai2 zoi3 zang1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 好啦，你說得對，不用再爭了。
examples.english_sentence: Okay, you're right — no need to argue anymore.

mandarin_meaning: 就这样吧 / 暂且如此 / 这样才好
english_meaning: That's how it should be / Let's leave it like this for now / This is best for now
explanation_mandarin: 口语用法，用来表示对当前做法或结论的肯定、接受或暂时将事情放在那样处理，相当于“就这样吧”“暂且如此”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to accept or conclude that the current way is fine for now, or to indicate leaving matters as they are. Equivalent to "let's leave it like that" or "that's how it should be for now."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你覺得咁樣最好，就系噉先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 gok3 dak1 gam2 joeng6 zeoi3 hou2, zau6 hai6 gam2 sin1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你觉得这样最好，那就先这样吧。
examples.english_sentence: If you think this is best, then let's leave it like this for now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事已經處理咗，暫時就系噉先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 ji5 ging1 cyu2 lei5 zo2, zaam6 si4 zau6 hai6 gam2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事已经处理了，暂时就这样吧。
examples.english_sentence: This matter has been handled; let's leave it at that for now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再鬧佢，係噉先好過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 nau6 keoi5, hai6 gam2 sin1 hou2 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再责备他了，暂时就这样比较好。
examples.english_sentence: Don't scold him any more — it's better to leave it like this for now.

mandarin_meaning: 就是這個意思／就是那個意思
english_meaning: That's what it means; that's the point
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用法，表示「就是這個意思」或用來總結或說明別人的意思或意圖。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to indicate "that's what it means" or to summarize/clarify someone's point or intention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔係我唔幫佢，係噉意我真係幫唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hai6 ngo5 m4 bong1 keoi5, hai6 gam2 ji3 ngo5 zan1 hai6 bong1 m4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不是我不幫他，是這個意思我真的幫不了。
examples.english_sentence: It's not that I won't help him — that's what I mean, I really can't help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你以為佢唔開心？唔係，係噉意佢太忙冇時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji5 wai6 keoi5 m4 hoi1 sam1? m4 hai6, hai6 gam2 ji3 keoi5 taai3 mong4 mou5 si4 gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你以為他不開心？不是，是這個意思他太忙沒時間。
examples.english_sentence: You think he's unhappy? No — it means he's too busy and has no time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘅唔係責怪你，係噉意提醒你小心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 ge3 m4 hai6 zaak3 gwaai3 nei5, hai6 gam2 ji3 tai4 jing4 nei5 siu2 sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說的不是責怪你，是這個意思提醒你小心一點。
examples.english_sentence: What he said wasn't to blame you; it meant to warn you to be more careful.

mandarin_meaning: 你這麼說／好吧（表示讓步或保留）
english_meaning: “If you say so” / “That's what you say” (used to concede or show mild skepticism)
explanation_mandarin: 口語化的廣東話表達，常用來表示讓步、勉強同意或對對方說法抱有保留或懷疑的語氣。相當於普通話的「你這麼說」或「好吧（如果你堅持）」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to concede or express mild skepticism/reservation about what someone has said. Similar to English "if you say so" or "that's what you say."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話自己冇偷嘢，係噉话？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 mou5 tau1 je5, hai6 gam2 waa6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說自己沒偷東西？（你這麼說）
examples.english_sentence: He says he didn't steal anything — if you say so?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 好啦，好啦，係噉话，我哋照你講做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hou2 laa1, hou2 laa1, hai6 gam2 waa6, ngo5 dei6 ziu3 nei5 gong2 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 好吧，好吧，那就這麼說，我們照你說的做。
examples.english_sentence: Alright, alright, if you say so — we'll do as you say.

mandarin_meaning: 耍威风；摆架子；装腔作势
english_meaning: to show off; to act big; to put on airs; to swagger
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语表达，指故意摆出气势或姿态以显示自己了不起、威风或高人一等的样子。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to put on airs or show off—deliberately act as if impressive or superior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日系威系势，好似自己好叻咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai6 wai1 hai6 sai3, hou2 ci5 zi6 gei2 hou2 lak1 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是摆架子，好像自己很了不起。
examples.english_sentence: He's always showing off, as if he's really impressive.

mandarin_meaning: 還是要 / 仍然要 / 即使如此也要
english_meaning: still have to; even so must
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用來表示即使存在某種情況或困難，說話者仍然認為有必要去做某事。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to indicate that, despite circumstances or difficulties, one still must or will do something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我知風好大，係都要出門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi1 fung1 hou2 daai6, hai6 dou1 jiu3 ceot1 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我知道風很大，但還是要出門。
examples.english_sentence: I know the wind is strong, but I still have to go out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔舒服，係都要去面試。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 syu1 fuk6, hai6 dou1 jiu3 heoi3 min6 si3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不舒服，但還是要去面試。
examples.english_sentence: He's not feeling well, but he still has to go to the interview.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 就算冇錢，係都要買張飛去睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zau6 syun3 mou5 cin2, hai6 dou1 jiu3 maai5 zoeng1 fei1 heoi3 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 就算沒錢，還是要買張票去看。
examples.english_sentence: Even if there's no money, I still want to buy a ticket to go see it.

mandarin_meaning: 考验（某人的技術、知識或反應）；考考、刁難
english_meaning: to test or quiz someone's skill, knowledge, or composure; to put someone on the spot
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語，指透過問問題或設難題來檢驗或挑戰某人的能力、反應或專業，常帶有刁難或考考的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression meaning to test or quiz someone's ability, knowledge, or reactions—often by asking tricky questions or putting them on the spot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新員工做錯嘢，老細就考師傅，問佢啲細節。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 jyun4 gung1 zou6 co3 je5, lou5 sai3 zau6 haau2 si1 fu6, man6 keoi5 di1 sai3 zit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新員工做錯事，老板就考验他，问他一些细节。
examples.english_sentence: The new employee made a mistake, and the boss tested him by asking about the details.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想畀人考師傅，答唔到就丟臉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 haau2 si1 fu6, daap3 m4 dou2 zau6 diu1 lim5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想被人考验，答不上来就丢脸。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to be put on the spot; if I can't answer I'll be embarrassed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日考師傅我，成日問啲好難嘅問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 haau2 si1 fu6 ngo5, sing4 jat6 man6 di1 hou2 naan4 ge3 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是考验我，总是问一些很难的问题。
examples.english_sentence: He constantly quizzes me, always asking difficult questions.

cantonese: 耕田唔養牛，自己攞難受
jyutping: gang1 tin4 m4 joeng5 ngau4, zi6 gei2 lo2 naan4 sau6
mandarin_meaning: 自作自受 / 自食其果
english_meaning: To suffer the consequences of one's own actions; to bring trouble on oneself.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面意思是耕田卻不養牛，結果自己受苦。比喻自己做了不當或自私的事，最後由自己承擔後果。相當於「自作自受」或「自食其果」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb-like saying: literally 'plough the field but don't keep the ox, you suffer yourself.' It means someone brings trouble on themselves and must bear the consequences of their own actions—similar to 'you reap what you sow' or 'self-inflicted suffering.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你明知唔應該咁做，依家埋怨無用——耕田唔養牛，自己攞難受。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ming4 zi1 m4 jing1 goi1 gam2 zou6, ji1 gaa1 maai4 jyun6 mou4 jung6 — gang1 tin4 m4 joeng5 ngau4, zi6 gei2 lo2 naan4 sau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你明知道不应该这样做，现在埋怨也没用——自作自受。
examples.english_sentence: You knew you shouldn't have done that; complaining now won't help — you're suffering the consequences yourself.

cantonese: 耕田唔养猪，犹如秀才唔读书
jyutping: gang1 tin4 m4 joeng5 zyu1, jau4 jyu4 sau3 coi4 m4 duk6 syu1
mandarin_meaning: 耕田不养猪，就像秀才不读书；比喻做事缺少必需的配套或忽略重要的補充工作，事情不完整。
english_meaning: Farming without raising pigs is like a scholar not reading; a proverb meaning to neglect an essential complementary task or miss a crucial part, resulting in something incomplete or pointless.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容做事缺乏配套、忽略關鍵步驟或只做部分而不完整，常用以批評做法不周全或本末倒置。
explanation_english: Used to describe doing things without the necessary complementary actions, neglecting crucial steps, or only doing part of something so that the result is incomplete; often used to criticize poor or misplaced priorities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 淨係讀書唔做實習，真係耕田唔養豬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing6 hai6 duk6 syu1 m4 zou6 sat6 zaap6, zan1 hai6 gang1 tin4 m4 joeng5 zyu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 只读书不做实习，真是耕田不养猪。
examples.english_sentence: Only studying without doing internships is really like farming without raising pigs.

mandarin_meaning: 面帶苦相且語氣不悅、常抱怨或顯得悶悶不樂的樣子
english_meaning: to look and sound bitter or sullen; appearing miserable or constantly complaining
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語短語，用來形容一個人的面容和說話語氣都很苦悶或不高興，常帶有抱怨或不滿的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase describing someone whose face and tone are bitter or sullen — often appearing unhappy or frequently complaining.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近成日苦口苦面，成日埋怨公司。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 seng4 jat6 fu2 hau2 fu2 min6, seng4 jat6 maai4 jyun6 gung1 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近常常面帶苦相，經常抱怨公司。
examples.english_sentence: He's been looking miserable and constantly complaining about the company recently.

mandarin_meaning: （一副）苦瓜脸 / 一副愁眉苦脸的表情
english_meaning: to have a sullen/sour/glum expression; a long face
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，比喻臉色像苦瓜一樣，看起來不高興、愁容或悶悶不樂，常用於形容人面部表情不悅或鬱悶。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial simile literally meaning "face like a bitter gourd." It describes someone who looks unhappy, sullen, or glum.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你點解成日苦瓜噉嘅面？發生咩事呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dim2 gaai2 sing4 jat6 fu2 gwaa1 gam2 ge3 min6? faat3 sang1 me1 si6 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你怎么总是一副苦瓜脸？发生什么事了？
examples.english_sentence: Why do you always have that glum look? What's wrong?

jyutping: fu2 gwaa1 lou1 ngau4 juk6, jyut6 lou1 jyut6 suk1
mandarin_meaning: 越帮越忙 / 越弄越糟（比喻越去干预或处理，结果越糟糕或越得不到）
english_meaning: The more you meddle/try to help, the worse it gets (the more you try to grab, the less you get).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口语俗语 / 谚语（短语）
explanation_mandarin: 港式俗语，字面意象是捞苦瓜和牛肉时越捞越缩，实际用来形容越去插手或越去抢，结果越糟或越得不到想要的东西。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong colloquial saying. Literally 'scooping bitter gourd and beef — the more you scoop the more it shrinks.' Figuratively it means that the more you meddle or try to grab something, the worse the outcome or the less you obtain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日插手，真係苦瓜捞牛肉，越捞越缩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 caap3 sau2, zan1 hai6 fu2 gwaa1 lou1 ngau4 juk6, jyut6 lou1 jyut6 suk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要总是插手，真是越帮越忙，越弄越糟。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep interfering — it's really a case of the more you meddle, the worse it gets.

jyutping: fu2 gwaa1 man1 aap3, fu2 gwo3 dai6 dai2
mandarin_meaning: 比别人更惨、非常辛苦（字面：苦瓜炖鸭，比弟弟还苦）
english_meaning: To be extremely miserable or unlucky; worse off than others (literally: 'bitter melon stewed with duck, bitterer than the younger brother')
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口语俗语 / 形容词性短语
explanation_mandarin: 这是粤语的俗语或俚语，用来夸张或幽默地形容某人生活、处境或遭遇非常辛苦、惨（比别人更糟）。字面意思并不需逐字理解，重在表达“比别人更苦、更倒霉”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying used jokingly or emphatically to describe someone's life or situation as extremely bitter/miserable. The literal image ('bitter melon stewed with duck, bitterer than the younger brother') is figurative—meaning 'worse off than others' or 'suffering a lot.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢依家嗰份工做得好慘，真係苦瓜炆鸭，苦过弟弟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji1 gaa1 go2 fan6 gung1 zou6 dak1 hou2 caam2, zan1 hai6 fu2 gwaa1 man1 aap3, fu2 gwo3 dai6 dai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在那份工作过得很惨，真是苦瓜炖鸭，苦过弟弟。
examples.english_sentence: He's really having a rough time at his job — it's like 'bitter melon stewed with duck,' he's worse off than his younger brother.

mandarin_meaning: 微不足道的人或事物；無足輕重的人/物
english_meaning: insignificant people or things; nobody/nothing (derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語/俚語，用來形容無足輕重或微不足道的人或事物，常帶貶義，用於輕視或貶低對象。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to describe people or things that are insignificant or trivial. Often derogatory and used to belittle the referent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好理啲虾人虾物講嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lei5 di1 haa1 jan4 haa1 mat6 gong2 ge3 je5
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別理那些微不足道的人說的話。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pay attention to what those insignificant people say.

cantonese: ‌虾冇乸，蛤冇公，塘虱唔会出涌
jyutping: haa1 mou5 naa5, gaap3 mou5 gung1, tong4 sat1 m4 wui5 ceot1 jung2
mandarin_meaning: 虾没有母的，蛤没有公的，塘虱不会上浮 —— 用来形容某事不可能或荒谬
english_meaning: Literally: 'Shrimp have no female, clams have no male, catfish won't surface' — an idiom used to say something is impossible or absurd
explanation_mandarin: 这是一句粤语俗语，用夸张的动植物性别或行为不可能的例子来表示某件事绝对不可能或荒谬，常用于否定或打趣地驳回他人的说法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial proverb that lists impossible biological facts (shrimp having no females, clams having no males, catfish not surfacing) to emphasize that something is impossible or ridiculous. Used to dismiss or poke fun at a claim.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話佢會返嚟？虾冇乸，蛤冇公，塘虱唔会出涌啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 keoi5 wui5 faan1 lai4? haa1 mou5 naa5, gaap3 mou5 gung1, tong4 sat1 m4 wui5 ceot1 jung2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说他会回来？不可能，虾没有母的，蛤没有公的，塘虱不会冒出来啦。
examples.english_sentence: You say he'll come back? No way — that's impossible.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）虾到上面；（引申）出现意外的额外收获或惊喜
english_meaning: Literal: shrimp on top. Colloquial: an unexpected extra or pleasant surprise/bonus.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚语 / 口语短语（可作感叹或动词短语）
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语表达，字面指食物上面有虾，常用来形容某事物或情況多出意外的好處或驚喜，也可幽默比喻意外收获。用法随意口語化，較常見於香港本地語境。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression. Literally ‘shrimp on top’—used to describe an unexpected extra or pleasant surprise (e.g., an extra topping on a dish or an unexpected bonus). Informal and commonly used in Hong Kong contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我叫嘅燒味飯竟然虾到上面，真係有驚喜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 giu3 ge3 siu1 mei6 faan6 ging2 jin4 haa1 dou3 soeng6 min6, zan1 hai6 jau5 ging1 hei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我点的烧味饭上面竟然有虾，真是个惊喜。
examples.english_sentence: The roast-meat rice I ordered actually has shrimp on top — what a pleasant surprise.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次合約多咗獎金，真係虾到上面，冇諗過會咁好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 hap6 joek3 do1 zo2 zoeng2 gam1, zan1 hai6 haa1 dou3 soeng6 min6, mou5 lam2 gwo3 wui5 gam2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次合同多了奖金，真是意外之喜，没想到会这么好。
examples.english_sentence: The contract came with extra bonus this time — an unexpected bonus; I didn't expect it to be so good.

mandarin_meaning: 进进出出；频繁出入（某处）
english_meaning: to come and go frequently; to go in and out repeatedly; to frequent a place
explanation_mandarin: 表示经常出入某个地点，来来往往或频繁进出某处，可用于描述人常去某个场所或自由出入的状态。
explanation_english: Indicates frequent coming and going to/from a place; used to describe someone who repeatedly goes in and out of a location or frequents a place.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺間酒吧行出行入，大家都習慣見到佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaan1 zau2 baa1 haang4 ceot1 haang4 jap6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 zaap6 gun3 gin3 dou2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常在那间酒吧进进出出，大家都习惯看到他。
examples.english_sentence: He comes and goes at that bar all the time; everyone is used to seeing him.

mandarin_meaning: 犯錯、走錯路；誤入歧途
english_meaning: to make a mistake; to go astray; to do the wrong thing
explanation_mandarin: 表示做錯事或判斷失誤、誤入歧途。常用來形容行為或決定上出了差錯或走錯路。
explanation_english: An idiomatic Cantonese expression meaning to make a mistake, go astray, or take a wrong course of action. Often used to describe errors in behaviour or judgement.
