examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰陣時我真係行差踏錯，害到屋企人擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zan6 si4 ngo5 zan1 hai6 haang4 caa1 daap6 co3, hoi6 dou3 uk1 kei5 jan4 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那時我真的犯了錯，害得家人擔心。
examples.english_sentence: Back then I really made a mistake and caused my family to worry.

mandarin_meaning: 讓開／走開（口語）
english_meaning: move aside; get out of the way
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用於催促或命令別人移開位置、讓出通道。語氣通常較急促，視語境可顯得粗魯或不客氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to urge someone to move aside or get out of the way. It is typically imperative and can sound abrupt or rude depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好企喺門口，行開行埋畀人過路啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 kei5 hai2 mun4 hau2, haang4 hoi1 haang4 maai4 bei2 jan4 gwo3 lou6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別站在門口，讓開讓人通過。
examples.english_sentence: Don't stand in the doorway; move aside so people can pass.

mandarin_meaning: （1）相處得來；（2）可行、行得通
english_meaning: (1) to get along (with someone); (2) to be feasible/workable
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語短語。一方面用來表示兩人或多人人際上是否能和睦相處（「相處得來」）；另一方面也可用來詢問或判斷某事是否可行、能否實現（「可行/行得通」）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase. It can mean (1) whether people get along with each other (i.e., are compatible), or (2) whether something is doable/feasible (i.e., will/work or not).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋兩個唔係好行得埋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 loeng5 go3 m4 hai6 hou2 heng4-dak1-maai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們兩個不太合得來。
examples.english_sentence: The two of us don't really get along.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 咁樣做行得埋嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam2-joeng6-zou6 heng4-dak1-maai4-maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這樣做可行嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Is doing it this way feasible?

jyutping: haang4 dak1 faai3, hou2 sai3 gaai3
mandarin_meaning: 行动要快，世界（/事情）才会更顺利
english_meaning: Move quickly and things will go well; act fast to seize opportunities
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面是「走得快，好世界」。常用來勸人或自勵做事要快、主動，才能把握機會或令事情順利。有時語氣務實、帶有世故意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying literally 'walk fast, good world.' It advises being quick and proactive so you can seize opportunities or make things run smoothly. Used as advice or self-encouragement, often with a pragmatic tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家市場咁快變，做生意要行得快，好世界先有機會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 si5 coeng4 gam2 faai3 bin3, zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 haang4 dak1 faai3, hou2 sai3 gaai3 sin1 jau5 gei1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在市場變化很快，做生意要行動快，才有機會。
examples.english_sentence: The market changes so fast now; in business you have to move quickly to have opportunities.

cantonese: 行得正，企得正，唔怕雷公在头顶
jyutping: hang4 dak1 zeng3, kei5 dak1 zeng3, m4 paa3 leoi4 gung1 zoi6 tau4 deng2
mandarin_meaning: 只要行得正、站得正、问心无愧，就不怕被人指控或遭报复。
english_meaning: If you behave uprightly and with a clear conscience, you have nothing to fear from accusations or punishment.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來表達只要做事光明正大、不虧心，就不必擔心別人會找麻煩或誣衊你。
explanation_english: This saying expresses that if one acts honestly and uprightly, one need not fear accusations or retaliation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你放心啦，佢行得正，企得正，唔怕雷公在头顶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 fong3 sam1 laa1, keoi5 hang4 dak1 zeng3, kei5 dak1 zeng3, m4 paa3 leoi4 gung1 zoi6 tau4 deng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你放心，他行得正、站得正，不怕有人來找麻煩。
examples.english_sentence: Don't worry; he's upright and honest — if you're innocent you have nothing to fear.

jyutping: haang4 bou6 lou6 dou1 daa2 dou3 teoi3
mandarin_meaning: （口語）連走路都會被打倒／連走路都會摔倒（形容人非常不穩、虛弱或醉得走不了路）
english_meaning: (colloquial) so unsteady/weak/drunk that you could be knocked over even while walking; barely able to keep on your feet
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語／俚語（描述狀態的短語）
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人狀態非常不穩、虛弱或醉酒，連走路這麼簡單的動作都可能被擊倒或摔倒。常用於口語和俚語場合。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who is extremely unsteady, weak, or drunk — to the extent that even walking could knock them over or make them fall. This is an informal, colloquial expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢醉到行步路都打倒褪，行得好唔穩，要人扶返佢先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 dou3 haang4 bou6 lou6 dou1 daa2 dou3 teoi3, haang4 dak1 hou2 m4 wan2, jiu3 jan4 fu1 faan1 keoi5 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他醉到連走路都會摔倒，走得很不穩，需要人扶著才行。
examples.english_sentence: He's so drunk he could be knocked over just walking; he can barely walk steadily and needs someone to support him.

jyutping: hang4 syun4 zau2 maa5 saam1 fan1 him2
mandarin_meaning: 行船走馬有三分險／凡事都有風險，做事要有心理準備並小心行事。
english_meaning: There is always some risk involved; things are inherently risky, so be prepared and cautious.
explanation_mandarin: 字面指行船與走馬時本有危險，現用作比喻凡事難免有風險，提醒人們要有心理準備並且謹慎行事。
explanation_english: Literally refers to the dangers of sailing and riding horses; metaphorically it means that everything carries some risk and one should be mentally prepared and act with caution.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意要有心理準備，行船走馬三分險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 jau5 sam1 lei5 zeon2 bei6, hang4 syun4 zau2 maa5 saam1 fan1 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意要有心理準備，行船走馬三分險。
examples.english_sentence: When doing business you should be mentally prepared — there's always some risk.

mandarin_meaning: 去花街；去紅燈區／去嫖妓
english_meaning: to go to the red-light district; to solicit prostitutes
explanation_mandarin: 「行花街」是粤语俗语，指到花街或紅燈區尋找性服務或嫖妓，有時作為委婉語使用。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang meaning to go to the red-light district or to solicit prostitutes; often used as a euphemism for visiting places that offer sexual services.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話今晚唔返屋企，要出去行花街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 gam1 maan5 m4 faan1 uk1 kei5, jiu3 ceot1 heoi3 hang4 faa1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说今晚不回家，要出去去花街（去嫖妓）。
examples.english_sentence: He said he won't come home tonight; he's going out to the red‑light district / to pick up prostitutes.

mandarin_meaning: 走走停停；徘徊、逗留
english_meaning: to walk around and stop repeatedly; to loiter or pace; to linger/hesitate
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，指在某處來回走動並不時停下，含有徘徊、猶豫或逗留的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to walk around and stop repeatedly—implying loitering, pacing, lingering, or hesitating.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街度行行企企，好似等緊人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gaai1 dou6 haang4 haang4 kei5 kei5, hou2 ci5 dang2 gan2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在街上走走停停，像是在等人。
examples.english_sentence: He's walking around and stopping on the street, as if waiting for someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友喺商場入面行行企企，父母要睇住佢哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 hai2 soeng1 coeng4 jap6 min6 haang4 haang4 kei5 kei5, fu6 mou5 jiu3 tai2 zyu6 keoi5 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友在商场里走走停停，父母要看着他们。
examples.english_sentence: Children are wandering about in the mall; parents need to keep an eye on them.

mandarin_meaning: 走霉运；倒霉
english_meaning: to have bad luck; to be unlucky; to experience a streak of misfortune
explanation_mandarin: 表示某人近期運氣不好，接二連三遇到不順利或麻煩的事。
explanation_english: Indicates that someone is having bad luck recently, repeatedly encountering misfortunes or troubles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近我好似行衰運，成日遇到啲麻煩嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 ngo5 hou2 ci5 hang4 seoi1 wan6, sing4 jat6 jyu6 dou3 di1 maa4 faan4 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近我好像走霉运，总是遇到麻烦事。
examples.english_sentence: Lately I seem to be having bad luck; I'm always running into trouble.

mandarin_meaning: 走路不看路；（骂人）你走路没长眼睛吗？
english_meaning: Can't you watch where you're going? (colloquial reproach for someone not paying attention while walking)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的口語說法，用來責備或抱怨別人走路不注意、擋路或撞到人，相當於「你走路不看路嗎？」
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to scold or complain when someone doesn't watch where they're going, bumps into others, or blocks the way — equivalent to "Can't you watch where you're going?"

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你行路唔帶眼呀？撞到我都唔講一聲！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 haang4 lou6 m4 daai3 ngaan5 aa3? zong6 dou3 ngo5 dou1 m4 gong2 jat1 seng1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你走路不看路吗？撞到我都不说一句话！
examples.english_sentence: Can't you watch where you're going? You bumped into me and didn't even say anything!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日行路唔帶眼，撞親人都唔理，真煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 haang4 lou6 m4 daai3 ngaan5, zong6 can1 jan4 dou1 m4 lei5, zan1 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是走路不看路，撞到人都不理，真烦人。
examples.english_sentence: He always doesn't watch where he's going; he bumps into people and doesn't care — really annoying.

jyutping: hang4 wan6 ji1 saang1 ji1 beng6 mei5
mandarin_meaning: 走運的“醫生”來收尾（指在事情快完成時才出現幫忙或搶功的情況）
english_meaning: A 'lucky doctor' who shows up only to finish/clean up at the end (i.e., someone who arrives at the last minute to help or to take credit)
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，用來形容某人只在事情快完成時才出現幫忙或收尾，往往帶有嘲諷或不滿，暗示對方捲土重來、趁勢搶功或僅靠走運才解決尾聲問題。
explanation_english: A colloquial slang phrase describing someone who only appears when a job is almost done to help finish it or to take credit. Often used sarcastically to imply opportunism or last-minute luck in resolving the final issues.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋個項目差唔多做好晒，佢而家先嚟幫手收尾，真係行运医生医病尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 go3 hong6 muk6 caa1 m4 do1 zou6 hou2 saai3, keoi5 ji4 gaa1 sin1 lai4 bong1 sau2 sau1 mei5, zan1 hai6 hang4 wan6 ji1 saang1 ji1 beng6 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們的項目差不多已經做好了，他現在才來幫忙收尾，真是走運的「醫生」來醫病尾。
examples.english_sentence: Our project was almost finished; he only came now to help wrap things up — what a 'lucky doctor' showing up to finish things and take credit at the end.

jyutping: haang4 wan6 haang4 dou3 goek3 zi2 (屘：罕用字，讀音不確定；疑為「麻」maa4)
mandarin_meaning: （疑為錯寫）走到腳趾麻/走到腳痺 — 形容走路或站立太久導致腳趾麻木或酸痛
english_meaning: Likely a nonstandard/misspelt phrase meaning 'walk until your toes are numb' — used to describe having walked or stood so long that your toes feel numb or sore.
explanation_mandarin: 此詞中的最後一字「屘」為罕用或誤寫字，並不常見。根據語境，較自然的說法應為「行到腳趾麻」或「行到腳痺」，用來形容走路或站立很久，腳趾或腳有麻木、酸痛的感覺。此表達多用於口語、廣東話地區（如香港）。
explanation_english: The final character 「屘」 is rare or likely a misspelling. Context suggests the intended phrase is probably "行到腳趾麻" (haang4 dou3 goek3 zi2 maa4) meaning "walk until your toes go numb." This is a colloquial Cantonese expression used to say one has walked or stood so long that their toes feel numb or sore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日行咗成日，行到脚趾麻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 haang4 zo2 sing4 jat6, haang4 dou3 goek3 zi2 maa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天走了一整天，走得腳趾都麻了。
examples.english_sentence: I walked all day today — my toes have gone numb.

mandarin_meaning: 街知巷闻（成语），意思是到处都知道，广为流传
english_meaning: widely known; known all over town; talked about everywhere
explanation_mandarin: 表示某件事或某人广为传播、人人皆知，几乎在街巷里都能听到别人谈论。
explanation_english: Indicates that something or someone is widely known and commonly talked about throughout the area; known by everyone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事已經街知巷聞，冇需要再解釋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 ji5 ging1 gaai1 zi1 hong6 man4, mou5 seoi1 jiu3 zoi3 gaai2 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事已经街知巷闻，不需要再解释。
examples.english_sentence: This matter is already widely known; there's no need to explain further.

mandarin_meaning: 袋袋平安（賀年祝福語，意指平安、也含有招財的雙關）
english_meaning: A New Year greeting wishing safety and peace (often a pun implying good fortune/prosperity)
explanation_mandarin: 「袋袋平安」是粵語常見的賀年祝福語，字面上可解作「每個袋子都平安」。常見於利是封、賀卡或贈禮上，既祝福平安也有諧音或雙關意味（暗指財袋、招財）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese festive greeting literally meaning “bags (or every bag) be safe.” Frequently used on red packets, cards, and gifts during Chinese New Year to wish safety and well-being; it often carries a playful pun suggesting prosperity (money bags).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年快樂，祝你袋袋平安！
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 faai3 lok6, zuk1 nei5 doi6 doi6 ping4 on1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新年快乐，祝你袋袋平安！
examples.english_sentence: Happy New Year! Wishing you safety and peace (and lots of prosperity)!

mandarin_meaning: 旁觀者；袖手旁觀、不介入提供幫助的人
english_meaning: bystander; someone who stands by and does not intervene or help
explanation_mandarin: 俗語/俚語，通常帶有貶義，指那些只在一旁觀看而不出手幫忙或干預的人。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang term, usually pejorative, referring to people who merely watch from the sidelines and do not step in to help or intervene.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲人淨係做觀音兵，唔會幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 jan4 zing6 hai6 zou6 gwaan1 jam1 bing1, m4 wui5 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些人只是做旁觀者，不會幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: Some people just act as bystanders and won't help.

jyutping: gwaan1 jam1 co5 giu2, kaau3 jan4 toi4 geoi2
mandarin_meaning: 依靠別人抬舉、仰仗他人來抬高自己（含貶義）
english_meaning: To rely on others to elevate or praise you; to depend on someone's support to gain status (pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 字面上是觀音坐在轎子裡，靠別人抬著。比喻不靠自己努力，而依賴別人的抬舉或捧場來獲得地位或好處，含有貶義。
explanation_english: Literally 'Guanyin sits in a sedan chair, relying on people to lift it.' Figuratively, it describes someone who depends on others' support or flattery to gain status or benefit, often with a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日想靠人抬舉，自己又唔肯努力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 soeng2 kaau3 jan4 toi4 geoi2, zi6 gei2 jau6 m4 hang2 nou5 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是想靠别人抬举，自己又不肯努力。
examples.english_sentence: He always wants to rely on others to praise him and won't work hard himself.

jyutping: gwaan1 jam1 pou4 saat3, nin4 nin4 sap6 baat3
mandarin_meaning: 愿观音菩萨保佑你年年都十八（永远年轻）
english_meaning: May Guanyin bless you to be eighteen every year (i.e. stay forever young)
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語或祝賀用語，借观音菩萨之名祈願對方年年十八，意指永葆青春。常在生日或讚美他人外表保養好時使用，語氣可真誠也可帶玩笑。
explanation_english: A colloquial blessing or saying that invokes Guanyin to wish someone 'eighteen every year,' meaning to remain forever young. Often used at birthdays or to compliment someone's youthful appearance; can be sincere or playful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 生日快樂！觀音菩薩，年年十八！
examples.jyutping_sentence: saang1 jat6 faai3 lok6! gwaan1 jam1 pou4 saat3, nin4 nin4 sap6 baat3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 生日快乐！愿你年年十八（永葆青春）！
examples.english_sentence: Happy birthday! May Guanyin bless you to be eighteen every year (i.e., stay forever young)!

mandarin_meaning: 愛睡的人／睡癡（俚語）
english_meaning: sleepyhead; someone who loves sleeping (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來戲稱特別愛睡覺或常常打瞌睡的人，帶有親暱或調侃的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to tease or affectionately call someone who loves sleeping or frequently dozes off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日咁鍾意訓覺，真係覺覺豬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 gam2 zung1 ji3 fan3 gok3, zan1 hai6 gok3gok3 zyu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是这么爱睡，真是个爱睡鬼。
examples.english_sentence: You always love sleeping — you're such a sleepyhead.

mandarin_meaning: 在我看來；依我看
english_meaning: in my opinion; if you ask me
explanation_mandarin: 用來表達說話者的個人看法或意見，相當於「在我看來」「依我看」。屬口語用法，常在廣東話日常對話中使用。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to introduce the speaker's personal opinion, equivalent to "in my opinion" or "if you ask me." Common in everyday Hong Kong Cantonese speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 計我話，今次唔好再幫佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gai3 ngo5 waa6, gam1 ci3 m4 hou2 zoi3 bong1 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在我看來，這次不要再幫他了。
examples.english_sentence: If you ask me, don't help him again this time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 計我話，你唔好再等佢，走啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gai3 ngo5 waa6, nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 dang2 keoi5, zau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 依我看，你不要再等他了，走吧。
examples.english_sentence: In my opinion, don't wait for him any longer — just go.

mandarin_meaning: 讀破字典／博覽群書（自稱或形容對很多知識、字詞很熟悉）
english_meaning: to claim or be regarded as having read widely/knowing every word; being very well-read (often used to describe someone who thinks they know everything)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，原意像「把字典讀破」，引申為自稱或被認為學識淵博、懂很多字詞，有時帶有誇耀或譏諷意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally meaning 'to have read the dictionary through'; it implies being very well-read or claiming to know a lot of words/knowledge. It can carry a boastful or slightly sarcastic tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日話自己讀破字膽，乜都識。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 waa6 zi6 gei2 duk6 po3 zi6 daam2, mat1 dou1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常說自己讀破字膽，什麼都懂。
examples.english_sentence: He always says he's read every word and knows everything.

mandarin_meaning: 外表像豆沙包般可愛、柔軟，但內心黑暗、狠毒或自私（俚語）
english_meaning: Looks sweet and harmless like a red‑bean bun (豆沙包) but is black‑hearted — malicious, hypocritical, or selfish (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人外表看起來甜美、無害，實際上心地陰險、刻薄或貪婪。常用於口語或評斷性描述中。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who appears sweet and harmless on the outside but is actually malicious, mean, or greedy. Commonly used in colloquial speech as a critical descriptor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢睇落好似豆沙包，但其實好黑心，成日呃人錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tai2 lok6 hou2 ci5 dau6 saa1 baau1, daan6 kei4 sat6 hou2 hak1 sam1, sing4 jat6 aak1 jan4 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看起來像個豆沙包，但其實很黑心，經常騙別人的錢。
examples.english_sentence: He looks like a sweet red‑bean bun, but he's actually black‑hearted and often cheats people out of their money.

mandarin_meaning: 赌场里没有父子（亲情），不讲人情，不会给予特殊照顾
english_meaning: In the casino there are no family ties — no favoritism or special treatment; the house shows no mercy
explanation_mandarin: 指在賭場或類似場合不會因為親屬、關係或人情而得到特殊優待或寬待，輸贏要自己承擔。
explanation_english: Says that in a gambling house (or similar settings) family ties and personal relationships don't matter — no special favors will be granted; losses must be borne by the individual.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好以為佢係你朋友，賭場無父子，輸咗唔會有人幫你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ji5 wai6 keoi5 hai6 nei5 pang4 jau5, dou2 coeng4 mou4 fu6 zi2, syu1 zo2 m4 wui5 jau5 jan4 bong1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別以為他是你朋友，賭場沒有父子，輸了不會有人幫你。
examples.english_sentence: Don't think he's your friend — the casino doesn't care about family ties; if you lose, nobody will help you.

cantonese: ‌趷起条尾就知到你屙屎定屙尿
jyutping: kot3 hei2 tiu4 mei5 zau6 zi1 dou3 nei5 o1 si2 ding6 o1 niu6
mandarin_meaning: 掀起你的（褲子/尾部）就知道你是在拉屎還是尿尿。
english_meaning: Lift up your tail (pants) and you'll know whether you're pooping or peeing. (Used metaphorically: a secret or true situation will be immediately exposed.)
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話俚語，字面意思是只要掀起對方的尾部就能分辨是在大便還是小便。引申義為某人的秘密、底細或真相一揭就明，常帶有嘲諷或侮辱語氣。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang phrase. Literally means that lifting someone's tail will reveal whether they are defecating or urinating. Figuratively it means a person's secret or true situation will be immediately exposed; often used mockingly or insultingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好呃我，趷起条尾就知到你屙屎定屙尿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ngaak1 ngo5, kot3 hei2 tiu4 mei5 zau6 zi1 dou3 nei5 o1 si2 ding6 o1 niu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別騙我，一掀開你的尾巴就知道你是在拉屎還是尿尿。
examples.english_sentence: Don't try to fool me — lift up your tail and we'll see whether you're pooping or peeing.

jyutping: dit3 dou2 zap1 dou3 go3 gat1
mandarin_meaning: 因祸得福；误打误撞捡到便宜
english_meaning: a blessing in disguise; to gain an unexpected small benefit from a mishap
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「跌倒卻撿到一個桔」，用來形容本來是不幸的事，結果反而獲得了好處或小利。
explanation_english: Literally 'fall down and pick up an orange.' Used to describe a situation where a misfortune unexpectedly brings a small benefit or good luck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢轉工唔成功，但最後簽咗更好嘅合約，真係跌倒執到個桔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zyun3 gung1 m4 sing4 gung1, daan6 zeoi3 hau6 cim1 zo2 gang1 hou2 ge3 hap6 joek3, zan1 hai6 dit3 dou2 zap1 dou3 go3 gat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他跳槽不成功，但最後簽了更好的合約，真是因禍得福。
examples.english_sentence: He failed to change jobs, but in the end signed a better contract — truly a blessing in disguise.

jyutping: dit3 dou2 laa1 faan1 zaak3 saa1
mandarin_meaning: 跌倒後拍拍身上的沙，繼續前進；比喻遭遇挫折後重新站起來繼續努力
english_meaning: to get up after a fall, brush the sand off and carry on; figuratively, to recover from a setback and continue trying
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東話的口語說法，字面意思是跌倒後把身上的沙揩掉再繼續走路，引申為遭遇挫折後不氣餒、重新振作繼續前進。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally meaning to fall, brush the sand off yourself, and keep going. It is used figuratively for recovering from a setback and continuing onward.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽失利唔代表完結，跌倒揦番拃沙，下一次再出戰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 sat1 lei6 m4 doi6 biu2 jyun4 git3, dit3 dou2 laa1 faan1 zaak3 saa1, haa6 jat1 ci3 zoi3 ceot1 zin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比賽失利不代表結束，跌倒後拍拍身上的沙，下一次再出戰。
examples.english_sentence: Losing the match doesn't mean it's over — get back up, brush yourself off, and fight again next time.

mandarin_meaning: 令人吃惊/出乎意料
english_meaning: to be astonished; to be taken aback; surprising
explanation_mandarin: 表示因为事情出乎意料而感到非常惊讶，通常为口语用法，字面意思是“眼镜掉了”，引申为大为惊讶。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression meaning to be greatly surprised or astonished by something unexpected; literally 'to drop one's glasses', implying disbelief or shock.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢突然辭職，真係跌眼鏡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dat6 jin4 ci4 zik1, zan1 hai6 dit3 ngaan5 geng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然辞职，真是令人吃惊。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly resigned — it was really surprising.

jyutping: geui3 dei6 wai3 zyu1 naa5, tai2 cin2 fan6 soeng6
mandarin_meaning: 為了錢而卑躬屈膝、討好別人
english_meaning: to humiliate oneself or act servile for money; to grovel or sell out for financial gain
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容為了錢而做出卑微或討好別人的行為，帶貶義。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression describing someone who debases themselves or panders to others for money; carries a derogatory sense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗錢，真係會跪地餵豬乸，睇錢份上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 cin2, zan1 hai6 wui5 geui3 dei6 wai3 zyu1 naa5, tai2 cin2 fan6 soeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了錢，真會卑躬屈膝，完全是看在錢的份上。
examples.english_sentence: For money, he'll really abase himself — it's all about the money.

mandarin_meaning: 跌跌撞撞、笨拙、手腳不靈活（口語）
english_meaning: to stumble or fumble about; to be clumsy and awkward (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 形容行動或做事笨拙、亂撞、手腳不靈活，常用於口語或方言表達。
explanation_english: Describes moving or acting clumsily and awkwardly, stumbling or fumbling about; a colloquial/idiomatic expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家踸蹄踸爪，連路都行唔穩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 seon3-tai4-seon3-zaau2, lin4 lou6 dou1 haang4 m4 wan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在跌跌撞撞，連路都走不穩。
examples.english_sentence: He's stumbling around and can't even walk steadily.

jyutping: gwo3 zo2 hoi2 zau6 hai6 san4 sin1
mandarin_meaning: 去了國外/別處就會過上很好的生活，好像成了神仙一樣
english_meaning: Once you go abroad (or leave), life will be much better — as if you become an immortal (used sarcastically or idealistically)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，通常用來形容有人認為離開本地（例如去外國）就能過上幸福無憂的生活，帶有理想化或誇張意味，有時含諷刺。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe the belief that leaving (e.g. going overseas) will lead to an ideal, carefree life — literally 'cross the sea and become an immortal.' It can be used earnestly or sarcastically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日話想过咗海就系神仙，唔想留喺香港做苦工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 waa6 soeng2 gwo3 zo2 hoi2 zau6 hai6 san4 sin1, m4 soeng2 lau4 hai2 hoeng1 gong2 zou6 fu2 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是說想出國，覺得過了海就像成了神仙，不想留在香港做苦工。
examples.english_sentence: He always says he wants to go abroad, thinking that once you cross the sea you'll be like an immortal — he doesn't want to stay in Hong Kong doing hard labor.

mandarin_meaning: 过河拆桥/过桥抽板：比喻利用别人之后忘恩负义，断绝来往。
english_meaning: To pull up the bridge after crossing — to take advantage of someone and then be ungrateful or sever ties; to betray someone's help.
explanation_mandarin: 形容在得到别人的帮助或好处之后，反过来断绝关系或忘记恩情，表现忘恩负义。
explanation_english: Describes the act of repaying kindness with ingratitude: after receiving help or benefit, one cuts ties or behaves ungratefully.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢幫完人之後就過橋抽板，真係好無情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bong1 jyun4 zi1 hau6 zau6 gwo3 kiu4 cau1 baan2, zan1 hai6 hou2 mou4 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他帮完人之后就过桥抽板，真是太没良心了。
examples.english_sentence: After he helped someone, he cut them off — really heartless.

mandarin_meaning: 过气的人；不再受欢迎或落伍的旧明星/人物
english_meaning: a has-been; someone who has fallen out of fashion or lost popularity
explanation_mandarin: 俚语，用来形容已过巅峰、名气或影响力下降、不再受欢迎的人，常用于艺人或公众人物，带贬义或戏谑意味。
explanation_english: Slang for a person who has passed their prime — no longer popular or influential. Often used for entertainers or public figures; usually derogatory or mocking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家已經係個過氣佬倌，冇人再約佢上節目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4gaa1 ji5ging1 hai6 go3 gwo3 hei3 lou2 gun1, mou5 jan4 zoi3 joek3 keoi5 soeng5 zit3 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在已经是个过气佬倌，没人再约他上节目。
examples.english_sentence: He's already a has-been; no one invites him onto shows anymore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好扮過氣佬倌喇，應該學啲新嘢去追上潮流。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 baan6 gwo3 hei3 lou2 gun1 laa3, jing1goi1 hok6 di1 san1 je5 heoi3 zeoi1 soeng5 ciu4lau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你别装作个过气佬倌了，应该学些新东西跟上潮流。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pretend to be a has-been; you should learn new things to keep up with the trends.

mandarin_meaning: 试水温；试探性参与，稍微涉入
english_meaning: to test the waters; to try something cautiously; to get slightly involved without fully committing
explanation_mandarin: 比喻性说法，字面意思是“过水会弄湿脚”，引申为先做试探性尝试或略微参与，不做彻底或正式的投入。
explanation_english: A metaphorical expression literally meaning 'cross the water and wet your feet'. It refers to testing the waters or becoming slightly involved to try something out without fully committing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係過水濕腳，未真正落場幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 gwo3 seoi2 sap1 goek3, mei6 zan1 zing3 lok6 coeng4 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只是试水，还没有真正下场帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: He's just testing the waters; he hasn't actually gone in to help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我只係過水濕腳，未正式做呢份工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi2 hai6 gwo3 seoi2 sap1 goek3, mei6 zing3 sik1 zou6 ni1 fan6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我只是试试水温，还没正式做这份工作。
examples.english_sentence: I'm just dipping my toes in; I'm not officially doing this job yet.

mandarin_meaning: 外來強者；突然出現並迅速佔據優勢的人或團體（常指從內地來港或外地來的強勁競爭者）
english_meaning: A newcomer or outsider who suddenly appears and quickly dominates; a dark horse or strong competitor from elsewhere (literally 'cross-river dragon').
explanation_mandarin: “过江龙”原指“过江而来的龙”，引申為來自外地且實力強勁、很快超越本地人的人或團體。在香港語境下有時特指來自內地的優秀人才或競爭者，語氣可中性或帶貶義，視語境而定。
explanation_english: Literally 'dragon that crossed the river.' Used figuratively for an outsider or newcomer who arrives from elsewhere and quickly shows superior ability or dominance. In Hong Kong contexts it can refer to strong competitors from the mainland; tone may be neutral or slightly pejorative depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今屆球賽出現咗幾個過江龍，佢哋打得好勁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 gaai3 kau4 coi3 ceot1 jin6 zo2 gei2 go3 gwo3 gong1 lung4, keoi5 dei6 daa2 dak1 hou2 ging6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 本届球赛出现了几个过江龙，他们打得很厉害。
examples.english_sentence: A few outsiders—literally 'cross-river dragons'—appeared in this tournament; they played extremely well.

mandarin_meaning: 把遇到的每個人都當成知己；對所有人過於親熱、隨便傾訴私事
english_meaning: to treat everyone one meets as a close friend/confidant; to be overly familiar and indiscreet with people
explanation_mandarin: 指對遇到的人都當作知己，容易向別人透露私人事情或過分親熱，帶有貶義，暗示缺乏分寸與保密性。
explanation_english: Refers to treating every person one meets as a close friend, readily revealing private matters or being overly familiar. It carries a negative sense, implying a lack of discretion and inability to keep confidences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好逢人知己，啲秘密成日都洩晒出去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 fung4 jan4 zi1 gei2, di1 bei3 mat6 seng4 jat6 dou1 sit3 saai3 ceot1 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對每個人都當成知己，秘密常常泄露出去。
examples.english_sentence: He treats everyone like a confidant; secrets often get leaked out.

cantonese: 闲时唔烧香，急时抱佛脚
jyutping: haan4 si4 m4 siu1 hoeng1, gap1 si4 pou5 fat6 goek3
mandarin_meaning: 平时不准备，到了紧要关头才匆忙应付或求助（平时不烧香，急时抱佛脚）
english_meaning: To neglect preparation until the last minute; to cram or seek help only when it's urgent.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻平常不做准备或不注意，等到遇到紧急情况时才仓促应付或请求帮忙。
explanation_english: A proverb describing someone who doesn't prepare in advance and only scrambles to fix things or ask for help when a crisis arrives.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好闲时唔烧香，急时抱佛脚，依家开始温书啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 haan4 si4 m4 siu1 hoeng1, gap1 si4 pou5 fat6 goek3, ji1 gaa1 hoi1 ci2 wan1 syu1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别平时不温习，到了紧急的时候才抱佛脚，现在开始复习吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't wait until the last minute to study; start reviewing now instead of cramming.

mandarin_meaning: 悠閒地；閒暇地；不忙碌地
english_meaning: leisurely; idly; in a relaxed/unhurried manner
explanation_mandarin: 表示處於悠閒、不忙碌或不緊張的狀態，屬口語用法，常用來形容人做事或待著的狀態。
explanation_english: Indicates a leisurely or idle state — not busy or hurried. It's a colloquial adverb used to describe how someone is doing something or spending time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢閒閒地坐喺度飲茶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haan4 haan4 dei6 co5 hai2 dou6 jam2 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他悠閒地坐在那裡喝茶。
examples.english_sentence: He sits there leisurely drinking tea.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日我閒閒地，冇嘢做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 ngo5 haan4 haan4 dei6, mou5 je5 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天我很閒，沒有事情做。
examples.english_sentence: I'm free today; nothing to do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢閒閒地唔返工，成日喺屋企瞓覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haan4 haan4 dei6 m4 faan1 gung1, sing4 jat6 hai2 uk1 kei5 fan3 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他閒閒地不去上班，整天在家睡覺。
examples.english_sentence: He's casually not going to work, staying home and sleeping all day.

mandarin_meaning: 有钱人不理会/摆出不在乎的态度
english_meaning: (slang) a rich person who ignores others; to act like a wealthy, indifferent person
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 动词短语 / 形容词短语（口语俚语）
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容有錢人或裝作有錢的人對別人的請求或困難不理會、不關心，帶有輕蔑或疏遠的含義，常見於口語。
explanation_english: Used to describe a wealthy person (or someone acting wealthy) who ignores or is indifferent to others' requests or problems. It carries a sense of aloofness or disdain and is common in colloquial Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰啲阔佬懒理我哋講嘅嘢，淨係顧住自己嘅利益。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 di1 fut3 lou2 laan5 lei5 ngo5 dei6 gong2 ge3 je5, zing6 hai6 gu3 zyu6 zi6 gei2 ge3 lei6 jik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些有錢人不理我们说的话，只顾自己的利益。
examples.english_sentence: Those rich people ignore what we say and only care about their own interests.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 自從有錢之後，佢成日阔佬懒理朋友，大家都覺得佢變咗一個人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zi6 cung4 jau5 cin2 zi1 hau6, keoi5 sing4 jat6 fut3 lou2 laan5 lei5 pang4 jau5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 gok3 dak1 keoi5 bin3 zo2 jat1 go3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 自从有钱之后，他常常摆出有錢人不理朋友的样子，大家都觉得他变了一个人。
examples.english_sentence: Since he got money, he's often acted like a rich guy who ignores his friends; everyone thinks he's changed.

mandarin_meaning: 夸口、吹牛、摆阔（夸张地说话或自夸）
english_meaning: to boast or brag; to show off (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，指大肆夸耀、吹嘘或摆阔，說話誇張、口氣大，常含貶義，用於非正式語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to boast, brag or show off. It describes speaking boastfully or exaggeratedly and is usually informal and mildly derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日阔口拿扒，講啲嘢都唔可信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 fut3 hau2 naa4 paa4, gong2 di1 je5 dou1 m4 ho2 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是夸口吹牛，說的話都不可信。
examples.english_sentence: He's always boasting; what he says can't be trusted.

jyutping: fong4 gwan1 zi2 bat1 fong4 siu2 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 字面意思是「防備君子而不防小人」，通常用來批評或提醒人不要只擔心表面上的有面子、體面的人（君子），而忽視那些表面不起眼但心術不正、會暗中作梗的小人。即提醒要小心小人。
english_meaning: Literally 'guard against gentlemen but not against petty people.' Used to criticize or warn against focusing only on obvious, respectable people while neglecting the petty, malicious people who cause trouble behind the scenes.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用來提醒或批評：不要只提防表面上的君子而忽略心機深、會暗中陷害人的小人，因為小人才更容易在背後搞事。
explanation_english: This proverb warns that one should not focus merely on guarding against obvious, respectable people ('gentlemen') while ignoring petty, vindictive people who act secretly. It emphasizes being cautious of small-minded people who can cause harm covertly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意要小心，唔好淨係防君子不防小人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 siu2 sam1, m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 fong4 gwan1 zi2 bat1 fong4 siu2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意要小心，別只防備表面上的君子而不防小人。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful in business; don't only guard against respectable people while neglecting petty, malicious ones.

mandarin_meaning: 死裡逃生（差點喪命但最後活下來）
english_meaning: to narrowly escape death; to have a close brush with death and survive
explanation_mandarin: 形容差一點就喪命，但最終倖存下來。常用來描述經歷重大危險或事故後活下來的情況。
explanation_english: Describes narrowly escaping death and surviving. Often used to describe surviving a serious danger or accident.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上星期阿明行山失足，差啲就險死還生，依家仲要係醫院休養。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 sing1 kei4 aa3 ming4 haang4 saan1 sat1 zuk1 caa1 di1 zau6 him2 sei2 waan4 saang1 ji1 gaa1 zung6 jiu3 hai6 ji1 jyun2 jau1 joeng5
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上星期阿明爬山時失足，差點就死裡逃生，現在還在醫院休養。
examples.english_sentence: Last week Ah Ming slipped while hiking and narrowly escaped death; he is still recuperating in the hospital.

mandarin_meaning: 比剃頭還危險；非常危險、差一點出事
english_meaning: extremely dangerous; narrowly escaping disaster
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容某件事或情況非常危險，差點發生意外或災禍。語感上表示情況驚險、險象頻生。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang/idiomatic expression meaning something is extremely dangerous or on the verge of disaster. It conveys a sense of narrow escape or high risk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啱啱嗰次旅行差啲遇到風暴，真係險過剃頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngaam1 ngaam1 go2 ci3 leoi5 hang4 caa1 di1 jyu6 dou3 fung1 bou6, zan1 hai6 him2 gwo3 tai3 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剛剛那次旅行差點遇到風暴，真的非常危險。
examples.english_sentence: On that trip we almost ran into a storm — it was really dangerous.

jyutping: gaak3 je6 jau4 zaa3 gwai2, mou5 lei4 fo2 hei3
mandarin_meaning: 字面：隔夜的油条，没有一点火气。引申：过了一夜后，怒气或冲动会消退；冷静下来再处理事情。
english_meaning: Literal: overnight fried dough (youtiao) has no heat. Figurative: after a night's sleep, anger or hot tempers cool down; sleep on it and you'll calm down.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俚語用「隔夜油炸鬼」作比喻，說明事情經過一夜後會冷卻，怒氣、衝動會減少，勸人不要一時衝動、應該隔夜再說或再決定。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquialism uses 'overnight youtiao' metaphorically to say that things cool off after a night; anger or impulsive feelings will fade. It advises not to act in the heat of the moment and to 'sleep on it.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好即刻決定，隔夜油炸鬼，冇厘火气，朝早先再講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zik1 hak1 kyut3 ding6, gaak3 je6 jau4 zaa3 gwai2, mou5 lei4 fo2 hei3, ziu1 zou2 sin1 zoi6 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要马上决定，隔夜的事冷靜一下，怒氣會消退，明早再說。
examples.english_sentence: Don't decide immediately — sleep on it; the anger will fade. Talk about it tomorrow morning.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：隔夜的素馨（花）。引申：比喻一時熱烈但很快冷卻、短暫的感情或熱度。
english_meaning: Literal: 'overnight jasmine'. Figurative: a short-lived affection or enthusiasm that fizzles out by the next day.
explanation_mandarin: “隔夜素馨”並非常見的正式成語，多用作口語或網路俚語。強調某種感情、熱度或興趣來得快去得也快，隔夜就消退了。
explanation_english: Not a standard formal idiom but used colloquially/slang-wise. It emphasizes a feeling or enthusiasm that rises quickly and fades by the next day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰段感情真係隔夜素馨，第二朝就無咗興趣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 dyun6 gam2 cing4 zan1 hai6 gaak3 je6 sou3 hing1, dai6 ji6 ziu1 zau6 mou5 zo2 hing3 ceoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那段感情真是隔夜的素馨，第二天早上就沒了興趣。
examples.english_sentence: That relationship was truly an 'overnight jasmine' — the interest was gone by the next morning.

jyutping: gaak3 je6 caa4, m4 dou2 m4 on1 lok6
mandarin_meaning: 隔夜的茶，不倒掉就不安心（字面上是劝人不要喝隔夜茶；引申为要放下旧事，否则心里不安）
english_meaning: Overnight tea — if you don't pour it out you won't be at ease (literally a warning not to drink overnight tea; figuratively to let go of old matters or grudges, or you'll feel unsettled)
explanation_mandarin: 这句粤语俗语字面意思是不要喝隔夜茶，要把隔夜的茶倒掉以免不舒服或不卫生；引申用法是劝人放下旧事、解决未完的事，否则心里难安。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying literally advises against drinking overnight tea and tells you to pour it out for health and comfort. Figuratively it urges people to let go of past matters or resolve unfinished business, otherwise they will feel uneasy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽見我留住啲茶杯，笑住講：「隔夜茶，唔倒唔安樂，倒咗啦。」
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 gin3 ngo5 lau4 zyu6 di1 caa4 bui1, siu3 zyu6 gong2: 'gaak3 je6 caa4, m4 dou2 m4 on1 lok6, dou2 zo2 laa3.'
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈看到我留着茶杯，笑着说：“隔夜茶，不倒掉就不安心，倒掉吧。”
examples.english_sentence: My mother saw me leaving the teacup and said with a smile, 'Overnight tea — if you don't pour it out you won't be at ease; throw it away.'

jyutping: gaak3 je6 fung1 lou4 dou1 ceoi1 dak1 zoek6
mandarin_meaning: （口語、俚語）能把已經冷掉或冷淡的事物重新點燃；能挽回冷卻的感情或扭轉冷場。
english_meaning: Figurative slang: able to revive something that has gone cold or dead; to rekindle interest/attract someone who has cooled off; to warm up a situation thought to be lost.
explanation_mandarin: 此短語字面為「連隔夜冷掉的爐都能吹著」，用來形容一個人或手段非常有功力，能夠把已經冷淡或無望的關係、氣氛或情況重新變熱或恢復。
explanation_english: Literally 'can even blow an overnight-cold stove alight'; used figuratively to describe someone or something that can revive a situation, rekindle interest or win back someone who had cooled off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁有魅力，連隔夜風爐都吹得着，啲舊愛都會搵返佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam3 jau5 mui6 lik6, lin4 gaak3 je6 fung1 lou4 dou1 ceoi1 dak1 zoek6, di1 gau6 oi3 dou1 wui5 wan2 faan1 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這麼有魅力，連冷掉的感情都能挽回，前任們都會來找他。
examples.english_sentence: He's so charismatic he can even rekindle relationships that went cold; his exes come back to him.

jyutping: gaak3 saan1 maai5 ngau4, hou2 cau2 zong6 coi2 sou3
mandarin_meaning: 字面上是「從山那邊買牛」，整句為粵語俗語，常用來形容盲目購買或下注但偶爾會意外中彩或有意外好運（即「碰運氣」）。此表達較口語、地域性強，部分用法或有變體。
english_meaning: Literally 'buying a cow from across the mountain' — a Cantonese colloquial saying describing buying or betting sight unseen; sometimes, despite being a blind gamble, one unexpectedly gets lucky.
explanation_mandarin: 「隔山买牛」比喻遠距離或看不清楚就貿然購買或決定；「好丑撞彩数」在此語境下表示雖然不太看好或條件差，但偶然撞中好運（中獎或遇上好事）。整句用作形容盲買碰運氣、偶有驚喜的情況。此俗語較為口語、地區性強，部分場合可能有不同寫法或變體。
explanation_english: The phrase 'gaak saan maai ngau' (buying a cow across the mountain) metaphorically refers to making a purchase or decision without seeing or inspecting — a blind gamble. The latter part implies that even something unattractive or unlikely can unexpectedly hit the jackpot. Overall it’s a colloquial Cantonese way to describe taking a blind chance and occasionally getting lucky. The expression is regional and informal; variants exist.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講起隔山買牛，好丑撞彩數，有時盲買都會嚟個驚喜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 hei2 gaak3 saan1 maai5 ngau4, hou2 cau2 zong6 coi2 sou3, jau5 si4 maan6 maai5 dou1 wui5 lai4 go3 ging1 hei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 說到「隔山买牛，好丑撞彩数」，有時盲目購買反而會有驚喜。
examples.english_sentence: Speaking of 'buying a cow from across the mountain' — sometimes blind purchases can turn up a pleasant surprise.

mandarin_meaning: （疑似）指隔年的月饼已经变质、干硬或不宜食用
english_meaning: Refers (apparently) to last year's mooncakes that have gone bad, dried out, or are otherwise inedible
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 短语 / 口語俚語（形容性短语）
explanation_mandarin: 此短語極為罕見或地方性用法，字面上指「隔年的月饼」，後半句（「膉／益晒」）可能用來形容月餅已經乾硬或變質。由於用字與寫法存在變體或不確定，粵語讀音與準確涵義在不同地區或語境可能有差異。
explanation_english: This phrase appears to be a rare or highly local expression. Literally it mentions "last year's mooncakes," with the latter part ("膉/益晒") apparently describing the mooncakes as dried out or spoiled. The exact characters, pronunciation and precise sense seem variable or uncertain across speakers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰盒係隔年月饼，膉（益）晒，唔好食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 hap6 hai6 gaak3 nin4 jyut6 beng2, [用法/讀音不詳] m4 hou2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那盒是隔年的月饼，膉（益）晒，别吃了。
examples.english_sentence: That box holds last year's mooncakes — they're dried out/spoiled; don't eat them.

mandarin_meaning: 指隔壁愛打聽、愛講閒話或多管閒事的鄰居（多為中老年婦女），相當於「愛管閒事的阿姨/大媽」。
english_meaning: An informal Cantonese term for a nosy neighbor (often an older woman) who gossips and meddles; a busybody next door.
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱，用來形容住在隔壁、喜歡窺探別人隱私、傳播閒話或多管閒事的人，語氣帶戲謔或輕微貶義，常用於香港口語。
explanation_english: A colloquial, slightly pejorative Cantonese phrase describing a nosy neighbor—typically an older woman—who peeks, gossips and meddles in others' affairs. Commonly used in Hong Kong vernacular.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隔篱二叔婆成日喺陽台望住人哋，見到啲嘢就去講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaak3 lei4 ji6 suk1 po4 sing4 jat6 hai2 joeng4 toi4 mong6 zyu6 jan4 dei6, gin3 dou2 di1 je5 zau6 heoi3 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 隔壁那個愛管閒事的阿姨經常在陽台偷看別人，看到什麼就去說。
examples.english_sentence: The nosy neighbor next door is always peeking from her balcony and gossiping whenever she sees something.

mandarin_meaning: 隔壁鄰居；附近的鄰人
english_meaning: neighbors; people living next door or nearby
explanation_mandarin: 表示住在隔壁或附近的人，常用於口語，強調鄰里關係或附近的人群。
explanation_english: Refers to people who live next door or nearby; commonly used in spoken Cantonese to emphasize neighborhood relations or nearby residents.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋成日同隔篱邻舍打招呼，關係幾好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sing4 jat6 tung4 gaak3 lei4 leon4 se3 daa2 ziu1 fu1, gwaan1 hai6 gei2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們經常和隔壁的鄰居打招呼，關係挺好。
examples.english_sentence: We often greet the neighbors next door; our relationship is quite good.

mandarin_meaning: 别人家的看起来总是更好（邻居的饭菜更香）
english_meaning: The neighbour's food (or others' things) always seems better — equivalent to 'the grass is greener on the other side'.
explanation_mandarin: 俗语，比喻总觉得别人拥有的比自己好，常用来劝人不要过分攀比或妒忌。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying meaning people tend to think others have it better; used to warn against envy or needless comparison.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日覺得人哋啲嘢好過你，隔篱饭香啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 gok3 dak1 jan4 dei6 di1 je5 hou2 gwo3 nei5, gaak3 lei4 faan6 hoeng1 ze3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別總覺得別人比你好，那只是隔壁的飯菜看起來更香罷了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always think others are better off — it's just that the neighbour's food smells better.

mandarin_meaning: 像靴子一樣大的腳（俚語），形容人笨拙、笨重或手腳不靈活
english_meaning: Literally 'boots-sized big feet' (slang) — describes someone clumsy, awkward, or heavy-footed
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容一個人動作笨拙、笨重或不靈活。字面上意指腳像靴子般大，帶有貶義或調侃意味，常用於日常口語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to describe someone who is clumsy, awkward, or heavy-footed. Literally refers to having feet as big as boots; often used teasingly or pejoratively in casual speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講真，佢靴咁大只脚，做嘢好笨，成日失手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 zan1, keoi5 hyut3 gam2 daai6 zek3 goek3, zou6 je5 hou2 ban6, sing4 jat6 sat1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 說實話，他很笨拙，做事總是出錯。
examples.english_sentence: To be honest, he's really clumsy and always makes mistakes.

jyutping: haai4 dai2 saa1, daan2 gon1 zeng6 zi3 on1 lok6
mandarin_meaning: 把鞋底的沙掸干净就能安心（比喻處理好小事或瑣碎問題就能心安、生活輕鬆）
english_meaning: Brush the sand off your shoes and you'll be at ease (figurative: deal with small annoyances or minor issues and you'll find peace/comfort)
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語字面意思是把鞋底的沙掸掉就能感到安樂，引申為先把生活中的小問題或瑣事處理乾淨，就能心安、生活輕鬆。
explanation_english: Literally ‘brush the sand off your shoes and you'll be comfortable.’ It figuratively advises handling small problems or trivial matters so you can be at peace and live more comfortably.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日為細碎嘅事煩惱，其實鞋底沙，扽干净至安樂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 wai6 sai3 seoi3 ge3 si6 faan4 nou5, kei4 sat6 haai4 dai2 saa1, daan2 gon1 zeng6 zi3 on1 lok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是為小事煩惱，其實把鞋底的沙掸乾淨就能心安。
examples.english_sentence: He always worries about small things; actually, brush the sand off your shoes and you'll be at ease.

jyutping: ding2 zyu6 sek6 mo4 zou6 hei3, hek3 lik6 bat1 tou2 hou2
mandarin_meaning: 做白工、徒劳无功；费力却得不到好处或认可
english_meaning: To make a lot of effort but gain no benefit or approval; a thankless or futile task
explanation_mandarin: 形容為某事付出很多努力，但結果沒有得到好處或別人的認同，白費力氣、徒勞無功。
explanation_english: Describes putting in strenuous effort or putting on a show that yields no reward or appreciation — a thankless, futile endeavor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再頂住石磨做戲，吃力不討好，反而攞嚟笑話自己。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 ding2 zyu6 sek6 mo4 zou6 hei3, hek3 lik6 bat1 tou2 hou2, faan2 ji4 lo2 lai4 siu3 waa6 zi6 gei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再做那種徒有其表的事，吃力不討好，反而讓自己被嘲笑。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep putting on a futile show; it's a thankless effort and will only make you a laughingstock.

mandarin_meaning: 受不了 / 忍受不了
english_meaning: cannot endure; can't stand; unable to cope
explanation_mandarin: 表示无法承受或忍受某事，常用于口语，形容被气到、难以应付或压力太大顶不住。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning one cannot endure or tolerate something; used to describe being unable to cope, annoyed, overwhelmed, or physically unable to take it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我真係頂唔順佢成日遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 seon6 keoi5 seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我真的受不了他總是遲到。
examples.english_sentence: I really can't stand him being late all the time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近工作太多，我頂唔順啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 gung1 zok3 taai3 do1, ngo5 ding2 m4 seon6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近工作太多，我受不了了。
examples.english_sentence: I've had so much work lately, I can't cope.

mandarin_meaning: 背心（無袖上衣、汗衫／背心）
english_meaning: singlet / tank top / sleeveless vest
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，指無袖的上衣或背心，常用於夏天或運動時作為內搭或單穿的衣服。在香港話語境中也可寫作「頂心衫／頂心杉」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term for a sleeveless top (singlet/tank top/vest). Commonly worn in summer or for sports, either as an undershirt or by itself. In Hong Kong usage it may appear as 頂心衫/頂心杉.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天我鍾意著頂心杉去行街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 ngo5 zung1 ji3 zoek3 ding2 sam1 saam1 heoi3 haang4 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天我喜歡穿背心去逛街。
examples.english_sentence: In summer I like to wear a singlet to go shopping.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做運動記得著頂心杉同短褲，會舒服啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 wan6 dung6 gei3 dak1 zoek3 ding2 sam1 saam1 tung4 dyun2 fu3, wui5 syu1 fuk6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做運動記得穿背心和短褲，會比較舒服。
examples.english_sentence: When exercising, remember to wear a singlet and shorts — it's more comfortable.

mandarin_meaning: 迎难而上；硬着头皮上，强行推进
english_meaning: to push forward despite obstacles; to confront a difficulty head-on; to forcefully press on
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指在遇到阻力或困難時不退縮，硬着頭皮向前衝或強行推進。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to not give up when facing resistance or difficulty, to tough it out and press forward or force one's way through.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果冇得退路，我哋只可以頂硬上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 mou5 dak1 teoi3 lou6, ngo5 dei6 zi2 ho2 ji5 ding2 ngaang6 soeng5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果没有退路，我们只能硬着头皮上。
examples.english_sentence: If there's no way to back out, we can only push forward.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話今次嘅項目好難，但我哋要頂硬上，唔好畏縮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 gam1 ci3 ge3 hong6 muk6 hou2 naan4, daan6 ngo5 dei6 jiu3 ding2 ngaang6 soeng5, m4 hou2 wai3 cuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说这次的项目很难，但我们要迎难而上，不要退缩。
examples.english_sentence: He said this project is difficult, but we must push on and not shrink back.

mandarin_meaning: 冷嘲熱諷／說風涼話，態度冷淡不熱心
english_meaning: sarcastic and cold; making snide remarks and showing an unsympathetic attitude
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容人說話冷淡、譏諷或不願幫忙，帶有輕視或挖苦意味。
explanation_english: Describes someone speaking in a cold, sarcastic, or flippant way—unsympathetic and often mocking rather than helpful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢成日都風涼水冷，根本唔想幫人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 seng4 jat6 dou1 fung1 loeng4 seoi2 laang5, gan1 bun2 m4 soeng2 bong1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話總是風涼水冷，根本不想幫人。
examples.english_sentence: He always speaks sarcastically and coldly; he basically doesn't want to help people.

jyutping: fung1 ceoi1 jyun4 seoi1, seoi1 tip3 dei6
mandarin_meaning: 倒霉透顶／非常倒霉（粤语俗语，利用“芫荽”与“衰”同音的双关）
english_meaning: extremely unlucky; down on one's luck (Cantonese colloquialism using a pun between '芫荽' and '衰')
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語／俚語（形容詞性短語）
explanation_mandarin: 這句是廣東話的俗語／俚語，字面意思是『風吹香菜，香菜（衰）貼在地上』，利用『芫荽』與『衰』（倒霉）同音，形容一個人非常倒霉、衰到極點，語氣常帶幽默或揶揄。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquialism that literally says 'the wind blows coriander, coriander (seoi = unlucky) lies flat on the ground.' It plays on the pun between '芫荽' (cilantro) and '衰' (seoi, unlucky) to describe someone who is extremely unlucky — often said with humorous or teasing tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打工輸晒錢又畀人炒，真係风吹芫荽，荽贴地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 gung1 syu1 saai3 cin2 jau6 bei2 jan4 caau2, zan1 hai6 fung1 ceoi1 jyun4 seoi1, seoi1 tip3 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他打工把錢都輸光了又被公司炒魷魚，真是倒霉透頂。
examples.english_sentence: He lost all his money working and then got fired — he's really down on his luck.

cantonese: 風吹雞蛋殼，財散人安樂
jyutping: fung1 ceoi1 gai1 daan6 hok3, coi4 saan3 jan4 on1 lok6
mandarin_meaning: 失去財物反而輕鬆無憂；錢財散去，人反而安逸、少了牽累。
english_meaning: When money is gone people may find peace; losing wealth can remove troubles and bring a simpler, less troubled life.
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語字面上說風把雞蛋殼吹散，錢散了人就安樂。意思是有時擁有財物會帶來麻煩與牽累，反而失去財物後可以過得輕鬆自在。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb literally says the wind blows away egg shells and when money scatters people are at ease. It means that wealth can bring troubles and burdens, and losing it can sometimes free people to live more peacefully.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢仲話如果蝕晒啲錢都唔緊要，風吹雞蛋殼，財散人安樂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zung6 waa6 jyu4 gwo2 sik1 saai3 di1 cin2 dou1 m4 gan2 jiu3, fung1 ceoi1 gai1 daan6 hok3, coi4 saan3 jan4 on1 lok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他還說就算把錢都賠光也沒關係，風吹雞蛋殼，財散人安樂。
examples.english_sentence: He even said that even if he lost all his money it would be fine — 'when money goes, people find peace.'

mandarin_meaning: 形容声势猛烈、来势汹涌；也可指做事张扬、抢风头。
english_meaning: An idiom describing great momentum or a strong, aggressive show of force; also used for being flashy or trying to steal the limelight.
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容事态或气势非常强烈、来势迅猛，或指做事张扬、爱抢风头。
explanation_english: Used to describe something moving forward with powerful momentum or force, or someone acting flashy/attention-seeking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司而家推新產品，宣傳做得好風頭火勢，吸引咗好多人注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ji4 gaa1 teoi1 san1 caan2 ban2, syun1 cyun4 zou6 dak1 hou2 fung1 tau4 fo2 sai3, kap1 jan5 zo2 hou2 do1 jan4 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司现在推出新产品，宣传做得很有声势，吸引了很多人的注意。
examples.english_sentence: The company is launching a new product and the promotion is being done with great fanfare, attracting a lot of attention.

cantonese: 風扇底下傾偈，講風涼話
jyutping: fung1 sin3 dai2 haa6 king1 gai2, gong2 fung1 loeng4 waa6
mandarin_meaning: 坐在舒服的地方聊天，卻說冷嘲熱諷或不體諒人的話（形容在旁邊輕鬆地發表冷淡、刻薄評論）
english_meaning: To sit comfortably (literally 'chatting under a fan') while making cold, insensitive, or sarcastic remarks — i.e., to make heartless comments from a detached, comfortable position.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話常用於指責對方在事不關己或處於舒適環境時，發表冷淡、刻薄或幸災樂禍的評論。前半句描寫坐在風扇底下舒服地聊天，後半句指說『風涼話』（冷嘲熱諷、不貼心的話）。
explanation_english: This expression criticizes someone who, from a comfortable or detached position ('chatting under a fan'), makes cold, sarcastic, or unsympathetic remarks. The first part depicts being relaxed; the second part ('say wind-cool words') means to utter insensitive or mocking comments.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你喺度風扇底下傾偈，講風涼話，有咩資格評頭品足？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai2 dou6 fung1 sin3 dai2 haa6 king1 gai2, gong2 fung1 loeng4 waa6, jau5 me1 zik1 gaap3 ping4 tau4 pan2 zuk1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在這裡坐在風扇底下聊天，說些冷嘲熱諷的話，有什麼資格評論別人？
examples.english_sentence: You're sitting here chatting under a fan and making cold remarks—what right do you have to criticize others?

cantonese: 風水佬唔呃得十年八年
jyutping: fung1 seoi2 lou2 m4 ngaak1 dak1 sap6 nin4 baat3 nin4
mandarin_meaning: 風水師不能永遠騙人；騙局終會被拆穿
english_meaning: You can't fool people forever — scams or lies will eventually be exposed.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語字面上指『風水師』騙不了人十年八年，實際用法泛指任何欺騙行為不可能永久隱瞞，遲早會被揭穿。常見於香港口語與輕蔑或警告語境。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying literally says a 'feng shui man' can't cheat people for ten or eight years — figuratively it warns that deception won't last and cons will eventually be found out. Commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese in a dismissive or cautionary tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲把戲遲早會被揭穿，風水佬唔呃得十年八年。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 baa2 hei3 ci4 zou2 wui5 bei6 kit3 cyun1, fung1 seoi2 lou2 m4 ngaak1 dak1 sap6 nin4 baat3 nin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的那些把戲遲早會被揭穿，騙不了人一輩子。
examples.english_sentence: His tricks will be exposed sooner or later — you can't fool people forever.

cantonese: 風水先生無定葬，占卦先生半路亡
jyutping: fung1 seoi2 sin1 saang1 mou4 ding6 zong3, zim1 gwaa3 sin1 saang1 bun3 lou6 mong4
mandarin_meaning: 字面意思是風水師無法為自己選定墓地，占卦（算命）的人也會在途中亡故。引申為專家難以把自己的本事用在自身，或再厄運面前也無能為力，強調命運難以預料和掌控。
english_meaning: Literally: 'The feng shui master doesn't get to choose his own burial; the fortune-teller dies halfway through.' Figuratively it means experts often cannot apply their skills to themselves and cannot control their own fate — fate is unpredictable.
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，用來諷刺或感嘆那些替人指點、預測的人，往往難以為自己或避免自己的不幸，強調人難以預料和掌握自身命運。
explanation_english: A proverb used to mock or lament that those who advise or predict for others often cannot help themselves; it emphasizes that people cannot always foresee or control their own destiny.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日幫人搵風水，自己屋企啲問題都解決唔到，真係應驗咗：風水先生無定葬，占卦先生半路亡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 bong1 jan4 wan2 fung1 seoi2, zi6 gei2 uk1 kei5 di1 man6 tai4 dou1 gaai2 kyut3 m4 dou3, zan1 hai6 jing3 jim6 zo2: fung1 seoi2 sin1 saang1 mou4 ding6 zong3, zim1 gwaa3 sin1 saang1 bun3 lou6 mong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常帮人看风水，但自己家的问题都解决不了，真应验了：风水先生无定葬，占卦先生半路亡。
examples.english_sentence: He often helps others with feng shui, but can't fix his own family's problems — it really proved true: feng shui masters don't get to choose their own grave; fortune-tellers die halfway through.

mandarin_meaning: 风水轮流转（时来运转、好运坏运交替；命运起伏）
english_meaning: The wheel of fortune turns; luck changes over time; fortunes fluctuate and one's turn will come.
explanation_mandarin: 表示好运和坏运会轮流出现，命运有起有落，鼓励人不要太灰心或得意忘形。
explanation_english: An idiom meaning that good and bad luck alternate and fortunes change over time; used to remind someone that situations are temporary and will turn around.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔使灰心，風水輪流轉，遲啲你就會返轉運。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 sai2 fui1 sam1, fung1 seoi2 leon4 lau4 zyun2, ci4 di1 nei5 zau6 wui5 faan1 zyun2 wan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不用灰心，风水轮流转，迟早你会转运。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be discouraged; the wheel of fortune turns and your luck will change.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家好窮，但風水輪流轉，將來可能會好返。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hou2 cung4, daan6 fung1 seoi2 leon4 lau4 zyun2, zoeng1 loi4 ho2 nang4 wui5 hou2 faan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在很穷，但风水轮流转，将来可能会好起来。
examples.english_sentence: He's poor right now, but fortunes alternate; he might be better off in the future.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢之前賺咗好多錢，依家蝕晒，真係風水輪流轉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi1 cin4 zaan6 zo2 hou2 do1 cin2, ji1 gaa1 sik1 saai3, zan1 hai6 fung1 seoi2 leon4 lau4 zyun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他以前赚了很多钱，现在亏得一干二净，真是风水轮流转。
examples.english_sentence: He used to make a lot of money but is losing everything now — it's truly that fortunes change.

mandarin_meaning: 形势兴盛、事业蓬勃发展，进展顺利
english_meaning: to flourish; to thrive; to gain momentum and prosper
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成语（可作形容词或动词）
explanation_mandarin: “风生水起”原指风吹起水面而波动，借以比喻事物发展快速、有生气、兴盛繁荣，常用于形容事业、行情或局势好转并迅速发展。
explanation_english: Literally describing wind creating ripples on water, this idiom figuratively means that something is thriving or gaining momentum. It's often used to describe businesses, projects, or situations that are developing rapidly and prosperously.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 自從公司換咗新管理層之後，生意風生水起，訂單成日嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zi6 cung4 gung1 si1 wun6 zo2 san1 gun2 lei5 cang4 zi1 hau6, saang1 ji3 fung1 saang1 seoi2 hei2, deng6 daan1 sing4 jat6 lei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 自从公司换了新管理层之后，生意风生水起，订单不断。
examples.english_sentence: Since the company brought in a new management team, business has been booming and orders keep coming in.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢開咗個網店後，生意慢慢風生水起，人氣愈來愈高。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 zo2 go3 mong5 dim3 hau6, saang1 ji3 maan6 maan6 fung1 saang1 seoi2 hei2, jan4 hei3 jyu6 loi4 jyu6 gou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她开了网店之后，生意慢慢风生水起，人气越来越高。
examples.english_sentence: After opening an online shop, their business gradually began to flourish and their popularity increased.

jyutping: gei1 sik6 lai6 zi1, baau2 sik6 wong4 pei4
mandarin_meaning: 字面：饥饿时吃荔枝，饱足时吃黄皮。引申：比喻人随环境或利益改变态度、只在需要或有利时才重视好处（有时含贬义）。
english_meaning: Literal: eat lychees when hungry, eat wampi (huangpi) when full. Figurative: describes people who change their preferences or attitudes according to circumstances — only valuing good things when they need them or when it's advantageous (often pejorative).
explanation_mandarin: 此俗语用两种水果作比喻，表达随境遇、利益而改变态度或取舍的行为。常用来批评见利忘义或投机取巧的人。
explanation_english: This proverb uses two fruits as a metaphor to describe adapting tastes or behavior to circumstances or advantage. It's often used critically of opportunistic people who only appreciate something when it benefits them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日搵方便，真係『饥食荔枝，饱食黄皮』，有利就貼近，無利就走晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 wan2 fong1 bin6, zan1 hai6 gei1 sik6 lai6 zi1, baau2 sik6 wong4 pei4, jau5 lei6 zau6 tip3 gan6, mou4 lei6 zau6 zau2 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是這樣，真是餓時吃荔枝、飽時吃黃皮，有利就靠近，沒利就全走了。
examples.english_sentence: He's always like that—literally 'eat lychees when hungry, eat wampi when full'—he only sticks around when there's something to gain, and leaves when there isn't.

mandarin_meaning: 胡亂、馬虎、亂七八糟
english_meaning: slapdash; messy; careless; nonsensical
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來形容事情做得很馬虎、混亂或說話胡扯、不可靠。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to describe something done carelessly or messily, or talk that is nonsense/unreliable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你啲功課做得鬼五馬六，老師都唔滿意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 di1 gung1 fo3 zou6 dak1 gwai2 ng5 maa5 luk6, lou5 si1 dou1 m4 mun5 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做的功課很馬虎，老師都不滿意。
examples.english_sentence: You did your homework sloppily; the teacher isn't satisfied.

jyutping: gwai2 paa3 ok3 jan4, se4 paa3 gwan3
mandarin_meaning: 鬼怕惡人，蛇怕棍（各有畏懼／各有克星）
english_meaning: Literally: 'ghosts fear evil people; snakes fear sticks.' Figuratively: everyone has something they fear; everyone has a weakness or nemesis.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語字面意思是鬼會怕惡人、蛇會怕棍，比喻沒有任何人或事物是絕對無敵的，每個人或事都有害怕或克制它的對象。
explanation_english: This proverb literally says ghosts fear evil people and snakes fear sticks. It means nothing is invincible—everyone or everything has something they fear or a nemesis.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢自以為無敵，但鬼怕惡人，蛇怕棍，總有佢怕嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi6 ji5 wai4 mou4 dik6, daan6 gwai2 paa3 ok3 jan4, se4 paa3 gwan3, zung2 jau5 keoi5 paa3 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他自以為無敵，但鬼怕惡人、蛇怕棍，總有他害怕的東西。
examples.english_sentence: He thinks he's invincible, but 'ghosts fear evil people, snakes fear sticks' — everyone has something they're afraid of.

mandarin_meaning: 被嚇了一跳 / 受到驚嚇
english_meaning: to be suddenly frightened; to get a big fright
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面意思是「鬼拍後枕」，用於形容被嚇到、受驚或突然驚嚇得很厲害。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "ghost slaps the back of the head." It describes being startled or getting a sudden, strong fright.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 半夜聽到窗外有怪聲，我嚇到鬼拍後枕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bun3 je6 teng1 dou3 coeng1 ngoi6 jau5 gwaai3 sing1, ngo5 haak3 dou3 gwai2 paak3 hau6 zam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 半夜听到窗外有怪声，我被吓了一跳。
examples.english_sentence: I heard a strange noise outside the window at midnight and got a huge fright.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到嗰個景象，大家都嚇到鬼拍後枕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 go2 go3 ging2 zoeng6, daa2 gaa1 dou1 haak3 dou3 gwai2 paak3 hau6 zam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到那个景象，大家都被吓坏了。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing that scene, everyone was terrified.

mandarin_meaning: 故意睜一隻眼閉一隻眼；欺騙、蒙騙別人
english_meaning: to turn a blind eye; to cheat/hoodwink someone (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，帶有貶義。可用來表示故意對錯誤或不當行為視而不見（睜一隻眼閉一隻眼），或表示用欺騙手法蒙騙他人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression with negative connotations. It can mean deliberately turning a blind eye to wrongdoing, or to deceive/hoodwink someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢答應我會還錢，結果鬼揞眼，唔見人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daap3 jing3 ngo5 wui5 waan4 cin2, git3 gwo2 gwai2 aam2 ngaan5, m4 gin3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他答應我會還錢，結果耍我一手，根本沒有打算還。
examples.english_sentence: He promised to pay me back, but ended up tricking me and never intended to repay.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司見到員工偷懶都鬼揞眼，無跟進。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gin3 dou2 jyun4 gung1 tau1 laan5 dou1 gwai2 aam2 ngaan5, mou5 gan1 zeon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司看到員工偷懶卻選擇睜一隻眼閉一隻眼，沒有跟進。
examples.english_sentence: The company saw employees being lazy but chose to turn a blind eye and didn't follow up.

mandarin_meaning: （太）吵死了／（真）吵得不得了
english_meaning: so damn noisy; extremely noisy
explanation_mandarin: 香港粤语口语用法，带有粗口/夸张成分。'鬼杀'为加强语气的粗俗用词，'咁嘈'表示程度（这么吵）。整体用来抱怨某处或某人非常吵闹。
explanation_english: A colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese expression with coarse emphasis. '鬼杀' is a vulgar intensifier and '咁嘈' means 'this/so noisy'. Used to complain that something or someone is extremely noisy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 樓上嘅鄰居經常夜晚開派對，鬼杀咁嘈，我訓唔到覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou4 soeng6 ge3 leon4 geoi1 ging1 soeng4 je6 maan5 hoi1 paai3 deoi6, gwai2 saat3 gam2 cou4, ngo5 fan3 m4 dou2 gok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 楼上的邻居经常晚上开派对，太吵了，我睡不着觉。
examples.english_sentence: The upstairs neighbors always throw parties at night — it's damn noisy, I can't sleep.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可唔可以細聲啲？鬼杀咁嘈！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 sai3 seng1 di1? gwai2 saat3 gam2 cou4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你能不能小声点？太吵了！
examples.english_sentence: Can you be quieter? It's so damn loud!

mandarin_meaning: 非常；極其（口語、帶誇張或粗俗語氣）
english_meaning: extremely; so (damn) — a coarse/colloquial intensifier
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用法，用來加強語氣，表示程度非常或極其。含有粗俗或誇張的語感，多用於非正式場合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial intensifier used to indicate a very high degree (e.g., 'so damn ...'). It has a coarse/vulgar tone and is used in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日鬼死咁忙，冇時間食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1jat6 gwai2 sei2 gam2 mong4, mou5 si4gaan3 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天忙得要命，沒有時間吃飯。
examples.english_sentence: He's so damn busy today; he doesn't have time to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 鬼畫符 (guǐ huà fú)：潦草或看不懂的字跡；比喻晦澀難懂或胡亂寫的東西
english_meaning: Illegible handwriting; gibberish; incomprehensible scrawl; used figuratively for something messy or nonsensical
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語（可作名詞或動詞短語）
partOfSpeech_english: idiom/phrase (can function as noun or verb)
explanation_mandarin: 原指像鬼那樣畫符，字跡潦草難辨。現多用來形容字寫得亂、看不懂，或比喻說話、文字晦澀、沒有條理。
explanation_english: Originally referring to talismanic writing by ghosts, implying messy or mysterious characters. Now commonly used to describe illegible handwriting or anything written/spoken that is confusing, disorganized, or nonsensical.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你寫嘅字好似鬼画符，我完全睇唔明。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 se2 ge3 zi6 hou2 ci5 gwai2 waak6 fu4, ngo5 jyun4 cyun4 tai2 m4 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你写的字像鬼画符，我完全看不懂。
examples.english_sentence: Your handwriting looks like gibberish — I can't read it at all.

mandarin_meaning: （粤语俚语）常当小撮合者或爱撮合别人的人
english_meaning: A Cantonese colloquial term for someone who acts as an informal matchmaker or is always trying to pair people up
explanation_mandarin: 「鸡仔媒人」是粤语口语/俚语，用来形容喜欢撮合别人、当小媒人的人，语气可带半开玩笑或轻微贬义，通常指非正式、爱凑热闹的撮合者。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression describing a person who likes to play matchmaker or constantly pairs others up. The term is often joking or mildly pejorative and implies an informal, meddling kind of matchmaker.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿珍成日做雞仔媒人，成日幫人介紹男女朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 zan1 sing4 jat6 zou6 gai1 zai2 mui4 jan4, sing4 jat6 bong1 jan4 gaai3 siu6 naam4 neoi5 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小珍总是当鸡仔媒人，经常帮别人介绍男女朋友。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Zhen is always playing matchmaker, constantly introducing people to potential partners.

mandarin_meaning: 鸡同鸭讲（形容彼此说话互相听不懂或沟通无效）
english_meaning: Talking past each other; unable to understand one another; communication fails
explanation_mandarin: 形容双方在交流时互相听不懂或意见不合，谈话毫无共识，沟通失败。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where two (or more) people are talking but fail to understand each other or reach common ground—i.e. talking past each other.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋開會嗰陣，大家意見完全唔同，成日雞同鴨講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hoi1 wui2 go2 zan6, daai6 gaa1 ji3 gin3 jyun4 cyun4 m4 tung4, sing4 jat6 gai1 tung4 aap3 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们开会的时候，大家意见完全不同，总是鸡同鸭讲。
examples.english_sentence: When we have meetings, everyone's opinions are completely different and we always end up talking past each other.

mandarin_meaning: 割不断 / 难以切断（形容关系或牵连很深，难以分开）
english_meaning: inseparable; hard to sever (describes a bond or entanglement that is difficult or impossible to break)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗语/成语（形容词性短语）
explanation_mandarin: 「鸡啄唔断」是粤语俗语，用来形容两者关系非常紧密或牵连复杂，难以分开或切断。也可引申指纠缠不清、断不了的事情。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiom meaning a bond or entanglement that cannot easily be broken. It is used to describe very close relationships or situations that are hard to sever or resolve.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個係兄弟，情分雞啄唔斷，點都會幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 hai6 hing1 dai6, cing4 fan6 gai1 zoek3 m4 dyun6, dim2 dou1 wui5 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们是兄弟，感情割不断，不管怎样都会互相帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: They're brothers; their bond is inseparable — they'll help each other no matter what.

mandarin_meaning: 膽小、懦弱
english_meaning: timid; cowardly; easily frightened
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，形容一個人很膽小、容易受驚或缺乏勇氣。比喻像雞一樣驚慌、逃避。常用於廣東話口語對話中，帶有貶義或調侃意味。
explanation_english: An informal/slang Cantonese term used to describe someone who is timid, easily frightened, or lacking courage. Literally likens the person to a chicken's skittishness. Often used in conversational Cantonese with a teasing or mildly derogatory tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鸡噉脚，唔敢一個人行夜路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gai1 gam2 goek3 , m4 gam2 jat1 go3 jan4 hang4 je6 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是膽小怕事，不敢一個人走夜路。
examples.english_sentence: He's always timid and won't dare to walk alone at night.

mandarin_meaning: 很少见；非常罕见（口语）
english_meaning: Extremely rare; seldom seen (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 口语俚语，常用来形容某事、某人或某种情况极为罕见或几乎不会发生，带有夸张或戏谑的语气。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression used to say that something or someone is extremely rare or unlikely to occur; often used with exaggeration or humor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日遲到？鸡屙尿，少见！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 ci4 dou3? gai1 o1 niu6, siu2 gin3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天迟到？真少见！
examples.english_sentence: He's late today? That's rare!

cantonese: 鸡忌发瘟，鸭忌离群，马忌眼瞓，牛忌脚震
jyutping: gai1 gei3 faat3 man1, aap3 gei3 lei4 kwan4, maa5 gei3 ngaan5 fan3, ngau4 gei3 goek3 zan3
mandarin_meaning: 各有各的忌讳和弱点；每个人或事物都有自己怕的或不擅长的地方。
english_meaning: Every creature has its own vulnerabilities; people each have their own fears or weaknesses. Don't force others beyond their nature.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用几种动物的“忌讳”比喻世人各有短长和畏惧，提醒人们要体谅差异，不要强求别人做不擅长或害怕的事。
explanation_english: This proverb lists each animal's weakness as a metaphor: everyone has their own limits and fears. It advises understanding and not forcing others to act against their nature.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做人各有長短，唔好咁逼人，正如話『鸡忌发瘟，鸭忌离群，马忌眼瞓，牛忌脚震』。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 jan4 gok3 jau5 coeng4 dyun2, m4 hou2 gam2 bik1 jan4, zing3 jyu4 waa6 'gai1 gei3 faat3 man1, aap3 gei3 lei4 kwan4, maa5 gei3 ngaan5 fan3, ngau4 gei3 goek3 zan3'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做人各有长短，不要这么逼人，就像说“鸡忌发瘟，鸭忌离群，马忌眼瞓，牛忌脚震”。
examples.english_sentence: Everyone has strengths and weaknesses; don't push people too hard. As the saying goes, 'Each animal has its own fear.'

mandarin_meaning: 笨拙；手脚不灵活；做事慌乱
english_meaning: clumsy; awkward; doing things in a hasty or disorderly way
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容人手脚笨拙、動作不靈活或做事慌亂、凌亂不利落。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is clumsy or awkward, or who does things in a hurried, messy, or unskillful way.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁雞手鸭脚，慢慢嚟，小心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 gai1 sau2 ngaap3 goek3, maan6 maan6 lai4, siu2 sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那么笨手笨脚，慢慢来，小心点。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so clumsy; take your time and be more careful.

jyutping: gai1 daa2 zam1, waa6 dou1 mou5 gam2 faai3
mandarin_meaning: 動作或說話來得非常快，連說話的時間都沒有／來不及回應
english_meaning: Someone acted or spoke extremely quickly — so fast that you couldn't even say a word or react.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，形容某人做事或說話速度非常快，讓人來不及回應或發言。字面上可能借用「雞打針」作比喻，但主要用法是強調速度之快。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to describe someone acting or speaking so quickly that others have no time to respond or speak. The literal image (a chicken getting an injection) serves as a vivid, idiomatic metaphor for rapid, jerky action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一開口就講晒成段嘢，雞打針，話都冇咁快，我根本反應唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 hoi1 hau2 zau6 gong2 saai3 sing4 dyun6 je5, gai1 daa2 zam1, waa6 dou1 mou5 gam2 faai3, ngo5 gan1 bun2 faan2 jing3 m4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一開口就把整段話說完，太快了，連說話的時間都沒有，我根本反應不過來。
examples.english_sentence: He opened his mouth and finished the whole chunk of speech — it was so fast, I didn't even have time to react.

jyutping: gai1 ceon1 gam2 mat6 dou1 bok3 ceot1 zai2
mandarin_meaning: （粗俗）形容某人性慾極強或極度興奮，甚至在不利或不合適的情況下也會有明顯的生理性反應（類似“會射/會有性反應”）。
english_meaning: Vulgar slang describing someone who is extremely horny or sexually aroused — to the point of showing an obvious physiological sexual reaction (e.g., ejaculation) even in unlikely or inappropriate circumstances.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 描述性短語（形容性慾狀態）
explanation_mandarin: 此短語屬於廣東話粗俗俚語，語氣下流，通常用來貶義或嘲諷某人性慾旺盛或反應過度。當中“鸡春”指性慾或春心，“咁密”表示程度高，“菢出仔/出仔”在此語境下指明顯的性生理反應。該詞帶強烈粗俗和貶義色彩，不宜在正式場合使用。
explanation_english: This is Cantonese vulgar slang used to mock or disparage someone for being extremely sexually aroused or having an excessive sexual reaction. "Gai chun" refers to sexual desire, "gam mat" emphasizes intensity, and "bok3 ceot1 zai2" (literally "produce/bring out a kid") here implies an obvious sexual/ejaculatory reaction. Strongly vulgar — avoid in formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一見啲艷照就雞春咁密都菢出仔，成日畀人笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 gin3 di1 jim6 ziu3 zau6 gai1 ceon1 gam2 mat6 dou1 bok3 ceot1 zai2, sing4 jat6 bei2 jan4 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一看到那些艷照就變得非常好色，甚至會有明顯的生理反應，經常被人取笑。
examples.english_sentence: He gets so turned on when he sees racy photos that he'd visibly have a sexual reaction — people often ridicule him.

mandarin_meaning: 形容微不足道、瑣碎的事情（相當於「雞毛蒜皮」）
english_meaning: trivial matters; petty, insignificant issues
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一些非常瑣碎、不值一提或無意義的小事或爭執，口語常用。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression describing matters that are petty, insignificant, or trivial—used to dismiss minor disputes or details.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好為啲雞毛鴨血嘅嘢爭拗，冇意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 wai6 di1 gai1 mou4 aap3 hyut3 ge3 je5 zang1 au2, mou5 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要為這些雞毛蒜皮的事情爭論，沒有意義。
examples.english_sentence: Don't argue over such trivial matters; it's pointless.

jyutping: gai1 daan2 mo2 gwo3 hing1 sei3 loeng5
mandarin_meaning: 形容過於小心或脆弱，做事戰戰兢兢（俚語/俗語）
english_meaning: A colloquial phrase describing someone who is overly cautious or fragile — acts as if worried about breaking an egg
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語用雞蛋比喻，形容一個人做事非常小心或怕出錯、過於膽小，像碰到雞蛋一樣生怕弄破。此表達屬口語、地區性用法，使用時帶有輕微戲謔或嘲諷意味。
explanation_english: This colloquial expression uses an egg as a metaphor to describe someone who is extremely cautious or timid, afraid of making mistakes — as if touching an egg would break it. It's informal, regionally used, and can carry a mildly teasing or critical tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做嘢咁驚撻，真係雞蛋摸過輕四兩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 je5 gam3 ging1 taat3, zan1 hai6 gai1 daan2 mo2 gwo3 hing1 sei3 loeng5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做事那么害怕出錯，真是鸡蛋摸过轻四两。
examples.english_sentence: You're so afraid of making mistakes — you're really acting like someone who'd tiptoe around an egg.

jyutping: gai1 sik6 fong3 gwong1 cung4, sam1 zi1 tou5 ming4
mandarin_meaning: （俗語）大家心裡非常清楚；一清二楚/心知肚明
english_meaning: An informal Cantonese expression meaning something is perfectly obvious or well known to everyone; 'it's obvious', 'everyone knows'.
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東俗語，前半句帶有形象的比喻，整句用來強調某件事非常明顯或大家都知道，不需多說。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying that uses a vivid image in the first half; the whole phrase emphasizes that something is very obvious or well known to everyone and needs no further explanation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢同老板走得咁近，雞食放光蟲，心知肚明。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tung4 lou5 baan2 zau2 dak1 gam2 gan6, gai1 sik6 fong3 gwong1 cung4, sam1 zi1 tou5 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他和老板走得那麼近，大家心知肚明。
examples.english_sentence: He's so close to the boss; it's obvious to everyone.

jyutping: gai1 bat1 daa2 jan4 ngaa4 gaau2 jyun5
mandarin_meaning: 形容人懦弱、沒有脾氣、遇事退縮（口語俚語）
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who is weak, spineless, or easily intimidated
explanation_mandarin: 字面上意為“雞腿打到人的牙關變軟”，引申指一個人遇到衝突或壓力時很快退縮、沒脾氣、不會頂得住。
explanation_english: Literally “a chicken thigh hits someone's jaw hinge and it becomes soft.” Figuratively it describes a person who quickly backs down, is spineless, or easily intimidated when facing conflict or pressure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一俾人鬧就縮埋，真係雞髀打人牙铰软。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 bei2 jan4 nau6 zau6 suk1 maai4, zan1 hai6 gai1 bat1 daa2 jan4 ngaa4 gaau2 jyun5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一被人骂就退缩，真是懦弱。
examples.english_sentence: He shrinks whenever someone yells at him — really spineless.

mandarin_meaning: 板着脸；面色不好，阴沉或生气
english_meaning: to have a sullen or scowling face; looking displeased or grumpy
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人面色不好、板著臉或顯得不高興、生氣，常用於口語。
explanation_english: An informal Cantonese expression describing someone who looks sullen, scowling, or visibly displeased.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日返工都黑口黑面，唔知發生咩事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 faan1 gung1 dou1 hak1 hau2 hak1 min6, m4 zi1 faat3 sang1 me1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他上班時總是板著臉，不知道發生了什麼事。
examples.english_sentence: He always goes to work with a sullen face; I don't know what's happened.

mandarin_meaning: 黑市女老板；在地下非法市場從事買賣的女性
english_meaning: black-market madam; a woman who runs or deals in illegal/underground trade
explanation_mandarin: 用來指在黑市或地下渠道從事走私、贓物交易或其他非法買賣的女性，常帶貶義或戲稱意味。
explanation_english: Refers to a woman who operates in the black market or underground trade—e.g., selling smuggled or illicit goods. Often used pejoratively or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大家小心啲，佢係黑市夫人，專門賣走私貨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 gaa1 siu2 sam1 di1, keoi5 hai6 hak1 si5 fu1 jan4, zyun1 mun4 maai6 zau2 si1 fo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大家小心点，她是黑市夫人，专门卖走私货。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful, she's a black-market madam who specializes in selling smuggled goods.

jyutping: hak1 gau2 tau1 sik6, baak6 gau2 dong3 zoi1
mandarin_meaning: 黑狗偷食，白狗受災（比喻有錯的人逍遙法外，無辜者反而受連累）
english_meaning: The guilty go unpunished while the innocent are blamed — scapegoating; the guilty escape and the innocent suffer.
explanation_mandarin: 此諺語用狗作比喻，表示真正做錯事的人逍遙，而無辜的人反而被指責或受到懲罰，含有替罪與冤枉之意。
explanation_english: This proverb uses dogs as a metaphor to say that the real wrongdoer escapes, while innocent people are blamed or punished — a situation of scapegoating and wrongful blame.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋一再推卸責任，結果黑狗偷食，白狗當災，冇人負責。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 jat1 zoi3 teoi1 se6 zaak3 jam6, git3 gwo2 hak1 gau2 tau1 sik6, baak6 gau2 dong3 zoi1, mou5 jan4 fu6 zaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們一再推卸責任，結果是黑狗偷食，白狗當災，沒有人負責。
examples.english_sentence: They kept shirking responsibility; as a result the guilty went free while the innocent were blamed — nobody took responsibility.

jyutping: hak1 baak6 tin1 ngo4, jat6 ngo4 (o1) je6 ngo4 (o1)
mandarin_meaning: 字面：黑白天鵝，日鵝（哦）夜鵝（哦）。實際用法：一種口語/網絡用的無厘頭短語或歌詞押韻片段，常用作玩笑、押韻填詞或表達交替／反覆的狀態。
english_meaning: Literal: "black-and-white swan, day-swan (oh) night-swan (oh)". Usage: a playful, nonsensical Cantonese phrase or lyric refrain used jokingly or as a meme; can imply alternation/flip-flopping or simply serve as a catchy/absurd chant.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語 / 俚語 / 歌詞片段
explanation_mandarin: 此短語並非傳統成語，多見於粵語歌詞、網絡留言或口語玩笑中。字面沒有固定深意，常作押韻或製造搞笑、荒誕效果；有時也用來形容事物或情緒日夜交替、反覆無常。
explanation_english: This phrase is not a classical idiom; it appears in Cantonese song lyrics, online posts, or casual speech as a playful, nonsensical refrain. It has no fixed literal meaning and is used for rhyme, comic/absurd effect, or to suggest alternating/flip-flopping states.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲人喺帖文下面留言：『黑白天鵝，日鵝哦夜鵝哦』，純粹係玩嘢好搞笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 jan4 hai2 tip3 man4 haa6 min6 lau4 jim4: 'hak1 baak6 tin1 ngo4, jat6 ngo4 o1 je6 ngo4 o1', seon4 seoi3 hai6 waan2 je5 hou2 gaau2 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人在貼文下面留言：「黑白天鵝，日鵝（哦）夜鵝（哦）」，純粹是在玩笑，很好笑。
examples.english_sentence: People commented under the post: "black-and-white swan, day-swan (oh) night-swan (oh)" — just joking around, it's hilarious.

mandarin_meaning: 比墨斗還黑；（臉色）非常陰沉、憂鬱或生氣，也可指皮膚/物件非常黑
english_meaning: literally 'blacker than an ink-line tool'; very dark (in color) or describing someone extremely sullen/angry/upset
explanation_mandarin: 常用來形容一個人的臉色很差、很陰沉或心情極差，也可用來形容皮膚或物件顏色非常黑。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone with a very sullen or bad-looking facial expression (angry/upset); can also describe a person’s skin or an object as very dark.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打完工返嚟，面色黑過墨斗，唔想講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 jyun4 gung1 faan1 lai4, min6 sik1 hak1 gwo3 mak6 dau2, m4 soeng2 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他下班回來，臉色黑得像墨斗，不想說話。
examples.english_sentence: He came back from work with a face as black as an ink-line tool, not wanting to talk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺海邊曬咗成個夏天，皮膚黑過墨斗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 hoi2 bin1 saai3 zo2 seng4 go3 haa6 tin1, pei4 fu1 hak1 gwo3 mak6 dau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在海邊曬了整個夏天，皮膚黑得像墨斗。
