examples.english_sentence: He spent the whole summer at the beach and his skin is as dark as an ink-line tool.

mandarin_meaning: （粤语俚语）形容经常黑着脸、面色阴沉或显得很严肃易怒的人，带有戏谑或调侃意味。
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang term for someone who often has a sullen or scowling face — used jokingly to describe a grumpy or stern-looking person.
explanation_mandarin: “黑面神”字面上是“黑脸的神”，用来戏称那些常常面无笑容、看起来不高兴或爱发牢骚的人。语气多为开玩笑或半真半假的批评。
explanation_english: Literally 'black-faced god', the term jokingly refers to someone who frequently wears a sour or stern expression. It’s used playfully or teasingly to call someone grumpy or stern-faced.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢呢排成日黑面神，唔知係咪遇到啲煩心事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ni1 paai4 sing4 jat6 hak1 min6 san4, m4 zi1 hai6 mai6 jyu6 dou3 di1 faan4 sam1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近常常黑著臉，不知道是不是遇到什麼煩心事。
examples.english_sentence: He's been scowling a lot lately; I wonder if he's dealing with something upsetting.

jyutping: ding2 wu4 soeng5 sou3, hou2 zaai1
mandarin_meaning: 装作虔诚或清高（尤指吃素或表现道德高尚），多带讽刺意味
english_meaning: to put on a show of piety or moral superiority (often by claiming vegetarianism); to be sanctimonious
explanation_mandarin: 此短語用於諷刺或批評某人表現得很虔誠、清高或特別崇尚素食，但實際上可能虛偽、不真誠。
explanation_english: This phrase is used to mock or criticize someone who acts very pious, ascetic, or morally superior (often emphasizing vegetarianism) while actually being insincere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鼎湖上素，好齋，講到好有道德；其實自己又唔係咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ding2 wu4 soeng5 sou3, hou2 zaai1, gong2 dou3 hou2 jau5 dou6; kei4 sat6 zi6 gei2 jau6 m4 hai6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是装得很虔诚、吃素、很有道德，其實並非如此。
examples.english_sentence: He always puts on a show of piety — claiming to be a vegetarian and very righteous — but in fact he's not.

mandarin_meaning: 家里/自己人有人看著（暗指天理或家人會知道），意指瞞不住、終會被發現或得到報應。
english_meaning: Literally "the home has eyes" — a Cantonese idiom meaning you can't hide things from family/justice; sooner or later people or fate will find out and expose or punish it.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，常用來表示做壞事或隱瞞的事瞞不住，或相信天理/家人會看見並討回公道或揭發真相。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to indicate that misdeeds or secrets won't remain hidden — family, others, or fate will see and expose them or ensure justice is done.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你偷嘢想瞞得過？家山有眼，遲早會畀人揭發。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tau1 je5 soeng2 maan4 dak1 gwo3? gaa1 saan1 jau5 ngaan5, ci4 zou2 wui5 bei2 jan4 git3 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你以為偷東西能瞞得過嗎？家山有眼，遲早會被人揭發。
examples.english_sentence: Do you think you can get away with stealing? You can't hide it — sooner or later someone will expose you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺外面扮晒有錢都冇用，家山有眼，回家之後好快就會被識破。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 ngoi6 min6 baan6 saai3 jau5 cin2 dou1 mou5 jung6, gaa1 saan1 jau5 ngaan5, wui4 gaa1 zi1 hau6 hou2 faai3 zau6 wui5 bei2 sik1 po3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在外面裝闊也沒用，家山有眼，回到家很快就會被識破。
examples.english_sentence: Showing off wealth outside is useless — your family will notice; once you're home it'll soon be seen through.

mandarin_meaning: 放低身段；稍微收敛、谦逊一点
english_meaning: to tone it down; lower one's pride or stance; be more humble or back off a bit
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，字面为“放下两两（量）”，引申为让人收起架子、放低姿态、谦逊一些，或在争执中退一步以缓和局面。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning 'put down two taels' — used figuratively to tell someone to lower their stance, be less proud, relax, or back off slightly to ease a situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁高傲，放低二两啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 gou1 ngou6, fong3 dai1 ji6 loeng5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你别那么高傲，放低身段吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so arrogant — tone it down and be more humble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 同老細講嘢時要識放低二两，唔好太硬頸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tung4 lou5 sai3 gong2 je5 si4 jiu3 sik1 fong3 dai1 ji6 loeng5, m4 hou2 taai3 ngaang6 geng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 和老板沟通时要懂得放低身段，不要太倔强。
examples.english_sentence: When talking with the boss, know how to be humble — don't be so stubborn.

mandarin_meaning: 大声发泄情绪（如生气或悲伤）；大声抱怨或哭喊
english_meaning: to loudly vent one's emotions (anger or sadness); to complain, shout, or cry out loudly
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語表達，表示以大聲的方式發洩情緒（例如生氣、抱怨或哭喊）。常見於日常對話，帶有粗略的口語色彩。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to let out or vent emotions loudly (for example anger, complaints, or crying). Common in everyday speech and carries an informal tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到個消息就放聲氣，喊咗好耐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 go3 siu1 sik1 zau6 fong3 seng1 hei3, haan3 zo2 hou2 noi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一听到那个消息就大声发泄情绪，哭了很久。
examples.english_sentence: When he heard the news, he burst into loud crying and cried for a long time.

mandarin_meaning: 放鴿子（放人鴿子）
english_meaning: to stand someone up; to bail on someone / to ghost someone
explanation_mandarin: 粤语／香港口語，字面是“放白鴿”，實際意思是未按約赴約或不回應對方，相當於普通話的“放鴿子”或“放飛機”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese/Hong Kong colloquial expression literally 'to release a white pigeon.' Idiomatically it means to fail to show up for an appointment or to ignore/ghost someone (i.e., to stand someone up).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢約咗我今晚食飯，最後放白鴿，連訊息都冇覆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 joek3 zo2 ngo5 gam1 maan5 sik6 faan6, zeoi3 hau6 fong3 baak6 gap3, lin4 seon3 sik1 dou1 mou5 fuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他约了我今晚吃饭，但最后放我鸽子，连信息都没回。
examples.english_sentence: He asked me out to dinner tonight but in the end stood me up — he didn't even reply to my messages.

mandarin_meaning: 放鸽子 / 爽约（未按约定出现或临时取消约会）
english_meaning: to stand someone up; to bail on plans; to not show up for a planned meeting
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，指约好见面或参加活动但未事先通知就未出现或临时爽约，令对方空等。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to fail to show up for an appointment or meeting without notice — to stand someone up or cancel/ bail on plans.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢又放我飛機，今次已經第三次喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau6 fong3 ngo5 fei1 gei1, gam1 ci3 ji5 ging1 dai6 saam1 ci3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他又放我飞机了，这已经是第三次了。
examples.english_sentence: He stood me up again; this is already the third time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好放我飛機，記得嚟啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 fong3 ngo5 fei1 gei1, gei3 dak1 lai4 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別放我飞机，记得来啊！
examples.english_sentence: Don't stand me up — remember to come!

mandarin_meaning: （口語）又……／而且……，表示並列或兼具兩種特質
english_meaning: a colloquial connective meaning 'and also' / 'moreover', used to link two qualities or clauses
explanation_mandarin: 「得嚟」是廣東話口語用法，常放在兩個形容詞、狀語或子句之間，表示兩者同時存在或並列，類似「而且、又」。有時帶有強調或出乎意料的語氣。
explanation_english: In colloquial Cantonese, '得嚟' functions as a connective particle placed between two adjectives/phrases to indicate that both qualities apply (similar to 'and also' or 'moreover'). It can also add emphasis or a slight sense of surprise.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢靚得嚟又有禮貌，大家都鍾意同佢做朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 leng3 dak1 lei4 jau6 jau5 lai5 maau6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 zung1 ji3 tung4 keoi5 zou6 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她漂亮而且有禮貌，大家都喜歡跟她做朋友。
examples.english_sentence: She's pretty and polite, so everyone likes to be her friend.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個菜甜得嚟又唔膩，好好食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 coi3 tim4 dak1 lei4 jau6 m4 ngai6, hou2 hou2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這道菜甜而不膩，很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: This dish is sweet but not cloying; very tasty.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢舖頭細得嚟齊全，買嘢都好方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 pou3 tau4 sai3 dak1 lei4 cai4 cyun4, maai5 je5 dou1 hou2 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她的店雖小卻很齊全，買東西很方便。
examples.english_sentence: Her shop is small yet well-stocked; shopping there is convenient.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）……得不得了 / 非常……（表示程度極高）
english_meaning: colloquial: 'so ... (that)' / extremely ... (used to indicate a very high degree)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 程度補語 / 副詞短語（口語）
explanation_mandarin: 「…到唔恨」是香港粵語口語用法，放在動詞或形容詞後面，表示到達極高程度，相當於普通話的「……得不得了」或「非常……」。常見於口語和年輕人口中。
explanation_english: “…dou3 m4 han6” is a colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese construction placed after a verb or adjective to indicate an extreme degree, equivalent to Mandarin "…得不得了" or English "so ... (that) / extremely ...". It is common in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢靚到唔恨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 leng3 dou3 m4 han6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她漂亮得不得了。
examples.english_sentence: She's so pretty (extremely pretty).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 條衫型到唔恨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tiu4 saam1 jing4 dou3 m4 han6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那件衣服帥到不像話。
examples.english_sentence: That outfit is insanely stylish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考到滿分，佢開心到唔恨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 dou3 mun5 fan1, keoi5 hoi1 sam1 dou3 m4 han6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考到滿分，他高興得不得了。
examples.english_sentence: He got full marks; he's so happy.

mandarin_meaning: （口语）达到某种程度／足够、彻底
english_meaning: (colloquial) to reach a certain degree; enough; completely/to the limit
explanation_mandarin: 「…到夠」是廣東話口語中常見的結構，通常跟在動詞或形容詞之後，用以強調已經到達某種程度或已經足夠、徹底，帶有完成或強調語氣。
explanation_english: "…dou3 gau3" is a colloquial Cantonese pattern attached after verbs or adjectives to emphasize that a limit/degree has been reached — i.e. something is enough, complete, or taken to the extreme.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚食到夠喇，唔好再買嘢畀我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 sik6 dou3 gau3 laa3, m4 hou2 zoi3 maai5 je5 bei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚吃够了，不要再给我买东西。
examples.english_sentence: I've eaten enough tonight; don't buy me any more.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢飲到夠，結果醉到行唔穩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jam2 dou3 gau3, git3 gwo2 zeoi3 dou3 haang4 m4 wan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他喝够了，结果醉得走路不稳。
examples.english_sentence: He drank enough and ended up so drunk he couldn't walk steadily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我行足一日，攰到夠，想瞓覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 haang4 zuk1 jat6, gui6 dou3 gau3, soeng2 fan3 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我走了一整天，累到够，想睡觉。
examples.english_sentence: I walked all day; I'm exhausted and want to sleep.

mandarin_meaning: 调皮、古灵精怪、爱搞笑
english_meaning: mischievous; playful; quirky; comically witty
explanation_mandarin: 「鬼馬」是香港粤语口语，常用来形容人性格诙谐、调皮、古灵精怪或爱搞笑，有时带亲切、调侃意味。
explanation_english: “Gwai maa” (鬼馬) is Hong Kong Cantonese slang describing someone who is playful, mischievous, quirky, or amusingly witty; often used with a fond or teasing tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日好鬼馬，成日整蠱人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hou2 gwai2 maa5, seng4 jat6 zing2 gu2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她经常很鬼马，总是捉弄别人。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is always very mischievous and constantly plays pranks on people.

mandarin_meaning: 目瞪口呆 / 傻眼
english_meaning: to be stunned or dumbfounded; jaw drops
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，用來形容因驚訝、意外或尷尬而完全愣住、說不出話來的狀態，相當於「目瞪口呆」或「傻眼」。通常帶口語色彩。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing being stunned, shocked, or left speechless (literally like one's false teeth falling out). It conveys a jaw-dropped, dumbfounded reaction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到佢唱歌嗰陣嗰啲花樣，我真係㓢咗棚牙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 keoi5 coeng3 go1 go2 zan6 go2 di1 faa1 joeng6, ngo5 zan1 hai6 zaap6 zo2 paang4 ngaa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到他唱歌時那些花樣，我真的目瞪口呆。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing the tricks he did while singing, I was really stunned.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嗰段古怪嘅故事，聽到大家都㓢咗棚牙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 go2 dyun6 gu2 gwaai3 ge3 gu3 si6, teng1 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 zaap6 zo2 paang4 ngaa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他講的那段奇怪故事，大家都聽得傻眼了。
examples.english_sentence: When he told that weird story, everyone was left dumbfounded.

mandarin_meaning: 龇牙；露出牙齒，咧嘴（通常表示憤怒、挑釁或狞笑）
english_meaning: to bare/gnash one's teeth; to grimace or show teeth (often indicating anger, hostility, or a menacing grin)
explanation_mandarin: 「㓢牙」是廣東話俚語/成語用法，與「龇牙」意思相近，指露出牙齒或咧嘴，常用以表示憤怒、挑釁、輕蔑或作勢威嚇。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term (variant of 齜/龇牙) meaning to bare or gnash one's teeth — used to show anger, hostility, contempt, or to menace someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到對方就㓢牙，睇落好嬲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 deoi3 fong1 zau6 zi1 ngaa4, tai2 lok6 hou2 nau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到對方就龇牙，看起來很生氣。
examples.english_sentence: He/She bared their teeth when they saw the other person; looked very angry.

mandarin_meaning: 嘘（表示让别人安静的拟声词，也见于「嘘寒问暖」等表示关心的用法）
english_meaning: shh; hush (an onomatopoeic interjection used to request silence); also appears in expressions about showing concern
explanation_mandarin: 「㗾／噓」是表示让别人安静的拟声词，常用于制止噪音或安抚。该字亦出现在如「嘘寒问暖」的慣用語中，表示關心慰問。
explanation_english: The character 㗾/噓 is an onomatopoeic interjection used to ask for silence (shh/hush). It can also appear in idiomatic expressions about showing concern (e.g., '嘘寒问暖').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 㗾！佢而家喺訓緊，唔好吵佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: heoi1! keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 fan3 gan2, m4 hou2 cau2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 嘘！他現在在睡覺，不要吵他。
examples.english_sentence: Shh! He's sleeping right now; don't disturb him.

mandarin_meaning: 頑皮鬼；愛搗蛋的人
english_meaning: rascal; mischievous person (playful insult for someone who is cheeky or naughty)
explanation_mandarin: 㜺鬼是廣東話口語的俗稱，用來形容頑皮、愛惡作劇或調皮搗蛋的人，語氣多半帶有調侃或親暱成分。
explanation_english: 㜺鬼 is a Cantonese colloquial slang term used to describe a mischievous or cheeky person (often a child). The tone is usually teasing or affectionate rather than seriously insulting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你呢個㜺鬼，成日都唔肯聽我講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ni1 go3 lei5 gwai2, seng4 jat6 dou1 m4 hang2 teng1 ngo5 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這個頑皮鬼，總是不肯聽我說話。
examples.english_sentence: You little rascal, you never listen to me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路㜺鬼成日搗亂，搞到屋企好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 lei5 gwai2 seng4 jat6 dou1 dou2 lyun6, gaau2 dou3 uk1 kei2 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩老是捣蛋，把家裡弄得很煩。
examples.english_sentence: The kid is always causing trouble and makes the house chaotic.

mandarin_meaning: 不詳 / 罕見詞彙（未有可靠記載）
english_meaning: Unclear / very rare Cantonese term (not well documented)
explanation_mandarin: 「㞘(䐁)底」是個非常罕見或已失傳的字詞組合，主流粵語辭典和文獻中沒有可靠或一致的解釋。可能為方言變體、古字或刻寫差異導致的罕用寫法。由於資料稀少，無法提供確切讀音與用法註釋。
explanation_english: The term "㞘(䐁)底" is an extremely rare or possibly obsolete Cantonese character combination with no reliable documentation in mainstream Cantonese references. It may be a dialectal variant, an archaic form, or a variant orthography. Due to scant evidence, precise pronunciation and usage cannot be confirmed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字㞘(䐁)底好少見，我都唔明意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 [unknown] hou2 siu2 gin3, ngo5 dou1 m4 ming4 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個字㞘(䐁)底很少見，我也不明白意思。
examples.english_sentence: The character 㞘(䐁)底 is very rare; I don't understand its meaning either.

mandarin_meaning: 戳、捅；誠摯、踏實（視語境而定）
english_meaning: to poke / to tap; earnest, sincere, dependable (sense depends on context)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 动词 / 形容词（視語境而定）
explanation_mandarin: 篤（duk1）可以表示用手指或物件輕按、戳、捅，也可表示為人踏實、誠懇、可靠（與「篤實」等複合詞相關）。
explanation_english: ‘篤’ (duk1) can mean to poke, tap, or prod with a finger or object. It can also appear in adjectives like ‘篤實’ meaning earnest, steady, or dependable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好篤我！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 duk1 ngo5!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別戳我！
examples.english_sentence: Don't poke me!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個好篤實嘅人，做嘢可靠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 hou2 duk1 sat6 ge3 jan4, zou6 je5 ho2 kaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是一個很踏實的人，做事可靠。
examples.english_sentence: He is a very dependable person; his work is reliable.

mandarin_meaning: 又臭又悶；形容空間悶熱、發臭或形容人情緒低落、悶悶不樂的狀態
english_meaning: Smelly and stuffy; describes a space that is foul and stifling or a person who is listless and sulky
explanation_mandarin: 「㤿憸腥悶」是香港粵語的粗俗口語，常用來形容房間或空氣又臭又悶，或引申形容人情緒沉悶、沒精神。多出現於非正式對話或略帶抱怨、貶義語境。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe an environment that is smelly and stuffy, or figuratively to describe someone who is gloomy and listless. It is informal and somewhat coarse, used mainly in casual complaint or derogatory contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間屋冇開窗幾日，真係㤿憸腥悶，啲空氣好唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 uk1 mou5 hoi1 coeng1 gei2 jat6, zan1 hai6 luk6 can1 seng1 mun6, di1 hung1 hei3 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間屋好幾天沒有開窗，真的又臭又悶，空氣讓人很不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: This flat hasn't had the windows opened for days — it's really smelly and stuffy; the air is uncomfortable.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見）形容人尖酸刻薄或小氣
english_meaning: (rare) describes someone sharp-tongued, petty, or mean
explanation_mandarin: 「㤿憸／淹尖」（讀作 jim1 zim1）為較罕見的粵語俗語或方言詞，常用來形容一個人尖酸刻薄、愛挑剔或小氣。此詞現代使用不普遍，屬口語／俚語範疇，地區性強。
explanation_english: '㤿憸 / 淹尖' (pronounced jim1 zim1) is a rare Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to describe someone who is sharp-tongued, petty, or mean. It is not widely used today and is regional/colloquial in nature.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做人好淹尖，成日對人指指點點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 jan4 hou2 jim1 zim1, sing4 jat6 deoi3 jan4 zi2 zi2 dim2 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為人很尖酸刻薄，總是指指點點。
examples.english_sentence: He is very sharp-tongued and petty, always criticizing others.

mandarin_meaning: 被騙、被宰（被坑）
english_meaning: to be cheated or ripped off
explanation_mandarin: 「㨘黄鱼」是香港粵語的俚語，用來形容在買賣或交易中被對方欺騙或敲詐，付了不相稱的價錢或吃虧。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning to be cheated, ripped off, or taken advantage of (usually in a transaction or purchase).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好畀佢㨘黄鱼，買嘢之前要比較價錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bei2 keoi5 ngaap3 wong4 jyu2, maai5 je5 zi1 cin4 jiu3 bei2 gaau3 gaa3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要讓他騙你，買東西之前要比較價格。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let him rip you off; compare prices before buying.

mandarin_meaning: 蹦蹦跳跳；跳来跳去
english_meaning: to hop/bounce around; to jump about energetically
explanation_mandarin: 口语拟声词，形容人或动物兴奋、活泼地跳来跳去或蹦跳。
explanation_english: A colloquial onomatopoeic expression describing someone or something energetically hopping or bouncing around with excitement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路喺公園㨢㨢跳，玩得好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 hai2 gung1 jyun4 beng6 beng6 tiu3, waan2 dak1 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子在公园里蹦蹦跳跳，玩得很开心。
examples.english_sentence: The kids are bouncing around in the park, having a great time.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見或古字（現代普通話讀音與含義不詳）
english_meaning: rare/archaic character (modern pronunciation and meaning unclear)
explanation_mandarin: 「㩋（箾）」為罕見或古字，在現代書面語與口語中極少使用。資料有限，無明確且統一的現代拼音或常用詞義。通常出現在古籍、名字或作為字形變體，日常交流中不常見。
explanation_english: The character 㩋 (variant 箾) is a rare or archaic character with very limited modern usage. Reliable information about its contemporary pronunciation and concrete meaning is scarce. It mainly appears in classical texts, proper names, or as a variant form; it is not used in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字好少見，係㩋（箾），一般唔會喺日常用到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 hou2 siu2 gin3, hai6 㩋 (箾), jat1 bun1 m4 wui5 hai2 jat6 seong4 jung6 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字很少见，是㩋（箾），一般不会在日常使用。
examples.english_sentence: This character is very rare — 㩋 (箾) — and is generally not used in daily life.

mandarin_meaning: 胡亂、敷衍、亂搞（口語俚語）
english_meaning: messing about; fooling around; doing things carelessly (slang)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 形容詞或動詞性片語
explanation_mandarin: 「㩧㩧斋」是廣東話的口語/俚語，常用來形容人做事隨便、亂搞或只是在玩弄敷衍、不認真。此詞較口語化且較罕見，常見於香港本地對話或網絡用語中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who is messing about, being sloppy, or not taking things seriously. Informal and relatively rare; typically found in Hong Kong speech or online conversations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日㩧㩧斋，做嘢真係唔夠認真。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 laap6 laap6 zaai1, zou6 je5 zan1 hai6 m4 gau3 jing6 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你總是胡亂應付，做事真的不夠認真。
examples.english_sentence: You always mess about; you're really not serious when you do things.

mandarin_meaning: 酥脆、非常脆
english_meaning: crispy; very crunchy (onomatopoeic, colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 常用于粤语口语，形容食物非常酥脆、咬下去会发出脆响的口感。亦为拟声词，书写时可见㩧㩧或卜卜。
explanation_english: A Cantonese onomatopoeic colloquial adjective used to describe food that is very crispy or crunchy — the kind that snaps or crackles when bitten.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢隻炸雞皮好㩧㩧脆，好好食！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 zaa3 gai1 pei4 hou2 bok3 bok3 ceoi3, hou2 hou2 sik6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这只炸鸡皮很酥脆，非常好吃！
examples.english_sentence: The fried chicken skin is super crispy — so tasty!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 買多一包啦，呢包薯片仲㩧㩧脆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maai5 do1 jat1 baau1 laa1, ni1 baau1 syu4 pin3 zung6 bok3 bok3 ceoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 多买一包吧，这包薯片还很酥脆。
examples.english_sentence: Buy another bag — these chips are still very crunchy.

mandarin_meaning: 嘲弄、取笑（口頭上嘲諷別人）
english_meaning: to mock or tease someone verbally; to make fun of someone
explanation_mandarin: 「㪉口」為廣東話俗語，指用言語嘲弄、挖苦或取笑他人，帶有戲謔或譏諷的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to tease, mock, or taunt someone verbally; often used for playful ribbing or sarcastic remarks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鍾意㪉口人，真係煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zung1 ji3 naau1 hau2 jan4, zan1 hai6 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天喜歡嘲弄別人，真的很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He always likes to make fun of people; it's really annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 夹；夹住；夹在中间（动词）
english_meaning: to pinch; to clamp; to press or trap between; to be caught/stuck between
explanation_mandarin: 表示用兩物件或手指把東西夾住、夾起或夾在兩者之間；口語中亦常用於描述「夾在（兩方）中間」的情況。
explanation_english: Refers to pinching or clamping something between two surfaces or fingers, or being caught/trapped between two sides. Commonly used in spoken Cantonese to describe physically clamping or being stuck between two parties.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你幫我㪉一下張紙，好唔好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 bong1 ngo5 gaap3 jat1 haa6 zoeng1 zi2, hou2 m4 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你幫我夾一下這張紙，好嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Can you help pinch/clamp this sheet of paper for me?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日夾喺兩個朋友中間，唔知點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gaap3 hai2 loeng5 go3 pang4 jau5 zung1 gaan1, m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是夾在兩個朋友之間，不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: He's always stuck between two friends and doesn't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 凑份/合伙分担（费用或责任）；分一份好处/份额
english_meaning: to chip in / to share the cost or responsibility; to take a share
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用語，指多人共同出錢或分攤費用、分擔責任，有時也用於表示分一份好處或佔一份利益。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to chip in (money) or share costs/responsibilities; can also mean to take a share of something (e.g., benefits or profits).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次買禮物我哋大家夾份出錢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 maai5 lai5 mat6 ngo5 dei6 daai6 gaa1 gaap3 fan6 ceot1 cin2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次买礼物我们大家一起凑钱吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's all chip in to buy a gift this time.

mandarin_meaning: 合夥、勾結（常含贬义）
english_meaning: to gang up; to collude; to team up (often with negative intent)
explanation_mandarin: 指幾個人串通或合夥做某事，往往帶有負面或不正當的意味（例如欺負、偷竊或陷害別人）。
explanation_english: Refers to several people joining forces or conspiring to do something, often with a negative or improper connotation (e.g., bullying, theft, or framing someone).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋夾夥偷嘢，結果俾人捉到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gaap3 fo2 tau1 je5, git3 gwo2 bei2 jan4 zuk1 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们合伙偷东西，结果被抓到。
examples.english_sentence: They teamed up to steal things and were caught.

mandarin_meaning: 被夹到手；夹住手
english_meaning: to get one's hand trapped/pinched (e.g. in a door, drawer or machine)
explanation_mandarin: 表示手被兩個物件夾住或被夾傷，常用於描述意外夾到手的情況。
explanation_english: Describes a hand being caught or pinched between objects (e.g. a door or machine). Commonly used to report an accident where someone’s hand is trapped.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小心啲，唔好畀門夾親手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 sam1 di1, m4 hou2 bei2 mun4 gaap3 can1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小心点，别让门把手夹到手。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful, don't let the door pinch your hand.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打工嘅時候唔小心畀機器夾親手，要去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 gung1 ge3 si4 hau6 m4 siu2 sam1 bei2 gei1 hei3 gaap3 can1 sau2, jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他工作時不小心被機器夾到手，要去看醫生。
examples.english_sentence: He accidentally got his hand caught in the machine at work and needs to see a doctor.

mandarin_meaning: 把東西夾住並阻擋；（口語）夾在中間擋住別人，或插隊、擠入別人中間造成阻礙
english_meaning: to wedge/sandwich and block; (colloquial) to interpose oneself and obstruct (e.g. cut in line or get in between people and block them)
explanation_mandarin: 「㪉（夾）擋」是廣東話口語，用於描述把某物夾住以致阻擋出路，或指人介入兩者之間而擋住他人。也可用來形容在排隊時插隊、擠進去佔位置的行為。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to wedge or sandwich something so that it blocks a way, or for a person to interpose between others and obstruct them. It can also be used to describe cutting into a line or squeezing into a space and blocking others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲箱夾擋咗出口，開唔到門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 soeng1 gaap3 dong2 zo2 ceot1 hau2, hoi1 m4 dou3 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些箱子夾住了出口，開不了門。
examples.english_sentence: The boxes are wedged and blocking the exit, the door won't open.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢企喺兩個人之間，夾擋住我哋講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kei5 hai2 loeng5 go3 jan4 zi1 gaan1, gaap3 dong2 zyu6 ngo5 dei6 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他站在兩個人之間，擋住我們說話。
examples.english_sentence: He stood between the two people and blocked us from talking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 排隊嘅時候唔好㪉（夾）擋，唔好插隊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: paai4 deoi2 ge3 si4 hau6 m4 hou2 gaap3 dong2, m4 hou2 caap3 deoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 排隊的時候不要夾擋，不要插隊。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cut in line while queuing; don't push in.

mandarin_meaning: 插隊；擠進隊伍或人群中
english_meaning: to cut in line; to squeeze into a queue or crowd
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語（俗語），指在排隊或人群中不按次序擠入或插入別人之間，等同於「插隊」。常帶有不禮貌或抱怨的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term meaning to insert oneself into a queue or crowd out of turn — i.e., to cut in line. Often used with a disapproving or annoyed tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好㪉檔，排緊隊㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gaap3 dong2, paai4 gan2 deoi6 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要插隊，我們在排隊。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cut in line — we're queuing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日有人㪉檔，等到好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 jau5 jan4 gaap3 dong2, dang2 dou3 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 總是有人插隊，真煩人。
examples.english_sentence: People keep cutting in line — it's so annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 串通；合谋；勾结
english_meaning: to collude; to conspire; to gang up (often to cheat or harm someone)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指兩人或多人一起密謀、串通，通常帶有欺騙或害人的意思。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to join together in a plot or collusion, often with the implication of cheating or harming someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好同佢哋一齊做嘢，驚佢哋夾計害我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 tung4 keoi5 dei6 jat1 cai4 zou6 je5, geng1 keoi5 dei6 gaap3 gai3 hoi6 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要和他們一起做事，怕他們會串通害我。
examples.english_sentence: Don't work with them; I'm afraid they'll conspire to harm me.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見粵語詞彙，無明確的權威對應詞；可能為地方口語或俗語，具體含義不詳
english_meaning: A rare/obscure Cantonese term; no well-documented meaning in standard references — likely a local colloquialism or slang with unclear definition
explanation_mandarin: 「㪠盅」在主要詞典和資料庫中極少見，缺乏權威釋義。此詞可能僅在特定圈子或地區口語中使用，語義、讀音及用法均未被普遍記錄，需本地語者補充說明或提供語料例證。
explanation_english: The term "㪠盅" is extremely rare and not attested in major dictionaries. It appears to be a local Cantonese colloquialism or slang with no widely documented meaning, pronunciation, or usage. Native speakers or corpus evidence would be needed to clarify its sense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「㪠盅」呢個字好少見，我都唔係好清楚佢嘅意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: [㪠盅: unknown] ni1 go3 zi6 hou2 siu2 gin3, ngo5 dou1 m4 hai6 hou2 cing1co2 keoi5 ge3 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「㪠盅」这个字很少见，我也不太清楚它的意思。
examples.english_sentence: '㪠盅' is a very rare word; I'm not really sure what it means either.

mandarin_meaning: 做得太过、過度反應（口語俚語）
english_meaning: to go overboard / to overreact (slang)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語動詞短語 / 俚語
explanation_mandarin: 「㷫过火屎」為廣東話俗語，形容某人做事、反應或說話太過分、過火或誇張，帶有貶義。常用於責備或提醒對方不要過分。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to describe someone who is going too far, overreacting, or being excessive. It is often used reproachfully or to warn someone not to be extreme.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好㷫过火屎，佢只係遲咗十分鐘啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 but6-gwo3-fo2-si2, keoi5 zi2 hai6 ci4 zo2 sap6 fan1 zung1 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別做得太過，他只是遲到了十分鐘而已。
examples.english_sentence: Don't go overboard — he was only ten minutes late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 討論可以，但唔好㷫过火屎變成人身攻擊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tou2 leon6 ho2 ji5, daan6 m4 hou2 but6-gwo3-fo2-si2 bin3 sing4 jan4 san1 gung1 gik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 可以討論，但不要做得太過變成人身攻擊。
examples.english_sentence: Discussion is fine, but don't overdo it and turn it into personal attacks.

mandarin_meaning: 鬧情緒、耍脾氣
english_meaning: to sulk; to be in a bad mood; to act grumpy
explanation_mandarin: 「㾓氣」為廣東話口語，指一個人心情不好、耍脾氣或鬧情緒，不太想與人互動。常用於形容短暫的鬧情緒狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to sulk or be in a bad mood—acting grumpy or throwing a brief tantrum. Used to describe someone temporarily moody and unwilling to interact.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家好㾓氣，唔想同人講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hou2 laap6 hei3, m4 soeng2 tung4 jan4 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在很鬧情緒，不想跟人說話。
examples.english_sentence: He's sulking right now and doesn't want to talk to anyone.

mandarin_meaning: 的确 / 确实
english_meaning: indeed; really; certainly
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示肯定或強調某事屬實，等同於「的確」「確實」。在廣東話書寫或網絡用語中，䃕確常用作「的確」的變體。
explanation_english: Used to affirm or emphasize that something is true or certain; equivalent to 'indeed' or 'certainly'. In Cantonese written or online usage, 䃕確 may appear as a variant spelling of 的確.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講得䃕確，冇得反駁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 dak1 dik1 kok3, mou5 dak1 faan2 pok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说得的确，没法反驳。
examples.english_sentence: What you said is indeed true; there's no way to refute it.

jyutping: ngaap1 cing1 (疑似讀音，資料罕見)
mandarin_meaning: 罕見粵語詞彙，現代用法與確切含義不明
english_meaning: A very rare/obscure Cantonese term; modern usage and exact meaning are unclear or obsolete
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 未知（罕見／可能為名詞或動詞）
explanation_mandarin: 「䅺青」一詞在主要粵語詞典與語料庫中罕見或缺乏明確記載。現存資料不足以確定標準讀音與明確語義，故在現代粵語中通常被視為罕見或過時詞彙。
explanation_english: The term "䅺青" is scarcely attested in major Cantonese dictionaries and corpora. There is insufficient evidence to determine a standard pronunciation or a definitive meaning; it is therefore treated as a rare or obsolete term in modern Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「䅺青」呢個詞好罕見，唔係日常用語，使用時要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 「ngaap1 cing1」 ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 ham5 gin3, m4 hai6 jat6 soeng4 jung6 jyu5, si3 jung6 si4 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: “䅺青”这个词很罕见，不是日常用语，使用时需谨慎。
examples.english_sentence: "䅺青" is a very rare term, not used in daily speech; be cautious when using it.

mandarin_meaning: 盯着/凝视
english_meaning: to stare; to gawk
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的擬聲詞／俗語，用來形容長時間盯着看、目不轉睛或瞪視對方。常見於口語或俚語表達。
explanation_english: A Cantonese onomatopoeic/slang expression used to describe staring or gaping at someone for a prolonged time. Common in colloquial speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度䒐䒏我，好攪笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 ding1 ding1 ngo5, hou2 gaau2 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在那裡盯着我看，真好笑。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps staring at me over there — it's kind of funny.

mandarin_meaning: 老薑；資深、有經驗的人
english_meaning: an experienced person; an old hand; a veteran
explanation_mandarin: 「䒐薑」的書寫形式較少見，可能為「老薑」（傳統寫法之一）的變體或俗寫。在廣東話口語中用來形容在某行業或某事有豐富經驗的人，相當於「老手」「資深人士」。屬非正式、口語或俗語用法。
explanation_english: The form "䒐薑" is rare and likely a variant or colloquial spelling of "老薑" (literally 'old ginger'). In Cantonese it is used informally to refer to someone experienced in a field — an old hand or veteran. Usage is informal/slang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺呢行做咗廿年，真係個䒐薑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ni1 hong4 zou6 zo2 jaa6 nin4, zan1 hai6 go3 lou5 goeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在這一行做了二十年，真是個老薑（資深人士）。
examples.english_sentence: He's worked in this industry for twenty years; he's really an old hand.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見或古字詞，據記載指各種小蟲（字形罕見，讀音與確切含義不詳）
english_meaning: An obscure/archaic term referring to various small insects (the characters are rare; pronunciation and exact meaning are uncertain).
explanation_mandarin: 「䗂蛧」由兩個罕見蟲字組成，現代漢語中極少使用。現存資料極少，通常被註為古書或字典中的罕見詞，可能用來泛指小昆蟲或雜蟲，但讀音與具體用法不明，屬於疑古或不確定詞彙。
explanation_english: The compound consists of two very rare insect characters and is almost never used in modern Chinese. Available references are scarce; it appears in some classical or lexical sources as a rare term, possibly referring generally to small insects or miscellaneous bugs. Its pronunciation and precise usage remain uncertain, so it is treated as an obscure/archaic lexical item.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有本古書提到『䗂蛧』，不過呢個詞好少見，讀音同意思唔太清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 bun2 gu2 syu1 tai4 dou3 '【讀音不詳】'，bat1 gwo3 ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 siu2 gin3，duk6 jam1 tung4 ji3 si1 m4 taai3 cing1 co2。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有本古書提到「䗂蛧」，不過這個詞很少見，讀音和意思不太清楚。
examples.english_sentence: An old book mentions '䗂蛧', but this term is rarely seen; its pronunciation and meaning are not very clear.

mandarin_meaning: 罕见词语 / 含义不明
english_meaning: Obscure/rare term — meaning unknown or not attested in major Cantonese sources
explanation_mandarin: 「䟴䟴板」一詞未見於主要粵語詞典或公開語料庫，屬於罕見或未確認的用法。字形中的「䟴」為罕見字，重疊形式可能暗示擬聲或加強語氣；「板」可作詞綴或名詞成分（如粵語中出現於某些稱謂、綽號中）。由於缺乏可靠資料，無法確定其準確讀音與確切含義，亦可能是方言、個別創造詞或筆誤。
explanation_english: The term "䟴䟴板" is not attested in major Cantonese dictionaries or corpora and appears to be an obscure or unconfirmed usage. The character 「䟴」 is rare; its reduplication may indicate an onomatopoeic or emphatic function, while 「板」 can serve as a suffix or noun element in Cantonese (e.g. in nicknames or titles). Due to lack of reliable sources, the exact pronunciation and meaning cannot be confirmed; it may be dialectal, a nonce coinage, or a misspelling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個詞「䟴䟴板」好罕見，我都唔知佢係咩意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ci4 '䟴䟴板' hou2 hon2 gin3, ngo5 dou1 m4 zi1 keoi5 hai6 me1 ji3si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个词「䟴䟴板」很罕见，我也不知道它是什么意思。
examples.english_sentence: The term '䟴䟴板' is very rare; I don't know what it means either.

mandarin_meaning: 飒飒声 / 颼颼声（風吹、樹葉摩擦或細微聲響）
english_meaning: a rustling/whistling sound (e.g., wind, leaves, or light fabric movement)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 擬聲詞（作名詞用，表示聲音）
explanation_mandarin: 「䪯䪯聲」是廣東話的擬聲詞，用來描述風聲、樹葉摩擦或細碎連續的嘶嘶、飒飒聲響，常用來形容夜間或微風時的聲音氛圍。
explanation_english: “䪯䪯聲” is a Cantonese onomatopoeia describing a rustling or whistling sound — for example wind through leaves or the soft, continuous whispering of fabric. It paints an atmospheric auditory image, often used for night or breezy scenes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚有風，窗外傳來䪯䪯聲，聽落幾寧靜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 jau5 fung1, coeng1 ngoi6 cyun4 loi4 sau1 sau1 sing1, teng1 lok3 gei2 ning4 zing6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夜里有风，窗外传来飒飒声，听起来很宁静。
examples.english_sentence: There was wind at night and a soft rustling sound came from outside the window — it sounded quite peaceful.

mandarin_meaning: 当当（拟声词，形容金属撞击或敲击发出的叮当、铿锵声）
english_meaning: An onomatopoeia for a metallic clanging/clanking sound (e.g., clang, clank, ding-dong).
explanation_mandarin: 䭦罉（又写作鐺）是粤语中的拟声词，用来模仿金属被敲击或碰撞时发出的响亮声响，常用于书面或口语描写声音效果。
explanation_english: 䭦罉 (also written 鐺) is a Cantonese onomatopoeia imitating the loud clanging or clanking sound of metal being struck or bumped. It's used in speech and writing to evoke that metallic sound effect.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚街市傳來䭦罉聲，好似有人撞到金屬嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 gaai1 si5 cyun4 loi4 dong1-dong1 sing1, hou2 ci5 jau5 jan4 zong6 dou3 gam1 suk6 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夜晚菜市场传来当当声，好像有人把金属物撞到了。
examples.english_sentence: At night the market echoed with a clanging sound, as if someone had knocked metal objects together.

jyutping: jat1 saam1 ng5 cat1 gau2, mou4 soeng1 (soeng1)
mandarin_meaning: 单身；没有配偶或伴侣（源自奇數無法配成雙）
english_meaning: single; without a partner or match (from counting odd numbers that cannot form pairs)
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語，用來形容一個人單身、沒有伴侶或沒有配對。字面來自「一三五七九」這些奇數無法配成雙，強調「無雙」的狀態。有時會在末尾加個「傷」作押韻（即「無雙傷」），語氣較口語化或帶玩笑成分。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to describe someone who is single or unmatched (has no partner). Literally refers to odd numbers '1,3,5,7,9' that cannot be paired, highlighting the 'no pair' state. Sometimes people append the character '傷' for rhyme ('mou soeng soeng'), giving a more jocular tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢到依家仲係一三五七九，無雙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dou3 ji4 gaa1 zung6 hai6 jat1 saam1 ng5 cat1 gau2, mou4 soeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他到现在还单身，没有另一半。
examples.english_sentence: He's still single up to now; he has no partner.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聖誕晚會大家都成雙入場，淨係佢一個人，我哋笑佢一三五七九無雙傷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing3 daan3 maan5 wui2 daai6 gaa1 dou1 seng4 soeng1 jap6 coeng4, zing6 hai6 keoi5 jat1 go3 jan4, ngo5 dei6 siu3 keoi5 jat1 saam1 ng5 cat1 gau2 mou4 soeng1 soeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 圣诞晚会大家都成双入场，只有他一个人，我们笑他一三五七九无双（伤）。
examples.english_sentence: At the Christmas party everyone came in pairs; only he came alone, so we teased him as 'one, three, five, seven, nine — no pair'.

mandarin_meaning: 每一個／一個個（強調群體中的每一人，常帶不滿）
english_meaning: each and every one / all of them (colloquial, often with a critical tone)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，用來強調一群人中的每一個人，常用於表示不滿、抱怨或批評，例如「一個二個都遲到」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to emphasize each member of a group, often used in complaints or criticism (e.g. "they're all late").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇吓，佢哋一個二個都遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5, keoi5 dei6 jat1 go3 ji6 go3 dou1 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看，他們一個個都遲到。
examples.english_sentence: Look, they're all late.

jyutping: jat1 go3 m4 goi1 sai2 sei2 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 只是一个，不会要命/不会致人于死（用来淡化事情的重要性或责备过度小题大做）
english_meaning: It's only one; it won't kill you (used to downplay something or scold someone for overreacting)
explanation_mandarin: 這句話是廣東話的口語說法，用來淡化某事的嚴重性或斥責對方太誇張、太小題大做，意思是「就一個而已，不會要了命的」。常用於請人嘗試或別太緊張時。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial phrase is used to downplay the seriousness of something or to reproach someone for overreacting. It literally means "it's only one, it won't kill (anyone)." Often used to tell someone to try something or not to be so worried.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁驚，試吓食一个唔该使死人啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 ging1, si3 haa5 sik6 jat1 go3 m4 goi1 sai2 sei2 jan4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別那麼怕，試著吃一個，沒事的，不會要命的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so scared — try eating one, it's fine; it won't kill you.

mandarin_meaning: 一言以蔽之 / 用一个字概括
english_meaning: In one word; to sum up briefly
explanation_mandarin: 在粤语口语中用于在一句话中把某事概括为一个字，常用于强调或引出对某事的简短评价。例如：‘一個字：正／慘／勁’。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to summarize something in a single word. Often used to emphasize or introduce a brief evaluation (e.g. 'In one word: great/awful/amazing').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套戲用一個字形容就係好睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 hei3 jung6 jat1 go3 zi6 jing4 joeng6 zau6 hai6 hou2 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部电影用一个字形容就是好看。
examples.english_sentence: This movie can be summed up in one word: entertaining.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試成績出咗，一個字：慘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 sing4 zik1 ceot1 zo2, jat1 go3 zi6: caam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考试成绩出来了，用一个字来形容：惨。
examples.english_sentence: The exam results are out — in one word: awful.

jyutping: jat1 go3 tin4 lo4 zaa3 wok6 tong1
mandarin_meaning: 比喻付出或幫助微不足道，作用不大（相當於「杯水車薪」）
english_meaning: A token effort; a drop in the ocean — something too small to make a real difference
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俗語，用來形容某人的付出或幫助太少，無法解決問題或改變局面，相當於「杯水車薪」。通常帶有貶義或諷刺意味。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe an effort or help that is so small it has no real effect — similar to 'a drop in the bucket' or 'a token effort'. Often used critically or ironically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁做只係一个田螺煠镬汤，根本幫唔到忙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 zou6 zi2 hai6 jat1 go3 tin4 lo4 zaa3 wok6 tong1, gan1 bun2 bong1 m4 dou3 mong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣做只是杯水車薪，根本幫不了忙。
examples.english_sentence: What you're doing is just a token effort; it won't help at all.

jyutping: jat1 go3 lai6 zi1 saam1 baa2 fo2
mandarin_meaning: 形容人性情火爆、容易激动或热情奔放（有时含易怒、脾气急躁之意）
english_meaning: Describes someone who is fiery-tempered, easily excited or passionately impulsive (sometimes implies quick to anger or short-tempered).
partOfSpeech_english: idiom / descriptive phrase (describing a person's temperament)
explanation_mandarin: 此短語用廣東話形容一個人個性火爆、做事衝動或熱情奔放，常帶有易怒或脾氣急躁的含義。
explanation_english: This Cantonese phrase is used to describe a person with a fiery temperament — energetic, easily excited or impulsive — often carrying the connotation of quick temper or irritability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係一個荔枝三把火，做嘢好衝但易發脾氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 lai6 zi1 saam1 baa2 fo2, zou6 je5 hou2 cung1 daan6 ji6 faat3 pei4 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她真是一个荔枝三把火，做事很冲动但容易发脾气。
examples.english_sentence: He/she really is 'one lychee three fires' — very impulsive and quick to get angry.

jyutping: jat1 go3 hin2 jat1 go3 juk6
mandarin_meaning: 各得一份；一人一份（表示公平分配或兩者對等）
english_meaning: Each gets one; one-for-one (indicating equal share or reciprocity)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面為「一個蚬一個肉」，用來形容雙方各有一份或對等分配，強調公平或一一對應。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "one clam, one piece of meat." It is used to indicate that each party gets a share or that things are one-to-one/reciprocal — emphasizing fairness or parity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次兩份獎金分得好清楚，真係一個蚬一個肉，冇人嬴多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 loeng5 fan6 zoeng2 gam1 fan1 dak1 hou2 cing1 coek3, zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 hin2 jat1 go3 juk6, mou5 jan4 jing4 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次兩份獎金分得很清楚，真的是一個蚬一個肉，沒有人贏多。
examples.english_sentence: This time the two bonuses were divided very clearly — it's truly one-for-one, nobody gets more.

mandarin_meaning: 瘦骨嶙峋的人；口語中用來形容非常瘦弱的人
english_meaning: a very skinny person; skin-and-bones (colloquial, pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 「一个骨」字面上是「一根骨頭」，在廣東話口語中用作俗稱，形容人非常瘦、少肉，看起來像只剩下骨頭。帶有非正式與輕微貶義的語氣。
explanation_english: "一个骨" literally means "one bone." In Cantonese colloquial speech it is used to describe someone extremely thin—skin-and-bones. It is informal and can be mildly derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇下佢，成日冇食嘢，真係一個骨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5 keoi5, sing4 jat6 mou5 sik6 je5, zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 gwat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看看他，整天不吃东西，真的瘦得像一根骨头。
examples.english_sentence: Look at him—he never eats. He's really just skin and bones.

jyutping: jat1 jan4 gai3 dyun2, ji6 jan4 gai3 coeng4
mandarin_meaning: 两人合计比一人更周全；集思广益
english_meaning: Two heads are better than one; collaborative thinking yields better plans
explanation_mandarin: 意思是一个人的计谋有限，两个人一起商量往往能想出更完善的办法，强调集思广益和合作的重要性。
explanation_english: The proverb says that one person's plan is limited while two people discussing can come up with better solutions. It emphasizes the value of collective wisdom and cooperation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事唔好淨係自己諗，一人計短，二人計長，等我哋一齊傾下啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei1 gin6 si6 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 zi6 gei2 lam2, jat1 jan4 gai3 dyun2, ji6 jan4 gai3 coeng4, dang2 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 king1 haa5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事不要只由你一个人决定，一人计短，二人计长，让我们一起商量一下吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't decide this by yourself; two heads are better than one — let's discuss it together.

synonyms: 三個臭皮匠，勝過一個諸葛亮

mandarin_meaning: 摔倒并翻滚（形容跌得很厉害或很狼狈）
english_meaning: to fall over and roll/tumble (usually describing a nasty or clumsy fall); can be used figuratively for a humiliating or chaotic collapse
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語成語，原指摔倒後滾動、翻滾多次，現多用來形容跌得很慘或很狼狽，有時比喻事情一敗塗地或混亂。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial idiom meaning to fall and roll repeatedly; describes a severe or humiliating tumble. It can also be used figuratively to describe a complete mess or fiasco.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢行路唔穩，結果一仆二轆跌咗落街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hang4 lou6 m4 wan2, git3 gwo2 jat1 puk1 ji6 luk6 dit3 zo2 lok6 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他走路不稳，结果一仆二轆地摔倒在街上。
examples.english_sentence: He was unsteady on his feet and ended up tumbling and rolling onto the street.

cantonese: 一代亲，二代表，三代嘴藐藐
jyutping: jat1 doi6 can1, ji6 doi6 biu2, saam1 doi6 zeoi2 miu5 miu5
mandarin_meaning: 形容家族或親屬關係隨代際推移由親密漸變為表面，到了第三代可能出現不尊重或輕視長輩的情形。
english_meaning: A Cantonese proverb describing how familial closeness often declines across generations — first generation is close, the second is more formal/representative, and by the third generation descendants may become disrespectful or contemptuous.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用來警示或感慨代際之間的親疏變化，提醒要注意教育與傳承，以免到下一代出現冷漠或不敬。
explanation_english: This saying comments on the deterioration of intergenerational closeness, warning or lamenting that without care and proper upbringing, respect and affection can fade by the third generation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日話：『一代亲，二代表，三代嘴藐藐』，我哋要好好教導細路尊敬長輩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 waa6: 'jat1 doi6 can1, ji6 doi6 biu2, saam1 doi6 zeoi2 miu5 miu5', ngo5 dei6 jiu3 hou2 hou2 gaau3 dou6 sai3 lou6 zyun1 ging3 coeng4 bui3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈常常说：「一代亲，二代表，三代嘴藐藐」，我們要好好教導孩子尊敬長輩。
examples.english_sentence: My mother often says, 'First generation close, second generation formal, third generation contemptuous' — we must teach children to respect elders.

jyutping: jat1 zak1 paa3 mou5, ji6 zak1 paa3 do1
mandarin_meaning: 一怕不够，二怕太多
english_meaning: First afraid of having too little, second afraid of having too much (i.e., worried about both shortage and excess)
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容在抉择或安排时顾虑两方面的矛盾，一方面担心不够（不足），另一方面又担心太多（过剩），常用于表达进退两难或无法取舍的情形。
explanation_english: Used to describe a dilemma where one worries about two opposite problems: either there will be too little or there will be too much. Often used to express indecision or being caught between two undesirable outcomes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新店開張，訂幾多貨好？一則怕冇，二則怕多，真係難揀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 dim3 hoi1 zoeng1, deng6 gei2 do1 fo3 hou2? jat1 zak1 paa3 mou5, ji6 zak1 paa3 do1, zan1 hai6 naan4 gaan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新店开张，订多少货好？一怕不够，二怕太多，真是难以抉择。
examples.english_sentence: When opening a new shop, how much stock should we order? One fear is it's not enough, the other that it's too much — it's really hard to decide.

mandarin_meaning: 非常長；（口語）說話或事情拖得很長、冗長
english_meaning: as long as a bolt of cloth — very long; (of speech or stories) long-winded, drawn-out
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語，形容詞/副詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 比喻很長，可以用來形容實體的長度，也常用來形容說話或敘述拖得很長、冗長。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning extremely long (literally 'as long as a bolt of cloth'). It can describe physical length or that someone/something is long-winded or drawn-out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢一匹布咁长，大家都冇晒耐性。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 jat1 pat1 bou3 gam2 coeng4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 mou5 saai3 noi6 sing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話說得很長，大家都沒耐性了。
examples.english_sentence: He talks on and on; everyone has lost patience.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 條圍巾長到一匹布咁长，可以圍晒兩圈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tiu4 wai4 gan1 coeng4 dou3 jat1 pat1 bou3 gam2 coeng4, ho2 ji5 wai4 saai3 loeng5 hyun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這條圍巾長得像一匹布那麼長，可以圍兩圈。
examples.english_sentence: The scarf is as long as a bolt of cloth — you can wrap it around twice.

mandarin_meaning: 一句话说尽 / 总之 / 简而言之
english_meaning: to sum up in one sentence; in short; to put it bluntly
explanation_mandarin: 用來把複雜或冗長的情況濃縮成一句話，常用於總結或直截了當地表達結論，語氣可以較為直接或略帶不客氣。
explanation_english: Used to condense a complex or lengthy situation into one sentence; often employed to summarize or state a conclusion bluntly. The tone can be direct and sometimes curt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 一句講晒，你唔應該再介入佢哋嘅事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat1 geoi3 gong2 saai3, nei5 m4 jing1 goi1 zoi6 gaai3 jap6 keoi5 dei6 ge3 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一句话说到底，你不应该再干预他们的事。
examples.english_sentence: To put it bluntly, you shouldn't interfere in their affairs anymore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 一句講晒，公司冇錢支持呢個計劃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat1 geoi3 gong2 saai3, gung1 si1 mou5 cin2 zi1 ci4 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一句话说到底，公司没有钱支持这个计划。
examples.english_sentence: In short, the company doesn't have the funds to support this plan.

mandarin_meaning: 一只屐（木屐）
english_meaning: a clog; a wooden shoe (one piece)
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指一只木屐（傳統的木製鞋）。在現代粵語口語中較少用，多見於書面、描述傳統文化或歷史場景時使用，也可作為指稱單隻木屐的說法。
explanation_english: Literally refers to a single wooden clog (traditional wooden shoe). It is relatively uncommon in modern spoken Cantonese and is mainly used in written language or when describing traditional/cultural or historical contexts. It denotes one clog (a single shoe).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市有間舊舖賣緊一只屐，話係古董。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 jau5 gaan1 gau6 pou3 maai6 gan2 jat1 zek3 gei3, waa6 hai6 gu2 dung2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市场有家旧店在卖一只木屐，说是古董。
examples.english_sentence: There was an old shop in the market selling a wooden clog, saying it was an antique.

jyutping: jat1 zek3 kwaai3 zi2 sik6 lin4 au2 git3 ngaan5
mandarin_meaning: 做事笨拙或用錯方法，反而害到自己或弄巧成拙
english_meaning: Doing something clumsily or with the wrong method and ending up causing trouble for oneself; making things worse for oneself
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語俗語／慣用語（描述性短語）
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面是用一只筷子去吃蓮藕會戳到眼睛，用來形容做事方法不當、笨拙或執拗，結果弄巧成拙、害到自己。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying. Literally ‘eating lotus root with one chopstick and poking the eye’; it describes doing something in an awkward, inappropriate or stubborn way that backfires or harms oneself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日一隻筷子食蓮藕，拮眼，做嘢成日失敗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 jat1 zek3 kwaai3 zi2 sik6 lin4 au2, git3 ngaan5, zou6 je5 sing4 jat6 sat1 baai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是做事笨拙、方法不對，結果常常失敗。
examples.english_sentence: He always does things the clumsy/wrong way and ends up failing.

jyutping: jat1 zek3 faai3 zi2 sik6 dau6 fu6, gaau2 zou1 saai3
mandarin_meaning: 把事情搞得一塌糊涂；把事情弄砸了
english_meaning: to mess something up completely; to botch things badly
explanation_mandarin: 比喻用不合适的办法或不熟练地去做某事，結果把事情弄得很糟或完全失敗。前半句字面是「用一根筷子吃豆腐」，形容方法不當或笨拙；後半句表示結果很糟糕。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase likening an ill-suited or clumsy attempt (literally 'eating tofu with one chopstick') to producing a completely ruined or botched result ("mess it up"). It describes doing something with the wrong method or lacking skill and ending up with a disaster.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一拎手就想自己整，結果一只筷子食豆腐，搞𱟽晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 ling2 sau2 zau6 soeng2 zi6 gei2 zing2, git3 gwo3 jat1 zek3 faai3 zi2 sik6 dau6 fu6, gaau2 zou1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一開始就想自己做，結果把事情弄得一塌糊涂。
examples.english_sentence: He tried to do it himself from the start, but ended up completely messing it up.

mandarin_meaning: 要不是…的話；否則
english_meaning: if not; otherwise; unless
explanation_mandarin: 一唔係嘅話是廣東話的口語連接短語，用於引出如果前項條件不成立時會發生的後果，相當於普通話的「否則」或「要不是⋯的話」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese connective used to introduce the consequence or alternative when the preceding condition does not hold; equivalent to 'otherwise' or 'if not'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你快啲呀，一唔係嘅話我哋會遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 faai3 di1 aa3, jat1 m4 hai6 ge3 waa6 ngo5 dei6 wui5 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你快點，否則我們會遲到。
examples.english_sentence: Hurry up, otherwise we'll be late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出門前鎖好門，一唔係嘅話可能會有危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 mun4 cin4 so2 hou2 mun4, jat1 m4 hai6 ge3 waa6 ho2 nang4 wui5 jau5 ngai4 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出門前把門鎖好，否則可能會有危險。
examples.english_sentence: Lock the door before you go out, otherwise there might be danger.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你應該準時交功課，一唔係嘅話老師會扣分。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jing1 goi1 zeon2 si4 gaau1 gung1 fo3, jat1 m4 hai6 ge3 waa6 lou5 si1 wui5 kau3 fan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你應該準時交作業，否則老師會扣分。
examples.english_sentence: You should hand in your homework on time, otherwise the teacher will deduct points.

mandarin_meaning: 一堆胡說／無聊的東西
english_meaning: a load of nonsense; meaningless talk
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，用來形容胡說、沒意義的話或無用的東西，有時帶貶義。
explanation_english: A colloquial slang term used to describe nonsense, meaningless talk, or something useless; often derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好聽佢講一嚿云，佢淨係想整蠱你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 teng1 keoi5 gong2 jat1 gau3 wan4, keoi5 zing6 hai6 soeng2 zing2 gu2 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別聽他說那些胡說，他只是想捉弄你。
examples.english_sentence: Don't listen to him spouting nonsense; he's just trying to mess with you.

mandarin_meaning: 一块饭；一份饭；（口语）谋生、糊口的一份收入/生计
english_meaning: a portion of rice; a meal; (colloquial) a livelihood / something one earns to make a living
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词（可作实词，口语亦可指生计）
explanation_mandarin: 「一嚿饭」字面上指一块或一份煮熟的米饭（量词「嚿」為粤语口语用法）。口语中常用作比喻，表示一份饭吃、谋生收入或生计，例如「搵一嚿饭食」表示靠某种工作谋生。
explanation_english: Literally 'a lump/portion of rice' (嚿 is a Cantonese classifier). It can mean a single meal or portion of rice. Colloquially it is used metaphorically to mean one's livelihood or earnings (e.g. 'to earn a living').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係靠打零工搵一嚿飯食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 kaau3 daa2 ling4 gung1 wan2 jat1 gau3 faan6 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只是靠打零工谋生。
examples.english_sentence: He only makes a living doing odd jobs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 晚餐有一嚿飯、一碗湯同埋一碟菜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maan5 caan1 jau5 jat1 gau3 faan6, jat1 wun2 tong1 tung4 maai4 jat1 dip6 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚餐有一份饭、一碗汤和一盘菜。
examples.english_sentence: Dinner had a portion of rice, a bowl of soup, and a plate of vegetables.

mandarin_meaning: 象征性或假装流的一点眼泪（用于博取同情）
english_meaning: a token/feigned tear — a symbolic or fake tear meant to elicit sympathy
explanation_mandarin: 「一壳眼泪」多用于粤语口语，指流得很少或是假装流的眼泪，通常是为了博取他人同情或达到某种目的。
explanation_english: In Cantonese colloquial use, this phrase refers to a very small or feigned tear — usually shed symbolically to gain sympathy or achieve some aim.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係流咗一壳眼泪，就想博人同情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 lau4 zo2 jat1 hok3 ngaan5 leoi6, zau6 soeng2 bok3 jan4 tung4 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只是流了一点象征性的眼泪，就想博取别人的同情。
examples.english_sentence: He only shed a token tear, trying to win people's sympathy.

jyutping: jat1 cyu3 hoeng1 cyun1 jat1 cyu3 lei6
mandarin_meaning: 各地风俗各不相同；各处有各处的规矩。
english_meaning: Each village has its own customs; customs and rules vary from place to place.
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示不同地方有不同的風俗習慣和規矩，勸人尊重當地習俗或不要以一概全。
explanation_english: Used to say that different places have different customs and rules; it advises respecting local practices and not assuming uniformity everywhere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 去旅行要尊重當地嘅習俗，一處鄉村一處例，唔好強行改變人哋做事嘅方式。
examples.jyutping_sentence: heoi3 leoi5 hang4 jiu3 zyun1 zung6 dong1 dei6 ge3 zaap6 zuk6, jat1 cyu3 hoeng1 cyun1 jat1 cyu3 lei6, m4 hou2 koeng4 hang4 goi2 bin3 jan4 dei6 zou6 si6 ge3 fong1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去旅行要尊重当地的习俗，一处乡村一处例，不要强行改变别人的做事方式。
examples.english_sentence: When travelling, respect local customs—each village has its own rules; don't force others to change how they do things.

mandarin_meaning: （口语）大约一个半月 / 一个多月
english_meaning: Cantonese colloquial expression meaning about one and a half months (roughly a little over one month).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 时间短语（名词短语/口语量词短语）
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语用法，用来表示大约一个半月或一个多月的时间长度，带有近似、非精确的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to indicate an approximate duration of about one and a half months (or a little over one month). It conveys an approximate, non-exact length of time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢返嚟香港已經有一头半個月喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faan1 lai4 hoeng1 gong2 ji5 ging1 jau5 jat1 tau4 bun3 go3 jyut6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他回香港已经有一个半月了。
examples.english_sentence: He's been back in Hong Kong for about a month and a half.

mandarin_meaning: 一下子 / 一齐 / 同时
english_meaning: all at once; simultaneously; in one go
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示事情在同一時間發生或一下子全部發生，等同於「一下子」「一齊」「同時」。較隨便非書面語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression indicating that something happens all at once or simultaneously. Equivalent to "all at once" or "in one go." Informal usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋一头烟走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 jat1 tau4 jin1 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们一下子都跑走了。
examples.english_sentence: They all ran off at once.

mandarin_meaning: 完全不明白；感到困惑
english_meaning: completely confused; at a loss; having no idea what's going on
explanation_mandarin: 形容對事情或情況完全不清楚、感到迷糊或困惑。
explanation_english: Describes being completely puzzled or confused about a situation; having no clear understanding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽完老師講解，我仍然一頭霧水，唔知佢講緊乜嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 jyun4 lou5 si1 gong2 gaai2, ngo5 jing4 jin4 jat1 tau4 mou6 seoi2, m4 zi1 keoi5 gong2 gan2 mat1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听完老师讲解，我还是一头雾水，不知道他在讲什么。
examples.english_sentence: After listening to the teacher's explanation, I'm still totally confused and don't know what he's talking about.

mandarin_meaning: 一目了然 / 非常明显、很容易理解
english_meaning: very obvious; perfectly clear; ridiculously simple
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容事情、问题或答案很简单、非常明显，一眼就看得出来（粤语口语用法）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to say something is extremely simple or obvious — clear at a glance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事一字咁浅，唔使諗咁多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 jat1 zi6 gam2 cin2, m4 sai2 lam2 gam2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事一目了然，不用想那么多。
examples.english_sentence: This matter is obvious; no need to overthink it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條題好簡單，一字咁浅，人人都答到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 tai4 hou2 gaan2 daan1, jat1 zi6 gam2 cin2, jan4 jan4 dou1 daap3 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这道题很简单，一目了然，人人都能答出来。
examples.english_sentence: This question is very simple — it's obvious, everyone can answer it.

jyutping: jat1 gaa1 bin6 ji4 loeng5 gaa1 zoek3 sou3
mandarin_meaning: 一方讓利，兩方受益
english_meaning: When one party makes a concession or gets a bargain, two parties benefit
explanation_mandarin: 表示某一方讓利或吃小虧，結果讓兩方或多方同時得到好處，常用來形容互利的交易或安排。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiom meaning that when one party gives a concession or takes a small loss, two parties (or multiple parties) end up benefiting. Used to describe mutually beneficial deals or arrangements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家商場做緊買一送一嘅優惠，大家都開心，一家便宜兩家着數。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 soeng1 coeng4 zou6 gan2 maai5 jat1 sung3 jat1 ge3 jau1 wai6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hoi1 sam1, jat1 gaa1 bin6 ji4 loeng5 gaa1 zoek3 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在商場在做買一送一的優惠，大家都很高興——一方便宜，兩方受益。
examples.english_sentence: The mall is running a buy-one-get-one promotion now; everyone's happy — one side gets a bargain and both sides benefit.

mandarin_meaning: 全家大小；全家人（年紀大小都有）
english_meaning: the whole family; everyone in the family (young and old)
explanation_mandarin: 表示一家人全部成員，含有老幼皆在的意思，常用於口語。
explanation_english: Refers to all members of a family (including both young and old); a colloquial expression used to indicate the entire household.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聖誕節我哋一家大細都返老家。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing3 daan3 zit3 ngo5 dei6 jat1 gaa1 daai6 sai3 dou1 faan1 lou5 gaa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 圣诞节我们全家人都回老家。
examples.english_sentence: At Christmas our whole family goes back to our hometown.

mandarin_meaning: 親力親為；親手親腳，親自動手做
english_meaning: to do something personally/by oneself; hands-on; single-handedly
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話成語，表示親自用手腳去做或親手操辦某事，不依賴他人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiom meaning to do something personally with one's own hands (and feet); to handle or manage something oneself rather than relying on others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一手一脚整哂間屋，唔使請人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 sau2 jat1 goek3 zing2 saai3 gaan1 uk1, m4 sai2 cing2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一手一脚把房子全部修好了，不需要請人。
examples.english_sentence: He renovated the whole house by himself; he didn't need to hire anyone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽咪嫌屋企亂，佢就一手一脚收拾晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 mi1 jim4 uk1 kei2 lyun6, keoi5 zau6 jat1 sau2 jat1 goek3 sau1 sap6 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽覺得家裡很亂，他就親自把家裡收拾好。
examples.english_sentence: Mom thought the house was messy, so he tidied it up himself.

mandarin_meaning: 一個接一個地翻滾或跌倒；連續滾落或相繼倒下（口語、擬聲）
english_meaning: to tumble/roll one after another; to fall in succession (colloquial, onomatopoeic)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容人或物件連續翻滾或相繼跌倒，帶有擬聲感，多用於粵語口語中，形象地表現動作連續且凌亂。
explanation_english: An onomatopoeic colloquial Cantonese phrase describing people or objects tumbling, rolling, or falling one after another; conveys a continuous, messy motion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲小朋友喺草地上玩，一扑一辘咁滾落，唔覺意跌親幾個。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 siu2 pang4 jau5 hai2 cou2 dei6 soeng6 waan2, jat1 pok3 jat1 luk6 gam2 gwan2 lok6, m4 gok3 ji3 dit3 can1 gei2 go3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友在草地上玩耍，一個接一個地滾下來，不小心摔著了好幾個。
examples.english_sentence: The kids were playing on the grass and tumbled down one after another; several of them accidentally fell.

mandarin_meaning: 一拍两散（表示双方关系或合作立即终止，各自分开）
english_meaning: to part ways immediately; to break up or split up abruptly
explanation_mandarin: 形容雙方（如情侶、合夥人、交涉各方）關係或合作在短時間內徹底結束，各自分開，互不聯絡或合作。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where parties (e.g. lovers, partners, negotiating sides) abruptly end their relationship or cooperation and go their separate ways, often with no further contact.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 經過嗰次爭執之後，佢哋就一拍兩散，之後冇再聯絡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging1gwo3 go2 ci3 zang1zik1 zi1hau6, keoi5dei6 zau6 jat1 paak3 loeng5 saan3, zi1hau6 mou5 zoi3 lyun4lok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 经过那次争执之后，他们就一拍两散，之后再也没有联络。
examples.english_sentence: After that argument, they immediately parted ways and never contacted each other again.

jyutping: jat1 man4 cin2 daai6 gwo3 bo3 gei1
mandarin_meaning: 因一點微小的錢或利益而自鳴得意、沾沾自喜
english_meaning: To be smug or boastful over a trivial amount of money; to take undue pride in a small sum
explanation_mandarin: 形容為了一點很少的錢或小利而覺得了不起、得意或吹噓，通常帶有貶義，形象地把一文錢說成比簸箕還“大”。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is proud or boastful about a very small amount of money or trivial gain; used pejoratively to mock petty pride.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢攞咗十蚊就一文钱大过簸箕，成日喺人面前講自己有錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lo2 zo2 sap6 man1 zau6 jat1 man4 cin2 daai6 gwo3 bo3 gei1, sing4 jat6 hai2 jan4 min6 cin4 gong2 zi6 gei2 jau5 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他拿到十塊錢就自鳴得意，整天在別人面前說自己有錢。
examples.english_sentence: He got ten dollars and immediately acted proud, always bragging in front of others that he's rich.

jyutping: jat1 gan1 gai1 sap6 ng5 loeng5 coeng2
mandarin_meaning: 表面看似有分量但實際可用/有價值的部分很少（徒有其表、華而不實）
english_meaning: Literally 'one catty of chicken, fifteen taels of intestines' — describes something that looks substantial but has little useful substance; hollow/poor quality
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容事物或人外表看似很多或很有價值，但實際有用的部分很少，或充滿無用、累贅的部分。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to describe something that appears abundant or valuable but actually contains little worthwhile material — more waste than substance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰隻雞真係一斤雞十五兩腸，冇乜肉得啲腸同骨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zek3 gai1 zan1 hai6 jat1 gan1 gai1 sap6 ng5 loeng5 coeng2, mou5 mat1 juk6 dak1 di1 coeng2 tung4 gwat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那只鸡真是一斤鸡十五两肠，几乎没有肉，只有肠和骨头。
examples.english_sentence: That chicken is really 'one catty chicken, fifteen taels of intestines' — there's hardly any meat, mostly intestines and bones.

cantonese: 一日省一口，一年剩一斗
jyutping: jat1 jat6 saang2 jat1 hau2, jat1 nin4 zing6 jat1 dau2
mandarin_meaning: 一天省下一口（吃），一年可剩下一斗——積少成多，強調小的節省或累積會變成大的收穫
english_meaning: Save a mouthful a day and you'll have a bushel at year's end — small savings add up; little by little accumulates into a lot.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用形象的比喻說明：每天節省一點（例如一口飯或一點錢），長久下來就能積累成可觀的成果，常用來鼓勵節儉或強調積少成多的道理。
explanation_english: A proverb that uses a vivid image to show that saving a little each day (e.g., a mouthful or a small amount of money) will accumulate into a substantial amount over time; used to encourage thrift and illustrate that small efforts add up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好睇少每一筆細細嘅開支，一日省一口，一年剩一斗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 tai2 siu2 mui5 jat1 bat1 sai3 sai3 ge3 hoi1 zi1, jat1 jat6 saang2 jat1 hau2, jat1 nin4 zing6 jat1 dau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要小看每一筆微小的開銷，一日省一口，一年剩一斗。
examples.english_sentence: Don't underestimate each small expense; save a mouthful a day, and you'll have a bushel in a year.

mandarin_meaning: 一会儿；暂时；短时间
english_meaning: for a short while; temporarily; a little while
explanation_mandarin: 表示時間短暫、暫時或一會兒，不指很長的時間。原本字面上可解作“一小时三刻”，但現代口語通常作“短時間”的意思。
explanation_english: Indicates a brief period of time or something that will only last for a short while. Historically could be read literally, but in modern usage it functions as an idiom meaning a short/temporary time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你等我一時三刻，馬上返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dang2 ngo5 jat1 si4 saam1 hak1, maa5 soeng5 faan1 lei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你等我一会儿，我马上回来。
examples.english_sentence: Wait for me for a little while; I'll be back soon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔會耽誤你太耐，只係一時三刻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 wui5 daam1 ng6 nei5 taai3 noi6, zi2 hai6 jat1 si4 saam1 hak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不会耽误你太久，只是一会儿。
examples.english_sentence: I won't keep you long; it's just for a short while.

mandarin_meaning: 暂时；偶尔；一会儿
english_meaning: temporarily; for a short while; occasionally
explanation_mandarin: 表示事情发生的频率不固定，或只持续一段短时间。多为口语用法，常用于粤语中表示“有时、偶尔”或“短暂地”。
explanation_english: Indicates that something happens occasionally or only for a short period. Colloquial Cantonese expression used to mean 'sometimes' or 'for a little while'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我一時半時會返屋企食飯，唔係成日都喺公司食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 si4 bun3 si4 wui5 faan1 uk1 kei5 sik6 faan6, m4 hai6 sing4 jat6 dou1 hai2 gung1 si1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我有时会回家吃饭，不是总在公司吃。
examples.english_sentence: I sometimes go home to eat; I'm not always eating at the office.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲嘢一時半時有，唔需要太擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 je5 jat1 si4 bun3 si4 jau5, m4 seoi1 jiu3 taai3 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些东西时有时无，不需要太担心。
examples.english_sentence: These things come and go sometimes; you don't need to worry too much.

jyutping: jat1 si4 m4 tau1 gai1 zou6 bou2 zoeng2
mandarin_meaning: 暂时不占小便宜，装作正人君子/当起道德标杆（通常含讽刺）
english_meaning: to temporarily stop doing petty, opportunistic things and pretend to be righteous/a moral authority (usually ironic)
explanation_mandarin: 形容某人平时有小聪明或占小便宜，但暂时装作正经、当道德或权威的样子，常带讽刺意味。
explanation_english: Describes someone who normally engages in petty opportunism but temporarily acts righteous or like a moral authority—usually said ironically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢平時成日偷雞，依家一時唔偷雞做保長，成日同我哋講道理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ping4 si4 seng4 jat6 tau1 gai1, ji1 gaa1 jat1 si4 m4 tau1 gai1 zou6 bou2 zoeng2, seng4 jat6 tung4 ngo5 dei6 gong2 dou6 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他平时总是占小便宜，現在却暂时装作正人君子、当起保长来，整天给我们讲大道理。
examples.english_sentence: He usually always takes little advantages, but now he's temporarily pretending to be righteous/a moral authority and keeps preaching to us.

mandarin_meaning: 有時候、偶爾
english_meaning: sometimes; occasionally
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用法，表示事情不常發生、偶爾會發生，等同於普通話的「有時候」或「偶爾」。常見於香港日常會話。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese adverb meaning occasionally or sometimes. Used in everyday Hong Kong Cantonese to indicate that something happens from time to time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我一时时會去旺角買嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 si4 si4 wui5 heoi3 wong6 gok3 maai5 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我有時會去旺角買東西。
examples.english_sentence: I sometimes go to Mong Kok to buy things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一时时唔記得帶鎖匙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 si4 si4 m4 gei3 dak1 daai3 so2 si4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他有時會忘記帶鑰匙。
examples.english_sentence: He sometimes forgets to bring his keys.

mandarin_meaning: 一是（用於列舉原因或理由，相當於「首先」）
english_meaning: firstly; first of all (used to list reasons or points)
explanation_mandarin: 「一是」常與「二是」連用，用來列舉原因或理由，表示第一個要點或第一個原因，語氣偏正式或書面。
explanation_english: "一是" is typically used with "二是" to list reasons or points. It introduces the first reason or point and is often used in more formal or written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔去，一是太忙，二是想休息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 heoi3, jat1 si6 taai3 mong4, ji6 si6 soeng2 jau1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不去，一是太忙，二是想休息。
examples.english_sentence: I'm not going: firstly I'm too busy, secondly I want to rest.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢答唔到，一是冇準備，二是亂估答案。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daap3 m4 dou2, jat1 si6 mou5 zeon2 bei6, ji6 si6 lyun6 gu2 daan6 ngon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他答不出來，一是沒準備，二是亂猜答案。
examples.english_sentence: He couldn't answer; first he didn't prepare, second he randomly guessed the answer.

mandarin_meaning: 一次性完成；一口气
english_meaning: in one go; all at once; in one continuous effort
explanation_mandarin: 表示在一次、不間斷的情況下完成某動作或事情，相當於普通話的「一口氣」或「一次性」。屬於口語用法，多見於廣東話。
explanation_english: Indicates completing an action or doing something in one continuous effort — equivalent to Mandarin '一口气' or English 'in one go / all at once'. Colloquial Cantonese usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我一條氣做晒啲工，宜家可以休息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 tiu4 hei3 zou6 saai3 di1 gung1, ji4 gaa1 ho2 ji5 jau1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我一次把工作做完，現在可以休息。
examples.english_sentence: I finished the work all in one go, now I can rest.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一條氣講晒佢所有嘢，冇畀人插嘴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 tiu4 hei3 gong2 saai3 keoi5 so2 jau5 je5, mou5 bei2 jan4 caap3 zeoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一次把所有話都說完了，沒讓別人插嘴。
examples.english_sentence: He talked through everything in one go, without letting others interrupt.

cantonese: 一条锁匙唔闻声，两条锁匙铃铃响
jyutping: jat1 tiu4 so2 si4 m4 man4 seng1, loeng5 tiu4 so2 si4 ling4 ling4 hoeng2
mandarin_meaning: 一个人知道可以保守秘密，两个人知道就容易传开
english_meaning: A secret kept by one person stays quiet; once a second person knows, it quickly spreads.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話諺語用鎖匙比喻秘密，意思是只有一個人知道的事情可以保密，但一旦有第二個人知道，就可能被洩露或傳開。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb uses keys as a metaphor for secrets: one person can keep a secret, but once a second person knows, it is likely to be revealed or spread.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事你唔好同其他人講，一条锁匙唔闻声，两条锁匙铃铃响。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 nei5 m4 hou2 tung4 kei4 taa1 jan4 gong2, jat1 tiu4 so2 si4 m4 man4 seng1, loeng5 tiu4 so2 si4 ling4 ling4 hoeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事你不要告诉别人，一个人知道可以保密，两个人知道就会传开。
examples.english_sentence: Don't tell others about this — a secret kept by one person stays quiet, but with two people it gets out.

jyutping: jat1 joeng6 mai5 joeng5 baak3 joeng6 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 同样的条件会造就出性格、兴趣和行为各不相同的人（俗语：一样的米养出百样人）。
english_meaning: Literally 'the same rice feeds a hundred kinds of people' — people raised or given the same conditions can turn out very differently; everyone has different tastes, temperaments, and choices.
explanation_mandarin: 用来说明即使在相同的环境或条件下成长，人们也会因为性格、兴趣或选择不同而表现各异，强调个体差异。
explanation_english: An idiom used to point out that even under the same circumstances or upbringing, people will develop differently — highlighting individual differences in personality, tastes, and choices.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 就算係同一個家庭長大，一樣米養百樣人，大家都有唔同嘅興趣同選擇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zau6 syun3 hai6 tung4 jat1 go3 gaa1 ting4 coeng4 daai6, jat1 joeng6 mai5 joeng5 baak3 joeng6 jan4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 jau5 m4 tung4 ge3 hing3 ceoi3 tung4 syun2 zaak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 即使在同一个家庭长大，一样米养百样人，每个人都有不同的兴趣和选择。
examples.english_sentence: Even if people grow up in the same family, the same rice feeds a hundred kinds of people — everyone has different interests and choices.

mandarin_meaning: 一下子就熟悉 / 一見如故
english_meaning: to hit it off immediately; to become familiar/comfortable after one meeting
explanation_mandarin: 「一次熟」是香港粵語口語用法，指與人第一次見面或短時間內就變得很熟絡、容易相處、很快打成一片。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used in Hong Kong meaning to become familiar or comfortable with someone immediately (to hit it off after one meeting).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋第一次見面已經一次熟，傾得好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 dai6 jat6 ci3 gin3 min6 ji5 ging1 jat1 ci3 suk6, king1 dak1 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們第一次見面就一下子很熟，聊得很開心。
examples.english_sentence: We hit it off right away the first time we met; we had a great conversation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新同事好快就一次熟，成日約埋一齊食晏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 tung4 si6 hou2 faai3 zau6 jat1 ci3 suk6, seng4 jat6 joek3 maai4 jat1 cai4 sik6 ngaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新同事很快就熟絡，經常約在一起吃午飯。
examples.english_sentence: The new colleagues bonded quickly and often go out for lunch together.

cantonese: 一次起，两次止，三次唔使指拟
jyutping: jat1 ci3 hei2, loeng5 ci3 zi2, saam1 ci3 m4 sai2 zi2 ji5
mandarin_meaning: 第一次可原諒，第二次要阻止，第三次就不用再提醒（直接處理）
english_meaning: Forgive it the first time, stop it the second time, and by the third time no need to be told — take action or don't tolerate it anymore.
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，用來表達對某種行為的容忍有次序：第一次可寬容，第二次應該制止，第三次則不再需要提醒，通常會直接採取行動或處罰。
explanation_english: A colloquial proverb advising a graduated response to repeated behavior: tolerate once, warn or stop on the second occurrence, and by the third occurrence no further warning is necessary — action or punishment is implied.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日遲到，記住一次起，兩次止，三次唔使指拟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 ci4 dou3, gei3 zyu6 jat1 ci3 hei2, loeng5 ci3 zi2, saam1 ci3 m4 sai2 zi2 ji5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要經常遲到，記住：第一次可原諒，第二次要制止，第三次就不用再提醒了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be late all the time. Remember: forgive once, stop the second time, and by the third time you don't need to be told.

synonyms: 一次可原諒，兩次警告，三次不再容忍
第一次容忍，第二次警告，第三次採取行動

mandarin_meaning: 一会儿/一段时间；一排（一列）
english_meaning: a while / a period of time; a row / a line
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词/量词短语（表示时间或排列）
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法。常用來表示一段不長的時間，相當於普通話的“一會兒/一陣子”；也可用作名詞，表示排列成一列的東西（即“一排”）。“一牌”有時作為俗寫與“一排”通用。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression. Commonly used to mean 'a while' or 'a period of time' (similar to Mandarin '一会儿/一阵子'); it can also refer to objects arranged in a row ('a row/line'). The variant '一牌' is sometimes used informally in writing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺門口等咗一排都未有人出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 mun4 hau2 dang2 zo2 jat1 paai4 dou1 mei6 jau5 jan4 ceot1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在门口等了好一会儿都没有人出来。
examples.english_sentence: I waited at the door for quite a while but nobody came out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 杯仔排成一排，睇落好整齊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bui1 zai2 paai4 seng4 jat1 paai4, tai2 lok6 hou2 zing2 cai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 杯子排成一排，看起來很整齊。
examples.english_sentence: The cups are arranged in a row; they look very neat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲人會寫作「一牌」，其實都係一樣意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 jan4 wui5 se2 zok3 "jat1 paai4", kei4 sat6 dou1 hai6 jat1 joeng6 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些人會寫作「一牌」，其實都是一樣的意思。
examples.english_sentence: Some people write it as '一牌', but actually it's the same meaning.

synonyms: 一會兒 / 一會 (yat1 wui5 / yi1 hui4)

cantonese: 一物治亦无，糯米治木虱
jyutping: jat1 mat6 zi6 jik6 mou4, no6 mai5 zi6 muk6 sat1
mandarin_meaning: 没有一种办法适用于所有情况；有时简单或奇特的偏方反而管用。
english_meaning: There is no one-size-fits-all remedy; sometimes a simple or odd fix works.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，意指並非所有問題都能用同一方法解決；在不同情況下要對症下藥，有時看似奇怪或樸素的方法反而有效。此語帶有民間智慧與實用主義色彩，來源多為口語俗談，具體出處不詳。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb meaning not every problem can be solved with the same method; one must apply the appropriate remedy case by case. Sometimes seemingly odd or simple solutions work. It reflects folk wisdom and practical thinking; exact origin is unclear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 處理呢啲老問題，唔可以淨係用一招，一物治亦无，糯米治木虱，要試唔同辦法先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyu3 lei5 ni1 di1 lou5 man6 tai4, m4 ho2 ji5 zing6 hai6 jung6 jat1 ziu1, jat1 mat6 zi6 jik6 mou4, no6 mai5 zi6 muk6 sat1, jiu3 si3 m4 tung4 baan6 faat3 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 处理这些老问题，不能只用一招，没有放之四海而皆准的方法，有时要尝试不同办法才行。
examples.english_sentence: Dealing with these long-standing problems can't be done with just one trick; there's no universal cure—sometimes you have to try different methods.

jyutping: jat1 gau2 fai3 jing4, baak3 gau2 fai3 seng1
mandarin_meaning: 人云亦云 / 一人发声，众人附和（众人跟随附和、盲从的现象）
english_meaning: One voice prompts many to echo — a bandwagon/herd-mentality effect where people mindlessly follow or pile on after an initial criticism or rumor.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻一個人先發聲批評或造謠，隨即很多人跟著附和、跟風，缺乏獨立判斷。
explanation_english: An expression describing how one person's criticism or rumor can trigger many others to echo or join in, showing herd mentality or blind agreement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新聞揭發咗一件事，起初只有一個人講，一狗吠形，百狗吠声，之後成班人都跟住鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 man4 kit3 faat3 zo2 jat1 gin6 si6, hei2 co1 zi2 jau5 jat1 go3 jan4 gong2, jat1 gau2 fai3 jing4, baak3 gau2 fai3 seng1, zi1 hau6 sing4 baan1 jan4 dou1 gan1 zyu6 naau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新闻揭发了一件事，起初只有一个人说，结果一人发声，众人附和，后来一群人都跟着骂他。
examples.english_sentence: A news story exposed something; at first only one person spoke up, but one voice led many to echo it — later a crowd joined in attacking him.

cantonese: 一生儿女债，半世老婆奴
jyutping: jat1 saang1 ji4 neoi5 zaai3, bun3 sai3 lou5 po4 nou4
mandarin_meaning: 一生為孩子負擔，半生做老婆的‘奴才’（形容婚姻與養育責任的沉重與屈從）
english_meaning: A life of debts to children, half a life as a wife's 'slave' — a cynical saying about lifelong parental responsibilities and being subservient in marriage.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語／成語式短語（名詞性短語）
explanation_mandarin: 這句話是俚語／諷刺語，形容一個人一輩子要為養育兒女承擔責任（像欠債一樣），而婚姻生活中又像成為老婆的‘奴隸’，帶有自嘲或對婚姻/家庭負擔的悲觀色彩。
explanation_english: A colloquial, often cynical saying that describes how a person spends their life bearing the burdens of raising children (like a debt) and spends a large part of life subservient to their wife. It is typically used jokingly or with pessimistic critique of marriage and family responsibilities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢每次講起養仔女嘅負擔都會話：「一生儿女债，半世老婆奴」，所以佢好驚結婚。
