examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mui5 ci3 gong2 hei2 joeng5 zai2 neoi5 ge3 fu6 daam1 dou1 wui5 waa6: "jat1 saang1 ji4 neoi5 zaai3, bun3 sai3 lou5 po4 nou4", so2 ji5 keoi5 hou2 ging1 git3 fan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他每次談到養孩子的負擔都會說：「一生兒女債，半世老婆奴」，所以他很怕結婚。
examples.english_sentence: Every time he talks about the burden of raising children he says, "A lifetime of debts to children, half a life a wife's slave," so he's afraid of getting married.

cantonese: 一百岁唔死都有新闻听
jyutping: jat1 baak3 seoi3 m4 sei2 dou1 jau5 san1 man4 teng1
mandarin_meaning: 活到一百歲也會有新聞可聽（比喻總有八卦/話題）
english_meaning: You'll have news to listen to even if you live to 100 (i.e., there will always be gossip/news; scandals never stop)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面意思是就算活到一百歲也不會缺新聞可聽。用來形容某人或某件事總會有八卦、話題或新聞，持續不斷。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning 'even if (someone) lives to 100 without dying, there will still be news to hear.' It describes situations or people that will always generate gossip or news — scandals/topics that never run out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做啲出位嘅嘢，將來一百歲唔死都有新聞聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zou6 di1 ceot1 wai6 ge3 je5, zoeng1 loi4 jat1 baak3 seoi3 m4 sei2 dou1 jau5 san1 man4 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常做些出格的事，將來活到一百歲也會有新聞可以聽。
examples.english_sentence: He often does outrageous things; even if he lives to 100, there will still be news about him.

mandarin_meaning: （飲茶點心）一盅茶和兩件點心
english_meaning: One cup/pot of tea and two dim sum items (a typical simple dim sum order)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語飲茶文化中的術語，字面意思為「一盅茶、兩件點心」，常用於點心店或酒樓表示一份簡單的飲茶點餐。有時也泛指簡單的一頓點心或少量食物。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term from yum cha (dim sum) culture meaning literally 'one cup/pot of tea and two dim sum pieces'. Used when ordering at tea houses to indicate a simple order; can also refer generally to a light/simple snack meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋去飲茶，叫一盅兩件啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 jam2 caa4, giu3 jat1 zung1 loeng5 gin6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们去饮茶，叫一盅两件吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go for dim sum — let's order one tea and two items.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日午餐我只要一盅兩件，唔想食太多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 ng5 caan1 ngo5 zi2 jiu3 jat1 zung1 loeng5 gin6, m4 soeng2 sik6 taai3 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天午餐我只要一盅两件，不想吃太多。
examples.english_sentence: For lunch today I'll just have one tea and two dim sum items; I don't want to eat too much.

mandarin_meaning: 一眼就把人或事物否定、忽视或冷落
english_meaning: to dismiss or ignore someone/ something at a single glance; to give the cold shoulder; to judge and reject immediately
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，形容對人或事物很快地以一眼便否定、冷落或不屑理會，帶有草率判斷或冷漠的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe dismissing, ignoring, or looking down on someone or something after a single glance. It implies snap judgment or cold indifference.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁快一眼关七，試下了解下先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 faai3 jat1 ngaan5 gwaan1 cat1, si3 haa5 liu5 gaai2 haa5 sin1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要这么快就一眼把人否定，先试着了解一下。
examples.english_sentence: Don't dismiss someone so quickly at a glance; try to understand them first.

jyutping: jat1 ngaan5 zam1 mou5 loeng5 tau4 lei6
mandarin_meaning: 不能两全其美 / 不能兩頭都佔便宜
english_meaning: You can't have it both ways; it's impossible to benefit both sides at once
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某件事或安排無法同時對雙方或兩個方面都有利，不能兩頭都佔便宜或兩面討好。
explanation_english: Used to say that something cannot be advantageous to both sides at the same time — you can't get benefits from both ends or please both parties simultaneously.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好諗住兩邊都攞好處，一眼针冇两头利。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lam2 zyu6 loeng5 bin1 dou1 lo2 hou2 co2，jat1 ngaan5 zam1 mou5 loeng5 tau4 lei6。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別想兩邊都佔便宜，這樣不可能兩全其美。
examples.english_sentence: Don't think you can get benefits from both sides — you can't have it both ways.

jyutping: jat1 zyun1 dau6 fu6 soeng2 sing1 sin1
mandarin_meaning: 痴心妄想／不自量力
english_meaning: wishful thinking; to grossly overestimate one's abilities or aspire to something far beyond one's capacity
explanation_mandarin: 形容能力、資格或條件不足卻妄想獲得過高地位或成就；比喻自不量力、痴心妄想。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone with limited ability or qualifications who unrealistically aspires to much higher status or achievements; akin to being deluded or out of one's depth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱識煮飯就想開餐廳，真係一砖豆腐想升仙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 sik1 zyu2 faan6 zau6 soeng2 hoi1 caan1 teng1, zan1 hai6 jat1 zyun1 dau6 fu6 soeng2 sing1 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他才剛會做飯就想開餐廳，真是痴心妄想。
examples.english_sentence: He just learned to cook and already wants to open a restaurant — that's wishful thinking.

mandarin_meaning: 一盤素菜 / 一盤齋菜
english_meaning: a plate of vegetarian food; a dish of vegetarian fare
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「一盤素食／一盤齋菜」，可用於描述家常的素菜，也常見於宗教或祭祀場合作供品。
explanation_english: Literally 'one plate of vegetarian food.' It refers to a plate of vegetarian/zhai (meat-free) dishes, used for everyday descriptions or as an offering in religious/ritual contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋食齋，我淨係整咗一碟齋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 sik6 zaai1, ngo5 zing6 hai6 zing2 zo2 jat1 dip6 zaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我們吃素，我只做了一盤素菜。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight we're eating vegetarian; I only made one plate of vegetarian food.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廟裏擺咗一碟齋俾神明作供品。
examples.jyutping_sentence: miu6 leoi5 baai2 zo2 jat1 dip6 zaai1 bei2 san4 ming4 zok3 gung1 ban2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 庙里摆了一盘素菜供奉神明。
examples.english_sentence: They placed a plate of vegetarian food in the temple as an offering to the deities.

jyutping: jat1 zung2 mai5 joeng5 baak3 zung2 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 不同的人有不同的喜好、性格或做法（相當於「各人有各人嘅做法」）
english_meaning: Different people have different tastes or ways of doing things — to each their own / different strokes for different folks.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容世間人物性情、喜好或處事方式各不相同，不能以一種標準去要求或評斷所有人。
explanation_english: Used to say that people differ in temperament, preferences, or ways of doing things; one standard cannot be applied to everyone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋唔好強迫佢改變，人生觀各有不同，一種米養百種人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 m4 hou2 koeng4 bik1 keoi5 goi2 bin3, jan4 sang1 gun1 gok3 jau5 bat1 tung4, jat1 zung2 mai5 joeng5 baak3 zung2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们不要强迫他改变，人生观各有不同，一種米養百種人。
examples.english_sentence: We shouldn't force him to change; people have different outlooks on life — to each their own.

mandarin_meaning: 一群（通常帶貶義的）人；一幫小集團或惹事的人
english_meaning: a clique/group of people (derogatory); a bunch of shady, troublesome or unreliable people
explanation_mandarin: 「一窿蛇」是香港廣東話俗語，字面為「一個洞的蛇」。用來貶稱一群成群結黨的人，暗示這班人團體性強且常惹事、靠不住或品行不良。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang used derogatorily to refer to a group or clique of people who act as a unit—often implying they are troublesome, shady, unreliable, or disreputable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰班一窿蛇成日喺度搞事，唔想理佢哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 baan1 jat1 lung4 se4 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 gaau2 si6, m4 soeng2 lei5 keoi5 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那幫人總是在那裡鬧事，我不想理他們。
examples.english_sentence: That bunch of troublemakers are always causing problems there — I don't want to deal with them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想同一窿蛇去嗰間酒吧，佢哋好嘈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 tung4 jat1 lung4 se4 heoi3 go2 gaan1 zau2 baa1, keoi5 dei6 hou2 cou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想和那幫人去那家酒吧，他們很吵。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to go to that bar with that crowd — they're really noisy.

jyutping: jat1 zuk1 gou1 daa2 sei2 jat1 syun4 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 以一人或少數人的過失或行為，連累或責罰整個群體；以偏概全、株連眾人。
english_meaning: To punish or condemn an entire group because of the actions of one (person); to tar everyone with the same brush; collective punishment.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面意思是「用一根竹篙打死整船的人」，比喻因為一個人的錯誤或過失而連累或懲罰整個團體、把所有人一概而論。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally meaning "using one bamboo pole to beat dead everyone on a boat." It figuratively criticizes punishing or blaming an entire group for the fault of one or a few, i.e., overgeneralizing or collective punishment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好因為一個人做錯，就一竹篙打死一船人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jan1wai6 jat1 go3 jan4 zou6 co3, zau6 jat1 zuk1 gou1 daa2 sei2 jat1 syun4 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要因为一个人犯错，就连累或惩罚整個團體。
examples.english_sentence: Don't punish the whole group because one person made a mistake.

mandarin_meaning: 一點點；極少，微不足道。
english_meaning: a tiny bit; a negligible amount; not even the slightest.
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，表示數量或程度極微，常用於否定句或強調微小程度。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression indicating a very small amount or degree; often used in negative sentences to emphasize that something is negligible or non-existent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家嘅態度，連一箇幾毫誠意都冇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 ge3 taai3 dou6, lin4 jat1 go3 gei2 hou4 sing4 ji3 dou1 mou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你現在的態度，連一點誠意都沒有。
examples.english_sentence: From your current attitude, you don't even have the slightest bit of sincerity.

mandarin_meaning: 一下子就猜中／一次就命中
english_meaning: to get it right in one try; to hit the target or jackpot on the first attempt
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面指用一根箸就夾中（目標），比喻一下子就猜對、命中或一次成功。常用於形容中六合彩、抽獎、猜測或做事一次就得手的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally meaning 'to pick it with one chopstick.' It figuratively means to get something right in one try, to hit the target, or to win immediately. Often used for winning a lottery, guessing correctly, or succeeding on the first attempt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次買六合彩，一箸夹中，贏咗成十萬蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 maai5 luk6 ho6 coi2, jat1 zyu6 gaap3 zung1, jeng4 zo2 seng4 sap6 maan6 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這次買六合彩，一下子就中了，贏了十萬元。
examples.english_sentence: He bought the Mark Six lottery this time and hit the jackpot in one go, winning HK$100,000.

mandarin_meaning: 一次就命中／一下就成功
english_meaning: to hit the target or succeed on the first try; to get it in one go
explanation_mandarin: 形容一次就命中目標或第一次就成功，常用作比喻某人或某事一試即成。
explanation_english: Describes hitting the target or achieving success on the first attempt; often used figuratively for accomplishing something in one try.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次面試一箸夾中，已經攞到份工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 min6 si5 jat1 zyu6 gaap3 zung1, ji5 ging1 lok6 dou3 fan6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這次面試一箸夾中，已經拿到那份工作。
examples.english_sentence: He aced the interview on the first try and already got the job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰位射手第一腳就一箸夾中，為球隊先開紀錄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 wai6 se6 sau2 dai6 jat1 goek3 zau6 jat1 zyu6 gaap3 zung1, wai6 kau4 deoi6 sin1 hoi1 gei2 luk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那位射手第一腳就一箸夾中，為球隊先開紀錄。
examples.english_sentence: The striker scored with his first shot, giving the team the opening goal.

mandarin_meaning: 滿腹怨氣／心裡憋着很多不滿或委屈（口語）
english_meaning: to be full of resentment or grievances; to have a belly full of complaints (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「一肚核」是廣東話口語，形容心裡充滿不滿、怨氣或委屈，常用來說某人悶在心裡、沒說出口的牢騷或怨恨。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone is full of resentment, grievances, or bottled-up complaints — literally 'a belly full of kernels/pits.' It describes having many unexpressed complaints or bitterness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔肯講清楚，搞到我一肚核。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 hang2 gong2 cing1 co2, gaau2 dou3 ngo5 jat1 tou5 hat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不肯說清楚，弄得我滿肚子怨氣。
examples.english_sentence: He won't explain clearly, leaving me full of resentment.

mandarin_meaning: 一个人包办；独自完成（也可作字面上的“一脚踢开”）
english_meaning: to handle everything single-handedly; to do it all by oneself (also literal: to kick open with one kick)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指由一個人獨自處理或包辦所有事情，有時也可指字面上的一腳踢開。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to take on or manage everything alone; sometimes used literally to mean kicking something open with one kick.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話自己可以一腳踢晒成個項目，結果忙到爆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 ho2 ji5 jat1 goek3 tek3 saai3 sing4 go3 hong6 muk6, git3 gwo2 mong4 dou3 baau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說自己可以一個人把整個項目都做完，結果忙翻了。
examples.english_sentence: He said he could handle the entire project by himself, but ended up swamped.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆唔想請人，想一腳踢晒所有工作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 m4 soeng2 ceng2 jan4, soeng2 jat1 goek3 tek3 saai3 so2 jau5 gung1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板不想請人，想一個人包辦所有工作。
examples.english_sentence: The boss doesn't want to hire anyone; he wants to do all the work himself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢氣到想一腳踢開門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hei3 dou3 soeng2 jat1 goek3 tek3 hoi1 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他氣得想一腳把門踢開。
examples.english_sentence: He was so angry he wanted to kick the door open.

mandarin_meaning: 一时的冷清或萧条会影响较长一段时间；短暂的衰退带来连锁性的长期影响（俗语/谚语）
english_meaning: A short slump can have prolonged effects; a brief period of poor business or activity can negatively affect several subsequent market days (proverb/idiom).
explanation_mandarin: 「一节淡三圩」形容某一时期（例如一個節日或一個時段）生意或情況很冷清，導致接下來多個市場日或一段時間都受影響。常用以形容短期的不景氣會產生較長時間的後果。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb describes how a single dull period (for example, during a festival or a trading day) can lead to extended poor performance over the following market days. It's used to say a short downturn can have lasting, cascading effects.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年農曆新年生意差，真係一節淡三圩，老細都擔心緊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 nung4 lik6 san1 nin4 sang1 ji3 caa1, zan1 hai6 jat1 zit3 taam5 saam1 wai1, lou5 sai3 dou1 daam1 sam1 gan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年農曆新年生意很差，真是一節淡三圩，老闆都很擔心。
examples.english_sentence: Business was bad this Lunar New Year — it's a case of 'one dull period affecting several market days', and the boss is worried.

synonyms: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩

mandarin_meaning: 浑身发痒 / 全身起小包（像被蚂蚁爬过）
english_meaning: itchy all over; the feeling of ants crawling on the skin; covered with small itchy bumps
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容全身發癢，好像有蚂蚁在皮膚上爬，或因叮咬、過敏、濕疹等而起許多小包、瘙癢感的狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing the sensation of being itchy all over as if ants are crawling on the skin; can also refer to being covered in many small itchy bumps from bites or an allergic reaction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 食完海鮮之後，佢成個人一身蚁，面紅晒，應該係敏感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sik6 jyun4 hoi2 sin1 zi1 hau6, keoi5 sing4 go3 jan4 jat1 san1 ngai5, min6 hung4 saat3, jing1 goi1 hai6 man5 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 吃完海鲜后，他浑身发痒，脸都红了，应该是过敏。
examples.english_sentence: After eating seafood he was itchy all over and his face turned red—probably an allergic reaction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天出汗多，成日都一身蚁，好唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 ceot1 hon6 do1, sing4 jat6 dou1 jat1 san1 ngai5, hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天出汗多，常常全身发痒，弄得很不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: In summer I sweat a lot and often feel itchy all over—it's really uncomfortable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件新衫有化學味，著咗之後我一身蚁，只好脫返沖涼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 san1 saam1 jau5 faa3 hok6 mei6, zoek3 zo2 zi1 hau6 ngo5 jat1 san1 ngai5, zi2 hou2 tok3 faan1 cung1 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新买的那件衣服有化学味，穿上后我全身发痒，只好脱下来冲凉。
examples.english_sentence: The new shirt had a chemical smell; after putting it on I started itching all over, so I had to take it off and shower.

mandarin_meaning: 一轮（一次回合、一次轮次）
english_meaning: a round; a turn; one cycle/session
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词 / 量词（表示一轮次、一次回合）
explanation_mandarin: 「一輪」常用來表示一次輪次或一回合，例如比賽的一輪、請飲食的一輪或輪到某人。用於口語，適用於遊戲、比賽、飲酒請客等情境。
explanation_english: 「一輪」 denotes one round, turn, or session. It is commonly used in spoken Cantonese for games, matches, buying a round of drinks, or indicating whose turn it is.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我請你飲一輪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 ceng2 nei5 jam2 jat1 leon4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我請你喝一輪（我請你一輪酒）。
examples.english_sentence: I'll buy you a round tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 到我一輪做嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dou3 ngo5 jat1 leon4 zou6 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 輪到我做事了。
examples.english_sentence: It's my turn to do the work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽打咗三輪，佢最後贏咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 daa2 zo2 saam1 leon4, keoi5 zeoi3 hau6 jing4 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比赛打了三轮，他最後赢了。
examples.english_sentence: They played three rounds of matches; he finally won.

mandarin_meaning: 一件破舊或很土的衣服；引申為形容穿著過時、俗氣的人或打扮
english_meaning: a shabby or unfashionable piece of clothing; by extension, used to describe someone dressed tackily or out of fashion
explanation_mandarin: 「一辘杉」是香港廣東話的俗語，通常用來形容衣服很舊、很土或很沒品味，也可以用來指人的打扮過時、不時髦。語氣帶貶義，屬口語用法，使用時需注意場合和對象。
explanation_english: “一辘杉” is Cantonese colloquial slang (commonly heard in Hong Kong) used to describe clothing that is shabby, old, or tacky. It can also refer to a person's unfashionable or dowdy dress. The term is derogatory and informal, so be careful about context and who you address it to.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好著嗰件一辘杉出街啦，太老土喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoek3 go2 gin6 jat1 luk6 saam1 ceot1 gaai1 laa3, taai3 lou5 tou2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別穿那件又舊又土的衣服出門了，太過時了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't wear that tacky old shirt out; it's way too unfashionable.

mandarin_meaning: 等一會兒 / 等一下
english_meaning: a moment; in a short while
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，表示短暫的時間，常用於請求對方稍等或說明某事會在短時間內發生。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning a short while or in a moment; commonly used to ask someone to wait briefly or to indicate something will happen soon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等我一適間就返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 jat1 sik1 gaan1 zau6 faan1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等我一下就回來。
examples.english_sentence: Wait for me a moment and I'll be back.

jyutping: jat1 bou6 tung1 syu1 tai2 dou3 lou5
mandarin_meaning: 终身遵循一本通书（黄历）上的说法；形容人迷信或固守旧习、死守一套做法
english_meaning: Literally 'read one almanac until old' — to be superstitious or to rigidly stick to one traditional guide or practice for life
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人非常迷信或固執，遇事總按同一本通書（或舊規矩）去做，不願改變或接受新做法。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who is very superstitious or stubbornly traditional—always following the same almanac or old rules for everything and unwilling to change.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咩事都要翻通書，真係一部通書睇到老。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 me1 si6 dou1 jiu3 faan1 tung1 syu1, zan1 hai6 jat1 bou6 tung1 syu1 tai2 dou3 lou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做什麼事都要翻通書，真是一部通書看到老。
examples.english_sentence: He checks the almanac for everything — he really sticks to one almanac for life.

mandarin_meaning: 全盘泡汤 / 完全失败 / 白费了
english_meaning: completely ruined; all for nothing; totally messed up
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語・俚語（形容結果的片語）
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面是「一個鑊裡的泡」，用來形容事情全部白費、徹底搞砸或整個計劃/努力完全失敗了。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang literally 'one wok of bubbles'. It describes a situation where everything is wasted or totally ruined — a plan or effort that ends up a complete failure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋準備咗幾個月嘅活動畀場地取消，全部一镬泡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 zeon2 bei6 zo2 gei2 go3 jyut6 ge3 wut6 dung6 bei2 coeng4 dei6 ceoi2 siu1, cyun4 bou6 jat1 wok6 paau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們準備了好幾個月的活動被場地取消，全部都泡湯了。
examples.english_sentence: The event we prepared for months was cancelled by the venue — it was all for nothing.

mandarin_meaning: 完蛋 / 完了 / 搞砸了
english_meaning: It's all over; we're done for; completely ruined
explanation_mandarin: 「一鑊熟」是香港粵語口語，字面為「一鍋煮熟」，用來形容事情完全失敗、完蛋或全部搞砸，常用於感嘆或表示無可挽回的壞結果。
explanation_english: “Yat wok suk” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang literally meaning “one wok cooked.” It describes a situation that is completely ruined or beyond saving — an expression of being done for or a total mess.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你唔睇清楚就簽名，唔小心就一鑊熟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 m4 tai2 cing1 co3 zau6 cim1 meng4, m4 siu2 sam1 zau6 jat1 wok6 suk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你不看清楚就签字，一不小心就完蛋了。
examples.english_sentence: If you sign without reading carefully, you'll be screwed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試之前冇溫習，今次應該一鑊熟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 zi1 cin4 mou5 wan1 zaap6, gam1 ci3 jing1 goi1 jat1 wok6 suk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考试前没复习，这次应该完蛋了。
examples.english_sentence: We didn't study before the exam; we're probably doomed this time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司出咗啲大錯，財務報表有問題，老闆話可能一鑊熟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ceot1 zo2 di1 daai6 co3, coi4 mou6 bou3 biu2 jau5 man6 tai4, lou5 baan2 waa6 ho2 nang4 jat1 wok6 suk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司出了大错，财务报表有问题，老板说可能完蛋了。
examples.english_sentence: The company made big mistakes and there are problems in the financials; the boss said we might be done for.

mandarin_meaning: 一锅粥（形容混乱、杂乱不堪的局面）
english_meaning: a complete mess; a muddle; everything mixed up; a shambles
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，字面為“一鍋粥”，用來比喻事情弄得非常混亂或雜亂，大家都不清楚狀況或不知道如何處理。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese idiom literally 'a pot of congee'. Used to describe a situation that is completely chaotic or a total mess where people are confused or don't know what to do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次個安排搞到一镬粥，大家都唔知點算。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 go3 ngon1 paai4 gaau2 dou3 jat1 wok6 zuk1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zi1 dim2 syun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次的安排弄得一锅粥，大家都不知道怎么办。
examples.english_sentence: This arrangement turned into a complete mess; nobody knows what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 一發財就擺闊、揮霍或變得趾高氣揚；愛顯擺
english_meaning: to show off or act arrogantly/flashily after coming into money; to put on airs
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來形容人一旦有錢或覺得有面子，就開始誇耀、揮霍或擺架子。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who, after getting money or status, starts showing off, spending extravagantly, or acting pretentious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱做老闆，啱啱賺咗啲錢，依家一阔三大，成日買名牌嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 zou6 lou5 baan2, aam1 aam1 zaan6 zo2 di1 cin2, ji4 gaa1 jat1 fut3 saam1 daai6, sing4 jat6 maai5 ming4 paai4 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛當上老闆，剛賺了點錢，現在就愛擺闊，老買名牌東西。
examples.english_sentence: He just became a boss and made some money; now he's showing off and always buying designer stuff.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好一阔三大，錢未穩陣唔好亂花。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 jat1 fut3 saam1 daai6, cin2 mei6 wan6 zan6 m4 hou2 lyun6 faa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別裝闊，錢還不穩定不要亂花。
examples.english_sentence: Don't act rich; don't spend recklessly when your finances aren't secure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢中咗六合彩，一阔三大，成班朋友都覺得佢變咗樣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zung1 zo2 luk6 ho6 coi2, jat1 fut3 saam1 daai6, sing4 baan1 pang4 jau5 dou1 gok3 dak1 keoi5 bin3 zo2 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他中了六合彩，一發財就擺闊，整班朋友都覺得他變了樣。
examples.english_sentence: He won the lottery and started showing off; the whole group of friends felt he had changed.

mandarin_meaning: 像一只木屐似的（比喻笨拙、粗魯或行為愚蠢）
english_meaning: literally 'like a single wooden clog' — figuratively: clumsily, awkwardly, or acting like an idiot
explanation_mandarin: 「一隻屐噉」為廣府口語／俚語，字面是「像一隻木屐那樣」，常用來形容一個人行為或做事笨拙、不靈活或愚蠢。有時帶貶義或戲謔意味，使用上屬非正式場合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase literally meaning "like a single wooden clog." It's used to describe someone acting clumsily, awkwardly, or foolishly. It is informal and can be derogatory or teasing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好似一隻屐噉，成日跌跌撞撞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 ci5 jat1 zek3 haai4 gam2, seng4 jat6 dit3 dit3 zong6 zong6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事像一只木屐似的，總是跌跌撞撞。
examples.english_sentence: He does things clumsily, like a wooden clog — always stumbling.

mandarin_meaning: 像狗一樣（被輕視、被侮辱或被粗暴對待）
english_meaning: like a dog (used to say someone is demeaned, treated badly or without respect)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語/俚語，形容詞/副詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 「一隻狗噉」是廣東話口語表達，通常用來形容被當作狗一樣看待或對待，帶有輕視、侮辱或不尊重的含義。
explanation_english: “一隻狗噉” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning 'like a dog' — used to indicate being treated with contempt, insulted, or shown no respect.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日對我一隻狗噉，唔尊重我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 deoi3 ngo5 jat1 zek3 gau2 gam2, m4 zyun1 zung6 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是把我當成一條狗一樣，不尊重我。
examples.english_sentence: He always treats me like a dog; he doesn't respect me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲老細成日將員工當一隻狗噉，唔俾面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 lou5 sai3 seng4 jat6 zoeng1 jyun4 gung1 dong3 jat1 zek3 gau2 gam2, m4 bei2 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些老闆經常把員工當作狗一樣，不給面子。
examples.english_sentence: The bosses often treat employees like dogs, giving them no respect.

mandarin_meaning: 像一只麻雀一样小／瘦小（比喻）
english_meaning: as small as a sparrow; very small/tiny (idiomatic simile)
explanation_mandarin: 「一隻雀噉」是廣東話口語的比喻說法，用來形容人或物體又小、又瘦、或微不足道，字面意思是「像一隻麻雀那樣」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese simile used to describe someone or something as very small, thin, or insignificant — literally 'like a sparrow.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細細個，得返一隻雀噉大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 sai3 go3, dak1 faan1 jat1 zek3 zoek3 gam2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他／她很小，只有一只麻雀那么大。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is very small — only as big as a sparrow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個袋細到一隻雀噉，放唔到幾多嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 doi2 sai3 dou3 jat1 zek3 zoek3 gam2, fong3 m4 dou2 gei2 do1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个包小得像一只麻雀，放不了多少东西。
examples.english_sentence: This bag is so small — like a sparrow — it can't hold much.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好細聲，好似一隻雀噉，大家聽唔清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 sai3 seng1, hou2 ci5 jat1 zek3 zoek3 gam2, daai6 gaa1 teng1 m4 cing1 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说话声音很小，像只麻雀，大家听不清楚。
examples.english_sentence: He speaks very softly, like a sparrow; everyone can't hear clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 以同样方式回报 / 以牙还牙（视语境可为正当回报或报复）
english_meaning: to reciprocate in kind; to give back the same (can mean tit-for-tat or repay equally)
explanation_mandarin: 表示用相同的方式回报對方，既可指正當的互惠回報，也可指以同樣手段回敬或报复（視语境而定）。
explanation_english: Means to repay someone in the same manner — can indicate fair reciprocity or a tit‑for‑tat retaliation depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果佢幫我，我都會一马还一马，幫返佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 keoi5 bong1 ngo5, ngo5 dou1 wui5 jat1 maa5 waan4 jat1 maa5, bong1 faan1 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果他幫助我，我也會以同樣方式回報，幫回他。
examples.english_sentence: If he helps me, I'll reciprocate in kind and help him back.

jyutping: jat1 gai1 sei2 jat1 gai1 ming4
mandarin_meaning: 用來形容一個人或一件事被淘汰或消失後，總會有其他人或事物代替；沒有人是不可替代的，事情會繼續發展。
english_meaning: Literally 'when one chicken dies, another chicken crows' — used to say that when one person or thing is gone, another will take its place; nobody is indispensable and life goes on.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語常用於工作、政治或感情情境，表示某人被取代或失去機會後，總會有人接替，無需過度悲觀或自責。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb is often used in contexts like jobs, politics, or relationships to indicate that when someone is replaced or loses an opportunity, others will step in — so there's no need to be overly pessimistic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要裁員，大家都話一鸡死一鸡鸣，唔使太擔心，總有人會頂上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 coi4 jyun4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 jat1 gai1 sei2 jat1 gai1 ming4, m4 sai2 taai3 daam1 sam1, zung2 jau5 jan4 wui5 deng2 soeng5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要裁員，大家都說「一鸡死一鸡鸣」，不用太擔心，總會有人頂替。
examples.english_sentence: The company is laying people off; everyone says 'when one chicken dies another crows' — don't worry too much, someone will fill the role.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 選舉輸咗都唔使灰心，一鸡死一鸡鸣，下一個參選人可能就會上位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: syun2 geoi2 syu1 zo2 dou1 m4 sai2 fui1 sam1, jat1 gai1 sei2 jat1 gai1 ming4, haa6 jat1 go3 caam1 syun2 jan4 ho2 nang4 zau6 wui5 soeng5 wai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 選舉輸了也不用沮喪，一鸡死一鸡鸣，下一位候選人可能就會上位。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be discouraged by losing the election; when one chicken dies another crows — the next candidate may well take the position.

mandarin_meaning: 一文不值 / 毫無價值
english_meaning: worthless; of no value; good-for-nothing
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來形容某物或某人毫無價值、不可靠或沒用，帶有輕蔑或貶低的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used to describe something or someone as worthless, useless, or unreliable. It carries a dismissive or derogatory tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢樣嘢七個一皮，唔值錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 joeng6 je5 cat1 go3 jat1 pei4, m4 zik6 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這東西一文不值，不值錢。
examples.english_sentence: This thing is worthless; it's not worth any money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個人七個一皮，唔可靠，唔好理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 cat1 go3 jat1 pei4, m4 ho2 kaau3, m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這個人一點也不可靠，別理他。
examples.english_sentence: He's totally unreliable — don't bother with him.

mandarin_meaning: 乱七八糟 / 一团乱
english_meaning: completely chaotic; in utter disorder; a total mess
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，用來形容情況非常混亂、雜亂無章，字面意為「像七個國家一樣混亂」。通常用於非正式語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning extremely chaotic or in complete disorder. Literally "as chaotic as seven countries," used informally to describe a messy situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日個辦公室七国咁乱，根本搵唔到我要嘅文件。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 go3 baan6 gung1 sat1 cat1 gwok3 gam2 lyun6, gan1 bun2 wan2 m4 dou2 ngo5 jiu3 ge3 man4 gin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天办公室乱得一塌糊涂，根本找不到我要的文件。
examples.english_sentence: The office is a complete mess today; I can't find the documents I need at all.

mandarin_meaning: 七姊妹／七姐妹；（天文）昴宿（昴星團）；泛指由七個（或多個）姊妹／外表相似的一組事物
english_meaning: seven sisters; (astronomy) the Pleiades; a group of seven women or a cluster of seven similar things
explanation_mandarin: 「七姊妹」字面上指七個姊妹。口語中亦常用來指天文上的昴宿（俗稱七姊妹）或泛指一組七個相似、成一組的事物或建築物。有時作地名或綽號使用。
explanation_english: Literally 'seven sisters' — refers to seven sisters. Colloquially it can mean the Pleiades star cluster (commonly called the Seven Sisters) or be used figuratively for a group of seven similar items, buildings, or a set of women. It is also used as a name/nickname in some local contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋係七姊妹，成日一齊出嚟玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai6 cat1 zi2 mui6, sing4 jat6 jat1 cai4 ceot1 lai4 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她們是七姊妹，經常一起出來玩。
examples.english_sentence: They are seven sisters and often hang out together.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚天好清，我見到天上嘅七姊妹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 tin1 hou2 cing1, ngo5 gin3 dou2 tin1 soeng6 ge3 cat1 zi2 mui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚天很清，我看到天上的七姊妹（昴宿）。
examples.english_sentence: The sky was clear tonight and I could see the Seven Sisters (the Pleiades).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰排屋村有幾座外形差唔多嘅樓，大家叫佢哋「七姊妹」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 paai4 uk1 cyun1 jau5 gei2 zo6 ngoi6 jing4 caa1 m4 do1 ge3 lau4, daai6 gaa1 giu3 keoi5 dei6 "cat1 zi2 mui6".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那一帶的屋村有幾座外形差不多的樓，大家叫它們「七姊妹」。
examples.english_sentence: That estate has several similarly shaped blocks that people call the 'Seven Sisters'.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）亂七八糟、七零八落
english_meaning: in a mess; all over the place; disorganized; scattered
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，形容事物或場所非常凌亂、無秩序，東西散落或安排混亂。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing something that is very messy, disordered, or scattered. Used for places, situations, or things that are chaotic or untidy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日整到屋企七支八离，搵嘢好辛苦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zing2 dou3 uk1 kei5 cat1 zi1 baat3 lei4, wan2 je5 hou2 san1 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常把家裡弄得七零八落，找東西很辛苦。
examples.english_sentence: He often leaves the house in a mess; it's hard to find things.

cantonese: 七月红云盖天顶，收好禾苗湾好艇
jyutping: cat1 jyut6 hung4 wan4 goi3 tin1 ding2, sau1 hou2 wo4 miu4 waan1 hou2 teng5
mandarin_meaning: 七月出现红色云层覆盖天空，预示将有暴风雨或台风来临，应尽快收割庄稼并把船靠岸停好。
english_meaning: A weather proverb: red clouds covering the sky in July signal impending storms or a typhoon — time to harvest crops and dock boats.
explanation_mandarin: 这是粤语地区的民间谚语，用来根据天空迹象预测天气。意思是若七月出现大片红云，通常预示有强风雨或台风，将影响农作物和航运，因而要赶紧收割庄稼并停好船只。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folk proverb used to predict weather from sky signs. It means that when red clouds cover the sky in July, storms or a typhoon are likely coming, so people should quickly harvest crops and secure/dock their boats.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆成日講：「七月紅雲蓋天頂，收好禾苗灣好艇」，見到紅雲我哋就趕住收晒稻穀同停船。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 sing4 jat6 gong2: "cat1 jyut6 hung4 wan4 goi3 tin1 ding2, sau1 hou2 wo4 miu4 waan1 hou2 teng5", gin3 dou3 hung4 wan4 ngo5 dei6 zau6 gon2 zyu6 sau1 saai3 dou6 guk1 tung4 ting4 syun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶常說：「七月紅雲蓋天頂，收好禾苗灣好艇」，看到紅雲我們就趕緊收割稻穀並把船靠岸停好。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma always says, 'When red clouds cover the sky in July, harvest the crops and dock the boats.' When we see red clouds we hurry to harvest the rice and secure the boats.

jyutping: cat1 jyut6 lok6 gam1, baat3 jyut6 lok6 ngan4
mandarin_meaning: 七月有丰厚收益，八月仍有收获但略少
english_meaning: July brings gold, August brings silver — i.e., a period of abundant earnings/harvest, with July being the richer month and August somewhat less
explanation_mandarin: 粤语地区的俗语，源自农渔经验，用来形容农历或季节性期间（通常是七、八两个月）收成或收益丰厚：七月最丰，八月仍有但较少。也泛指在特定时间段会有较好的收入或运气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb originating from agricultural and fishing experience. It describes seasonal abundance — July yields the greatest gains ("gold"), while August still yields gains but less ("silver"). It is also used more generally to mean a time of plentiful earnings or good fortune.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年生意好好，真係七月落金，八月落銀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 saang1 ji3 hou2 hou2, zan1 hai6 cat1 jyut6 lok6 gam1, baat3 jyut6 lok6 ngan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年生意很好，真是七月落金，八月落银。
examples.english_sentence: Business has been great this year — truly 'July brings gold, August brings silver.'

mandarin_meaning: 形容極為窮困、走投無路或處於絕境（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: A colloquial expression meaning utterly penniless or in dire straits; completely broke and desperate.
explanation_mandarin: 此為廣東話口語或俚語，用來形容人非常窮困或處於無路可走的絕境，語氣偏口語化、有強烈強調意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to describe someone who is extremely poor or trapped in a desperate situation. The tone is informal and emphatic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱失業，依家真係七窮六絕，連飯錢都冇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ngaam1 ngaam1 sat1 jip6, ji1 gaa1 zan1 hai6 cat1 kung4 luk6 zyut6, lin4 faan6 cin2 dou1 mou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛剛失業，現在真是窮得要命，連飯錢都沒有。
examples.english_sentence: He just lost his job and is now completely broke — he doesn't even have money for a meal.

mandarin_meaning: 形容在一群人或事物中顯得特別突出、出眾（可譯為「一枝獨秀」或「出類拔萃」）
english_meaning: An idiom meaning to stand out; the one outstanding or most eye‑catching person/thing among many
explanation_mandarin: 「七葉一枝花」比喻在很多人或事物中只有一個特別突出、引人注目的存在，常用來形容某人或某物最搶眼、最出眾。
explanation_english: Literally 'seven leaves, one flower.' Used figuratively to describe someone or something that stands out among many—especially an individual who is particularly attractive or eye‑catching.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺班入面真係七葉一枝花，最搶眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 baan1 jap6 min6 zan1 hai6 cat1 jip6 jat1 zi1 faa1, zeoi3 coeng2 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在班裡真的是一枝獨秀，最搶眼。
examples.english_sentence: He/She really stands out in the class — the most eye‑catching.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺婚禮嗰陣，新娘真係七葉一枝花，大家睇到都讚佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 fan1 lai5 go2 zan6, san1 noeng4 zan1 hai6 cat1 jip6 jat1 zi1 faa1, daai6 gaa1 tai2 dou3 dou1 zaan3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在婚禮上，新娘真是最搶眼，大家看到都稱讚她。
examples.english_sentence: At the wedding the bride was truly the standout; everyone praised her.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司嗰位新同事一出場就好吸引，大家都覺得佢係七葉一枝花。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 go2 wai2 san1 tung4 si6 jat1 ceot1 coeng4 zau6 hou2 kap1 jan5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 gok3 dak1 keoi5 hai6 cat1 jip6 jat1 zi1 faa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司那位新同事一出場就很吸引，大家都覺得他是七葉一枝花。
examples.english_sentence: The new colleague at the company drew attention as soon as they appeared; everyone thought they were a standout.

mandarin_meaning: 交给我 / 有我在（别担心，我来处理）
english_meaning: Leave it to me; I've got this / Count on me
explanation_mandarin: 「万大有我」是粵語口語俚語，常用來表示「別擔心、交給我處理」或「有我在，不會出問題」。語氣帶自信或保證的意味，常見於朋友或熟人之間。
explanation_english: “万大有我” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to mean “leave it to me” or “count on me.” It conveys confidence and assurance that the speaker will take care of something or that things will be fine with them involved. Commonly used among friends or acquaintances.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事交畀我，万大有我，唔使擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 gaau1 bei2 ngo5, maan6 daai6 jau5 ngo5, m4 sai2 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事交给我，万大有我，不用担心。
examples.english_sentence: Leave this to me — I've got this, don't worry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去派對唔知點去？万大有我，我會帶路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 paai3 deoi6 m4 zi1 dim2 heoi3? maan6 daai6 jau5 ngo5, ngo5 wui5 daai3 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去派对不知道怎么去？万大有我，我会带路。
examples.english_sentence: Not sure how to get to the party tonight? Count on me — I'll show the way.

mandarin_meaning: 用幾個簡單快速的手勢來表達或示範（口語）
english_meaning: Using a few quick hand gestures to express or demonstrate something (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，強調用幾個迅速、簡單的手勢就能表達意思或示範動作，帶有隨意、快捷的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression emphasizing that a few quick, simple hand gestures are sufficient to convey an idea or demonstrate an action; implies speed and casualness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢用三兩下手勢就解釋到點做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 saam1 loeng5 haa6 sau2 sai3 zau6 gaai2 sik1 dou3 dim2 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他用幾個簡單的手勢就把怎麼做解釋清楚了。
examples.english_sentence: He explained how to do it clearly with just a few quick hand gestures.

jyutping: saam1 go3 neoi5 jan4 jat1 go3 wai1
mandarin_meaning: 三個女人聚在一起容易鬧事／愛八卦、起衝突（俗語）
english_meaning: Saying that when multiple women gather there is likely to be gossip, quarrel or drama
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東話俗語，用來形容幾個女人聚在一起時容易有閒言閒語、爭吵或製造戲劇性的場面。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to suggest that when several women gather they are likely to gossip, bicker, or create drama.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好介入，三個女人一個圩，插手只會更複雜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gaai3 jap6, saam1 go3 neoi5 jan4 jat1 go3 wai1, caap3 sau2 zi2 wui5 gang3 fuk1 zaap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別插手，三個女人在一起容易鬧事，插手只會讓事情更複雜。
examples.english_sentence: Don't get involved — when three women are together there's likely to be drama; intervening will only make things more complicated.

cantonese: 三个手指揸田螺，十拿九稳
jyutping: saam1 go3 sau2 zi2 zaa1 tin4 lo4, sap6 naa4 gau2 wan2
mandarin_meaning: 几乎肯定、十有八九会成功（相当稳妥）
english_meaning: practically certain; almost guaranteed; a sure thing
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語/俗語，形容詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俗語，用來形容事情非常有把握、成功或結果很穩妥。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to describe something that is very likely to succeed or is almost certain — essentially 'a sure thing.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意有咁多利好消息，三個手指揸田螺，十拿九穩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3 jau5 gam2 do1 lei6 hou2 siu1 sik1, saam1 go3 sau2 zi2 zaa1 tin4 lo4, sap6 naa4 gau2 wan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这笔生意有这么多利好消息，十拿九稳。
examples.english_sentence: This deal has so many positive signs; it's practically a sure thing.

mandarin_meaning: 乱七八糟；一塌糊涂
english_meaning: completely messy; in total disorder
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俗語，用來形容事情或地方非常混亂、凌亂、不成樣子，意思接近「亂七八糟」。常見於香港口語中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe something as completely messy or in utter disorder, similar in meaning to "a complete mess" or "in a right old muddle." Commonly used in Hong Kong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企搞到三九兩丁七，我唔知點執好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 gaau2 dou3 saam1 gau2 loeng5 ding1 cat1, ngo5 m4 zi1 dim2 zap1 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家里弄得乱七八糟，我不知道怎么收拾好。
examples.english_sentence: The house is a complete mess — I don't know how to tidy it up.

mandarin_meaning: 完全不懂 / 毫無所知
english_meaning: completely clueless; know nothing about it
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，字面為“三九不認識七”，用來形容對某事物完全不了解或一竅不通。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial idiom literally meaning "three nine doesn't know seven," used to indicate that someone is totally ignorant or clueless about something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你問佢歷史嘅嘢，佢三九唔识七。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 man6 keoi5 lik6 si2 ge3 je5, keoi5 saam1 gau2 m4 sik1 cat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你問他歷史的事，他完全不懂。
examples.english_sentence: You asked him about history; he's completely clueless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事我都三九唔识七，唔好問我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 ngo5 dou1 saam1 gau2 m4 sik1 cat1, m4 hou2 man6 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事我也完全不懂，別問我。
examples.english_sentence: I have no idea about this matter — don't ask me.

mandarin_meaning: 可能是「三文鱼」的错写或戏称，指鮭鱼（salmon）
english_meaning: Likely a misspelling or joking form of '三文魚' (salmon)
explanation_mandarin: 「三來魚」並非標準詞彙，常見於口語或網絡上作為誤寫或戲稱，正確應為「三文魚」，即鮭魚。
explanation_english: Not a standard lexical item; often appears as a typo or joke for '三文魚' (salmon). The correct term is '三文魚'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有人將三文魚寫成三來魚，係打錯字定係玩嘢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 jan4 zoeng1 saam1 man4 jyu4 se2 sing4 saam1 loi4 jyu4, hai6 daa2 co3 zi6 ding6 hai6 waan2 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人把三文鱼写成三来鱼，这是打错字还是在开玩笑？
examples.english_sentence: Someone wrote 三文魚 as 三來魚 — is it a typo or a joke?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚煮三文魚，唔好再用「三來魚」呢個錯字啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 zyu2 saam1 man4 jyu4, m4 hou2 zoi3 jung6 'saam1 loi4 jyu4' ni1 go3 co3 zi6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚煮三文鱼，别再把它写成“三来鱼”这个错字了。
examples.english_sentence: We're cooking salmon tonight — don't write it as the misspelling '三來魚'.

jyutping: saam1 jyun4 gung1 tou2 dei6, sek3 san1 (變體: saam1 jyun4 gung1 tou2 dei6, sik1 san1)
mandarin_meaning: （道教/民間祈祝語）願三元宮和土地神保佑／賜福身體平安
english_meaning: A Taoist/folk blessing: "May the Three Yuan Palace and the Earth God bless/protect (your) body."
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句民間或道教用的祝禱語，提到“三元宮”（道教神祇或廟宇名）和“土地”（土地神），用來祈求保佑、平安或保護身體。口語中有時會見到“錫身”或寫作“惜身”的變體，意指賜予恩佑或憐惜保護之意。
explanation_english: This is a folk/Taoist blessing invoking the "Three Yuan Palace" and the Earth God (local deity) to ask for protection or blessings for one's body. Spoken forms may use 錫身 (sek3 san1) or the variant 惜身 (sik1 san1), both conveying the idea of bestowing care or protection.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 逢年過節，啲老人家去廟入面會講『三元宮土地，錫身』，祈求平安。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fung4 nin4 gwo3 zit3, di1 lou5 jan4 gaa1 heoi3 miu6 jap6 min6 wui5 gong2 'saam1 jyun4 gung1 tou2 dei6, sek3 san1', kei4 kau4 ping4 on1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 逢年過節，老人家到廟裡會念『三元宮土地，錫身』，祈求平安。
examples.english_sentence: During festivals, the older folks go to the temple and say, 'May the Three Yuan Palace and the Earth God bless the body,' praying for safety.

jyutping: saam1 fan1 ngaan4 sik1 dong3 daai6 hung4
mandarin_meaning: 把微小的優點或成就誇大；小題大作
english_meaning: To exaggerate a minor merit or achievement; to make a mountain out of a molehill
explanation_mandarin: 形容把只有一點點價值或成績誇張成很了不起的樣子，常用於批評自誇或誇大事實的人。
explanation_english: Describes treating a small advantage or achievement as if it were very important; often used to criticize someone who exaggerates or boasts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日將三分颜色当大红，自我感覺好高，實際上冇乜本事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 cing4 jat6 zoeng1 saam1 fan1 ngaan4 sik1 dong3 daai6 hung4, zi6 ngo5 gam2 gok3 hou2 gou1, sat6 zai3 soeng6 mou5 mat1 bun2 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是把一點小成就誇大，自我感覺很高，實際上沒什麼本事。
examples.english_sentence: He always blows his minor achievements out of proportion, has an inflated self-image, but actually doesn't have much ability.

mandarin_meaning: 用幾句話；簡短數語地說；亦可含有用幾句花言巧語或敷衍了事的意味
english_meaning: in a few words; with a few glib words — briefly or tersely, sometimes implying glibness, persuasion, or perfunctory speech
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，字面為“三個口、兩條舌”，用來表示用很少的話說明或交代；有時帶有輕率、敷衍或靠幾句花言巧語達成目的的含義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally 'three mouths, two tongues'. It means saying something in very few words or speaking briefly; it can also imply speaking glibly or using a few smooth words to persuade or brush something off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢用三口兩脷就呃到嗰啲人信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 saam1 hau2 loeng5 lei6 zau6 aak1 dou3 go2 di1 jan4 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只用幾句花言巧語就騙到那些人相信他。
examples.english_sentence: He managed to get those people to believe him with just a few glib words.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：三只手；引申：能同時做多件事、擅長多工，或（帶有諷刺）指愛插手別人事務的人（香港口語俚語）
english_meaning: Literally 'three hands'. Colloquially, someone who can handle many tasks at once (very multi‑tasking), or joking/pejoratively, a person who meddles in others' affairs (Hong Kong slang).
explanation_mandarin: 「三只手」為香港口語俚語，字面意思是「有三隻手」。常用來形容能同時處理多項工作或事務的人（具讚賞意味），亦可用作諷刺，指喜歡插手、干涉別人事務的人。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong colloquial/slang expression literally meaning 'three hands'. It is used to describe someone who can manage multiple tasks at once (praising their dexterity/multi‑tasking), or sarcastically to call someone a meddler who sticks their hands into other people’s business.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢可以同時搞幾個project，真係有三只手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ho2 ji5 tung4 si4 gaau2 gei2 go3 project, zan1 hai6 saam1 zek3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他可以同时做好几个项目，真是有三只手。
examples.english_sentence: He can handle several projects at once — he really has three hands.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做三只手啦，畀啲人自己諗辦法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 saam1 zek3 sau2 laa1, bei2 di1 jan4 zi6 gei2 lam2 baan6 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別當三只手了，讓別人自己想辦法。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a 'three hands' — let people figure it out themselves.

mandarin_meaning: （粤语口语）形容人很无知、糊涂或不识相
english_meaning: Cantonese slang describing someone who is clueless, oblivious, or behaves without common sense
explanation_mandarin: 「三唔识七」是廣東話俗語，字面是「三不認識七」，用來形容一個人甚麼都不懂、糊塗、或做事不識相、不得體，常用作責備或不滿的口語表達。
explanation_english: “三唔识七” is a Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning “three doesn't know seven.” It describes someone who is clueless, confused, oblivious, or behaves in an inconsiderate or tactless way. Often used informally to scold or express annoyance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都三唔识七，做錯嘢仲唔肯認錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 dou1 saam1 m4 sik1 cat1, zou6 co3 je5 zung6 m4 hang2 jing6 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是一副什麼都不懂的樣子，做錯了還不肯認錯。
examples.english_sentence: He's always clueless — makes mistakes and still refuses to admit them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺會議入面，佢三唔识七就亂插嘴，令大家都唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 wui6 ji5 jap6 min6, keoi5 saam1 m4 sik1 cat1 zau6 lyun6 caap3 zeoi2, ling6 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在會議上，他不識相地亂插嘴，讓大家都覺得不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: In the meeting, he rudely butted in (acting clueless), making everyone uncomfortable.

jyutping: san1 gaap3 baan2 soeng5 diu1 faa1, haak1 bok6
mandarin_meaning: 表面華麗但內容廉價或虛浮，且態度刻薄、苛刻
english_meaning: Superficially ornate on cheap material — pretentious or showy but essentially cheap; also mean or stingy in character
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 片語／俗語（用來形容人或行為，具貶義）
partOfSpeech_english: idiom/slang (descriptive phrase, derogatory; functions like an adjective)
explanation_mandarin: “三夹板上雕花”字面是把雕花刻在便宜的三夾板上，形容外表裝飾得很講究但本質很廉價、徒有其表；後接“刻薄”時強調行為或性情尖酸刻薄、令人反感。
explanation_english: Literally "carving flowers on plywood" — describes something or someone that is superficially ornate or pretentious on a cheap base (form over substance). When paired with "刻薄" it emphasizes a mean, spiteful or harsh character beneath the showy appearance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日扮嘢，三夹板上雕花，刻薄，冇人鍾意佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 baan6 je5, san1 gaap3 baan2 soeng5 diu1 faa1, haak1 bok6, mou5 jan4 zung1 ji3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是裝腔作勢，外表虛華卻刻薄，沒有人喜歡他。
examples.english_sentence: He's always putting on a show — superficially flashy but mean; nobody likes him.

mandarin_meaning: 三岁看八十 / 三岁定终身（俗语）
english_meaning: What is set at three (years old) determines how you'll be at eighty — childhood habits/character largely shape one's whole life.
explanation_mandarin: 表示一個人的性格、習慣或命運在幼年時期已基本形成，三歲時的表現或習慣會影響到一生，難以改變。
explanation_english: A proverb meaning that a person's character, habits, or destiny are largely formed in early childhood — what is established by age three tends to persist throughout life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 正所謂三歲定八十，細個嘅習慣好難改。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 so2 wai6 saam1 seoi3 ding6 baat3 sap6, sai3 go3 ge3 zaap6 gwaan3 hou2 naan4 goi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 正所谓三岁定八十，小时候的习惯很难改。
examples.english_sentence: As the saying goes, 'what's set at three lasts until eighty' — childhood habits are hard to change.

cantonese: 三年唔發市，發市當三年
jyutping: saam1 nin4 m4 faat3 si5, faat3 si5 dong1 saam1 nin4
mandarin_meaning: 三年不發市，發市當三年
english_meaning: If there is no prosperity for three years, when prosperity returns treat it as making up for three years (i.e. seize the opportunity and make up for lost time).
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容多年沒有好時機或好景氣，當好時機回來時，就應該把握好、全力彌補過去幾年的損失。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb meaning that after a long drought of opportunity or prosperity, when good times return you should treat them as compensating for the lost years — seize the chance and make up for lost time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話：三年唔發市，發市當三年，依家有生意就要盡力做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6: saam1 nin4 m4 faat3 si5, faat3 si5 dong1 saam1 nin4, ji1 gaa1 jau5 saang1 ji3 zau6 jiu3 zeon6 lik6 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說：「三年不發市，發市當三年」，現在有生意就要全力以赴。
examples.english_sentence: He said, 'If there's no prosperity for three years, when it returns treat it as making up for three years' — so now when there's business we must go all out.

mandarin_meaning: 動作麻利、利索、迅速利落（粵語用法）
english_meaning: doing things quickly and efficiently; briskly and nimbly
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容一個人做事動作快、乾脆利落、麻利。常用作狀態副詞來修飾動作。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing actions done swiftly and neatly; used as an adverbial phrase to indicate nimble, efficient movements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你快啲，三手兩腳收埋啲嘢啦，遲到喇！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 faai3 di1, saam1 sau2 loeng5 goek3 sau1 maai4 di1 je5 laa1, ci4 dou3 laa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你快一點，把東西迅速收好，要遲到了！
examples.english_sentence: Hurry up, quickly pack your things — we're going to be late!

mandarin_meaning: 敷衍了事；做事馬虎、不認真
english_meaning: slapdash; done carelessly or perfunctorily; half‑hearted
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，用來形容做事草率、敷衍、不仔細、不徹底。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase describing action done carelessly or perfunctorily — not thorough or done with proper attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好三扒兩撥，做完嘅嘢請檢查清楚先交俾我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 saam1 paa4 loeng5 but3 zou6 jyun4 ge3 je5 cing2 gim2 caa4 cing1 co2 sin1 gaau1 bei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要敷衍了事，做完的事情請檢查清楚再交給我。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be slapdash — check your work thoroughly before handing it to me.

mandarin_meaning: 小氣的人；吝嗇鬼
english_meaning: a cheapskate; a stingy person
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗稱，用來形容非常小氣、吝嗇、不願意花錢的人。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who is very stingy or unwilling to spend money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係三斂子，連朋友食飯都唔肯埋單。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 saam1 lim5 zi2, lin4 pang4 jau5 sik6 faan6 dou1 m4 hang2 maai4 daan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個小氣鬼，連和朋友吃飯都不肯埋單。
examples.english_sentence: He's really stingy — he won't even pick up the bill when dining with friends.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意唔好太三斂子，客人會走嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 sang1 ji3 m4 hou2 taai3 saam1 lim5 zi2, haak3 jan4 wui5 zau2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意不能太小氣，顧客會跑掉的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be too stingy in business; customers will walk away.

jyutping: saam1 gan1 zyu1 tau4, dak1 baa2 zeoi2
mandarin_meaning: 既笨又多嘴（贬义俚语）
english_meaning: a derogatory Cantonese slang meaning someone who is stupid but talkative/mouthy
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人又笨又愛多嘴、喜歡發表無知或不必要的意見，帶有貶義，常見於廣東話口語中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used to describe someone who is both foolish and mouthy—talks a lot or speaks nonsense; derogatory and used in colloquial speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度亂講，真係三斤豬頭，得把嘴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 dou6 lyun6 gong2, zan1 hai6 saam1 gan1 zyu1 tau4, dak1 baa2 zeoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在那裡亂說話，真是又笨又多嘴。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks nonsense — really stupid and a loudmouth.

jyutping: saam1 gang1 ceot1 sai3, hoi6 si4 (hoi6 sei2) jan4
mandarin_meaning: 一句粵語俗諺，利用「亥時」與「害死」的諧音戲謔地說某人在三更（深夜）出生，暗指此人兇猛、易惹事或命途不佳，通常用來打趣或形容某人性格粗暴。
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese saying that puns on 'hai hour' (亥時 hoi6 si4) and 'to kill' (害死 hoi6 sei2). It jokingly suggests someone born at the third watch of the night is dangerous/unlucky and will 'harm' others — used to tease someone as fierce or troublemaking.
explanation_mandarin: 此語靠時間名與動詞的諧音構成雙關，主要是戲謔或誇張地形容一個人兇悍或命格不佳，並非字面意思的殺人。
explanation_english: This phrase uses a pun between a time term and a verb to jokingly describe someone as fierce, unlucky, or troublemaking; it is figurative, not a literal claim of violence.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日咁衝動，啲人都話佢係『三更出世，亥时（害死）人』。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gam2 cung1 dung6, di1 jan4 dou1 waa6 keoi5 hai6 'saam1 gang1 ceot1 sai3, hoi6 si4 (hoi6 sei2) jan4'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是这么冲动，大家都笑说他是“三更出世，亥时（害死）人”。
examples.english_sentence: He's always so impulsive; people jokingly say he's 'born at the third watch — he'll harm people at the hai hour'.

cantonese: 三月三，擂棰大棍都种生
mandarin_meaning: 三月三，连杵子大棍都能发芽（表示春回大地、万物复苏）
english_meaning: On the third day of the third month even pestles and big sticks sprout (i.e. spring has arrived; everything is coming to life).
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用誇張的說法形容農曆三月初三左右春意濃，萬物復甦、草木發芽，表示春天來臨。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb that uses hyperbole (even pestles and big sticks sprout) to describe how, around the third day of the third lunar month, spring is in full swing and everything comes back to life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 三月三，擂棰大棍都种生，成村啲草木都開始發芽，春天真係到啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: saam1-jyut6-saam1, leoi4-ceoi4-daai6-gwan3-dou1-zung2-saang1, seng4-cyun1-di1-cou2-muk6-dou1-hoi1-ci2-faat3-ngaa4, ceon1-tin1-zan1-hai6-dou3-laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 三月三，连杵子和大棒都能发芽，整个村子的草木都开始发芽，春天真的到了。
examples.english_sentence: On the third day of the third month even pestles and big sticks seem to sprout — the village's plants are budding and spring has really arrived.

mandarin_meaning: 三朝回门
english_meaning: third-day return (bride's return to her parental home after the wedding)
explanation_mandarin: 傳統婚俗之一，指新娘在婚禮後第三日回娘家（或夫妻一同回女方家）拜訪父母、行禮或送禮，表示問候與回訪。
explanation_english: A traditional wedding custom in which the bride (or the couple) returns to the bride's parental home on the third day after the wedding to visit her parents, pay respects, and often exchange gifts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋婚禮後第三日會三朝回門，返去見父母。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 fan1 lai5 hau6 dai6 saam1 jat6 wui5 saam1 ziu1 wui4 mun4 faan1 heoi3 gin3 fu6 mou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们婚礼后第三天会三朝回门，回娘家见父母。
examples.english_sentence: They will observe the 'three-day return' on the third day after the wedding and go back to the bride's family to see her parents.

cantonese: 三朝大雾一朝风，一冷冷弯弓
jyutping: saam1 ziu1 daai6 mou6 jat1 ziu1 fung1, jat1 laang5 laang5 waan1 gung1
mandarin_meaning: 形容天气或局势突然急剧变化；也用来比喻事态一朝转变，变化迅速
english_meaning: Describes a sudden and dramatic change in weather or circumstances; used metaphorically for a swift reversal of situation
explanation_mandarin: 原本直指气候：连续几天大雾，可能在某一天突然刮起风；一遇寒冷就会带来明显影响。引申为任何情况可能在短时间内突变，提醒人们注意变化并做好准备。
explanation_english: Literally refers to weather changing abruptly (after several foggy mornings there may be a windy one; a single cold snap can have a strong effect). By extension it warns that situations can turn quickly and unexpectedly, so be prepared.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家天氣好變，真係三朝大雾一朝风，一冷冷弯弓，出門記得帶外套。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 tin1 hei3 hou2 bin3, zan1 hai6 saam1 ziu1 daai6 mou6 jat1 ziu1 fung1, jat1 laang5 laang5 waan1 gung1, ceot1 mun4 gei3 dak1 daai3 ngoi6 tou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在天气多变，真是“三朝大雾一朝风，一冷冷弯弓”，出门记得带外套。
examples.english_sentence: The weather is so changeable right now — really 'three mornings of fog, one morning of wind; one cold snap can change things.' Remember to bring a jacket when you go out.

jyutping: saam1 ziu1 hung4 wan4 jat1 ziu1 fung1
mandarin_meaning: 長期的興旺或恩寵可能會在一瞬間衰落，指興衰迅速、榮華轉瞬即逝
english_meaning: A long period of prosperity or favour can suddenly collapse; a rapid reversal of fortune or sudden downfall after a time of glory
explanation_mandarin: 形容一個人、家族、公司或政權曾經興盛一段時間，但在短時間內突然衰落或失勢。
explanation_english: Describes someone, an organization, or a regime that enjoyed a period of prosperity or favour but then experiences a sudden and rapid decline.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間公司昔日好叻，但而家倒閉，真係三朝紅雲一朝風。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 gung1 si1 sik6 jat6 hou2 lak6, daan6 ji4 gaa1 dou3 bai3, zan1 hai6 saam1 ziu1 hung4 wan4 jat1 ziu1 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家公司昔日很风光，但现在倒闭，真是三朝红云一朝风。
examples.english_sentence: This company used to be very successful, but now it's closed down — truly a sudden reversal of fortune.

jyutping: saam1 tiu4 gau2, mai5 ngaat3 sau2
mandarin_meaning: 別插手 / 别动手
english_meaning: Hands off; don't meddle or touch (it)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俚語，用來警告或制止別人插手、干預或用手碰某件事物。語氣通常較直接，常見於香港口語。詞源不明，屬俗語或方言表達。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang admonition used to warn or stop someone from intervening, meddling, or touching something. It functions as a direct 'hands off' command and is commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese; origin is unclear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢走埋去干預人哋嘅事，我就話：『三條九，咪喐手。』
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zau2 maai4 heoi3 gon1 jyu6 jan4 dei6 ge3 si6, ngo5 zau6 waa6: 'saam1 tiu4 gau2, mai5 ngaat3 sau2.'
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他走過去干預別人的事，我就說：『別插手。』
examples.english_sentence: He went over and tried to interfere in others' affairs, and I said, 'Hands off.'

jyutping: saam1 bou6 lo2 maai4 loeng5 bou6
mandarin_meaning: 很快；一下子就完成（口語）
english_meaning: very quickly; in no time (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，表示在短時間內、幾個動作/步驟之內就完成某事或很快發生，多用於讚賞效率或形容事情迅速。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to do something very quickly or complete it in just a few steps; often used to praise efficiency or indicate something will happen imminently.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好高效，三步擸埋两步就完成晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 gou1 haau6, saam1 bou6 lo2 maai4 loeng5 bou6 zau6 jyun4 sing4 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很高效，轉眼間就全部完成了。
examples.english_sentence: He works very efficiently — he finished everything in no time.

mandarin_meaning: 三脚猫功夫（拙劣的、本领浅薄的技艺）
english_meaning: poor/shoddy skill; superficial or half‑baked ability
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容某人的技艺或本领很差、只是皮毛、不够熟练或专业。
explanation_english: Describes someone's skill or ability as poor, superficial, or amateurish — not proficient or professional.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲廚藝只係三脚猫功夫，煮出嚟啲餸唔夠好食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 ceoi4 ngai6 zi2 hai6 saam1 goek3 maau1 gung1 fu1, zyu2 ceot1 lai4 di1 sung3 m4 gau3 hou2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的厨艺只是三脚猫功夫，做出来的菜不好吃。
examples.english_sentence: His cooking is just shoddy — the dishes he makes aren't tasty.

mandarin_meaning: 经常见面／常来往（口语）
english_meaning: to meet up frequently; to socialize often (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 表示彼此经常见面、聚会或来往，多用于粤语口语，形容朋友或熟人之间频繁社交。
explanation_english: Indicates meeting or socializing frequently; a colloquial Cantonese phrase used to describe friends or acquaintances who get together regularly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋兩個細個就識，依家仍然三茶兩飯見面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 loeng5 go3 sai3 go3 zau6 sik1, ji1 gaa1 jing4 jin4 saam1 caa4 loeng5 faan6 gin3 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们两个人从小就认识，现在仍然经常见面。
examples.english_sentence: We have known each other since childhood and still meet up frequently.

mandarin_meaning: 打多份工/身兼數職的人
english_meaning: a person who does multiple odd jobs; jack-of-all-trades (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「三行佬」是廣東話口語，通常指身兼多份工作或在不同行業之間打零工的人，含中性或略帶鄙稱的語感，常用來形容生活靠兼職維持的人。
explanation_english: “Sam-hong-lou” is Cantonese slang referring to someone who does multiple part-time jobs or odd jobs across different trades. It is colloquial and can be neutral or mildly derogatory, describing a person who makes a living through various small jobs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿榮係個三行佬，朝早送貨、下午做水電，夜晚喺茶餐廳幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 wing4 hai6 go3 saam1 hong4 lou2, ziu1 zou2 sung3 fo3, haa6 ng5 zou6 seoi2 din6, je6 maan5 hai2 caa4 caan1 teng1 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿榮是個三行佬，早上送貨、下午做水電，晚上在茶餐廳幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Wing is a 'sam-hong-lou' — he delivers goods in the morning, does plumbing/electrical work in the afternoon, and helps at a cha chaan teng at night.

mandarin_meaning: （粤语方言）一种小鱼的俗称，词汇罕见、地区性强
english_meaning: A regional Cantonese name for a small/lesser-known fish; a rare/obscure dialectal term
explanation_mandarin: 「三鱮」為粵語地區的方言或俗稱，用來指代某種小魚或地方性魚類名稱。此詞較為罕見，書面及普通話資料有限，主要見於地方口語或長者說法中。
explanation_english: “三鱮” is a regional Cantonese/dialectal name used to refer to a certain small fish or a local fish species. The term is rare and chiefly found in local spoken usage; it is not common in standard written sources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢種細魚喺街市有人叫做三鱮，唔係好常見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zung2 sai3 jyu4 hai2 gaai1 si5 jau5 jan4 giu3 zou6 saam1 zuk1, m4 hai6 hou2 soeng4 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这种小鱼在菜市场有人称为“三鱮”，不常见。
examples.english_sentence: This small fish is called “三鱮” at the market; it's not commonly seen.

mandarin_meaning: 小型魚類；（俚語）比喻無足輕重的人或小角色
english_meaning: a small fish; (slang) an insignificant person or small-time character
explanation_mandarin: 「三鱮魚」原指一種小型魚類，在廣東話口語中也常被用作俚語，形容人微不足道或沒什麼能力、地位的人。語氣可以帶輕蔑或戲謔成分。
explanation_english: Literally refers to a small fish. In Cantonese colloquial usage it is also used as slang to describe someone insignificant, ineffective, or a minor/unimportant character. The tone can be dismissive or teasing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識講大話，喺公司度就係個三鱮魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 gong2 daai6 waa6, hai2 gung1 si1 dou6 zau6 hai6 go3 saam1 zuk1 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會說大話，在公司裡就是個無足輕重的人。
examples.english_sentence: He only talks big; at the company he's just an insignificant person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 菜檔有啲新鮮嘅三鱮魚，可以買嚟煎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: coi3 dong3 jau5 di1 san1 sin1 ge3 saam1 zuk1 jyu4, ho2 ji5 maai5 lai4 zin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 菜檔有些新鮮的三鱮魚，可以買來煎。
examples.english_sentence: The stall has some fresh 'san zuk' fish; you can buy them to pan-fry.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：三黄四月；無廣泛公認的成語或固定含義，屬地方或口語用法
english_meaning: Literally "three yellow, fourth month"; not a widely recognized idiom — a rare/regional colloquial expression with no established universal meaning
explanation_mandarin: 「三黄四月」在主流粵語詞典中無明確條目。字面上由「三黃」與「四月」構成，可能在某些地域或語境下作俚語或戲謔用法，但沒有普遍認可的固定含義。使用時意義多依語境而定，亦可能是聽錯或誤傳的詞語。
explanation_english: There is no widely recognized idiomatic meaning for "三黄四月" in standard Cantonese. Literally composed of "three yellow" and "fourth month," it appears to be a rare or regional colloquialism without an established, universal sense. Its meaning depends on context and it may be a localized slang, playful coinage, or a misheard expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講「三黄四月」係咩意思？我真係未聽過呢個講法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 "saam1 wong4 sei3 jyut6" hai6 me1 ji3si1? ngo5 zan1 hai6 mei6 teng1 gwo3 ni1 go3 gong2 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說「三黄四月」是什麼意思？我真的沒聽過這種說法。
examples.english_sentence: What do you mean by "三黄四月"? I've really never heard that expression.

mandarin_meaning: 敷衍地点头 / 只是点头应付
english_meaning: to nod perfunctorily; to give a token nod of agreement without real engagement
explanation_mandarin: 「三點頭」是廣東話口語，形容人只是表面上點頭應付，並沒有真正聆聽或同意，多用來批評敷衍的態度。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to nod merely as a formality — to give a token or perfunctory nod without genuinely listening or agreeing. Often used to criticize a dismissive or perfunctory attitude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽我講嘢淨係三點頭，好明顯係敷衍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 ngo5 gong2 je5 zing6 hai6 saam1 dim2 tau4, hou2 ming4 hin2 hai6 fu1 jin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他听我說話只是敷衍地点頭，很明顯是在應付我。
examples.english_sentence: He only nodded perfunctorily while I was talking — clearly just going through the motions.

jyutping: soeng5 dou1 saan1 lok6 jau4 wok6
mandarin_meaning: 上刀山下油锅；赴汤蹈火，愿意冒极大危险或吃苦去做某事
english_meaning: To willingly face extreme danger or hardship; to go through severe risks/trials for someone or something
explanation_mandarin: 形容為了某個目標或為了幫助別人而願意冒極大的危險或吃盡苦頭。
explanation_english: Describes being willing to undergo extreme danger or hardship in order to achieve something or help someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗幫朋友，佢真係肯上刀山落油镬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 bong1 pang4 jau5, keoi5 zan1 hai6 hang2 soeng5 dou1 saan1 lok6 jau4 wok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了帮朋友，他真愿意上刀山下油锅。
examples.english_sentence: To help his friend, he is really willing to go through extreme danger.

cantonese: 上屋搬下屋，唔见一箩谷‍
mandarin_meaning: 到处找也找不到/费劲心力却一无所获
english_meaning: Search high and low but can't find a thing; all effort for nothing
explanation_mandarin: 形容到处翻找或到处奔走却什么也没找到，或者努力付出却没有任何收获。字面意思是搬上搬下房子也看不见一箩（篮）谷（粮）。常用于抱怨找不到东西或徒劳无功。
explanation_english: Describes searching everywhere or working hard but finding nothing — efforts are in vain. Literally: "move from the upper house to the lower house, yet not a single basket of grain is seen." Used to complain about being unable to find something or getting no results despite effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我搵咗成日，上屋搬下屋，唔见一箩谷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5_wan2_zo2_sing4_jat6_soeng5_uk1_bun1_haa6_uk1_m4_gin3_jat1_lo4_guk1
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我找了一整天，翻遍了上下屋子，还是一无所获。
examples.english_sentence: I've been looking all day, searched high and low, and still couldn't find a thing.

mandarin_meaning: 不可能/難以實現（形容某事荒謬或很難做到）
english_meaning: Impossible / very difficult to achieve (used to say something is unrealistic or absurd)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面是「上山去抓蟹」，意指做一件不合常理或幾乎不可能做到的事，常帶有否定或嘲諷語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally meaning "go up the mountain to catch crabs." It describes something absurdly unrealistic or virtually impossible to do, often used with a dismissive or mocking tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你諗住一個禮拜內攞三份專業證書？上山抓蟹，難。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 lam2 zyu6 jat1 go3 lai5 baai3 noi6 lo2 saam1 fan6 zyun1 jip6 zing3 syu1? soeng5 saan1 zaa1 haai5, naan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你打算一個禮拜內拿到三個專業證書？不可能吧。
examples.english_sentence: You plan to get three professional certificates in one week? That's impossible.

cantonese: 上山擒虎易，开口求人难‍
jyutping: soeng5 saan1 kam4 fu2 ji6, hoi1 hau2 kau4 jan4 naan4
mandarin_meaning: 比喻因为自尊、害羞或顾虑面子而不愿意向别人开口求助，开口求助反而比做困难的事更难。
english_meaning: A proverb meaning it's often harder to ask others for help than to do a difficult or dangerous task oneself — pride or embarrassment make asking difficult.
explanation_mandarin: 这句话用夸张的比喻说明：与其去完成看似艰难的事，不如开口求助更难，强调人们因面子或自尊不愿开口。
explanation_english: This saying uses a vivid comparison to emphasize that asking for help is often more difficult than tackling a hard task, because people hesitate due to pride or embarrassment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁固執，寧願自己做晒都唔肯開口求人，真係「上山擒虎易，開口求人難」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 gu3 zap1, ning4 jyun6 zi6 gei2 zou6 saai3 dou1 m4 hang2 hoi1 hau2 kau4 jan4, zan1 hai6 "soeng5 saan1 kam4 fu2 ji6, hoi1 hau2 kau4 jan4 naan4".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這麼固執，寧願自己做完也不肯開口求人，真是「上山擒虎易，開口求人難」。
examples.english_sentence: He's so stubborn that he'd rather do everything himself than ask for help — truly, it's easier to catch a tiger on a mountain than to open one's mouth and beg for assistance.

jyutping: soeng5 dak1 saan1 do1 jyu6 zoek6 fu2
mandarin_meaning: 多做危险的事就难免遇到危险（上山多遇虎）
english_meaning: If you take more risks or often go into dangerous situations, you're more likely to run into trouble (lit. the more you go up the mountain, the more likely you are to meet tigers).
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗语，用來形容經常去做危險或冒險的事情，就很容易遇到麻煩或危險。可用來警告或評論某人行為冒險。
explanation_english: A proverb used to say that if someone frequently engages in risky or dangerous activities, they are likely to encounter trouble. Often used to warn or comment on someone's risky behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做啲危險嘅生意，真係上得山多遇着虎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zou6 di1 ngai4 him2 ge3 sang1 ji3, zan1 hai6 soeng5 dak1 saan1 do1 jyu6 zoek6 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常做一些危险的生意，真是上山多遇虎。
examples.english_sentence: He often takes risky ventures; it's no wonder he runs into trouble (literally: the more you go up the mountain, the more likely you are to meet tigers).

mandarin_meaning: （1）上水：香港新界北區的上水（地名）。（2）上水（碎）：非正式口語或網絡用法，可能表示「徹底弄壞/慘敗/被打得很慘」等含義，屬於地區性俚語/俗語，含義不穩定。
english_meaning: (1) Sheung Shui: a place name in the New Territories of Hong Kong. (2) "...seoi" usage: an informal/slang expression (regionally used) that can imply being completely ruined/broken or utterly beaten/defeated; meaning is non-standard and context-dependent.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 專有名詞 / 俚語（視用法而定）
explanation_mandarin: 「上水」通常指香港的新界地名上水。括號中的「（碎）」見於口語或網絡語境，並非標準詞彙，其用法帶有強烈口語色彩且地域性高。合用時常用以誇張地表達「被徹底打敗、輸得很慘」或「徹底搞爛/弄碎」，具體含義需依上下文判斷。
explanation_english: "上水" usually refers to the Hong Kong place name Sheung Shui. The parenthetical "(碎)" appears in colloquial or online usage and is not standard. When combined, it is an informal, region-specific expression often used to exaggerate being completely beaten/defeated or thoroughly ruined/broken; exact meaning depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝去上水買嘢，坐錯車要返轉頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 heoi3 soeng5 seoi2 maai5 je5, co5 co3 ce1 jiu3 faan1 zyun2 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上去上水買東西，坐錯車要折回。
examples.english_sentence: I went to Sheung Shui this morning to buy something, took the wrong bus and had to go back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 昨晚打波畀人上水碎，成隊人都輸晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zok3 maan5 daa2 bo1 bei2 jan4 soeng5 seoi2 seoi3, sing4 deoi6 jan4 dou1 syu1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚打球被人打得很慘，整隊人都輸光了。
examples.english_sentence: Last night we played and got totally smashed — the whole team lost.

mandarin_meaning: 上牌／上排（口語）
english_meaning: to register/get a plate; (colloquial) to be placed on a waiting list or roster
explanation_mandarin: 「上牌」常見意思是為車輛辦理牌照登記並領取車牌；在口語中也有人用寫作「上排」，指把人或事放上名單、排隊或列入輪候名單（即上等待名額或排列位置）。
explanation_english: “上牌” commonly means to register a vehicle and obtain its licence plate. Colloquially (sometimes written as 上排), it can also mean being put onto a list or roster — i.e. placed on a waiting list or scheduled in turn.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日去車房上牌喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 heoi3 ce1 fong4 soeng5 paai4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天去車行上牌了。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going to the garage today to register the car and get the licence plates.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你已經上排，等通知啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji5 ging1 soeng5 paai4, dang2 tung1 zi1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你已經上排，等通知吧。
examples.english_sentence: You're already on the waiting list — wait for the notification.

mandarin_meaning: 上门补习（到学生家里或住所进行辅导）
english_meaning: to provide private tutoring at a student's home; home tutoring (tutor comes to the student's residence)
explanation_mandarin: 指老師到學生家裡或住所進行一對一或小班的輔導教學，通常由家教或補習導師上門授課。
explanation_english: Refers to a tutor visiting a student's home to provide one-on-one or small-group lessons; home-based private tuition where the tutor comes to the student's residence.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢每星期都會上門補習一個學生，教佢英文。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mui5 sing1 kei4 dou1 wui5 soeng5 mun4 bou2 zaap6 jat1 go3 hok6 saang1, gaau3 keoi5 jing1 man4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他每星期都会到学生家里上门补习，教他英文。
examples.english_sentence: He goes to a student's home every week to give private tutoring, teaching him English.

cantonese: 上面蒸松糕，下面卖凉粉‍
jyutping: soeng6 min6 zing1 cung4 gou1, haa6 min6 maai6 loeng4 fan2
mandarin_meaning: 表面装得体面，实际上做见不得人的事情；表里不一，虚伪
english_meaning: To put on a respectable appearance while doing shameful or disreputable things underneath; hypocritical/two-faced
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語 / 口語短語（描述性）
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，用來形容某人表面看起來光鮮、正經，實際上暗地裡做卑劣或見不得人的勾當，意思接近「表裡不一」或「外表一套，背后一套」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to describe someone who maintains a respectable or decent outer appearance while secretly engaging in lowly or disgraceful activities. Similar in meaning to "two-faced" or "keeping up appearances."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日上面蒸松糕，下面卖凉粉，表面一套，背后一套，真係唔可信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 soeng6 min6 zing1 cung4 gou1, haa6 min6 maai6 loeng4 fan2, biu2 min6 jat1 tou3, bui3 hau6 jat1 tou3, zan1 hai6 m4 ho2 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是在表面上装得体面，实际上却干着见不得人的勾当，表面一套，背后一套，真的不可信。
examples.english_sentence: He always puts on a respectable appearance but secretly does shameful things — all show on the outside, different behind the scenes; really untrustworthy.

mandarin_meaning: 輕輕地爬下來 / 慢慢爬下
english_meaning: to crawl/ climb down gently; to descend slowly and quietly
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示以輕柔、慢速的方式往下爬或下來，常用於小動物或小孩，強調動作輕柔且不發出聲音。
explanation_english: A colloquial verb phrase meaning to crawl or climb down gently and slowly. Often used for small animals or children, emphasizing a quiet, delicate descent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隻小貓下爬輕輕咁落嚟，冇發出聲嚇醒主人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zek3 siu2 maau1 haa6 paa4 hing1 hing1 gam2 lok6 lai4, mou5 faat3 ceot1 seng1 haak1 sing2 zyu2 jan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小貓輕輕地爬下來，沒有發出聲音吵醒主人。
examples.english_sentence: The kitten crawled down gently without making a sound to wake its owner.

mandarin_meaning: 施蠱、使人著迷或上癮（迷惑、施巫術）
english_meaning: to cast a spell on / to bewitch; figuratively, to fascinate or make someone obsessed/addicted
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語或民間說法，原指以蠱術或巫術迷惑、詛咒他人；在口語中亦可比喻某事物使人著迷或上癮。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/folk term originally referring to using 'gu' (a kind of curse/spell) to bewitch someone; figuratively used to mean something that captivates or addictively fascinates people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有人話佢畀人下蠱，成日做惡夢同頭暈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 jan4 waa6 keoi5 bei2 jan4 haa6 gu2, sing4 jat6 zou6 ok3 mung6 tung4 tau4 wan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人說他被下蠱，總是做惡夢和頭暈。
examples.english_sentence: Someone said he was bewitched; he keeps having nightmares and feeling dizzy.

mandarin_meaning: 不僅；不只是（表示不只局限於某一情況，還有其他）
english_meaning: not only; not just (indicating something is more than or beyond a single case)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 副詞短語（表示遞進／補充）
explanation_mandarin: 用於句首或句中，表示某事不只如此，還有其他情況或更進一步的內容，常與「仲／還／而且」等連用。
explanation_english: Used before or within a clause to indicate that something is not limited to what was just mentioned — there is more or an additional point; often pairs with words like "also/ furthermore/ moreover."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個計劃不單止可以幫助學生，仲可以改善社區環境。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 bat1 daan1 zi2 ho2 ji5 bong1 zo6 hok6 saang1, zung6 ho2 ji5 goi2 sin6 se5 keoi1 waan4 ging2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个计划不单止能帮助学生，还能改善社区环境。
examples.english_sentence: This plan not only helps students, it can also improve the community environment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔單止遲到，仲冇交功課。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 daan1 zi2 ci4 dou3, zung6 mou5 gaau1 gung1 fo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不只是迟到，还没交作业。
examples.english_sentence: He's not only late, he also hasn't handed in his homework.

mandarin_meaning: 可疑；令人懷疑、不可靠
english_meaning: suspicious; dubious; causing doubt or mistrust
explanation_mandarin: 用來描述某事或某人令人產生懷疑、不太可靠或看似可疑的情況，常用於書面或正式語境。
explanation_english: Used to describe something or someone that arouses suspicion or seems unreliable/dubious; often used in more formal or written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢位證人嘅供詞有啲不審，法官要再查。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wai2 zing3 jan4 ge3 gung1 ci4 jau5 di1 bat1 sam2, faat3 gwan1 jiu3 zoi3 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這位證人的供詞有些可疑，法官要再查。
examples.english_sentence: The witness's testimony is somewhat suspicious; the judge needs to investigate further.

mandarin_meaning: 不僅／不只是
english_meaning: not only; not limited to
explanation_mandarin: 「不特」多用於書面或較正式的語境，表示不僅僅如此、並非只限於某一情況，可與「不僅」、「不只是」、「不單止」互換。口語常用「唔止」、「唔單止」。
explanation_english: "不特" is mainly used in written or formal contexts to mean "not only" or "not limited to". It is equivalent to "not only"/"not just". In spoken Cantonese, people more commonly say "唔止" or "唔單止".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個政策嘅影響不特限於城市，鄉村都會受影響。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zing3 caak3 ge3 jing2 hoeng2 bat1 dak6 haan6 jyu1 sing4 si5, hoeng1 cyun1 dou1 wui5 sau6 jing2 hoeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個政策的影響不僅限於城市，鄉村也會受到影響。
examples.english_sentence: The effects of this policy are not limited to the city; rural areas will also be affected.

mandarin_meaning: 不僅；不只
english_meaning: not only; not merely
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示不僅僅是某事物或範圍，還包含其他情況或範疇，屬於較書面或文言的表達。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that something is not limited to a single thing or scope and includes other cases; a more formal or literary expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅貢獻不特止喺本地，仲影響到國際上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 gung3 hin3 bat1 dak6 zi2 hai6 bun2 dei6, zung6 jing2 hoeng2 dou3 gwok3 zai3 soeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的貢獻不僅限於本地，還影響到國際上。
examples.english_sentence: His contributions are not limited to the local area; they also have an international impact.

mandarin_meaning: 表示世事无常，人的际遇会轮流变化，大家都会有起落。
english_meaning: The world goes round — fortunes change; everyone's turn will come; what goes around comes around.
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容人生或時運會有起有落，常用來安慰失意的人或提醒人們不要自滿。
explanation_english: A colloquial saying meaning that life and fortunes change over time; used to comfort someone who is unlucky or to warn against complacency.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好灰心，世界輪流轉，遲早你都會有機會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 fui1 sam1, sai3 gaai3 leon4 lau4 zyun2, ci4 zou2 nei5 dou1 wui5 jau5 gei1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别灰心，世界轮流转，迟早你也会有机会。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be discouraged — the world goes round; sooner or later you'll get your chance.

mandarin_meaning: 世界藝術；有時用作機構或活動名稱（不常用，常見於專有名詞或書面語）
english_meaning: literally 'world art' or 'generational art/skill'; can be used as a proper name for festivals or organizations; not common in everyday speech, often literary or titular
explanation_mandarin: 由「世」（世界/世代）和「藝」（藝術/技藝）組成，通常指世界性的藝術或代代相傳的藝術／技藝。該詞並不常見於口語，常見於專有名詞或書面語境。
