explanation_english: Composed of 世 (world/generation) and 藝 (art/skill). It usually refers to world-scale art or arts/skills passed down through generations. The term is not common in colloquial speech and often appears in proper names or literary contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今屆嘅藝術節叫「世藝節」，匯聚咗世界各地嘅傳統同當代表演。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 gaai3 ge3 ngai6 seot6 zit3 giu3 「sai3 ngai6 zit3」, wui6 zeoi6 zo2 sai3 gaai3 gok3 dei6 ge3 cyun4 tung2 tung4 dong1 doi6 biu2 jin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 本屆藝術節名為「世藝節」，匯聚了世界各地的傳統和當代表演。
examples.english_sentence: This year's arts festival, called the 'World Arts Festival' (世藝節), brings together traditional and contemporary performances from around the world.

cantonese: 世间上边处有唔食饭嘅神仙
jyutping: sai3 gaan1 soeng6 bin1 cyu3 jau5 m4 sik6 faan6 ge3 san4 sin1
mandarin_meaning: 世上哪有不吃饭的神仙
english_meaning: There are no immortals who don't eat (i.e. nobody can live without material needs; you can't expect people to do things for free)
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示世上沒有不吃東西的人，意指人人都有生理或物質需求，不可能無償或不吃不喝地生活。常用以反駁不切實際的期待或要求別人無償付出。
explanation_english: Used to say that no one can live without eating; everyone has material or physical needs. It's used to rebut unrealistic expectations or the idea that people will do things for free.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話會免費幫你做晒啲嘢？世间上边处有唔食饭嘅神仙呀！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 wui5 min5 fai3 bong1 nei5 zou6 saai3 di1 je5? sai3 gaan1 soeng6 bin1 cyu3 jau5 m4 sik6 faan6 ge3 san4 sin1 aa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說會免費幫你做完所有事？世上哪有不吃飯的神仙啊！
examples.english_sentence: He says he'll finish all that work for you for free? There's no such thing as an immortal who doesn't eat!

synonyms: 世上沒有人會無償付出所有

mandarin_meaning: 尷尬；丟臉；令人難為情
english_meaning: embarrassing; awkward; causing shame or discomfort
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，表示讓人覺得尷尬、丟臉或難為情，常用於描述場面或行為令人不自在。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial adjective meaning embarrassing or awkward — used to describe situations or actions that cause shame or discomfort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁遲，好丟時呀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 ci4, hou2 diu1 si4 aa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這麼遲，很尷尬/很丟臉。
examples.english_sentence: You're so late — it's really embarrassing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺眾人面前跌倒，真係丟時。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 zung3 jan4 min6 cin4 dit3 dou2, zan1 hai6 diu1 si4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在眾人面前摔倒，真是很尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: He fell in front of everyone — that's really embarrassing.

mandarin_meaning: 以極低價格拋售／賤賣，清貨降價
english_meaning: to sell off at throwaway/very low prices; to slash prices to clear stock
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，常用於商業語境，指把商品以非常低的價格賣出以清理庫存或促銷。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used in commercial contexts meaning to sell goods at very low prices (often to clear stock or as a clearance sale).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢批衫太多，要丟架（價）清貨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 pat1 saam1 taai3 do1, jiu3 diu1 gaa3 (gaa3) cing1 fo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這批衣服太多，要以超低價清貨。
examples.english_sentence: There are too many of these clothes; we need to clear them at throwaway prices.

mandarin_meaning: 丢脸 / 丢人
english_meaning: to lose face; to feel embarrassed; to be humiliated (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口語，表示感到尷尬或丟臉、丟人的狀態，相當於普通話的“丢脸/丢人”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to feel embarrassed or to lose face; used to say someone is humiliated or ashamed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我真係好丢架，喺會上講錯晒啲資料。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 hou2 diu1 gaa3, hai2 wui6 soeng5 gong2 co3 saai3 di1 zi1 liu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我真的很丢人，在會議上把資料全部說錯了。
examples.english_sentence: I was so embarrassed — I got all the information wrong during the meeting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔識答人問題，當場丢架。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 sik1 daap3 jan4 man6 tai4, dong1 coeng4 diu1 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不會回答別人的問題，當場丟人。
examples.english_sentence: He couldn't answer people's questions and was embarrassed on the spot.

mandarin_meaning: 去你媽的 / 操你媽（粗俗咒罵）
english_meaning: A very strong Cantonese curse meaning 'fuck your mother' (extremely offensive insult)
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話罵人用語，等同或變體於「屌你老母」，用來表達憤怒或侮辱，屬極度冒犯性的詞語，應避免在正式場合使用。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese expletive used to insult or express strong anger, equivalent to or a variant of "屌你老母". It is highly offensive and should be avoided in formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你丟那媽做乜嘢呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 diu2 naa5 maa1 zou6 mat1 je5 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你他媽在做什麼？
examples.english_sentence: What the hell are you doing, you motherfucker?

cantonese: 两个哑仔嗌交，唔知边个着
jyutping: loeng5 go3 aa3 zai2 aai3 gaau1 m4 zi1 bin1 go3 zoek3
mandarin_meaning: 两个人互相争执，外人难以判断谁对谁错
english_meaning: When two people argue and neither side can be clearly judged right or wrong; outsiders can't tell who's at fault
explanation_mandarin: 俗语，用来形容双方各执一词、互不相让，外人无法分辨是非或判断责任归属。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying used to describe a situation where both parties are arguing and neither side can be clearly judged right or wrong, so outsiders can't determine who is at fault.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件事兩邊都唔肯認錯，真係兩個啞仔嗌交，唔知邊個着。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 si6 loeng5 bin1 dou1 m4 hang2 jing6 co3, zan1 hai6 loeng5 go3 aa3 zai2 aai3 gaau1, m4 zi1 bin1 go3 zoek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事双方都不肯认错，真是两个哑巴吵架，外人难以判断谁对谁错。
examples.english_sentence: Both sides refuse to admit mistakes in this matter — it's really 'two mute people arguing', and outsiders can't tell who's right.

synonyms: 兩個哑巴吵架，外人莫辨是非

cantonese: 两仔爷报佳音，代代（袋袋）平安
jyutping: loeng5 zai2 je4 bou3 gaa1 jam1, doi6 doi6 (doi6 doi6) ping4 on1
mandarin_meaning: （賀年祝福語）兩位/兩個孩子（或象徵帶來喜訊的人）報來好消息，祝願世世代代平安；用「袋袋平安」可作雙關，暗指財源滾滾。
english_meaning: A festive blessing meaning 'the two lads bring good news; may generations (and even every 'bag') be safe' — a New Year greeting wishing lasting peace and prosperity, with a pun on 'bags' implying wealth.
explanation_mandarin: 此句常見於賀年場合或利是封等慶祝用語。前半句「兩仔爺報佳音」表示有人帶來好消息或喜慶；後半句「代代（袋袋）平安」為祝願世代平安，若用「袋袋平安」則帶有雙關意味，祝財運亨通。
explanation_english: This expression is used as a New Year blessing or festive slogan. The first part ('two lads bring good news') signals good tidings; the second part ('generations/bags safe') wishes safety and continuity. Using 'bags' (袋袋) is a pun that also wishes for abundant wealth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋喺利是封上寫住「兩仔爺報佳音，袋袋平安」，祝新一年行大運。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai2 lei6 si6 fung1 soeng6 se2 zyu6 "loeng5 zai2 je4 bou3 gaa1 jam1, doi6 doi6 ping4 on1", zuk1 san1 jat1 nin4 hang4 daai6 wan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們在利是封上寫著「兩仔爺報佳音，袋袋平安」，祝新年好運。
examples.english_sentence: They wrote 'Two lads bring good news, bags of peace' on the red envelope to wish good fortune in the new year.

cantonese: 两公婆见鬼，唔系你就系我
jyutping: loeng5 gung1 po4 gin3 gwai2, m4 hai6 nei5 zau6 hai6 ngo5
mandarin_meaning: 不是你就是我（兩人之間只能有一個人被責備或吃虧）
english_meaning: Either you or me (one of the two will be the one to suffer/be blamed)
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語俗語，字面是「兩個夫妻見鬼」，後半句「唔係你就係我」表示在兩個人中只能有一個人被責備、倒霉或被選中，常用於互相推卸責任或競爭情境，語氣帶幽默或無奈。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying. Literally 'two spouses see a ghost — if it's not you it's me.' It means that between two people only one will be blamed or suffer; used jokingly or resignedly when shifting blame or describing a competition where only one can be chosen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司淨係有一個位升職，兩公婆見鬼，唔系你就係我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 zing6 hai6 jau5 jat1 go3 wai2 sing1 zik1, loeng5 gung1 po4 gin3 gwai2, m4 hai6 nei5 zau6 hai6 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司只有一個升職名額，不是你就是我。
examples.english_sentence: The company only has one promotion slot — it's either you or me.

mandarin_meaning: 兩邊都顧不上／兩頭落空（兩邊都無法達成目的）
english_meaning: to please or succeed at neither end; to end up stuck in the middle; neither side benefits
explanation_mandarin: 形容想兩邊都做好或討好兩方，但結果兩邊都無法達成或得不到好處，兩頭落空。
explanation_english: Describes trying to satisfy or accommodate both sides but failing to achieve either one, ending up with neither side satisfied.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢想兩邊都討好，結果兩頭唔到岸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 loeng5 bin1 dou1 tou2 hou2, git3 gwo2 loeng5 tau4 m4 dou3 ngon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他想兩邊都討好，結果兩頭不到岸。
examples.english_sentence: He tried to please both sides, but ended up pleasing neither.

jyutping: loeng5 tau4 m4 sau6 zung1 gaan1 sau6
mandarin_meaning: 两边都不承担责任，中间的人或事受到损失或委屈（夹在中间吃亏）
english_meaning: Both ends refuse to take responsibility, so the person in the middle bears the loss or suffers.
explanation_mandarin: 形容兩邊互相推諉、不願承擔，結果夾在中間的人或部門吃虧、受氣或承受損失。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where two sides refuse to accept responsibility, leaving the person or party in the middle to suffer or take the blame.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件事兩頭唔受，中間個人就要食苦頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 si6 loeng5 tau4 m4 sau6 zung1 gaan1 go3 jan4 zau6 jiu3 sik6 fu2 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事兩頭都不接受，中間的人只好吃苦頭。
examples.english_sentence: Both parties refuse to accept responsibility for this matter, so the person in the middle has to suffer.

mandarin_meaning: 兩頭猶豫、搖擺不定（在兩邊之間猶豫或想討好兩邊）
english_meaning: to be indecisive; to waver between two sides; to try to please both sides
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語，用來形容一個人在兩個選擇或兩方之間猶豫不決，或者想同時討好兩邊而不作明確抉擇。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who hesitates between two choices or tries to please both sides instead of making a clear decision.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日兩头揗，快啲決定啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 loeng5 tau4 lam2, faai3 di1 kyut3 ding6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要總是兩頭猶豫，快點決定吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep wavering—decide quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做事兩头揗，成日遲手遲腳，做唔到好嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 loeng5 tau4 lam2, sing4 jat6 ci4 sau2 ci4 goek3, zou6 m4 dou3 hou2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事猶豫不決，總是慢吞吞，做不好事情。
examples.english_sentence: He hesitates when handling tasks, always slow and not getting things done well.

mandarin_meaning: 兩面派；指表裡不一、兩面三刀、對人一套背後又一套的人
english_meaning: a two-faced person; double-dealer; someone who is insincere and betrays or speaks ill behind others' backs
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容口是心非、表面一套背後又做另一套、在不同人面前說不同話以圖取利或出賣別人的人。
explanation_english: A figurative term for someone who is two-faced or duplicitous — appears friendly or agreeable in front of you but speaks ill of or betrays you behind your back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個兩頭蛇，面前對你笑，背後就出賣你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 loeng5 tau4 se4, min6 cin4 deoi3 nei5 siu3, bui3 hau6 zau6 ceot1 maai6 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個兩頭蛇，當面對你笑，背後卻出賣你。
examples.english_sentence: He's a two-faced person: he smiles to your face and betrays you behind your back.

jyutping: go3 sam1 sap6 ng5 sap6 luk6
mandarin_meaning: 三心兩意 / 猶豫不決
english_meaning: fickle; indecisive; unable to make up one's mind
explanation_mandarin: 表示心思不定、三心兩意，拿不定主意或經常反覆變卦。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is indecisive or fickle — can't make up their mind and frequently changes their decisions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好個心十五十六，快啲決定啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 go3 sam1 sap6 ng5 sap6 luk6, faai3 di1 kyut3 ding6 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別三心兩意，快點決定吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so indecisive — make a decision quickly!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日個心十五十六，轉嚟轉去做唔完嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 go3 sam1 sap6 ng5 sap6 luk6, zyun2 lei4 zyun2 heoi3 zou6 m4 jyun4 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是三心兩意，換來換去做不完事情。
examples.english_sentence: He is always indecisive, keeps switching and never finishes anything.

mandarin_meaning: 普普通通／一般般／中等
english_meaning: so-so; mediocre; average
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示事物或表現既不差亦不出色，屬於一般或中等程度。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning something is neither bad nor outstanding — just average or mediocre.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳啲菜對我嚟講中中庭庭，冇乜特別。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 coi3 deoi3 ngo5 lai4 gong2 zung1_zung1_ting4_ting4, mou5 mat1 dak6_bit6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這家餐廳的菜對我來說很一般，沒有什麼特別。
examples.english_sentence: The dishes at this restaurant are so-so to me; nothing special.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次面試表現中中庭庭，可能要再努力先有機會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 min6 si5 biu2 jin2 zung1_zung1_ting4_ting4, ho2 nang4 jiu3 zoi3 nou5 lik6 sin1 jau5 gei1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次面試表現一般，可能要再努力才有機會。
examples.english_sentence: This interview performance was so-so; you may need to work harder to have a chance.

mandarin_meaning: 中间人 / 中介 / 媒人
english_meaning: middleman; intermediary; broker; matchmaker (contextual)
explanation_mandarin: 指在兩方之間居中協調、傳達信息或撮合的人，可指中間人、經紀或媒人。常用於商務談判、居間介紹或撮合關係等情況。
explanation_english: Refers to a person who stands between two parties to coordinate, convey messages, or broker arrangements. Can mean a middleman, agent/broker, or matchmaker depending on context. Commonly used in business, negotiations, or introductions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想做中人，麻煩你哋自己商量。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 zou6 zung1 jan4, maa4 faan4 nei5 dei6 zi6 gei2 soeng1 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想當中間人，你們自己商量吧。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to be the middleman; you guys decide among yourselves.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做中人，幫兩邊談判，最後達成協議。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zung1 jan4, bong1 loeng5 bin1 taam4 pun3, zeoi6 hau6 daat6 sing4 hip3 ji5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他當中間人，幫雙方談判，最後達成協議。
examples.english_sentence: He acted as the middleman, helped both sides negotiate, and they finally reached an agreement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個中人，專門幫人介紹認識，幾叻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 zung1 jan4, zyun1 mun4 bong1 jan4 gaai3 siu6 jing6 sik1, gei2 lek1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是個媒人，專門幫人介紹認識，很厲害。
examples.english_sentence: He's a matchmaker who specializes in introducing people to each other; he's pretty good at it.

mandarin_meaning: 中场球；指出现在比赛中场（中路、半場）区域的球，通常由中场球员处理或控制。
english_meaning: midfield ball; a ball that is in the middle area of the field (the midfield or central zone), usually handled or controlled by midfield players.
explanation_mandarin: 体育用语，常见于足球、篮球等球类运动，指发生在中场区域、由中场球员掌控或需要中场组织的球。
explanation_english: A sports term (commonly used in football/soccer and basketball) referring to a ball that occurs in the midfield area and is typically managed or organized by the midfield players.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 場上中界球控制得好，球隊就可以主導比賽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: coeng4 soeng6 zung1 gaai3 kau4 hung3 zai3 dak1 hou2, kau4 deoi2 zau6 ho2 ji5 zyu2 dou6 bei2 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 场上中界球控制得好，球队就可以主导比赛。
examples.english_sentence: If the team controls the midfield balls well, they can dictate the match.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 教練叫中場球員注意中界球的傳遞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaau3 lin6 giu3 zung1 coeng4 kau4 jyun4 zyu3 ji3 zung1 gaai3 kau4 dik1 cyun4 dai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 教练叫中场球员注意中界球的传递。
examples.english_sentence: The coach told the midfielders to pay attention to distributing balls in the middle.

cantonese: 中秋月不明，花生少收成
jyutping: zung1 cau1 jyut6 bat1 ming4, faa1 saang1 siu2 sau1 sing4
mandarin_meaning: 中秋的月亮不明亮，預示花生的收成會少
english_meaning: If the Mid-Autumn moon isn't bright, the peanut harvest will be poor
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句粵語俗語／諺語，根據天象或氣候預兆來推測農作物收成，意思是中秋時若月色昏暗，通常預示花生等農作物產量會減少。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb that uses a natural omen (the brightness of the Mid-Autumn moon) to predict agricultural yields. It means that if the moon around Mid-Autumn is dim, the peanut harvest is likely to be poor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 農夫話：中秋月不明，花生少收成，大家要早啲準備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nung4 fu1 waa6: zung1 cau1 jyut6 bat1 ming4, faa1 saang1 siu2 sau1 sing4, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zou2 di1 zeon2 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 農民說：中秋月不明，花生少收成，大家要提前準備。
examples.english_sentence: The farmer said: If the Mid-Autumn moon isn't bright, the peanut harvest will be small, so everyone should prepare early.

mandarin_meaning: 喜歡
english_meaning: to like; to be fond of
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話常用口語，表示對人或事物有好感或偏好，相當於普通話的「喜歡」。可作動詞使用。
explanation_english: A common Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to like or be fond of someone or something; indicates preference or affection.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我好中意呢個新電話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 ni1 go3 san1 din6 waa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我很喜歡這部新電話。
examples.english_sentence: I really like this new phone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你中意食咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zung1 ji3 sik6 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你喜歡吃什麼？
examples.english_sentence: What do you like to eat?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢已經鍾意佢好耐喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5 ging1 zung1 ji3 keoi5 hou2 noi6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他已經喜歡她很久了。
examples.english_sentence: He has liked her for a long time.

mandarin_meaning: 临时匆忙 / 在紧急时刻仓促行事
english_meaning: to act hurriedly or in a flurry at the last minute; to deal with something in a rushed, improvised way
explanation_mandarin: 表示在紧急或临到时刻仓促、匆忙地应对或行动，常带有临时、措手不及或不从容的意味。
explanation_english: Indicates acting hurriedly or frantically when faced with an urgent situation or at the last minute; often implies improvised, rushed, or disorganized behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好臨急臨忙先嚟搵我，早啲講啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lam4 gap1 lam4 mong4 sin1 lai4 wan2 ngo5, zou2 di1 gong2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要临到紧要关头才来找我，早点说吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't wait until the last minute to come to me—tell me earlier.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日臨急臨忙，做嘢好亂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 lam4 gap1 lam4 mong4, zou6 je5 hou2 lyun6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是临急临忙，做事很乱。
examples.english_sentence: He always acts in a hurry and is very disorganized.

mandarin_meaning: 临时匆忙开始（做某事/开设活动/开帖等），通常准备不足或仓促应付
english_meaning: to hastily start something at the last minute, often without adequate preparation; to scramble to set up a project/event/thread in a rush
explanation_mandarin: “临急开坑”用于口语或网络语境，表示在事情快到期或情况紧急时，匆忙开始某件事或临时开设一个项目/帖子等，带有准备不足或仓促应付的含义。
explanation_english: Used in spoken and online Cantonese, “臨急開坑” means to start something hastily at the last minute (e.g., a project, event, or online thread), implying insufficient preparation and a rushed approach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好等到最後先臨急開坑，會做得好差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 dang2 dou3 zeoi3 hau6 sin1 lam4 gap1 hoi1 haang1, wui5 zou6 dak1 hou2 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要等到最后才临急开坑，会做得很差。
examples.english_sentence: Don't wait until the last minute to hastily start something — it'll turn out poorly.

mandarin_meaning: 临时发生紧急情况；在最后一刻临时有急事
english_meaning: at the last minute due to an urgent matter; sudden and urgent
explanation_mandarin: 表示事情在临近时刻突然出现紧急情况，通常用来说明因突发状况而临时改变计划或无法如约。
explanation_english: Describes a situation that becomes urgent or sudden at the last minute; often used to explain a change of plans or inability to attend because of an unexpected urgent matter.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我臨時臨急有嘢出咗，去唔到你哋嘅聚會，唔好意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lam4 si4 lam4 gap1 jau5 je5 ceot1 zo2, heoi3 m4 dou3 nei5 dei6 ge3 zeoi6 wui2, m4 hou2 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我临时有急事，去不了你们的聚会，抱歉。
examples.english_sentence: Something urgent came up at the last minute; I can't make it to your gathering. Sorry.

mandarin_meaning: 临到年老才开始学某项技能（常带贬义，指为时已晚或徒劳无益）。
english_meaning: To take up a skill late in life (often pejorative, implying it's too late or futile).
explanation_mandarin: “临老学吹打”字面是临到年老才学吹打（吹奏和打击乐器），常用来比喻人在年纪大了才开始学新事物，含有为时已晚或效果不佳的意味。
explanation_english: Literally 'learning wind and percussion in old age.' Used metaphorically to describe someone who starts learning something late in life, often with the connotation that it's too late or unlikely to be successful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今年五十幾歲先開始學彈結他，俾人笑話係臨老學吹打。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 nin4 ng5 sap6 gei2 seoi3 sin1 hoi1 ci2 hok6 daan6 git3 taa1, bei2 jan4 siu3 waa6 hai6 lam4 lou5 hok6 ceoi1 daa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今年五十多岁才开始学弹吉他，被人笑话是临老学吹打。
examples.english_sentence: He only started learning guitar in his fifties; people mock him, calling it 'taking up something late in life.'

cantonese: 为人为到底，送佛送到系
jyutping: wai4 jan4 wai4 dou3 dai2, sung3 fat6 sung3 dou3 sai1
mandarin_meaning: 做人或做事要做到彻底；既然要帮就帮到底
english_meaning: Do something all the way / go the whole hog — if you help or commit to something, see it through to the end
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語用來形容做人或辦事情要堅持到底、徹底完成；既然答應或開始做，就不要半途而廢。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying meaning one should be thorough and see things through; if you promise to help or do something, do it completely rather than stopping halfway.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做人一向好實在，為人為到底，送佛送到西。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 jan4 jat1 hoeng3 hou2 sat6 zoi6, wai4 jan4 wai4 dou3 dai2, sung3 fat6 sung3 dou3 sai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為人一向很實在，做事做到底，既然要幫就幫到底。
examples.english_sentence: He's always been dependable — he sees things through; if he's going to help, he helps all the way.

mandarin_meaning: 为了糊口、为生计奔波；辛苦谋生
english_meaning: to hustle to make a living; to run around working hard to earn money
explanation_mandarin: 口語表達，指為了維持生計而四處奔波、辛苦工作。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression meaning to work hard or run around to earn a living and support oneself or one's family.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家為口奔驰，每日都做兩份工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 wai4 hau2 ban1 ci4, mui5 jat6 dou1 zou6 loeng5 fan6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在为口奔驰，每天都做两份工作。
examples.english_sentence: He is hustling to make a living now, working two jobs every day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做呢行係為口奔驰，無時間顧自己。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 ni1 hong4 hai6 wai4 hau2 ban1 ci4, mou5 si4 gaan3 gu3 zi6 gei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做这行是为口奔驰，没时间照顾自己。
examples.english_sentence: Working in this line is just to earn a living, leaving no time to take care of oneself.

mandarin_meaning: 無法原諒 / 不能放下
english_meaning: cannot forgive; unable to let go (hold a grudge)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，用來表示對別人的行為或事情無法原諒或放下，常帶有怨懟或耿耿於懷的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning one cannot forgive or let go (holds a grudge) about someone's action or an event. It often conveys resentment or inability to move on.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘅事，我真係為唔過佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 ge3 si6, ngo5 zan1 hai6 wai6 m4 gwo3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做的事，我真的無法原諒他。
examples.english_sentence: I really can't forgive what he did.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你諗住我會為唔過你就錯喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 nam2 zyu6 ngo5 wui5 wai6 m4 gwo3 nei5 zau6 co3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你以為我會對你耿耿於懷就錯了。
examples.english_sentence: If you think I'll hold a grudge against you, you're mistaken.

mandarin_meaning: 凑合；将就；勉强可以；能過得去
english_meaning: passable; just acceptable; to get by; to make do
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示某事物或某做法雖然不完美，但勉強可以接受或夠用，類似「將就」「凑合」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning something is barely acceptable or adequate — not ideal but good enough to get by. Similar to 'make do' or 'passable'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間酒店雖然唔豪華，但按價錢嚟講為得過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 zau2 dim3 seoi1 jin4 m4 hou4 waa4, daan6 on3 gaa3 cin2 lai4 gong2 wai4 dak1 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家酒店虽然不豪华，但按价格来说凑合得过。
examples.english_sentence: This hotel isn't luxurious, but for the price it's passable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔鍾意呢道菜，但將就下都為得過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 ni1 dou6 coi3, daan6 zoeng1 zau6 haa5 dou1 wai4 dak1 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不喜欢这道菜，但将就一下也凑合得过。
examples.english_sentence: I don't like this dish, but it's acceptable if I make do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁敷衍做嗰份工作，老闆肯定話唔為得過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 fuk1 jin2 zou6 go2 fan6 gung1 zok3, lou5 baan2 hang2 ding6 waa6 m4 wai4 dak1 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这么敷衍做那份工作，老板肯定会说不能将就/不能接受。
examples.english_sentence: If you do that job so perfunctorily, the boss will definitely say it's not acceptable.

jyutping: wai6 lou5 bat1 zyun1, gaau3 waai6 zi2 syun1
mandarin_meaning: 年紀大了卻不自重、不守長者體面，反而給子孫做壞榜樣。
english_meaning: An elder who does not behave with dignity or respect, thereby setting a bad example and corrupting the younger generation.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容長輩年紀大了卻不檢點、不尊重禮儀或做出不良行為，對子孫有不良影響，成為壞榜樣。
explanation_english: Used to describe an elder who, despite their age, behaves improperly or without dignity and thus becomes a bad influence or example for their descendants.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為老不尊，教壞子孫，啲孫仔都學晒佢啲壞習慣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 lou5 bat1 zyun1, gaau3 waai6 zi2 syun1, di1 syun1 zai2 dou1 hok6 saai3 keoi5 di1 waai6 zaap6 gwaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他年紀大了卻不自重，給子孫做壞榜樣，孫子都學了他的壞習慣。
examples.english_sentence: He, though elderly, behaves without dignity and sets a bad example for his descendants; the grandchildren have picked up his bad habits.

mandarin_meaning: 愛吃的人；貪吃的人（粤語俚語）
english_meaning: a foodie / someone who loves to eat (playful slang for a greedy eater)
explanation_mandarin: 「为食猫」是粤語的一個俚語，用來形容非常愛吃或貪吃的人，語氣多為戲稱或親切的調侃。
explanation_english: “For-eating cat” (Cantonese slang) describes someone who loves to eat or is greedy for food; often used playfully to tease a foodie.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你真係個為食貓，見到嘢食就停唔到口。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 go3 wai4 sik6 maau1, gin3 dou3 je5 sik6 zau6 ting4 m4 dou3 hau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你真的是個愛吃的人，看到東西就停不下來。
examples.english_sentence: You're really a foodie — when you see food you can't stop eating.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司有免費午餐，成班為食貓都走埋嚟試新嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jau5 min5 fai3 ng5 caan1, seng4 baan1 wai4 sik6 maau1 dou1 zau2 maai4 lai4 si3 san1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司有免費午餐，整群愛吃的人都過來嘗新東西。
examples.english_sentence: The company had a free lunch, and a bunch of foodies all came over to try the new dishes.

mandarin_meaning: 主角；小說、戲劇、電影等的主要人物
english_meaning: protagonist; main character (the principal figure in a story, play, or film)
explanation_mandarin: 指作品中的主要人物，故事情節通常以此人物的經歷或行為為主線展開。
explanation_english: Refers to the main character in a work of fiction (story, play, film, etc.); the plot typically centers on this person's experiences or actions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺部戲入面係主人公，所有情節都圍住佢發展。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 bou6 hei3 jap6 min6 hai6 zyu2 jan4 gung1, so2 jau5 cing4 zit3 dou1 wai4 zyu6 keoi5 faat3 zin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在那部戲裡是主人公，所有情節都圍繞著他展開。
examples.english_sentence: He is the protagonist in that film; all the events revolve around him.

mandarin_meaning: （口語、帶貶義）愛發號施令或跋扈的女人；亦可指女主人／女店主
english_meaning: A bossy or domineering woman; (also) the female owner/hostess
explanation_mandarin: 「主人婆」常用作粵語口語，通常帶貶義，指喜歡管人、發號施令或跋扈的女性；在中性語境也可指房子或店舖的女主人或女店主。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "主人婆" is a colloquial term often used derogatorily for a domineering, bossy woman who orders others around; in neutral contexts it can simply mean a female owner or hostess.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好似個主人婆，成日指手畫腳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 ci5 go3 zyu2 jan4 po4, sing4 jat6 zi2 sau2 waak6 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她很像主人婆，总是指手画脚。
examples.english_sentence: She seems like a bossy woman, always telling people what to do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺屋企佢係主人婆，連小事都要插手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 uk1 kei2 keoi5 hai6 zyu2 jan4 po4, lin4 siu2 si6 dou1 jiu3 caap3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在家里她是主人婆，连小事都要插手。
examples.english_sentence: At home she's the bossy lady, meddling even in small matters.

mandarin_meaning: 其一……其二……（首先……其次……）
english_meaning: first..., second... (used to list points/reasons)
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用來列舉或說明次序的慣用語，相當於「首先……其次……」。常見於口語或非正式書寫。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to enumerate points or reasons — equivalent to 'first..., second...'. Common in spoken Cantonese and informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我冇去旅行，久一冇錢，久二忙緊工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mou5 heoi3 leoi5haang4, gau2 jat1 mou5 cin2, gau2 ji6 mong4 gan2 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我沒去旅行，第一沒錢，第二忙著工作。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't go on a trip: first I had no money, second I was busy with work.

mandarin_meaning: 久而久之；時間長了之後
english_meaning: over time; in the long run; eventually
explanation_mandarin: 表示經過較長時間後，情況逐漸發生變化或產生結果。為口語常用的副詞性短語，相當於普通話的“久而久之”。
explanation_english: Indicates that after a long period something gradually changes or happens. A colloquial adverbial phrase equivalent to Mandarin '久而久之' — 'over time' or 'in the long run.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你日日都咁做，久時久佢都會習慣㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jat6 jat6 dou1 gam2 zou6, gau2 si4 gau2 keoi5 dou1 wui5 zaap6 gwaan3 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你天天這樣做，久而久之他會習慣的。
examples.english_sentence: If you do that every day, over time he'll get used to it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個項目拖得太耐，久時久成本會上升。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 hong6 muk6 to1 dak1 taai3 noi6, gau2 si4 gau2 sing4 bun2 wui5 soeng5 sing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 項目拖得太久，久而久之成本會上升。
examples.english_sentence: If the project is delayed too long, in the long run the costs will increase.

mandarin_meaning: 只不过
english_meaning: just; merely; only; it's just that
explanation_mandarin: 用来表示程度或原因上的限制，意为“只是、不过”，常用于口語或書面中的轉折說法。
explanation_english: Used to indicate limitation in degree or reason, meaning "just" or "merely"; often used to soften or introduce a contrast/explanation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢之不過冇時間，唔係唔想幫你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi1 bat1 gwo3 mou5 si4 gaan3, m4 hai6 m4 soeng2 bong1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只是沒有時間，不是因為不想幫你。
examples.english_sentence: He's just short on time; it's not that he doesn't want to help you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我之不過係想試下啫，唔代表我唔認真。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi1 bat1 gwo3 hai6 soeng2 si3 haa5 ze1, m4 doi6 biu2 ngo5 m4 jing6 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我只是想先試一下，不代表我不認真。
examples.english_sentence: I'm just trying it out; it doesn't mean I'm not serious.

mandarin_meaning: 是不是／不是嗎
english_meaning: isn't it? / right? (question tag used to seek confirmation)
explanation_mandarin: 「之唔系」是廣東話口語或網絡用語，用作句末的附加疑問，表示尋求對方確認或強調某事，語氣接近「是不是／不是嗎」。在香港口語與網上文本中較常見，屬非正式用法。
explanation_english: “之唔系” is a colloquial Cantonese/question-tag expression used at the end of a sentence to seek confirmation or emphasize something, similar to “isn't it?” or “right?”. It is informal and often seen in spoken Hong Kong Cantonese and online text.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日會返工，之唔系？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 wui5 faan1 gung1, zi1 m4 hai6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天會去上班，不是嗎？
examples.english_sentence: You're going to work today, aren't you?

jyutping: wu1 wan4 soeng5 deng2, fung1 jyu5 m4 sai2 ceng2
mandarin_meaning: 乌云压顶，风雨不需要邀请就会来临；比喻祸患或麻烦不可避免，即将发生。
english_meaning: Dark clouds overhead, wind and rain need no invitation — indicates that trouble or misfortune is imminent and unavoidable.
explanation_mandarin: 是一句粤语俗语，字面指天空乌云密布，风雨自然会来；引申为当征兆出现时，灾祸或麻烦往往不可避免，形容险象环生或凶多吉少的局面。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally describing dark clouds gathering and wind and rain arriving without invitation. Figuratively it means that once ominous signs appear, trouble or disaster is likely inevitable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司業績持續下跌，烏云上頂，風雨唔使請。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jip6 zik1 ci4 zuk6 haa6 dit3, wu1 wan4 soeng5 deng2, fung1 jyu5 m4 sai2 ceng2
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司业绩持续下滑，乌云压顶，风雨不需邀请就会来临。
examples.english_sentence: With the company's results continuing to fall, dark clouds gather overhead — trouble will come without needing an invitation.

cantonese: 乌云拦东，唔系雨就系风
jyutping: wu1 wan4 laam4 dung1, m4 hai6 jyu5 zau6 hai6 fung1
mandarin_meaning: 乌云聚集在东方，要么下雨要么刮风；比喻有不祥的征兆，可能会有麻烦或祸事发生。
english_meaning: Dark clouds gather in the east — either rain or wind; an ominous sign meaning trouble or bad events are likely coming.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粤语俗语，用天气的征兆比喻不好的预兆，表示可能会有麻烦、变故或不幸即将发生。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb-like saying that uses a weather sign as a metaphor for an ominous warning — it implies that trouble or misfortune is likely imminent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到市中心開始烏雲密布，我阿婆話：烏雲攔東，唔係雨就係風，大家小心啲啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou2 si5 zung1 sam1 hoi1 ci2 wu1 wan4 mat6 bou6, ngo5 aa3 po4 waa6: wu1 wan4 laam4 dung1, m4 hai6 jyu5 zau6 hai6 fung1, daai6 gaa1 siu2 sam1 di1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到市中心开始乌云密布，我奶奶说：乌云拦东，不是要下雨就是要刮风，大家要小心。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing dark clouds gather over the city center, my grandma said: 'Dark clouds in the east — it's either rain or wind,' meaning everyone should be careful.

mandarin_meaning: 孤身一人；單打獨鬥，獨自完成某事（口語）
english_meaning: alone; single-handed; doing something by oneself without help
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語（表狀態/方式，類似形容詞/副詞用法）
partOfSpeech_english: colloquial phrase (descriptive; can function like an adjective/adverb)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，表示一個人獨自去做某事或獨自面對某情況，含有不依靠他人或單獨行動的意思，常見於香港日常用語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to be alone or to do something single-handedly. It describes acting or facing a situation without others' help or company; commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今次要乌哩单刀去旅行，冇人陪我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ci3 jiu3 wu1 lei1 daan1 dou1 heoi3 leoi5 hang4, mou5 jan4 pui4 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次我要孤身一人去旅行，没人陪我。
examples.english_sentence: This time I'm going on the trip alone; no one is coming with me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日乌哩单刀做嘢，唔鍾意搵人幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 wu1 lei1 daan1 dou1 zou6 je5, m4 zung1 ji3 wan2 jan4 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常獨自一人做事，不喜歡找人幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: He/she often works alone and doesn't like to ask for help.

mandarin_meaning: 黑漆漆／漆黑一片，形容非常黑暗；也可指深夜或光線極少的時候
english_meaning: pitch-dark; completely dark; (colloquially) very late at night or in total darkness
explanation_mandarin: 「烏燈黑火」是廣東話口語，形容環境極為昏暗或漆黑，沒有光亮；亦可用來指夜深或天色很晚。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning extremely dark or pitch-black (no light); can also refer to very late at night or an area with very little lighting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家咁夜，街邊烏燈黑火，唔好一個人行夜路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 gam2 je6, gaai1 bin1 wu1 dang1 hak1 fo2, m4 hou2 jat1 go3 jan4 haang4 je6 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在這麼晚，街上黑漆漆的，不要一個人夜行。
examples.english_sentence: It's so late and the streets are pitch-dark; don't walk alone at night.

jyutping: wu1 jing4 lau1 maa5 mei5, jat1 paak3 loeng5 saan3
mandarin_meaning: 一拍两散；一有争执或矛盾就分道扬镳，关系或合作立即结束
english_meaning: To part ways at the first sign of trouble; a relationship or cooperation breaks off immediately after a quarrel
explanation_mandarin: 形容双方在发生争执或出现问题时，马上各走各路，合作或关系迅速瓦解，不再继续。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where two parties immediately split up or end their cooperation at the first disagreement or problem.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋一吵就乌蝇搂马尾，一拍两散，冇得再合作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 jat1 caau3 zau6 wu1 jing4 lau1 maa5 mei5, jat1 paak3 loeng5 saan3, mou5 dak1 zoi3 hap6 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们一吵架就一拍两散，不能再合作。
examples.english_sentence: They part ways at the first quarrel; they can't cooperate anymore.

mandarin_meaning: 指經常犯錯或鬧出烏龍、出糗的人，帶戲謔或輕蔑意味（口語/俚語）
english_meaning: A slangy nickname meaning "king of blunders" — someone who frequently makes silly mistakes or causes embarrassing mix-ups.
explanation_mandarin: 「烏龍王」為粵語／俚語用法，用來形容老是出錯、鬧烏龍或成為笑柄的人，通常帶有調侃或輕微貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to label a person who repeatedly makes mistakes or causes embarrassing incidents. Usually joking or mildly derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日搞錯嘢，大家都叫佢烏龍王。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gaau2 co3 je5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 giu3 keoi5 wu1 lung4 wong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是搞錯事情，大家都叫他烏龍王。
examples.english_sentence: He always messes things up; everyone calls him the 'king of blunders'.

jyutping: wu1 gwai1 paa4 mun4 haam2, m4 dit3 m4 zeon3
mandarin_meaning: 形容人做事犹豫不前、不主动，只有在出问题或被逼时才行动。
english_meaning: Describes someone who is hesitant or passive and won't take action unless something goes wrong or they are forced to.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用乌龟爬门槛的形象，比喻人做事拖沓或过于谨慎，不主动进取，往往要等到“跌”了（出了事）才会去做。
explanation_english: The saying uses the image of a turtle crawling along a doorstep to illustrate a person who is slow, overly cautious, or passive—only acting when something goes wrong or they are forced to.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好似烏龜爬門檻，唔跌唔進，等到出事先嚟處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 ci5 wu1 gwai1 paa4 mun4 haam2, m4 dit3 m4 zeon3, dang2 dou3 ceot1 si6 sin1 lai4 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事像乌龟爬门槛，不跌不进，等到出事才来处理。
examples.english_sentence: He works like a turtle crawling the doorstep—won't move unless something goes wrong; he waits until there's a problem to deal with it.

mandarin_meaning: 拟声词，表示轻快的碰撞或弹跳声；口语中也可用来形容轻快、有弹性的感觉或声音。
english_meaning: An onomatopoeia representing a light 'ping-ping' tapping or bouncing sound; colloquially can describe something springy or lively.
explanation_mandarin: 「乒乒」多用作擬聲詞，模仿輕快的敲擊或彈跳聲。常見於口語描述物件彈跳、敲擊或電子提示音等情況。
explanation_english: Used as an onomatopoeia to mimic light tapping or bouncing sounds. Common in colloquial speech to describe bouncing objects, taps, or notification-like sounds.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個籃球喺地下彈到乒乒聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 laam4 kau4 hai2 dei6 haa6 daan6 dou3 ping1 ping1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 篮球在地上弹起来发出“乒乒”的声音。
examples.english_sentence: The basketball bounced on the ground making a 'ping ping' sound.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 電話響乒乒兩聲，我就知道有新訊息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: din6 waa2 hoeng2 ping1 ping1 loeng5 seng1, ngo5 zau6 zi1 dou6 jau5 san1 seon3 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 电话响了“乒乒”两声，我就知道有新消息。
examples.english_sentence: The phone made two 'ping ping' sounds, so I knew there was a new message.

mandarin_meaning: 乒乓的聲音；常用來形容乒乓球拍擊或器物碰撞發出的清脆聲響
english_meaning: the 'ping-pong' sound; onomatopoeic for the crisp pinging/clattering noise (e.g. table-tennis or small objects hitting)
explanation_mandarin: 模仿聲音的詞語，用來描述像「乒」、「乓」那樣的清脆撞擊聲，既可指打乒乓球的聲音，也可形容碗碟或金屬物件碰撞的響聲。
explanation_english: An onomatopoeic noun representing a crisp 'ping-pong' noise. It can refer to the sound of a table-tennis ball being struck or to similar clinking/clattering sounds from objects hitting each other.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚我喺度聽到廳入面傳嚟乒乓聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 ngo5 hai2 dou6 teng1 dou3 ting1 jap6 min6 cyun4 loi4 ping1 pong1 sing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚上我听到客厅里传来乒乓声。
examples.english_sentence: At night I heard ping-pong sounds coming from the living room.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隔離屋有人練習打乒乓球，成日都聽到乒乓聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaak3 lei4 uk1 jau5 jan4 lin6 zaap6 daa2 ping1 pong1 kau4, sing4 jat6 dou1 teng1 dou3 ping1 pong1 sing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 隔壁有人练习打乒乓球，经常能听到乒乓声。
examples.english_sentence: Someone next door practices table tennis; you can often hear the ping-pong sounds.

mandarin_meaning: 乖寶寶（戲稱，用於小孩、寵物或親密對象，表示聽話/可愛）
english_meaning: literally 'good pig' — a slang term of endearment meaning 'good/obedient little one' (used playfully or teasingly for children, pets, or close people)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，字面為「乖」+「豬」，常作愛稱或戲稱，稱呼小孩、寵物或親密的人，含義接近「乖寶寶」或「聽話的人」。語氣多為親昵或打趣，有時帶輕微揶揄，屬非正式用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term combining '乖' (obedient/good) and '豬' (pig). Used as an affectionate or teasing pet name for children, pets, or close people — similar to 'good little one' or 'good piggy'. Informal and can be playful or mildly teasing depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 乖豬，快啲食飯啦，唔好玩手機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gwai1 zyu1, faai3 di1 sik6 faan6 laa1, m4 hou2 waan2 sau2 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 乖豬，快點吃飯，不要玩手機。
examples.english_sentence: Good pig, hurry up and eat, don't play with your phone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽咪成日叫隻小狗做乖豬，好可愛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 seng4 jat6 giu3 zek3 siu2 gau2 zou6 gwai1 zyu1, hou2 ho2 oi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽常常叫小狗「乖豬」，很可愛。
examples.english_sentence: Mom always calls the puppy 'good pig'—so cute.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁聽話，真係乖豬喎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 teng1 waa6, zan1 hai6 gwai1 zyu1 wo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這麼聽話，真是乖豬喔。
examples.english_sentence: You're so obedient — you're really a 'good pig'.

mandarin_meaning: 這是什麼鬼／這是什麼東西（用於驚訝、不滿或不解）
english_meaning: What the heck is this? / What is this thing? (expression of surprise, annoyance, or disbelief)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俚語，用來表示驚訝、不滿或不解，相當於「這是什麼鬼？」或「這是甚麼東西？」
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to show surprise, annoyance, or bewilderment — roughly equivalent to "what the heck is this?"

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個乜哩零青嚟㗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 mat1 lei1 ling4 cing1 lai4 gaa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個是什麼東西？
examples.english_sentence: What is this thing?

mandarin_meaning: 什么话 / 你在说什么 / 开什么玩笑
english_meaning: What are you saying? / What the heck? (expressing disbelief or challenging a statement)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，用于表示惊讶、不相信或反驳别人的话，类似“你在说什么？”或“开什么玩笑？”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to show surprise, disbelief, or to challenge what someone said. Similar to "what are you talking about?" or "what the heck?"

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講乜嘢話？我完全唔明你講緊乜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 mat1 je5 waa6? ngo5 jyun4 cyun4 m4 ming4 nei5 gong2 gan2 mat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说什么？我完全不明白你在说什么。
examples.english_sentence: What are you saying? I totally don't understand what you're talking about.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話佢贏咗一百萬？乜嘢話！我唔信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 keoi5 jing4 zo2 jat1 baak3 maan6? mat1 je5 waa6! ngo5 m4 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说他赢了一百万？开什么玩笑！我不信。
examples.english_sentence: He said he won a million? What the heck! I don't believe it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話你識整電腦？乜嘢話，連開機都唔識？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 nei5 sik1 zing2 din6 nou5? mat1 je5 waa6, lin4 hoi1 gei1 dou1 m4 sik1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说你会修电脑？开什么玩笑，连开机都不会？
examples.english_sentence: You say you can fix computers? What are you talking about — you can't even turn one on?

mandarin_meaning: （口語）什麼東東／亂七八糟的事／胡說
english_meaning: a colloquial expression for unspecified nonsense or something ridiculous; 'what-ever/what-not' or 'rubbish/nonsense'
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俚語，用來表示某件事或說話內容不明確、荒謬或令人不屑，常帶貶義或不屑的語氣，相當於「什麼東西／胡說」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to refer to something vague, ridiculous, or nonsensical. It often conveys disdain or dismissal and is similar to saying 'what-ever/whatnot' or calling something 'nonsense'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講啲乜头乜路，我都唔想聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 di1 mat1 tau4 mat1 lou6, ngo5 dou1 m4 soeng2 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是說些亂七八糟的話，我也不想聽。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks nonsense; I don't want to listen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講啲乜头乜路嘢，講清楚啲啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 di1 mat1 tau4 mat1 lou6 je5, gong2 cing1 co2 di1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說些什麼亂七八糟的東西，說清楚一點吧。
examples.english_sentence: What kind of nonsense are you talking about? Say it more clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 什么鬼 / 干什么
english_meaning: What the hell? / What on earth? (expressing surprise, annoyance or disbelief)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，帶有驚訝、不滿或困惑的語氣，類似「幹什麼」「搞什麼鬼」。常用於非正式場合或口語中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese interjection expressing surprise, annoyance, or disbelief—similar to "what the hell" or "what on earth." Used informally in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你乜斜呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 mat1 ce4 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你干什么啊？
examples.english_sentence: What the hell are you doing?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我琴日約咗佢，佢冇嚟，乜斜唔覆我？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 kam4 jat6 joek3 zo2 keoi5, keoi5 mou5 lai4, mat1 ce4 m4 fuk1 ngo5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我昨天约了他，他没来，怎么还不回我？
examples.english_sentence: I arranged to meet him yesterday, he didn't show up—what the hell, he didn't reply to me?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喂，你乜斜咁講啊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai3, nei5 mat1 ce4 gam2 gong2 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 喂，你为什么那样说？
examples.english_sentence: Hey, why are you saying that?

mandarin_meaning: 你在說什麼／胡說、表示難以置信或反駁的口語感嘆詞
english_meaning: What are you talking about? / Nonsense! (colloquial expression of disbelief or rebuttal)
explanation_mandarin: 「乜说话」是廣東話的口語用法，常用來表示不相信、反駁或覺得對方說得荒謬，相當於普通話的「你在說什麼／胡說」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to show disbelief, to rebut, or to say that something is nonsense—equivalent to "What are you talking about?" or "Nonsense!"

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話佢買咗部新車？乜说话！佢邊有錢啫？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 keoi5 maai5 zo2 bou6 san1 ce1? mat1 syut3 waa6! keoi5 bin1 jau5 cin2 ze3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說他買了一輛新車？你在說什麼！他哪有錢？
examples.english_sentence: He said he bought a new car? What are you talking about! How could he have the money?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你遲到一個鐘，仲話我遲？乜说话！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ci4 dou3 jat1 go3 zung1, zung6 waa6 ngo5 ci4? mat1 syut3 waa6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你遲到一個小時，還說我遲到？你在說什麼！
examples.english_sentence: You were an hour late and you still say I'm late? What are you talking about!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你啱啱講乜说话啊？我未聽清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 aam1 aam1 gong2 mat1 syut3 waa6 aa3? ngo5 mei6 teng1 cing1 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你剛才說什麼啊？我沒聽清楚。
examples.english_sentence: What did you just say? I didn't hear clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 什麼 / 什麼東西
english_meaning: what; what (thing); used colloquially to ask 'what' or as an exclamation
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示「什麼」，可用於詢問事物或作為驚訝、不滿等感嘆語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term meaning 'what'. Used to ask about something or as an exclamation to express surprise, disbelief, or annoyance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講乜野？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 mat1 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在說什麼？
examples.english_sentence: What are you saying?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢樣嘢係乜野？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 joeng6 je5 hai6 mat1 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個東西是什麼？
examples.english_sentence: What is this thing?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今朝做緊乜野？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ziu1 zou6 gan2 mat1 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天早上在做什麼？
examples.english_sentence: What was he doing this morning?

mandarin_meaning: （口语、俚语）表示惊讶、不满或觉得荒谬，类似“什么鬼”“开什么玩笑”
english_meaning: Colloquial/slang exclamation expressing disbelief, annoyance, or that something is nonsense (similar to “what the hell” / “what the heck”)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感叹词 / 口语 / 俚语
explanation_mandarin: “乜（歪）”由“乜”与“歪”组合，用于粤语口语中对对方的话或行为表示质疑、不满或轻蔑，语气可带惊讶或责备。
explanation_english: “乜（歪）” combines the Cantonese interrogative “乜” with “歪” as a colloquial/slang marker. It is used to question or dismiss what someone said or did, conveying disbelief, annoyance, or that something is absurd.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講啲乜歪嘢啊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 di1 mat1 waai1 je5 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在说什么鬼话啊？
examples.english_sentence: What nonsense are you talking?

jyutping: gau2 jyut6 sau1 leoi4, sap6 jyut6 sau1 loi6
mandarin_meaning: （廣東話俗諺）指九月多雷雨，十月天氣轉涼或進入收成時節。該諺語為時令說法，文中「爧」字較少見，解釋有多種可能（如指霜、收穗等）。
english_meaning: A Cantonese proverb about seasonal change/harvest: 'September brings thunder, October brings ...' — traditionally referring to more thunderstorms in September and cooling/harvest time in October. Used literally for weather/harvest timing and figuratively to mean it's time to reap results or face consequences. Note: the character '爧' is rare and its exact meaning varies by source.
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東話的時令諺語，用來描述季節、天氣或農事節氣的變化。語句字面為「九月多雷、十月有爧」，實際口傳中「爧」字罕見，常被解釋為霜、收穗或泛指十月的收成與天氣轉涼。亦可引申為「到了時候要收尾或承擔結果」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese seasonal proverb describing weather/harvest changes. Literally ‘September collects thunder, October collects (爧)’. The character '爧' is uncommon and variously interpreted (e.g., frost, harvest spike, or generally the arrival of cooler/harvest time). Figuratively it can mean ‘the time to gather results or face consequences’.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆成日講：九月收雷，十月收爧，出海要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 sing4 jat6 gong2: gau2 jyut6 sau1 leoi4, sap6 jyut6 sau1 loi6, ceot1 hoi2 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶常說：九月多雷雨，十月要注意（或是收穫時節），出海要小心。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma always says: 'September brings thunder, October brings ...' — be careful when going out to sea.

mandarin_meaning: 乞丐相 / 一副可憐樣
english_meaning: to have a beggar-like, pitiful appearance; to look miserable or pitiable
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞（口語）/ 名詞短語
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，形容一個人的外表或表情看起來可憐、破落或像在討飯，常用來表示可憐或輕微貶義或戲謔。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term describing someone who looks pitiful, shabby, or as if begging; often used jokingly or with mild derogation to elicit pity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好擺乞兒相啦，抬頭行路！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 baai2 hat1 ji4 soeng1 laa1, toi4 tau4 haang4 lou6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別擺出乞丐相，抬頭走路！
examples.english_sentence: Don't put on that beggar-like look — hold your head up when you walk!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗搏同情擺乞兒相，結果大家都冇理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 bok3 tung4 cing4 baai2 hat1 ji4 soeng1, git3 gwo2 daai6 gaa1 dou1 mou5 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了博取同情擺出乞丐相，結果大家都不理會。
examples.english_sentence: He put on a pitiful, beggar-like face to gain sympathy, but in the end nobody paid attention.

jyutping: maai5 haam4 jyu4 fong3 saang1, bat1 gu3 sei2 wut6
mandarin_meaning: 比喻做徒劳无益或毫无意义的举动；也可指明知无用或有害仍然去做、不顾后果的鲁莽行为。
english_meaning: A slang/idiomatic expression meaning to perform a pointless or futile gesture; to do something obviously useless or to act recklessly regardless of consequences.
explanation_mandarin: “买咸鱼放生”字面上像把已死或无用的咸鱼放生，形容做無用的表面功夫或徒劳的行为；“不顾死活”加强语气，指不顾后果或明知无用仍然去做。
explanation_english: Literally 'buy salted fish and release it, not caring about life or death.' It satirically describes doing a meaningless or futile act (a pointless gesture) or acting heedlessly without regard for consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日買咸鱼放生，做啲明知冇用嘅嘢，根本就係浪費時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 maai5 haam4 jyu4 fong3 saang1, zou6 di1 ming4 zi1 mou5 jung6 ge3 je5, gan1 bun2 zau6 hai6 long6 fai3 si4 gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是做徒劳无益的举动，做一些明知无用的事，根本就是浪费时间。
examples.english_sentence: He always makes futile gestures, doing things that are obviously useless — it's a complete waste of time.

jyutping: maai5 ding6 gwaan1 coi4 gwat6 ding6 dam2, teng1 sei2
mandarin_meaning: 买好棺材、挖好坟，听天由命；表示事情已成定局，只能认命或等死。
english_meaning: Literally 'buy the coffin and dig the grave, just accept death' — to resign oneself to the inevitable; accept that there's no turning back.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來形容情況無可挽回、注定失敗或遭遇災難，只有認命或等待結果，帶有無奈和消極的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression conveying resignation — the situation is hopeless or decided, so one accepts the outcome (often with a sense of helplessness).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 咁樣搞落去，真係要买定棺材掘定氹，听死啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam2 joeng6 gaau2 lok6 heoi3, zan1 hai6 jiu3 maai5 ding6 gwaan1 coi4 gwat6 ding6 dam2, teng1 sei2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这样下去，真要买好棺材、挖好坟，听天由命了。
examples.english_sentence: If things keep going like this, we'll have to buy the coffin and dig the grave — just resign ourselves to death.

mandarin_meaning: （俚语）做表面功夫；敷衍了事
english_meaning: colloquial/slang: to do something perfunctorily; to go through the motions; a token gesture
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 动词短语（口语 / 俚语）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語說法，字面是「買水那樣」，用來形容人做事只是表面應付、敷衍，沒有真正投入或認真處理。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression literally meaning "like buying water." It describes doing something superficially or perfunctorily — merely a token effort rather than sincere or thorough action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好淨係買水噉头，真係幫下手啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 maai5 seoi2 gam2 tau4, zan1 hai6 bong1 haa5 sau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別只是做表面功夫，真的幫一下忙吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just do it half‑heartedly — actually help out, please.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲承諾多數都係買水噉头，唔可靠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 sing4 nok6 do1 sou3 dou1 hai6 maai5 seoi2 gam2 tau4, m4 ho2 kaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的承诺多數都是敷衍了事，不可靠。
examples.english_sentence: Most of his promises are just token gestures — not reliable.

mandarin_meaning: 胡说八道／瞎扯（粗俗俚语）
english_meaning: to talk nonsense / to spout bullshit (vulgar slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语粗俗俚语，表示某人说话没有道理或胡扯，常带蔑视或不耐烦的语气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar slang phrase meaning to talk nonsense or bullshit. Used to dismiss or criticize someone's words, often with contempt or impatience.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日乱噏廿四，唔好信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 lyun6 jap1 jaa6 sei3, m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是胡说八道，别信他。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks nonsense; don't trust him.

mandarin_meaning: 胡乱说话、没必要地乱讲（常见写法为「亂噏無謂」）
english_meaning: To talk nonsense or ramble pointlessly; dismissively saying someone's remarks are pointless.
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俚语，用来形容或指责别人胡乱说话、讲一些没有意义或不必要的话。常见写法为「亂噏無謂」，多用于制止或反驳对方的言论。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to describe or rebuke someone who is talking nonsense or saying pointless things. Often written as '亂噏無謂' and used to stop or criticize unnecessary remarks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好亂噏無謂啦，講啲有用嘅嘢好唔好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lyun6 ap1 mou4 wai6 laa1, gong2 di1 jau5 jung6 ge3 je5 hou2 m4 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要乱说没必要的，能不能说点有用的？
examples.english_sentence: Don't talk nonsense for no reason — can you say something useful?

mandarin_meaning: 乱七八糟 / 一团糟
english_meaning: completely messed up; in total chaos; a complete mess
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，表示某事物或场面非常混乱、乱成一团，常用于口语中强调混乱程度。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning something is extremely chaotic or a total mess; commonly used colloquially to emphasize disorder.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇下間房，亂晒龍！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5 gaan1 fong4, lyun6 saai3 lung4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看看房间，乱七八糟！
examples.english_sentence: Look at the room — it's a total mess!

mandarin_meaning: （口語）非常混亂、亂七八糟
english_meaning: (slang) extremely messy; in utter chaos
explanation_mandarin: 「乱过嚿云」是廣東話口語/俚語，用來形容場面、地方或局面非常混亂、沒有秩序，類似普通話的「亂七八糟」或「一塌糊塗」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to describe a situation, place, or state that is extremely chaotic or a complete mess, similar to Mandarin '乱七八糟' or English 'a complete mess'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間屋乱过嚿云，唔知道點收拾先好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 uk1 lyun6 gwo3 gau3 wan4, m4 zi1 dou3 dim2 sau1 sap6 sin1 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間屋亂得要命，不知道該怎麼收拾才好。
examples.english_sentence: This room is a total mess; I don't know how to tidy it up.

jyutping: gon1 lung4 wong4 kai3 zai2, zau1 jat6 cing1
mandarin_meaning: 形容只在星期日才打扫、很少整理（用于戏谑或调侃）
english_meaning: Joking phrase describing someone who only cleans once a week (on Sundays); rarely tidies up
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句粵語的戲謔語句，用來形容某人平時不愛打掃或整理家務，只會在星期日大掃除一次。語句押韻，常見於口語和玩笑中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese joking phrase used to describe someone who rarely tidies and only does a big clean on Sundays. The line is rhyming and used colloquially or humorously.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢屋企成日都唔整潔，淨係乾隆皇契仔，周日清。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 uk1 kei5 sing4 jat6 dou1 m4 zing2 git3, zing6 hai6 gon1 lung4 wong4 kai3 zai2, zau1 jat6 cing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他家里平時都不整理，只在星期日才打掃。
examples.english_sentence: He hardly ever tidies his place — he only cleans on Sundays.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見詞，語義不詳；在部分粵語語境中可能用作俚語，表示「胡說、瞎扯」或「無聊的話」。此解釋屬推測，該詞較為罕見或為地區性用法。
english_meaning: Obscure/rare term; possibly a Cantonese slang word used to mean 'nonsense' or 'rubbish talk'. This interpretation is tentative — the term is uncommon or regionally limited.
explanation_mandarin: 「乾骾」並非標準書面詞彙，出現頻率低。根據零散語料和口語使用，可能用來形容某人說的話是胡扯或無聊的話，但具體來源與確切含義不穩定，屬於罕見或地區性俚語。
explanation_english: Not a standard written term and rarely seen. Based on scattered usage in spoken Cantonese, it may be used to label someone's speech as nonsense or idle talk. The exact origin and meaning are uncertain — treat interpretations as tentative and regionally limited.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好理佢講嘅乾骾，佢淨係喺度講大話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5 gong2 ge3 gon1 gon2, keoi5 zing6 hai6 hai2 dou6 gong2 daai6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別理他說的「乾骾」，他只是在說瞎話。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pay attention to the '乾骾' he's saying; he's just talking nonsense.

jyutping: lyun6 gwan3 daa2 sei2 lou5 si1 fu6
mandarin_meaning: 人多勢眾，即使是有經驗的老手也可能被多數人壓倒或擊敗。
english_meaning: Even an experienced master can be overwhelmed by a crowd; sheer numbers can overcome expertise.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語 / 俗語，動詞短語
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容人多力量大，眾人合力可以把有經驗的人或強者擊敗或壓倒，常用來提醒不要小看多人合力的威力。
explanation_english: An idiom meaning that many people working together can overwhelm an expert; used to warn not to underestimate the power of numbers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好小睇啲新人，亂棍打死老師傅，佢哋人多可以搞掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 siu2 tai2 di1 san1 jan4, lyun6 gwan3 daa2 sei2 lou5 si1 fu6, keoi5 dei6 jan4 do1 ho2 ji5 gaau2 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要小看那些新手，人多勢眾，連老手也難以抵擋，他們人多可以搞定。
examples.english_sentence: Don't underestimate the newcomers — many people together can overwhelm even an expert; with enough people they can get it done.

mandarin_meaning: 乱葬岗（指集中掩埋無名屍體的地方；也比喻造成大量人員傷亡或失敗的地方）
english_meaning: mass grave (a burial place for unclaimed or many dead); figuratively, a place or situation where many people 'fall' or fail
explanation_mandarin: 原指把無主屍體或在戰亂、疫病等情況下大量屍體集中掩埋的場所；引申為形容某處或某情況導致大量人員喪失、失敗或遭受重大損失。
explanation_english: Originally refers to a site where unclaimed corpses or many bodies from war/plague are buried together; figuratively used to describe a place or situation that causes many casualties, failures, or heavy losses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰度以前係亂葬岡，依家已經改建做公園。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 dou6 ji5 cin4 hai6 lyun6 zong6 gong1, ji1 gaa1 ji5 ging1 goi2 gin3 zou6 gung1 jyun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那裡以前是亂葬崗，現在已經改建成公園。
examples.english_sentence: That place used to be a mass grave; it's now been redeveloped into a park.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司成日裁員，搞到成個部門變咗亂葬岡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 sing4 jat6 coi4 jyun4, gaau2 dou3 sing4 go3 bou6 mun4 bin3 zo2 lyun6 zong6 gong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司經常裁員，搞得整個部門像個亂葬崗。
examples.english_sentence: The company keeps laying people off, turning the whole department into a 'mass grave' (i.e., many people losing their jobs).

synonyms: 亂葬崗（異體字/普通話寫法：乱葬岗）

mandarin_meaning: 什麼都沒有；一場空；徒勞無功
english_meaning: nothing at all; all for nothing; zilch
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容某事結果一無所獲、徒勞或完全沒有（通常帶有失望或輕蔑的語氣）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang interjection used to indicate that something resulted in nothing or was all for nothing, often carrying a tone of disappointment or dismissal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我等咗成個下午，點知最後係了哥毛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dang2 zo2 seng4 go3 haa6 ng5, dim2 zi1 zeoi3 hau6 hai6 liu5 go1 mou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我等了整個下午，結果什麼也沒有。
examples.english_sentence: I waited the whole afternoon, and in the end there was nothing.

mandarin_meaning: 不肯让步
english_meaning: refuse to give in; unwilling to yield
explanation_mandarin: “争唔落”是廣東話口語，表示雙方互不讓步、堅持己見，無法達成一致或停止爭執。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning that parties refuse to concede or back down; neither side is willing to yield in an argument or dispute.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個為咗嗰件細事爭唔落，成日吵到夜晚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 wai6 zo2 go2 gin6 sai3 si6 zaang1 m4 lok6, sing4 jat6 caau3 dou3 je6 maan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们两个人为那件小事争执不下，经常吵到晚上。
examples.english_sentence: They wouldn't give in over that small matter and argued until late at night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆同部門經理為職位爭唔落，最後人都走晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 tung4 bou6 mun4 ging1 lei5 wai6 zik1 wai2 zaang1 m4 lok6, zeoi3 hau6 jan4 dou1 zau2 saat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板和部门经理为职位互不让步，最后大家都走光了。
examples.english_sentence: The boss and the department manager wouldn't yield over the position, and in the end everyone left.

mandarin_meaning: 争天斗地 / 与天地抗争
english_meaning: to contend with heaven and earth; to defy limits or strive fiercely
explanation_mandarin: “争天共地”字面意思是与天地争斗，常用来形容不顾一切、极力争取或挑衅权威与自然的态度，表示极端的奋斗或野心（近义：争天斗地）。
explanation_english: Literally 'to contend with heaven and earth.' An idiom describing someone who defies limits or fights fiercely against all odds—used for extreme ambition, reckless confrontation, or desperate striving.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢諗住可以爭天共地，最後只係自討苦吃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lam2 zyu6 ho2 ji5 zang1 tin1 gung6 dei6, zeoi3 hau6 zi2 hai6 zi6 tou2 fu2 hek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他以为可以与天地争斗，最后只是在自讨苦吃。
examples.english_sentence: He thought he could contend with heaven and earth, but in the end he only made things harder for himself.

mandarin_meaning: 事情的原因；起因
english_meaning: the cause or reason of an event; root cause
explanation_mandarin: 指導致某件事發生的原因或起因，語氣較書面或正式。
explanation_english: Refers to the cause or reason that led to a particular event; a somewhat formal or written term.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你知唔知件事嘅事因係乜嘢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zi1 m4 zi1 gin6 si6 ge3 si6 jan1 hai6 mat1 je5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你知道這件事的事因是什麼嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Do you know what the cause of this matter is?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方仍然未查清楚件事嘅事因。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 jing4 jin4 mei6 caa4 cing1 co2 gin6 si6 ge3 si6 jan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方仍然未查清楚這件事的事因。
examples.english_sentence: The police still haven't clarified the cause of the incident.

mandarin_meaning: 事情緊急時採取臨時、權宜或倉促的做法
english_meaning: To take makeshift or improvised measures when things become urgent; to act hastily in an emergency.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容遇到緊急情況時，採取臨時、權宜的做法，通常含有不得已或不夠完善的意味。
explanation_english: Used to describe taking temporary, makeshift measures in an urgent situation; implies necessity and that the solution may be improvised or imperfect.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 事急馬行田，暫時先咁做啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si6 gap1 maa5 hang4 tin4, zaam6 si4 sin1 gam2 zou6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 事情緊急，只能先暫時這樣做。
examples.english_sentence: It's an emergency — we'll have to do it this way for now.

mandarin_meaning: 只有在事情緊急時才會採取行動；到了緊要關頭人才會做平時不會做的事
english_meaning: Only when things are urgent will one act; when push comes to shove people do things they normally wouldn't.
explanation_mandarin: 形容平時不會採取的做法，只有在事情緊急或到了關鍵時刻才會出現，強調臨急才行動或採取非常規手段。
explanation_english: Describes doing things one normally wouldn't do — people only take action or resort to unconventional measures when matters become urgent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單嘢唔可以拖，事緊馬行田，要即刻搞掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 je5 m4 ho2 ji5 to1, si6 gan2 maa5 haang4 tin4, jiu3 zik1 hak1 gaau2 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事不能拖，事情緊急，必須立刻解決。
examples.english_sentence: This can't be postponed — it's urgent; we must resolve it immediately.

mandarin_meaning: 盲目跟从/跟屁虫（贬义）
english_meaning: a blind follower; someone who follows stubbornly without independent thought (derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 用作贬义的粤语俚语，指对某人盲目跟随、毫无主见的人，常用来责备别人没有独立判断。
explanation_english: A derogatory Cantonese slang phrase used to describe someone who blindly follows another person and lacks independent judgment; often used to scold someone for being a sycophant or blind follower.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日二仔底、死跟阿強，冇自己諗法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ji6 zai2 dai2, sei2 gan1 aa3 koeng4, mou5 zi6 gei2 lam2 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是跟着阿强，盲目从众，没有自己的想法。
examples.english_sentence: He always follows Ah Keung blindly, with no independent thoughts.

mandarin_meaning: 二叔（父親的第二個弟弟或家族中排行第二的叔叔）
english_meaning: second uncle (father's second younger brother; the uncle who is second in order among father's younger brothers)
explanation_mandarin: 指父親的弟弟中的第二位，屬於家族稱謂。粵語日常用法中可直接稱呼或提到這位親戚。
explanation_english: A kinship term referring to the father's second younger brother (the uncle who is second in birth order among the father's younger brothers). Used as a family relation term in Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我個二叔喺佐敦開茶餐廳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 ji6 suk1 hai2 zo2 deon1 hoi1 caa4 caan1 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我二叔在佐敦開茶餐廳。
examples.english_sentence: My second uncle runs a cha chaan teng in Jordan.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我爸爸個二叔，我哋好熟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 baa4 baa1 go3 ji6 suk1, ngo5 dei6 hou2 suk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是我爸爸的二叔，我們很熟。
examples.english_sentence: He is my father's second younger brother; we're close.

jyutping: ji6 suk1 gung1 got3 fo4, mong6 haa6 zit3
mandarin_meaning: 坐視不理；旁觀、觀望結果而不出手幫忙
english_meaning: To stand by and watch without helping; to wait and see the outcome as a bystander
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容只在一旁觀看、不參與或不出手幫忙，帶有批評或嘲諷的語氣，類似“坐視不理”或“袖手旁觀”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying describing someone who merely watches from the sidelines and doesn't help, often used critically or mockingly—similar to 'to sit on the sidelines' or 'to stand by and do nothing.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做二叔公割禾，望下截，快啲嚟幫手啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 ji6 suk1 gung1 got3 fo4, mong6 haa6 zit3, faai3 di1 lai4 bong1 sau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別當旁觀者只等著看結果，快點過來幫忙！
examples.english_sentence: Don't just stand there watching like a bystander—come help quickly!

cantonese: 二叔婆养猪，够晒好心机
jyutping: ji6 suk1 po4 joeng5 zyu1, gau3 saai3 hou2 sam1 gei1
mandarin_meaning: （某人）很有心机／很会算计（常带戏谑或讽刺）
english_meaning: Someone is very scheming or calculating (often said jokingly or sarcastically).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語（形容詞性用法）
explanation_mandarin: 「二叔婆养猪，够晒好心机」是一句廣東話口語，帶有幽默或譏諷意味，用來形容某人心思縝密、很會算計或別有用心。前半句为戲謔性的配語，重在強調後半句的評價。
explanation_english: This Cantonese slang phrase is a humorous/sarcastic way to say someone is very scheming or full of ulterior motives. The first part is a playful filler while the second part, '夠晒好心機', emphasizes the judgment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日扮傻，其實二叔婆養豬，夠晒好心機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 baan6 so4, kei4 sat6 ji6 suk1 po4 joeng5 zyu1, gau3 saai3 hou2 sam1 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是裝傻，其實很有心機。
examples.english_sentence: He always pretends to be dumb, but actually he's really scheming.

cantonese: 二叔婆抌心口，自有分数
jyutping: ji6 suk1 po4 paak3 sam1 hau2, zi6 jau5 fan1 sou3
mandarin_meaning: 即便有人拍着胸口说自己清白，也终有分晓（公道/报应）
english_meaning: Even if someone beats their chest swearing they're innocent, justice or the reckoning will come in time.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語式的廣東話表達，帶有鄉土色彩。用來表示即使某人一再宣稱自己無辜或自我辯白，事情最終會有分曉、會有公道或報應。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese proverb-like saying. It means that even if someone repeatedly swears they are innocent, the truth, justice, or karmic reckoning will eventually reveal itself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話自己冇做錯，二叔婆抌心口，自有分數，時間會證明一切。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 mou5 zou6 co3, ji6 suk1 po4 paak3 sam1 hau2, zi6 jau5 fan1 sou3, si4 gaan3 wui5 zing3 ming4 jat1 cai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说自己没有做错，拍着胸口说自己无辜，但自有分晓，时间会证明一切。
examples.english_sentence: He says he didn't do anything wrong, swearing on his chest, but the reckoning will come — time will prove everything.

jyutping: ji6 sei3 luk6 baat3 daan1, mou5 dak1 bin3
mandarin_meaning: 已成定局，无法改变
english_meaning: It's a done deal / it's settled and cannot be changed
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俗語，用來表示某事已經決定或固定，沒有改變的可能，常在日常對話中使用。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to say that something is already decided or fixed and cannot be changed; commonly used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司已經批准咗個計劃，二四六八单，冇得变。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ji5 ging1 bat1 zo2 go3 gai3 waak6, ji6 sei3 luk6 baat3 daan1, mou5 dak1 bin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司已经批准了这个计划，已成定局，无法改变。
examples.english_sentence: The company has already approved the plan — it's a done deal and can't be changed.

mandarin_meaning: 擺出愚蠢、傻氣的表情；形容人看起來傻愣或做傻樣。
english_meaning: to wear a silly/stupid-looking expression; describes someone who looks foolish or daft.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俚語，通常用來形容一個人擺出愚蠢、傻氣的表情或樣子，帶有輕微嘲弄或戲謔意味，常見於香港地區的口語用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe someone wearing a silly or foolish-looking expression. It often carries a teasing or mildly derogatory tone and is common in Hong Kong spoken usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做咁二花面颈啦，大家講緊嘢啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 gam3 ji6 faa1 min6 geng2 laa1, daai6 gaa1 gong2 gan2 je5 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別擺出那副愚蠢的表情，我們只是在說話而已。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make that silly face; we're just talking.

mandarin_meaning: 低檔、破舊或環境髒亂的場所（俗稱，用於形容廉價、沒規模的小店或小館子）
english_meaning: a low-end, shabby or seedy establishment (slang for a cheap, small shop or joint)
explanation_mandarin: 「二釐館」為廣東話俗語，用來形容店鋪或場所質素低、規模小、環境差或帶有陳舊、廉價、甚至有點不乾淨的感覺。詞源帶有「二釐/二厘」意指很小的價錢或低廉程度，與「館」結合表示場所。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term for a place that is low-class, rundown, or seedy — a cheap, small establishment with poor conditions. The element "二釐/二厘" evokes a very small/cheap amount, combined with "館" (place) to indicate low quality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間二釐館又細又亂，唔好入去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 ji6 lei4 gun2 jau6 sai3 jau6 lyun6, m4 hou2 jap6 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那家二釐館又小又亂，別進去。
examples.english_sentence: That dive is small and messy — don't go in.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺二釐館度做嘢，聽日放工請食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ji6 lei4 gun2 dou6 zou6 je5, ting1 jat6 fong3 gung1 ceng2 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在二釐館工作，明天下班請吃飯。
examples.english_sentence: He works at a dive; he's treating me to dinner after work tomorrow.

cantonese: 云往东，翻大风；云往西，淋死鸡
jyutping: wan4 wong5 dung1, faan1 daai6 fung1; wan4 wong5 sai1, lam4 sei2 gai1
mandarin_meaning: 云往东，刮大风；云往西，下大雨（民间凭云的方向判断将来是刮风还是下雨的谚语）
english_meaning: If the clouds move east, expect strong winds; if the clouds move west, expect heavy rain (a folk proverb using cloud direction to predict weather).
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句粵語的民間諺語，根據雲的運行方向來預測天氣：雲向東走常被認為會刮風，雲向西走則容易下大雨（「淋死雞」是形容雨下得很大的誇張說法）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folk proverb that predicts weather from cloud movement: clouds moving east are taken as a sign of strong winds, while clouds moving west indicate heavy rain. The phrase "淋死雞" is a colloquial exaggeration meaning to rain very heavily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽見到天空咁樣，就話：'雲往東，翻大風；雲往西，淋死雞'，叫我哋快啲收衫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 gin3 dou3 tin1 hung1 gam2 joeng6, zau6 waa6: 'wan4 wong5 dung1, faan1 daai6 fung1; wan4 wong5 sai1, lam4 sei2 gai1', giu3 ngo5 dei6 faai3 di1 sau1 saam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈看到天空这样，就说：‘云往东，翻大风；云往西，淋死鸡’，叫我们快点收衣服。
examples.english_sentence: When Mom saw the sky like that she said, 'If clouds head east, big winds; if clouds head west, heavy rain,' and told us to quickly bring in the laundry.

mandarin_meaning: 五味子（Schisandra chinensis），一種中藥材和藥用果實
english_meaning: Schisandra (Schisandra chinensis); the five-flavor berry, a medicinal fruit used in traditional Chinese medicine
explanation_mandarin: 五味子是五味子科植物的乾燥果實，因併有酸、甜、苦、辛、鹹等五味而得名。常用於補益肺腎、止咳、收斂以及製作藥酒和保健飲品。
explanation_english: Schisandra is the dried fruit of Schisandra chinensis, named the "five-flavor berry" because it contains sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, and salty tastes. It is used in traditional Chinese medicine to support lung and kidney function, stop coughs, astringe, and to make medicinal wines or tonics.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗一袋五味子，打算整藥酒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 jat1 doi2 ng5 mei6 zi2, daa2 syun3 zing2 joek6 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他买了一袋五味子，打算泡药酒。
examples.english_sentence: He bought a bag of schisandra berries to make medicinal wine.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見或古稱，非現代漢語常用詞；可能為植物名或「五味子」的誤寫/異體（確切含義不明，需參考典籍）
english_meaning: A rare or archaic term; not used in modern speech. Possibly a botanical name or a variant/misspelling of 'Schisandra (五味子)'; exact meaning unclear and chiefly found in historical texts.
explanation_mandarin: 「五斂子」在現代粵語與普通話中並非常用詞。文獻中偶見此寫法，可能為古代植物名或是對「五味子」等藥用植物名稱的異寫，但沒有確切、廣泛接受的現代定義。查閱具體典籍或古籍詞條可獲更多資訊。
explanation_english: The term '五斂子' is not common in modern Cantonese or Mandarin. It appears rarely in historical or classical sources and may be a botanical name or a variant/misspelling of '五味子' (Schisandra). There is no clear, widely accepted modern definition; consult historical texts for context-specific meanings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺古書入面，你有時會見到「五斂子」呢個詞，但現代資料好少講佢係乜嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gu2 syu1 jap6 min6, nei5 jau5 si4 wui5 gin3 dou2 "ng5 lim5 zi2" ni1 go3 ci4, daan6 jin6 doi6 zi1 liu2 hou2 siu2 gong2 keoi5 hai6 mat1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在古書中，有時會看到「五斂子」這個詞，但現代資料很少說明它是什麼。
examples.english_sentence: In old books you sometimes see the term '五斂子', but modern sources rarely explain what it is.

mandarin_meaning: 五爪金龙（象征皇权的龙，常见于皇室纹饰）
english_meaning: Five-clawed golden dragon (the imperial dragon symbolizing imperial authority)
explanation_mandarin: 在中国传统文化和服饰纹饰中，五爪金龙是皇权的象征。古代只有皇帝或与皇权有关的物品才可使用五爪龙图案，代表至高无上的权力与尊贵。
explanation_english: In traditional Chinese culture and ornamentation, the five-clawed golden dragon is an imperial symbol. Historically the five-clawed dragon was reserved for the emperor and things associated with imperial authority, representing supreme power and nobility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢幅龍袍上繡咗一條五爪金龍，代表皇權。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fuk1 lung4 pou4 soeng6 sau3 zo2 jat1 tiu4 ng5 zaau2 gam1 lung4, doi6 biu2 wong4 kyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件龙袍上绣着一条五爪金龙，代表皇权。
examples.english_sentence: This dragon robe is embroidered with a five-clawed golden dragon, representing imperial authority.

mandarin_meaning: （疑为误写）五斗柜；五抽屉的柜子
english_meaning: Likely a misspelling of 'five-drawer cabinet' (chest of five drawers)
explanation_mandarin: 「五筒櫃」並非標準詞彙，常被視為對「五斗櫃」的誤寫或口誤。正確的詞應為「五斗櫃」（五抽屜的櫃子），指有多個抽屜用來收納衣物或雜物的櫃子。
explanation_english: “五筒櫃” is not a standard term and is often a misspelling or mispronunciation of “五斗櫃” (five-drawer cabinet). The correct term refers to a chest or cabinet with multiple drawers used for storing clothes or miscellaneous items.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好寫錯，應該係五斗櫃唔係五筒櫃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 se2 co3, jing1 goi1 hai6 ng5 dau2 gwai6 m4 hai6 ng5 tung2 gwai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別寫錯了，應該寫五斗柜，不是五筒柜。
examples.english_sentence: Don't write it wrong; it should be '五斗柜' (five-drawer cabinet), not '五筒櫃'.

mandarin_meaning: （俚语、粗口）形容某人极其无用、可笑或该受谴责；字面上可直译为“五行缺屌”
english_meaning: Vulgar Cantonese slang insulting someone as utterly useless/pathetic; literally 'the five elements are missing a dick.'
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚语 / 骂人用语（感叹词 / 名词用法）
explanation_mandarin: 「五行欠屌」是香港廣東話的粗口俚語，帶強烈貶義與嘲諷意味。用來指某人非常沒用、可笑或令人厭惡。字面可拆為「五行」（五行）+「欠」（缺少）+「屌」（粗俗字眼），並非真正與五行概念相關，而是以誇張、粗俗的方式表達蔑視。
explanation_english: This is a vulgar Cantonese slang insult used to express strong contempt — describing someone as completely useless, pathetic, or deserving of scorn. Literally composed of 'five elements' + 'missing' + a crude term for the male genitalia; it is an emphatic, obscene way to ridicule someone and is not related to the traditional five elements concept.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日遲到，做嘢又唔負責，真係五行欠屌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3, zou6 je5 jau6 m4 fu6 zaak3, zan1 hai6 ng5 hang4 him3 diu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是迟到，做事又不負責，真是五行欠屌。
examples.english_sentence: He's always late and irresponsible — he's completely useless (literally: 'five elements missing a dick').

mandarin_meaning: 五颜六色 (wǔ yán liù sè)：多种颜色，形容色彩丰富；也可比喻事物多姿多彩或种类繁多。
english_meaning: Colorful; multi‑colored; having many different colors. Can be used literally or figuratively to mean varied or vibrant.
explanation_mandarin: 用于描述颜色繁多、色彩鲜艳的事物，也常用作比喻，表示事物丰富多彩或样式多样。
explanation_english: Describes something that has many different colors or is very colorful. Often used literally for appearance or figuratively to indicate variety or vibrancy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢件衫五颜六色，好搶眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin6 saam1 ng5 ngaan4 luk6 sik1, hou2 coeng2 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她的衣服五颜六色，很抢眼。
examples.english_sentence: Her clothes are colorful and very eye-catching.

mandarin_meaning: 差不多；一般般；不特别好也不算太差
english_meaning: so-so; mediocre; neither particularly good nor particularly bad
explanation_mandarin: 香港口語俚語，用來形容事物或表現普通、勉強過得去，不突出也不糟糕，屬於中等或差強人意的情況。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong colloquial/slang expression used to describe something as ordinary or mediocre — acceptable but not impressive; neither notably good nor notably bad.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅食物亞保亞勝，唔會特別想再嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 sik6 mat6 aa3 bou2 aa3 sing3, m4 wui5 dak6 bit6 soeng2 zoi3 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间餐厅的食物一般般，不会特别想再来。
examples.english_sentence: The food at this restaurant is so-so; I wouldn't particularly want to come back.

cantonese: 亚兰卖猪，一千唔卖卖八百
jyutping: aa3 laan4 maai6 zyu1, jat1 cin1 m4 maai6, maai6 baat3 baak3
mandarin_meaning: 形容人做事或講話前後矛盾、反常或任性（拒絕一個較高的價錢，反而接受較低的價錢），用來批評刁難或怪脾氣的行為。
english_meaning: Describes someone acting perversely or illogically — contradicting themselves or being contrary (e.g. refusing to sell for 1,000 but selling for 800). Used to criticize stubborn, unreasonable, or contradictory behavior.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，比喻人行為或說話前後不一致、反常或故意刁難、任性。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying used to describe someone whose actions or words are inconsistent or perverse — being contrary or unreasonable in behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢成日好似亞兰卖猪，一千唔卖，卖八百，講嘢前後唔一樣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 seng4 jat6 hou2 ci5 aa3 laan4 maai6 zyu1, jat1 cin1 m4 maai6, maai6 baat3 baak3, gong2 je5 cin4 hau6 m4 jat1 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事總是像「亞蘭賣豬」，一千不賣，卻賣八百，說話前後不一致。
examples.english_sentence: He always acts like 'aa laan selling pigs' — refusing at 1,000 but selling at 800; his words don't match his actions.

cantonese: 亚均卖大头鱼，好噏唔噏
jyutping: aa3 gwan1 maai6 daai6 tau4 jyu4, hou2 jap6 m4 jap6
mandarin_meaning: （口語）阿均在吹牛/胡说，真的假的？
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese expression accusing someone of talking nonsense or bragging — 'is he for real or just making it up?'
explanation_mandarin: 這句話是粵語的口語或俚語，用來形容某人講大話、誇大或胡扯，句尾的「好噏唔噏」帶有質疑或反問的語氣。
explanation_english: This is a Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to say someone is lying, bragging, or exaggerating. The ending 'hou jap m4 jap' (好噏唔噏) is a skeptical rhetorical question — 'really or not?'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話可以一星期內賺到十萬，亚均卖大头鱼，好噏唔噏？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 ho2 ji5 jat1 sing1 kei4 noi6 zaan6 dou3 sap6 maan6, aa3 gwan1 maai6 daai6 tau4 jyu4, hou2 jap6 m4 jap6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说一周可以赚十万，阿均在吹牛，真的假的？
