examples.english_sentence: He says he can make 100k in a week — Ah Kwan is talking nonsense; is that for real or not?

mandarin_meaning: 字面：老太婆的发髻；口语/俚语：形容老土、过时或不时髦（带有戏谑或轻蔑意味）。该短语地区性强，来源不详，使用时多为非正式场合。
english_meaning: Literal: an old woman's hair bun. Colloquial/slang: used to call something or someone old-fashioned, out-of-date, or unfashionable; often joking or slightly derisive. Regional and informal usage; origin unclear.
explanation_mandarin: “亚婆髻，安嘅”字面上指老太太的发髻。在粤语口语中常用作形容某人打扮、说话或行为显得老土、过时或不合潮流，语气可戏谑或轻蔑。此用法属非正式、区域性表达，资料与来源较少，实际含义和语感可能随语境而异。
explanation_english: The phrase literally refers to an old woman's hair bun. In Cantonese colloquial use it tends to describe someone's appearance, style, or behaviour as old-fashioned or out-of-date, often with a teasing or slightly derogatory tone. Usage is informal and regionally specific; origins are unclear and nuance depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你著得咁老土，真係亞婆髻，安嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoek3 dak1 gam3 lou5 tou2, zan1 hai6 aa3 po4 gat1, on1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你穿得这么老土，真是“亚婆髻”，太过时了。
examples.english_sentence: You're dressed so old-fashioned—really like an 'old woman's bun', so out of date.

jyutping: aa3 beng1 maai5 fo2 sek6, gaau3 gwo3 sin1 zi1
mandarin_meaning: （口語）吹牛、誇口，聲稱比別人更早知道或預告某事；言過其實
english_meaning: Colloquial slang meaning to boast or claim to know something before everyone else (to act like a prophet); to talk boastfully or rashly without proof
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東話的俚語或俗語，較為地區性和口語化。大意用來形容某人愛吹牛、言之過早或自以為了然於胸、比先知還早發言。字面成分（買火石、先知）多為比喻或戲謔，實際含義以語境為主，讀音或字形在不同社群可能有變體。
explanation_english: This is a Cantonese colloquial/slang expression, regional and informal. It describes someone who brags, speaks prematurely, or claims to know things before others (as if they were a prophet). The literal elements (buying flint, prophet) are metaphorical or jocular; the exact nuance depends on context and local usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁亞崩买火石，噭过先知，等結果出咗先講啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 aa3 beng1 maai5 fo2 sek6, gaau3 gwo3 sin1 zi1, dang2 git3 gwo2 ceot1 zo2 sin1 gong2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別那樣吹牛、說得比先知還早，先等結果出來再說吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't brag like you know things before anyone else — wait for the results before you talk.

jyutping: aa3 beng1 joeng5 gau2 , zyun2 sing3
mandarin_meaning: （俚語）養了狗之後性格或行為改變
english_meaning: (slanga) to change one’s personality or behaviour after getting a dog
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語網絡或口語用法，帶有調侃意味，指某人養了狗後變得比較黏人、溫柔或行為習慣改變。有時也用來形容對狗特別上心、生活被狗佔據。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase, often jokingly used to describe someone whose personality or habits change after getting a dog — becoming more affectionate, attentive, or otherwise different in behaviour. It can also imply being overly absorbed in caring for the dog.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢亞崩養狗，轉性晒，成日帶隻狗去公園。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aa3 beng1 joeng5 gau2 zyun2 sing3 saai3 , sing4 jat6 daai3 zek3 gau2 heoi3 gung1 jyun4 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他養了狗之後性格完全改變了，整天帶着狗去公園。
examples.english_sentence: He totally changed after getting a dog — he’s always taking the dog to the park.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）形容場面非常混亂、狼藉，像被屠宰般血腥凌亂。
english_meaning: slang describing a scene of utter chaos and messiness, as if something were slaughtered — used to say things are a complete shambles.
explanation_mandarin: 字面上把「崩」與「劏羊」的意象結合，用血腥、被拆解的畫面比喻場面混亂或亂成一團。常用於口語，強調程度嚴重、非常凌亂。
explanation_english: Literally evokes the image of collapsing and butchering a sheep; metaphorically used to describe scenes that are extremely chaotic, messy, or in shambles. It's a colloquial/slang expression emphasizing severity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 昨晚喺個酒吧嗌交，搞到亞崩劏羊，啲枱都打爛晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zok3 maan5 hai2 go3 zau2 baa1 aai3 gaau1, gaau2 dou3 aa3 bang1 tong3 joeng4, di1 toi2 dou1 daa2 laan6 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚在酒吧吵架，弄得一團糟，連桌子都被打爛了。
examples.english_sentence: Last night there was a fight at the bar — it turned into total chaos; even the tables were smashed.

jyutping: aa3 beng1 giu3 gau2, jyut6 giu3 jyut6 zau2
mandarin_meaning: 越叫越走；越是叫嚷或责骂，越把人赶走
english_meaning: The more you shout (or scold), the more they walk away — efforts to call/hold someone back only drive them further away
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，用來形容越是呼喊、責罵或挽留某人，反而使對方越發離開或逃避，表示勸說或責備無效且適得其反。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying that describes how shouting, scolding, or trying too hard to hold someone back often has the opposite effect — the person moves further away. It describes attempts to persuade or reprimand that backfire.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣成日鬧佢，只會亞崩叫狗，越叫越走，最後佢會離開你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 seng4 jat6 naau6 keoi5, zi2 wui5 aa3 beng1 giu3 gau2, jyut6 giu3 jyut6 zau2, zeoi3 hau6 keoi5 wui5 lei4 hoi1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这样老是骂他，只会越骂越把人赶走，最后他会离开你。
examples.english_sentence: If you keep scolding him like that, you'll only push him away — the more you shout, the further he'll go; in the end he'll leave you.

jyutping: aa3 beng1 ceoi1 siu1, saai1 seng1 waai6 hei3
mandarin_meaning: 装腔作势、吹嘘（有时带性暗示），浪费口舌并破坏气氛
english_meaning: To put on a show or brag (sometimes with sexual undertones); a waste of words that spoils the mood
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話俗語，用來形容某人愛裝腔作勢或吹噓（有時帶性意味），但實際上徒勞無功，白費口舌，還弄壞氣氛。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression describing someone who puts on a show or brags (occasionally with sexual innuendo), but in reality it's pointless — a waste of breath that ruins the atmosphere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識亚崩吹箫，嘥声坏气，實際乜都做唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 aa3 beng1 ceoi1 siu1, saai1 seng1 waai6 hei3, sat6 zai3 mat1 dou1 zou6 m4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會裝腔作勢、吹噓，浪費口舌，實際上什麼都做不到。
examples.english_sentence: He only puts on a show and wastes everyone's breath; in reality he can't do anything.

cantonese: 亚崩咬狗虱，唔死有排慌
jyutping: aa3 beng1 ngaau5 gau2 sat1, m4 sei2 jau5 paai4 fong1
mandarin_meaning: 倒霉到极点，遭遇極大麻煩或苦難；即使沒死，也會有一段時間非常慌亂/受苦。
english_meaning: Extremely unlucky or in a terrible predicament — you'll suffer or be in trouble for a long time; even if you don't die, you'll be in a long-lasting mess.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語俚語，形容詞短語/感嘆語
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容人或事遇到極為倒霉或嚴重的麻煩，語氣誇張且帶有嘲諷或同情意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression describing extreme bad luck or a severe predicament. It's hyperbolic and can be used to mock or sympathize with someone's long-lasting trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢投資輸晒成身家，真係亞崩咬狗虱，唔死有排慌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tau4 zi1 syu1 saai3 sing4 san1 gaa1, zan1 hai6 aa3 beng1 ngaau5 gau2 sat1, m4 sei2 jau5 paai4 fong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他投資把所有家當都輸光了，真是倒霉透顶，即使沒死也會有一段時間很慌張/受苦。
examples.english_sentence: He lost his entire investment; he's really unbelievably unlucky — even if he doesn't die he'll be in trouble for a long time.

jyutping: aa3 bo1 haau6 dang1, jau5 zoek6 jau5 m4 zoek6
mandarin_meaning: 时有时无；断断续续，不稳定
english_meaning: hit-and-miss; intermittent; on-and-off; inconsistent
explanation_mandarin: 俗语或俚语，用来形容某事物或某人的表现、状态、功能等不稳定、断续或有时有效有时无效。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang phrase used to describe something that is inconsistent or intermittent — working or present sometimes but not at other times.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我部電話最近訊號好差，亞波校灯，有着有唔着，打唔通人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bou6 din6 waa2 zeoi3 gan6 seon3 hou6 caa1, aa3 bo1 haau6 dang1, jau5 zoek6 jau5 m4 zoek6, daa2 m4 tung1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我手機最近訊號很差，时有时无，打不通人。
examples.english_sentence: My phone's signal has been terrible lately — it's hit-and-miss, I can't get through to people.

jyutping: aa3 lung4 maai6 bou3, m4 gong2 ni1 pat1 (bat1)
mandarin_meaning: 装聋作哑（假装听不见或不回应以逃避责任或回避问题）
english_meaning: to play dumb / pretend not to hear or respond in order to avoid responsibility or avoid answering
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容有人故意裝聾作啞、不作解釋或不承認，以迴避責任或問話。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who deliberately feigns deafness or ignorance and refuses to respond or admit something to avoid responsibility or questioning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司發現差錯，但老細問起嘅時候佢就亞聾賣布，唔講呢匹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 faat3 jin6 caa1 co3, daan6 lou5 sai3 man6 hei2 ge3 si4 hau6 keoi5 zau6 aa3 lung4 maai6 bou3, m4 gong2 ni1 pat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司发现了差错，但老板一问起时他就装聋作哑，不作解释。
examples.english_sentence: The company found a mistake, but when the boss asked, he played dumb and wouldn't say a word.

jyutping: aa3 lung4 siu1 paau3, dak1 zan6 jin1
mandarin_meaning: 闹一阵子就没了；短暂的喧闹或做秀
english_meaning: a brief burst of fuss/noise or show that quickly dies down
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人或某件事搞得很熱鬧、張揚，卻只持續很短的一段時間，過後很快平息或消失。
explanation_english: Describes someone or something that causes a lot of noise or a showy fuss for a short time, then quickly fades away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日響街度亞聋燒炮，得阵烟，過幾日又冇聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hoeng2 gaai1 dou6 aa3 lung4 siu1 paau3, dak1 zan6 jin1, gwo3 gei2 jat6 jau6 mou5 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在街上大吵大鬧，鬧一陣就沒了，過幾天又沒聲了。
examples.english_sentence: He's always making a fuss on the street — all noise for a while, and then it's gone after a few days.

cantonese: 亚聋送殡，唔听佢支死人笛
jyutping: aa3 lung4 sung3 ban6, m4 teng1 keoi5 zi1 sei2 jan4 dik6
mandarin_meaning: 装聋作哑，对别人的劝告或哀求充耳不闻
english_meaning: to pretend not to hear; to ignore someone's pleas or warnings; deliberately indifferent
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗语/成语（口语化的惯用说法）
explanation_mandarin: 比喻对别人的劝告、请求或责备故意不听、不理，表现得冷漠或固执。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying used to describe someone who deliberately ignores pleas, advice, or reproaches — acting as if deaf and indifferent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我同佢講咁多次，佢都唔理，真係亚聋送殡，唔听佢支死人笛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 gong2 gam2 do1 ci3, keoi5 dou1 m4 lei5, zan1 hai6 aa3 lung4 sung3 ban6, m4 teng1 keoi5 zi1 sei2 jan4 dik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我跟他讲了这么多次，他都不理，真是装聋作哑，对别人的哀求充耳不闻。
examples.english_sentence: I've told him so many times but he ignores it — he's really pretending not to hear people's pleas.

cantonese: 亚茂整饼，冇嗰样整嗰样
jyutping: aa3 mau6 zing2 beng2, mou5 go2 joeng6 zing2 go2 joeng6
mandarin_meaning: 隨便湊合、臨時亂整（隨手把缺乏的東西湊成另一樣）
english_meaning: to improvise or cobble something together; to do something haphazardly or make do with whatever is available
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語用來形容做事隨便、臨時湊合或亂整，沒有計劃或章法，常帶有貶義，指成品質素低或不合預期。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who improvises or puts things together haphazardly without planning; often implies poor quality or a slapdash result.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次佢幫手準備午餐，係亚茂整饼，冇嗰样整嗰样，整到大家都唔識食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 keoi5 bong1 sau2 zeon2 bei6 ng5 caan1, hai6 aa3 mau6 zing2 beng2, mou5 go2 joeng6 zing2 go2 joeng6, zing2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 sik1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次他帮忙准备午餐，随便凑合、乱整一通，弄得大家都不想吃。
examples.english_sentence: This time he helped prepare lunch and just improvised and slapped things together; as a result nobody wanted to eat it.

cantonese: 亚驼卖虾米，大家都唔掂
jyutping: aa3 to4 maai6 haa1 mai5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 dim6
mandarin_meaning: 連（連某人/某情況）都去做低微工作，大家都不行／都很無能
english_meaning: Even (so-and-so) is selling dried shrimp — nobody is capable; used to criticize that everyone is useless or the situation is hopeless
explanation_mandarin: 這句是廣東話的俚語，用來諷刺或抱怨某處境或某個團隊很糟糕、沒有人能勝任。字面上是「亞驼去賣蝦米」，帶有誇張和戲謔成分，暗示連平常不會做某種卑微工作的人也去做，凸顯無能或窮困。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to mock or complain that a situation or group is so bad that nobody is competent. Literally «Á-tuó sells dried shrimp», the expression is hyperbolic and humorous, implying even someone unexpected is doing menial work — highlighting incompetence or desperation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司咁亂，老細唔理，亞驼卖虾米，大家都唔掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gam2 lyun6, lou5 sai3 m4 lei5, aa3 to4 maai6 haa1 mai5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司這麼混亂，老闆不管，連亞驼都去賣蝦米，大家都不行。
examples.english_sentence: The company is such a mess and the boss does nothing — even Á-tuó is selling dried shrimp; nobody can handle it.

jyutping: aa3 to4 ming6, sei2 dou1 m4 dak1 dim6
mandarin_meaning: 倒霉到極點，做任何事都辦不到（根本不可能成功）
english_meaning: Extremely unlucky/hopeless — nothing works or can be done, basically impossible to succeed.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語/俚語（形容詞或感嘆語）
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人或情況非常倒霉或無可救藥，做任何事都無法成功。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone or a situation that is extremely unlucky or hopeless — nothing can be achieved, it's impossible to get it done.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近真係亞驼命，死都唔得掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 zan1 hai6 aa3 to4 ming6, sei2 dou1 m4 dak1 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近真倒霉，什麼事都做不好，根本不可能成功。
examples.english_sentence: He's been really unlucky lately — nothing he does works; it's hopeless.

jyutping: aa3 to4 haang4 lou6, cung1 cung1 (zung1 zung1) dei6
mandarin_meaning: 拖着脚走，沉重地、咚咚作响地走
english_meaning: to trudge or plod along; to walk heavily or stomp with thudding steps
explanation_mandarin: 形容走路時步伐沉重、腳步聲響，像是拖著腳或用力踏地。常用來描寫人走路慢而沉重或心情沉悶時的步態。
explanation_english: Describes walking with heavy, thudding steps—dragging one's feet or stomping, giving a plodding or lumbering gait. Often used to portray tired, heavy-footed, or dejected walking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日亞驼行路，舂舂地，好似好攰咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 aa3 to4 haang4 lou6, cung1 cung1 dei6, hou2 ci5 hou2 gui6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是拖著脚走，沉重地走着，好像很累。
examples.english_sentence: He always trudges along, stomping heavily, as if he's very tired.

mandarin_meaning: （聖經人名）亞伯；也用作譯名或外文名字的音譯。注意與「阿伯」（指伯父或年長男性）不同。
english_meaning: Abel (biblical figure); a transliteration of names like 'Abe' or part of names such as 'Abraham'. Note: different from '阿伯' (uncle/elder man).
explanation_mandarin: 「亞伯」多見於聖經或作為人名的漢字譯法，例如舊約人物亞伯（Abel）。它與口語中稱呼長輩的「阿伯」是不同的字、不同意思。
explanation_english: “亞伯” is commonly used as the Chinese transliteration of the biblical name Abel or as part of transliterated personal names. It is distinct from the colloquial Cantonese term “阿伯” meaning an older man or 'uncle'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 亞伯係聖經入面嘅人物。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 hai6 sing3 ging1 jap6 min6 ge3 jan4 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 亞伯是聖經裡面的人物。
examples.english_sentence: Abel is a figure in the Bible.

synonyms: 亞伯拉罕 (作人名的一部分)
阿伯 (音近，但意思不同，指年長男性或伯父)

mandarin_meaning: 曾祖父
english_meaning: great-grandfather
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的俗稱或方言用語，通常指曾祖父（父親的祖父），在某些地區或年長一代中使用較多。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/dialectal term typically referring to one's great-grandfather (paternal great-grandfather). Common in some regions and older generations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我亞公已經過世好耐喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 gung1 ji5 ging1 gwo3 sai3 hou2 noi6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的曾祖父已經去世很久了。
examples.english_sentence: My great-grandfather passed away a long time ago.

mandarin_meaning: 大叔 / 阿叔（指中年男性）
english_meaning: uncle; middle-aged man (used to refer to an older/ middle-aged male)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語稱呼，指中年或較年長的男性。類似普通話的“大叔”或“阿叔”。語氣可親切、普通或帶輕微不敬，視語境而定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term for a middle-aged or older man. Similar to Mandarin 'dàshū' ('uncle'). Depending on context it can be affectionate, neutral, or mildly dismissive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰位亞叔成日喺街市幫人搬嘢，好有人情味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 wai6 aa3 suk1 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 si5 bong1 jan4 bun1 je5, hou2 jau5 jan4 cing4 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那位大叔經常在街市幫人搬東西，很有人情味。
examples.english_sentence: That uncle often helps people carry things at the market — very warm-hearted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好叫佢細佬，叫佢亞叔啦，佢已經四十幾喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 giu3 keoi5 sai3 lou2, giu3 keoi5 aa3 suk1 laa3, keoi5 ji5 ging1 sei3 sap6 gei2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要叫他小弟，叫他亞叔吧，他已經四十幾了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't call him 'little brother' — call him 'uncle'; he's already in his forties.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）姑媽；對年長女性的稱呼，常作阿姑的書寫變體
english_meaning: aunt (paternal aunt or an older woman addressed as 'aunt')
explanation_mandarin: 「亞姑」在廣東話中多用作稱呼姑媽（父親的姊妹）或對較年長婦女的親切稱呼。書寫上常見變體為「阿姑」。屬口語用法，在香港和廣東話使用者中普遍理解。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "亞姑" is a colloquial term used to refer to an aunt (usually the father's sister) or as a familiar form of address for an older woman. It is often written as "阿姑" in other contexts. This is a spoken, family-oriented term commonly understood in Hong Kong and Cantonese-speaking communities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我亞姑今日返咗香港探我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 gu1 gam1 jat6 faan1 zo2 hoeng1 gong2 taam3 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的姑媽今天回香港來看我。
examples.english_sentence: My aunt came back to Hong Kong today to visit me.

mandarin_meaning: 老太太；祖母（口語）
english_meaning: grandma; old woman (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，指年紀較大的婦人或祖母。可作親切稱呼或泛指老奶奶，語氣和語境會影響禮貌性。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for an elderly woman or grandmother. It can be used affectionately or to refer generally to old ladies; tone and context determine whether it's polite.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我亞婆今日返嚟我哋屋企，同我哋一齊食午飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 po4 gam1 jat6 faan1 lai4 ngo5 dei6 uk1 kei2, tung4 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 sik6 ng5 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我奶奶今天回到我们家，和我们一起吃午饭。
examples.english_sentence: My grandma came to our house today and had lunch with us.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰位亞婆成日喺公園餵鴿仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 wai6 aa3 po4 sing4 jat6 hai2 gung1 jyun4 wai6 gap3 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那位老太太常常在公园喂鸽子。
examples.english_sentence: That old woman often feeds pigeons in the park.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好叫人做亞婆，聽落有啲唔禮貌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 giu3 jan4 zou6 aa3 po4, teng1 lok6 jau5 di1 m4 lai5 maau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要叫别人「亞婆」，听起来有点不礼貌。
examples.english_sentence: Don't call someone 'aa-po' — it sounds a bit rude.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）祖母；奶奶（通常指父親的母親，粵語稱法）
english_meaning: grandmother (colloquial Cantonese; often refers to paternal grandmother)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，指祖母、奶奶，常用於日常稱呼。書寫上常見變體有「阿嫲」或「嫲嫲」。在香港口語中使用頻繁，語氣親切。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term for 'grandmother' (often the paternal grandmother). Common in Hong Kong speech and used familiarly; variants include 阿嫲 and 嫲嫲.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我星期日會帶亞嫲去街市買餸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing1 kei4 jat6 wui5 daai3 aa3 maa4 heoi3 gaai1 si5 maai5 sung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我星期日會帶奶奶去菜市場買菜。
examples.english_sentence: I'll take grandma to the market on Sunday.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 亞嫲成日話佢細個嗰陣好窮，但係仍然好開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa4 sing4 jat6 waa6 keoi5 sai3 go3 go2 zan6 hou2 kung4, daan6 hai6 jing4 jin4 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶常說她小時候很窮，但還是很快樂。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma often says she was poor when she was young, but she was still happy.

mandarin_meaning: 小官、小職員（帶貶義）
english_meaning: a low-ranking official or petty bureaucrat (derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，通常帶貶義，用來形容職位低微但愛擺架子、或在官場/機構中只做細務且權力有限的小官員或小職員。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term, usually derogatory, referring to a low-ranking official or petty clerk — someone who has little real power but acts officious or self-important.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係做署裏面啲細務，係個亞官仔啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 zou6 cyu5 leoi5 min6 di1 sai3 mou6, hai6 go3 aa3 gwaan1 zai2 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只是做署里的一些细务，是个小官而已。
examples.english_sentence: He's only handling minor office tasks; he's just a low-ranking official.

mandarin_meaning: 人名或暱稱（亞茂 / 阿茂）
english_meaning: Personal name or nickname (A-Mau / Ah Mau)
explanation_mandarin: 「亞茂」並非常見的通用詞彙，通常用作人名或暱稱。字面上「亞」常作名字用字或姓氏，「茂」有茂盛、繁盛之意。日常粵語口語中更常見的變體為「阿茂」。
explanation_english: “亞茂” is not a common lexical item but is typically used as a personal name or nickname. Literally, 亞 can appear in names or as a surname and 茂 means luxuriant/prosperous. In Cantonese speech the variant “阿茂” (Ah Mau) is more frequently heard.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 亞茂今日唔嚟上班，可能病咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 mau6 gam1 jat6 m4 lai4 soeng5 baan1, ho2 nang4 beng6 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 亚茂今天不上班，可能生病了。
examples.english_sentence: A-Mau didn't come to work today; he might be sick.

mandarin_meaning: 交工资 / 交粮食（交付钱财或实物）
english_meaning: to pay wages; to hand over money; (literally) to deliver grain
explanation_mandarin: 「交糧」字面意思是交付糧食（古時向官府或地主上繳糧食）。在廣東話與香港口語中也常用作付出錢財或支付工資的意思（相當於「發工資」「付薪」或一般的「交錢」）。
explanation_english: Literally 'to hand over grain' (historically used for delivering grain to authorities). In Cantonese/Hong Kong usage it is commonly used to mean handing over money or paying wages (similar to 'pay salary' or more generally 'pay up').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司每個月二十號交糧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 mui5 go3 jyut6 ji6 sap6 hou6 gaau1 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司每个月20号发工资。
examples.english_sentence: The company pays salaries on the 20th of each month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 以前農村每年要交糧畀官府。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji5 cin4 nung4 cyun1 mui5 nin4 jiu3 gaau1 loeng4 bei2 gun1 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 以前農村每年要交粮给官府。
examples.english_sentence: In the past, villagers had to deliver grain to the authorities every year.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見、方言用語）形容冷清、蕭條或氣氛冷淡
english_meaning: A rare/regional Cantonese slang meaning (roughly) deserted, cold, or having a chilly/awkward atmosphere
explanation_mandarin: 「亨棚冷」為廣東地區罕見的俗語/方言用法，字面上可拆為「亨／棚／冷」，通常用來形容場所或場面很冷清、沒人氣，或形容人覺得尷尬、冷場。詞源與使用範圍不廣，屬口語、區域性表達。
explanation_english: “亨棚冷” is a rare/regional Cantonese slang expression. Literally composed of the characters 亨, 棚, 冷, it is typically used to describe a place or situation that is quiet/deserted or an atmosphere that is chilly/awkward. It is colloquial and regionally limited; usage is uncommon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢排鋪頭生意唔好，成條街都亨棚冷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 paai4 pou3 tau2 saang1 ji3 m4 hou2, seng4 tiu4 gaai1 dou1 hang1 paang4 laang5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近店鋪生意不好，整條街都很冷清。
examples.english_sentence: Business has been bad lately — the whole street is deserted.

mandarin_meaning: 亲自出面/亲自处理
english_meaning: to do something personally; to handle personally
explanation_mandarin: 表示亲自出面或亲自做事，强调自己动手或亲自处理事务。
explanation_english: Indicates doing something personally or handling matters oneself; emphasizes personal involvement and hands-on action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆親力親為處理呢次危機，員工都好佩服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 can1 lik6 can1 wai4 cyu2 lei5 ni1 ci3 ngai4 gei1, jyun4 gung1 dou1 hou2 pui3 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板亲力亲为处理这次危机，员工都很佩服。
examples.english_sentence: The boss handled this crisis personally; the staff were very impressed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗確保工程順利，佢親力親為監督每一個步驟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 kok3 bou2 gung1 cing4 seon6 lei6, keoi5 can1 lik6 can1 wai4 gaam1 duk1 mui5 jat1 go3 bou6 zau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了确保工程顺利，他亲力亲为监督每一个步骤。
examples.english_sentence: To ensure the project ran smoothly, he personally supervised every step.

jyutping: can1 saang1 zai2 bat1 jyu4 gan6 san1 cin2
mandarin_meaning: 亲生儿子不如随身的钱 / 身边的钱
english_meaning: Money on hand is more valuable/reliable than one's biological son (i.e. cash is more dependable than family ties).
explanation_mandarin: 一句粤语俗语，意思是現金在手比親人（例如親生兒子）更實用或可靠，反映世俗重視金錢的觀念。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb meaning that cash you have on you is more useful or reliable than one's own children; reflects a pragmatic or materialistic attitude that prefers money for security.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽成日講：親生仔不如近身錢，攞住啲錢先至放心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 gong2: can1 saang1 zai2 bat1 jyu4 gan6 san1 cin2, lo2 zyu6 di1 cin2 sin1 zi3 fong3 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我妈妈常说：亲生儿子不如随身的钱，拿着钱才放心。
examples.english_sentence: My mom often says: money on hand is better than a son — holding money is what makes her feel secure.

cantonese: 亲生仔唔似近身钱，靠买米不及自耕田
jyutping: can1 saang1 zai2 m4 ci5 gan6 san1 cin2, kaau3 maai5 mai5 bat1 kap6 zi6 gaang1 tin4
mandarin_meaning: 親生兒子不如身邊的錢，靠買米不如自己耕田（強調自力更生，不如依靠自己）
english_meaning: A biological son isn't as reliable as money on you; buying rice isn't as good as farming your own field — emphasizes self-reliance and producing your own sustenance rather than depending on others.
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語用誇張的比喻說明血緣或外援未必可靠，比不上隨身的現金或自己勞動所得，勸人要自力更生、依靠自己的努力。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb uses a striking comparison to say that even close kin may not be as dependable as having money on hand, and that buying food is inferior to growing it yourself — a warning to value self-reliance and one's own labor over depending on others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老豆成日講：親生仔唔似近身錢，靠買米不及自耕田，叫我自己搵食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 dau6 seng4 jat6 gong2: can1 saang1 zai2 m4 ci5 gan6 san1 cin2, kaau3 maai5 mai5 bat1 kap6 zi6 gaang1 tin4, giu3 ngo5 zi6 gei2 waan2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 爸爸常說：親生兒子不如身邊的錢，靠買米不如自己耕田，叫我要靠自己謀生。
examples.english_sentence: My dad often says, 'A biological son isn't like money on you; buying rice doesn't compare to farming your own field,' telling me to support myself.

jyutping: jan4 jat1 sai3, mat6 jat1 sai3
mandarin_meaning: 人生一世，萬物有其壽命/定數，世事無常
english_meaning: People and things each have their own lifetime/fate; life and things are transient
explanation_mandarin: 表示人生和萬物皆有各自的生命與定數，強調世事無常與對得失看淡的態度。
explanation_english: A proverb expressing that people and objects each have their own lifespan and fate; it emphasizes impermanence and an attitude of acceptance toward change.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企啲舊嘢係有回憶，但人一世，物一世，總有一日要放手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei5 di1 gau6 je5 hai6 jau5 wui4 jik1, daan6 jan4 jat1 sai3, mat6 jat1 sai3, zung2 jau5 jat1 jat6 jiu3 fong3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡的舊東西有回憶，但人生一世，物件也有壽命，總有一天要放手。
examples.english_sentence: Old things at home hold memories, but people and things are transient; someday you have to let go.

cantonese: 人丑望衣装，鬓丑望花傍
jyutping: jan4 cau2 mong6 ji1 zong1, ban6 cau2 mong6 faa1 bong6
mandarin_meaning: 外貌不佳的人靠衣着或饰品来弥补和装扮自己
english_meaning: A proverb saying that people who consider themselves unattractive rely on clothing or accessories to compensate for their looks
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，意思是外貌不佳的人會透過穿衣打扮或戴飾品來彌補形象，常帶自嘲或評論他人重視外表的意味。
explanation_english: A saying that describes how people compensate for a perceived lack of attractiveness by dressing up or using ornaments; often used jokingly or to comment on vanity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢自嘲話：'人丑望衣装，鬓丑望花傍'，所以成日買衫買頭飾補償。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi6 caau4 waa6: 'jan4 cau2 mong6 ji1 zong1, ban6 cau2 mong6 faa1 bong6', so2 ji5 sing4 jat6 maai5 saam1 maai5 tau4 sik1 bou2 soeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她自嘲地说：'人丑望衣装，鬓丑望花傍'，所以总是买衣服和头饰来弥补。
examples.english_sentence: She joked, 'If you're ugly you rely on clothes; if your temples are unattractive you rely on hair ornaments,' so she always buys clothes and hair accessories to compensate.

cantonese: 人争一口气，树争一层皮
jyutping: jan4 zang1 jat1 hau2 hei3, syu6 zang1 jat1 cang4 pei4
mandarin_meaning: 人都想保全面子或尊嚴；每個人都會為了自己的利益或體面而爭辯或堅持。
english_meaning: People fight to preserve a bit of pride or dignity; everyone will resist losing what matters to their honor.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語比喻人為了面子、尊嚴或小小的利益都會努力爭取或堅持不讓步，就像樹會保護自己的樹皮一樣。
explanation_english: This proverb likens people’s desire to keep face or dignity to a tree protecting its bark — everyone will strive to hold on to even a small piece of pride or advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔肯承認錯，話係面子問題，真係人爭一口氣，樹爭一層皮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 hang2 sing4 jing6 co3, waa6 hai6 min6 zi2 man6 tai4, zan1 hai6 jan4 zang1 jat1 hau2 hei3, syu6 zang1 jat1 cang4 pei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不肯承认错误，说是面子问题，真的是人争一口气，树争一层皮。
examples.english_sentence: He won’t admit his mistake, saying it’s a matter of face — it’s really a case of 'people fight for a bit of pride, trees for a layer of bark.'

cantonese: 人人识和尚，和尚唔识人
jyutping: jan4 jan4 sik1 wo4 soeng6, wo4 soeng6 m4 sik1 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 人人都认识和尚，可和尚却不认识任何人（用来形容只有别人认识某人，但那人不认识或不理会别人）
english_meaning: Everyone knows the monk, but the monk doesn't know anyone (used to describe one-sided recognition or an aloof person who doesn't acknowledge others)
explanation_mandarin: 表示人际关系不对等：别人都认识或熟悉某人，但那人却不认识或不理会他人，常带讽刺或抱怨意味。
explanation_english: Describes an asymmetric social situation: many people know or recognize someone, but that person does not recognize or acknowledge others. Often used sarcastically to complain about aloofness or selective recognition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗老闆之後就好高傲，真係人人識和尚，和尚唔識人，見員工都唔打招呼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 lou5 baan2 zi1 hau6 zau6 hou2 gou1 ngou6, zan1 hai6 jan4 jan4 sik1 wo4 soeng6, wo4 soeng6 m4 sik1 jan4, gin3 jyun4 gung1 dou1 m4 daa2 ziu1 fu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做了老板之后变得很高傲，真是人人识和尚，和尚不识人，看到员工都不打招呼。
examples.english_sentence: After becoming the boss he got very arrogant — really: everyone knows him, but he doesn't know anyone; he doesn't even greet his employees.

mandarin_meaning: （年紀）很小的小孩；年紀幼小
english_meaning: very young; a little child; small/young person
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語說法，用來形容年紀很小或體型嬌小的人，常用於指小朋友或尚未成熟的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to describe someone who is very young or small in stature, often referring to children or people who are not yet mature.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢人仔細細，仲未識得照顧自己。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan4 zai2 sai3 sai3, zung6 mei6 sik1 dak1 ziu3 gu3 zi6 gei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他年紀很小，還不會照顧自己。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is still very young and can't take care of themselves yet.

mandarin_meaning: 人的生命比什麼都重要（與「生命重於泰山」相近）
english_meaning: Human life is more important than anything; life is paramount.
explanation_mandarin: 用來強調人的生命至為重要，常用於緊急或危險情況，表示應把救人或保護生命放在首位，而非顧及財物或其他考量。
explanation_english: Used to stress that human life is of the highest importance. Often said in emergencies or dangerous situations to indicate that saving or protecting life takes precedence over property or other concerns.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 發生火災嗰陣，記住人命大過天，唔好為咗拎嘢返屋企冒險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 sang1 fo2 zoi1 go2 zan6, gei3 zyu6 jan4 ming6 daai6 gwo3 tin1, m4 hou2 wai6 zo2 ling1 je5 faan1 uk1 kei5 mou6 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 發生火災時要記住人命大過天，不要為了拿東西回家冒險。
examples.english_sentence: During a fire, remember that life is more important than anything — don't risk going back in to grab things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到病人咁危險，醫生話人命大過天，必須緊急搶救。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 beng6 jan4 gam2 ngai4 him2, ji1 sang1 waa6 jan4 ming6 daai6 gwo3 tin1, bit1 seoi1 gan2 gap1 coeng2 gau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到病人這麼危險，醫生說人命大過天，必須緊急搶救。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing the patient in such danger, the doctor said life is paramount and immediate rescue is necessary.

cantonese: 人善畀人欺，马善畀人骑
jyutping: jan4 sin6 bei2 jan4 hei1, maa5 sin6 bei2 jan4 kei4
mandarin_meaning: 人善被人欺，马善被人骑（好人容易吃亏，太善良或太顺从会被利用或欺负）
english_meaning: If you're too kind or too submissive, people will take advantage of you.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話的意思是如果一個人太善良、太好相處或太順從，就容易被別人欺負或利用。
explanation_english: This proverb warns that people who are overly kind or submissive tend to be taken advantage of or bullied.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我媽成日都講：人善畀人欺，唔好畀人利用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maa1 sing4 jat6 dou1 gong2: jan4 sin6 bei2 jan4 hei1, m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 lei6 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我妈妈经常说：人善被人欺，不要让别人利用你。
examples.english_sentence: My mom always says: 'If you're too nice you'll be taken advantage of; don't let others use you.'

mandarin_meaning: 別人；人家
english_meaning: other people; others; somebody else
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法的代詞，表示“別人”或“人家”，可作主語、賓語或表示所有關係（人地嘅...）。常見於香港口語中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese pronoun meaning 'other people' or 'others'. It can function as subject, object, or possessive (e.g. 人地嘅...) and is common in Hong Kong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 人地話佢好叻，你點唔信？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jan4 dei6 waa6 keoi5 hou2 lak1, nei5 dim2 m4 seon3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別人說他很厲害，你為什麼不相信？
examples.english_sentence: People say he's really capable — why don't you believe it?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好亂用人地嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lyun6 jung6 jan4 dei6 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要隨便用別人的東西。
examples.english_sentence: Don't use other people's things without permission.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 人地已經做到，你仲未開始？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jan4 dei6 ji5 ging1 zou6 dou3, nei5 zung6 mei6 hoi1 ci2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別人已經做到了，你還沒開始？
examples.english_sentence: Others have already finished it — you haven't even started?

jyutping: jan4 do1 tau1 ngau4 mou4 zeoi6
mandarin_meaning: 人多偷牛无罪（字面：人多偷牛不算有罪）——用来形容人多时，坏事更容易被掩盖或被容忍，集体行为稀释个人责任。
english_meaning: Literal: "If many people, stealing a cow isn't a crime." An idiom meaning that wrongdoing committed by a crowd is more likely to be tolerated or go unpunished; collective participation dilutes individual responsibility.
explanation_mandarin: 该俗语用以讽刺或批评在多人参与时，违规或违法行为更易被忽视或纵容，强调“从众”会弱化个体应承担的责任。
explanation_english: A colloquial/proverbial expression criticizing the idea that when many people are involved, misdeeds are easier to hide or excuse. It highlights how crowd behavior can weaken individual accountability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋成班人一齊做壞事，好似人多偷牛無罪噉，根本唔驚畀人發現。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 sing4 baan1 jat1 cai4 zou6 waai6 si6, hou2 ci5 jan4 do1 tau1 ngau4 mou4 zeoi6 gam2, gan1 bun2 m4 ging1 bei2 jan4 faat3 jin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们一大帮人一起做坏事，好像“人多偷牛无罪”一样，根本不怕被人发现。
examples.english_sentence: They all did the bad things together, like 'when many people are involved, stealing a cow isn't a crime,' so they weren't afraid of being found out.

mandarin_meaning: 人多嘴杂（很多人、说话多且意见纷乱）
english_meaning: Many people and many mouths — a situation with lots of people, opinions, gossip or noise; chaotic and hard to reach consensus.
explanation_mandarin: 形容人多、说话杂、意见纷乱，场面嘈杂或难以统一意见，也可指因人数众多而产生的闲言碎语或干扰。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where many people are present and many differing opinions or gossip are voiced; noisy, chaotic, and difficult to reach agreement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事人多口雜，最好唔好喺度討論。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 jan4 do1 hau2 zaap6, zeoi3 hou2 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 tou2 leon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事人多嘴杂，最好不要在这里讨论。
examples.english_sentence: This matter attracts too many people and too much gossip; it's best not to discuss it here.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開會時人多口雜，意見好難統一。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 wui2 si4 jan4 do1 hau2 zaap6, ji3 gin3 hou2 naan4 tung2 jat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开会时人多嘴杂，意见很难统一。
examples.english_sentence: When there are many people at the meeting, there are many conflicting opinions and it's hard to reach consensus.

cantonese: 人多好做作，人少好食作
jyutping: jan4 do1 hou2 zou6 zok3, jan4 siu2 hou2 sik6 zok3
mandarin_meaning: 人多时爱做作、摆架子；人少时则更能放松享受（有时也指小范围内更方便吃好或占便宜）。
english_meaning: When there are many people, people tend to act pretentiously or put on a show; when there are few, it's easier to relax and enjoy (sometimes implying it's easier to eat well or take advantage in a small group).
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用來描述人在不同人數面前的不同表現：人多時會比較做作、擺架子或討好他人；人少時則較能放鬆、親近或專心享受，有時也帶有『小圈子比較容易享受或占便宜』的意思。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying describes how people behave differently depending on the crowd size: with many people present they tend to be showy, pretentious, or obsequious; with few people they can relax, be more intimate, or genuinely enjoy themselves. It can also imply that in small groups it's easier to 'eat well' or take advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰晚婚禮到處都係人，大家表現得好做作；返到屋企得幾個人先可以慢慢食，真係人多好做作，人少好食作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 maan5 fan1 lai5 dou3 cyu3 dou1 hai6 jan4, daai6 gaa1 biu2 jin2 dak1 hou2 zou6 zok3; faan1 dou3 uk1 kei5 dak1 gei2 go3 jan4 sin1 ho2 ji5 maan6 maan6 sik6, zan1 hai6 jan4 do1 hou2 zou6 zok3, jan4 siu2 hou2 sik6 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那晚婚禮到處都是人，大家表現得很做作；回到家只有幾個人才能慢慢吃，真是人多好做作，人少好食作。
examples.english_sentence: That night's wedding was packed and everyone was so performative; only when we got home with a few people could we eat slowly. Truly: with many people it's easy to be pretentious, with few it's easier to enjoy.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）因為人多而導致慌亂或混亂，與「人多手忙腳亂」意思相近
english_meaning: (colloquial) When there are many people and things become chaotic or disorganized; everyone is flustered
explanation_mandarin: 形容因為人多或場面擁擠，導致大家慌張、做事沒有條理，安排混亂。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where the presence of many people causes confusion and disorder; people become flustered and actions lack coordination.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰日人多手脚乱，大家都唔知做乜好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 jat6 jan4 do1 sau2 goek3 lyun6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zi1 zou6 mat1 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那天人多手脚乱，大家都不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: That day it was chaotic with too many people; nobody knew what to do.

jyutping: jan4 do1 zaa3 gau2 m4 jin6
mandarin_meaning: 人多手雜 / 太多人參與反而把事情弄壞
english_meaning: Too many people involved spoil the job; too many cooks spoil the broth
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語字面上說若有很多人一起煮狗，狗就不會煮得軟，意指人多反而容易因為意見不一或互相干擾，把事情弄糟。相當於中文的“人多手雜”或英語的“Too many cooks spoil the broth”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally meaning 'if many people boil a dog, it won't become tender.' It means that when too many people are involved, the task often goes wrong due to interference or conflicting opinions — equivalent to 'too many cooks spoil the broth.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事唔好叫咁多人嚟幫手，人多煠狗唔腍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 m4 hou2 giu3 gam2 do1 jan4 lei4 bong1 sau2, jan4 do1 zaa3 gau2 m4 jin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事不要找那麼多人來幫手，人多手雜（人多反而弄壞）。
examples.english_sentence: Don't get so many people to help with this; too many people will spoil the job.

synonyms: Too many cooks spoil the broth

mandarin_meaning: 很多人；一群人（口語）
english_meaning: a lot of people; a group/a crowd (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用法，表示很多人或一群人在一起，常用於非正式場合描述人多或成群的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning many people or a group/crowd. Used informally to describe places or situations with lots of people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚派對門口人夥，排咗好耐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 paai3 deoi6 mun4 hau2 jan4 fo2, paai4 zo2 hou2 noi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚派對門口有很多人，排了很久。
examples.english_sentence: There are lots of people at the party entrance tonight; they've been queuing for a long time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成條街人夥，行唔到路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 tiu4 gaai1 jan4 fo2, haang4 m4 dou3 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 整條街都是人，走不了路。
examples.english_sentence: The whole street is crowded; you can't walk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋去買嘢嗰陣，市集入面人夥，要小心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 maai5 je5 go2 zan6, si5 zaap6 jap6 min6 jan4 fo2, jiu3 siu2 sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們去買東西的時候，市集裡面很多人，要小心一點。
examples.english_sentence: When we went shopping the market was packed; be a bit careful.

mandarin_meaning: 形容人非常愚蠢、没脑筋（贬义）
english_meaning: Derogatory phrase describing someone as very stupid or brainless
explanation_mandarin: 俗语，用来责骂或嘲讽别人愚笨、缺乏常识或判断力。
explanation_english: A colloquial insult used to mock someone as foolish, lacking common sense or good judgment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日遲到，真係人頭豬腦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ci4 dou3, zan1 hai6 jan4 tau4 zyu1 nou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是迟到，真是人头猪脑！
examples.english_sentence: He's always late; what an idiot!

mandarin_meaning: 人心不知足 / 人總是沒有滿足
english_meaning: People's hearts are never satisfied; human greed is insatiable.
explanation_mandarin: 表示人心總是難以滿足，常用來形容貪婪或不知足的人或行為。
explanation_english: Expresses that people are hard to satisfy; commonly used to describe greed or a person who is never content.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 人心冇厌足，佢而家有車有樓都覺得未夠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jan4 sam1 mou5 jim6 zuk1, keoi5 ji4 gaa1 jau5 ce1 jau5 lau4 dou1 gok3 dak1 mei6 gau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 人心不知足，他現在有車有房也覺得不夠。
examples.english_sentence: People's hearts are never satisfied; even though they now have a car and a flat, they still feel it's not enough.

cantonese: 人心隔肚皮，冷饭隔筲箕
jyutping: jan4 sam1 gaak3 tou5 pei4, laang5 faan6 gaak3 saau1 gei1
mandarin_meaning: 人心难以揣测，人与人之间有隔阂，旧情或旧事难以恢复
english_meaning: You cannot read another person's heart; there are barriers between people, and past feelings or matters are hard to restore
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東俗語由兩句並列成分組成。前半句「人心隔肚皮」指人心難以捉摸，看不透別人的真實想法；後半句「冷飯隔筲箕」以比喻形容隔著器物而難以融合或回復，總體用來強調人與人之間的隔閡或舊情難返。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb consists of two parallel parts. The first, “人心隔肚皮,” means people’s hearts are hard to read; the second, “冷饭隔筲箕,” uses a simile (cold rice separated by a winnowing basket) to emphasize separation and difficulty of reuniting or restoring past warmth. Together it stresses interpersonal barriers or that old feelings are hard to rekindle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋分咗手，雖然想復合，但人心隔肚皮，冷飯隔筲箕，冇咁容易。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 fan1 zo2 sau2, seoi1 jin4 soeng2 fuk6 hap6, daan6 jan4 sam1 gaak3 tou5 pei4, laang5 faan6 gaak3 saau1 gei1, mou5 gam2 jung4 ji6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们分手了，虽然想复合，但人心隔肚皮，冷饭隔筲箕，不那么容易。
examples.english_sentence: They broke up; although they want to get back together, you can't read people's hearts and it's not easy to rekindle old feelings.

cantonese: 人怕三分虎，虎怕七分人
jyutping: jan4 paa3 saam1 fan1 fu2, fu2 paa3 cat1 fan1 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 人怕三分虎，虎怕七分人（谚语）——比喻表面凶猛或强势的事物令人畏惧，但多数人有勇气或计谋时，强者也会畏惧。
english_meaning: People fear a little of a tiger's ferocity, but a tiger fears most people's courage — a proverb meaning that outward fierceness can intimidate, yet numbers, resolve or cleverness of people can overcome a threat.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語強調表面上的威嚇有時能讓人退縮，但若多數人有膽量或智慧，連看似可怕的對象也會害怕。
explanation_english: This proverb emphasizes that a show of fierceness can intimidate people, but when people are courageous, numerous, or clever, even a formidable threat can be put off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話做人唔好成日示弱，記住人怕三分虎，虎怕七分人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 zou6 jan4 m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 si6 joek6, gei3 zyu6 jan4 paa3 saam1 fan1 fu2, fu2 paa3 cat1 fan1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说做人不要总是示弱，要记住人怕三分虎，虎怕七分人。
examples.english_sentence: He said you shouldn't always show weakness — remember the proverb: people fear a bit of a tiger, but a tiger fears most people's courage.

jyutping: jan4 paa3 soeng1 sam1, syu6 paa3 bok3 pei4
mandarin_meaning: 人害怕受伤，树害怕被剥去树皮（比喻人人都有脆弱的一面，害怕被伤害）
english_meaning: People fear being hurt, just as trees fear having their bark peeled off (a metaphor meaning everyone has vulnerabilities and fears being harmed).
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用比喻说明人会害怕感情上或精神上的伤害，就像树害怕被剥去树皮一样，提醒人们要小心不要伤害别人，也表达人人都有脆弱之处。
explanation_english: A proverb that uses a metaphor: people fear emotional or psychological hurt just as trees fear having their bark stripped. It warns to be careful not to hurt others and acknowledges human vulnerability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣講好傷人，記住人怕伤心，树怕剥皮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 gong2 hou2 soeng1 jan4, gei3 zyu6 jan4 paa3 soeng1 sam1, syu6 paa3 bok3 pei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这样说很伤人，记住“人怕伤心，树怕剥皮”。
examples.english_sentence: What you said is hurtful — remember that people fear being hurt, just like trees fear losing their bark.

jyutping: jan4 paa3 dong6, mai5 paa3 saai1
mandarin_meaning: 人怕被揭短，米怕被篩檢（比喻事物或人都害怕被檢視或挑剔）
english_meaning: People fear being exposed; rice fears the sieve — a proverb meaning everyone dislikes scrutiny or being picked apart.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東俗語字面上說人害怕被揭短、米害怕被篩選，實際用來比喻人或東西都怕被檢查、挑毛病或被當眾揭穿缺點。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb literally says people fear being exposed and rice fears being sifted. Figuratively it means people (or things) dislike scrutiny, inspection, or being picked apart and criticized.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺會議上唔好太出風頭，始終人怕𫩳，米怕筛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 wui6 ji5 soeng6 m4 hou2 taai3 ceot1 fung1 tau4, ci2 zung1 jan4 paa3 dong6, mai5 paa3 saai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在會議上不要太出風頭，總之人怕被揭短，米怕被篩。
examples.english_sentence: Don't show off too much in the meeting — after all, people fear exposure and rice fears being sifted.

jyutping: jan4 cing4 daai6 gwo3 zing3 ming4
mandarin_meaning: 人情比證明更重要 / 靠關係勝過靠證件或資格
english_meaning: Connections/personal favors matter more than certificates or formal proof
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容在某些情況或社會關係網中，人情（關係、面子、好處）比正式的證明或資格更能決定結果或獲得優惠。
explanation_english: Used to describe situations where personal favors, relationships, or social capital carry more influence than formal proof, documents, or qualifications.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺香港，申請嗰啲優惠時，人情大過證明，有時關係重過資格。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 hoeng1 gong2, san1 cing2 go2 di1 jau1 wai6 si4, jan4 cing4 daai6 gwo3 zing3 ming4, gwaan1 hai6 jau5 si4 zung6 gwo3 zi1 gaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在香港，申請那些優惠時，人情比證明更重要，有時關係比資格更重要。
examples.english_sentence: In Hong Kong, when applying for certain benefits, connections matter more than documents; sometimes relationships trump qualifications.

cantonese: 人情留一线，日后好相见
jyutping: jan4 cing4 lau4 jat1 sin3, jat6 hau6 hou2 soeng1 gin3
mandarin_meaning: 做人要留餘地/留一線，以便日後仍能和睦相處或保全關係。
english_meaning: Leave some goodwill or leeway so that you can get along or meet pleasantly in the future.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話勸人處事不要把話或行為做得太絕，要給對方留面子或餘地，方便將來仍能保持良好關係或再見面時不尷尬。
explanation_english: A proverb advising people not to be too harsh or final in words or actions; leave someone some face or leeway so future relations or meetings remain cordial.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁絕情，做人要記住人情留一線，日后好相見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 zyut6 cing4, zou6 jan4 jiu3 gei3 zyu6 jan4 cing4 lau4 jat1 sin3, jat6 hau6 hou2 soeng1 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要這麼絕情，做人要記得給別人留餘地，日後好相見。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so heartless; remember to leave people some leeway so you can get along when you meet again.

mandarin_meaning: 人情重于债务/金钱
english_meaning: Social favors/obligations are considered more important than financial debts/money
explanation_mandarin: 表示在人际关系中，人情（人面、帮忙、情义）比金钱或债务更重要，常用来说明宁愿欠人情也不计较金钱得失。
explanation_english: Expresses that social obligations, favors, or face are valued above monetary debts; often used to indicate one prioritizes relationships over strictly accounting money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢幫咗我咁多，我點可以計較錢？人情緊過債。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bong1 zo2 ngo5 gam2 do1, ngo5 dim2 ho2 ji5 gai3 gaau3 cin2? jan4 cing4 gan2 gwo3 zai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他帮了我这么多，我怎么能计较钱？人情重于债。
examples.english_sentence: He helped me so much — how can I haggle over money? Favors are more important than debts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺香港搵人幫手，常常要顧及人情，人情緊過債，唔好淨係睇錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 hoeng1 gong2 wan2 jan4 bong1 sau2, soeng4 soeng4 jiu3 gu3 kap1 jan4 cing4, jan4 cing4 gan2 gwo3 zai3, m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 tai2 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在香港找人帮忙时，常常要顾及人情，人情重于债，不要只看钱。
examples.english_sentence: In Hong Kong, when asking for help you often need to consider social ties — favors matter more than debts; don't just look at money.

cantonese: 人无千日好，花无百日红
jyutping: jan4 mou4 cin1 jat6 hou2, faa1 mou4 baak3 jat6 hung4
mandarin_meaning: 人不会永远顺利，好景不常在
english_meaning: Nothing stays good forever; good times don't last.
explanation_mandarin: 用来表示人的好运或兴盛的状态不会永远持续，提醒人们看淡盛衰、珍惜当下或有所防备。
explanation_english: A proverb expressing that good fortune or prosperity is temporary; it warns that success and good times are transient and encourages caution or acceptance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢依家有錢，但要記住人無千日好，花無百日紅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji1 gaa1 jau5 cin2, daan6 jiu3 gei3 zyu6 jan4 mou4 cin1 jat6 hou2, faa1 mou4 baak3 jat6 hung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在有钱，但要记住人无千日好，花无百日红。
examples.english_sentence: He has money now, but remember that good times don't last.

cantonese: 人无生活计，枉食人间米
jyutping: jan4 mou4 saang1 wut6 gai3, wong5 sik6 jan4 gaan1 mai5
mandarin_meaning: 人若没有谋生的办法或计划，就白白吃着人间的饭（含责备不自立或成为负担之意）
english_meaning: If someone has no means or plan to make a living, they're merely wasting others' resources; a reproach against not being self-reliant.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用来责备或劝诫那些没有谋生能力或不肯自立的人，意思是没有生计还白吃人间的饭，是对不自立、懒惰或依赖他人的批评。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb used to rebuke or warn people who lack the means or will to support themselves. It implies that without a livelihood, living off others is shameful or wasteful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢無穩定工作又懶，大家都話佢人無生活計，枉食人間米。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou4 wan2 ding6 gung1 zok3 jau6 laan5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 keoi5 jan4 mou4 saang1 wut6 gai3, wong5 sik6 jan4 gaan1 mai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他沒有穩定工作又懶，大家都說他人無生活計，枉食人間米。
examples.english_sentence: He has no steady job and is lazy; everyone says he has no way to support himself and is just living off others.

jyutping: jan4 jau5 sat1 sau2, maa5 jau5 sat1 tai4
mandarin_meaning: 每個人都有可能犯錯，失誤在所難免。
english_meaning: Everyone makes mistakes; even the best can slip up.
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示人難免會犯錯，遇到失誤不應過分苛責，強調寬容和理解。
explanation_english: Used to express that people inevitably make mistakes; errors are unavoidable and one should be tolerant rather than overly critical.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次做錯咗，唔好太難為佢，畢竟人有失手，馬有失蹄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 zou6 co3 zo2, m4 hou2 taai3 naan4 wai4 keoi5, bat1 ging3 jan4 jau5 sat1 sau2, maa5 jau5 sat1 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他这次做错了，不要太为难他，毕竟人有失手，马有失蹄。
examples.english_sentence: He made a mistake this time; don't be too hard on him — after all, everyone makes mistakes.

mandarin_meaning: 形容表情或行為呆板、不自然、反應遲鈍的人（口語、貶義）
english_meaning: a person who is stiff, expressionless, or rigid in behavior (colloquial/slang, often pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 「人板」是香港粵語的口語或俚語，用來形容一個人面無表情、動作或反應很呆板、不自然，通常帶有輕微貶義或戲稱成分。
explanation_english: “人板” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang used to describe someone who is deadpan, stiff, or slow to react—often used pejoratively or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都好人板，講咩都冇反應。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 hou2 jan4 baan2, gong2 me1 dou1 mou5 faan2 jing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她總是很呆板，說什麼都沒有反應。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is always so stiff and expressionless; doesn't react to anything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面試嗰陣佢好人板，點都唔自然，最後冇錄取。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 si3 go2 zan6 keoi5 hou2 jan4 baan2, dim2 dou1 m4 zi6 jin4, zeoi3 hau6 mou5 luk6 ceoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面試時他/她很呆板，什麼都不自然，最後沒有被錄取。
examples.english_sentence: During the interview he/she was very stiff and unnatural, and in the end wasn't hired.

cantonese: 人横有所恃，大食有指拟
jyutping: jan4 waang4 jau5 so2 si6, daai6 sik6 jau5 zi2 ji5
mandarin_meaning: 有人撐腰、有門路（口語俗語）
english_meaning: Those who act arrogantly have backing; the powerful/rich have connections (colloquial proverb).
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用來形容有人橫行或仗勢欺人，是因為背後有人撐腰；有權勢或有錢的人則有門路和人安排、出手。語氣偏口語、帶批評或無奈意味，區域性較強。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial proverb says that people who behave arrogantly often have someone supporting them; the powerful or wealthy have connections and people to carry out things. It is a critical/ironic observation about backing, influence, and patronage; used informally and regionally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講起黑社會，真係人横有所恃，大食有指拟，佢哋乜都做得出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 hei2 hak1 se5 wui2, zan1 hai6 jan4 waang4 jau5 so2 si6, daai6 sik6 jau5 zi2 ji5, keoi5 dei6 mat1 dou1 zou6 dak1 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 說到黑社會，真的有人倚仗勢力、有靠山，他們什麼都做得出來。
examples.english_sentence: Talking about the triads, it's true they have backing and connections; they'd do anything.

jyutping: jan4 sei2 lau4 ming4, fu2 sei2 lau4 pei4
mandarin_meaning: 人死留名，虎死留皮（谚语）
english_meaning: A proverb meaning people strive to leave a lasting reputation or legacy after death (literally: a person leaves a name when he dies; a tiger leaves its skin).
explanation_mandarin: 表示人們希望死後能留下名聲或功績，以便被後世紀念。常用來形容追求名譽、功勳或遺澤的行為或動機。
explanation_english: Expresses the idea that people hope to leave a name (reputation or legacy) after death so they will be remembered. Often used to describe actions motivated by a desire for fame, reputation, or lasting achievements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一生為國家犧牲，真係做到人死留名，虎死留皮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 sang1 wai6 gwok3 gaa1 hei1 sang1, zan1 hai6 zou6 dou3 jan4 sei2 lau4 ming4, fu2 sei2 lau4 pei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一生为国家牺牲，真是做到了人死留名，虎死留皮。
examples.english_sentence: He sacrificed his life for the country and truly left a lasting name — a man leaves a name when he dies, a tiger leaves its skin.

mandarin_meaning: 像熊一樣的人；指外表魁梧、動作笨拙或性格粗獷的人（口語、俚語用法）
english_meaning: literally 'human bear'; colloquial term for a person who is bear‑like — big, hulking, clumsy, or rough in manner (can be affectionate or mildly pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 「人熊」是粵語俗稱，用來形容某人外表或舉止像熊，通常意指高大、笨拙、粗獷，有時帶親暱或略帶貶義的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term describing someone who is bear‑like in appearance or behavior — typically big, clumsy, or rough. Depending on context it can be affectionate (a gentle giant) or mildly critical.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係人熊，行路成日撞到人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jan4 hung4, haang4 lou6 sing4 jat6 zong6 dou3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他像隻熊，走路總是會撞到人。
examples.english_sentence: He's like a bear — he always bumps into people when he walks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好小看佢，佢其實係個人熊，但心腸好好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 siu2 hon3 keoi5, keoi5 kei4 sat6 hai6 go3 jan4 hung4, daan6 sam1 coeng4 hou2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別小看他，他其實是個外表粗獷但心地很好的人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't underestimate him — he's a big bear of a person, but he's very kind‑hearted.

mandarin_meaning: 熟人不拘礼节／熟人之间不太讲礼貌
english_meaning: Being too familiar without observing proper manners; 'familiarity breeds informality' (negative sense)
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容与人关系熟络，以致不太讲礼貌或不拘小节；有时含批评意味，指因过于亲近而失去礼貌或不顾及场合。
explanation_english: Describes a situation where people are so familiar with each other that they don't observe proper manners or formalities. Often has a critical tone, implying rudeness or lack of consideration due to over-familiarity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋係老鄉，人熟礼唔熟，講嘢好隨便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai6 lou5 hoeng1, jan4 suk6 lei5 m4 suk6, gong2 je5 hou2 ceoi4 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们是老乡，熟人之间不太讲礼貌，说话很随便。
examples.english_sentence: They're from the same hometown; among themselves they're too familiar and not very polite — they speak very casually.

mandarin_meaning: 年纪小却很机灵、老练或狡猾；举止像大人或显得很世故
english_meaning: Literally 'small person, big ghost' — describes someone (often a child) who is unusually clever, shrewd, precocious, or cheekily worldly-wise for their age
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容词性短语（口语/习语）
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容年纪小却很机灵、老练或爱耍小聪明的人。语气可带半开玩笑或轻微贬义，常用于评价小朋友或年轻人行为超出年龄应有的成熟或狡猾。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone—usually a child or young person—who behaves more shrewdly, precociously, or cunningly than their age suggests. The tone can be playful or mildly critical.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢人細鬼大，成日講啲似大人先會講嘅道理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan4 sai3 gwai2 daai6, sing4 jat6 gong2 di1 si6 daai6 jan4 sin1 wui5 gong2 ge3 dou6 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他人小鬼大，总是说些像大人才会说的道理。
examples.english_sentence: He's small but very shrewd; he always talks like an adult.

jyutping: jan4 lou5 zing1, gwai2 lou5 ling4
mandarin_meaning: 形容人年紀大了反而更機靈、狡猾，不容易被騙。
english_meaning: A proverb saying people tend to become more shrewd or crafty with age; older people are harder to fool.
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話俗語，用來形容人年紀大了但經驗豐富、反而更加機靈、會耍手段，難以上當受騙。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying that describes how age and experience often make people more astute or crafty; they become harder to deceive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好以為可以呃到佢，佢人老精，鬼老灵，唔易上當。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 ji5 wai4 ho2 ji5 aak1 dou3 keoi5, keoi5 jan4 lou5 zing1, gwai2 lou5 ling4, m4 ji6 soeng5 dong3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別以為可以騙到他，他人老精、鬼老靈，不容易上當。
examples.english_sentence: Don't think you can fool him — he's old and crafty; people like that are hard to trick.

jyutping: jan4 jiu3 heoi1 sam1, fo2 jiu3 hung1 sam1
mandarin_meaning: 做人要虚心；处事要留有余地（字面为“人要虚心，火要空心”），比喻谦虚待人并为事情保留余地。
english_meaning: Literally 'people should be humble, fire should have an empty center.' A proverb meaning be modest and leave room/space — be humble and keep some reserve or flexibility when handling matters.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用押韻的形式提醒人要謙虛（人要虛心），同時用“火要空心”作比喻，表示做事要留有餘地或有分寸，不要過於剛硬或自滿。出處不一，但屬民間勸誡語句，常用於提醒人處事態度。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb, phrased to rhyme, reminds people to be humble (people should have a modest heart) and uses 'fire should be hollow' as a metaphor to advise leaving room or margin when acting — don’t be rigid or overly self-assured. It's a folk saying used to caution about attitude and approach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯成日同我講：人要虚心，火要空心，唔好自以為係，做事要留一手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 sing4 jat6 tung4 ngo5 gong2: jan4 jiu3 heoi1 sam1, fo2 jiu3 hung1 sam1, m4 hou2 zi6 ji5 wai6 hai6, zou6 si6 jiu3 lau4 jat1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老伯常對我說：人要虛心，火要空心，不要自以為是，做事要留一手。
examples.english_sentence: The old man often tells me: 'People should be humble, and fire should be hollow' — meaning don't be conceited; leave some room when you act.

jyutping: jan4 jiu3 min6, syu6 jiu3 pei4
mandarin_meaning: 人要脸，树要皮（意指要顾及面子／体面）
english_meaning: People need 'face', just as trees need bark — i.e. people care about dignity/keeping face.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用比喻表达：人需要面子、顧及体面，不喜欢当众丢脸或承认错误。
explanation_english: A proverb that uses a metaphor: people need 'face' (dignity) and thus care about appearances and saving face.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢輸咗都唔肯認錯，話人要面，樹要皮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 syu1 zo2 dou1 m4 hang2 jing6 co3, waa6 jan4 jiu3 min6, syu6 jiu3 pei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他输了都不肯认错，说人要脸，树要皮。
examples.english_sentence: He lost but refused to admit his mistake, saying that people need face just like trees need bark.

mandarin_meaning: 跟風附和 / 轉述別人所說的話
english_meaning: to parrot what others say; to repeat or echo others' words (often implying lack of independent thought)
explanation_mandarin: 用來指責某人沒有主見，只是重複或附和別人的說法，亦可指轉述別人的話。常帶有貶義，表示隨波逐流或缺乏獨立思考。
explanation_english: Used to accuse someone of merely repeating what others say or echoing gossip; it can also mean passing along what someone else said. Often has a negative connotation, implying a lack of independent thought.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係人講你又講，自己諗一諗啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 jan4 gong2 nei5 jau6 gong2, zi6 gei2 lam2 jat1 lam2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別只是跟著別人說，自己想一想吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just parrot what others say; think for yourself.

mandarin_meaning: 人間蒸發；消失得無影無蹤（突然完全失去聯絡或下落不明）
english_meaning: to disappear without a trace; to vanish (suddenly stop contacting others or be untraceable)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞短語（口語/成語性用法）
explanation_mandarin: 比喻某人突然完全失去聯絡或行蹤不明，好像從人間蒸發一樣。可用於描述自願隱匿或神秘失蹤。
explanation_english: A figurative expression meaning someone suddenly loses all contact or whereabouts, as if they 'vanished from the world.' It can describe intentional disappearance or mysterious vanishing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢自從上次失蹤之後就人間蒸發，電話都唔接。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi6 cung4 soeng6 ci3 sat1 zung1 zi1 hau6 zau6 jan4 gaan1 zing1 faat3, din6 waa2 dou1 m4 zip3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他自從上次失蹤之後就人間蒸發，電話都不接。
examples.english_sentence: He disappeared without a trace after going missing last time; he doesn't answer calls.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話要人間蒸發，搬去外國重新開始生活。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 jiu3 jan4 gaan1 zing1 faat3, bun1 heoi3 ngoi6 gwok3 cung4 san1 hoi1 ci2 saang1 wut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說要人間蒸發，搬到外國重新開始生活。
examples.english_sentence: He said he wanted to disappear from the world and moved abroad to start life over.

jyutping: jan4 kaau3 ji1 zong1, fat6 kaau3 gam1 zong1
mandarin_meaning: 人靠衣装，佛靠金装（意思是外表和装饰会影响别人对人的看法）
english_meaning: Clothes make the man; appearance and presentation influence how one is perceived.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語強調外表、打扮和包裝會影響別人對一個人的評價，甚至用來形容連佛像也靠華麗的裝飾來顯得莊嚴。
explanation_english: This proverb stresses that appearance, dress, and presentation affect how people are judged. It even metaphorically says that a Buddha statue benefits from gold ornamentation — presentation matters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出席面試要著得專業啲，人靠衣装，佛靠金装。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 zik1 min6 si5 jiu3 zoek3 dak1 zyun1 jip6 di1, jan4 kaau3 ji1 zong1, fat6 kaau3 gam1 zong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 参加面试要穿得专业一点，人靠衣装，佛靠金装。
examples.english_sentence: When attending an interview you should dress more professionally — clothes make the man; presentation matters.

mandarin_meaning: 別人的面子；顧及或給予別人的面子（口語）
english_meaning: someone's 'face' or reputation; to save someone’s face / to show respect by not embarrassing them
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（口語短語，可與「給/畀」組成動詞短語）
explanation_mandarin: 指社會或個人的顏面、體面；在口語中常與「畀/給」連用，表示給予或保全他人的面子，避免讓對方難堪或丟臉。
explanation_english: Refers to a person's social 'face' or reputation. Commonly used colloquially with verbs like 'give' (e.g., 'give someone face') to mean showing respect or avoiding embarrassing someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好重視人面子，唔鍾意喺人面前失禮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 zung6 si6 jan4 min6 zi2, m4 zung1 ji3 hai2 jan4 min6 cin4 sat1 lai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很重視別人的面子，不喜歡在別人面前失禮。
examples.english_sentence: He cares a lot about face; he doesn't like being embarrassed in front of others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好當住大家面前鬧佢，畀佢人面子啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 dong3 zyu6 daai6 gaa1 min6 cin4 nau6 keoi5, bei2 keoi5 jan4 min6 zi2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要當著大家的面罵他，給他些面子吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't scold him in front of everyone — give him some face.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 香港人好重視人面子，唔想丟人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 jan4 hou2 zung6 si6 jan4 min6 zi2, m4 soeng2 diu1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 香港人很重視面子，不想丟臉。
examples.english_sentence: People in Hong Kong care a lot about face; they don't want to lose face.

mandarin_meaning: 今年／今年的時候（口語）
english_meaning: this year / this time of the year (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「今年時」為廣東話口語用法，常用作表示「今年」或「今年的時候」。與「今年」或「今年的時候」意義相近，多見於口語和香港地區用法。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning 'this year' or 'this time of the year.' It is mainly used in spoken Cantonese (especially in Hong Kong) and is roughly interchangeable with '今年' or 'this year.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年時公司冇乜加人工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 si4 gung1 si1 mou5 mat1 gaa1 jan4 gung1
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年公司幾乎沒有加薪。
examples.english_sentence: This year the company hardly gave any pay raises.

jyutping: gam1 jat6 m4 zi1 teng1 jat6 si6
mandarin_meaning: 今天不知道明天的事
english_meaning: Nobody knows what will happen tomorrow; the future is unpredictable; take things one day at a time.
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「今天不知道明天的事」，表示未來不可預料，勸人不要過度擔心或過早作打算，常用於口語中。
explanation_english: Literally 'today doesn't know tomorrow's matters.' It conveys that the future is unpredictable and is used to tell someone not to worry or over-plan for the future; commonly used colloquially.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司啲安排仲未定，今日唔知听日事，唔好太早擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 di1 on1 paai4 zung6 mei6 ding6, gam1 jat6 m4 zi1 teng1 jat6 si6, m4 hou2 taai3 zou2 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司的安排还没定，今天不知道明天的事，不要太早担心。
examples.english_sentence: The company's arrangements aren't finalized yet — you can't know what will happen tomorrow, so don't worry prematurely.

synonyms: 今日有今日，聽日有聽日

jyutping: gam1 si4 m4 tung4 wong5 jat6
mandarin_meaning: 今非昔比 / 与过去大不相同
english_meaning: Times have changed; it's not like the old days
explanation_mandarin: 表示现在与过去有明显差异，常用于感叹事物、人物或时代的变化。
explanation_english: Used to note or lament that the present is markedly different from the past; often said about changes in things, people, or eras.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家嘅香港真係今时唔同往日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 ge3 hoeng1 gong2 zan1 hai6 gam1 si4 m4 tung4 wong5 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在的香港確實與從前大不相同。
examples.english_sentence: Today's Hong Kong really isn't like it used to be.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 以前嗰間茶餐廳成日都好多人，但今时唔同往日，門口而家都冇人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji5 cin4 go2 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 sing4 jat6 dou1 hou2 do1 jan4, daan6 gam1 si4 m4 tung4 wong5 jat6, mun4 hau2 ji4 gaa1 dou1 mou5 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 以前那家茶餐廳常常人很多，但如今已大不如前，門口現在都沒人。
examples.english_sentence: That cha chaan teng used to be packed, but times have changed — now there's no one at the door.

mandarin_meaning: 現在的東西；當代物品
english_meaning: modern things; contemporary items; current stuff
explanation_mandarin: 「今物」一般指現代或時下流行的事物、物品，常用於口語，帶有「現在的東西」之意，偶爾用來與傳統或舊物作對比。
explanation_english: Refers to contemporary or modern items—things of the present time. Commonly used colloquially to mean 'current stuff' or 'modern goods', often contrasted with traditional or old items.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲今物我用唔慣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 gam1 mat6 ngo5 jung6 m4 gwaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些現代東西我用不習慣。
examples.english_sentence: I can't get used to these modern things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係追求今物，要重視傳統文化。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 zeoi1 kau4 gam1 mat6, jiu3 zung6 si6 cyun4 tung2 man4 faa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只追求現代物品，要重視傳統文化。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just pursue modern goods; value traditional culture.

mandarin_meaning: 缠着（人）/黏人，纠缠不放
english_meaning: to cling to someone; to pester or be overly clingy
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語/俚語，形容人（尤指小孩或伴侶）黏著別人、纏著不放、令人覺得煩。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term describing someone (often a child or partner) who clings to or pesters another person persistently; used to call someone 'clingy' or bothersome.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日仔纏住我，真係煩死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zai2 cin4 zyu6 ngo5, zan1 hai6 faan4 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天缠着我，真是烦死了。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps pestering me all the time; it's so annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個女仔好仔纏，成日纏住媽媽唔肯走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 neoi5 zai2 hou2 zai2 cin4, sing4 jat6 cin4 zyu6 maa4 maa1 m4 hang2 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个小女孩很黏人，总是缠着妈妈不肯离开。
examples.english_sentence: The little girl is very clingy; she keeps clinging to her mother and won't let go.

mandarin_meaning: 孩子；儿子；小孩（粤语口语）；也可作小名或轻蔑称呼
english_meaning: child; kid; son; (colloquial) lad, youngster; can be used affectionately or pejoratively
explanation_mandarin: 「仔」在粵語中常用作名詞，指小孩或兒子，也可作親暱稱呼（如「阿仔」）。寫作「仔」或「崽」，後者有時在口語中帶粗俗或貶義。亦可作詞綴表示小或親暱（如「雞仔」），在不同語境中語氣可由親熱到輕蔑。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "仔" (also written "崽") is commonly a noun meaning child, kid, or son. It can be used affectionately (e.g. "阿仔") or pejoratively depending on context. It also appears as a diminutive suffix. The variant "崽" can carry a rougher or insulting tone in some usages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我個仔今日返學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 zai2 gam1 jat6 faan1 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的儿子今天去上学。
examples.english_sentence: My son went to school today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢班仔好嘈，唔好理佢哋啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 baan1 zai2 hou2 cou4, m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5 dei6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些孩子很吵，别理他们了。
examples.english_sentence: These kids are very noisy; don't pay them any attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿仔，食飯啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 zai2 sik6 faan6 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 孩子，吃饭吧！
examples.english_sentence: Kid, eat your meal!

mandarin_meaning: 代代平安（dài dài píng'ān）——祈愿子孙后代世代平安无事。
english_meaning: May generations be safe and peaceful; a blessing wishing peace and safety for successive generations.
explanation_mandarin: 常作为祝福语，表示祈愿家族或后代世代平安，常见于新年祝辞、对联、贺卡和祭祀场合。
explanation_english: A traditional auspicious blessing used to wish that a family or descendants remain safe and peaceful for generations; commonly used in New Year greetings, couplets, cards, and ceremonial contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年到，大家互相祝福，祝你同屋企人代代平安。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 dou3, daai6 gaa1 wu6 soeng1 zuk1 fuk1, zuk1 nei5 tung4 uk1 kei2 jan4 doi6 doi6 ping4 on1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新年到了，大家互相祝福，祝你和家人代代平安。
examples.english_sentence: With the New Year here, everyone exchanges blessings—wishing you and your family peace and safety for generations.

mandarin_meaning: 以为自己很了不起
english_meaning: to think you're so great / as if you're the best (sarcastic)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，帶嘲諷或不屑，用來反駁或譏諷別人自以為很厲害或很重要。
explanation_english: A colloquial, sarcastic Cantonese phrase used to mock or dismiss someone who acts like they're very impressive or important.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你以為你大晒咩？真係唔好咁自滿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji5 wai4 nei5 daai6 saai3 me1? zan1 hai6 m4 hou2 gam2 zi6 mun5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你以为你很了不起吗？真的不要那麼自滿。
examples.english_sentence: Do you think you're so great? Really, don't be so full of yourself.

jyutping: ji5 wai4 wan6 dou3, jyun4 loi4 sam1 zou6
mandarin_meaning: 以为好运来临，结果反而心里烦躁或失望
english_meaning: Thought good luck had arrived, but actually felt restless/anxious or disappointed
explanation_mandarin: 表示原本以为会有好运或好结果，结果事与愿违，反而感到心烦、焦躁或失望。常用于形容期待落空后的失落心情。
explanation_english: Expresses that one expected good luck or a positive outcome, but things turned out differently and one feels restless, anxious, or disappointed. Used to describe the feeling after expectations are dashed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我以為運到，原來心燥，買咗張六合彩以為會中獎，點知冇中。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 wai4 wan6 dou3, jyun4 loi4 sam1 zou6, maai5 zo2 zoeng1 luk6 hap6 coi2 ji5 wai4 wui5 zung1 zoeng2, dim2 zi1 mou5 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我以为走运，结果心里焦躁，我买了张六合彩以为会中奖，没想到没中。
examples.english_sentence: I thought I was lucky, but actually felt restless — I bought a lottery ticket thinking I'd win, but it didn't hit.

synonyms: 以為好運來到，結果失落

mandarin_meaning: 供熟手參考 / 供有經驗者使用
english_meaning: intended for experienced hands; for seasoned practitioners to refer to or use
explanation_mandarin: 書面或口語用語，表示某些資料、指引或工作是給有經驗的人參考或處理，不太適合新手或未經驗者。
explanation_english: A written or spoken expression indicating that certain information, instructions, or tasks are meant for experienced people to reference or handle, and are not suitable for novices.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本維修手冊主要以資熟手參考，新手唔好隨便跟住做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 wai4 sau1 sau2 caak3 zyu2 jiu3 ji5 zi1 suk6 sau2 caam1 haau2, san1 sau2 m4 hou2 ceoi4 bin6 gan1 zyu6 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這本維修手冊主要供熟手參考，新手不要隨便照做。
examples.english_sentence: This maintenance manual is mainly for experienced hands to refer to; novices shouldn't just follow it casually.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲難度高嘅手術通常只以資熟手處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 naan4 dou6 gou1 ge3 sau2 seot6 tung1 soeng4 zi2 ji5 zi1 suk6 sau2 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 難度高的手術通常只由熟手處理。
examples.english_sentence: High-difficulty surgeries are usually handled only by experienced practitioners.

mandarin_meaning: 還說／竟然還說（口語）
english_meaning: still say; even say; (colloquial) expressing surprise, disbelief, or adding emphasis ('and yet you say...')
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 副词/口语用法（表示驚訝或反駁）
partOfSpeech_english: adverbial phrase / colloquial discourse particle (expressing surprise, contradiction or emphasis)
explanation_mandarin: 「仲話」是粵語口語表達，常用於回應或反駁前述話語，帶有驚訝、不相信或強調的語氣，類似普通話的「還說」或「竟然還說」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to respond to or contradict a prior statement, conveying surprise, disbelief, or emphasis. It corresponds to Mandarin '還說' or English 'and yet you say...' / 'still say...'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你已經食咁多，仲話唔餓？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji5 ging1 sik6 gam2 do1, zung6 waa6 m4 ngo6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你已經吃那麼多，還說不餓？
examples.english_sentence: You've already eaten so much — and you still say you're not hungry?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我明明先到，佢仲話我遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ming4 ming4 sin1 dou3, keoi5 zung6 waa6 ngo5 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我明明先到，他還說我遲到。
examples.english_sentence: I clearly arrived first, yet he says I was late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔止遲到，仲話冇帶份工作報告。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zi2 ci4 dou3, zung6 waa6 mou5 daai3 fan6 gung1 zok3 bou3 gou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不只遲到，還說沒帶工作報告。
examples.english_sentence: Not only was he late, he even says he didn't bring the work report.

mandarin_meaning: 仍然/還/更（口語用法，表示仍然、還是、甚至更）
english_meaning: still / yet / even / more (colloquial Cantonese adverb used to indicate continuation, emphasis, or comparison)
explanation_mandarin: 「仲」是粵語常用的副詞（口語），表示動作或狀態的延續（還、仍然）、未發生（仲未）或比較上的程度（仲好過 = 更好）。有時以「重」作同音通用字書寫，但用法與普通話的「還/仍然/更」相似，但多用於口語和香港粵語語境。
explanation_english: “仲” (zung6) is a common Cantonese colloquial adverb meaning 'still' or 'yet', used to indicate continuation (still), non-occurrence (as in '仲未' = not yet), or to add emphasis/comparison ('仲好過' = even better). The character 重 is often used interchangeably in informal writing. It is primarily a spoken Cantonese feature.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你仲未食飯呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zung6 mei6 sik6 faan6 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你還沒吃飯嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Haven't you eaten yet?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家仲喺度，未走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zung6 hai2 dou6, mei6 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在還在這裡，沒走。
examples.english_sentence: He's still here; he hasn't left.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試我考得仲好過上次。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 ngo5 haau2 dak1 zung6 hou2 gwo3 soeng6 ci3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次考試我考得比上次還好。
examples.english_sentence: I did even better on this exam than last time.

mandarin_meaning: 重新估价；再次评估
english_meaning: to re-evaluate; to reassess; to reappraise (an estimate or value)
explanation_mandarin: 指對事物、價值或情況進行再次估計或重新評估，常用於資產估價、風險評估或在情況改變後重新計算預期等場合。在口語中「仲估」或寫作「重估」皆可見。
explanation_english: Refers to estimating or assessing something again — for example revaluating assets, reassessing risks, or recalculating expectations after circumstances change. Colloquially written/pronounced as 仲估 or 重估.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要重估啲物業嘅價值。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 zung6 gu2 di1 mat6 jip6 ge3 gaa3 zik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要重新估算这些物业的价值。
examples.english_sentence: The company needs to re-evaluate the value of the properties.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 市場變咗，我哋要重估投資風險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si5 coeng4 bin3 zo2, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 zung6 gu2 tau4 zi1 fung1 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市场变了，我们要重新评估投资风险。
examples.english_sentence: The market has changed; we need to reassess the investment risks.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）還、再、更加；（作動詞）再增加、增添（可表示程度上的更甚或數量上的再加）
english_meaning: (colloquial) still / even more / additionally; (verb) to add on / add further
explanation_mandarin: 「仲加」為廣東話口語用法，可作程度副詞表示「更加、還要」，亦可作動詞表示「再增加、再添上」。有時用「重加」作通俗寫法，但發音相同。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used either as an adverb meaning 'still / even more / additionally' or as a verb meaning 'to add on / add further'. Sometimes written with the character 重 informally, but pronounced the same.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試比上次難，仲加咗好多題目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 bei2 soeng6 ci3 naan4, zung6 gaa1 zo2 hou2 do1 tai4 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次考试比上次难，而且还加了很多题目。
examples.english_sentence: This exam is harder than the last one, and they even added a lot more questions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部手機本身已經好貴，仲加埋運費之後就更貴啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 sau2 gei1 bun2 san1 ji5 ging1 hou2 gwai3, zung6 gaa1 maai4 wan6 fai3 zi1 hau6 zau6 gang3 gwai3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部手机本来就很贵，加上运费之后更贵了。
examples.english_sentence: This phone was already expensive; after adding the shipping fee it's even pricier.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐廳喺菜單上仲加咗幾款新菜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 teng1 hai2 coi3 daan1 soeng5 zung6 gaa1 zo2 gei2 fun2 san1 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餐厅在菜单上又加了几道新菜。
examples.english_sentence: The restaurant added several new dishes to the menu.

mandarin_meaning: 殡葬工人/验尸官（口語，指處理遺體或驗屍的人）
english_meaning: mortician / coroner (colloquial term for someone who handles corpses or conducts post-mortem examinations)
explanation_mandarin: 「仵作佬」是廣東話口語，通常指處理遺體、辦理殮葬或負責驗屍的人。可指殯儀師、殮房工作人員或在某些語境下指驗屍官/法醫。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 仵作佬 is an informal term referring to a person who handles corpses, undertakes mortuary work, or examines bodies (i.e., morticians, undertakers, or in some contexts coroners/forensic examiners).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我阿叔係仵作佬，成日要處理遺體。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 suk1 hai6 ng5 zok3 lou2, seng4 jat6 jiu3 cyu5 lei5 wai4 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我叔叔是殡葬工作者（仵作），經常要處理遺體。
examples.english_sentence: My uncle is a mortician; he often has to handle corpses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺啲古裝戲入面，仵作佬會負責驗屍搵出死因。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 di1 gu2 zong1 hei3 jap6 min6, ng5 zok3 lou2 wui5 fu6 zaak3 jim6 si1 wan2 ceot1 sei2 jan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在一些古裝劇裡，仵作負責驗屍以找出死因。
examples.english_sentence: In some period dramas, the coroner is responsible for examining bodies to determine the cause of death.

mandarin_meaning: 能夠容忍/承受；允許（口語）
english_meaning: to be able to tolerate/endure; to allow/permit (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「任得」是廣東話口語用法，表示能夠容忍或允許某種行為或情況。常見於問句或否定句，用來詢問或否定是否可以忍受、承受或容許。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to be able to tolerate/endure something or to allow/permit it. Frequently used in questions or negatives to ask or state whether someone can stand or permit a behavior or situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你任得佢咁樣對你咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jam6 dak1 keoi5 gam2 joeng6 deoi3 nei5 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你能容忍他這樣對你嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Can you tolerate him treating you like that?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔任得成日加班，身體會出問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 jam6 dak1 sing4 jat6 gaa1 baan1, san1 tai2 wui5 ceot1 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我受不了天天加班，身體會出問題。
examples.english_sentence: I can't stand working overtime every day; my health will suffer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司唔會任得你成日遲到，遲早會有麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 m4 wui5 jam6 dak1 nei5 sing4 jat6 ci4 dou3, ci4 zou2 wui5 jau5 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司不會容忍你老是遲到，遲早會出事。
examples.english_sentence: The company won't tolerate you being late all the time; you'll get into trouble sooner or later.

mandarin_meaning: 袖手旁观；站在一旁不介入、不帮忙
english_meaning: to stand by; to be a bystander; to watch without intervening or helping
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指在别人遇到事情或需要帮助时，只站在旁边观望而不出手相助或介入。
explanation_english: Colloquial expression meaning to stand on the sidelines and watch when someone needs help or when something happens, without intervening or assisting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到有人打街坊，唔好淨係企人旁，快啲報警或幫手！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou2 jau5 jan4 daa2 gaai1 fong1, m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 kei5 jan4 pong4, faai3 di1 bou3 ging2 waak6 bong1 sau2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到有人打邻居，别只是站在旁边，快点报警或帮忙！
examples.english_sentence: If you see someone assaulting a neighbor, don't just stand by — call the police or help!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢面對困難嗰陣，啲朋友淨係企人旁，冇人出手。
