examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 min6 deoi3 kwan3 naan4 go2 zan6, di1 pang4 jau5 zing6 hai6 kei5 jan4 pong4, mou5 jan4 ceot1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他面对困难时，朋友们只是站在旁边，沒人出手相助。
examples.english_sentence: When he faced difficulties, his friends just stood by; nobody stepped in to help.

jyutping: kei5 hai2 seng4 lau4 tai2 maa5 daa2 gaau1
mandarin_meaning: 站在一旁看热闹（袖手旁观）
english_meaning: to stand by and watch a fight/drama; be a mere spectator
explanation_mandarin: 形容只是站在一旁看別人爭吵或打鬥，不參與也不出手幫忙，帶有看熱鬧或事不關己的意味。
explanation_english: Describes standing by to watch others argue or fight without intervening; being a spectator who enjoys or merely observes the drama.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係企喺城樓睇馬打交，去幫手啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 kei5 hai2 seng4 lau4 tai2 maa5 daa2 gaau1, heoi3 bong1 sau2 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只是站在一旁看热闹，去帮忙吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't just stand by and watch — go help!

mandarin_meaning: （口語）站到一旁/靠边站；也可指在争执中站到一方或不参与
english_meaning: (colloquial) stand to one side / move aside; can also mean take a side in a dispute or stay out of it
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，原意是移到一邊、讓開或靠邊站。常見的正寫為「企埋一邊」（「邊」字，jyutping: bin1）。在社交語境下也可指在衝突或討論中選邊站或置身事外。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to move to the side or get out of the way. The more common written form is 企埋一邊 (邊 = bin1). It can also figuratively mean taking sides in an argument or staying on the sidelines.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好企埋一便擋住路，閃開啲啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 kei5 maai4 jat1 bin6 dong2 zyu6 lou6, saan2 hoi1 di1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要挡在路上，让开一点。
examples.english_sentence: Don't stand in the way — move aside a bit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日企埋一便，見到事就唔幫忙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 kei5 maai4 jat1 bin6, gin3 dou3 si6 zau6 m4 bong1 mong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要总是站在一边，看到事情就不帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always stand on the sidelines and refuse to help when something happens.

mandarin_meaning: 整潔、得體、乾淨（口語）
english_meaning: neat; tidy; well-presented (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「企裏」（亦常寫作「企理」）為香港粵語口語用字，用來形容衣著、儀表或環境整潔、得體、看起來利落。例如形容人穿得整齊或房間收拾得好。
explanation_english: "企裏" (often written as "企理") is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial adjective used to describe someone or something as neat, tidy, or well-presented. It commonly refers to clothing, appearance, or a tidy environment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢著得好企裏，成個人好精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoek3 dak1 hou2 kei5 leoi5, seng4 go3 jan4 hou2 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他穿得很整齊，看起來很有精神。
examples.english_sentence: He dresses very neatly and looks energetic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 辦公室要企裏啲，先可以有效率咁做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baan6 gung1 sat1 jiu3 kei5 leoi5 di1, sin1 ho2 ji5 jau5 haau6 leot6 gam2 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 辦公室要整潔一些，才可以有效率地工作。
examples.english_sentence: The office should be tidier so work can be done more efficiently.

mandarin_meaning: 在櫃台工作／站櫃（尤指化妝品專櫃）
english_meaning: to work at / man a shop counter (especially a cosmetics counter); to stand at a sales counter serving or promoting products
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指在商店的櫃台站崗、招呼顧客並推銷商品，常用於化妝品專櫃的銷售工作。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to stand and work at a shop counter — greeting customers and selling products; commonly used for cosmetics counter sales staff.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家喺銅鑼灣嗰間百貨公司企身櫃，做化妝品銷售員。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 tung4 lo4 waan1 go2 gaan1 baak3 fo3 gung1 si1 kei5 san1 gwai6, zou6 faa3 zong1 ban2 siu1 sau6 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她現在在銅鑼灣那間百貨公司的櫃台工作，做化妝品銷售員。
examples.english_sentence: She's currently working at a cosmetics counter in the department store in Causeway Bay.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做企身櫃幾辛苦，要長時間企住同埋不停推銷產品。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 kei5 san1 gwai6 gei2 san1 fu2, jiu3 coeng4 si4 gaan1 kei5 zyu6 tung4 maai4 bat1 ting4 teoi1 siu1 caan2 ban2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 當櫃台銷售很辛苦，需要長時間站立並且不停推銷產品。
examples.english_sentence: Working at a counter is quite tiring — you have to stand for long periods and continuously promote products.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：站立的琴；可能指直立式樂器（如直立鋼琴）。該詞在粵語中屬罕用或非標準用法。
english_meaning: Literal: a standing/upright instrument; possibly refers to an upright piano. The term is rare or nonstandard in Cantonese.
explanation_mandarin: 由「企」（站立）、「身」（身體）及「琴」（樂器）三字組成，字面可理解為「直立的樂器」。在正規詞典中少見，可能為口語、地方用法或寫法誤用。
explanation_english: Composed literally of 'stand' (企), 'body' (身) and 'instrument' (琴); can be interpreted as an upright/standing musical instrument. It is uncommon in standard Cantonese and may be a regional, colloquial, or erroneous usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間琴行有一把企身琴，係好罕見嘅老式直立鋼琴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 kam4 hong4 jau5 jat1 baa2 kei5 san1 kam4, hai6 hou2 ham5 gin3 ge3 lou5 sik1 zik6 lap6 gong1 kam4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這家琴行有一把企身琴，是很罕見的老式直立鋼琴。
examples.english_sentence: This music shop has a '企身琴' — a very rare old upright piano.

mandarin_meaning: 站（站立）
english_meaning: to stand; to stand up; to stay standing
explanation_mandarin: 「企」是粤语常用动词，表示直立站着。字形「徛」为同义异体字，常在书写或方言文本中出现。可用于描述人或物处于站立状态，或命令/请求别人站好。
explanation_english: “企” is a common Cantonese verb meaning to stand (upright). The character “徛” is a variant form used in writing or dialectal contexts. It describes someone or something being in a standing position or used to tell/request someone to stand.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你企喺門口等我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 kei5 hai2 mun4 hau2 dang2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你站在門口等我。
examples.english_sentence: Stand/wait for me at the door.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友唔好企喺度跑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 m4 hou2 kei5 hai2 dou6 paau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友不要站在那裡跑。
examples.english_sentence: Kids, don't run while standing there.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公車到站，請企穩啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong1 ce1 dou3 zaam6, ceng2 kei5 wan2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公車到站，請站穩一點。
examples.english_sentence: The bus has arrived; please stand steady.

mandarin_meaning: 会弹不会唱 (只会弹奏乐器但不会唱歌)
english_meaning: Can play (an instrument) but can't sing; used to describe someone who is skilled at one part (instrumental) but not at singing
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，字面意思是會彈奏樂器但不會唱歌。常用於形容一個人在某方面有能力，但在另一相關方面欠缺，或具體指只會彈奏、不會唱歌。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning 'can play (an instrument) but can't sing.' Often used to describe someone who is competent in one aspect but lacking in another, or specifically someone who plays an instrument but doesn't sing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢會彈唔會唱，所以我哋請咗另一個做主唱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wui5 daan6 m4 wui5 coeng3, so2 ji5 ngo5 dei6 cing2 zo2 ling6 jat1 go3 zou6 zyu2 coeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他会弹不会唱，所以我们请了别人做主唱。
examples.english_sentence: He can play (an instrument) but can't sing, so we hired someone else to be the lead singer.

mandarin_meaning: 误会、误解别人的意思
english_meaning: to misunderstand someone's meaning; to get the wrong idea
explanation_mandarin: 表示把別人的話或意圖理解錯誤，產生誤會或誤解。
explanation_english: To incorrectly understand someone’s words or intentions, resulting in a misunderstanding or getting the wrong idea.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好會錯意，我唔係反對你，我只係擔心啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 wui5 co3 ji3, ngo5 m4 hai6 faan2 deoi3 nei5, ngo5 zi2 hai6 daam1 sam1 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別會錯意，我不是反對你，我只是擔心而已。
examples.english_sentence: Don't get the wrong idea — I'm not against you, I'm just worried.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好容易會錯意，要講清楚啲先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 jung4 ji6 wui5 co3 ji3, jiu3 gong2 cing1 co2 di1 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很容易會誤解，要說清楚一點才行。
examples.english_sentence: He/She easily gets the wrong idea; you need to explain more clearly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 對唔住，我會錯意咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: deoi3 m4 zyu6, ngo5 wui5 co3 ji3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 對不起，我誤會了。
examples.english_sentence: Sorry, I misunderstood.

mandarin_meaning: 小孩；孩子（方言、爱称）
english_meaning: kid; child (affectionate, dialectal term)
explanation_mandarin: 口语、方言称呼，带亲昵意味，指小孩或幼小的人，常用于地方性或口语语境中作为爱称。
explanation_english: A colloquial, dialectal affectionate term for a child or little one. Used informally to refer to kids with a tone of endearment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個伢伢好得意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 nga4 nga4 hou2 dak1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个小孩很可爱。
examples.english_sentence: This kid is very cute.

mandarin_meaning: （音譯自英語 bomb）炸彈；（俚語）（比喻）徹底失敗、轟然爆裂的聲響
english_meaning: Loanword from English 'bomb': an explosive device; (slang) to fail badly; an onomatopoeic 'boom' sound
explanation_mandarin: 「伯姆」通常是從英文 bomb 音譯而來。在粵語口語或書寫中可用作指炸彈，也可作俚語使用，表示演出或作品慘敗（像英文的 "the movie bombed"），有時也用作擬聲詞表達爆炸、巨響。
explanation_english: “伯姆” is a transliteration of the English word 'bomb'. In Cantonese usage it can refer to an explosive device, be used slangily to mean that something failed badly (as in 'the show bombed'), or serve as an onomatopoeic word for an explosion/boom.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方喺工廈搵到一個可疑嘅伯姆，要封鎖現場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 hai2 gung1 haa6 wan2 dou3 jat1 go3 ho2 ji4 ge3 baak3 mou2, jiu3 fung1 so2 jin6 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方在工廈找到一個可疑的伯姆（炸彈），要封鎖現場。
examples.english_sentence: The police found a suspicious 'bomb' in the industrial building and had to cordon off the scene.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰套電影真係伯姆，入場觀眾好少，評價又差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 tou3 din6 jing2 zan1 hai6 baak3 mou2, jap6 coeng4 gun1 zung3 hou2 siu2, ping4 gaa3 jau6 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那部電影真是『伯姆』（徹底失敗），入場觀眾很少，評價又差。
examples.english_sentence: That movie really bombed — very few people attended and the reviews were poor.

mandarin_meaning: 伯母（父親哥哥的妻子）；對長輩女性的稱呼（粵語、方言用法）
english_meaning: aunt (specifically the wife of one's father's elder brother); a respectful form of address for an older woman (regional Cantonese usage)
explanation_mandarin: 「伯孃」為粵語或南方方言中對父親長兄的妻子的稱呼，相當於普通話的「伯母」。在某些地區也可用作對較年長女性的敬稱，屬於親屬稱謂或口語用語，較有地區色彩，部分情況下可寫作「伯娘」。
explanation_english: “伯孃” is a Cantonese/regional term used to refer to the wife of one's father's elder brother (equivalent to Mandarin '伯母'). It can also be used as a respectful form of address for an older woman. It is a kinship term with regional/colloquial flavor and may appear in variant spellings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我伯孃成日整嘢畀我食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 baak3 noeng4 sing4 jat6 zing2 je5 bei2 ngo5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我伯母经常给我做东西吃。
examples.english_sentence: My aunt (my father's elder brother's wife) often makes things for me to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 猜測、估計
english_meaning: to guess; to estimate (informal/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「估厘」是香港粵語俗語，用來表示對某事作粗略猜測或估計，通常語氣較口語、隨意，沒有確實證據。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term meaning to make a rough guess or estimate. It is informal and implies a tentative, unconfirmed conjecture.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好淨係估厘，問清楚先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 gu2 lei4, man6 cing1 co2 sin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要只是猜測，先問清楚吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just guess — ask and find out first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我都係估厘嚟講，未有實證。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dou1 hai6 gu2 lei4 lai4 gong2, mei6 jau5 sat6 zeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我也只是估計，沒有實證。
examples.english_sentence: I'm only estimating; there's no solid proof.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你估厘下佢幾時返嚟？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gu2 lei4 haa5 keoi5 gei2 si4 faan1 lai4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你猜一下他什麼時候回來？
examples.english_sentence: Take a guess — when will he be back?

mandarin_meaning: 猜想；估计；认为
english_meaning: to guess; to suppose; to reckon
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用法，表示對某事作出猜測或估計，常用於日常對話中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to indicate a guess or supposition about something; commonly used in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我估話佢今日唔返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gu2 waa6 keoi5 gam1 jat6 m4 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我猜他今天不去上班。
examples.english_sentence: I guess he won't go to work today.

mandarin_meaning: （方言）你（第二人称）
english_meaning: you (second-person pronoun, dialectal)
explanation_mandarin: “伲”为方言或古字，部分地区的口语或方言书写中用来表示“你”。在现代标准书面语中较少见，常用于方言色彩的表达或文学作品中。
explanation_english: “伲” is a dialectal/archaic character used in some Chinese dialects (including colloquial Cantonese contexts) to mean 'you'. It is uncommon in modern standard written Chinese and appears mainly in dialectal writing or literary usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 伲食咗飯未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你吃饭了吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you eaten yet?

mandarin_meaning: 伶牙俐齿（líng yá lì chǐ）：口齿灵活、言辞机敏，善于应答或辩说。
english_meaning: Eloquent; quick-witted and glib-tongued — having quick, fluent, and persuasive speech.
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容人口齿伶俐、反应机敏，语言表达流利且善于应对、辩论或社交场合。
explanation_english: Describes someone whose speech is nimble and quick, able to respond deftly; often used for people who are eloquent or good at arguing/communicating.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢伶牙俐齒，喺面試入面答問題特別得體。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ling4 ngaa4 lai6 ci2, hai2 min6 si5 jap6 min6 daap3 man6 tai4 dak6 bit6 dak1 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他伶牙俐齿，在面试中回答问题特别得体。
examples.english_sentence: He is eloquent; he answered questions in the interview particularly well.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面對記者佢表現得伶牙俐齒，應付自如。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 deoi3 gei3 ze2 keoi5 biu2 jin2 dak1 ling4 ngaa4 lai6 ci2, jing3 fu6 zi6 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面对记者他表现得伶牙俐齿，应付自如。
examples.english_sentence: Facing reporters, he was eloquent and handled them with ease.

mandarin_meaning: 看起來像樣；像模像樣
english_meaning: to look proper/presentable; to have the appearance of being competent (sometimes superficially)
explanation_mandarin: 表示外表或行為看起來像樣、有樣子，常用來形容雖然有模有樣但有時只是表面功夫。
explanation_english: Describes something or someone that appears proper or presentable; can imply that the appearance may be superficial or merely for show.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講得好似模似樣，其實都唔識做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 dak1 hou2 ci5 mou4 ci5 joeng6, kei4 sat6 dou1 m4 sik1 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說得很像樣，其實都不會做。
examples.english_sentence: He talks as if he knows what he's doing, but actually he doesn't.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做得有啲似模似樣，但仲有好多位要改善。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 dak1 jau5 di1 ci5 mou4 ci5 joeng6, daan6 zung6 jau5 hou2 do1 wai6 jiu3 goi2 sin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做得有點像樣，但還有很多地方要改進。
examples.english_sentence: What you did looks somewhat proper, but there are still many areas to improve.

mandarin_meaning: 佃丁 (diàndīng)：租種土地或受雇為地主耕作的農民，俗稱佃農或佃戶，常見於舊時社會。
english_meaning: Tenant farmer; hired farmhand or sharecropper (historical rural agricultural worker).
explanation_mandarin: 指在農村中承租土地或受地主雇用從事耕作的農民，多用於描述舊時的農業社會和勞動關係。
explanation_english: Refers to rural workers who rented land or were hired by landlords to cultivate fields. The term is mainly used in historical contexts to describe traditional agricultural labourers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我阿爺以前係個佃丁，一生都喺鄉下耕作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3je4 ji5cin4 hai6 go3 din6 ding1, jat1 saang1 dou1 hai6 hoeng1haa6 gaang1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我爷爷以前是个佃丁，一生都在乡下耕作。
examples.english_sentence: My grandfather used to be a tenant farmer; he farmed in the countryside his whole life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊時啲地主請佃丁嚟幫手種田。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 si4 di1 dei6 zyu2 ceng2 din6 ding1 lai4 bong1 sau2 zung3 tin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 旧时地主请佃丁来帮忙种田。
examples.english_sentence: In old times, landlords hired tenant farmers to help plant the fields.

mandarin_meaning: 佃户的儿子
english_meaning: tenant farmer's son
explanation_mandarin: 原指佃户（承租土地耕作的農戶）的兒子。此詞帶有鄉村、務農背景色彩，現代口語中較少使用，屬較為書面或方言性的稱呼。
explanation_english: Originally refers to the son of a tenant farmer (a family who rents land to farm). The term conveys a rural, agricultural background. It is relatively uncommon in modern spoken usage and is more of an archaic or dialectal designation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係一個佃個仔，成日返屋企幫手喺田度做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jat1 go3 tin3 go3 zai2, sing4 jat6 faan1 uk1 kei2 bong1 sau2 hai2 tin4 dou6 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是一个佃户的儿子，经常回家帮忙干农活。
examples.english_sentence: He is a tenant farmer's son and often goes home to help with farm work.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見、古漢字，現代漢語中無常用讀音或固定含義，偶見於古籍或人名中。
english_meaning: A rare/archaic Chinese character with no common modern pronunciation or fixed meaning; occasionally seen in classical texts or personal names.
explanation_mandarin: 「佄」為罕見的漢字，現代漢語和粵語中並無廣泛使用或約定俗成的讀音與詞義，主要在古籍、刻本或個別人名中出現。
explanation_english: The character '佄' is rare and archaic. It has no widely accepted modern Mandarin or Cantonese pronunciation or meaning and is mainly encountered in classical texts or certain proper names.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「佄」好少見，通常只喺古文或者人名度見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 '佄' hou2 siu2 gin3, tung1 soeng4 zi2 hai2 gu2 man4 waak6 ze2 jan4 ming4 dou6 gin3 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字“佄”很少见，通常只在古文或者人名中出现。
examples.english_sentence: The character '佄' is rarely seen; it's usually only found in classical texts or personal names.

mandarin_meaning: 罕用或已失用的漢字（現代粵語中幾乎未見使用）
english_meaning: A very rare or obsolete Chinese character (hardly attested in modern Cantonese)
partOfSpeech_english: rare/obsolete character (no clear part of speech)
explanation_mandarin: 「佊」為漢字中極為罕見或已失用的字，現代粵語與白話文中幾乎沒有使用紀錄，更多出現於字典或古籍的字目中。
explanation_english: The character '佊' is extremely rare or obsolete. It has little to no attestation in modern Cantonese or everyday written Chinese, and is mainly encountered in dictionaries or classical texts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「佊」好少見，喺現代廣東話入面差唔多用唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 (佊) hou2 siu2 gin3, hai2 jin6 doi6 gwong2 dung1 waa2 jap6 min6 caa1 m4 do1 jung6 m4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字“佊”很少见，在现代粤语里差不多用不到。
examples.english_sentence: This character '佊' is rarely seen and is almost never used in modern Cantonese.

mandarin_meaning: 小時候；從小
english_meaning: since childhood; when (one was) young
explanation_mandarin: 「低細」是廣東話口語，表示從小的時候、年幼時期，常作時間副詞使用，相當於普通話的「小時候/從小」。
explanation_english: “低細” is a Cantonese colloquial expression meaning 'since childhood' or 'when (one) was young.' It functions as a temporal adverb and is equivalent to Mandarin '小時候' or '從小'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我低細就鍾意踢波。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dai1 sai3 zau6 zung1 ji3 tek3 bo1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小時候就喜歡踢足球。
examples.english_sentence: I liked playing football since I was young.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢低細就識得幫人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dai1 sai3 zau6 sik1 dak1 bong1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她從小就會幫助別人。
examples.english_sentence: He/She has helped others since childhood.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我低細係香港長大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dai1 sai3 hai6 hoeng1 gong2 coeng4 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小時候在香港長大。
examples.english_sentence: I grew up in Hong Kong.

mandarin_meaning: 坐月 / 做月子（產後坐月的期間或在坐月中心居住休養）
english_meaning: postpartum confinement; to stay (often at a confinement centre or at home) for the traditional month of postpartum recuperation
explanation_mandarin: 「住月」指產婦在生產後的一段傳統休養期內（通常約一個月）接受調養與照顧。用法上強調在特定場所居住休養，例如在坐月中心或回家由長輩照顧。與「坐月」意思相近，但「住月」更強調「住」在某處接受照顧。
explanation_english: “住月” refers to the traditional postpartum confinement period (typically about one month) when a new mother rests and receives care and special dietary treatment. The term emphasizes staying (住) at a particular place for recuperation — for example, at a confinement centre or at home with family help. It is similar to “坐月” but stresses residence for the confinement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱生完寶寶，依家喺坐月中心住月。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 saang1 jyun4 bou2 bou2, ji1 gaa1 hai6 co5 jyut6 zung1 sam1 zyu6 jyut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她剛生完寶寶，現在在坐月中心坐月（住月）。
examples.english_sentence: She just had a baby and is now staying at a confinement centre for her postpartum month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打算返屋企由媽媽幫手住月，唔去坐月中心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 syun3 faan1 uk1 kei2 jau4 maa4 maa1 bong1 sau2 zyu6 jyut6, m4 heoi3 co5 jyut6 zung1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她打算回家由媽媽幫忙坐月，不去坐月中心。
examples.english_sentence: She plans to do her confinement at home with her mother's help instead of going to a confinement centre.

mandarin_meaning: 月嫂；坐月子期間照顧產婦和嬰兒的護理人員
english_meaning: confinement nanny (a maternity helper who cares for the mother and baby during the postpartum confinement period)
explanation_mandarin: 指在坐月子期間負責照顧產婦和嬰兒、準備坐月餐並提供護理與生活協助的女性工作者，類似「月嫂」。
explanation_english: A woman who provides care for the mother and newborn during the postpartum confinement period — preparing confinement meals, assisting with baby care and breastfeeding, and offering postpartum nursing and household help. Equivalent to 'yue sao' or 'confinement nanny'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我請咗個住月婆幫手，佢好識整坐月餐同照顧嬰兒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ceng2 zo2 go3 zyu6 jyut6 po4 bong1 sau2, keoi5 hou2 sik1 zing2 zou6 jyut6 caan1 tung4 ziu3 gu3 jing1 ji4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我请了一个住月婆帮忙，她很会做坐月子餐并照顾婴儿。
examples.english_sentence: I hired a confinement nanny to help; she is good at making confinement meals and taking care of the baby.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 好多家庭會喺媽媽臨盆之前開始搵住月婆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hou2 do1 gaa1 ting4 wui5 hai2 maa4 maa1 lam4 pun4 zi1 cin4 hoi1 ci2 wan2 zyu6 jyut6 po4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 很多家庭会在孕妇临产前开始找住月婆。
examples.english_sentence: Many families start looking for a confinement nanny before the mother goes into labor.

mandarin_meaning: 拖手拖脚（拖拉、磨蹭）
english_meaning: to dawdle; to drag one's feet; to loaf around
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，形容做事拖拉、慢吞吞或閒着不做事、磨蹭。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to dawdle, procrastinate, or stand around doing nothing — to be slow or dilatory in action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度佗手㨢腳，快啲做啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 to1 sau2 to1 goek3, faai3 di1 zou6 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在這裡拖手拖脚，快點做吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't just stand around dawdling — hurry up and do it!

cantonese: 佛争一炷香，人争一口气
jyutping: fat6 zang1 jat1 zyu3 hoeng1, jan4 zang1 jat1 hau2 hei3
mandarin_meaning: 佛争一炷香，人争一口气（人們為了面子、尊嚴或一點小利而爭執，即使是微不足道的事情也要較勁）
english_meaning: Literally: 'Buddhas vie for an incense stick, people vie for a mouthful of qi.' Figuratively: people often fight over pride or small matters; petty competitiveness and concern for face/dignity.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來形容人為了面子、尊嚴或一點小利而爭執、較勁，常用以批評為瑣碎之事爭鬥的行為。
explanation_english: This proverb describes people who argue or compete over face, dignity, or trivial gains. It criticizes petty disputes where pride causes people to fight over insignificant things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司啲小事都要計較，好似佛爭一炷香，人爭一口氣咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 di1 siu2 si6 dou1 jiu3 gai3 gaau3, hou2 ci5 fat6 zang1 jat1 zyu3 hoeng1, jan4 zang1 jat1 hau2 hei3 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司裡的小事都要計較，真是佛争一炷香、人争一口气。
examples.english_sentence: People at the company argue even over trivial matters — it's a case of 'Buddhas quarrel over an incense, people quarrel over a bit of pride.'

mandarin_meaning: 佛手（柑）/佛手橼（柑類的一種，學名Citrus medica var. sarcodactylis）
english_meaning: Buddha's hand citron (a fragrant citrus fruit with finger-like segments)
explanation_mandarin: 一種柑橘類果實，外形常呈指狀分裂（故稱「佛手」），可作調味、入藥、做香料或製成蜜餞與果醬，亦具觀賞價值。
explanation_english: A type of citrus fruit (Buddha's hand citron) often with finger-like lobes. Used for fragrance, culinary flavoring, traditional medicine, candied fruit, and ornamental purposes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市見到新鮮嘅佛手橼，好想買返嚟做蜜餞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 gin3 dou3 san1 sin1 ge3 fo2 sau2 jyun4, hou2 soeng2 maai5 faan1 lai4 zou6 mat6 zin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在菜市場看到新鮮的佛手橼，很想買回來做蜜餞。
examples.english_sentence: I saw fresh Buddha's hand citron at the market and really wanted to buy it to make candied fruit.

mandarin_meaning: 佛肚竹（fó dǔ zhú）：一种观赏竹，学名常指 Bambusa ventricosa，茎节膨大似肚，常作为盆栽或景观植物。
english_meaning: Buddha belly bamboo (Bambusa ventricosa): an ornamental bamboo species with swollen internodes resembling a belly, often grown as potted plants or decorative bonsai.
explanation_mandarin: 佛肚竹为热带、亚热带常见的观赏竹类，茎节呈膨大状，因形似佛像的肚部而得名。常用于盆栽、庭院或景观美化，喜温暖湿润及充足光照并需适度修剪管理。
explanation_english: Buddha belly bamboo is an ornamental bamboo native to tropical/subtropical regions. Its swollen culms give it a belly-like appearance, hence the name. It is commonly used as a potted plant or landscape specimen; it prefers warm, humid conditions and moderate light with occasional pruning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市嗰邊有檔賣佛肚竹，啲盆栽好受歡迎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 go2 bin1 jau5 dong3 maai6 fat6tou5zuk1, di1 pun4 zoi1 hou2 sau6 fun1 jing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在街市那边有摊子卖佛肚竹，这些盆栽很受欢迎。
examples.english_sentence: There's a stall at the market selling Buddha belly bamboo; those potted plants are very popular.

mandarin_meaning: 胡鬧；裝瘋賣傻；故意惹事
english_meaning: to act up; to mess around; to behave foolishly or provocatively
explanation_mandarin: 「作七」是香港粵語俚語，指無理取鬧、裝傻或故意鬧事、作態，引起別人注意或惹人不快的行為。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term meaning to act foolishly, make a scene, or deliberately cause trouble or annoyance. Often used to tell someone to stop messing around or being dramatic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺度作七啦，我哋真係要正經啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 zok3 cat1 laa1, ngo5 dei6 zan1 hai6 jiu3 zeng3 ging1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要在這裡胡鬧了，我們真的要正經一點。
examples.english_sentence: Don't act up here; we really need to be more serious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一飲醉就開始作七，成晚搞到大家都唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 jam2 zeoi3 zau6 hoi1 ci2 zok3 cat1, sing4 maan5 gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一喝醉就開始胡鬧，整晚讓大家都不高興。
examples.english_sentence: He starts acting up when he's drunk, making everyone unhappy all night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好作七啦，快啲返工啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zok3 cat1 laa1, faai3 di1 faan1 gung1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別鬧了，快點去上班吧。
examples.english_sentence: Stop messing around; hurry back to work.

jyutping: zok3 ji1 aap3 goek3 bui3, jat1 geoi2 loeng5 dak1
mandarin_meaning: 一舉兩得（做一件事同時得到兩種好處）
english_meaning: To achieve two gains with one action; to kill two birds with one stone.
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東俗語式的表達，字面上把兩個動作並列（作揖與𢯎腳背），用來形容做一件事同時得到兩個好處或完成兩個目的。語氣上帶有幽默或口語色彩，常用來形容「一舉兩得」。
explanation_english: A humorous Cantonese expression that juxtaposes two actions (a polite bow and the odd action of scratching/kicking the back of the foot) to mean accomplishing two beneficial outcomes at once. It’s colloquial and used like “kill two birds with one stone.”

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話可以幫我寄件，又可以賺返啲里數，真係作揖𢯎脚背，一舉兩得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 gei3 gin6, jau6 ho2 ji5 zaan6 faan1 di1 lei5 sou3, zan1 hai6 zok3 ji1 aap3 goek3 bui3, jat1 geoi2 loeng5 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說可以幫我寄東西，又可以賺回一些里數，真是作揖𢯎脚背，一舉兩得。
examples.english_sentence: He said he could help send my package and also earn some reward miles — really killing two birds with one stone.

mandarin_meaning: 你最近好吗？/你过得怎么样？
english_meaning: How have you been? / How are you doing (lately)?
explanation_mandarin: 这是粤语中的口语问候，用来打招呼并询问对方近况。其中“幾/几”在此相当于普通话的“最近/怎么样”，等同于“你最近好吗？”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial greeting used to ask about someone's recent wellbeing. The word 幾 (gei2) here functions like “recently/how” and the phrase is equivalent to “How have you been?” or “How are you doing lately?”

examples.cantonese_sentence: 好耐冇見，你幾好嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3, nei5 gei2 hou2 maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 好久不见，你最近好吗？
examples.english_sentence: Long time no see — how have you been?

cantonese: 你唔嫌我箩疏，我唔嫌你米碎‍
jyutping: nei5 m4 jim4 ngo5 lo4 so1, ngo5 m4 jim4 nei5 mai5 seoi3
mandarin_meaning: 你不介意我囉嗦（或有缺点），我也不介意你小气（或有缺点）。
english_meaning: If you don't mind my flaws (e.g. being nagging), I won't mind yours (e.g. being stingy).
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用於形容雙方互相包容彼此缺點，常見於口語或半開玩笑的語境，用以強調為了相處而互相忍讓。
explanation_english: A colloquial saying that expresses mutual tolerance of each other's flaws—used jokingly or sincerely to indicate that people put up with one another's faults to get along.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋相處就係咁，你唔嫌我箩疏，我唔嫌你米碎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 soeng1 cyu3 zau6 hai6 gam2, nei5 m4 jim4 ngo5 lo4 so1, ngo5 m4 jim4 nei5 mai5 seoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们相处就是这样，你不介意我啰嗦，我也不介意你小气。
examples.english_sentence: That's how we get along: if you don't mind my nagging, I won't mind your stinginess.

mandarin_meaning: 你们 (nǐmen)
english_meaning: you (plural)
explanation_mandarin: 在粤语中用于表示第二人称复数，相当于普通话的“你们”。口语常写作“你哋”，在简体或非正式书写中有时写作“你地”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese second-person plural pronoun equivalent to Mandarin '你们' (nǐmen). Commonly written as '你哋' in Cantonese orthography; '你地' is also used informally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你地今日去邊度？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 gam1 jat6 heoi3 bin1 dou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你们今天去哪里？
examples.english_sentence: Where are you (all) going today?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你地要飲咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 jiu3 jam2 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你们要喝什么？
examples.english_sentence: What do you (all) want to drink?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事會唔會影響到你地？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 wui5 m4 wui5 jing2 hoeng2 dou3 nei5 dei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事会不会影响到你们？
examples.english_sentence: Will this matter affect you (all)?

cantonese: 你有你乾坤，我有我日月
jyutping: nei5 jau5 nei5 gon1 kwan1, ngo5 jau5 ngo5 jat6 jyut6
mandarin_meaning: 你有你的乾坤，我有我的日月（各有各的天地；各有各的生活或看法）
english_meaning: To each their own; each person has their own domain/ways/perspective
explanation_mandarin: 表示每個人有自己的一片天地、生活方式或觀念，互不干涉或各自堅持意見。常用於表達各自不同而不打算改變對方的態度。
explanation_english: Expresses that everyone has their own realm, lifestyle, or viewpoint; often used to mean 'to each their own' or that both sides stick to their positions without interfering.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺嗰件事上好難達成共識，算啦，你有你乾坤，我有我日月。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 go2 gin6 si6 seong6 hou2 naan4 daat6 sing4 gung6 sik1, syun3 laa1, nei5 jau5 nei5 gon1 kwan1, ngo5 jau5 ngo5 jat6 jyut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在那件事上很難達成共識，算了，你有你的乾坤，我有我的日月。
examples.english_sentence: We couldn't reach an agreement on that matter — never mind, to each their own.

cantonese: 你有關門計，我有過牆梯
jyutping: nei5 jau5 gwaan1 mun4 gai3, ngo5 jau5 gwo3 coeng4 tai1
mandarin_meaning: 你有你的办法/计策，我也有对策；对方设防，我也有应对或绕过的方法。
english_meaning: For every trick or barrier you set up, I have a way to get around it; I have countermeasures or alternative means.
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話俗語，用來表示對方每出一招，自己也有應對的辦法或替代方案，不會輕易被限制或阻擋。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying meaning that for every move someone makes to block or limit you, you have a countermeasure or a way around it — you won't be easily stopped.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司想封死我哋嘅渠道，你有關門計，我有過牆梯，總之唔會畀人阻住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 soeng2 fung1 sei2 ngo5 dei6 ge3 ceoi4 dou6, nei5 jau5 gwaan1 mun4 gai3, ngo5 jau5 gwo3 coeng4 tai1, zung2 zi1 m4 wui5 bei2 jan4 zo2 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司想封死我們的渠道，你有關門計，我有過牆梯，總之不會被人阻止。
examples.english_sentence: The company wants to shut down our channels, but for every trick you have, I have a way around it — we won't be stopped.

jyutping: nei5 nam2 nei5, m4 hou2 nam2 gwo3 gaak3 lei4
mandarin_meaning: 别自作多情／别想得太远（别自作主张、别太过分地幻想或自以为是）
english_meaning: Don't get ahead of yourself / Don't be presumptuous (stop daydreaming or assuming you'll get something you won't)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语用语，带有责备或揶揄意味，用来警告或嘲讽对方不要自以为是、不要想太多或妄自期待别人的东西。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression, often used mockingly or admonishingly to tell someone not to be presumptuous, not to daydream, or not to expect something beyond their reach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你以为自己会拣到佢？你谂你，唔好谂过隔篱啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji5 wai6 zi6 gei2 wui5 gaan2 dou3 keoi5? nei5 nam2 nei5, m4 hou2 nam2 gwo3 gaak3 lei4 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你以为你会被选中？别自作多情，别想得太远了！
examples.english_sentence: You think you'll be chosen? Don't get ahead of yourself — don't be presumptuous!

mandarin_meaning: 他们 / 她们 / 它们 (tāmen)
english_meaning: they / them
explanation_mandarin: 「佢地」是廣東話口語中表示第三人稱複數的代詞，等同普通話的「他們/她們/它們」。書寫上常見正字為「佢哋」，但很多口語或非正式文字會用「地」作替代。
explanation_english: 「佢地」 is the Cantonese plural third-person pronoun equivalent to Mandarin 'tāmen' and English 'they/them'. The standard written form is usually 佢哋, but 地 is commonly used informally in writing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢地今日唔返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gam1 jat6 m4 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们今天不用上班。
examples.english_sentence: They aren't working today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你見唔見到佢地？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gin3 m4 gin3 dou2 keoi5 dei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有没有看到他们？
examples.english_sentence: Did you see them?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢地話會遲啲先到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 waa6 wui5 ci4 di1 sin1 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们说会晚一点才到。
examples.english_sentence: They said they'll arrive a bit later.

mandarin_meaning: 動作遲緩、慢吞吞（口語、方言）
english_meaning: slow-moving; sluggish (colloquial/dialectal)
explanation_mandarin: 「佮佮𠶧」為粵語口語詞，形容人或事物動作緩慢、沒有精神或反應遲鈍。常用作形容人做事慢吞吞或拖拖拉拉。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone or something that moves slowly or is sluggish. Often used to describe a person who is slow in action or procrastinates.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做嘢唔好咁佮佮𠶧，快啲做完啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 je5 m4 hou2 gam2 gaak3 gaak3 ngaap6, faai3 di1 zou6 jyun4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做事不要那麼慢吞吞，快點做完吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so sluggish doing your work — finish it quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見漢字，常作姓氏，也可視為「而」的異體字
english_meaning: rare/archaic character; used as a surname; variant of the character "而"
explanation_mandarin: 「佴」為罕見字，現代漢語中較少使用，常見於人名或古籍資料中。有時被視為「而」的異體字或用作姓氏。
explanation_english: The character 佴 is rare in modern usage. It appears mainly in personal names or classical texts and is sometimes treated as a variant of the character "而". It is also used as a surname.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佴係我阿媽嘅姓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 hai6 ngo5 aa3 maa1 ge3 sing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 佴是我媽媽的姓。
examples.english_sentence: The surname 佴 is my mother's surname.

mandarin_meaning: （文言）使、讓；古文中的語助或使役結構，現代粵語很少單獨使用
english_meaning: A literary/classical Chinese expression meaning 'to make/let' (causative); a classical usage rarely used in modern Cantonese
explanation_mandarin: 「使也」多見於文言文，為「使」(使役、使得) 加上語氣或判斷色彩的「也」，用來表示使喚、令或作句末判斷。現代廣東話口語中罕見，通常只在古文或書面語參考時出現。
explanation_english: “使也” appears in classical/literary Chinese as a combination of the causative verb '使' (to make/let) with the particle '也'. It conveys a causative or emphatic sense in classical texts. It is rarely used in everyday Cantonese and mainly encountered in literary or historical contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢句「使也」係文言用法，現代廣東話好少用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 geoi3 'sai2 jaa5' hai6 man4 jin4 jung6 faat3, jin6 doi6 gwong2 dung1 waa2 hou2 siu2 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個「使也」是文言用法，現代粵語很少使用。
examples.english_sentence: The term '使也' is a literary usage; modern Cantonese rarely uses it.

mandarin_meaning: 耍横；仗势欺人；摆架子
english_meaning: to bully or act domineering; to use strong-arm tactics
explanation_mandarin: 指用強勢或威脅的手段欺壓、擺架子或仗勢欺人，使別人屈服或讓步。
explanation_english: Refers to using forceful or intimidating tactics to bully, intimidate, or act arrogantly so that others yield or make concessions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺公司入面，佢成日使横手，大家都唔敢反對。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gung1 si1 jap6 min6, keoi5 seng4 jat6 sai2 waang4 sau2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 gam2 faan2 deoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在公司里面，他经常耍横，大家都不敢反对。
examples.english_sentence: At the company, he often bullies others; nobody dares to oppose him.

jyutping: si2 ngau4 jiu3 sik1 ngau4 san1 fu2
mandarin_meaning: 用牛要爱惜牛（因為牠辛苦）；引申為對為你辛勞的人要體諒和珍惜
english_meaning: If you make the ox work, you should take care of it — i.e. appreciate and treat those who work for you with care; don't overwork or mistreat hardworking people.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語俗語，字面意思是「使喚牛的時候要愛惜牠，因為牠很辛苦」，引申為提醒人們要體諒、珍惜為自己付出或辛勞的人，不要只利用或剝削他們。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally meaning 'if you use an ox, you should cherish the ox because it is hardworking.' Figuratively it reminds people to sympathize with and appreciate those who work hard for you, rather than merely using or exploiting them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意要靠員工，你唔好淨係搵佢哋出力，記住使牛要惜牛辛苦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 kaau3 jyun4 gung1, nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 wan2 keoi5 dei6 ceot1 lik6, gei3 zyu6 si2 ngau4 jiu3 sik1 ngau4 san1 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意要靠員工，你不要只讓他們出力，記住：使牛要惜牛辛苦（要珍惜為你辛勞的人）。
examples.english_sentence: Running a business depends on employees — don't just use their labor; remember 'if you make the ox work, take care of it' — appreciate those who work hard for you.

jyutping: si2 tung4 ngan4 gaap3 daai6 seng1
mandarin_meaning: 炫耀钱财；卖弄财富、摆阔
english_meaning: to flaunt one's money; to show off wealth ostentatiously
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，意思是在别人面前夸耀或炫耀自己的金钱，故意高调消费或摆阔以吸引注意。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to flaunt money or show off wealth through conspicuous spending or ostentatious displays to attract attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺街度使銅銀夾大聲，買名牌袋出嚟俾人睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai6 gaai1 dou6 si2 tung4 ngan4 gaap3 daai6 seng1, maai5 ming4 paai4 doi6 ceot1 lei4 bei2 jan4 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是在街上炫耀钱财，买名牌包给人看。
examples.english_sentence: He's always flaunting his money on the street, buying designer bags to show off to people.

mandarin_meaning: 工頭；領班
english_meaning: foreman; supervisor; person in charge of a crew
explanation_mandarin: 「使頭」為粵語口語，指負責指揮或分配工作的領班或工頭，有時帶有口語或輕微貶義，常用於工地或臨時工作團隊中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for a foreman or the person who directs and assigns tasks to a crew. Often used in contexts like construction sites or work teams and can carry an informal or slightly dismissive tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 工地嗰個使頭好嚴格。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 dei6 go2 go3 si2 tau4 hou2 jim4 gaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個工地的工頭很嚴格。
examples.english_sentence: The foreman at the construction site is very strict.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你係唔係嗰班人嘅使頭？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai6 m4 hai6 go2 baan1 jan4 ge3 si2 tau4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你是不是那班人的工頭？
examples.english_sentence: Are you the foreman of that crew?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好同佢頂嘴，佢係使頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 tung4 keoi5 ding2 zeoi2, keoi5 hai6 si2 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別跟他頂嘴，他是工頭。
examples.english_sentence: Don't talk back to him; he's the boss/foreman.

mandarin_meaning: 侄媳妇（侄子的妻子）
english_meaning: nephew's wife
explanation_mandarin: 表示親屬關係，指「侄子」的妻子。此寫法帶有方言或舊式用法色彩，現代普通話通常說「侄媳婦」或「侄媳」。
explanation_english: Refers to a familial relationship: the wife of one's nephew. This spelling/term has a dialectal or old-fashioned feel; modern Mandarin/Cantonese commonly use "侄媳婦" / "侄媳".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我個侄抱婦，叫阿珍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 go3 zat6 bou3 fu5, giu3 aa3 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她是我侄子的妻子，叫阿珍。
examples.english_sentence: She is my nephew's wife; her name is Ah Jan.

mandarin_meaning: 按時/在適當的時候
english_meaning: at the proper time; in due course; on time
explanation_mandarin: 表示在適當或約定的時間發生或做某事，強調按時或在合適時機進行。
explanation_english: Indicates doing something at the appropriate or appointed time; emphasizes punctuality or acting in due course.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要依時依候嚟上堂，唔好遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 ji1 si4 ji1 hau6 lai4 soeng5 tong4, m4 hou2 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要按时来上课，不要迟到。
examples.english_sentence: You should come to class on time; don't be late.

mandarin_meaning: 保安（保全人員）
english_meaning: security guard (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語稱呼，指在商場、屋苑、公司等處負責保安、巡邏或維持秩序的職員。語氣較口語化，有時帶輕微貶義或親暱色彩，正式說法為「保安員」或「保安人員」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for a security guard — someone employed to provide security, patrol, or maintain order at places like malls, residential estates, or companies. It's informal and can be slightly dismissive or familiar; the more formal terms are "security guard" or "security personnel."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰位保安仔好好人，見到我唔識路就幫我指路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 wai6 bou2 on1 zai2 hou2 hou2 jan4, gin3 dou3 ngo5 m4 sik1 lou6 zau6 bong1 ngo5 zi2 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那位保安人員很熱心，看到我不認識路就幫我指路。
examples.english_sentence: The security guard was very nice — he helped direct me when I didn't know the way.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企附近有班夜晚巡邏嘅保安仔，令我覺得安心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei5 fu6 gan6 jau5 baan1 je6 maan5 seon4 lo4 ge3 bou2 on1 zai2, ling6 ngo5 gok3 dak1 on1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我家附近有夜間巡邏的保安人員，讓我覺得安心。
examples.english_sentence: There are security guards patrolling near my home at night, which makes me feel safe.

mandarin_meaning: 信用卡
english_meaning: credit card
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，為「信用咭／信用卡」的簡稱，常用於香港，當中的「咭」是粵語對「卡」的寫法。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese abbreviation for "信用咭/信用卡" (credit card). Commonly used in Hong Kong; 咭 is the Cantonese form for "card."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我冇帶信咭，點付錢呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mou5 daai3 seon3 kaat1, dim2 fu6 cin2 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我沒有帶信用卡，怎麼付錢啊？
examples.english_sentence: I didn't bring my credit card — how should I pay?

mandarin_meaning: 輕信；容易相信別人，容易受騙
english_meaning: gullible; easily believing others; easily duped
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，形容一個人容易相信別人或輕易上當受騙。屬於俚語/口語用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term describing someone who readily believes others or is easily tricked/taken advantage of.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁信皮，俾佢呃咗都唔知？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 seon3 pei4, bei2 keoi5 ngok6 zo2 dou1 m4 zi1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這麼容易相信，給他騙了都不知道？
examples.english_sentence: You're so gullible — you don't even realize when he tricks you?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好信皮，成日俾人利用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 seon3 pei4, seng4 jat6 bei2 jan4 lei6 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的很容易相信人，經常被別人利用。
examples.english_sentence: He's really gullible and often gets used by others.

mandarin_meaning: 著手；開始著手做某事
english_meaning: to set about; to begin taking action
explanation_mandarin: 書面或古漢語用詞，表示開始動手去做某事、著手辦理。
explanation_english: A literary/classical expression meaning to begin to take action or set about doing something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 事情咁緊急，我哋要即刻俶手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si6 cing4 gam2 gan2 gap1, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 zik1 hak1 cuk1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 事情這麼緊急，我們要立刻著手。
examples.english_sentence: The matter is so urgent, we must start right away.

mandarin_meaning: 竟然/出乎意料地這麼早
english_meaning: surprisingly so early; unexpectedly early
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示某事發生得比預期要早，帶有驚訝或意外的語氣。此寫法中的「䍇」可能是書寫變體或誤寫，常見口語形式為「倒咁早」或「倒係咁早」。
explanation_english: Used to express surprise that something happens earlier than expected. The character '䍇' here may be a variant or a typo; the common spoken form is '倒咁早' (dou3 gam2 zou2).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 倒䍇咁早就收工？
examples.jyutping_sentence: dou3 gam2 zou2 zau6 sau1 gung1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 竟然這麼早就下班？
examples.english_sentence: You're getting off work so early already?

mandarin_meaning: 倒（出）便便；清理便盆/貓砂盆等的糞便（口語、粗俗）
english_meaning: to empty out feces; to remove poop from a chamber pot, litter box, etc. (colloquial, vulgar)
explanation_mandarin: 「倒屎」在粵語中主要是指把便便倒出或清理便盆、貓砂盆等的排泄物，語氣較口語甚至粗俗。日常多用於家務或照顧寵物時的情境，不是正式用語。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "倒屎" primarily means to empty or remove feces (for example from a chamber pot or litter box). It is colloquial and can be vulgar. Commonly used in household or pet-care contexts rather than formal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚要幫阿媽倒屎盆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 bong1 aa3 maa1 dou3 si2 pun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我要幫媽媽倒便盆裡的屎。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight I need to empty the chamber pot for my mother.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 要清理貓砂盆，記得要先倒屎再換貓砂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jiu3 cing1 lei5 maau1 saa1 pun4, gei3 dak1 jiu3 sin1 dou3 si2 zoi3 wun6 maau1 saa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 要清理貓砂盆，記得要先把便便倒出來再換貓砂。
examples.english_sentence: When cleaning the cat litter box, remember to empty the poop first before changing the litter.

mandarin_meaning: 這麼早 / 這麼早起 / 太早了（帶不滿或驚訝）
english_meaning: so early / ridiculously early (often expressing annoyance or surprise)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俚語，帶有粗俗色彩，用來形容某人、某事出現或開始得非常早，常帶有不滿、驚訝或抱怨的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase (somewhat coarse) used to say someone or something is extremely early — often conveys annoyance, surprise, or complaint.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你倒屎咁早打嚟做咩呀？我仲未起身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dou3 si2 gam2 zou2 daa2 lai4 zou6 me1 aa3? ngo5 zung6 mei6 hei2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這麼早打電話來做什麼？我還沒起床。
examples.english_sentence: Why are you calling so early? I haven't gotten up yet.

mandarin_meaning: 搬弄是非的女人；愛說人壞話、挑撥離間的女子
english_meaning: a woman who stirs up trouble/gossips and badmouths others; a troublemaking busybody (derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，帶貶義，通常指喜歡搬弄是非、說別人壞話或挑撥離間的女人。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang (derogatory). Refers to a woman who stirs up trouble, gossips, badmouths others, or intentionally creates conflict.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好理佢，佢就係個倒屎婆，鍾意講人壞話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5, keoi5 zau6 hai6 go3 dou3 si2 po4, zung1 ji3 gong2 jan4 waai6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別理她，她就是個搬弄是非的女人，喜歡說別人壞話。
examples.english_sentence: Don't bother with her — she's a troublemaking woman who likes to badmouth others.

mandarin_meaning: 倒霉；遇到厄運、不順利的事
english_meaning: to have bad luck; to encounter misfortune or a run of unlucky events
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，表示某人遭遇不順、倒楣或接二連三發生不好的事情，常用來形容一日中連續碰到壞事。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to be unlucky or experience a streak of misfortunes—used to describe events going wrong repeatedly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日真係倒竈，朝早搭巴士遲到，返到公司又停電。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 dou2 zou6, ziu1 zou2 daap3 baa1 si2 ci4 dou3, faan1 dou3 gung1 si1 jau6 ting4 din6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天真是倒霉，早上搭公車遲到，回到公司又停電。
examples.english_sentence: I'm really unlucky today—I was late on the bus this morning, and when I got to the office the power was out.

mandarin_meaning: 不詳（罕見或方言用字，資料不足）
english_meaning: Unknown/rare term (insufficient data)
explanation_mandarin: 條目中的字「𠶲」為罕見字或非常用字。在現有公開字典與語料庫中找不到可靠的讀音與確切釋義。此詞可能為地區性俚語、俗寫、字形替代或輸入錯誤。若能提供上下文或替代正字，才能進一步確認用法與意思。
explanation_english: The character "𠶲" in this entry appears to be a rare or nonstandard character. Reliable pronunciation and precise meaning cannot be found in available dictionaries or corpora. This item may be a regional slang, a colloquial spelling, a typographical variant, or an input error. Providing context or a normalized spelling would allow for further verification.

mandarin_meaning: 镇定、冷静、泰然自若
english_meaning: calm, composed, unperturbed
explanation_mandarin: 表示在面對突發或壓力情況下不慌張、保持冷靜和從容。
explanation_english: Describes being unflustered and composed when facing pressure or unexpected situations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢遇到咩事都咁淡定，真係好令人佩服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jyu6 dou3 me1 si6 dou1 gam2 daam6 ding6, zan1 hai6 hou2 ling6 jan4 pui3 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他遇到什么事都那么淡定，真的很令人佩服。
examples.english_sentence: He stays so calm no matter what happens; it's really admirable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試前佢都好淡定，一啲都唔緊張。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 cin4 keoi5 dou1 hou2 daam6 ding6, jat1 di1 dou1 m4 gan2 zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考试前他很淡定，一点都不紧张。
examples.english_sentence: He was very calm before the exam, not nervous at all.

mandarin_meaning: 倔強、固執（不容易讓步或不輕易接受他人意見）
english_meaning: stubborn; headstrong; obstinate (unwilling to yield or accept others' opinions)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，形容一個人很倔強、固執，常常堅持己見、不願讓步或聽從別人意見。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone who is very stubborn or headstrong — they stick to their own views and are unwilling to yield or listen to others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好倔头路，成日都唔聽人嘅意見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 gwat6 tau4 lou6, sing4 jat6 dou1 m4 teng1 jan4 ge3 ji3 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是很倔強，總是不聽別人的意見。
examples.english_sentence: He is really stubborn; he never listens to other people's opinions.

mandarin_meaning: 倔强的人；固执、不肯妥协的人（口语/俚语）
english_meaning: A very stubborn person; someone obstinate and unwilling to yield (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個非常固執、不易妥協或改變主意的人，帶有口語或俚語色彩，多見於廣東話語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term for someone extremely stubborn and unwilling to compromise or change their mind.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好倔尾龍，做咩都唔肯改。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 gwat6 mei5 lung4, zou6 me1 dou1 m4 hang2 goi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個倔強的人，做什麼都不肯改變。
examples.english_sentence: He's really stubborn; he refuses to change no matter what.

jyutping: kyut3 mei5 lung4 baai3 saan1, gaau2 fung1 gaau2 jyu5
mandarin_meaning: 爱惹事、搅局、制造麻烦的人或行为（粤语俗语）
english_meaning: Someone who stirs up trouble or makes a scene; to meddle and cause disturbances (Cantonese slang/idiom).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 片語（俗語/俚語，動詞/描述性短語）
explanation_mandarin: 這句粤語俗語用來形容喜歡惹事、挑撥或在場合中製造紛擾、搗亂的人或行為。字面上是形容『倔尾龍』（愛出風頭或愛扯後腿的人）去『拜山』（到處活動或出現），然後『搅风搅雨』（攪局、製造事端）。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial phrase describes someone who likes to cause trouble, meddle, or create disturbances — literally saying the troublemaking figure goes about 'worshipping the mountain' and 'stirring wind and rain.' It refers to a person who makes a scene or stirs things up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺公司度做倔尾龙拜山，搅风搅雨，搞到大家都唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gung1 si1 dou6 zou6 kyut3 mei5 lung4 baai3 saan1, gaau2 fung1 gaau2 jyu5, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常在公司惹是生非、搅局，弄得大家都不开心。
examples.english_sentence: He is always stirring up trouble at the office, making a scene and making everyone unhappy.

mandarin_meaning: 倔强、固执（口语）
english_meaning: stubborn; obstinate (slang, colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俗語，形容一個人非常倔強、固執，不易妥協或改變主意。有時可作貶義或半開玩笑地說。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term describing someone very stubborn or obstinate, unwilling to compromise or change their mind. Can be used pejoratively or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好倔籠，根本唔聽人講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 kyut3 lung4, gan1 bun2 m4 teng1 jan4 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很倔强，根本不听别人的话。
examples.english_sentence: He's very stubborn; he doesn't listen to others at all.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再同佢爭辯，佢太倔籠，改唔到主意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 tung4 keoi5 zang1 bin6, keoi5 taai3 kyut3 lung4, goi2 m4 dou3 zyu2 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再跟他争辩，他太倔强，改不了主意。
examples.english_sentence: Don't argue with him anymore; he's too stubborn and won't change his mind.

mandarin_meaning: 固执；倔强
english_meaning: stubborn; obstinate; headstrong
explanation_mandarin: 形容人性格执拗、不容易妥协或改变主意，常坚持己见。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is unwilling to change their mind or yield; persistent in their own opinion or behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好倔，唔肯認錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 gwat6, m4 hang2 jing6 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很倔，不肯认错。
examples.english_sentence: He's very stubborn and won't admit he's wrong.

mandarin_meaning: 凭什么 / 为什么（带有质疑或不满语气）
english_meaning: Why/What for (used to question or challenge someone's reason, often with incredulity or displeasure)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俚语，字面为“借什么”，常用来质疑对方的理由、权利或行为，有时带不满或讽刺的语气。括号内的“歪”可指“歪理”或加强语气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression literally meaning "borrow what." It is used to challenge or question someone's reason, right, or action, often with incredulous, annoyed, or sarcastic tone. The optional "歪" can allude to "twisted/reasoning" (歪理) or simply strengthen the tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你借乜鬧我呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ze3 mat1 nau6 ngo5 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你凭什么骂我？
examples.english_sentence: What right do you have to scold me?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢借乜唔聽我哋嘅意見？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ze3 mat1 m4 teng1 ngo5 dei6 ge3 ji3 gin3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他凭什么不听我们的意见？
examples.english_sentence: Why won't he listen to our opinion?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你借乜要咁做？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ze3 mat1 jiu3 gam2 zou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你凭什么要这样做？
examples.english_sentence: Why on earth would you do that?

mandarin_meaning: 找藉口；借故
english_meaning: to find an excuse; to use a pretext
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語，表示用各種藉口或理由推脫、逃避責任或佔便利。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to make excuses or use a pretext to avoid responsibility or to gain an advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日借頭借路唔做自己份內嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ze3 tau4 ze3 lou6 m4 zou6 zi6 gei2 fan6 noi6 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天找藉口不做自己分內的事。
examples.english_sentence: He always finds excuses to avoid doing his own tasks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日借頭借路，做實啲你份工啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 ze3 tau4 ze3 lou6, zou6 sat6 di1 nei5 fan6 gung1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別總是找藉口，踏實做你的工作吧。
examples.english_sentence: Stop making excuses and do your job properly.

mandarin_meaning: 歪借（不正當/不誠實地借用或占用別人東西）
english_meaning: to 'borrow' something in a crooked/unscrupulous way (take or use someone else's things without proper permission or intention to return)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俚語，指以不正當或不誠實的方式借用、占用別人東西或資源，常帶責備或調侃意味，可能指偷拿、拖延還錢或借而不還。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to borrow or take something in a crooked or improper way—e.g., taking someone else's belongings without proper permission, failing to return borrowed items, or borrowing with no intention to repay. Often used critically or jokingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再借歪啲人嘅嘢嚟用，遲啲要還㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 ze3 waai1 di1 jan4 ge3 je5 lai4 jung6, ci4 di1 jiu3 waan4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要歪借別人的東西來用，遲早要還的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't 'borrow' other people's stuff crookedly — you'll have to return it sooner or later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢上次借歪啲錢，直到人追佢先還。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng6 ci3 ze3 waai1 di1 cin2, zik6 dou3 jan4 zeoi1 keoi5 sin1 waan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他上次歪借了錢，直到別人催他才還。
examples.english_sentence: Last time he 'borrowed' money in a crooked way; he only paid it back after people chased him.

mandarin_meaning: （文言）衰弱、臥病或跛行，形容行動不便或無力。
english_meaning: Literary term describing debilitation or lameness — prostrate, feeble, or having great difficulty moving.
explanation_mandarin: 偃蹇為文言詞，常用以形容人因年老或疾病而衰弱無力、臥病不起或行動蹣跚、跛行，現代較少用於口語，多見於古文或書面表達。
explanation_english: A classical/literary expression used to describe someone who is debilitated — bedridden, feeble, or lame and having difficulty moving. It is rare in everyday speech and mostly appears in literary or historical texts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢位老伯因病長期偃蹇，行動非常困難。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wai2 lou5 baak3 jan1 beng6 coeng4 kei4 jin2 gin2, hang4 dung6 fei1 soeng4 kwan3 naan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这位老伯因病长期偃蹇，行动非常困难。
examples.english_sentence: This elderly man has been debilitated by illness for a long time and has great difficulty moving.

mandarin_meaning: 假裝是香港人的人；偽裝成香港人的行為或狀態
english_meaning: a fake Hongkonger; someone who pretends to be from Hong Kong or imitates Hong Kong identity/behavior
explanation_mandarin: 帶貶義的俚語，用來形容那些並非真正香港人，卻假裝或模仿香港口音、習慣、文化的人或行為。
explanation_english: A derogatory slang term for people who are not genuinely from Hong Kong but pretend to be — by imitating accent, mannerisms, or claiming a Hong Kong identity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢根本係內地嚟，淨係扮本地人，真係假港。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gan1 bun2 hai6 noi6 dei6 lai4, zing6 hai6 baan6 bun2 dei6 jan4, zan1 hai6 gaa2 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他根本是內地來的，只是假扮本地人，真是假香港人。
examples.english_sentence: He's actually from the mainland; he's just pretending to be local — a fake Hongkonger.

mandarin_meaning: 偽裝成混凝土外觀的建築（或比喻外表看似堅固但實際品質差或脆弱）
english_meaning: a building that looks like concrete/solid but is fake (or metaphorically, something/someone that appears sturdy on the outside but is poor quality or weak inside)
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱，用來形容外觀看似由混凝土構成、很堅固的建築，但實際上只是裝飾或劣質材料；也常用作比喻，指外表強硬或堅固但內在脆弱或徒有其表的人或事物。
explanation_english: Colloquial/slang term for a building that appears to be made of concrete and solid but is actually decorative or built with poor materials; also used metaphorically for people or things that look tough on the outside but are weak or insubstantial inside.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢幢樓望落好似好堅固，其實係假石屎樓，牆係裝飾板嚟嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zong6 lau4 mong6 lok6 hou2 ci5 hou2 gin1 gu3, kei4 sat6 hai6 gaa2 sek6 si2 lau4, coeng4 hai6 zong1 sik1 baan2 lai4 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這棟樓看起來很堅固，實際上是假的混凝土樓，牆是裝飾板做的。
examples.english_sentence: This building looks very sturdy but is actually a fake-concrete building; the walls are decorative panels.

mandarin_meaning: 出丑；丢脸；出洋相
english_meaning: to make a fool of oneself; to embarrass oneself; to act in a way that causes ridicule or loss of face
explanation_mandarin: 指做出令自己難堪或顯得可笑的行為，讓自己在別人面前出醜或丟臉。
explanation_english: Refers to behaving in a way that makes oneself look ridiculous or embarrassed in front of others; to cause oneself to lose face or be laughed at.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺人面前做丑人，準備好先講啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 jan4 min6 cin4 zou6 cau2 jan4, zeon2 bei6 hou2 sin1 gong2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要在人前出丑，先准备好再说吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't embarrass yourself in front of others; prepare first before speaking.

jyutping: zou6 dou3 ci2 gun1 hang4 ci2 lai5
mandarin_meaning: 既然做了這個官，就要有官樣、按規矩行事（有時含諷刺作官後擺架子之意）
english_meaning: Now that one holds the office, one should behave according to the dignity and rules of that position (sometimes used sarcastically about putting on airs after gaining office).
explanation_mandarin: 這句話字面意思是「既然做到了這個官位，就要按該職位的禮儀和規矩行事」。常用來提醒或批評某人在擔任職務後應該有相應的態度和行為；有時帶有諷刺，指人因做了官而擺架子。
explanation_english: Literally, "having reached this official position, act accordingly." It reminds or criticizes someone that, having taken a post, they must behave with the corresponding dignity and follow its norms. It can be used neutrally or sarcastically to point out someone putting on airs after getting a position.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家做市長，做到此官行此礼，講嘢都要有分寸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zou6 si5 zoeng2, zou6 dou3 ci2 gun1 hang4 ci2 lai5, gong2 je5 dou1 jiu3 jau5 fan6 cyun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在做了市長，既然當了這個官就要有官樣，說話也要有分寸。
examples.english_sentence: Now that he's the mayor, having been in that office he should act the part and be measured in his speech.

mandarin_meaning: 做手脚；篡改、作弊或暗中操弄
english_meaning: to tamper with, rig, fiddle with, or cheat (e.g., manipulate results or processes)
explanation_mandarin: 表示暗中篡改、作弊或偷偷操縱某事，使結果改變或不公正，常用於描述賽事、票箱、數據等被人作假或操控。
explanation_english: Means secretly tampering with, manipulating, or rigging something (such as results, ballots, or data) to change the outcome or make it unfair; commonly used for contests, votes, records, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰場比賽好似有人做咗手腳，結果好唔公平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 coeng4 bei2 coi3 hou2 ci5 jau5 jan4 zou6 zo2 sau2 goek3, git3 gwo2 hou2 m4 gung1 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那場比賽好像有人做手腳，結果很不公平。
examples.english_sentence: It looks like someone tampered with that competition; the outcome was very unfair.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方懷疑有人喺投票箱做咗手腳，已經開始調查。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 waai4 ji4 jau5 jan4 hai2 tau4 piu3 soeng1 zou6 zo2 sau2 goek3, ji5 ging1 hoi1 ci2 diu6 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方懷疑有人在投票箱做手腳，已經開始調查。
examples.english_sentence: The police suspect someone tampered with the ballot box and have begun an investigation.

mandarin_meaning: 製造場面/大做文章；故意出鋒頭或表演給人看（相當於「做戲」）
english_meaning: to make a big scene; to put on a show; to stage a spectacle—deliberately dramatize or perform to attract attention
explanation_mandarin: 指故意誇張或製造場面、表演性地吸引他人注意，常帶有作秀或不真誠的意味。
explanation_english: Refers to deliberately creating a dramatic scene or spectacle—acting exaggeratedly or theatrically to draw attention, often implying showiness or insincerity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日為咗啲小事就做大戲，大家都唔想理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 wai6 zo2 di1 siu2 si6 zau6 zou6 daai6 hei3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 soeng2 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常為小事大做文章，大家都不想理他。
examples.english_sentence: He always makes a big scene over small things; nobody wants to pay attention to him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺度做大戲，專心做嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 zou6 daai6 hei3, zyun1 sam1 zou6 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在這裡鬧場，專心做事吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make a scene here; focus on your work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲政客成日喺記者會度做大戲，討好選民。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 zing3 haak3 seng4 jat6 hai2 gei3 ze2 wui6 dou6 zou6 daai6 hei3, tou2 hou2 syun2 man4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些政客在記者會上經常做戲討好選民。
examples.english_sentence: Some politicians often stage shows at press conferences to win voters' favor.

mandarin_meaning: 做好人（做个好人）；在粤语中常指表现得善良、乐于助人，有时含被利用或过于迁就的贬义
english_meaning: to be a good person; to act like the good guy — often used to mean being overly nice or a pushover who gets taken advantage of
explanation_mandarin: “做好人”字面上是“做个好人”。在粤语口语中既可指真心做好事、待人友善，也常带有负面含义，指过分迁就别人、好心却被利用、不懂拒绝的行为或态度。
explanation_english: Literally 'be a good person.' In Cantonese it can simply mean doing good or being kind, but in Hong Kong usage it often implies being overly accommodating or a 'nice guy' who gets taken advantage of.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日話要做好人，點解次次都俾人利用？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4jat6 waa6 jiu3 zou6 hou2 jan4, dim2gaai2 ci3 ci3 dou1 bei2 jan4 lei6jung6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是說要做好人，為什麼每次都被人利用？
examples.english_sentence: He always says he wants to be a good person — why does he get used every time?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係做好人，要學識講唔，唔好俾人利用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6hai6 zou6 hou2 jan4, jiu3 hok6 sik1 gong2 m4, m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 lei6jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只顧做好人，要學會說不，不要被人利用。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just try to be a good person — learn to say no so you won't be taken advantage of.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話佢唔係做好人，佢只係想幫下手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 keoi5 m4 hai6 zou6 hou2 jan4, keoi5 zi2hai6 soeng2 bong1 haa6 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說他不是在做好人，他只是想幫忙一下。
examples.english_sentence: He says he's not trying to play the good guy — he just wants to help a little.

mandarin_meaning: 不顾丢脸与否，勇敢去做／管它好坏
english_meaning: to do something regardless of whether it makes you look good or foolish; don't care about embarrassment—just go for it
explanation_mandarin: 俗语，用来劝人不要顾及面子或外表是否好看，勇敢去做某事，即便可能会出丑。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression encouraging someone to act without worrying about looking silly or losing face—do it whether it turns out well or poorly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好諗太多，今晚你上台就做好做丑啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 nam2 taai3 do1, gam1 maan5 nei5 soeng5 toi4 zau6 zou6 hou2 zou6 cau2 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別想太多，今晚你上台就做好做丑吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't overthink it—just go onstage tonight and do it even if you might look silly!

mandarin_meaning: 做家庭傭工／從事家務工作
english_meaning: to work as a domestic helper / to do domestic work in someone else's home
explanation_mandarin: 「做家庭工」常用於香港粵語，指受僱到別人家裡從事家務或擔任家庭傭工（例如外籍家庭傭工）。也可廣義指做家務工作。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, "做家庭工" means to be employed as a domestic helper or to perform household chores in someone else's home (often referring to foreign domestic helpers). It can also more generally mean doing domestic work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家係做家庭工，朝早要五點起身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hai6 zou6 gaa1 ting4 gung1, ziu1 zou2 jiu3 ng5 dim2 hei2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她現在在做家庭傭工，早上要五點起床。
examples.english_sentence: She currently works as a domestic helper and has to get up at 5 a.m.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做家庭工嘅工資通常係按月發放。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 gaa1 ting4 gung1 ge3 gung1 zi1 tung1 soeng4 hai6 on3 jyut6 faat3 fong3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做家庭傭工的工資通常按月發放。
examples.english_sentence: Wages for domestic helpers are usually paid monthly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你想唔想去外國做家庭工？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 soeng2 m4 soeng2 heoi3 ngoi6 gwok3 zou6 gaa1 ting4 gung1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你想不想去外國當家庭傭工？
examples.english_sentence: Do you want to go abroad to work as a domestic helper?

mandarin_meaning: 當聊天室/房間的管理員或主持人
english_meaning: to act as the host/admin/moderator of a chatroom or online room
explanation_mandarin: 口語／網絡用語，指在聊天室或群組中擔任管理員或主持人，負責監督、管理成員與處理糾紛或投訴。
explanation_english: A colloquial/online term meaning to serve as the host/admin/moderator of a chatroom or online room, responsible for monitoring the room, managing members, and handling disputes or complaints.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我做廳長，你可唔可以幫手睇下廳？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 zou6 ting1 zoeng2, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 sau2 tai2 haa5 ting1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我當聊天室的管理員，你可以幫忙看一下嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I'm the chatroom host tonight; can you help watch the room?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做廳長要處理投訴同管理成員，唔係得閒玩嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 ting1 zoeng2 jiu3 cyu2 lei5 tau4 sou3 tung4 gun2 lei5 sing4 jyun4, m4 hai6 dak1 haan4 waan2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 當聊天室管理員要處理投訴和管理成員，不是閒來玩的。
examples.english_sentence: Being the chatroom host involves handling complaints and managing members; it's not just a casual pastime.

jyutping: zou6 gwaan3 hat1 ji4 laan5 zou6 gwaan1
mandarin_meaning: 習慣了乞討或依賴的生活，不願意當官或承擔職責
english_meaning: Used to being a beggar/dependent, unwilling to become an official or take on responsibility; resistant to moving up or taking on duties
explanation_mandarin: 形容人習慣於低依賴、沒有責任感或不肯擔當，遇到需要負責或提升時就不願意接受或改變。
explanation_english: Describes someone accustomed to a dependent or low-status way of life who is unwilling to accept an official role or responsibility; reluctant to take on duties or rise to a higher position.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做慣乞兒，懶做官，有嘢要負責就唔肯做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 gwaan3 hat1 ji4 , laan5 zou6 gwaan1 , jau5 je5 jiu3 fu6 zaak3 zau6 m4 hang2 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他習慣了乞討/依賴的生活，不願意當官，有事情要負責就不肯做。
examples.english_sentence: He's used to a dependent life and won't take on official duties; whenever there's something to be responsible for, he refuses to do it.

mandarin_meaning: 裝傻／裝作不知道、裝作不理會
english_meaning: to play dumb; to feign ignorance or indifference
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，指故意裝作不知道或不回應，表示不配合或假裝無動於衷。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to pretend not to know, act dumb, or feign indifference/refusal to cooperate.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆叫佢做多啲嘢，佢就做木唔理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 giu3 keoi5 zou6 do1 di1 je5, keoi5 zau6 zou6 muk6 m4 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板叫他做更多的事，他就裝傻不理會。
examples.english_sentence: The boss asked him to do more work, but he played dumb and ignored it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方問佢有冇見到，佢一直做木頭，似乎唔知情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 man6 keoi5 jau5 mou5 gin3 dou3, keoi5 jat1 zik6 zou6 muk6 tau4, ci5 fu4 m4 zi1 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方問他有沒有看到，他一直裝作不知道，似乎不知情。
examples.english_sentence: When the police asked him if he had seen anything, he kept playing dumb, as if he didn't know.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做木，快啲幫手啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 muk6, faai3 di1 bong1 sau2 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別裝傻，快點幫忙啦！
examples.english_sentence: Don't pretend not to know — hurry up and help!

mandarin_meaning: 當門面、出資作開頭或代持（作為代表或掩護）
english_meaning: to front; to act as the frontman or provide initial capital; to be the nominal representative or cover (often for a deal or scheme)
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，'做頭'為俚語，通常指為一項生意或安排充當門面、出資做開頭或代持，有時亦用來形容為非法或灰色交易作掩護的前台（即 '做人頭'）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, '做頭' usually means to act as the front (frontman), to provide initial capital or to hold nominally for someone else. It can also mean serving as a cover for illicit or gray transactions—essentially 'to front' or 'to be the front person'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意要有人肯做頭先至可以開始。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3 jiu3 jau5 jan4 hang2 zou6 tau4 sin1 zi3 ho2 ji5 hoi1 ci2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這筆生意需要有人肯做頭，才能開始。
examples.english_sentence: This business deal needs someone willing to front it before it can start.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔肯做頭，因為驚到時要負責。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 hang2 zou6 tau4, jan1 wai6 geng1 dou3 si4 jiu3 fu6 zak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不肯做頭，因為害怕到時要負責。
examples.english_sentence: He won't act as the frontman because he's afraid he'll be held responsible later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有人搵佢做頭，叫佢做人頭收錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 jan4 wan2 keoi5 zou6 tau4, giu3 keoi5 zou6 jan4 tau4 sau1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人找他做頭，叫他做人頭收錢。
examples.english_sentence: Someone asked him to be the frontman to collect the money (to act as a front).

mandarin_meaning: 偶然之间；碰巧、意外地
english_meaning: by chance; accidentally; unexpectedly
explanation_mandarin: 表示事情是偶然發生的，含有意外或巧合的意思，常用作副詞性短語，說明發生方式或狀況並非計劃中。
explanation_english: Indicates that something happened by chance, implying an unexpected or coincidental occurrence. Used as an adverbial phrase to describe the manner or circumstance of an event.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺街市偶然之間遇到佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 gaai1 si5 ngau5 jin4 zi1 gaan1 jyu6 dou3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在街市偶然遇到他。
examples.english_sentence: We happened to meet him at the market.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事係偶然之間發生嘅，唔係預咗嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 hai6 ngau5 jin4 zi1 gaan1 faat3 sang1 ge3, m4 hai6 jyu6 zo2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事是偶然發生的，不是預先計畫的。
examples.english_sentence: This happened by chance; it wasn't planned in advance.

mandarin_meaning: （可能為非標準用法或誤寫）可能指「偷懶」或「偷閒」，也可按字面理解為「偷偷被雨淋／偷偷淋濕」
english_meaning: Not a standard Cantonese term; likely a misspelling/variant of 'to slack off' (偷懶) or 'to take a brief rest' (偷閒). Literally it could mean 'to be/get wet secretly'.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語動詞 / 俚語（非標準）
explanation_mandarin: 「偷淋」並非常見或標準的廣東話詞彙。多數情況下可能是把「偷懶」或「偷閒」寫錯或口語化的變體，用來表示偷偷放鬆、不用心工作；按字面也可理解為偷偷被雨淋濕。此詞使用罕見，屬非正規用法。
explanation_english: “偷淋” is not a common or standard Cantonese word. It is likely a misspelling or colloquial variant of '偷懶' (to slack off) or '偷閒' (to steal a moment's rest). Colloquially it may be used to mean secretly slacking off; literally it could mean 'to get wet secretly'. Usage is rare and nonstandard.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日唔想做嘢，偷淋咗一陣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 m4 soeng2 zou6 je5, tau1 lam4 zo2 jat1 zan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天不想做事，偷懶了一會兒。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't feel like working today; I slacked off for a while.

mandarin_meaning: 溜走；摆脱（责任、约会或纠缠）；逃避
english_meaning: to sneak away; to ditch someone; to shirk or avoid (responsibility, an appointment, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 「偷甩」是廣東話口語，常用於形容偷偷溜走、放人鴿子或擺脫責任、約會等情況，帶有輕蔑或不負責任的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese informal/slang verb meaning to sneak away, bail on someone, or shirk/avoid responsibilities or commitments. Often implies irresponsibility or rudeness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿明成日偷甩唔做家務。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 ming4 sing4 jat6 tau1 lat1 m4 zou6 gaa1 mou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿明总是溜掉不做家务。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Ming always shirks doing the housework.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢約咗人出嚟，但最後偷甩咗佢，冇嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 joek3 zo2 jan4 ceot1 lei4, daan6 zeoi3 hau6 tau1 lat1 zo2 keoi5, mou5 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他约了人出来，但最后放了对方鸽子，没来。
examples.english_sentence: He arranged to meet someone but bailed at the last minute and didn't show up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺公司入面佢偷甩咗啲責任，搞到其他人要收拾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gung1 si1 jap6 min6 keoi5 tau1 lat1 zo2 di1 zak6 jam6, gaau2 dou3 kei4 taa1 jan4 jiu3 sau1 sap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在公司里他甩掉了一些责任，导致其他人要收拾残局。
examples.english_sentence: At work he shirked some responsibilities, causing others to have to clean up the mess.

mandarin_meaning: 偷偷變瘦；悄悄減肥
english_meaning: to secretly lose weight; to slim down quietly
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俗語，指在別人不注意或不公開的情況下變瘦或悄悄減肥。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to lose weight quietly or without others noticing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近偷瘦咗，好似有啲病咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 tau1 sau3 zo2, hou2 ci5 jau5 di1 beng6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她最近悄悄瘦了，好像有點生病似的。
examples.english_sentence: They've secretly lost weight recently; they look a bit ill.

mandarin_meaning: 偷看；偷瞄（偷偷看別人）
english_meaning: to sneak a peek; to take a furtive glance
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，形容偷偷看別人或東西，常用於偷望異性或對某人/事物有興趣但不敢公開看時。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term meaning to secretly look at someone or something—often used for furtive glances at an attractive person or when peeking without wanting to be noticed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度偷眼屎啦，直接同佢講啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 tau1 ngaan5 si2 laa1, zik6 zip3 tung4 keoi5 gong2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在那裡偷看了，直接跟他／她說吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't sneak a peek—just go and talk to them directly.

mandarin_meaning: 可能是“偷懒”或“偷闲”的錯寫／網路用語，意指悄悄地偷時間休息或偷懒
english_meaning: Likely a nonstandard/misspelled slang of 'to slack off' or 'to steal a moment of rest'; to quietly take time off or be lazy
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞（非正式／俚語或錯寫）
explanation_mandarin: 「偷霖」並非標準粵語詞彙，較常見的是「偷懶」或「偷閒」。在網路或口語環境中，有時有人用「偷霖」作為玩笑或錯寫，用來表達偷偷休息、偷懶或抽空歇息的意思。使用時注意這非正規寫法，正式場合應用「偷懶／偷閒」。
explanation_english: “偷霖” is not a standard Cantonese word. It appears as a nonstandard/typo/slang variant of “偷懶” (to slack off) or “偷閒” (to steal a bit of free time). Online or colloquial speakers may use it playfully to mean quietly taking a break or being lazy. It is informal and not recommended in formal writing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺公司偷霖，叫老細都睇唔出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 gung1 si1 tau1 lam4, giu3 lou5 sai3 dou1 tai2 m4 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在公司偷霖（可能指偷懶／偷閒），老闆也看不出來。
examples.english_sentence: He always 'tau lam' at the office (likely meaning slacks off/takes secret breaks); the boss can't tell.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日放假唔想做嘢，要偷霖一下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 fong3 gaa3 m4 soeng2 zou6 je5, jiu3 tau1 lam4 jat1 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天放假不想做事，要偷霖一下（偷個懶/偷個閒）。
examples.english_sentence: It's a day off and I don't want to work—I want to 'tau lam' for a bit (take it easy).

mandarin_meaning: 可以玩玩，不要太認真 / 享受曖昧但不要招致麻煩或責任
english_meaning: Have a fling but don't get involved in serious consequences; enjoy casual flirting but avoid causing trouble or commitment
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容只想享受短暫的曖昧或刺激，不想發展成嚴重或要負責任的關係，提醒或自述不要惹來麻煩。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to describe enjoying a brief fling or casual flirtation without wanting it to become serious or cause trouble; it warns against getting involved deeply.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你如果淨係想偷風莫偷雨，就唔好畀人誤會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jyu4 gwo2 zing6 hai6 soeng2 tau1 fung1 mok6 tau1 jyu5, zau6 m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 ng6 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你只是想玩玩，就不要讓人誤會。
examples.english_sentence: If you only want a fling, don't let others misunderstand.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司內部有傳聞佢偷風莫偷雨，結果影響咗大家嘅信任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 noi6 bou6 jau5 cyun4 man4 keoi5 tau1 fung1 mok6 tau1 jyu5, git3 gwo2 jing2 hoeng2 zo2 daai6 gaa1 ge3 seon3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司內部傳出他有偷情的傳聞，結果影響了大家的信任。
examples.english_sentence: There were rumors in the company that he was having affairs, and it ended up affecting everyone's trust.

jyutping: tau1 sik6 m4 wui5 giu2 zeoi2
mandarin_meaning: 偷情但不露出破綻／不表現出來
english_meaning: To cheat (on a partner) but not show it / to hide one's infidelity
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語的俗語，意思是出軌或偷情，但在外表或行為上不會露出端倪／馬腳，能夠掩飾得很好。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase meaning someone is cheating on their partner but doesn't show any signs — their infidelity is well hidden.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好以為偷食唔會挢嘴就冇事，啲人遲啲都會發現㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ji5 wai6 tau1 sik6 m4 wui5 giu2 zeoi2 zau6 mou5 si6, di1 jan4 ci4 di1 dou1 wui5 faat3 jin6 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要以為偷情不會露出馬腳就沒事，人遲早會發現的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't think you can cheat and not show it — people will find out eventually.

jyutping: tau1 gai1 m4 dou2 sik1 baa2 mai5
mandarin_meaning: 偷鸡不成，蚀把米（想占便宜却失败，反而赔了本钱）
english_meaning: To try to gain an advantage or a quick profit through a trick or shortcut but fail and end up worse off (to try to steal a chicken but lose the rice used as bait).
explanation_mandarin: 形容想要占便宜或耍小聪明，结果计划失败，反而遭受损失。
explanation_english: Describes attempting to get an easy gain or outsmart others, but the plan backfires and one suffers a loss instead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢諗住喺拍賣會低價買件古董，點知係假貨，真係偷鸡唔到蚀把米。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 nam2 zyu6 hai2 paak3 maai6 wui2 dai1 gaa3 maai5 gin6 gu2 dung2 , dim2 zi1 hai6 gaa2 fo3 , zan1 hai6 tau1 gai1 m4 dou2 sik1 baa2 mai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他想在拍卖会上以低价买到一件古董，结果是赝品，真是偷鸡不成，蚀把米。
examples.english_sentence: He tried to buy an antique cheaply at the auction, but it turned out to be a fake — he tried to get a bargain and ended up worse off.

mandarin_meaning: 小偷；愛佔小便宜的人（粵語口語、貶義）
english_meaning: a petty thief; someone who habitually takes small things or advantages (colloquial, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「偷鹽蛇」是粵語口語用語，字面是「偷鹽的蛇」，用來形容經常偷小東西或占小便宜、行為見不得人的人。語氣通常帶貶義，多用於非正式語境。
explanation_english: “Tou jim se” (literally 'salt-stealing snake') is a Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to describe someone who frequently steals small items or takes petty advantages. It is derogatory and used in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做偷鹽蛇，成日拎人嘅嘢又唔講一聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 tau1 jim4 se4, sing4 jat6 ling1 jan4 ge3 je5 jau6 m4 gong2 jat1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別做偷鹽蛇，老是拿別人的東西又不說一聲。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a 'tau jim se'—constantly taking other people's things without saying a word.

mandarin_meaning: 未查到（可能為罕用字、古字或書寫錯誤，非廣泛使用的粵語詞彙）
english_meaning: Not found / unknown (possibly a rare character, archaic form, or a misspelling; not an established Cantonese word)
explanation_mandarin: 「傒」與「醯」均為較罕見或古滯字形，在常見粵語詞典與語料庫中未見作常用詞彙。可能是誤寫、古文用字或某方言的罕用詞，缺乏可靠詞義與讀音資料，故無法提供確定解釋。
