explanation_english: A metaphorical slang saying meaning you cannot shirk responsibility or avoid blame unless there is some 'oil' — i.e. a bribe, favor, or other help to make it possible.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次事咁大，冇油唔甩得镬，冇人肯幫佢頂镬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 si6 gam3 daai6, mou5 jau4 m4 lat1 dak1 wok6, mou5 jan4 hang2 bong1 keoi5 ding2 wok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次事情這麼嚴重，沒有油就甩不了鍋，沒有人願意幫他頂鍋。
examples.english_sentence: This matter is so serious; without oil you can't dodge the blame — nobody is willing to take the fall for him.

mandarin_meaning: 沒有漏洞、破綻
english_meaning: no loopholes; airtight; without any gaps or flaws
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指事物或安排非常周全、沒有可以利用的空隙或破綻。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning something is so thorough or well arranged that there are no loopholes, gaps, or flaws to exploit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢份報告做得好仔細，冇漏罅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 bou3 gou3 zou6 dak1 hou2 zai2 sai3, mou5 lau6 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的報告做得很仔細，沒有漏洞。
examples.english_sentence: His report was very thorough; there were no loopholes.

mandarin_meaning: 一種廣東話俚語／粗口，含義大致為「沒用、毫無價值」或「一無是處」，但詞彙非常罕見且字形與讀音存在不確定性
english_meaning: A very rare Cantonese slang/expletive roughly meaning "useless/worthless" or "nothing at all"; the phrase is obscure and the pronunciation of the last two characters is uncertain
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感嘆詞／俚語（粗口色彩，使用時帶輕蔑或不屑）
explanation_mandarin: 「冇爪蠄𮔚」是一個極為罕見的廣東話俗語或粗口詞組。前兩字「冇爪」可解作「沒有用處」或加強語氣，但後兩個字（蠄、𮔚）在現代用字與讀音上均不穩定，可能為方言字或擬聲／古字的變體。整體用法通常用於表達輕蔑、不屑或形容某物毫無價值。由於來源與讀音不確定，日常交流中較少見。
explanation_english: "冇爪蠄𮔚" is an extremely rare Cantonese colloquial/expletive phrase. The first two characters, 冇 (mou5) and 爪 (zaau2), are readable, with 冇 meaning "not have"; the last two characters are uncommon and their pronunciations/meanings are uncertain and may be dialectal or archaic variants. The phrase is used informally to express contempt or to call something completely useless or worthless. Because of its rarity and uncertain pronunciation, it is not common in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件嘢真係冇爪蠄𮔚，唔好浪費時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 je5 zan1 hai6 mou5 zaau2 (後兩字讀音不詳)，m4 hou2 long6 fai3 si4 gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這東西真是冇爪蠄𮔚，別浪費時間。
examples.english_sentence: This thing is really "冇爪蠄𮔚" — don't waste your time.

mandarin_meaning: 無家可歸；沒有遮蔽或依靠，露宿街頭或處於孤立無援、困窘的狀況
english_meaning: Literally 'no tiles to cover the head' — homeless or without shelter; figuratively exposed, unprotected, or in a desperate, unsupported situation
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語說法，字面意思是「沒有瓦片遮住頭」，用來形容沒有住所或沒有依靠，處境艱難。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning literally 'no roof (tiles) to cover the head'. It describes being homeless or, more generally, being exposed and without protection or support.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢失咗屋，依家真係冇瓦遮頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sat1 zo2 uk1, ji4 gaa1 zan1 hai6 mou5 ngaa5 ze1 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他失去了房子，現在真的沒有遮蔽（無家可歸）。
examples.english_sentence: He lost his home and now truly has no roof over his head.

mandarin_meaning: 不过瘾 / 不尽兴 / 不满足
english_meaning: not satisfying; unsatisfying; not enough fun or excitement; (also) no craving
explanation_mandarin: 表示某事物未能满足期待、不过瘾、好玩/刺激不足；亦可指没有瘾头、没有渴望（如戒烟后）。常用于口语。
explanation_english: Expresses that something fails to satisfy expectations—unsatisfying, not exciting enough, or not fun enough; can also mean having no craving (e.g., after quitting). Common colloquial usage in Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套戲真係冇瘾，冇乜驚喜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 hei3 zan1 hai6 mou5 jan2, mou5 mat1 ging1 hei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部戏真是不过瘾，没什么惊喜。
examples.english_sentence: This movie is really unsatisfying; there aren't many surprises.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次手遊更新唔夠好，我打咗兩局就覺得冇瘾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 sau2 jau4 gung1 san1 m4 gau3 hou2, ngo5 daa2 zo2 loeng5 guk6 zau6 gok3 dak1 mou5 jan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次手游更新不够好，我打了两局就觉得不过瘾。
examples.english_sentence: This mobile game update isn't good enough; I played two rounds and already felt unsatisfied.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢戒咗煙好耐，宜家話冇瘾喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gaai3 zo2 jin1 hou2 noi6, ji4 gaa1 waa6 mou5 jan2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他戒烟已经很久了，现在说不再有瘾了。
examples.english_sentence: He's quit smoking for a long time; now he says he no longer has cravings.

jyutping: mou5 ji5 caa4 wu4, dak1 baa2 zeoi2
mandarin_meaning: 只會說話、不願意聽別人的人（比喻）
english_meaning: Someone who only talks and won't listen; all mouth and no ears
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容只顧說話、不聽別人意見的人。字面意思是「沒有耳朵的茶壺，只有嘴」，形象地說明只講不聽的特點。
explanation_english: Used to describe a person who talks a lot but refuses to listen to others. Literally 'a teapot with no ears, only a mouth', picturing someone who is all talk and no listening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日淨係講，唔聽人講，真係冇耳茶壺，得把嘴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zing6 hai6 gong2, m4 teng1 jan4 gong2, zan1 hai6 mou5 ji5 caa4 wu4, dak1 baa2 zeoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是只會說話，不聽別人，真是只會說不會聽。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks and doesn't listen; really all mouth and no ears.

mandarin_meaning: 不願意聽、不理會別人意見；固執、不聽勸
english_meaning: refuses to listen; stubborn; won't heed advice or pay attention to what others say
explanation_mandarin: 「冇耳藤喼」是香港廣東話的俗語，用來形容一個人不願意聽別人說話或勸告，態度固執或故意充耳不聞。通常帶有貶義或戲謔意味，常用於口語。語源帶有比喻性，暗示「沒有耳朵」或「像藤製的袋子一樣聽不進去」。
explanation_english: "冇耳藤喼" is Hong Kong Cantonese slang used to describe someone who refuses to listen to others or heed advice — stubborn or deliberately ignoring what is said. It is colloquial and often mildly derogatory or teasing. The phrase metaphorically implies having no ears or being like a bag that doesn't take anything in.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日冇耳藤喼，講咩都唔聽，最後先至後悔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 mou5 ji5 tang4 gaap3, gong2 me1 dou1 m4 teng1, zeoi6 hau6 sin1 zi3 hau6 fui3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是冇耳藤喼，什麼都不聽，最後才後悔。
examples.english_sentence: He always refuses to listen; he never hears anything and only regrets it in the end.

jyutping: mou5 ji5 tang4 gaap3 - kaau3 tok3
mandarin_meaning: 用來罵人或表達不滿，指不聽勸告、沒用或靠不住的人；亦可作感嘆詞表示氣憤（類似「靠」、「可惡」）。
english_meaning: Colloquial insult/exclamation. Refers to someone who is useless, stubborn, or doesn't listen; can also be used as an exclamation of frustration (similar to "damn it").
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語；名詞或感嘆詞（視語境而定）
partOfSpeech_english: slang; noun or interjection (depending on context)
explanation_mandarin: 「冇耳藤喼」字面荒誕，香港口語中用來形容不聽人勸告、固執或沒用的人；「靠托」常跟「靠」類似，作為加強語氣的罵人或感嘆用語。兩者常連用以表達強烈不滿或鄙夷。
explanation_english: Literally nonsensical phrasing; in Hong Kong Cantonese it's used to describe someone who won't listen, is stubborn, or useless. "Kaau tok" (靠托) often functions like the expletive "kaau" (靠), used to intensify annoyance or insult. The two can be used together to express strong frustration or contempt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日唔聽人講，真係冇耳藤喼，靠托！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 m4 teng1 jan4 gong2, zan1 hai6 mou5 ji5 tang4 gaap3, kaau3 tok3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你总是不听别人说话，真是个不听劝、没救的人，靠托！
examples.english_sentence: You never listen to anyone—you're hopeless/unreliable, damn it!

jyutping: mou5 ji5 tang4 gap3, kaau3 tok3
mandarin_meaning: 沒有可靠的根據或消息，只能靠人情或託關係
english_meaning: No solid evidence or reliable sources; must rely on favors/connections or hearsay
explanation_mandarin: 此為香港粵語口語俚語，用來形容事情缺乏可靠耳目或證據，得靠託人、靠關係或人情才能辦成，語氣常帶無奈或批評意味。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial slang phrase describing a situation that lacks reliable information or evidence, so one has to depend on favors, connections, or hearsay to get things done. The tone often conveys resignation or mild criticism.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次申請冇任何證據，真係冇耳藤喼，靠托先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 san1 cing2 mou5 jam6 ho4 zing3 geoi3, zan1 hai6 mou5 ji5 tang4 gap3, kaau3 tok3 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次申請沒有任何證據，真的是沒有可靠的消息來源，只能靠託關係才行。
examples.english_sentence: This application has no supporting evidence — there really are no reliable sources; we can only get it done by relying on connections/favors.

mandarin_meaning: 没胆量的混蛋／懦夫（口语侮辱用语）
english_meaning: cowardly scum / cowardly ruffian (pejorative insult)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話粗俗的侮辱說法，用來罵人很懦弱、沒膽量且可鄙的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang insult used to call someone cowardly and contemptible — literally 'no-guts bandit/class', used to demean someone's bravery and character.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到有人起衝突就走，真係冇胆匪类。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 jau5 jan4 hei2 cung1 dat6 zau6 zau2, zan1 hai6 mou5 daam2 fei2 leoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一看到有人发生冲突就跑，真是没胆量的懦夫。
examples.english_sentence: He runs away whenever there's a conflict — what a cowardly scoundrel.

mandarin_meaning: 无可救药 / 无药可救
english_meaning: beyond help; incurable; hopeless; beyond remedy
explanation_mandarin: 表示病情、性格或行为坏到无法挽救或纠正，已经没有办法医治或改变。
explanation_english: Used to say that a condition, behavior, or person is beyond cure or help — hopeless and beyond remedy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲壞習慣真係冇药医。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 waai6 zaap6 gwaan3 zan1 hai6 mou5 joek6 ji1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的坏习惯真是无药可救。
examples.english_sentence: His bad habits are really beyond help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢病得好嚴重，醫唔到，醫生話真係冇药医。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 beng6 dak1 hou2 jim4 zung6, ji1 m4 dou2, ji1 sang1 waa6 zan1 hai6 mou5 joek6 ji1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他病得很严重，治不好，医生说真是无药可救。
examples.english_sentence: He's very ill and can't be cured; the doctor said he's really beyond help.

mandarin_meaning: 沒睡 / 睡不着
english_meaning: didn't sleep; sleepless; couldn't fall asleep
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語（形容詞/動詞片語）
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示沒有睡著或整晚睡不着，常用來抱怨失眠或形容疲倦。
explanation_english: Cantonese colloquial expression meaning one didn't sleep or was unable to fall asleep; used to complain about insomnia or describe being sleepless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚冇覺眼，成晚瞓唔着。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 mou5 gok3 ngaan5, seng4 maan5 fan3 m4 zoek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚沒睡，整晚都睡不着。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't sleep tonight; I couldn't fall asleep all night.

mandarin_meaning: 睡不好；睡得不安稳（难以入睡或整夜睡得不稳）
english_meaning: can't sleep well; have trouble sleeping; sleep restlessly
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語說法，表示無法好好入睡或睡得不安穩，通常因為擔心、緊張、工作壓力或環境問題而導致睡眠品質差。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to be unable to sleep well or to sleep restlessly. It is commonly used when worry, stress, overtime work, or an uncomfortable environment causes poor sleep.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近老闆加班多，我成日都冇觉好瞓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 lou5 baan2 gaa1 baan1 do1, ngo5 sing4 jat6 dou1 mou5 gok3 hou2 fan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近老闆加班多，我老是睡不好。
examples.english_sentence: Lately the boss has been assigning a lot of overtime, and I always can't sleep well.

mandarin_meaning: 不用着急 / 不必急
english_meaning: no need to hurry; don't rush; take your time
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語（表示勸慰或緩和語氣）
explanation_mandarin: 「冇走盏」是香港廣東話的口語說法，常用來安慰或提醒對方不用著急、可以慢慢來。語氣較隨意、口語化，屬於俚語/口語短語。
explanation_english: “冇走盏” is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to tell someone there is no need to hurry — to reassure or remind them to take their time. It's informal and commonly used in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你趕住去開會？冇走盏，仲有十幾分鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gon2 zyu6 heoi3 hoi1 wui6? mou5 zau2 zaam2, zung6 jau5 sap6 gei2 fan1 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你趕著去開會嗎？不用著急，還有十幾分鐘。
examples.english_sentence: Are you rushing to the meeting? No need to hurry — there's still over ten minutes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做功課唔好太急，冇走盏，慢慢整好啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 gung1 fo3 m4 hou2 taai3 gap1, mou5 zau2 zaam2, maan6 maan6 zing2 hou2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做作業不要太趕，不用著急，慢慢做好一點。
examples.english_sentence: Don't rush your homework. No need to hurry — take your time and do it better.

mandarin_meaning: 沒有退縮；沒有逃跑（沒膽怯）
english_meaning: didn't chicken out; didn't back down; didn't run away
explanation_mandarin: 「冇走鸡」是粵語口語或俚語，字面上「沒有跑（像雞）」，用來表示沒有膽怯或沒有退縮，通常用來形容在壓力或危機下仍堅持、不逃避。
explanation_english: "冇走鸡" is a Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase literally meaning "didn't run (like a chicken)". It expresses that someone didn't chicken out or back down — they stood firm and didn't escape or give up under pressure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢面對困難冇走鸡，一直堅持落去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 min6 deoi3 kwan3 naan6 mou5 zau2 gai1, jat1 zik6 gin1 ci4 lok6 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他面對困難沒有退縮，一直堅持下去。
examples.english_sentence: He didn't chicken out when facing difficulties; he kept persevering.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽好緊張，但佢冇走鸡，最終攞到獎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 hou2 gan2 zoeng1, daan6 keoi5 mou5 zau2 gai1, zeoi3 zung1 lo2 dou3 zoeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比賽很緊張，但他沒有退縮，最終拿到獎。
examples.english_sentence: The competition was tense, but he didn't chicken out and ended up winning a prize.

mandarin_meaning: 沒道理；荒謬；無聊，說話或行為沒有意義或說不通
english_meaning: nonsense; absurd; makes no sense; pointless
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俗語，用來形容某事或某人說話、行為毫無道理、荒謬或沒有意義。常帶有不屑或抱怨的語氣。括號內為常見的口語變體或讀法標示。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe something or someone as nonsensical, absurd, or pointless. Often carries a tone of disdain or complaint. The parenthesis shows a common variant/pronunciation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日講啲嘢冇釐傝𠎷(搭霎)，我真係聽唔明。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 gong2 di1 je5 mou5 lei4 tau4 (daap3 saat3), ngo5 zan1 hai6 teng1 m4 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是說些沒道理／很荒謬的話，我真的聽不懂。
examples.english_sentence: You always say nonsense (冇釐傝𠎷(搭霎)); I really can't understand.

mandarin_meaning: 沒道理；荒謬、不合邏輯
english_meaning: nonsense; makes no sense; absurd
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，表示某事或某人說的話沒有道理、荒謬或不合常理。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to say that something or someone's words are absurd, make no sense, or are illogical.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嗰啲嘢真係冇釐頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 go2 di1 je5 zan1 hai6 mou5 lei4 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說那些話真是沒道理。
examples.english_sentence: What he said really makes no sense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次嘅計劃完全冇釐頭，唔知點解要咁做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 ge3 gai3 waak6 jyun4 cyun4 mou5 lei4 tau4, m4 zi1 dim2 gaai2 jiu3 gam2 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次的計畫完全沒有道理，不知道為什麼要這樣做。
examples.english_sentence: This plan is completely nonsensical; I don't know why they want to do it like this.

mandarin_meaning: 沒有陰功 / 沒有福氣；倒楣、不走運（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: literally 'no yin meritorious deeds' — slang meaning unlucky, having no spiritual merit or good fortune; used to say someone is out of luck or doesn't deserve to be spared
explanation_mandarin: 「冇陰功」字面指沒有陰德或功德，在廣東話口語中用來表示缺乏『陰德』或福報，因而遭遇不幸或被責備。常用於自嘲或形容某人倒楣、不走運。
explanation_english: Literally 'no yin (hidden) merit.' In Cantonese slang it expresses lack of spiritual merit or good fortune, so someone suffers misfortune, gets blamed, or is simply unlucky. Often used self-deprecatingly or to comment that someone is out of luck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日落咗重注，全部輸晒，真係冇陰功。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 lok6 zo2 zung6 zyu3, cyun4 bou6 syu1 saai3, zan1 hai6 mou5 jam1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天下了大注，全部輸光了，真是沒福氣。
examples.english_sentence: I placed a big bet today and lost everything — I'm really out of luck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日幫人，但有時做咗嘢都唔會有人記得，冇陰功啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 bong1 jan4, daan6 jau5 si4 zou6 zo2 je5 dou1 m4 wui5 jan4 gei3 dak1, mou5 jam1 gung1 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常幫人，但有時做了事也不會有人記得，沒陰功罷了。
examples.english_sentence: He often helps others, but sometimes no one remembers; he just doesn't have the 'yin merit'.

mandarin_meaning: 沒必要那麼誇張／沒那麼嚴重
english_meaning: Not that extreme; don't exaggerate; no need to go that far
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，用來表示事情沒有說得那麼誇張或嚴重，類似「沒必要那麼誇張」或「沒有那麼嚴重」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to say something is not as extreme or serious as someone is making it out to be — similar to 'don't exaggerate' or 'it's not that bad.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講得太誇張啦，冇雷公咁远。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 dak1 taai3 kwaa1 zoeng1 laa1, mou5 leoi4 gung1 gam3 jyun5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說得太誇張了，沒必要那麼誇張。
examples.english_sentence: You're exaggerating; it's not that extreme.

mandarin_meaning: 不在乎；不关心；無所謂
english_meaning: don't care; not interested; couldn't be bothered
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語／形容詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話粗俗或口語用法，表示對某事或某人不在乎、不介意、懶得理會。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase meaning to be indifferent or not care about something; used to say one couldn't be bothered or won't bother to deal with it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對嗰件事真係冇𠸎掕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 go2 gin6 si6 zan1 hai6 mou5 ngaa5 laam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對那件事真的不在乎。
examples.english_sentence: He really doesn't care about that.

mandarin_meaning: 沒辦法；無可奈何（粵語口語）
english_meaning: no way; nothing can be done; helpless (Cantonese colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「冇𪐀㨢」是一個粵語口語短語，書寫會用罕見字形（𪐀㨢），主要用來表達對某事無計可施或無奈的心情。此詞在不同社區可能有不同寫法與讀音，屬於非正式用語，來源與確切發音在文獻中較少記錄，因此常以口語形式出現。
explanation_english: “冇𪐀㨢” is a colloquial Cantonese phrase written with uncommon characters (𪐀㨢). It is used to express helplessness or that there is nothing one can do about a situation. The spelling and exact pronunciation vary by community and are not well documented in formal sources; it is mainly used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我試晒所有辦法，依家真係冇𪐀㨢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 si3 saai3 so2 jau5 baan6 faat3, ji4 gaa1 zan1 hai6 mou5 (讀音不詳)。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我試了所有辦法，現在真的是沒辦法了。
examples.english_sentence: I've tried every possible way; now there really is nothing I can do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再諗啦，佢哋已經決定，冇𪐀㨢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 lam2 laa3, keoi5 dei6 ji5 ging1 kyut3 ding6, mou5 (讀音不詳).
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別再想了，他們已經決定，沒辦法改變。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep thinking about it; they've already decided — there's nothing to be done.

mandarin_meaning: 承担全单；请客；付账
english_meaning: to pick up the tab; to pay the whole bill; to treat everyone
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話表達，表示負責支付整個帳單或請客（付清大家的消費）。常用於聚餐或外出時決定誰付錢。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to pay the entire bill or treat everyone. Commonly used when deciding who will cover the cost at a meal or outing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚你寫包單定係大家AA？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 nei5 se2 baau1 daan1 ding6 hai6 daai6 gaa1 AA?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚你請客還是大家各付各的？
examples.english_sentence: Are you treating tonight or are we splitting the bill?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日寫包單，啲朋友好鍾意佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 se2 baau1 daan1, di1 pang4 jau5 hou2 zung1 ji3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常買單，朋友們很喜歡他。
examples.english_sentence: He often pays for everyone; his friends like him.

mandarin_meaning: 該死／他媽的（粗口感嘆詞，用以表達憤怒或懊惱）
english_meaning: A vulgar expletive used to express anger or annoyance; roughly "damn it" or a stronger "fuck"
explanation_mandarin: 「冚床布」是廣東話口語的粗口感嘆詞，用於表達憤怒、不滿或懊惱。語氣粗俗，常在情緒激動時使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar interjection used to express anger, frustration, or annoyance. It is coarse and typically used in emotionally charged situations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 冚床布，今晚又落雨，計劃又要取消！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ham2 cong4 bou3, gam1 maan5 jau6 lok6 jyu5, gai3 waak6 jau6 jiu3 ceoi2 siu1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 該死，今晚又下雨，計劃又要取消！
examples.english_sentence: Damn it, it's raining again tonight — our plan has to be cancelled!

mandarin_meaning: （粗俗用語）用作咒罵或表達憤怒的語詞，常見於複合罵人詞語（如「冚家剷」），大致相當於「去你媽的／去你全家」等辱罵用法。注意字形有時見作「咸」，但語義與廣東話粗口用法相關。
english_meaning: A vulgar Cantonese expletive used to curse or express strong anger; appears in compounds like "冚家剷" meaning "fuck the whole family." Highly offensive slang.
explanation_mandarin: 「冚」原本字義有「蓋」「覆」等，但在香港粵語口語中成為粗口用字，常與其他字結合構成罵人語（例如「冚家剷」「冚你老母」），具有強烈侮辱性，應注意場合禁用。
explanation_english: Originally the character carries meanings like "to cover," but in Hong Kong Cantonese it is used as a coarse curse word. It commonly appears in insulting compounds (e.g. "冚家剷", "冚你老母") and is highly offensive — avoid in polite contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 冚家剷！佢點可以咁樣做？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ham2 gaa1 caan2! keoi5 dim2 ho2 ji5 gam2 joeng6 zou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去你全家！他怎麼可以這樣做？
examples.english_sentence: Fuck his whole family! How could he do that?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講咗一大輪粗口，仲話『冚你老母』。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 zo2 jat1 daai6 leon4 cou1 hau2, zung6 waa6 'ham2 nei5 lou5 mou5'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他講了一大串粗口，還說「去你媽的」。
examples.english_sentence: He said a string of swear words and even said 'fuck your mother.'

mandarin_meaning: （有點）鹹 / 稍微鹹一點
english_meaning: a bit salty; slightly saltier
explanation_mandarin: 「咸啲」表示味道上比平常略鹹，可用於描述食物或要求加鹽使食物稍微更鹹。正字為「咸」（粵語讀作 haam4）。有時口語或打字錯誤會見到「冚啲」，但標準寫法應為「咸啲」。
explanation_english: “咸啲” (haam4 di1) means 'a bit salty' or 'slightly saltier'. It's used to describe that a dish is somewhat salty or to request that something be made a little saltier. The standard character is 咸; the variant 冚 is sometimes seen colloquially or by mistake.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢碗湯咸啲，唔係我鍾意嘅口味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wun2 tong1 haam4 di1, m4 hai6 ngo5 zung1 ji3 ge3 hau2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這碗湯有點鹹，不是我喜歡的口味。
examples.english_sentence: This bowl of soup is a bit salty; it's not to my taste.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 可以幫我加少少鹽嗎？我想佢咸啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 gaa1 siu2 siu2 jim4 maa3? ngo5 soeng2 keoi5 haam4 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 可以幫我加一點鹽嗎？我想要它稍微鹹一點。
examples.english_sentence: Could you add a little salt for me? I want it a bit saltier.

mandarin_meaning: 去你妈的 / 去你的（粗口）
english_meaning: a vulgar Cantonese curse equivalent to "fuck you" or "fuck off"
explanation_mandarin: 香港粗口俚語，用來表示憤怒、咒罵或藐視對方，語氣非常粗俗，通常等同於「去你媽的」或「去死」。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang/expletive used to express anger, insult, or contempt toward someone. Very coarse in tone; roughly equivalent to "fuck you" or "fuck off."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做咗啲咁衰嘅嘢，我真係想同佢講：冚（咸）巴唥！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 zo2 di1 gam3 seoi1 ge3 je5, ngo5 zan1 hai6 soeng2 tung4 keoi5 gong2: ham2 baa1 laap6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做了这么坏的事，我真想跟他说：去你妈的！
examples.english_sentence: You did something so awful — I really want to tell him: fuck you!

mandarin_meaning: 去你全家 / 操你全家（粗俗）
english_meaning: Fuck/ damn your whole family (vulgar insult)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話粗口，用來詛咒或辱罵對方及其全家，語氣非常強烈且冒犯，多見於口語與粗俗語境。
explanation_english: A very vulgar Cantonese curse used to damn or insult someone's entire family. It is an offensive expletive used in angry or contemptuous speech, mainly in colloquial and coarse contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢撞到我都唔理，我真係想講：冚家鏟！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zong6 dou3 ngo5 dou1 m4 lei5, ngo5 zan1 hai6 soeng2 gong2: ham2 gaa1 caan2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他撞到我都不理，我真想說：去你全家！
examples.english_sentence: He bumped into me and ignored me; I really wanted to say: fuck your whole family!

mandarin_meaning: 非常糟糕、又爛又令人厭惡
english_meaning: utterly awful / crappy and disgusting
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語粗俗俚語，用來強烈貶低某人或某事，表示非常差、爛、又令人討厭或噁心。
explanation_english: A coarse Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase used to strongly put down a person or thing, meaning extremely bad/rotten and repulsive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢態度冤崩烂臭，成日遲到又敷衍，大家都唔想同佢一齊做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 taai3 dou6 jyun1 beng1 laan6 cau3, sing4 jat6 ci4 dou3 jau6 fuk1 jin5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 soeng2 tung4 keoi5 jat1 cai4 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的態度又差又爛又討厭，經常遲到又敷衍，大家都不想和他一起工作。
examples.english_sentence: His attitude is awful, rotten and obnoxious—always late and perfunctory; nobody wants to work with him.

jyutping: jyun1 zyu1 tau4 jyu6 zoek3 mung4 bei6 pou4 saat3
mandarin_meaning: 衰上加衰；倒霉接二连三
english_meaning: To be unlucky and then encounter even worse misfortune; misfortune upon misfortune
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容本來已經倒霉的人又遇上更糟的事或更倒霉的人，表示運氣越來越差。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is already unlucky and then runs into even worse situations or people — misfortune on top of misfortune.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係冤豬頭遇着盟鼻菩薩，啱啱輸咗波，返到屋企又斷電。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 jyun1 zyu1 tau4 jyu6 zoek3 mung4 bei6 pou4 saat3, aam1 aam1 syu1 zo2 bo1, faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 jau6 dyun6 din6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是衰上加衰，剛輸了比賽，回到家又停電。
examples.english_sentence: He's really unlucky — he just lost the match and when he got home the power went out again.

mandarin_meaning: 冬菇（香菇，一種食用菌）
english_meaning: shiitake mushroom (edible fungus, often called shiitake or dried shiitake)
explanation_mandarin: 「冬菰」為粵語中常見的稱呼，指的是香菇（shiitake），可鮮用或乾燥保存，用於炖湯、煮菜或提鮮。字形上常見變體「冬菇」。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 冬菰 refers to shiitake mushrooms (香菇). They can be used fresh or dried and are commonly added to soups and dishes for flavor. The character 菰 is a variant; 冬菇 is the more common form.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚煲湯我想加啲冬菰，咁會更香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 bou1 tong1 ngo5 soeng2 gaa1 di1 dung1 gu1, gam2 wui5 gang3 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚煲汤我想加些冬菇，这样会更香。
examples.english_sentence: I want to add some shiitake mushrooms to the soup tonight; it will be more fragrant.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 超市有晒乾嘅冬菰賣，可以買返煲湯用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ciu1 si5 jau5 saai3 gon1 ge3 dung1 gu1 maai6, ho2 ji5 maai5 faan1 bou1 tong1 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 超市有晒干的冬菇卖，可以买回去炖汤用。
examples.english_sentence: The supermarket sells sun-dried shiitake mushrooms; you can buy some to use in soups.

mandarin_meaning: 洗澡 / 淋浴
english_meaning: to take a shower; to bathe
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，意思是洗澡或淋浴，清潔身體。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to wash/bathe or take a shower; to clean one's body.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我返到屋企先沖涼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei5 sin1 cung1 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我回到家才洗澡。
examples.english_sentence: I'll take a shower when I get home.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 沖涼記得關水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cung1 loeng4 gei3 dak1 gwaan1 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 洗澡記得關水。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to turn off the water when you shower.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友唔鍾意沖涼，成日喊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 m4 zung1 ji3 cung1 loeng4, sing4 jat6 haam3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友不喜歡洗澡，總是哭。
examples.english_sentence: The child doesn't like taking a bath and always cries.

mandarin_meaning: 冷笑話（俗稱，不太好笑或令人尷尬的玩笑）
english_meaning: a 'cold' or lame joke (a joke so corny or unfunny it causes awkwardness)
explanation_mandarin: 指那種令人覺得冷場、無聊或尷尬的笑話，類似「冷笑話」；「gag」為英語借詞，用於口語中表示笑料或梗。
explanation_english: Refers to a joke that is corny, unfunny, or causes an awkward silence—similar to a 'cold joke' or 'groaner'. 'Gag' is an English loanword used colloquially to mean a joke or gag.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講冷gag，令到氣氛好尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 laang5 gag3, ling6 dou3 hei3 fan1 hou2 gaam1 gaai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是說冷笑話，弄得氣氛很尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps telling cold gags (lame jokes), which makes the atmosphere very awkward.

jyutping: laang5 hong6 daam1 zuk1 gon1, zik6 ceot1 zik6 jap6
mandarin_meaning: 直來直去；性格直爽或無所顧忌地出入、行為坦率（有時帶有不夾着面子或不講緘默的負面意味）
english_meaning: literally 'carrying a bamboo pole in a cold alley, coming and going straight' — describes someone blunt and straightforward who comes and goes freely; can be neutral (frank) or slightly negative (tactless/shameless)
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語用來形容人為人直率、行為坦蕩、來去無拘，也可暗含粗魯、不拘小節或不顧他人感受的意思，視語境可正面或負面理解。
explanation_english: This Cantonese phrase describes a person who is blunt and straightforward, who comes and goes without restraint. Depending on context it can be a neutral/positive remark about frankness or a negative comment implying tactlessness or shamelessness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做人好冷巷擔竹竿，直出直入，講嘢從來唔拐彎抹角。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 jan4 hou2 laang5 hong6 daam1 zuk1 gon1, zik6 ceot1 zik6 jap6, gong2 je5 cung4 loi4 m4 gwaai2 waan1 mut6 gok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為人很直爽，說話做事直來直去，從不拐彎抹角。
examples.english_sentence: He's very straightforward — he comes and goes and speaks bluntly, never beating around the bush.

jyutping: laang5 sau2 zap1 go3 jit6 zin1 deoi1
mandarin_meaning: 接烫手山芋（接手一件麻烦或棘手的事）
english_meaning: to end up holding the hot potato — to take on an awkward, troublesome or unwanted task
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，字面意思是用冷手去拿热煎堆，暗指不情愿或无奈地接手一件麻烦、棘手或别人不想要的事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquialism literally meaning 'with cold hands pick up a hot sesame ball.' It describes being left (or forced) to take on a troublesome or awkward task that others avoid — equivalent to 'holding the hot potato.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 咁嘅問題冇人想做，最後仲係你冷手執個熱煎堆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam2 ge3 man6tai4 mou5 jan4 soeng2 zou6, zeoi6hau6 zung6 hai6 nei5 laang5 sau2 zap1 go3 jit6 zin1 deoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这种问题没人想做，最后还是你接了烫手山芋。
examples.english_sentence: No one wants to handle this problem; in the end you were left holding the hot potato.

cantonese: 冷死唔着三条裤，饿死唔同外父做
jyutping: laang5 sei2 m4 zoek3 saam1 tiu4 fu3, ngo6 sei2 m4 tung4 ngoi6 fu6 zou6
mandarin_meaning: 宁可冻死也不穿三条裤子，宁可饿死也不愿依靠妻家的父亲（不愿靠女方家庭或为钱屈服）
english_meaning: I'd rather freeze than put on three pairs of pants; I'd rather starve than depend on my wife's father — a humorous way to say one would rather suffer than lose pride or become dependent on in-laws.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語帶有誇張和幽默意味，用來表達一種自尊心或骨氣：寧可自己受苦也不願降低身段、依靠或屈從於別人（尤其是靠妻家或做有失尊嚴的事）。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial saying, expressed with exaggeration and humor, conveys pride or stubborn independence: one would rather suffer than compromise dignity, accept dependence, or submit to others (especially relying on the wife's family or doing something demeaning).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強話：'冷死唔着三條裤，饿死唔同外父做'，佢就係咁有骨氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 waa6: 'laang5 sei2 m4 zoek3 saam1 tiu4 fu3, ngo6 sei2 m4 tung4 ngoi6 fu6 zou6', keoi5 zau6 hai6 gam2 jau5 gwat1 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强说：'宁可冻死也不穿三条裤子，宁可饿死也不依靠妻家的父亲'，他就是这么有骨气。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Keung said, 'I'd rather freeze than wear three pairs of pants; I'd rather starve than depend on my wife's father.' He's that proud.

cantonese: 冷过唔知冷，热过唔知热
jyutping: laang5 gwo3 m4 zi1 laang5, jit6 gwo3 m4 zi1 jit6
mandarin_meaning: 冷了也感觉不到，热了也感觉不到；对外界变化或他人感受漠不关心、麻木
english_meaning: Literally 'doesn't feel cold when it's cold, doesn't feel hot when it's hot' — used to describe someone who is indifferent, oblivious, or emotionally numb/insensitive
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俚語用冷熱作比喻，形容一個人對外在變化或他人感受無反應、麻木或冷漠，不太在意別人的情緒或處境。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial phrase uses cold and heat metaphorically to describe a person who is unresponsive, emotionally numb, or indifferent to changes or other people's feelings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做事冷過唔知冷，熱過唔知熱，從來唔理人啲感受。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 laang5 gwo3 m4 zi1 laang5, jit6 gwo3 m4 zi1 jit6, cung4 loi4 m4 lei5 jan4 di1 gam2 sau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事冷漠，對人感受毫不在意。
examples.english_sentence: He works in an indifferent way, completely unconcerned about other people's feelings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講咁多佢都唔理，真係冷過唔知冷，熱過唔知熱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 gam3 do1 keoi5 dou1 m4 lei5, zan1 hai6 laang5 gwo3 m4 zi1 laang5, jit6 gwo3 m4 zi1 jit6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說那麼多他也不理，真是冷漠無感。
examples.english_sentence: No matter how much you say, he doesn't care — truly indifferent and unresponsive.

mandarin_meaning: 指剩饭剩菜及其汤汁；比喻陈旧、被反复翻炒的内容或素材。
english_meaning: Leftover rice and gravy/sauce; leftovers. Figuratively, stale or rehashed material (old content being brought up again).
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法：原指吃不完的冷飯和菜汁（剩菜），也用來比喻沒有新意、被翻炒過的話題或內容。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese: literally leftover rice and gravy (food). Figuratively used for something stale or rehashed, such as old news or recycled content.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢碟冷饭菜汁係前日嗰啲餸，唔好食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dip6 laang5 faan6 coi3 zap1 hai6 cin4 jat6 go2 di1 sung3, m4 hou2 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这盘冷饭菜汁是前天的菜，别吃了。
examples.english_sentence: This plate of leftover rice and gravy is from the day before yesterday — don't eat it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢寫嗰篇文章淨係冷饭菜汁，冇咩新見解。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 se2 go2 pin1 man4 zoeng1 zing6 hai6 laang5 faan6 coi3 zap1, mou5 me1 san1 gin3 gaai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他写的那篇文章只是老调重弹，没有什么新见解。
examples.english_sentence: His article is just reheated material — there are no new insights.

jyutping: dung3 seoi2 cung1 caa4, mou5 mei6
mandarin_meaning: 用冷水泡茶，没味道；比喻很无聊或索然无味
english_meaning: literally 'brew tea with cold water, no taste' — figuratively: dull, tasteless, boring, lacking interest
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，原指用冷水泡茶會沒有味道，常用來比喻事物很乏味、沒有吸引力或沒有滋味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning something is bland or uninteresting. Literally 'brewing tea with cold water' implies it lacks flavor; used to describe boring or tasteless things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套劇好悶，真係冻水冲茶，冇味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 kek6 hou2 mun6, zan1 hai6 dung3 seoi2 cung1 caa4, mou5 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部剧很无聊，真是索然无味。
examples.english_sentence: This show is really boring — it's totally tasteless.

mandarin_meaning: 冷天 / 天氣寒冷
english_meaning: cold day; cold weather
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指天氣寒冷的日子或狀態，相當於普通話的“冷天/天冷”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning a cold day or cold weather, equivalent to Mandarin '冷天' or '天冷'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日好凍，凍天要著多啲衫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 hou2 dung3, dung3 tin1 jiu3 zoek3 do1 di1 saam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天很冷，冷天要多穿衣服。
examples.english_sentence: It's very cold today; on cold days you should wear more clothes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 凍天出門要戴手套，手好易凍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dung3 tin1 ceot1 mun4 jiu3 daai3 sau2 tou3, sau2 hou2 ji6 dung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 冷天出门要戴手套，手很容易冷。
examples.english_sentence: On cold days you should wear gloves when going out; hands get cold easily.

mandarin_meaning: （……）一下 / 稍微……一下
english_meaning: do something briefly / for a short while; a bit; soften a request (Cantonese colloquial pattern)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 副词性短语（表示程度或短暂）
explanation_mandarin: 「几…下」是廣東話口語用法，通常放在動詞前或後，表示動作持續很短、稍微或嘗試性地做一下，也常用來緩和請求或命令的語氣。例如「等我幾下」相當於普通話的「等我一下」。
explanation_english: The Cantonese colloquial pattern 'gei2 ... haa6' is used before or after a verb to indicate a short or brief action, a quick try, or to soften a request. It corresponds to Mandarin '...一下' and English '...for a bit / briefly'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等我幾下，我去拎嘢出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 gei2 haa6, ngo5 heoi3 ling1 je5 ceot1 loi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等我一下，我去拿东西出来。
examples.english_sentence: Wait for me a bit; I'll go get something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 幫我睇幾下呢份報表得唔得？
examples.jyutping_sentence: bong1 ngo5 tai2 gei2 haa6 ni1 fan6 bou3 biu2 dak1 m4 dak1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 帮我看一下这份报表可以吗？
examples.english_sentence: Can you take a quick look at this report for me?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 試幾下呢部機先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si3 gei2 haa6 ni1 bou6 gei1 sin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 先试一下这台机器吧。
examples.english_sentence: Try this machine briefly first.

mandarin_meaning: 几十、上百 / 很多（口语）
english_meaning: dozens or even hundreds; a lot (colloquial, vague exaggeration)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示數量很多，模糊地說有幾十到幾百，常帶誇張或概估的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression to indicate a large, unspecified quantity — roughly 'tens or even hundreds'. Often used as a vague exaggeration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰啲退貨堆成山，估唔到會有几十百件咁多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 di1 teoi3 fo3 deoi1 seng4 saan1, gu2 m4 dou3 wui5 jau5 gei2 sap6 baak3 gin6 gam2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些退貨堆成一座山，沒想到會有几十百件那麼多。
examples.english_sentence: Those returned goods are piled up like a mountain — I didn't expect there to be dozens or even hundreds of items.

mandarin_meaning: 这么闲 / 这么有空
english_meaning: so idle; so free (having a lot of spare time)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语用法，表示某人有很多空闲时间或无事可做，常带有惊讶或轻微责备的语气。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression indicating someone has a lot of free time or is very idle; often carries a tone of surprise or mild reproach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你几咁闲啊，仲有时间帮我洗碗？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gei2 gam2 haan4 aa3, zung6 jau5 si4 gaan3 bong1 ngo5 sai2 wun2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这么闲，还能有时间帮我洗碗吗？
examples.english_sentence: You're so free — you even have time to help me wash the dishes?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真系几咁闲，成日都喺屋企睇电视。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 gei2 gam2 haan4, sing4 jat6 dou1 hai2 uk1 kei5 tai2 din6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的是这么闲，整天都在家看电视。
examples.english_sentence: He's really that idle — he stays at home watching TV all day.

jyutping: gei2 daai6 zau6 gei2 daai6, ziu1 jip6 zeoi3 daai6
mandarin_meaning: 不管多大，总有人/事物更大（字面：再大也有蕉叶最大）
english_meaning: No matter how big something is, there's always something bigger (literally: however big, the banana leaf is biggest)
explanation_mandarin: 這句粤語俗語字面意思是「不管多大，蕉葉最大」。常用於打趣或挖苦自滿的人，表示總有更大或更厲害的東西，不要自以為是。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying literally meaning "however big, the banana leaf is biggest." It's used jokingly or sarcastically to remind someone not to be complacent — there's always something bigger or more powerful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日話自己嘅餐廳好出名，我就笑住話：「幾大就幾大，蕉葉最大。」
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 waa6 zi6 gei2 ge3 caan1 teng1 hou2 ceot1 ming4, ngo5 zau6 siu3 zyu6 waa6: 'gei2 daai6 zau6 gei2 daai6, ziu1 jip6 zeoi3 daai6.'
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是說自己的餐廳很有名，我笑著說：「幾大就幾大，蕉葉最大。」（意思是：再大也有人更大。）
examples.english_sentence: He keeps saying his restaurant is famous. I laughed and said, "No matter how big, there's always something bigger."

mandarin_meaning: 有點／挺……（口語用法，為「幾」+「係」的口語結構，用來加強語氣）
english_meaning: pretty/quite (colloquial Cantonese structure combining 'gei' + copula 'hai' for emphasis)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 副詞（程度）+ 連繫動詞（口語結構）
explanation_mandarin: 「几系」是廣東話口語中把「幾」（表程度）和「係」（系動詞）連用的表達，用來在說話中加強語氣，常放在形容詞前，例如「几系好」表示「挺／有點好」。主要出現在口語、非正式語境。
explanation_english: "Gei hai" is a colloquial Cantonese structure combining the degree word "gei" (quite/pretty) with the copula "hai" (to be). It's used in speech to add emphasis before an adjective (e.g. "gei hai hou" = "pretty good"). Common in informal, spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部電影几系好睇喎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 din6 jing2 gei2 hai6 hou2 tai2 wo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這部電影挺好看的。
examples.english_sentence: This movie is pretty good.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢几系叻，成日幫到手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gei2 hai6 lek1, sing4 jat6 bong1 dou3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他挺厲害的，經常能幫上忙。
examples.english_sentence: He's pretty capable and always helpful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試几系難，不過唔係好差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 gei2 hai6 naan4, bat1 gwo2 m4 hai6 hou2 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次考試有點難，不過並不是很差。
examples.english_sentence: This exam was kinda hard, but not that bad.

mandarin_meaning: 很難做到 / 難以實現 / 很難才會發生
english_meaning: hard to achieve; difficult to obtain or for something to happen
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示某件事很難達成或很難出現，需要很多條件或努力才會發生。常見於廣東話口語表達。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to say that something is difficult to achieve or obtain — it will only happen with considerable effort or under rare conditions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢隻限量版手袋，真係几难先至买到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 han6 loeng6 baan2 sau2 doi2, zan1 hai6 gei2 naan4 sin1 zi3 maai5 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這款限量版手袋真的很難才買得到。
examples.english_sentence: This limited-edition handbag is really hard to get.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 想喺短時間內升做經理，對佢嚟講幾难先至。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng2 hai2 dyun2 si4 gaan3 noi6 sing1 zou6 ging1 lei5, deoi3 keoi5 lai4 gong2 gei2 naan4 sin1 zi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 想在短時間內升任經理，對他來說很難才行。
examples.english_sentence: Getting promoted to manager within a short time is very difficult for him.

cantonese: 凡事留一线，日后好相见
jyutping: faan4 si6 lau4 jat1 sin3, jat6 hau6 hou2 soeng1 gin3
mandarin_meaning: 凡事留有余地，日后好相处／好相见（不要把事情做绝，给彼此留下回旋余地）
english_meaning: Leave some leeway / Don't burn bridges — act so future reconciliation or contact remains possible.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話提醒人們處事應該留有餘地，不要把事情做絕或徹底得罪對方，這樣日後還能和平相處或再見面。
explanation_english: A proverb advising people to be conciliatory and not to take irreversible actions; keep a way to reconcile or meet on good terms in the future.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋啱啱吵完，我叫佢哋凡事留一線，日後好相見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 aam1 aam1 caau2 jyun4, ngo5 giu3 keoi5 dei6 faan4 si6 lau4 jat1 sin3, jat6 hau6 hou2 soeng1 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们刚吵完，我叫他们凡事留一线，日后好相见。
examples.english_sentence: They just finished arguing; I told them to leave some leeway so they can get along in the future.

mandarin_meaning: 部首/偏旁，像一個開口的容器或方盒，常作字形構件使用
english_meaning: a radical/component shaped like an open box or container; used as a graphical element in Chinese characters
explanation_mandarin: 凵不是常用作獨立詞的字，主要作為漢字的部首或偏旁，表示開口或容器的形狀，出現在多個字的構形中。
explanation_english: 凵 is not commonly used as a standalone word. It functions mainly as a Chinese character radical or component, representing an open box or container shape and appears in the structure of various characters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字嘅部首係凵，代表一個開口嘅器具。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 ge3 bou6 sau2 hai6 ham4, doi6 biu2 jat1 go3 hoi1 hau2 ge3 hei3 geoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字的部首是凵，代表一个开口的器具。
examples.english_sentence: The radical of this character is 凵, representing an open-mouthed container.

mandarin_meaning: 使出渾身解數；傾盡所有本領或手段
english_meaning: to pull out all the stops; to use every trick or resource; to go all out
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語，形容把所有本領或手段都用盡，通常為達成目的或爭取勝利而全力以赴。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to use all one’s tricks, skills, or resources — to go all out to achieve a goal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗贏比賽，佢出盡八寶，乜嘢招數都試過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 jing4 bei2 coi3, keoi5 ceot1 zeon6 baat3 bou2, mat1 je5 ziu1 sou3 dou1 si3 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了贏比賽，他使出渾身解數，什麼招數都試過。
examples.english_sentence: To win the competition, he pulled out all the stops and tried every trick.

mandarin_meaning: 到明年／明年時候
english_meaning: next year (at that time) / when next year comes
explanation_mandarin: 「出年時」是廣東話的口語時間表達，意指「到明年時候」或「明年」，用來表示在明年某個時段發生的事。
explanation_english: “出年時” is a Cantonese colloquial time expression meaning “when next year comes” or simply “next year,” used to indicate something occurring at a time in the next year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我出年時會去英國讀書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ceot1 nin4 si4 wui5 heoi3 jing1 gwok3 duk6 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我到明年時會去英國讀書。
examples.english_sentence: I'll go to study in the UK next year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你出年時有冇時間幫我？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ceot1 nin4 si4 jau5 mou5 si4 gaan3 bong1 ngo5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你明年有沒有時間幫我？
examples.english_sentence: Do you have time to help me next year?

jyutping: ceot1 dak1 teng1 tong4, jap6 dak1 ceoi4 fong4
mandarin_meaning: 既能在社交場合出面得體，又能在家下廚做家務；形容能幹、多才多藝（常用於形容女性）
english_meaning: Able to present oneself well in public/social situations and also capable in the kitchen/at home; denotes practical versatility (often used about women).
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人在外能應酬、在家又能料理家務或下廚，強調社交與家務兩方面都能勝任。
explanation_english: An idiom describing someone who is competent both socially (presentable in public) and domestically (able to cook/handle household tasks); emphasizes versatility across social and home roles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日出席酒會，返到屋企又煮得一手好餸，真係出得廳堂，入得廚房。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ceot1 zik6 zau2 wui6, faan1 dou3 uk1 kei5 jau6 zyu2 dak1 jat1 sau2 hou2 sung3, zan1 hai6 ceot1 dak1 teng1 tong4, jap6 dak1 ceoi4 fong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她經常出席酒會，回到家又能做出一手好菜，真是既會應酬又會下廚。
examples.english_sentence: She often attends receptions and, when she gets home, can cook excellent dishes — truly capable both socially and in the kitchen.

jyutping: ceot1 lou4 tit3, m4 daa2 m4 dak1
mandarin_meaning: 剛出爐的熱門／必勝項目（要下注／參與才能不錯過）
english_meaning: A freshly announced sure‑thing / hot favourite (you must bet/on it or you’ll miss out).
explanation_mandarin: 此廣東話俚語常見於賽馬或打賭語境，字面上「出爐」指剛出來、最新，「鐵」帶有「鐵定／必勝」意思；合起來表示剛出來的熱門或必勝選擇，說話者強調「不下注/不跟進就不行」。也可引申做比喻，用來形容任何剛出現的看似必成之事物。
explanation_english: This Cantonese slang phrase is common in horse‑racing or betting contexts. Literally, 'ceot1 lou4' (just out of the oven) + 'tit3' (from 'tit3 ding6' = certain) yields a 'fresh, sure thing'. It signals a newly revealed hot favorite that one 'must' bet on. It can also be used metaphorically for any newly emerged 'can't-miss' opportunity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚嗰場馬係出炉铁，唔打唔得！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 go2 coeng4 maa5 hai6 ceot1 lou4 tit3, m4 daa2 m4 dak1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚那場馬是剛出爐的鐵，不下注不行！
examples.english_sentence: Tonight's race is a fresh hot favourite — you have to bet on it!

mandarin_meaning: 作弊；在考試或比賽中以不正當手段獲取答案或幫助
english_meaning: to cheat (especially in exams); to obtain answers or assistance by unfair means
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用語，通常指在考試、測驗或比賽中用作弊的方法（如偷看、傳答案、事先透漏試題等）取得優勢。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to cheat, typically in exams or competitions — e.g., by peeking, passing answers, or leaking questions beforehand.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺考試入面出猫仔，俾監考發現咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 haau2si3 jap6min6 ceot1 maau1 zai2, bei2 gaam1haau2 fat3jin4 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在考试中作弊，被监考发现了。
examples.english_sentence: He cheated in the exam and was caught by the invigilator.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好出猫仔，大家公平啲做啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 ceot1 maau1 zai2, daai6gaa1 gung1ping4 di1 zou6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要作弊，大家公平一點做吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cheat — everyone should do it fairly.

cantonese: 出门弯弯腰，回家有柴烧
jyutping: ceot1 mun4 waan1 waan1 jiu1, wui4 gaa1 jau5 coi4 siu1
mandarin_meaning: 出门勤劳、辛苦工作，回家就有饭吃、柴火可烧；强调勤劳能带来生计
english_meaning: Work hard when you go out and you'll have enough to live on when you return home; a proverb encouraging diligence because it brings sustenance.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粤语俗语，字面是出门要弯腰干活，回家就有柴可烧，意指通过勤劳和努力可以得到生活所需，劝诫不要懒惰。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally meaning 'bend your back when you go out, and you'll have firewood to burn when you get home.' It teaches that hard work brings the necessities of life and warns against laziness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿妈成日同我讲：出门弯弯腰，回家有柴烧，叫我唔好偷懒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 seng4 jat6 tung4 ngo5 gong2: ceot1 mun4 waan1 waan1 jiu1, wui4 gaa1 jau5 coi4 siu1, giu3 ngo5 m4 hou2 tau1 laan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈经常对我说：出门弯弯腰，回家有柴烧，叫我不要偷懒。
examples.english_sentence: My mother often tells me, 'Work hard when you go out and you'll have something to live on when you return,' urging me not to be lazy.

mandarin_meaning: 出門忘帶重要東西；出門遇上倒霉／不順
english_meaning: To go out unprepared or to encounter bad luck immediately after leaving; (colloquial) to forget something important when going out
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的口語俗語，字面是「出門沒有六月」。常用來形容匆忙出門而忘記帶重要東西，或剛出門就遇到不順或倒霉的情況。用法非正式，帶有地區色彩。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "go out without June." It is used to describe leaving home unprepared (e.g. forgetting something important) or immediately running into bad luck after going out. Informal and regionally used.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝趕住出門，結果出門无六月，連部電話都唔記得拎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 gon2 zyu6 ceot1 mun4, git3 gwo2 ceot1 mun4 mou5 luk6 jyut6, lin4 bou6 din6 waa2 dou1 m4 gei3 dak1 ling1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上匆忙出門，結果出門忘了重要的東西，連手機都忘了帶。
examples.english_sentence: I rushed out this morning and ended up going out unprepared—I even forgot my phone.

mandarin_meaning: 出風頭；顯擺、搶風頭
english_meaning: to show off; to hog the limelight; to draw attention to oneself
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，指為了引人注意而故意表現、顯擺或搶風頭，通常含貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to act ostentatiously or deliberately seek attention—i.e., to show off or hog the limelight. It usually carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鍾意出鷯哥，成班人都覺得好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zung1 ji3 ceot1 liu4 go1, sing4 baan1 jan4 dou1 gok3 dak1 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是愛出鷯哥，大家都覺得很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He always shows off; the whole group finds it annoying.

jyutping: dou1 cit3 dau6 fu6 - loeng5 bin1 gwong1
mandarin_meaning: （常寫作「刀切豆腐兩邊光／兩面光」）兩邊都討好、兩邊都得到好處或不表態以免得罪任何一方。
english_meaning: Literally “cutting tofu so both sides are smooth”; idiomatically to please or accommodate both sides, to avoid taking a side, or to give benefits so both parties are satisfied.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人或做法試圖兩面討好或同時照顧雙方利益，或因不願表態而兩邊都保留。注意用字通常為「兩邊光」或「兩面光」，用「便」多為誤寫。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone or an approach that tries to please both sides or cater to both interests, or that avoids taking a stand. The usual written forms are “兩邊光” or “兩面光”; the character 便 in the user-provided form is likely a misspelling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做事成日刀切豆腐兩邊光，唔肯表態。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 sing4 jat6 dou1 cit3 dau6 fu6 loeng5 bin1 gwong1, m4 hang2 biu2 toi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事總是兩面討好，不肯表態。
examples.english_sentence: He always tries to please both sides and won't take a stand.

mandarin_meaning: 刁鑽、古怪、難相處（形容人故意刁難或扭捏）
english_meaning: being difficult, contrary, or deliberately awkward; picky and uncooperative
explanation_mandarin: 「刁侨扭拧」是粵語口語說法，用來形容一個人性格古怪、難相處、故意扭捏或挑剔，不願配合別人。屬於非正式或地方性用語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression describing someone who is awkward, deliberately contrary, picky, or uncooperative. It's informal and often used to criticize a person's attitude or behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日刁侨扭拧，唔肯幫人，大家都覺得好難頂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 diu1 kiu4 nau2 ning2, m4 hang2 bong1 jan4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 gok3 dak1 hou2 naan4 deng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是刁鑽扭捏，不肯幫人，大家都覺得很難相處。
examples.english_sentence: He's always being difficult and awkward and refuses to help — everyone finds him hard to get along with.

mandarin_meaning: 随时/很可能/在很短时间内
english_meaning: at any minute; very likely; easily; in no time
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示在很短的時間內就會發生、隨時可能發生，或表示某事很容易發生/程度很高。
explanation_english: Colloquial adverb used to indicate something could happen at any moment, happens very quickly, or is very likely/easy to occur.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢分分鐘遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan1 fan1 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他分分钟会迟到。
examples.english_sentence: He could be late at any moment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家天氣咁差，分分鐘落雨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 tin1 hei3 gam2 caa1, fan1 fan1 lok6 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在天气这么差，分分钟会下雨。
examples.english_sentence: The weather is so bad now, it could rain any minute.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢分分鐘發火，要小心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan1 fan1 faat3 fo2, jiu3 siu2 sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他分分钟就会发火，你要小心点。
examples.english_sentence: He can get angry at any moment; you should be careful.

jyutping: fan1 gam1 tung4 mei6, duk6 sik6 naan4 fei4
mandarin_meaning: 分甘同味，独食难肥（大家一起分享利益與苦樂；獨自佔有難以致富/無法長久）
english_meaning: Share the sweet and the savory; you can't prosper by eating alone — cooperate and share benefits rather than hoarding.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話勸人要與他人同享利益與困難，強調合作和分享的重要性；若獨自霸佔，反而難以長久或難以富有。
explanation_english: A proverb advising people to share gains and hardships; it emphasizes cooperation and sharing. Hoarding or trying to benefit alone will not lead to lasting prosperity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意唔好淨係諗住自己，分甘同味，獨食難肥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 nam2 zyu6 zi6 gei2, fan1 gam1 tung4 mei6, duk6 sik6 naan4 fei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意不要只想着自己，分甘同味，独食难肥。
examples.english_sentence: When doing business, don't think only of yourself — share the gains; you can't prosper by eating alone.

mandarin_meaning: 零星、局部陣雨（粵語俗語，罕見）
english_meaning: intermittent/patchy showers; localized short rain (colloquial/rare Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 字面為「分開的龍雨」，實際上是一個較罕見的粵語俗語，用來形容雨勢局部、間歇、像分散的雨帶，只在某些地區下雨，語義接近「陣雨」「驟雨」。
explanation_english: Literally 'split dragon rain', this is a rare colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe patchy or localized showers that fall intermittently in certain areas. It is close in meaning to 'showers' or 'sudden rain'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 天氣報告話今日會有分龍雨，下晝出門記得帶把遮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tin1 hei3 bou3 gou3 waa6 gam1 jat6 wui5 jau5 fan1 lung4 jyu5, haa6 zau3 ceot1 mun4 gei3 dak1 daai3 baa2 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 天氣預報說今天會有分龍雨，下午出門記得帶把傘。
examples.english_sentence: The weather report says there will be patchy showers today; remember to bring an umbrella when you go out this afternoon.

mandarin_meaning: 形容關係非常親密，密不可分
english_meaning: Describes a relationship so close that the parties are inseparable
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容兩個人或事物關係非常親近、難以分開，像把肉切下來也不會離開皮一樣。
explanation_english: Used to describe two people or things that are extremely close and cannot be separated, like flesh that does not leave the skin when cut.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個感情好到切肉不離皮，日日都黐埋一齊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 gam2 cing4 hou2 dou3 cit3 juk6 bat1 lei4 pei4, jat6 jat6 dou1 ci1 maai4 jat1 cai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们两个人感情好到切肉不离皮，天天都黏在一起。
examples.english_sentence: Their relationship is so close, like flesh that doesn't leave the skin; they're together every day.

jyutping: cit3 coi3 dou1 tai3 tau4, ngaa4 jin1
mandarin_meaning: 無厘頭的俚語／胡說八道（字面上沒有連貫意義）
english_meaning: A nonsensical Cantonese chant/slang — basically 'nonsense' or 'gibberish' (literal words don't form a coherent meaning).
explanation_mandarin: 「切菜刀剃头，牙烟」是一句廣東話的口語俚語或戲謔用語，字面組合沒有連貫含義，常用來形容或回應胡說亂講、無厘頭的話，帶有戲謔或輕蔑的語氣。來源不明，多見於日常閒聊或小朋友打趣時使用。
explanation_english: “切菜刀剃头，牙烟” is a colloquial Cantonese nonsensical phrase. Its literal words do not create a coherent meaning. It is used playfully or dismissively to label someone’s talk as nonsense or absurd, often in casual conversation or teasing contexts. Origin is unclear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咪再講啲切菜刀剃头，牙烟啦，我聽唔明你講乜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 mai6 zoi3 gong2 di1 cit3 coi3 dou1 tai3 tau4, ngaa4 jin1 laa1, ngo5 teng1 m4 ming4 nei5 gong2 mat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再說那些切菜刀剃头，牙烟了，我聽不懂你在說什麼。
examples.english_sentence: Stop saying that '切菜刀剃头，牙烟' nonsense — I can't understand what you're saying.

cantonese: 刘义打番鬼，越大越好睇
jyutping: lau4 ji6 daa2 faan1 gwai2, jyut6 daai6 jyut6 hou2 tai2
mandarin_meaning: （俚語）越大越好看。通常半開玩笑地稱讚尺寸較大，常用於指胸部或其他醒目尺寸。「刘义打番鬼」作為俗語式的前綴或感嘆語，並無固定字面意思，主要用來加強語氣。
english_meaning: (slang) 'The bigger, the better-looking.' Often used jokingly to praise larger size (commonly referring to breasts or other prominent features). The initial part 'Lau Yi daa faan gwai' functions as a jocular prefix with no literal meaning and mainly adds emphasis.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 感歎語 / 短語
explanation_mandarin: 這句是香港廣東話的口語或俚語說法，通常用來半開玩笑地讚美某物（如胸部、裝飾等）尺寸越大越顯眼、更好看。前半段「刘义打番鬼」並無明確字面解釋，屬於強調語氣的俗語成分，使用時需注意場合，因為可能帶有性暗示或不禮貌的意味。
explanation_english: This is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression typically used jokingly to praise that something (e.g., breasts, a noticeable feature) looks better when larger. The front part 'Lau Yi daa faan gwai' has no clear literal meaning and acts as an emphatic, jocular prefix. Use with caution as it can be sexually suggestive or impolite depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講真，嗰對胸，刘义打番鬼，越大越好睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 zan1, go2 deoi3 hung1, lau4 ji6 daa2 faan1 gwai2, jyut6 daai6 jyut6 hou2 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 說真的，那對胸，真的是越大越好看！(「刘义打番鬼」為俚語前綴，用來加強語氣)
examples.english_sentence: Honestly, that pair of breasts — the bigger the better-looking! (The 'Lau Yi daa faan gwai' part is a slangy prefix to add emphasis.)

cantonese: 刘备借荆州，一借冇回头
jyutping: lau4 bei6 je3 ging1 zau1, jat1 je3 mou5 wui4 tau4
mandarin_meaning: 刘备借荆州，一借不回头
english_meaning: To borrow something and never return it; used metaphorically for taking advantage and not giving back (originates from Liu Bei borrowing Jingzhou).
explanation_mandarin: 源自三国故事，指借用别人的东西或地盘后不归还，也用于形容占了便宜却不肯归还或悔改。
explanation_english: Derived from the Three Kingdoms story of Liu Bei borrowing Jingzhou, it means to borrow something and not return it; metaphorically describes taking advantage and refusing to give back or change one's ways.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做劉備借荊州，一借冇回頭，借咗嘢就要還返。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 lau4 bei6 je3 ging1 zau1, jat1 je3 mou5 wui4 tau4, je3 zo2 je5 zau6 jiu3 waan4 faan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別做“刘备借荆州，一借不回头”，借了东西就要还。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be like 'Liu Bei borrowing Jingzhou' — if you borrow something, return it; don't be someone who never gives it back.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）是第一次嗎？／是新手嗎？
english_meaning: First time? / Are you a newbie? (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「初不初」是粵語口語或俚語問句，詢問對方是否第一次做某事或是否是新手，語氣常帶調侃、試探或關心，書面上常寫作「初不初」但口語用「初唔初」，「初」讀作 co1。
explanation_english: '初不初' is a Cantonese colloquial/slang question meaning 'Is it your first time?' or 'Are you a newbie?'. It is often used teasingly, to check someone's inexperience, or to show mild concern. Although sometimes written with 不, spoken Cantonese uses 唔 (m4).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你第一次玩呢個遊戲，初唔初？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dai6 jat6 ci3 waan2 ni1 go3 jau4 hei3, co1 m4 co1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你第一次玩这个游戏，是新手吗？
examples.english_sentence: Is this your first time playing this game? Are you a newbie?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你新嚟，初唔初？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 san1 lai4, co1 m4 co1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你是新來的，是不是第一次？
examples.english_sentence: You're new here — is it your first time?

jyutping: co1 hon4 seoi2 nyun5, wui4 nyun5 seoi2 hon4
mandarin_meaning: 字面：初次變冷時水還暖；回暖時水又變冷。引申：比喻事物變化反覆、表面現象與實際情況相反或難以捉摸。
english_meaning: Literal: when the season first turns cold the water is warm; when it warms again the water is cold. Figurative: describes things that fluctuate, are counterintuitive, or where appearances can be misleading.
explanation_mandarin: 此語用自然現象作比喻，說明情況常有反覆或表象與實際相反，不宜過早下結論或武斷行事。
explanation_english: This proverb uses a natural observation as a metaphor to warn that situations can reverse or be deceptive; it advises caution and that one should not draw hasty conclusions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 近排天氣成日反覆，真係初寒水暖，回暖水寒，唔好太快做決定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gan6 paai4 tin1 hei3 sing4 jat6 faan2 fuk1, zan1 hai6 co1 hon4 seoi2 nyun5, wui4 nyun5 seoi2 hon4, m4 hou2 taai3 faai3 zou6 kyut3 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近天氣老是反覆，真是“初寒水暖，回暖水寒”，不要太快做决定。
examples.english_sentence: The weather's been so changeable lately — truly 'at the first cold the water is warm; when it warms again the water is cold' — don't make decisions too quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 判處死刑；（口語）比喻使某人遭受嚴重後果或注定失敗
english_meaning: to sentence (someone) to death; (colloquial) to doom someone or guarantee severe consequences
explanation_mandarin: 口語或書面可用，字面上等同「判處死刑」。在口語中也常用作比喻，表示某人或某事注定完蛋或會有嚴重後果。
explanation_english: Can be used literally to mean 'sentence to death'. Colloquially it's often used figuratively to mean that someone or something is doomed or will face severe consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家咁樣做等於幫自己判死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 gam2 joeng6 zou6 dang2 jyu1 bong1 zi6 gei2 pun3 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你现在这样做等于替自己判死（比喻把自己置于无法挽回的境地）。
examples.english_sentence: What you're doing now is like sentencing yourself to death (figuratively: you're dooming yourself).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆發現你偷嘢，基本上就係判死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 faat3 jin6 nei5 tau1 je5, gei1 bun2 soeng6 zau6 hai6 pun3 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板发现你偷东西，基本上就是判死（比喻必定会被解雇或遭遇严重后果）。
examples.english_sentence: If the boss finds out you stole something, it's basically a death sentence (figuratively: you'll be fired or in big trouble).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺有死刑制度嘅地方，法官可以判死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 jau5 sei2 hang4 zai3 dou6 ge3 dei6 fong1, faat3 gun1 ho2 ji5 pun3 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在有死刑制度的地方，法官可以判處死刑。
examples.english_sentence: In places where the death penalty exists, judges can sentence someone to death.

jyutping: ping3 (用作「拚/拼」意義；注意：字「判」本身作「判斷/判刑」讀 paan3)
mandarin_meaning: 拼、拚、拼命、努力一搏（口語/俗語用法；有時以「判」作借字）
english_meaning: to give it one's all; to fight/struggle hard; to risk or go all out
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話口語中，「拚/拼」表示努力奮鬥、拼命一搏，有時會見到把「拚/拼」寫作「判」的俗寫。要注意的是，字面上「判」作「判斷/判刑」時讀作 paan3，與此處的口語用法不同。
explanation_english: In Cantonese colloquial speech, 拚/拼 means to struggle, strive, or go all out (to do one's utmost). The character 判 is sometimes used informally as a variant writing, but 判 as the character for 'judge/sentence' is read paan3 and is a different word.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚唔好灰心，拚一拚啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 m4 hou2 fui1 sam1, ping3 jat1 ping3 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚不要灰心，拼一拼吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't lose heart tonight — give it a try!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗嗰份工拚命做，想升職。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 go2 fan6 gung1 ping3 ming6 zou6, soeng2 sing1 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了那份工作拼命做，想升職。
examples.english_sentence: He worked like crazy at that job hoping to get promoted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽到尾嗰陣，兩隊都係拚到盡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 dou3 mei5 go2 zan6, loeng5 deoi6 dou1 hai6 ping3 dou3 zeon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比賽到最後時刻，兩隊都拼到最後一刻。
examples.english_sentence: At the end of the match, both teams fought all the way.

mandarin_meaning: 功利、唯利是圖（口語俗語）
english_meaning: being overly profit‑oriented; money‑grubbing (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「利利市市（是是）」為粵語口語俗語，通常用來形容一個人非常功利、只顧利益或金錢，帶有貶義。此短語為重疊用法，偶爾見到以「是是」作為變體的寫法，語感上強調「十分注重利害得失」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese reduplicated phrase used to describe someone who is extremely profit‑oriented or focused only on money/benefit. It is pejorative. The reduplication intensifies the sense of being calculating; a variant writing using the characters for "si6 si6" is sometimes seen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢真係利利市市，成日淨係諗點樣賺錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 zan1 hai6 lei6 lei6 si5 si5, sing4 jat6 zing6 hai6 nam2 dim2 joeng6 zaan6 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事真的很功利，總是只想著怎麼賺錢。
examples.english_sentence: He's really money‑oriented — always just thinking about how to make money.

mandarin_meaning: 红包 / 压岁钱
english_meaning: red envelope (lucky money given during festivals, esp. Lunar New Year)
explanation_mandarin: 指華人在節日（尤其是農曆新年）用紅色信封包裝的錢，作為祝福或壓歲之用；亦可作動詞，表示給或收這些紅包（如「派利是」「收利是」）。
explanation_english: Refers to the red envelope containing money given during festivals (especially Lunar New Year) as a gesture of blessing/luck; can also be used as a verb meaning to give or receive such envelopes (e.g. "to give red envelopes").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 農曆新年大家會派利是。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nung4 lik6 san1 nin4 daai6 gaa1 wui5 paai3 lei6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 农历新年大家会派利是。
examples.english_sentence: Everyone gives out red envelopes during Lunar New Year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路通常會好期待收利是。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 tung1 soeng4 wui5 hou2 kei4 doi6 sau1 lei6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子通常很期待收利是。
examples.english_sentence: Children usually look forward to receiving red envelopes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你收咗幾多利是？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sau1 zo2 gei2 do1 lei6 si6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你收了多少利是？
examples.english_sentence: How many red envelopes did you get?

jyutping: lei6 si6 fung1 (also lei6 si5 fung1)
mandarin_meaning: 利是封 / 红包（包着钱的礼金信封，用于农历新年、婚礼等场合）
english_meaning: red envelope (a money-filled envelope given as a gift on Lunar New Year, weddings, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語中指包着钱的红包信封，常在農曆新年、婚礼、拜年或其他庆祝场合由長輩或主人派给晚輩或賓客。書寫上有利是（利市）兩種俗寫，讀音多為 lei6 si6 fung1（亦有 lei6 si5 變體）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term for the red envelope containing money, traditionally given during Lunar New Year, weddings, and other celebratory occasions. It is a cultural gift symbolizing luck and blessings. The term is written as 利是 (or the variant 利市) and pronounced lei6 si6 fung1 (with an alternate reading lei6 si5).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年會有好多利是封俾小朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 wui5 jau5 hou2 do1 lei6 si6 fung1 bei2 siu2 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新年會有很多利是（紅包）給小朋友。
examples.english_sentence: There will be many red envelopes given to children during the Lunar New Year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今次結婚收到啲利是封幾多錢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 ci3 git3 fan1 sau1 dou3 di1 lei6 si6 fung1 gei2 do1 cin2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這次結婚收到的利是有多少錢？
examples.english_sentence: How much money did you receive in red envelopes at your wedding?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 長輩通常會喺婚禮或者新年派利是封。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng2 bui3 tung1 soeng4 wui5 hai2 fan1 lai5 waak6 ze2 san1 nin4 paai3 lei6 si6 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 長輩通常會在婚禮或新年派發利是（紅包）。
examples.english_sentence: Elders usually give out red envelopes at weddings or during the Lunar New Year.

mandarin_meaning: 合眼緣；稱心如意
english_meaning: to be pleasing to the eye; to one's liking
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，用來表示某物或某人合乎自己的喜好或看起來讓人滿意、順眼。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning something or someone is pleasing or appealing to the speaker — i.e., to one's liking or easy on the eyes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫好到眼，我買咗喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 hou2 dou3 ngaan5, ngo5 maai5 zo2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件衣服很合我眼缘，我买了。
examples.english_sentence: This piece of clothing is really to my liking — I bought it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嗰個笑容好到眼，我一見就鍾意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go2 go3 siu3 jung4 hou2 dou3 ngaan5, ngo5 jat1 gin3 zau6 zung1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他／她的笑容很讨人喜欢，我一看就喜欢。
examples.english_sentence: His/her smile is very pleasing — I liked it at first sight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你擺得好到眼，屋企睇落舒服好多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 baai2 dak1 hou2 dou3 ngaan5, uk1 kei5 tai2 lok6 syu1 fuk6 hou2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你摆得很好看，家里看起来舒服多了。
examples.english_sentence: You arranged it very pleasingly; the home looks much more comfortable.

mandarin_meaning: 能制服／壓得住／打得過（某人或某事）
english_meaning: to be able to control, overpower, or beat (someone/something); to be able to handle
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，表示有能力制服、壓制或打敗對方或處理某事，常含壓倒或勝過的意思。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to be able to control, overpower, or defeat someone/something; implies having the ability to handle or dominate a person or situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好以為自己好勁就可以制得過所有人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ji5 wai6 zi6 gei2 hou2 ging6 zau6 ho2 ji5 zai3 dak1 gwo3 so2 jau5 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要以为自己很强就能制服所有人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't assume you're so strong that you can overpower everyone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢拳擊好勁，未必有人制得過佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kyun4 gik6 hou2 ging6, mei6 bat1 jau5 jan4 zai3 dak1 gwo3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他拳击很厉害，未必有人能打得过他。
examples.english_sentence: He's very good at boxing; not many people can beat him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面對一班唔守規矩嘅學生，老師未必可以一個人制得過佢哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 deoi3 jat1 baan1 m4 sau2 gwai1 zeoi2 ge3 hok6 saang1, lou5 si1 mei6 bat1 ho2 ji5 jat1 go3 jan4 zai3 dak1 gwo3 keoi5 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面对一群不守规矩的学生，老师未必能一个人管得住他们。
examples.english_sentence: Facing a group of unruly students, the teacher may not be able to control them alone.

mandarin_meaning: 控制；（作為名詞）開關、按鈕
english_meaning: to control; (noun) a switch or button
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，"制/掣"可作動詞，表示控制、掌控或支配；作名詞時常指開關、按鈕（如遙控掣）。在口語和香港粵語中常見。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "制/掣" can be a verb meaning to control or dominate; as a noun it often refers to a switch or button (e.g. remote control). Common in colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我搵唔到遙控掣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 wan2 m4 dou2 jiu4 hung3 zai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我找不到遙控器。
examples.english_sentence: I can't find the remote control.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日想制人，唔肯聽意見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 soeng2 zai3 jan4, m4 hang2 teng1 ji3 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是想控制別人，不肯聽取意見。
examples.english_sentence: He always wants to control others and refuses to listen to opinions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好攞掣做主，大家一齊商量。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lo2 zai3 zou6 zyu2, daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 soeng1 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要擅自做主，大家一起商量。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make decisions on your own; let's discuss it together.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）嫖妓；另有時被誤寫為「刷機」，指刷手機/升級系統
english_meaning: Slang: to solicit/hire a prostitute; occasionally a misspelling of '刷機' (to flash/update a phone)
explanation_mandarin: 在香港廣東話中，『雞』常作為指代賣淫者的俚語，『刷雞』用來表示去嫖妓或找性工作者。有時在網絡上也會見到把技術詞『刷機』（更新或刷手機系統）誤寫成『刷雞』，此為書寫/打字錯誤或玩笑用法。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, '雞' is slang for a prostitute, and '刷雞' is used to mean going to solicit or hire a sex worker. Separately, some people mistakenly write '刷機' (flash/update a phone) as '刷雞' online; that usage is a misspelling or joking typo.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日去刷雞，咁樣好危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 heoi3 caat3 gai1, gam2 joeng6 hou2 ngai4him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要老去嫖妓，這樣很危險。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep going to solicit prostitutes; that's dangerous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有人將「刷機」寫成「刷雞」，其實係講手機刷ROM。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 jan4 zoeng1 'caat3 gei1' se2 sing4 'caat3 gai1', kei4 sat6 hai6 gong2 sau2 gei1 caat3 ROM.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人把「刷機」寫成「刷雞」，其實是指給手機刷ROM（刷機）。
examples.english_sentence: Some people write '刷機' as '刷雞' by mistake; it's actually referring to flashing a phone's ROM (刷機).

mandarin_meaning: 赤裸、裸體
english_meaning: naked; bare; unclothed
explanation_mandarin: 表示沒有穿衣服、赤裸的狀態；有時也可用作動詞，表示呈現赤裸或露出本來面目。
explanation_english: Indicates the state of being without clothes (naked or bare). It can be used as an adjective or verb to describe someone who is unclothed or figuratively exposed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺屋企赤晒身走出嚟，嚇咗我一跳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 uk1 kei2 cek3 saai3 san1 zau2 ceot1 lai4, haak3 zo2 ngo5 jat1 tiu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在家裡赤裸著走出來，嚇了我一跳。
examples.english_sentence: He came out of the house naked and startled me.

cantonese: 剃头佬教仔，有得刮就刮
jyutping: tai3 tau4 lou2 gaau3 zai2, jau5 dak1 gwaat3 zau6 gwaat3
mandarin_meaning: 剃头的教儿子：有机会就刮（客人）──趁机取利 / 有利可图就去做
english_meaning: A barber telling his son to shave whenever there's a chance — meaning seize opportunities to profit; take advantage of available chances (often with an opportunistic tone).
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俗語，用以形容遇到有利可圖或有機會賺取利益的情況，就應該立即把握去做，帶有趁機取利或務實行事的含意。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying advising that when an opportunity to profit or benefit presents itself, one should take it. It conveys a practical or opportunistic attitude toward seizing chances.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做人做生意要實際，剃頭佬教仔，有得刮就刮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 jan4 zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 sat6 zai3, tai3 tau4 lou2 gaau3 zai2, jau5 dak1 gwaat3 zau6 gwaat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做人做生意要实际，剃头佬教仔，有得刮就刮。
examples.english_sentence: Be practical in life and business — as the proverb says, if there's a chance to profit, take it.

jyutping: tai3 tau4 lou2 zau2 bou3 ging2, laan5 gwaat3
mandarin_meaning: 形容懒惰、逃避责任，宁可去告状或抱怨也不愿亲自做事。
english_meaning: Describes someone who is lazy and shirks responsibility — they'd rather complain or report than do the work themselves.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻做事懶、推諉責任的人，遇到問題不自己動手解決，反而去告狀或抱怨。
explanation_english: A metaphor for a person who is lazy and evasive of duties; when problems arise they avoid doing the work and prefer to complain or report instead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿斌真係剃头佬走报警，懒刮，連自己份內嘅嘢都唔肯做，淨係識投訴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 ban1 zan1 hai6 tai3 tau4 lou2 zau2 bou3 ging2, laan5 gwaat3, lin4 zi6 gei2 fan6 noi6 ge3 je5 dou1 m4 zou6, zing6 hai6 sik1 tau4 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿斌真是剃头佬走报警，懒刮，连自己分内的事都不做，只会投诉。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Bin is really the type who 'the barber runs to call the police, too lazy to shave' — he avoids his duties, won't do his work and only complains.

jyutping: tai3 tau4 m4 sap1 seoi2, gon1 gwaat3
mandarin_meaning: 做事粗率、草率，未經充分準備或不細心地處理
english_meaning: to do something carelessly or roughly without proper preparation; to handle things perfunctorily
explanation_mandarin: 比喻做事不細心、草率敷衍，好像剃頭時不先潤濕就乾刮一樣，容易出問題或造成不良後果。
explanation_english: A metaphor meaning to act carelessly or hastily—like shaving without wetting the hair first (a rough dry shave)—often leading to mistakes or bad results.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢成日剃頭唔濕水，乾刮，搞到成件事有問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 sing4 jat6 tai3 tau4 m4 sap1 seoi2, gon1 gwaat3, gaau2 dou3 sing4 gin6 si6 jau5 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事總是粗率敷衍，結果把整件事情搞砸了。
examples.english_sentence: He always does things carelessly and roughly, and ends up messing the whole thing up.

mandarin_meaning: 古代的一種耙地器具；亦作人名或地名（罕見、古字）
english_meaning: An archaic harrowing tool (used to till or break up soil); also appears as a rare surname or place-name
explanation_mandarin: 「剅」為罕見古字，古時可指耙地用的器具，也見於人名、地名。現代漢語中不常用，常被視為文獻或地名用字。
explanation_english: 剅 is a rare, archaic character historically referring to a harrow or similar agricultural implement; it can also appear in surnames or place names. It is uncommon in modern usage and mainly found in historical texts or toponyms.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「剅」好罕見，古書入面先見到，係指耙地嘅器具。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 "lau4" hou2 hon2 gin3, gu2 syu1 jap6 min6 sin1 gin3 dou3, hai6 zi2 paa4 dei6 ge3 hei3 geoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字「剅」很罕见，只在古书里看到，指耙地的器具。
examples.english_sentence: The character '剅' is very rare, seen only in old books; it refers to a tool used for harrowing the soil.

mandarin_meaning: 非常罕見或非標準詞語；可能是拼寫或輸入錯誤。按字面可解作「規則/準則的戲劇」，但並無固定用法或常見意義。
english_meaning: A very rare or non-standard term; likely a typo or misspelling. Literally "rule/standard + drama", but has no established meaning in Cantonese.
explanation_mandarin: 「則劇」並非粵語常用詞彙，網絡或口語中很少見。常見的「戲劇」一詞在粵語中寫作「戲劇」(hei3 guk6)。遇到「則劇」多數是打字、輸入或拼寫錯誤，或是個別人創造的非標準用法。
explanation_english: "則劇" is not a commonly used Cantonese word. It rarely appears in writing or speech. The familiar word for drama is "戲劇" (hei3 guk6). Instances of "則劇" are most likely typos, input errors, or idiosyncratic/non-standard coinages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「則劇」呢個詞唔常見，可能係打錯字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zak1 guk6 ni1 go3 ci4 m4 soeng4 gin3, ho2 nang4 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「則劇」這個詞不常見，可能是打錯字。
examples.english_sentence: "則劇" is not commonly seen; it may be a typo.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你係指「戲劇」，應該寫做「戲劇」，唔係「則劇」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 hai6 zi2 "hei3 guk6", jing1 goi1 se2 zou6 "hei3 guk6", m4 hai6 "zak1 guk6".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你指的是「戲劇」，應該寫作「戲劇」，不是「則劇」。
examples.english_sentence: If you mean "戲劇" (drama), it should be written as "戲劇", not "則劇".

mandarin_meaning: （口語、貶義）傢伙、混蛋
english_meaning: (colloquial, derogatory) jerk; bastard; lousy fellow
explanation_mandarin: 「則紙」是廣東話俗語，常用作貶義稱呼某人，表示討厭或輕蔑。語氣可從輕蔑到粗俗不等，視語境而定。
explanation_english: "則紙" is a Cantonese colloquial/slang term used derogatorily to refer to a person (e.g. a jerk or rascal). Tone can range from mild contempt to coarse insult depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好理嗰個則紙，佢成日講大話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lei5 go2 go3 zak1 zi2, keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 daai6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別理那個傢伙，他常常說謊。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pay attention to that jerk; he lies all the time.

mandarin_meaning: 未確認的粵語俚語／非標準詞彙，疑為擬聲或戲謔用語，可能用於形容輕鬆打鬧、戲弄或胡鬧（需語境確認）。
english_meaning: Unverified Cantonese slang/nonstandard term, likely an onomatopoeic or playful expression; possibly used to describe light teasing, horseplay, or nonsense (meaning uncertain without context).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語／口語（疑似擬聲詞，可作感嘆或動詞用）
partOfSpeech_english: slang/colloquial (likely onomatopoeic; could function as interjection or verb)
explanation_mandarin: 「削坺坺」不是標準書面詞彙，無法在主要辭典找到確切記載。字形中「坺」為罕用字，整詞可能為某圈子或網路上的口語用法，常見情況是用作擬聲或戲謔表達。若需精確含義或讀音，請提供更多語境或說話者來源。
explanation_english: “削坺坺” is not a standard written word and does not appear in major dictionaries. The character 坺 is rare; the whole expression is likely a community- or internet-specific colloquialism, probably onomatopoeic or playful. It may indicate light teasing or fooling around. For precise meaning and pronunciation, more context or the speaker/source is needed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺論壇見到有人用「削坺坺」，但我唔知佢講緊咩意思。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在論壇看到有人用「削坺坺」，但我不知道他在說什麼意思。
examples.english_sentence: I saw someone use “削坺坺” on the forum, but I don't know what they mean.

jyutping: cin4 sai3 lou1 lyun6 gwat1 tau4
mandarin_meaning: （口語）形容某人好像前世欠下孽債或做了壞事，今生總是惹事、運氣差或麻煩不斷。
english_meaning: A colloquial/slang expression meaning someone seems to have bad karma from a past life — prone to causing or encountering trouble; 'born to cause trouble' or 'karma from a past life'.
explanation_mandarin: 「前世捞乱骨头」常用於廣東話口語，帶有半開玩笑、半責備的語氣，指某人總是惹麻煩或倒楣，彷彿前世做了壞事所以今生要還報。
explanation_english: Used primarily in Cantonese informally (often jokingly or reproachfully) to say a person frequently causes or attracts trouble as if they had bad karma from a previous life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係前世捞乱骨头，成日惹到麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 cin4 sai3 lou1 lyun6 gwat1 tau4, sing4 jat6 je5 dou3 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是前世造孽，總是惹麻煩。
examples.english_sentence: He must have bad karma from a past life — he always gets into trouble.

mandarin_meaning: 前面那一排／前面那一批（視語境而定）
english_meaning: the row/line/group in front; the ones ahead; the previous batch/turn (context-dependent)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用法，表示位於前面的那一排（人或物）或指前一組/前一輪。常用於排隊、合照或描述先前的一批次。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning the row/line or group in front, or the previous batch/turn depending on context. Commonly used when referring to people ahead in a queue, the front row in a photo, or an earlier round.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好插隊，前嗰排嘅人仲未輪到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 caap3 deoi6, cin4 go2 paai4 ge3 jan4 zung6 mei6 leon4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要插隊，前面的那一排人還沒輪到。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cut in line; the people in the row ahead haven't been served yet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我想企前嗰排，咁可以影得靚啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 kei5 cin4 go2 paai4, gam2 ho2 ji5 jing2 dak1 leng3 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想站在前面那一排，這樣拍照會比較好看。
