examples.english_sentence: I want to stand in the front row so the photos will look better.

mandarin_meaning: 吹毛求疵；對瑣碎小事過分挑剔
english_meaning: to nitpick; to be overly critical about trivial details
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用語，表示對細微或瑣碎的地方過度挑剔、吹毛求疵，常令他人不快。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to be excessively critical or picky about minor details; often causes annoyance to others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日剔土邊，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 tik1 tou2 bin1, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他／她總是吹毛求疵，弄得大家不高興。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is always nitpicking, making everyone unhappy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做報告時唔好剔土邊，講重點就得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 bou3 gou3 si4 m4 hou2 tik1 tou2 bin1, gong2 zung6 dim2 zau6 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做報告時不要吹毛求疵，講重點就行了。
examples.english_sentence: When you present, don't nitpick — just state the main points.

mandarin_meaning: （香港口語）欺騙、坑騙他人（俗語）
english_meaning: Cantonese slang for cheating or conning someone; to rip someone off
explanation_mandarin: 「剗雞」是香港粵語俗語，常指以各種手段欺騙或坑騙別人（尤其指騙取金錢或佔人便宜）。語氣偏口語、帶貶義。
explanation_english: “剗雞” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang meaning to cheat, con, or rip someone off (often to take money or advantage). It is colloquial and derogatory in tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日剗雞，唔好同佢做生意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 caat3 gai1, m4 hou2 tung4 keoi5 zou6 saang1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常剗雞，不要跟他做生意。
examples.english_sentence: He often cheats people — don't do business with him.

mandarin_meaning: 把某人所有錢財掏空、榨乾（俚語）
english_meaning: to fleece someone; to strip someone of all their money (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱的廣東話俚語，指把某人身上或財產的錢全部掏光、榨乾，使對方一無所有。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang meaning to drain someone of all their money or possessions; to completely fleece someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人剥光猪，身上連一蚊都冇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 bok3 gwong1 zyu1, san1 soeng6 lin4 jat1 man1 dou1 mou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人把所有錢都掏光了，身上連一塊錢都沒有。
examples.english_sentence: He got completely fleeced; he didn't even have one dollar left on him.

jyutping: bok3 pei4 tin4 gai1, sei2 dou1 m4 bai3 ngaan5
mandarin_meaning: 厚顏無恥、極其不知悔改或非常無恥、臉皮厚到無所顧忌
english_meaning: Extremely shameless or brazen; utterly unrepentant (literally: 'skin a frog, won't even close eyes in death' — used to describe someone shameless or defiantly unashamed).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語/俗語（感嘆或形容短語）
partOfSpeech_english: slang/idiomatic phrase (colloquial, used as an adjective or exclamation)
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俚語用誇張的比喻形容一個人非常厚顏無恥、不知悔改或毫無羞恥心，即使處於極端情況也不會感到羞愧。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression that uses a vivid metaphor to describe someone as extremely shameless or defiantly unrepentant — someone who shows no shame even in extreme circumstances.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人揭穿偷嘢都唔承認，真係剥皮田鸡，死都唔闭眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 kit3 cyun1 tau1 je5 dou1 m4 sing4 jing6, zan1 hai6 bok3 pei4 tin4 gai1, sei2 dou1 m4 bai3 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人揭穿偷東西還不承認，真是厚顏無恥，死也不閉眼。
examples.english_sentence: He was exposed stealing but still won't admit it — truly shameless, unrepentant to the end.

mandarin_meaning: 当看热闹；做看客；袖手旁观
english_meaning: to watch from the sidelines; to be a bystander enjoying the spectacle (often used slangily for watching a quarrel or incident without intervening)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，字面是剥花生，实际指站在一旁看热闹、不参与，只当看客或围观别人发生的事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning 'peel peanuts'; used to describe someone who stands by and watches an event (often a quarrel or scandal) without taking part — an onlooker who enjoys the spectacle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度淨係剥花生，出手幫手啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 zing6 hai6 bok3 faa1 sang1, ceot1 sau2 bong1 sau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只是站在那儿看热闹，出来帮忙吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just stand there and watch; help out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 兩個人吵架，隔離嘅人就喺度剥花生睇熱鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: loeng5 go3 jan4 caau3 gaa3, gaak3 lei4 ge3 jan4 zau6 hai2 dou6 bok3 faa1 sang1 tai2 jit6 naau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 两个人吵架，旁边的人就在看热闹。
examples.english_sentence: Two people are arguing; the people nearby are just watching the spectacle.

mandarin_meaning: 割、切断（文言或罕用）
english_meaning: to cut; to sever (archaic/rare usage)
explanation_mandarin: 「剦」為罕用或文言字，義近「割」、「切斷」，現代粵語一般以「割」「切」替代。常見於古籍或書面語中，不常出現在口語。
explanation_english: 剦 is a rare/archaic character meaning to cut or sever, similar to 割 or 切. It is chiefly literary and seldom used in modern spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢用刀剦咗條繩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 dou1 got3 zo2 tiu4 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他用刀割斷了繩子。
examples.english_sentence: He cut the rope with a knife.

mandarin_meaning: （非標準/罕見粵語詞）字面可理解為「帶有輕微腥味」，也可引申為比喻的「略帶可疑或不潔的氣息」。
english_meaning: A rare/non-standard Cantonese term. Literally '副 (secondary) + 腥 (fishy smell)'; likely means 'slightly fishy' (a faint fishy odor) or figuratively 'a hint of suspicion/unsavoury feeling'.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞（非標準用法／罕見）
explanation_mandarin: 「副腥」在粵語中並非廣泛使用的詞彙。由字面組成，可指食物帶有輕微的腥味（如魚或海鮮未處理乾淨），在口語中也可能被借喻為帶有一點可疑或不潔的氣息。更常用的說法為「微腥」或「有腥味」。
explanation_english: Not a widely attested Cantonese word. Based on its characters, it can describe a faint fishy odor (e.g. slightly fishy seafood) and may be used metaphorically to indicate a hint of suspicion or something unsavoury. More common expressions are '微腥' or '有腥味'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢塊魚肉有啲副腥，要洗一洗先煮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 faai3 jyu4 juk6 jau5 di1 fuk1 sing1, jiu3 sai2 jat1 sai2 sin1 zyu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這塊魚肉有點副腥，要洗一洗才煮。
examples.english_sentence: This piece of fish has a slight '副腥' smell; it needs rinsing before cooking.

mandarin_meaning: 割稻、收割穀物
english_meaning: to reap/harvest (grain); to cut rice plants
explanation_mandarin: 指在田地裡把稻穀或其他穀物割下、收成的動作。
explanation_english: Refers to the action of cutting down rice plants or harvesting grain in the fields.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 農夫喺田度割禾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nung4 fu1 hai2 tin4 dou6 got3 wo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 農夫在田裡割稻。
examples.english_sentence: The farmer is cutting the rice in the field.

mandarin_meaning: 铲草；除草
english_meaning: to weed; to remove grass/weeds (using a hoe/shovel); to mow/clear vegetation
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是用铲子铲掉草或杂草，常用于园艺或农务场景，相当于“除草、割草”。
explanation_english: Literally 'to shovel/mow grass' — to remove grass or weeds (often with a hoe/shovel). Commonly used in gardening or agricultural contexts; equivalent to 'weed' or 'mow the lawn'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽叫我去花園剷草。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 giu3 ngo5 heoi3 faa1 jyun4 caan2 cou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈叫我去花园铲草。
examples.english_sentence: Mom told me to go to the garden to weed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 春天到咗，要剷草同施肥，先至有好收成。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceon1 tin1 dou3 zo2, jiu3 caan2 cou2 tung4 si1 fei4, sin1 zi3 jau5 hou2 sau1 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 春天到了，要铲草和施肥，才能有好收成。
examples.english_sentence: Spring has arrived; we need to weed and fertilize to get a good harvest.

mandarin_meaning: 把（某人）所有钱财掏光、榨干；使一无所有（粤语俚语）
english_meaning: Cantonese slang meaning to clean someone out financially; to fleece someone or take all their money
explanation_mandarin: 「劏光猪」是粤语俚语，字面上有“把猪宰光”的意思，实际用来形容把某人身上的钱或财物全部夺走或榨干，常见于赌博、诈骗或被抢等语境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally meaning 'to gut/kill the pig' but used figuratively to describe cleaning someone out financially — taking all of a person's money or assets. Often used in contexts like gambling losses, scams, or robberies.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上星期我畀人劏光猪，身上連零錢都冇晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 sing1 kei4 ngo5 bei2 jan4 tong3 gwong1 zyu1, san1 soeng6 lin4 ling4 cin2 dou1 mou5 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上星期我被人把钱都掏光了，身上连零钱都没有了。
examples.english_sentence: Last week someone cleaned me out — I didn't even have any spare change on me.

jyutping: tong3 zyu1 dang3, soeng5 can1 zau6 sei2
mandarin_meaning: 坐上去就完蛋 / 一旦參與就會出大問題（比喻）
english_meaning: If you sit on it you're done for; (figurative) get involved and you'll be ruined / it's a trap
explanation_mandarin: 這是香港粵語的俚語。字面上說坐在劏豬用的凳子一坐上去就會死，實際上是誇張的比喻，用來警告某件事或機會極度危險或會惹大麻煩，意指一旦參與就完蛋。語氣口語、粗俗，帶負面貶義。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase. Literally 'sit on the pig‑butchering stool and you die'; figuratively a hyperbolic warning that something is extremely dangerous or a trap — if you get involved you'll be doomed. Colloquial and coarse in tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好接嗰份工，係劏豬凳，上親就死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zip3 go2 fan6 gung1, hai6 tong3 zyu1 dang3, soeng5 can1 zau6 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要接那份工作，像劏豬凳，一上去就完蛋。
examples.english_sentence: Don't take that job — it's a trap; if you get into it you'll be done for.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見）字面意思：剖開一隻白鶴；可能為地方俗語或誤寫，並無廣泛通用的慣用義
english_meaning: Literally 'to gut a white crane' (rare/obscure). Possibly a local slang or a mistaken/rare term; not widely used with a fixed idiomatic meaning.
explanation_mandarin: 此詞極為罕見或地方用語，按字面可理解為「劏（剖開）白鶴」。在廣泛語料中沒有固定的慣用義，亦可能是誤寫或口語偏差。
explanation_english: This term is extremely rare or local. Literally it reads 'to gut a white crane'. There is no widely attested idiomatic meaning in general Cantonese usage; it may be a local slang, archaic form, or a miswriting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個詞好少人講，只有阿伯阿婆先會講「劏白鹤」，佢哋話係字面意思——剖開一隻白鶴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 siu2 jan4 gong2, zi2 jau5 aa3 baak3 aa3 po4 sin1 wui5 gong2 "tong3 baak6 hok6", keoi5 dei6 waa6 hai6 zi6 min6 ji3 si1 — pau2 hoi1 jat1 zek3 baak6 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个词很少人说，只有老一辈才会说“劏白鹤”，他们说是字面意思——剖开一只白鹤。
examples.english_sentence: This word is rarely used; only the older generation says '劏白鹤', and they say it's literal — to gut a white crane.

mandarin_meaning: 惹人生氣／刺激、挑釁別人（廣東話俚語）
english_meaning: to provoke/annoy or tease someone (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「劖眼」是廣東話的口語／俚語，用來形容故意刺激、挑釁或惹人生氣，使人不舒服或生氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to provoke, tease, or annoy someone — to do or say something that irritates or upsets them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日劖我眼，真係好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 cam3 ngo5 ngaan5, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是惹我，真的很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He always picks on me; it's really annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 不要、別（口語助詞）
english_meaning: don't; do not (colloquial prohibitive particle)
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話中用作禁止或勸阻的詞，常見寫法為「咪」，用在動詞前表示不要做某事。例如「你咪咁嘈」。字形「劘」較罕見或作異體字。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese prohibitive particle meaning 'don't' or 'do not'. Commonly written as "咪" and placed before verbs to tell someone not to do something (e.g. "你咪咁嘈"). The character "劘" is rare and sometimes appears as an alternate form.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咪咁嘈啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 mai1 gam2 cou3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別這麼吵了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so noisy.

mandarin_meaning: 不確定（可能為罕見方言詞或錯別字），字面為「力＋藷（薯，甘藷）」；在主流詞典與語料中無可靠記載，可能是小圈子俚語或綽號用法
english_meaning: Uncertain/obscure (possibly a rare regional slang or a typo). Literally "force + sweet potato"; not attested in standard references and likely a niche slang or nickname
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語/不確定（可能作名詞或綽號）
partOfSpeech_english: slang / uncertain (likely a noun or nickname)
explanation_mandarin: 「力藷」在公開的粵語詞典與語料庫中沒有穩定詞條。單字「藷」為薯（甘藷、番薯）的異體字；合成詞可能是某些社群的俚語、綽號或打字錯誤。具體含義需視使用語境判斷，故建議在遇到此詞時向說話者求證來源或解釋。
explanation_english: “力藷” is not attested in major Cantonese references. The character 藷 is a variant of 薯 (sweet potato). The compound may be a community-specific slang term, a nickname, or a misspelling. Its exact meaning depends on context, so ask the speaker for clarification when encountered.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日自稱力藷，但大家都唔清楚佢想講乜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zi6 cing1 lik6 syu4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 cing1 co2 keoi5 soeng2 gong2 mat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常自称“力藷”，但大家都不清楚他想表达什么。
examples.english_sentence: He often calls himself "力藷", but nobody is clear what he means.

mandarin_meaning: 煽動、添枝加葉、誇大或渲染事件
english_meaning: to hype up, exaggerate, or fan the flames (of a story or rumor)
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語俗語，指對事情添油加醋、誇大其詞或刻意渲染以吸引注意或製造話題。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term meaning to exaggerate, add sensational details, or deliberately hype or stir up a story or rumor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再加風啦，事實根本唔係咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gaa1 fung1 laa1, si6 sat6 gan1 bun2 m4 hai6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再添枝加葉了，事實根本不是這樣。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep hyping it up; the facts aren't like that.

mandarin_meaning: 非常厉害／好到不行（口语）
english_meaning: extremely impressive/awesome; insanely good or powerful (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「劲到爆」是粤语口语，表示某事或某人非常厉害、强劲或好到极点，带有夸张和感叹的语气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang intensifier meaning something is extremely powerful, impressive, or awesome. It conveys exaggerated praise or strong emphasis.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢首歌勁到爆！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 sau2 go1 ging6 dou3 baau3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这首歌好到爆！
examples.english_sentence: This song is insanely awesome!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打機嘅技術勁到爆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 gei1 ge3 gei6 seot6 ging6 dou3 baau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他打游戏的技术好到爆。
examples.english_sentence: His gaming skills are crazy good.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試成績勁到爆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 sing4 zik1 ging6 dou3 baau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次考试成绩好到爆。
examples.english_sentence: This exam result is unbelievably good.

mandarin_meaning: 形势凶险、被夹击或处于被四面围攻的危险局面
english_meaning: in a dire, dangerous situation; hemmed in and under attack from multiple sides
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容局勢非常危險或處於被夾擊、四面受敵的困境，帶有口語或俗語色彩。
explanation_english: Describes a very dangerous or precarious situation where one is being squeezed or attacked from multiple sides; colloquial/idiomatic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個生意做唔掂，債主成日上門追數，供應商又停貨，依家真係勢凶夹狼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 saang1 ji3 zou6 m4 dim6, zai3 zyu2 sing4 jat6 soeng5 mun4 zeoi1 sou3, gung1 jing3 soeng1 jau6 ting4 fo3, ji1 gaa1 zan1 hai6 sai3 hung1 gaap3 long4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的生意做不下去，债主天天上门催债，供应商也停供，现在真是形势凶险、被夹击。
examples.english_sentence: His business is failing; creditors keep coming to demand repayment and suppliers have stopped delivering — now he's really in a dire, hemmed-in situation.

mandarin_meaning: 棒、很厲害（口語）
english_meaning: awesome; great; (colloquially) better/outstanding
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感嘆詞 / 形容詞（口語）
explanation_mandarin: 「勝嘅」為廣東話口語用法，常用來稱讚或強調某事物比其他更好或更出色，與「勝嘢」或「好勁」意思相近。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to praise or emphasize that something is better or outstanding. Similar in use to 'awesome' or 'that's great.' Often a variant of '勝嘢.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次嘅表現真係勝嘅！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 ge3 biu2 jin2 zan1 hai6 sing3 ge3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次的表现真是棒极了！
examples.english_sentence: This performance was really awesome!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你整嘅蛋糕好好味，勝嘅！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zing2 ge3 daan6 gou1 hou2 hou2 mei6, sing3 ge3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做的蛋糕很好吃，真棒！
examples.english_sentence: The cake you made is delicious — awesome!

mandarin_meaning: 麻烦你了；辛苦你了
english_meaning: Sorry to trouble you / Thanks for your trouble
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的客套用語，常用於請求別人幫忙或在別人幫忙後表示歉意或感謝，語氣較禮貌且帶有敬意。
explanation_english: A Cantonese polite expression used when asking someone for help or to acknowledge/thank someone for the trouble they have taken. It conveys politeness and mild deference.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 勞煩晒你幫我遞份文件畀上司。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou4 faan4 saai3 nei5 bong1 ngo5 dai6 fan6 man4 gin2 bei2 soeng6 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 麻烦你把这份文件递交给上司。
examples.english_sentence: Sorry to trouble you to hand this document to the boss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 明天下午要搬嘢，勞煩晒大家幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ming4 tin1 haa6 ng5 jiu3 bun1 je5, lou4 faan4 saai3 daai6 gaa1 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天下午要搬东西，麻烦大家帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: We're moving things tomorrow afternoon — sorry to trouble everyone for help.

mandarin_meaning: 沒得說/沒得講；沒有討論或商量的餘地，已成定局
english_meaning: there's nothing to be said / no room for discussion or negotiation; it's inevitable or pointless to argue
explanation_mandarin: 用於口語，表示事情已成定局或沒有討論、商量的餘地，通常帶有無可改變或無意義再爭論的含義。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression indicating there is no room for discussion or negotiation — something is already decided or it's pointless to argue further.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢已經走咗，依家再講都勢冇話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5 ging1 zau2 zo2, ji1 gaa1 zoi3 gong2 dou1 sai3 mou5 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他已經走了，現在再說也沒得說/沒意義。
examples.english_sentence: He's already gone; it's pointless to talk about it now.

mandarin_meaning: 形勢凶險、兇狠有威脅性（口語說法）
english_meaning: ominous and menacing; dangerously fierce or aggressive (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語或俚語，用來形容人或情況看起來很凶狠、有威脅性、危險，帶有比喻性的「像狼一樣兇」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression describing a person or situation as menacing, fierce, or dangerously threatening — metaphorically like a wolf.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次佢出手好猛，勢凶夾狼，唔好同佢撈上嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 keoi5 ceot1 sau2 hou2 mung5, sai3 hung1 gaap3 long4, m4 hou2 tung4 keoi5 laau1 soeng5 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次他出手很猛，勢凶夾狼，別和他扯上關係。
examples.english_sentence: He came at us really aggressively — ominous and ferocious; don't get involved with him.

mandarin_meaning: 裝作有藝術感／裝腔作勢（刻意擺出很有型或很有藝術感的樣子）
english_meaning: pretentious artyness; putting on airs to appear artistic or stylish
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，用來形容某人故意擺出很有藝術感或很有型的樣子，帶有做作或賣弄的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial slang term describing affected behavior where someone deliberately poses as arty or stylish; implies pretentiousness or showing off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺IG度擺出啲好勢藝嘅相，睇落好做作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 IG dou6 baai2 ceot1 di1 hou2 sai3 ngai6 ge3 soeng2, tai2 lok6 hou2 zou6 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她總是在IG上擺出很有「勢藝」的照片，看起來很做作。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is always posting very 'artsy-pretentious' photos on IG; it comes off as very affected.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁勢藝啦，做返自己就得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam3 sai3 ngai6 laa1, zou6 faan1 zi6 gei2 zau6 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別那麼裝腔作勢，做回自己就行了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so pretentious/arty — just be yourself.

mandarin_meaning: 均勻；分布或質地平滑一致（較文言或少見）
english_meaning: even; uniform; evenly distributed (literary/rare)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞/副詞（描述分佈或質地）
explanation_mandarin: 表示事物分佈、質地或狀態均勻、一致。此詞在廣東話或文獻中較少見，可理解為「均勻」的近義詞。
explanation_english: Indicates that something is even or uniform in distribution or texture. This term is relatively rare/literary in Cantonese and functions similarly to '均勻' (even).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個蛋糕嘅質地好勻洵，入口好綿密。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 daan6 gou1 ge3 zat1 dei6 hou2 wan4 seon4, jap6 hau2 hou2 min4 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個蛋糕的質地很均勻，入口很綿密。
examples.english_sentence: The texture of this cake is very even and it melts in the mouth.

mandarin_meaning: 勾引年长者；搭讪（通常指对年纪较大的人示好或引诱）
english_meaning: to hit on / seduce (typically an older person); to flirt with
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，指向年紀較大的人示好、搭訕或引誘，屬非正式或俚語用法，語氣可帶貶義。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang verb meaning to hit on, flirt with, or seduce someone (often an older person). Informal and can carry a negative or teasing tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺酒吧勾老啲年長嘅客人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 zau2 baa1 gou1 lou5 di1 nin4 coeng4 ge3 haak3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常在酒吧勾引年長的客人。
examples.english_sentence: He often hits on older customers at the bar.

mandarin_meaning: 包台 / 包桌（預訂並包下整張桌子，通常需付費或點餐以確保獨佔）
english_meaning: to book or buy out a table (reserve a table exclusively, often by paying or ordering enough to occupy it)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，指預訂並包下整張桌子或包場位置，常見於餐廳、夜店或卡拉OK，暗含需付費或點夠數量以確保獨佔使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to reserve and effectively buy out a table (or area) for exclusive use, commonly used in restaurants, clubs or KTV; often implies paying or ordering enough to secure the table.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋包咗檯，唔使擔心冇位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 baau1 zo2 toi4, m4 sai2 daam1 sam1 mou5 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我们包了桌，不用担心没有位子。
examples.english_sentence: We booked a table for tonight, so no need to worry about not having a seat.

mandarin_meaning: 一包米 / 一袋米
english_meaning: a bag of rice
explanation_mandarin: 指包裝好的一包米，通常指購買或儲存用的米袋。
explanation_english: Refers to a packaged bag of rice, typically the unit purchased or stored for household use.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗一包米，夠我哋屋企用一個月。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 jat1 baau1 mai5, gau3 ngo5 dei6 uk1 kei2 jung6 jat1 go3 jyut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我買了一包米，夠我們家用一個月。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a bag of rice; it'll last our household for a month.

jyutping: bou1 cing1 tin1 dyun6 on3, mou5 dak1 king1
mandarin_meaning: 包青天斷案，沒得商量（決定已定，不能再討論）
english_meaning: The decision is final; no room for discussion (lit. 'Judge Bao decides the case, no arguing')
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示事情已經有最終決定，不能再協商或改變，帶有強調結論不可挑戰的語氣。引用包青天（公正的代名詞）來強調判定的權威性。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that a decision is final and not open to further negotiation; it emphasizes that the verdict is authoritative and cannot be contested, invoking Judge Bao (a symbol of fairness) for authority.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢已經決定唔返轉頭，包青天斷案，冇得傾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5 ging1 kyut3 ding6 m4 faan1 zyun2 tau4, bou1 cing1 tin1 dyun6 on3, mou5 dak1 king1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他已經决定不會改變，包青天斷案，沒得商量。
examples.english_sentence: He's already decided not to change his mind — the decision is final; there's no discussion.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）把脖子包住；（口語/俚語）讓某人承擔責任或代人頂罪、把麻煩推給別人
english_meaning: (literal) to wrap someone's neck; (slang) to make someone take the blame or shoulder someone else's trouble/responsibility
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞（口語/俚語，也有字面用法）
explanation_mandarin: 口語中常用來形容把責任、過失或麻煩全部推給某人，讓他替他人承擔（類似“頂罪”）。也可作字面意思，指把東西包住頸部。
explanation_english: In colloquial use it usually means to pin responsibility or blame onto someone else (similar to 'make someone take the fall'). Literally it can mean to wrap or cover someone's neck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司出事，老闆想搵人包頂頸，唔好畀佢呃到你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ceot1 si6, lou5 baan2 soeng2 wan2 jan4 baau1 ding2 geng2, m4 hou2 bei2 keoi5 ngaau4 dou3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司出事，老板想找人包顶颈（顶罪），别让他骗到你。
examples.english_sentence: The company ran into trouble; the boss wants to find someone to take the fall. Don't let him trick you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔想俾人包頂頸，所以唔肯做替罪羔羊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 baau1 ding2 geng2, so2 ji5 m4 hang2 zou6 tai3 zeoi6 gou1 joeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不想被人包顶颈，所以不肯做替罪羔羊。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't want to be made to take the blame, so he refuses to be the scapegoat.

mandarin_meaning: 化化聲（擬聲詞）：表示輕微碎裂、摩擦或低聲嘀咕的聲音，也可用來形容東西很快碎散或聲音細小模糊。
english_meaning: An onomatopoeic Cantonese term representing a soft crumbling/rustling or muttering sound; can be used literally for things that crumble/make faint cracking noises or figuratively for someone muttering indistinctly.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 擬聲詞（可做狀聲/副詞用）
partOfSpeech_english: Onomatopoeia (used adverbially or as a descriptive sound word)
explanation_mandarin: 「化化聲」常用作擬聲詞，模仿細碎崩裂、脆響或低聲嘀咕的聲音。可用來描述食物、紙張等被咬或弄碎時發出的細碎聲，或形容人低聲喃喃、自言自語的聲音。
explanation_english: “化化聲” is an onomatopoeic Cantonese expression imitating a soft crumbling/crackling or murmuring sound. It describes faint brittle noises (e.g., crispy food, crumbling paper) or the sound of someone muttering under their breath.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢塊餅乾好脆，一啖咬落去就化化聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 faai3 beng2 gon1 hou2 ceoi3, jat1 daam2 ngaau5 lok6 heoi3 zau6 faa3 faa3 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這塊餅乾很脆，一口咬下去就發出化化聲。
examples.english_sentence: This biscuit is so crispy — it goes 'hua-hua' (a crumbling crackle) when you bite it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺廚房度化化聲講嘢，我聽唔清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ceoi4 fong2 dou6 faa3 faa3 seng1 gong2 je5, ngo5 teng1 m4 cing1 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在廚房裡化化聲地說話，我聽不清楚。
examples.english_sentence: He was muttering in the kitchen; I couldn't make out what he was saying.

mandarin_meaning: 花花公子；善於勾引或追求異性的男子（俚語）
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang term for a womanizer/Casanova — a man skilled at seducing or charming women.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面意義為「化骨龍」，用來形容在情場上非常擅長追求或勾引女性的人，含貶義或玩笑意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression (literally 'bone-melting dragon') used to describe a man who is very adept at courting or seducing women; often carries a joking or pejorative tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日換女朋友，真係個化骨龍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 wun6 neoi5 pang4 jau5, zan1 hai6 go3 waa6 gwat1 lung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常換女朋友，真是個花花公子。
examples.english_sentence: He frequently changes girlfriends; he's really a womanizer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小心啲，佢係化骨龍，唔好輕信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 sam1 di1, keoi5 hai6 waa6 gwat1 lung4, m4 hou2 hing1 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小心一點，他是化骨龍，不要輕信他。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful; he's a womanizer — don't trust him easily.

mandarin_meaning: （被）露出破绽了／露餡了
english_meaning: You've been exposed; a flaw/loophole has been revealed.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語俚語／短語（感嘆/動詞片語）
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，常用「北」代替「被」來表示某人的秘密、錯誤或系統的漏洞被發現或被揭穿。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression meaning someone’s mistake, secret, or a system loophole has been exposed. Note: here the character 北 is used informally to represent the passive marker ('been').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲證據有問題，依家北漏洞喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 zing3 geoi3 jau5 man6 tai4, ji4 gaa1 bei6 lau6 dung6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的證據有問題，現在露出破綻了。
examples.english_sentence: His evidence is flawed — now the loophole has been exposed.

mandarin_meaning: 來自北方的冷風；常指在轉暖期間或暖流過後仍然出現或殘留的一股寒意（殘留的北風吹來的寒意）
english_meaning: A northerly cold wind or a lingering cold snap from the north — a late/lingering chill often occurring at the end of winter or after a warm spell.
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，指由北方吹來的冷風或殘留的寒流，常用來形容在回暖期間仍突然出現或殘留的寒冷天氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial term for a cold northerly wind or lingering cold snap. Used to describe a sudden or remaining chill from the north, often felt when temperatures should be warming up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家話返暖，但今日朝早仲有北風尾，好凍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 waa6 faan1 nyun5, daan6 gam1 jat6 ziu1 zou2 zung6 jau5 bak1 fung1 mei5, hou2 dung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在說回暖，但今天早上還有北風吹來的寒意，很冷。
examples.english_sentence: They say it's getting warmer, but there's still a northerly chill this morning — it's cold.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出街記得著多件衫，夜晚可能會有北風尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 gaai1 gei3 dak1 zoek3 do1 gin6 saam1, je6 maan5 ho2 nang4 wui5 jau5 bak1 fung1 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出門記得多穿一件，晚上可能會有北風吹來的寒意。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to wear an extra layer when you go out — there might be a northerly chill tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：白色的匙羹（勺子）
english_meaning: Literal: white spoon (a spoon that is white, often porcelain or plastic)
explanation_mandarin: 「匙羹白」字面意思是「白色的匙羹」。此詞在現代粵語中較罕見或帶方言/口語色彩，主要以字面用法出現，並無普遍固定的比喻義或常見俚語用法。
explanation_english: Literally 'white spoon'. This expression is rare in modern Cantonese and is primarily used literally to refer to a white spoon (often porcelain or plastic). It is not a common idiom or slang with a widely recognized figurative meaning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老一輩有時會講「匙羹白」，其實係指白色嘅匙羹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jat1 bui3 jau5 si4 wui5 gong2 "si4 gang1 baak6", kei4 sat6 hai6 zi2 baak6 sik1 ge3 si4 gang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老一辈有时会说“匙羹白”，其实是指白色的匙羹。
examples.english_sentence: The older generation sometimes say '匙羹白', which actually refers to a white spoon.

mandarin_meaning: 匙羹／持羹：勺子、汤匙（多用于古文、方言或書面語）
english_meaning: spoon; ladle (especially for soup) — an older or dialectal term for a spoon
explanation_mandarin: 「匙羹」字面上指盛湯用的勺子，在廣東話及古文、方言中可見此用法。括號內的「持」為同音變體或誤寫情況，實際語義仍為「勺子／湯匙」。此詞較偏書面或古雅，現代口語常用「湯匙」「勺子」。
explanation_english: Literally refers to the spoon or ladle used for soup. The form appears in Cantonese and older/written Chinese; the character 持 in parentheses represents a variant or alternative character with the same pronunciation, but the meaning remains 'spoon'. This term is somewhat archaic or dialectal — modern speech typically uses tong1 ci4 (湯匙) or 'spoon'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好用手拎湯，攞匙羹食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jung6 sau2 ling1 tong1, lo2 ci4 gang1 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要用手拿汤，拿勺子吃吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't use your hands to scoop the soup; use a spoon to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 匚 (fāng) — 漢字的部首之一，表示箱、匣的形狀或容器的概念。
english_meaning: The radical '匚' — a Chinese character component meaning a box or container; used as a character radical.
explanation_mandarin: 匚本身少單獨作字使用，常作為漢字的部首，表示與箱、匣或容器相關的字形或意義。
explanation_english: 匚 is rarely used alone as a character; it commonly appears as a radical in Chinese characters, indicating shapes or meanings related to boxes, chests, or containers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 匚係漢字嘅部首，通常表示箱匣嘅形狀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fong1 hai6 hon3 zi6 ge3 bou6 sau2, tung1 soeng4 biu2 si6 soeng1 hap6 ge3 jing4 zong6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 匚是漢字的部首，通常表示箱匣的形狀。
examples.english_sentence: 匚 is a Chinese character radical, usually denoting the shape of a box or chest.

mandarin_meaning: 工匠的工作臺；用來加工或放置材料的臺子（如木匠的工作台）
english_meaning: a craftsman's workbench; a bench or table used by a tradesperson for working on materials
explanation_mandarin: 指工匠在作坊中用來加工、固定或休息的臺子或床臺，常見於木工或其他手工藝行業，也可泛指工作台。
explanation_english: Refers to the bench or table a craftsman uses in a workshop to work on, fix, or rest materials. Common in carpentry and other manual trades; can also be used more generally for a workbench.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺匠牀度整木櫃，好熟練。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 zoeng6 coeng4 dou6 zing2 muk6 gwai6, hou2 suk6 lin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在匠床上做木柜，很熟练。
examples.english_sentence: He is making a wooden cabinet at the workbench; very skilled.

jyutping: ji1 dak1 tau4 lai4 goek3 cau1 gan1
mandarin_meaning: 治好了頭，腳卻抽筋（比喻治標不治本或一處糾正反而引起其他問題）
english_meaning: Literally 'cure the head and the legs cramp' — an idiom meaning a remedy that fixes one problem but causes another / treating symptoms rather than the root cause
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容處理問題或治療時表面上解決了某個部分，卻引起其他問題；常用來批評做法不當、治標不治本或有副作用。
explanation_english: Used to describe a situation where handling or treating a problem seemingly fixes one aspect but creates another problem; often used to criticize improper solutions that treat symptoms rather than root causes or produce side effects.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司搞啲短期措施，醫得頭嚟腳抽筋，最後反而出事更多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gaau2 di1 dyun2 kei4 cou3 sik1, ji1 dak1 tau4 lai4 goek3 cau1 gan1, zeoi3 hau6 faan2 ji4 ceot1 si6 gang1 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司採取了一些短期措施，治好了頭卻讓腳抽筋，最後反而出現更多問題。
examples.english_sentence: The company implemented short-term measures that fixed one thing but caused other problems; in the end, even more issues came up.

mandarin_meaning: 表示數量109,007（十万九千七）
english_meaning: the cardinal number 109,007
explanation_mandarin: 一個基數詞，用來表示數量或金額，數值為一零九千零七（109,007）。在粵語口語中可直接用於報價、計算等情況。
explanation_english: A cardinal number used to indicate the quantity 109,007. Commonly used in Cantonese to state amounts, prices, counts, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部車賣緊要十萬九千七蚊，真係唔平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 ce1 maai6 gan2 jiu3 sap6 maan6 gau2 cin1 cat1 man1, zan1 hai6 m4 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这辆车要卖十万九千七块，真是不便宜。
examples.english_sentence: This car is being sold for $109,007 — it's really not cheap.

mandarin_meaning: 有點奇怪、離譜或傻
english_meaning: odd/weird; ridiculous; a bit crazy
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話俗語，用來形容行為、想法或說話很奇怪、離譜或有點瘋癲。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression used to describe actions, ideas, or remarks that are odd, ridiculous, or a bit crazy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日咁做真係十三点。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 gam2 zou6 zan1 hai6 sap6 saam1 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天這樣做真是有點離譜。
examples.english_sentence: What you did today is really kind of ridiculous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲主意聽落好十三点，唔會得㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 zyu2 ji3 teng1 lok6 hou2 sap6 saam1 dim2, m4 wui5 dak1 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的那些主意聽起來很離譜，行不通的。
examples.english_sentence: His ideas sound pretty crazy; they won't work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔明點解佢會做出咁十三点嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 ming4 dim2 gaai2 keoi5 wui5 zou6 ceot1 gam2 sap6 saam1 dim2 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不明白他為何會做出這麼離譜/奇怪的事。
examples.english_sentence: I don't understand why he'd do something so weird.

jyutping: sap6 saam1 dim2 zung1, seng1 daai6 gaap3 ok3
mandarin_meaning: （俚語）又大聲又惡劣／很囂張討人厭
english_meaning: A slang phrase describing someone who is very loud and unpleasant/aggressive
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語、俚語（形容詞片語／評價性短語）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的俚語，用來形容一個人態度很差、說話又大聲又討厭，帶有貶義。“十三点钟”在此作強調語氣，表示程度很厲害。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used to describe someone with a bad attitude who speaks loudly and is obnoxious or mean. 'Thirteen o'clock' here is an emphatic colloquial intensifier, indicating a high degree. The phrase is derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日見到佢就十三点钟，聲大夾惡，真係唔想理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 gin3 dou3 keoi5 zau6 sap6 saam1 dim2 zung1, seng1 daai6 gaap3 ok3, zan1 hai6 m4 soeng2 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 每次看到他就是又大聲又惡劣，真不想理他。
examples.english_sentence: Every time I see him he's loud and nasty; I really don't want to deal with him.

jyutping: sap6 go3 neoi5 gau2 go3 zaak6
mandarin_meaning: 十个女人九个贼（俗语），含有贬义，指大多数女人不可靠或虚伪。
english_meaning: “Of ten women, nine are thieves” — a derogatory proverb implying that most women are untrustworthy or deceitful.
explanation_mandarin: 这句粤语俗语用夸张的方式表达对女性的不信任或蔑视，带有性别偏见和贬义，常用于非正式对话中评价女性的品行或忠诚度。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb that exaggerates to express distrust or contempt toward women, implying most are deceitful. It is misogynistic and derogatory, used in informal speech to criticize women's trustworthiness or fidelity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強成日講「十个女九个贼」，我覺得好有性別歧視。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 sing4 jat6 gong2 'sap6 go3 neoi5 gau2 go3 zaak6', ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 jau5 sing3 bit6 kei4 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强老是说“十个女九个贼”，我觉得很有性别歧视。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Keung keeps saying "of ten women, nine are thieves" — I think it's very sexist.

cantonese: 十个瓦罉九个盖，𢫏嚟𢫏去𢫏唔冚
jyutping: sap6 go3 ngaa4 gong1 gau2 go3 goi3, jaap6 lai4 jaap6 heoi3 jaap6 m4 ham2
mandarin_meaning: 大家各執己見、互相推諉，事情來回拖延、無法解決
english_meaning: Everyone insists on their own view and keeps passing the matter around; things are shuffled back and forth and never get resolved.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容多數人各有主張，互相推諉或爭論，事情一直來回拖延，無法定案或解決。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing a situation where many people insist on their own positions, pass responsibility or argue back and forth, and the issue never gets settled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次計劃討論到最後都未決定，十个瓦罉九个盖，𢫏嚟𢫏去𢫏唔冚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 gai3 waak6 tou2 leon6 dou3 zeoi3 hau6 dou1 mei6 kyut3 ding6, sap6 go3 ngaa4 gong1 gau2 go3 goi3, jaap6 lai4 jaap6 heoi3 jaap6 m4 ham2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次计划讨论到最后都没有决定，大家各持己见，推来推去，问题解决不了。
examples.english_sentence: This time the plan discussion ended without a decision — everyone stuck to their own views, pushing things back and forth and nothing gets settled.

cantonese: 十二月雷公叫，有谷冇处粜
jyutping: sap6 ji6 jyut6 leoi4 gung1 giu3, jau5 guk1 mou5 cyu3 tiu3
mandarin_meaning: 十二月打雷，穀物豐收但無處可賣（市面供過於求）
english_meaning: If thunder sounds in December, there will be a bumper harvest but nowhere to sell it (market glut)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗諺。字面意思是十二月打雷預示五穀豐收，但因為人人都有收成，市場供過於求，反而難以賣出好價錢。引申指某事造成大量產出或普遍擁有，導致價值下降或無利可圖。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folk proverb. Literally, thunder in December signals a plentiful grain harvest, but because everyone harvests, there is nowhere to sell it — a market glut. Figuratively used when abundance leads to oversupply and diminished value or opportunity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年村入面啲農民收成咁好，真係十二月雷公叫，有谷冇处粜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 cyun1 jap6 min6 di1 nung4 man4 sau1 sing4 gam2 hou2, zan1 hai6 sap6 ji6 jyut6 leoi4 gung1 giu3, jau5 guk1 mou5 cyu3 tiu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年村裡的農民收成這麼好，真是「十二月打雷，有谷沒地方賣」。
examples.english_sentence: The farmers in the village had such a good harvest this year — it's really 'if thunder sounds in December, there will be grain but nowhere to sell'.

jyutping: sap6 ji6 dim2 bun3 zung1, zi2 tin1 duk1 dei6
mandarin_meaning: 夸张地做出指点或擺架子的姿態，像要指挥天地（用來形容言行誇張、氣焰囂張或愛指點別人）
english_meaning: To make exaggerated, grandiose gestures and act imperiously — literally 'twelve thirty, pointing at heaven and overseeing earth'; used to describe showing off, bossing others, or making a big fuss.
explanation_mandarin: 「十二点半钟，指天督地」是廣東口語表達，形容一個人言行誇張、動作誇大、擺出一副氣焰很高或好像要指揮天地的樣子。多帶貶義，可用來說某人愛裝腔作勢或愛指手畫腳。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone who behaves exaggeratedly and imperiously, making grand gestures as if directing heaven and earth. Often derogatory; used to label boastful, showy, or bossy behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢飲醉咗，喺街度大嗌大叫，仲指住天鬧人，真係十二點半鐘，指天督地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jam2 zeoi3 zo2, hai2 gaai1 dou6 daai6 aai3 daai6 giu3, zung6 zi2 zyu6 tin1 nou6 jan4, zan1 hai6 sap6 ji6 dim2 bun3 zung1, zi2 tin1 duk1 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他醉了，在街上又叫又嚷，還指着天罵人，真是「十二点半钟，指天督地」。
examples.english_sentence: He was drunk, shouting in the street and pointing at the sky while berating people — really acting like 'twelve thirty, pointing at heaven and overseeing earth' (i.e., making exaggerated, bossy gestures).

mandarin_meaning: 十個人中有九個；大多數人
english_meaning: Nine out of ten people; the vast majority
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語／成語（口語化的說法）
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示某種情況或特徵在大多數人中很普遍，類似「十之八九」、「大多數人」的意思。屬於俗語或成語性質的表達，用來概括性地描述普遍現象。
explanation_english: A colloquial proverb used to indicate that a certain trait or situation is very common — literally 'nine out of ten people.' Similar in meaning to 'most people' or 'nine times out of ten.' Often used to generalize about common behaviors, opinions, or outcomes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講到食嘢，我哋屋企十人生九品都鍾意食辣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 dou3 sik6 je5, ngo5 dei6 uk1 kei2 sap6 jan4 saang1 gau2 ban2 dou1 zung1 ji3 sik6 laat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 說到吃東西，我們家十個人中有九個喜歡吃辣。
examples.english_sentence: When it comes to food, nine out of ten people in our family like spicy food.

cantonese: 十几人分食一分烟，无厘瘾头
jyutping: sap6 gei2 jan4 fan1 sik6 jat1 fan1 jin1, mou4 lei4 jan2 tau4
mandarin_meaning: 字面：十几个人分着一根烟；引申：形容非常小气、抠门，或形容一件事荒谬、没意思、毫无吸引力。
english_meaning: Literally 'more than ten people share one cigarette.' Figuratively used to call someone extremely stingy/petty, or to describe something as absurd and unappealing (no fun/no appeal).
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俚语。前半句字面描绘多人共用极少的东西，常用来形容人很小气或吝啬；“无厘瘾头”带有“没有趣味/没有吸引力、荒谬”的意思。语气通常带贬义，用于日常评价。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase. The first half literally depicts many people sharing a tiny thing (a cigarette) and is used to criticise someone as very stingy; the '無厘瘾头' part implies something is nonsensical or has no appeal. It is derogatory and used informally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日計較，十几人分食一分烟，無厘瘾头，大家都唔鍾意同佢一齊出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gai3 gaau3, sap6 gei2 jan4 fan1 sik6 jat1 fan1 jin1, mou4 lei4 jan2 tau4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3 tung4 keoi5 jat1 cai4 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是斤斤计较，十几个人分着一根烟，真是又小气又没意思，大家都不愿意和他一起出去。
examples.english_sentence: He's always so petty — more than ten people sharing one cigarette; it's stingy and no fun, so no one wants to go out with him.

jyutping: sap6 zi6 mei6 jau5 jat1 waak6
mandarin_meaning: 完全沒有經驗／一無所知（口語）
english_meaning: completely inexperienced; not having even the slightest experience or trace of knowledge
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，用來形容一個人對某事毫無經驗或一點也不懂，強調連「一畫」都沒有，等同於「一無所知」或「毫無經驗」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe someone who is completely inexperienced or knows nothing about something, emphasizing they don't even have 'a single stroke'—equivalent to 'totally clueless' or 'no experience at all.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢冇經驗，十字未有一画，點夠資格做呢份工？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 mou5 ging1 jim6, sap6 zi6 mei6 jau5 jat1 waak6, dim2 gau3 zi1 gaak3 zou6 ni1 fan6 gung1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事沒有經驗，完全一無所知，怎麼有資格做這份工作？
examples.english_sentence: He has no work experience at all—completely inexperienced—how can he be qualified for this job?

cantonese: 十字街心跑馬，頭頭是道
jyutping: sap6 zi6 gaai1 sam1 paau2 maa5, tau4 tau4 si6 dou6
mandarin_meaning: 說話條理清楚、滔滔不絕且有板有眼
english_meaning: to speak fluently and coherently, in a confident and authoritative manner
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，用來形容一個人說話有條理、說得有根有據、像專家一樣滔滔不絕。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial idiom describing someone who speaks in an organized, confident, and authoritative way—as if they know what they're talking about.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好有條理，十字街心跑馬，頭頭是道，大家都信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 jau5 tiu4 lei5, sap6 zi6 gaai1 sam1 paau2 maa5, tau4 tau4 si6 dou6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話很有條理，十字街心跑馬，頭頭是道，大家都相信他。
examples.english_sentence: He speaks very coherently and authoritatively; everyone trusts him.

mandarin_meaning: 十月非常炎热／热得要命
english_meaning: It's unbearably hot in October; 'October heat is killing (me)' (colloquial exaggeration)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，用來形容即使已到十月（秋季）天氣仍然非常炎熱，帶有誇張和抱怨語氣，常見於香港或廣東地區的日常對話。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/exclamatory phrase used to describe unexpectedly or uncomfortably hot weather in October (autumn). It's an exaggerated complaint common in Hong Kong and Guangdong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家已經十月，天氣仲咁熱，真係十月火歸天！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 ji5 ging1 sap6 jyut6, tin1 hei3 zung6 gam2 jit6, zan1 hai6 sap6 jyut6 fo2 gwai1 tin1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在已经十月了，天气还这么热，真是十月火归天！
examples.english_sentence: It's already October and it's still this hot — it's really unbearably hot in October!

cantonese: 十月火归脏，唔离芥菜汤
jyutping: sap6 jyut6 fo2 gwai1 zong6, m4 lei4 gai3 coi3 tong1
mandarin_meaning: （粤语俗语）入十月（入冬）要注意养生，常喝芥菜汤以护脏腑和抵御寒气。
english_meaning: A Cantonese folk saying advising that when October / the start of winter arrives one should drink mustard-green (芥菜) soup to protect the internal organs and keep healthy.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話是廣東話的民間養生諺語。十月入冬，人體脏腑容易受寒或有內熱、消化不適等，民間流行以芥菜湯等熱湯調理身體，因此有「十月火归脏，唔离芥菜汤」的說法，強調冬季飲湯補養。
explanation_english: This is a Cantonese folk health proverb. When October (the start of winter) comes, people believe the internal organs are more vulnerable to imbalance; traditionally mustard-green soup (and other warming soups) are recommended to nourish and protect the body, so the saying emphasizes drinking such soup in the cold season.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿嬸成日講：十月火归脏，唔离芥菜汤，天冷就要飲返碗暖湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 sam2 seng4 jat6 gong2: sap6 jyut6 fo2 gwai1 zong6, m4 lei4 gai3 coi3 tong1, tin1 laang5 zau6 jiu3 jam2 faan1 wun2 nyun5 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿姨常說：十月一到，身体要注意，少不了芥菜汤，天冷時要喝一碗熱湯。
examples.english_sentence: Auntie often says: 'When October comes, you should take care of your health — you can't go without mustard-green soup; when it's cold, have a hot bowl of soup.'

jyutping: sap6 jyut6 gaai3 coi3, hei2 sam1
mandarin_meaning: 字面：十月的芥菜；引申：在某個時節或條件成熟時開始萌生念頭或打算（開始有想做某事的念頭）
english_meaning: Literally 'October mustard greens, get a mind' — figuratively, to begin to have an idea or urge; to start planning or getting the notion to do something when the time/conditions are right.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，通常用來形容人在某個時節或機會來臨時，開始有念頭或打算去做某件事，帶有開始萌動想法的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial proverb used to describe someone beginning to have ideas or the urge to do something when the season or circumstances are right; it conveys the notion of thoughts or plans starting to emerge.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強最近十月芥菜，起心想創業，成日諗生意點做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 zeoi3 gan6 sap6 jyut6 gaai3 coi3, hei2 sam1 soeng2 cong3 jip6, sing4 jat6 nam2 saang1 ji3 dim2 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强最近十月芥菜，起心想创业，经常想生意怎么做。
examples.english_sentence: Keung has recently been getting the idea of starting a business; he's always thinking about how to run it.

jyutping: sap6 jyut6 gaau1 seon2, hak1 sam1
mandarin_meaning: 表面看起來好或客氣，但內心卻壞、兩面三刀（表裡不一）
english_meaning: Looks good or polite on the surface but is mean, two-faced, or has bad intentions underneath
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 形容詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話俗語，用來形容一個人表現得很好或很客氣，但實際上心地不好或虛偽、兩面派。字面上把特定時令的茭笋比喻為「黑心」，引申為外表與內心不一致。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang/idiom used to describe someone who appears nice or polite outwardly but is actually mean, hypocritical, or two-faced. Literally compares an October bamboo shoot as having a 'black heart', implying a hidden defect beneath a pleasant exterior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講得好客氣，但其實十月茭笋，黑心，唔可以信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 dak1 hou2 haak3 hei3, daan6 kei4 sat6 sap6 jyut6 gaau1 seon2, hak1 sam1, m4 ho2 ji5 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说话很客气，但其实表里不一、心肠很黑，不能相信他。
examples.english_sentence: He talks very politely, but in fact he's two-faced and mean — you can't trust him.

jyutping: sap6 jyut6 ze3 tau4, tim4 dou3 mei5
mandarin_meaning: 十月甘蔗從頭到尾都很甜（比喻從開始到結束都很美好/甜蜜）
english_meaning: Literally: 'sugarcane in October is sweet to the end.' Figuratively: something (often a relationship or venture) that is sweet/good from beginning to end.
explanation_mandarin: 這是粵語俗語，字面指十月採收的甘蔗從頭到尾都甜，用來形容一件事、關係或運勢從開始到結束都很順利、甜蜜或持續良好。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally saying that sugarcane harvested in October is sweet all the way through. It metaphorically describes something—often a relationship or business—that stays pleasant, successful, or affectionate from start to finish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個拍拖多年，感情一直好好，十月蔗頭，甜到尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 paak3 to1 do1 nin4, gam2 cing4 jat1 zik6 hou2 hou2, sap6 jyut6 ze3 tau4, tim4 dou3 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們兩個交往多年，感情一直很好，真是從頭甜到尾。
examples.english_sentence: They've been dating for years; their relationship has always been great—really sweet from start to finish.

mandarin_meaning: 十问九不知（大多数情况下不知道/不清楚）
english_meaning: Most of the time one won't know; very likely to be unaware or have no clue
explanation_mandarin: 表示在大多數情況下不知道或不熟悉某事，常用來形容對某件事毫無頭緒或很少人知道。
explanation_english: Indicates that in most cases people do not know or are unfamiliar with something; commonly used to say one has no clue or that most people are unaware.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事我十問九唔知，你問多兩個人先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 ngo5 sap6 man6 gau2 m4 zi1, nei5 man6 do1 loeng5 go3 jan4 sin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事我十問九不知，你還是多問幾個人吧。
examples.english_sentence: I hardly know anything about this; you'd better ask a few more people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 對於新政策，大家十問九唔知，政府要加強宣傳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: deoi3 jyu1 san1 zing3 cak1, daai6 gaa1 sap6 man6 gau2 m4 zi1, zing3 fu2 jiu3 gaa1 koeng4 syun1 cyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 對於新政策，大家十問九不知，政府要加強宣傳。
examples.english_sentence: Regarding the new policy, most people won't know about it; the government needs to step up publicity.

synonyms: 十問九不知 (普通話形式)

jyutping: sap6 zek3 sau2 zi2 maa1 maai4
mandarin_meaning: 齊心協力；大家一起合力（口語）
english_meaning: to all pitch in; everyone working together; united effort (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 形容大家把力量或人手聚在一起，齊心協力共同完成某事，常用於強調需要集體參與或協作。
explanation_english: Describes everyone combining efforts or hands together to accomplish something; used colloquially to emphasize collective participation or teamwork.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件大工程要十隻手指孖埋先得，唔可以淨係得幾個人做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 daai6 gung1cing4 jiu3 sap6 zek3 sau2 zi2 maa1 maai4 sin1 dak1, m4 ho2 ji5 zing6 hai6 dak1 gei2 go3 jan4 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這項大工程需要大家齊心協力才能完成，不能只有幾個人做。
examples.english_sentence: This big project requires everyone to work together; it can't be done by just a few people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 準備大型節目嘅時候，十隻手指孖埋好重要，唔可以靠一兩個人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeon2 bei6 daai6 jing4 zit3 muk6 ge3 si4 hau6, sap6 zek3 sau2 zi2 maa1 maai4 hou2 zung6 jiu3, m4 ho2 ji5 kaau3 jat1 loeng5 go3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 準備大型節目時，大家齊心協力很重要，不能靠一兩個人。
examples.english_sentence: When preparing a large-scale show, it's important for everyone to work together; you can't rely on just one or two people.

mandarin_meaning: 眾多的聲音；喧鬧、人聲鼎沸（口語）
english_meaning: a multitude of voices; noisy crowd; many different voices/opinions (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「千千声」是廣東話口語，字面指「成千上萬的聲音」，常用來形容場所很嘈雜、人聲眾多，或引申為有很多不同的聲音與意見。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally meaning 'thousands of voices.' It is used to describe a noisy, crowded place full of voices or, figuratively, a situation with many different voices or opinions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 遊行果日街上真係千千聲，根本聽唔到主持人講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau4 hang4 go2 jat6 gaai1 soeng6 zan1 hai6 cin1 cin1 seng1, gan1 bun2 teng1 m4 dou3 zyu2 ci4 jan4 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 遊行那天街上真的人聲鼎沸，根本聽不到主持人講話。
examples.english_sentence: That day at the march the streets were full of voices — it was so noisy you could hardly hear the host speak.

jyutping: cin1 gaan2 maan6 gaan2, gaan2 go3 laan6 dang1 zaan2
mandarin_meaning: 千挑万选，偏偏选了个破烂；明明有很多选择，却选了最差的那个。
english_meaning: After considering many options, end up choosing the worst one; to pick a dud despite many choices.
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容明明有很多选择或可能性，结果偏偏选到最差或最不合适的那个，带有无奈或责怪的语气。
explanation_english: Used to describe a situation where, despite having many choices, someone ends up choosing the worst or most unsuitable option; conveys frustration or reproach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋睇咗咁多部電話，千拣万拣，拣个烂灯盏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 tai2 zo2 gam2 do1 bou6 din6 waa2, cin1 gaan2 maan6 gaan2, gaan2 go3 laan6 dang1 zaan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们看了这么多手机，千挑万选，偏偏选了个破烂。
examples.english_sentence: We looked at so many phones, and after all that choosing we picked a dud.

mandarin_meaning: 千万不要 / 绝对不要
english_meaning: absolutely don't; for heaven's sake don't; be sure not to
explanation_mandarin: 口語中用來強烈勸阻或警告別人不要做某事，相當於「千萬不要」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to strongly advise or warn someone not to do something — equivalent to 'absolutely don't' or 'for heaven's sake don't'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 千祈唔好同佢講我哋嘅計劃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cin1 kei4 m4 hou2 tung4 keoi5 gong2 ngo5 dei6 ge3 gai3 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 千万不要跟他/她说我们的计划。
examples.english_sentence: For heaven's sake, don't tell him/her about our plan.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 千祈唔好遲返，今晚有重要會議。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cin1 kei4 m4 hou2 ci4 faan1, gam1 maan5 jau5 zung6 jiu3 wui6 ji5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 千万不要晚回，今晚有重要会议。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be late getting back — there's an important meeting tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 生气 / 发脾气
english_meaning: to get angry; to lose one's temper
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，字面是「升氣球」，用來形容人突然生氣、發脾氣或情緒激動。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally meaning "inflate a balloon," used to describe someone suddenly getting angry or losing their temper.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一見到啲問題就升氣球，講嘢好激動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 gin3 dou3 di1 man6 tai4 zau6 sing1 hei3 kau4, gong2 je5 hou2 gik1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一看到问题就生气，说话很激动。
examples.english_sentence: He gets angry as soon as he sees problems and speaks very emotionally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好挑佢嘅痛處，會令佢升氣球。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 tiu1 keoi5 ge3 tung4 co3, wui5 ling6 keoi5 sing1 hei3 kau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别去触他的痛处，会让他生气。
examples.english_sentence: Don't poke his sore spot; it'll make him get angry.

jyutping: ng5 si4 faa1 luk6 si4 bin3
mandarin_meaning: 反覆無常；見異思遷
english_meaning: fickle; changeable; inconstant
explanation_mandarin: 形容一個人性情多變或喜歡反覆，常在短時間內改變主意或感情。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is changeable or fickle—often altering their mind or affections in a short time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日午時花六時變，唔適合畀佢處理重要嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ng5 si4 faa1 luk6 si4 bin3, m4 sik1 hap6 bei2 keoi5 cyu2 lei5 zung6 jiu3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常反覆無常，不適合交給他處理重要的事情。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is always fickle and inconstant; not suitable to entrust important tasks to him/her.

mandarin_meaning: 不冷不熱；含糊、模棱兩可、態度不明顯或不熱情
english_meaning: lukewarm; indifferent; noncommittal; vague
explanation_mandarin: 「半咸淡」是廣東話口語，字面為「半鹹半淡」。常用來形容人對某事態度不熱烈、不明確或語氣、表現含糊，也可用來形容食物味道不夠重、淡而無味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "half salty, half bland." It is used to describe a lukewarm or noncommittal attitude, vague or indifferent behaviour/tone. It can also describe food that is under-seasoned or bland.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對呢件事態度半咸淡，唔肯表態。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 ni1 gin6 si6 taai3 dou6 bun3 haam4 daam6, m4 hang2 biu2 taai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對這件事態度不冷不熱，不肯表態。
examples.english_sentence: He has a lukewarm attitude toward this matter and refuses to take a stance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個湯煮得半咸淡，唔夠味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 tong1 zyu2 dak1 bun3 haam4 daam6, m4 gau3 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個湯調得有點淡，不夠味。
examples.english_sentence: This soup is a bit bland — not flavorful enough.

jyutping: bun3 je6 sik6 wong4 gwaa1, m4 zi1 tau4 mei5
mandarin_meaning: （俚語）半夜做出莫名其妙或不合時宜的事，讓人摸不着頭緒。字面含義為「半夜吃黃瓜，不知道頭尾」。
english_meaning: A slang expression meaning to do something random or inexplicable late at night; used to say something is confusing or makes no sense. Literally: "eat a cucumber at midnight, don't know head or tail."
explanation_mandarin: 此語多用於口語，帶調侃或貶義，形容某人言行莫名其妙或事情前因後果不清，讓人不明所以。有時含有粗俗或戲謔意味（「食黃瓜」在粵語亦可指手淫，視語境而定）。
explanation_english: This colloquial slang is used to mock or criticize something as inexplicable or nonsensical, implying the speaker (or action) lacks clear beginning or end. Note: in Cantonese, "食黃瓜" can also be a crude euphemism for masturbation, so the phrase can carry jokingly vulgar connotations depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺群組半夜發咗幾句奇怪嘅說話，大家都話係「半夜食黃瓜，唔知頭尾」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 kwan4 zou2 bun3 je6 faat3 zo2 gei2 geoi3 kei4 gwaai3 ge3 syut3 waa6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 hai6 'bun3 je6 sik6 wong4 gwaa1, m4 zi1 tau4 mei5'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在群組半夜發了幾句奇怪的話，大家都說是「半夜食黃瓜，唔知頭尾」。
examples.english_sentence: He posted some strange messages in the group late at night; everyone said it was so random that nobody knew what was going on.

jyutping: bun3 je6 gai1 tai4 m4 zi1 cau2
mandarin_meaning: 半夜鸡啼，不知羞（不知羞耻）
english_meaning: Utterly shameless; having no sense of shame (literally: 'rooster crows at midnight, doesn't know shame')
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，用来形容某人非常不要脸、毫无羞耻心，带有责备或讽刺意味，借“半夜鸡啼”夸张地强调对方很无耻。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to describe someone who is extremely shameless or has no sense of embarrassment. The image of a rooster crowing at midnight is used for emphasis and sarcasm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做，真係半夜鸡啼，唔知丑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 zou6, zan1 hai6 bun3 je6 gai1 tai4, m4 zi1 cau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这样做，真是半夜鸡啼，不知羞耻。
examples.english_sentence: What you're doing is really shameless.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）累得半死；拼命、差点丧命（视语境而定）
english_meaning: A colloquial expression meaning 'half a life' used to indicate extreme exhaustion ('almost dead from tiredness') or having risked/wasted a lot (to have 'put one's life on the line'), depending on context.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語，名詞性短語／慣用語
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面為“半條命”，常用來形容非常累、辛苦到像要死掉，或形容為某事付出極大代價、冒生命危險或幾乎喪命。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally 'half a life'. It commonly describes being extremely exhausted or suffering severe hardship ('almost dead from exhaustion'), and can also imply risking or sacrificing a lot (even one's life) for something, depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做呢份工，成日加班，我真係辛苦到半條命。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 ni1 fan6 gung1, sing4 jat6 gaa1 baan1, ngo5 zan1 hai6 san1 fu2 dou3 bun3 tiu4 ming6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做这份工作，经常加班，我真的累得要命／累得半死。
examples.english_sentence: With this job and constant overtime, I'm really exhausted to death.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗準備考試，我讀書讀到半條命。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 zeon2 bei6 haau2 si3, ngo5 duk6 syu1 duk6 dou3 bun3 tiu4 ming6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了准备考试，我读书读到快要累死了。
examples.english_sentence: I studied so hard to prepare for the exam that I was nearly worn out.

jyutping: bun3 tung4 seoi2, mou5 liu6 jau6 jing6 lek1
mandarin_meaning: 半桶水，沒真本事卻裝聰明
english_meaning: Half-baked; having little real ability but pretending to be clever
explanation_mandarin: 形容人知識或能力膚淺，卻愛表現或裝懂，很愛自以為是。
explanation_english: Describes someone with superficial knowledge or little real skill who nevertheless shows off or pretends to be clever.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講到好醒，其實係半桶水，冇料又認叻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 dou3 hou2 sing2, kei4 sat6 hai6 bun3 tung4 seoi2, mou5 liu6 jau6 jing6 lek1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是說得很聰明，其實是半桶水，沒真本事還裝聰明。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks like he's very smart, but he's half-baked — no real ability and just pretends to be clever.

mandarin_meaning: 半月；新月（弦月）
english_meaning: crescent moon; half moon; crescent-shaped
explanation_mandarin: 指月亮的一個階段或形狀，呈半月或新月的弧形；也可用來形容其他呈半月形或弧形的物件、疤痕等。
explanation_english: Refers to the crescent (half) shape of the moon; can also describe other objects or marks that are crescent-shaped (e.g., scars).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚見到個半邊月，好靚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 gin3 dou2 go3 bun3 bin1 jyut6, hou2 leng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚看到一弯半月，很漂亮。
examples.english_sentence: I saw a crescent moon tonight; it's beautiful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢張面有個半邊月形嘅疤，係以前打波跌傷時留下嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoeng1 min6 jau5 go3 bun3 bin1 jyut6 jing4 ge3 baa1, hai6 ji5 cin4 daa2 bo1 dit3 soeng1 si4 lau4 haa6 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他脸上有一个半月形的疤，是以前打球受伤时留下的。
examples.english_sentence: He has a crescent-shaped scar on his face; it was left from a past injury while playing ball.

mandarin_meaning: 半边莲（字面为半边的莲花）；亦可指某些植物的俗称。偶尔在口语或网络用法中被比喻为“片面、不完整”
english_meaning: half-lotus (literally); a common name for certain flowers. Occasionally used metaphorically to mean 'one-sided' or 'incomplete' in colloquial contexts
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词（植物名）；比喻用时仍作名词
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指“半邊的蓮花”，在廣東話裡可作某些花卉的俗稱。並非廣泛固定的成語，偶爾會在口語或網絡語境中用作比喻，表示事物或說法只呈現一邊、不完整。
explanation_english: Literally 'half-lotus'. Used as a common name for certain flowering plants. Not a widely established idiom; sometimes used colloquially or online as a metaphor for something one-sided or incomplete.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 花園入面種咗幾棵半邊蓮，好靚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faa1 jyun4 jap6 min6 zung6 zo2 gei2 fo1 bun3 bin1 lin4, hou2 leng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 花園裡種了幾株半邊蓮，很漂亮。
examples.english_sentence: There are several 'half-lotus' plants in the garden; they're very pretty.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢篇報道好片面，淨係講到一面，好似半邊蓮咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 pin1 bou3 dou6 hou2 pin3 min6, zing6 hai6 gong2 dou3 jat1 min6, hou2 ci5 bun3 bin1 lin4 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这篇报道很片面，只讲到一面，好像半边莲一样。
examples.english_sentence: This report is very one-sided, only presenting one side, like a 'half-lotus'.

mandarin_meaning: 桌头；桌面；（桌子的）主位
english_meaning: table top; on the table; the head seat at a table
explanation_mandarin: 指桌子的上端或表面，也可指坐在桌子主位的位置。在廣東話日常用語中可用來表示「在桌子上」或「桌子的頭位」。
explanation_english: Refers to the top or surface of a table, or the seat at the head of a table. In Cantonese it’s used to indicate something is on the table or to refer to the head position at a table.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 坐喺卓頭位嘅人通常係主人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: co5 hai2 coek3 tau4 wai6 ge3 jan4 tung1 soeng4 hai6 zyu2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 坐在桌子主位的人通常是主人。
examples.english_sentence: The person sitting at the head of the table is usually the host.

mandarin_meaning: 敷衍、草率、隨便處理事情
english_meaning: to do something perfunctorily or carelessly; half‑hearted, not thorough
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，形容做事不認真、敷衍了事或草率隨便地處理。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing actions that are done carelessly, perfunctorily, or without seriousness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢成日單單打打，交唔到合格嘅成果。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 seng4 jat6 daan1 daan1 daa2 daa2, gaau1 m4 dou2 hap6 gaak3 ge3 sing4 gwo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事总是敷衍，交不出合格的成果。
examples.english_sentence: He always does his work half‑heartedly and can't deliver acceptable results.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好單單打打咁講，要講清楚原因。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 daan1 daan1 daa2 daa2 gam2 gong2, jiu3 gong2 cing1 co2 jyun4 jan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要这样随便说，要把原因讲清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say it so casually; explain the reason clearly.

mandarin_meaning: （麻将术语）只听西风牌的单张听，即只差西风一张牌就能和牌
english_meaning: (mahjong) a single-tile wait on the West wind; waiting only for the West tile to win
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話的麻將用語中，『單吊西』表示牌面只差一張西風牌就能胡牌，也就是只聽西（單張等待西牌）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese mahjong terminology, '單吊西' indicates a single-tile wait for the West wind tile — you can win only if the West tile appears.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家單吊西，等緊最後一張西出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 daan1 diu3 sai1, dang2 gan2 zeoi3 hau6 jat1 zoeng1 sai1 ceot1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在單吊西，等最後一張西牌出來。
examples.english_sentence: I'm on a single wait for West; waiting for the last West tile to come out.

jyutping: daan1 liu6 tung4 bou1, jit6 dak1 faai3
mandarin_meaning: 单料铜锅，很快就热起来
english_meaning: A single-piece (pure) copper pot heats up quickly
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是指整件由铜制成的锅（单料铜锅）传热快、加热迅速。也可用于口语中比喻某物或某人容易“热起来”或反应快（例如热情或脾气容易上来），但主要用法是描述厨具的导热性能。
explanation_english: Literally refers to a pot made entirely of copper (single-piece copper pot) that heats up quickly. Primarily used to describe cookware's fast heat conduction. Figuratively, it can be used colloquially to describe something or someone that warms up or reacts quickly (e.g., quick temper or quick to get enthusiastic).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個单料铜煲真係热得快，煲汤几快就滚咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 daan1 liu6 tung4 bou1 zan1 hai6 jit6 dak1 faai3, bou1 tong1 gei2 faai3 zau6 gwan2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个单料铜锅真的很快就热了，炖汤很快就开了。
examples.english_sentence: This single-piece copper pot really heats up quickly; the soup starts boiling in no time.

jyutping: daan1 ngaan5 zai2 tai2 bong2, jat1 ngaan5 tai2 saai3
mandarin_meaning: 一眼看尽 / 一目了然
english_meaning: to see or grasp everything at a glance; to understand/notice all details in one look
explanation_mandarin: 口语俚语，表示只需看一眼就能把列表或情況的重點、細節看清楚或看完，形容觀察或判斷非常迅速。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression meaning someone can take in a list or situation and notice all key points or details with a single glance — i.e., to grasp everything very quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢分析嘢好快，單眼仔睇榜，一眼睇晒啲重點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan1 sik1 je5 hou2 faai3, daan1 ngaan5 zai2 tai2 bong2, jat1 ngaan5 tai2 saai3 di1 zung6 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他分析事情很快，一眼就把要点都看完了。
examples.english_sentence: He analyzes things very quickly — he can glance at the list and take in all the key points at once.

jyutping: daan1 ngaan5 lou2 tai2 lou5 po4, jat1 ngaan5 gin3
mandarin_meaning: 一眼就看见 / 一目了然
english_meaning: obvious at a glance; can be seen/recognized immediately
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語來自粵語口語，字面意思為「單眼佬看老婆，一眼就看見」。比喻某事或某種關係非常明顯，一看就能看出來；語氣常帶幽默或戲謔，屬港式俗語用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying literally meaning "a one-eyed man looks at his wife and sees (her) at one glance." It is used metaphorically to say something is immediately obvious or instantly recognizable. The tone is often humorous or jocular; it's a Hong Kong colloquialism.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰件事咁明顯，真係單眼佬睇老婆，一眼見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gin6 si6 gam2 ming4 hin2, zan1 hai6 daan1 ngaan5 lou2 tai2 lou5 po4, jat1 ngaan5 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那件事非常明显，真是一眼就看得出来。
examples.english_sentence: That matter is so obvious — you can really see it at a glance.

mandarin_meaning: 单身汉；未婚或没有伴侣的男人（口语）
english_meaning: a single man; bachelor (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: “单身寡佬”是粤语口语，指未婚或没有伴侣的男人，语气可带调侃或同情。
explanation_english: “单身寡佬” is a Cantonese colloquial term for a man who is single (no spouse/partner). It can be used teasingly or sympathetically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你仲係单身寡佬咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zung6 hai6 daan1 san1 gwaa2 lou2 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你还是单身汉吗？
examples.english_sentence: Are you still a bachelor?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢已經三十幾歲，仲係单身寡佬，唔急住結婚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5 ging1 saam1 sap6 gei2 seoi3, zung6 hai6 daan1 san1 gwaa2 lou2, m4 gap1 zyu6 git3 fan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他已经三十多岁了，还是单身汉，不急着结婚。
examples.english_sentence: He's already in his thirties and still single; he's not in a hurry to get married.

cantonese: 单车落坡，踩（睬）都唔踩（睬）
jyutping: daan1 ce1 lok6 po1, caai2 (coi2) dou1 m4 caai2 (coi2)
mandarin_meaning: 比喻對人或事情置之不理、毫不在意（相當於『不理會／不屑一顧』）
english_meaning: An idiom meaning to ignore something or someone completely; to be indifferent — literally 'a bike going downhill, whether you pedal or pay attention or not, you don't.'
explanation_mandarin: 字面上說單車下坡，踩不踩都無所謂，用來形容對別人的話、批評或事件完全不理會、不放在心上。
explanation_english: Literally describes a bicycle coasting downhill so pedaling (or paying attention) is irrelevant; used figuratively to indicate someone is completely indifferent or ignores something/someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人鬧都唔理，真係單車落坡，踩（睬）都唔踩（睬）。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 nau6 dou1 m4 lei5, zan1 hai6 daan1 ce1 lok6 po1, caai2 (coi2) dou1 m4 caai2 (coi2).
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人罵也不理，真是單車落坡，踩（睬）都不踩（睬），完全不在乎。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't even respond when people scold him — he's totally indifferent, like a bike going downhill that doesn't need pedaling.

mandarin_meaning: 把滯銷或賣不完的東西當作剩貨處理；引申為被當作次等或被忽視（俚語）
english_meaning: Literally 'sell leftover sugarcane'. Colloquially, to sell off unsold/leftover goods cheaply; figuratively, to be treated as unwanted or neglected (slang).
explanation_mandarin: 字面是把賣剩的甘蔗賣掉。廣東話口語用法指商品賣不完、淪為剩貨或被低價處理，也可用來形容人或物被輕視、當作次等對待。屬於非正式用語，常見於香港粵語語境。
explanation_english: Literally refers to selling leftover sugarcane. In Cantonese slang it describes goods that remain unsold and are sold off as leftovers or at a low price; it can also metaphorically describe people or things being treated as unwanted or of low value. Informal usage, common in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲水果賣唔晒，只好賣剩蔗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 seoi2 gwo2 maai6 m4 saai3, zi2 hou2 maai6 sing6 ze3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些水果卖不完，只好当作滞销品处理。
examples.english_sentence: These fruits can't all be sold; we'll have to sell them off as leftovers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲舊衫擺喺舊貨市場，啲人話係賣剩蔗，賣得好平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 gau6 saam1 baai2 hai2 gau6 fo3 si5 coeng4, di1 jan4 waa6 hai6 maai6 sing6 ze3, maai6 dak1 hou2 peng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些旧衣服在旧货市场卖，人们说是滞销货，卖得很便宜。
examples.english_sentence: Those old clothes are at the flea market; people say they're leftovers and they're selling very cheaply.

jyutping: maai6 sing6 ze3, zau1 wai4 ping4
mandarin_meaning: 把不要的東西或麻煩推給別人；依賴他人或推卸責任（粤語俗語）
english_meaning: A Cantonese colloquialism meaning to pass unwanted things or problems onto others; to freeload or shirk responsibility.
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語字面是「賣剩蔗，周圍憑」，用來形容把自己不要的東西、麻煩或責任推給別人，或靠別人解決，帶有貶義。
explanation_english: Literally 'sell leftover sugarcane, depend on the surroundings.' Used colloquially to describe offloading unwanted items or problems onto others or relying on others instead of taking responsibility; pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日賣剩蔗，周圍憑，唔肯負責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 maai6 sing6 ze3, zau1 wai4 ping4, m4 hang2 fu6 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是把爛攤子推給別人，不肯負責任。
examples.english_sentence: He always dumps his leftover problems on others and won't take responsibility.

mandarin_meaning: 卖剩的（鸭）；清仓甩卖；引申为不受欢迎或被抛弃
english_meaning: To sell leftover (ducks); to clear unsold stock (often at a discount); figuratively someone or something considered unwanted or left behind
explanation_mandarin: 「卖剩鸭」是粤语俚语/短语，字面指把卖不出的（通常指烧腊或熟食中的）鸭卖掉。引申为清理卖剩的库存或以折扣出售不受欢迎的商品；有时带贬义，用来形容某人被视为“剩下”、不被要。属于口语用法。
explanation_english: “卖剩鸭” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase. Literally it means selling roast ducks that didn't sell. Figuratively it refers to clearing unsold stock (often by discount) and can be used derogatorily to describe someone as unwanted or left over. It is an informal verb phrase.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲燒鴨今日賣得唔好，做到夜晚仲要賣剩鴨減價。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 siu1 aap3 gam1 jat6 maai6 dak1 m4 hou2, zou6 dou3 je6 maan5 zung6 jiu3 maai6 zing6 aap3 gaam2 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 燒鴨今天賣得不好，做到晚上還要賣剩鴨減價。
examples.english_sentence: The roast ducks didn't sell well today; by evening they still had to mark down the leftover ones.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細鋪要做促銷，因為有啲貨賣剩鴨，想快啲清走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 pou3 jiu3 zou6 cuk1 siu1, jan1 wai6 jau5 di1 fo3 maai6 zing6 aap3, soeng2 faai3 di1 cing1 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小店要做促銷，因為有些貨賣剩鴨，想快點清走。
examples.english_sentence: The small shop needs to run a sale because some stock is leftover and they want to clear it quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好用賣剩鴨去形容人，會好傷人感情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jung6 maai6 zing6 aap3 heoi3 jing4 jung4 jan4, wui5 hou2 soeng1 jan4 gam2 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要用賣剩鴨去形容人，會很傷人的感情。
examples.english_sentence: Don't use '賣剩鴨' to describe people; it can be very hurtful.

mandarin_meaning: 用好听的话讨好别人；谄媚、拍马屁
english_meaning: to flatter someone with sweet talk; to butter someone up; to curry favor by saying pleasant things
explanation_mandarin: “卖口乖”是粤语口语，指用甜言蜜语或刻意讨好别人的说法和行为，常带有贬义，意思接近“拍马屁”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to use flattering words or act sweetly to please someone. It usually has a pejorative sense, similar to "to flatter" or "to brown-nose."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日賣口乖，阿媽都識睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 maai6 hau2 gwaai1, aa3 maa1 dou1 sik1 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你别总是卖口乖，妈妈也看得出来。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep flattering them; mom can see right through it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日對上司賣口乖，想升職。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 deoi3 soeng5 si1 maai6 hau2 gwaai1, soeng2 sing1 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常对上司卖口乖，想升职。
examples.english_sentence: He constantly flatters his boss because he wants a promotion.

mandarin_meaning: 故意在公眾面前做作式表白，以博取關注
english_meaning: to stage or show off a romantic confession publicly to attract attention; a performative, attention-seeking confession
explanation_mandarin: 「卖告白」通常是粵語口語或網絡用語，指為了吸引別人注意而公開或誇張地表白（多帶表演性或做作成分）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to make a public or exaggerated confession of love (or feelings) as a performance to gain attention; an attention-seeking, showy confession.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日喺IG度賣告白，睇落好做作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 hai2 IG dou6 maai6 gou3 baak6, tai2 lok6 hou2 zou6 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別老是在IG上賣弄式表白，顯得很做作。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep posting performative confessions on IG — it looks so fake.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺台上賣告白，其實只係想上鏡吸引媒體。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 toi4 soeng6 maai6 gou3 baak6, kei4 sat6 zi2 hai6 soeng5 geng2 kap1 jan5 mui4 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在台上賣弄式表白，其實只是為了上鏡和吸引媒體。
examples.english_sentence: He staged a public confession on stage, but it was really just to be on camera and attract media attention.

jyutping: maai6 haam4 jyu4 sik6 haam4 jyu4 si2
mandarin_meaning: 賣鹹魚吃鹹魚屎（比喻厚顏無恥、貪婪或自作自受）
english_meaning: Literally 'sell salted fish and eat salted fish shit.' A vulgar Cantonese slang/idiom used to describe someone who is shameless, greedy, hypocritical or behaving self-defeatingly.
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是賣鹹魚卻吃鹹魚的糞便，常用來斥責或嘲諷別人厚顏無恥、貪婪或自相矛盾的行為，也可含有自作自受的意味。
explanation_english: The literal image is selling salted fish but eating its feces. Used to scold or mock someone as shameless, greedy, hypocritical, or acting in a self-defeating way. Vulgar in tone and often used colloquially.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁樣做，賣咸魚食咸魚屎，真係冇廉恥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 joeng6 zou6, maai6 haam4 jyu4 sik6 haam4 jyu4 si2, zan1 hai6 mou5 lim4 ci2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要這樣做，賣鹹魚吃鹹魚屎，真沒廉恥。
examples.english_sentence: Don't do that — selling salted fish and eating salted fish shit; it's really shameless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日呃人搵錢，真係賣咸魚食咸魚屎，大家都唔信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 aak1 jan4 wan2 cin2, zan1 hai6 maai6 haam4 jyu4 sik6 haam4 jyu4 si2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常騙人賺錢，真是賣鹹魚吃鹹魚屎，大家都不相信他。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps cheating people to make money — really selling salted fish and eating salted fish shit; nobody trusts him.

mandarin_meaning: 吹牛；誇大其詞
english_meaning: to brag; to boast; to exaggerate
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，用來形容某人誇大事實、吹噓或賣弄，多為口語且帶貶義。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who brags, exaggerates, or talks big to impress others; informal and often pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度賣大包，講到自己好叻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 mai6 daai6 baau1, gong2 dou3 zi6 gei2 hou2 lek1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常在那裡吹牛，說自己很厲害。
examples.english_sentence: He's always bragging there, saying he's really great.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好信佢，佢而家又賣大包。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5, keoi5 ji4 gaa1 jau6 mai6 daai6 baau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別相信他，他現在又在吹牛。
examples.english_sentence: Don't trust him; he's bragging again.

cantonese: 卖布唔带尺，存心不量（良）
jyutping: maai6 bou3 m4 daai3 cek3, cyun4 sam1 bat1 loeng4
mandarin_meaning: 卖布不带尺，存心不良；比喻故意欺骗或有恶意欺诈
english_meaning: Literally 'selling cloth without a ruler — deliberately dishonest'; an idiom describing someone intentionally cheating or acting in bad faith
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容故意不誠實、蓄意欺騙他人。原意指賣布的人不帶尺子，故意占便宜或坑人。
explanation_english: Used to describe deliberate dishonesty or intentional cheating. Literally refers to a cloth seller who doesn't bring a measuring ruler, implying intent to shortchange customers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間舖頭賣布唔帶尺，存心不良，買嘢要小心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 pou3 tau4 maai6 bou3 m4 daai3 cek3, cyun4 sam1 bat1 loeng4, maai5 je5 jiu3 siu2 sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間店卖布不带尺，存心不良，买东西要小心一点。
examples.english_sentence: That shop sells cloth without bringing a ruler — deliberately dishonest; be careful when buying.

mandarin_meaning: 出卖/拐卖（人口）；把人卖作苦力或其他被剥削的工作
english_meaning: to sell people (human trafficking); to sell someone into forced labor or, figuratively, to sell someone out/betray them
explanation_mandarin: 「卖猪仔」原指把人（尤其是年輕人或兒童）販賣到外地做苦力或受剝削的工作，現今也用來指拐賣人口或比喻出賣、背叛他人。
explanation_english: Originally referred to selling people (often young people or children) as laborers overseas; nowadays it commonly means human trafficking and is also used figuratively to mean betraying or selling someone out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 以前有啲窮家細路俾人賣豬仔去外國做苦力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji5 cin4 jau5 di1 kung4 gaa1 sai3 lou6 bei2 jan4 maai6 zyu1 zai2 heoi3 ngoi6 gwok3 zou6 fu2 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 过去有些穷人家的孩子被人贩子贩卖到外国做苦力。
examples.english_sentence: In the past, some poor families' children were sold by traffickers to foreign countries to work as laborers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話啲旅行社違法，將人賣豬仔去做黑工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 di1 leoi5 hang4 se5 wai4 faat3, zoeng1 jan4 maai6 zyu1 zai2 heoi3 zou6 hak1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說那些旅行社违法，把人卖去做黑工。
examples.english_sentence: He said those travel agencies illegally sold people to work as undocumented laborers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔會賣你豬仔，你可以信我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 wui5 maai6 nei5 zyu1 zai2, nei5 ho2 ji5 seon3 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不会把你出卖，你可以相信我。
examples.english_sentence: I won't sell you out; you can trust me.

mandarin_meaning: 装傻；装无辜（故意表现得天真或不知情以躲避责任或博取同情）
english_meaning: to play dumb; to feign innocence or act cute to avoid responsibility or gain sympathy/advantage
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，指故意装作不懂、不知道或无辜，以逃避责任或取得同情、好处。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term meaning to deliberately pretend ignorance or innocence (or act cute) in order to avoid responsibility or obtain sympathy/benefit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再賣生藕啦，做錯嘢就要負責。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi6 maai6 saang1 au2 laa3, zou6 co3 je5 zau6 jiu3 fu6 zaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要再卖生藕了，做错事就要负责。
examples.english_sentence: Don't play dumb anymore; if you made a mistake you must take responsibility.

jyutping: maai6 faa1 gu1 neoi5 caap3 zuk1 jip6
mandarin_meaning: （字面）卖花的姑娘把竹叶插上；（引申）形容女子精心打扮、装饰，带有俏皮或卖弄风情的意味。
english_meaning: Literal: 'the flower-selling girl inserts bamboo leaves.' Figurative: describes a girl who dresses up or adorns herself coquettishly; used playfully to describe decorative or showy grooming.
explanation_mandarin: 此短語常見於粵語語境或民間語言，用作比喻：既可指字面上的插飾動作，也常用來形容女子精心打扮、愛美或故意賣弄風情，有時帶戲謔或輕微貶義，亦可指過於矯飾的行為。
explanation_english: This Cantonese phrase can be literal (a flower seller inserting bamboo leaves) but is often used figuratively to describe a girl who carefully adorns herself or acts coquettishly. It is colloquial and can be playful, mildly teasing, or imply overly showy grooming.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢靚到好似卖花姑娘插竹叶咁，成日喺度整理頭飾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 leng3 dou3 hou2 ci5 maai6 faa1 gu1 neoi5 caap3 zuk1 jip6 gam2, sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 zing2 lei5 tau4 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她漂亮得像个卖花姑娘插着竹叶一样，总是在整理头饰。
examples.english_sentence: She looked so pretty, like a flower seller tucking bamboo leaves in her hair, always adjusting her hair ornaments.

mandarin_meaning: 自卖自夸；为自己的商品或行为吹嘘
english_meaning: To praise one's own goods or sing one's own praises; self-promotion or self-praise to boost sales
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是卖花时夸赞花的香味，比喻自己夸耀、推销自己的东西或行为，含有自夸、自吹自擂的意味。
