examples.jyutping_sentence: jiu3 wan2 cin2, zau6 jiu3 ceot1 san1 fu2 lik6; m4 ceot1 san1 fu2 lik6, dim2 dak1 sai3 gaan1 coi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 要赚钱，就要付出辛苦勞動；不付出辛苦勞動，怎能獲得世間的財富？
examples.english_sentence: If you want to make money you must work hard; without hard work, how can you obtain wealth?

mandarin_meaning: 联系不到你；到不了你（无法接触或到达某人）
english_meaning: can't reach you; unable to contact or get to you
explanation_mandarin: 用于粵語中表示無法聯絡、找到或到達某人，通常與動詞連用（例如「打唔到你」「搵唔到你」）。單獨使用較少見。
explanation_english: A Cantonese phrase expressing inability to reach, contact, find, or get to someone. It is normally used with verbs (e.g., '打唔到你', '搵唔到你') and is rarely used on its own.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 打唔到你，個電話一直打唔通。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daa2 m4 dou3 nei5, go3 din6 waa2 jat1 zik6 daa2 m4 tung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 打不到你的電話，電話一直打不通。
examples.english_sentence: I couldn't call you; the phone kept being unreachable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我去到嗰度，但係搵唔到你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 heoi3 dou3 go2 dou6, daan6 hai6 wan2 m4 dou3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我到了那裡，但是找不到你。
examples.english_sentence: I arrived there but couldn't find you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我試過發訊息，但係聯絡唔到你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 si3 gwo3 faat3 seon3 sik1, daan6 hai6 lyun4 lok3 m4 dou3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我試過發信息，但是聯絡不到你。
examples.english_sentence: I tried messaging you, but I couldn't get in touch with you.

cantonese: 唔到冬至唔寒，唔到夏至唔热
jyutping: m4 dou3 dung1 zi3 m4 hon4, m4 dou3 haa6 zi3 m4 jit6
mandarin_meaning: 不到冬至不冷，不到夏至不热
english_meaning: Not cold until the Winter Solstice, not hot until the Summer Solstice (i.e. seasonal extremes arrive only at their proper times)
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是要到冬至才會真正寒冷、要到夏至才會真正炎熱。用來說明季節變化按時節來，或比喻事情要到合適的時間才會發生。
explanation_english: Literally, 'It isn't cold until the Winter Solstice; it isn't hot until the Summer Solstice.' Used to say that seasonal extremes come at their proper times, or figuratively that things happen only when the right time comes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年成個秋天都好暖，真係唔到冬至唔寒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 sing4 go3 cau1 tin1 dou1 hou2 nyun5，zan1 hai6 m4 dou3 dung1 zi3 m4 hon4。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年整個秋天都很暖和，真是不到冬至不冷。
examples.english_sentence: This whole autumn has been very warm — it's really not cold until the Winter Solstice.

synonyms: 不到冬至不冷，不到夏至不热
時候未到 / 時機未到

mandarin_meaning: 應付不來；無法對付／控制（某人或某事）
english_meaning: can't handle; unable to cope with or deal with (someone/something)
explanation_mandarin: 表示無法應付或對付某人或某事，通常用於力量、情況或工作量超出可處理範圍的情形。
explanation_english: Indicates inability to cope with or deal with someone or something — typically used when a person, situation, or workload is beyond one's capacity to handle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢太勁，我哋唔制得過佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 taai3 ging6, ngo5 dei6 m4 zai3 dak1 gwo3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他太厲害，我們應付不了他。
examples.english_sentence: He's too strong; we can't handle him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家啲客太多，我哋唔制得過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 di1 haak3 taai3 do1, ngo5 dei6 m4 zai3 dak1 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在客人太多，我們應付不來。
examples.english_sentence: There are too many customers now; we can't cope.

jyutping: m4 faat3 fo2, dong3 beng6 maau1
mandarin_meaning: 不发火，装作病猫；比喻遇到责难或冲突时不反击、示弱以避免纷争
english_meaning: Don't get angry, act like a sick cat; figuratively, to not retaliate and feign weakness or passivity to avoid conflict
explanation_mandarin: 形容遇到激怒或挑衅時選擇保持沉默、不還手或示弱，以免惹生事端或激化矛盾。
explanation_english: Describes choosing not to react or retaliate when provoked, pretending to be weak or passive in order to avoid trouble or escalate conflict.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人鬧都唔發火，當病貓，想息事寧人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 naau6 dou1 m4 faat3 fo2, dong3 beng6 maau1, soeng2 sik1 si6 ning4 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人骂也不发火，装作病猫，想息事宁人。
examples.english_sentence: He gets scolded but doesn't get angry; he acts like a sick cat to avoid making trouble.

jyutping: m4 tung4 cong4 m4 zi1 bei6 laan6
mandarin_meaning: 只有真正同床或同居後，才會發現對方的缺點或問題
english_meaning: You won't discover someone's flaws or problems until you share a bed (i.e., live closely or become intimately involved)
explanation_mandarin: 這是廣東話的口語說法，比喻只有在非常親密或共同生活時，才會發現對方真正的缺點、習慣或麻煩之處。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning that only after close, intimate cohabitation (literally sharing a bed) will one discover a partner's real shortcomings, habits, or problems.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋拍緊拖，但仍未同居，我都有啲驚，唔同床唔知被烂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 paak3 gan2 to1, daan6 jing4 mei6 tung4 geoi1, ngo5 dou1 jau5 di1 ging1, m4 tung4 cong4 m4 zi1 bei6 laan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们在谈恋爱，但还没同居，我有点担心，毕竟不到同床很难发现对方的缺点。
examples.english_sentence: We're dating but not living together yet; I'm a bit worried — you don't know someone's flaws until you share a bed.

mandarin_meaning: 不听劝/不听劝告
english_meaning: to ignore advice or warnings; refuse to listen; be stubborn
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语/俚语，表示不听别人的劝告或警告，固执、任性地按自己的方式行事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase meaning to ignore advice or warnings — stubbornly refuse to heed others' counsel.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都唔听笛，人哋点样讲都冇用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 m4 teng1 dik6, jan4 dei6 dim2 joeng6 gong2 dou1 mou5 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是不听劝，别人怎么劝都没有用。
examples.english_sentence: He never listens to advice; no matter how others try to persuade him it's useless.

mandarin_meaning: 不合適/說得不妥（口語）
english_meaning: not the right thing to say / inappropriate / off-topic (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「唔啱偈」是廣東話口語，用來表示某句話不合時宜、不妥當或離題，通常帶有批評或提醒的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to say that something said is inappropriate, untimely, off-topic, or just not right — often used to criticize or warn.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家呢個時候講笑唔啱偈，佢啱啱失業。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 ni1 go3 si4 hau6 gong2 siu3 m4 aam1 gai3, keoi5 aam1 aam1 sat1 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在這個時候開玩笑不合時宜，他剛剛失業。
examples.english_sentence: It's not the right time to joke; he just lost his job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣講，聽落有啲唔啱偈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 gong2, teng1 lok6 jau5 di1 m4 aam1 gai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你那樣說，聽起來有點不妥。
examples.english_sentence: The way you say that sounds a bit off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰啲資料唔啱偈，唔好信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 di1 zi1 liu2 m4 aam1 gai3, m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些資料不對，不要相信他。
examples.english_sentence: That information is wrong, don't trust him.

mandarin_meaning: 不僅／不只是
english_meaning: not only; not merely
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示不只是某一情況，常與「仲/還/亦」等連用，表示還有其他情況或程度。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that something is not limited to one condition; often paired with words like "also" (e.g. "not only... but also...").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔單止好聰明，仲好努力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 daan1 zi2 hou2 cung1 ming4, zung6 hou2 nou5 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不僅聰明，還很努力。
examples.english_sentence: He is not only smart, but also very hardworking.

mandarin_meaning: 悄悄地；默默地；不聲張
english_meaning: quietly; silently; stealthily; without drawing attention
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，表示悄悄地、不出聲或不張揚地做某事，常用於描述人悄悄離開或秘密進行的行為。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to do something quietly or without attracting attention; often used to describe someone leaving or acting secretly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔声唔声就走咗，冇同我講一聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 seng1 m4 seng1 zau6 zau2 zo2，mou5 tung4 ngo5 gong2 jat1 seng1。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他悄悄地走了，沒跟我說一聲。
examples.english_sentence: He left quietly without telling me.

mandarin_meaning: 不够 / 不足
english_meaning: not enough; insufficient; lacking
explanation_mandarin: 表示數量、程度或時間不足，可作謂語或用於數量前，屬口語用法。
explanation_english: Indicates an insufficient amount, degree, or time. Commonly used predicatively or before quantities; colloquial Cantonese expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔夠錢買呢件衫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gau3 cin2 maai5 ni1 gin6 saam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我没有足够的钱买这件衣服。
examples.english_sentence: I don't have enough money to buy this shirt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 時間唔夠，我要跑快啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si4 gaan3 m4 gau3, ngo5 jiu3 paau2 faai3 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 时间不够，我得跑得快一点。
examples.english_sentence: There's not enough time; I need to run faster.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個份量唔夠兩個人食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 fan6 loeng6 m4 gau3 loeng5 go3 jan4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这一份不够两个人吃。
examples.english_sentence: This portion isn't enough for two people.

mandarin_meaning: 不夠過癮／不夠滿足／不夠（令人滿意）
english_meaning: not satisfying; not enough to satisfy; unsatisfying
explanation_mandarin: 「唔夠喉」是香港粵語的口語說法，表示某事物不足以令人滿足或過癮，或覺得不夠精彩、不夠份量。
explanation_english: “唔夠喉” is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial expression meaning something is not enough to satisfy or is unsatisfying — e.g., not impressive, not substantial, or not enough to hit the spot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢杯咖啡唔夠喉，太淡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bui1 gaa3 fe1 m4 gau3 hau4, taai3 daam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這杯咖啡不夠味，太淡了。
examples.english_sentence: This coffee isn't satisfying — it's too weak.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚場演唱會只唱咗幾首歌就完，真係唔夠喉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 coeng4 jin2 coeng3 wui6 zi2 coeng3 zo2 gei2 sau2 go1 zau6 jyun4, zan1 hai6 m4 gau3 hau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚的演唱會只唱了幾首歌就結束，真是不夠過癮。
examples.english_sentence: The concert tonight ended after only a few songs — it was really unsatisfying.

mandarin_meaning: 不夠格 / 不夠水準；(能力或表現)不足
english_meaning: not good/qualified enough; insufficient or inadequate
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用來表示某人或某事在能力、資格或表現上達不到標準或不夠格。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to say someone or something is insufficient, not up to standard, or not qualified.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢申請隊長嘅職位，但評審話佢唔够嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 san1 cing2 deoi6 zoeng2 ge3 zik1 wai6, daan6 ping4 sam2 waa6 keoi5 m4 gau3 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他申請隊長職位，但評審說他不夠格。
examples.english_sentence: He applied for the captain position, but the judges said he's not qualified.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢位廚師經驗唔够嚟做主廚，仲需要再練習。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wai2 cyu4 si1 ging1 jim6 m4 gau3 lai4 zou6 zyu2 cyu4, zung6 seoi1 jiu3 zoi3 lin6 zaap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這位廚師經驗不足以擔任主廚，還需要再練習。
examples.english_sentence: This chef doesn't have enough experience to be head chef yet; he needs more practice.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日嘅表現唔够嚟，下一次再努力啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 ge3 biu2 jin2 m4 gau3 lai4, haa6 jat1 ci3 zoi3 nou5 lik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天的表現不夠好，下次再努力。
examples.english_sentence: Your performance today wasn't good enough; try harder next time.

mandarin_meaning: 不夠強 / 不是對手
english_meaning: not strong enough; not a match; not convincing
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語口語用語，表示力量、能力或說服力不足；也可指不是對手、比不上別人。常用來形容人、隊伍、論點或證據不夠強。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase meaning someone or something is not strong/competent/convincing enough — i.e., not a match or not up to the task. Used for people, teams, arguments, evidence, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋隊真係唔夠打，今次贏唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 deoi6 zan1 hai6 m4 gau3 daa2, gam1 ci3 jing4 m4 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們隊真的不夠強，這次贏不了。
examples.english_sentence: Their team really isn't strong enough; they won't win this time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你個理由唔夠打，老闆唔會接受。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 go3 lei5 jau4 m4 gau3 daa2, lou5 baan2 m4 wui5 zip3 sau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你的理由不夠有力，老闆不會接受。
examples.english_sentence: Your reason isn't strong enough; the boss won't accept it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我個論點唔夠打，講唔服佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 leon6 dim2 m4 gau3 daa2, gong2 m4 fuk6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的論點不夠有說服力，說服不了他。
examples.english_sentence: My argument isn't strong enough; I can't convince him.

mandarin_meaning: 微不足道；少得可怜（数量或程度太少，起不到作用）
english_meaning: negligible; paltry; too little to make a difference
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俚语，字面可理解为“连牙缝都塞不足”，用来形容数量或程度非常少，微不足道，通常用于钱、资源或效果太少而无法达到目的或解决问题。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression literally suggesting something is too small to even wedge between the teeth; it describes an amount or degree so trivial or paltry that it is negligible and won't achieve the intended effect.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 哎呀，呢份錢唔夠攝牙罅，根本解決唔到問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ai1 aa3, ni1 fan6 cin2 m4 gau3 sip3 ngaa4 hat6, gan1 bun2 gaai2 kyut3 m4 dou3 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 哎呀，这点钱太少了，根本解决不了问题。
examples.english_sentence: Ah, this amount of money is negligible; it won't solve the problem at all.

mandarin_meaning: 喘不过气 / 没有气力
english_meaning: out of breath; breathless; lacking energy
explanation_mandarin: 「唔够气」字面意思是呼吸不足，常用來形容運動後氣喘、呼吸困難或體力不足。有時也可指因驚訝或激動而短暫喘不過氣。
explanation_english: Literally 'not enough breath.' Used to describe being out of breath after exertion, short of breath, or lacking stamina. It can also describe briefly being winded from surprise or strong emotion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我跑咗兩圈而家真係唔夠氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 paau2 zo2 loeng5 hyun1 ji4gaa1 zan1hai6 m4 gau3 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我跑了两圈，现在真的喘不过气。
examples.english_sentence: I ran two laps and I'm really out of breath now.

mandarin_meaning: 不够调皮；不够顽皮（太乖或不够活泼）
english_meaning: not cheeky / not mischievous enough; too well-behaved or not playful
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语表达，用来形容一个人不够调皮、顽皮或不够活泼，常带有轻微打趣或责备的语气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to say someone is not cheeky or mischievous enough—too well-behaved or not lively. Often used teasingly or lightly reproachful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日唔够皮，连讲笑都冇心情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 m4 gau3 pei4, lin4 gong2 siu3 dou1 mou5 sam1 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天不够调皮，连开玩笑的心情都没有。
examples.english_sentence: You're not being cheeky today; you don't even feel like joking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 班小朋友太乖，唔够皮，老師話佢哋唔夠活潑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baan1 siu2 pang4 jau5 taai3 gwaai1, m4 gau3 pei4, lou5 si1 waa6 keoi5 dei6 m4 gau3 wut6 put3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些小朋友太乖，不够调皮，老师说他们不够活泼。
examples.english_sentence: The kids are too well-behaved and not cheeky enough; the teacher says they're not lively enough.

mandarin_meaning: 不要做手脚/不要耍手段（不要篡改、偷工或作弊）
english_meaning: Don't tamper / don't fiddle / don't cheat / don't mess around
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，多用作命令或警告，意思是不要暗中篡改、作弊、偷工減料或耍手段。有時亦可泛指不要耍花招、不要馬虎了事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial imperative used to warn or order someone not to tamper, fiddle, cheat, or cut corners. It can also broadly mean 'don't play tricks' or 'don't be sloppy'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好手脚，呢件事要公平處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sau2 goek3, ni1 gin6 si6 jiu3 gung1 ping4 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要做手脚，這件事要公平處理。
examples.english_sentence: Don't tamper with things; this matter must be handled fairly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做嘢唔好手脚，唔好偷工減料，做到紮實啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 je5 m4 hou2 sau2 goek3, m4 hou2 tau1 gung1 gaam2 liu6, zou6 dou3 zaat3 sat6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做事不要做手脚，不要偷工減料，要做得踏實一點。
examples.english_sentence: When working, don't cut corners or cheat; do the job thoroughly.

mandarin_meaning: 不安、不安乐
english_meaning: uneasy; restless; not at peace
explanation_mandarin: 表示心情或狀態不平靜、感到不安、擔憂或坐立不安。
explanation_english: Indicates a state of being unsettled, anxious, or not at ease—feeling restless or uneasy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近成日覺得唔安樂，夜晚都瞓唔着。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 seng4 jat6 gok3 dak1 m4 on1 lok6, je6 maan5 dou1 fan3 m4 zoek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近经常觉得不安，晚上都睡不着。
examples.english_sentence: He's been feeling uneasy lately; he can't sleep at night.

mandarin_meaning: 不開胃；不提起食慾（也可引申為不吸引、提不起興趣）
english_meaning: not appetizing; unappetizing (can also figuratively mean unappealing or fails to arouse interest)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容食物不會引起食慾，也可用在比喻語境表示某事物不吸引人或令人提不起興趣。
explanation_english: Used to describe food that does not stimulate appetite; figuratively, it describes something that is unappealing or fails to arouse interest.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢碟嘢真係唔开胃，我冇胃口食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dip6 je5 zan1 hai6 m4 hoi1 wai6, ngo5 mou5 wai6 hau2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這道菜真不開胃，我沒胃口吃。
examples.english_sentence: This dish is really not appetizing; I don't have an appetite to eat it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我覺得呢本書好悶，完全唔开胃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gok3 dak1 ni1 bun2 syu1 hou2 mun6, jyun4 cyun4 m4 hoi1 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我覺得這本書很無聊，完全不吸引人。
examples.english_sentence: I find this book very dull — it's completely unappealing.

jyutping: m4 dong3 gaa1 m4 zi1 coi4 mai5 gwai3
mandarin_meaning: 不当家不知柴米贵
english_meaning: You don't know the cost and difficulty of running a household until you manage it yourself.
explanation_mandarin: 意思是没有亲自掌管家务或家计的人，无法体会日常开支与操持家庭的辛苦和成本。
explanation_english: A proverb meaning that someone who has never managed household affairs won't understand how costly and difficult everyday living and household management are.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 以前我覺得屋企唔使咁節省，直到我開始自己理家計，先知唔當家唔知柴米貴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji5 cin4 ngo5 gok3 dak1 uk1 kei2 m4 sai2 gam2 zit3 seng2, zi3 dou3 ngo5 hoi1 ci2 zi6 gei2 lei5 gaa1 gai3, sin1 zi1 m4 dong3 gaa1 m4 zi1 coi4 mai5 gwai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 以前我觉得家里不用那么节省，直到我开始自己打理家计，才知道不当家不知柴米贵。
examples.english_sentence: I used to think we didn't need to be so frugal at home, until I started managing the household finances myself and realized you don't know how expensive living is until you run the household.

mandarin_meaning: 没空 / 没有空闲
english_meaning: not free; have no free time; busy; unavailable
explanation_mandarin: 表示没有空闲时间，无法抽时间做某事。常用于口语，表示忙碌或无法赴约。
explanation_english: Indicates not having free time; unable to make time for something. Commonly used colloquially to say one is busy or unavailable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家唔得闲，等我做晒先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4gaa1 m4 dak1 haan4, dang2 ngo5 zou6 saai3 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我现在没空，等我做完再说。
examples.english_sentence: I'm not free right now; wait until I finish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都唔得闲，約唔到佢出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4jat6 dou1 m4 dak1 haan4, joek3 m4 dou2 keoi5 ceot1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是没空，约不到他出来。
examples.english_sentence: He's always busy; you can't get him to come out.

mandarin_meaning: 不行 / 不可以 / 没用
english_meaning: won't work; no good; impossible; unacceptable
explanation_mandarin: 用於口語，表示某事行不通、不合適或無用，帶有否定與不被接受的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to indicate something won't work, is unacceptable, or is hopeless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個方法唔得𠶧，我哋要諗其他辦法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 fong1faat3 m4 dak1 gaa3, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 nam2 kei4 taa1 baan6faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个方法不行，我们要想其他办法。
examples.english_sentence: This method won't work; we need to think of other solutions.

mandarin_meaning: 不忿、不滿；感到冤屈或不平
english_meaning: to feel aggrieved, resentful, displeased or indignant
explanation_mandarin: 表示對某事感到不滿或冤屈，有不平或憤懣的情緒，語氣可偏口語或帶有輕微憤怒。
explanation_english: Indicates feeling aggrieved, resentful, or displeased about something—a sense of injustice or indignation. Often used colloquially.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對嗰個決定好唔忿，覺得好唔公平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 go2 go3 kyut3 ding6 hou2 m4 fan5, gok3 dak1 hou2 m4 gung1 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對那個決定感到不忿，覺得很不公平。
examples.english_sentence: He felt aggrieved by that decision and thought it was very unfair.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到佢噉講，我真係有啲唔忿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 keoi5 gam2 gong2, ngo5 zan1 hai6 jau5 di1 m4 fan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到他那樣說，我真的有點不忿。
examples.english_sentence: Hearing him say that, I really felt a bit resentful.

mandarin_meaning: 不服气；感到不平、不满、怨恨
english_meaning: to feel resentful, aggrieved, or unwilling to accept something; to be upset or feel unfairly treated
explanation_mandarin: 表示對某事或結果感到不滿、不平或不甘心，有怨懟、心裡覺得不公平的情緒。
explanation_english: Expresses a feeling of resentment or indignation — being upset, unconvinced, or feeling that something is unfair.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考得咁好但冇獎學金，佢好唔忿气。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 dak1 gam2 hou2 daan6 mou5 zoeng2 hok6 gam1, keoi5 hou2 m4 fan5 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考试考得那么好却没有奖学金，他很不服气。
examples.english_sentence: He did so well in the exams but didn't get the scholarship; he's very resentful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到個同事升職，心裡好唔忿气。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou2 go3 tung4 si6 sing1 zik1, sam1 lei5 hou2 m4 fan5 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到同事升职，心里很不服气。
examples.english_sentence: He saw a colleague get promoted and felt very aggrieved.

jyutping: m4 paa3 gwaan1, zeoi3 paa3 gun2
mandarin_meaning: 不怕官，最怕被管（怕被人管轄或管束、監督）
english_meaning: Not afraid of officials or authority, but most afraid of being controlled, supervised, or micromanaged.
explanation_mandarin: 表示與其怕權勢或當官，不如更怕被人管束、干涉或監督，強調被約束或受控制比權勢本身更令人反感。
explanation_english: A proverb that means people fear being controlled or micromanaged more than they fear officials or authority; it emphasizes dislike of restriction, supervision, or interference.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強話佢唔怕官，最怕管，唔想畀人管佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 waa6 keoi5 m4 paa3 gwaan1, zeoi3 paa3 gun2, m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 gun2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强说他不怕官，最怕被管，不想被人管。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Keung said he's not afraid of officials; what he fears most is being controlled — he doesn't want others to control him.

cantonese: 唔怕犯天条，至怕犯众憎
jyutping: m4 paa3 faan6 tin1 tiu4, zi3 paa3 faan6 zung3 zang1
mandarin_meaning: 不怕觸犯天條（或上天、道德規範），最怕得罪大眾／招致公眾憎惡。
english_meaning: Not afraid to offend heavenly law or moral rules, but most afraid of incurring the hatred or disapproval of the public; fearing public opinion above higher principles.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人或某些做法對上天、道德規範不太在意，但非常在乎大眾的看法或怕被大家唾棄。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who doesn't mind violating moral or 'heavenly' rules but is extremely concerned about public opinion and fears being disliked by the masses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲政客為咗選票，唔怕犯天条，至怕犯众憎，凡事都顧住唔得罪大眾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 zing3 haak3 wai6 zo2 syun2 piu3, m4 paa3 faan6 tin1 tiu4, zi3 paa3 faan6 zung3 zang1, faan4 si6 dou1 gu3 zyu6 m4 dak1 zeoi6 daai6 zung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了拉票，政客不怕違背天條，最怕得罪大眾，所以處處顧慮不敢得罪選民。
examples.english_sentence: To win votes, politicians may not fear breaking moral rules, but they dread alienating the public, so they avoid offending voters.

mandarin_meaning: 不值得（為此）
english_meaning: not worth it; not worth the trouble/effort
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話表達，表示某件事或某個行為不值得花時間、力氣或金錢去做，或不值得因此而得意/自滿。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression indicating that something is not worth spending time, effort, or money on — or not worth getting proud/angry about.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗呢點小利搞到咁樣，真係唔抵得颈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 ni1 dim2 siu2 lei6 gaau2 dou3 gam2 joeng6, zan1 hai6 m4 dai2 dak1 geng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了這點小利益搞成這樣，實在不值得。
examples.english_sentence: It's really not worth getting like this over such a small profit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家嬲都唔抵得颈，唔關你事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 nau1 dou1 m4 dai2 dak1 geng2, m4 gwaan1 nei5 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你現在生氣也不值得，這和你沒關係。
examples.english_sentence: It's not worth you getting angry now; it's not your fault.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）表示某種情況下某人的反應是可以理解的；難怪／不能怪別人
english_meaning: Colloquial expression meaning 'no wonder' or 'you can't blame someone (for...)' — indicates that a reaction is understandable given the situation.
explanation_mandarin: 「唔教人」常用於句中或句尾，通常接在句子前或前一子句之後並跟隨一個動詞或形容詞，表達在某種情況下某人的反應或行為是情理之中，帶有「難怪、不能怪別人」的意思，常用於反問句或感嘆句。
explanation_english: Used in colloquial Cantonese to indicate that a person's reaction is understandable given the circumstances. It often appears before a verb or at the end of a clause and functions like 'no wonder' or 'you can't blame someone (for...)', frequently used in rhetorical questions or exclamations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁夜先返屋企，唔教人擔心？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 je6 sin1 faan1 uk1 kei2, m4 gaau3 jan4 daam1 sam1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這麼晚才回家，難怪會讓人擔心？
examples.english_sentence: You come home so late — no wonder people are worried?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日唔交功課，唔教人唔生氣？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 m4 gaau1 gung1 fo3, m4 gaau3 jan4 m4 sang1 hei3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常不交作業，難怪別人生氣？
examples.english_sentence: He always doesn't hand in his homework — can't blame people for being upset?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個老闆成日遲發糧，唔教人轉工？
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 lou5 baan2 sing4 jat6 ci4 faat3 loeng4, m4 gaau3 jan4 zyun2 gung1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老闆經常遲發薪水，難怪員工會換工作？
examples.english_sentence: The boss frequently pays salaries late — no wonder people change jobs?

cantonese: 唔望今年竹，只望明年笋
jyutping: m4 mong6 gam1 nin4 zuk1, zi2 mong6 ming4 nin4 seon2
mandarin_meaning: 不指望今年，有所期待於明年（不寄望短期回報，寄望來年會有好轉）
english_meaning: Don't expect gains this year; hope for (better) returns next year — i.e. not expecting short‑term payoff but looking to future improvement.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語字面說不看重今年的“竹”，只期待明年的“笋”。實際用法是表示不寄望今年有回報或好轉，而是把希望放在來年，常用於投資、做生意或長期計劃需要時間見效的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying literally meaning 'don't expect bamboo this year, only expect bamboo shoots next year.' It means not to expect immediate returns and to place hope on improvements next year. Commonly used about business, investments, or plans that take time to pay off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年生意差，我哋唔好心急，唔望今年竹，只望明年笋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 saang1 ji3 caa1, ngo5 dei6 m4 hou2 sam1 gap1, m4 mong6 gam1 nin4 zuk1, zi2 mong6 ming4 nin4 seon2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年生意不好，我們不要心急，不指望今年有收穫，只希望明年會好轉。
examples.english_sentence: Business is bad this year; let's not rush — we don't expect gains this year, only hope for improvements next year.

mandarin_meaning: 不倫不類；非此非彼；不上不下
english_meaning: neither fish nor fowl; neither one thing nor the other; ambiguous/mediocre
explanation_mandarin: 表示某事物或某人的狀態介乎兩者之間，既不好也不壞、不倫不類，常帶貶義。
explanation_english: Describes something or someone that is neither one thing nor another — indistinct, unimpressive, or awkwardly in-between; often derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲設計真係唔湯唔水，睇落唔係幾好又唔係幾差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 cit3 gai3 zan1 hai6 m4 tong1 m4 seoi2 ，tai2 lok6 m4 hai6 gei2 hou2 jau6 m4 hai6 gei2 caa1 。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的設計真是不倫不類，看起來不太好也不太差。
examples.english_sentence: His/her design is really neither here nor there — it doesn't look particularly good or particularly bad.

mandarin_meaning: 不僅；不止（並非只有……）
english_meaning: not only; not merely; not just
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示並非只有某事或某情況，常用來引出後項以說明還有其他情況或補充內容，相當於普通話的“不僅/不止”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning 'not only' or 'not merely'. It introduces additional information or a contrasting item, equivalent to Mandarin '不僅/不止'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔淨衹識講英文，仲識日文同韓文。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zing6 zi2 sik1 gong2 jing1 man4, zung6 sik1 jat6 man4 tung4 hon4 man4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不僅會說英文，還會說日語和韓語。
examples.english_sentence: He not only speaks English, but also Japanese and Korean.

mandarin_meaning: 不顧後果／不管天命（口語）
english_meaning: to not care about consequences or fate; to act recklessly/defiantly
explanation_mandarin: 「唔理天胎」為香港粵語口語用法，表示不顧後果、不在乎別人或天命的看法，採取魯莽或放任的行為或態度。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to disregard consequences or fate; to act recklessly or defiantly without caring what others (or 'heaven') think.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話唔理天胎辭職，結果今日就走人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 m4 lei5 tin1 toi1 ci4 zik1 , git3 gwo2 gam1 jat6 zau6 zau2 jan4 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說不顧後果要辭職，結果今天就走了。
examples.english_sentence: He said he'd resign regardless of the consequences, and in the end he left today.

mandarin_meaning: 完全不理会；不搭理
english_meaning: to ignore completely; to refuse to pay attention (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语俚语，用来表示对人或事情完全不理会、不搭理，语气常带有不屑或厌烦。字面为“不能理会鼻子”，为习用说法的夸张表达。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase used to express complete disregard or refusal to engage with someone or something. Often carries a dismissive or annoyed tone. Literally ‘can’t mind the nose,’ but idiomatic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鬧人，我都唔理得个鼻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 nau6 jan4, ngo5 dou1 m4 lei5 dak1 go3 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是骂人，我都完全不理会。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps scolding people; I just ignore him completely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你再講我都唔理得个鼻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoi3 gong2 ngo5 dou1 m4 lei5 dak1 go3 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你再说我也完全不理会。
examples.english_sentence: Say whatever you want — I still won't pay any attention.

jyutping: m4 beng6 m4 beng6, jat1 beng6 jiu3 ming6
mandarin_meaning: 平時沒病，但一旦生病就非常嚴重，甚至危及生命；也可比喻一旦出事後果非常嚴重。
english_meaning: Usually appears fine, but when illness (or a problem) occurs it's severe or life-threatening; can be used literally for health or figuratively for serious consequences.
explanation_mandarin: 口語表達，形容人平時看似沒事，但一生病就很嚴重，可能危及生命；也可用來比喻事物一旦出問題後果嚴重。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression describing someone who seems fine normally but whose illness becomes very serious or life-threatening; can also be used figuratively to say that when a problem occurs the consequences are severe.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽平時睇落好健康，但佢唔病唔病，一病要命，我哋好擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 maa1 ping4 si4 tai2 lok6 hou2 gin6 hong1, daan6 keoi5 m4 beng6 m4 beng6, jat1 beng6 jiu3 ming6, ngo5 dei6 hou2 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我妈妈平时看起来很健康，但她一生病就要命，我们很担心。
examples.english_sentence: My mother usually seems healthy, but when she gets sick it's life-threatening — we're very worried.

mandarin_meaning: 看不惯；无法忍受（某人的言行或某种情况）
english_meaning: cannot stand; find intolerable or displeasing (cannot bear to look at someone/something)
explanation_mandarin: 表示对某人或某事看不顺眼、心里觉得不能接受或无法忍受，常用于口语。
explanation_english: A colloquial phrase expressing that one finds someone or something displeasing or intolerable and cannot bring oneself to look at them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲態度我真係唔睇得过眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 taai3 dou6 ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 tai2 dak1 gwo3 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的态度让我真的看不惯。
examples.english_sentence: I really can't stand his attitude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個房间咁亂，我真係唔睇得过眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 fong4 gaan1 gam2 lyun6, ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 tai2 dak1 gwo3 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个房间这么乱，我真的看不惯。
examples.english_sentence: I really can't stand how messy this room is.

jyutping: m4 zi1 cau2 zi6 dim2 se2
mandarin_meaning: 不知道「丑」这个字怎么写。
english_meaning: Don't know how to write the character '丑'.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，用來表示不會或不記得怎麼寫字（此處特指「丑/醜」這個字）。常用於談論中文書寫或當場需要寫字但不清楚寫法時的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning you don't know how to write the character '丑' (醜). Used when someone cannot recall or write that character, typically in spoken, casual contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 要寫『醜』字嗰陣，我真係唔知丑字点写。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jiu3 se2 cau2 zi6 go2 zan6, ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 zi1 cau2 zi6 dim2 se2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 要写“丑”字的时候，我真的不知道丑字怎么写。
examples.english_sentence: When I had to write the character '丑', I really didn't know how to write it.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）不知道有多好／挺好的（表示程度或有點讚賞，有時也可字面理解為不確定多好）
english_meaning: (colloquial) don't know how good (it is); (used as an intensifier) quite/pretty (good)
explanation_mandarin: 「唔知幾好」在廣東話中常用作程度副詞，含有「非常/挺/頗」的語氣，用來強調某事物不易用言語形容的好；也可按字面理解為「不確定有多好」。語氣可正面或帶諷刺/保留。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "唔知幾好" is a colloquial adverbial phrase often used to indicate a high degree ("quite/very good")—literally "don't know how good"—implying something is hard to describe or surprisingly good. It can also be used more literally to express uncertainty about how good something is, and the tone may be sincere or ironic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部手機唔知幾好，用落又快又順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 sau2 gei1 m4 zi1 gei2 hou2, jung6 lok6 jau6 faai3 jau6 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這部手機不知道多好，使用起來又快又順。
examples.english_sentence: This phone is really great; it runs fast and smoothly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嗰啲理由唔知幾好，聽落怪怪哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 go2 di1 lei5 jau4 m4 zi1 gei2 hou2, teng1 lok6 gwaai3 gwaai3 dei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他講的那些理由不知道多好，聽起來怪怪的。
examples.english_sentence: The reasons he gave aren't exactly convincing; they sound a bit off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 買唔買呢件衫？唔知幾好，依家有折可以諗下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maai5 m4 maai5 ni1 gin6 saam1? m4 zi1 gei2 hou2, ji1 gaa1 jau5 zit3 ho2 ji5 lam2 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 買不買這件衣服？不知道多好，現在有折扣可以考慮一下。
examples.english_sentence: Should I buy this shirt? Not sure how good it is, but it's on sale now so I could consider it.

mandarin_meaning: 不知道（常用於表示不知道在哪裡或不知道怎麼辦）
english_meaning: don't know / have no idea (often about location or situation)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，為「不知道（在哪／怎麼辦）」的簡略說法。常用於回答他人詢問或表示對情況不明、不知道該如何處理。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression, a shortened way to say 'don't know' (often about location or what to do). Used to answer questions or express ignorance about a situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你啲文件放喺邊呀？我真係唔知埞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 di1 man4 gin2 fong3 hai2 bin1 aa3? ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 zi1 dei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你的文件放在哪裡？我真的是不知道。
examples.english_sentence: Where did you put the documents? I really don't know.

jyutping: m4 zi1 sei2 zi6 dim2 se2
mandarin_meaning: 不知道该怎么办 / 无计可施（口语）
english_meaning: don't know what to do; at a loss; clueless (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 字面是“不知道怎麼把‘死’字寫”，在廣東話口語中作為感嘆或自嘲的表達，表示遇到棘手情況時不知道如何處理、無計可施或手足無措。
explanation_english: Literally 'don't know how to write the character for "die".' In Cantonese colloquial use it is an emphatic/exasperated expression meaning one has no idea what to do, is at a loss, or powerless to solve a problem.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老細話要減人，大家都唔知死字點寫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 sai3 waa6 jiu3 gaam2 jan4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zi1 sei2 zi6 dim2 se2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板说要裁员，大家都不知道该怎么办。
examples.english_sentence: The boss said there will be layoffs; everyone is at a loss and doesn't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 不像人样/不像人的行为；太过分、残忍（口语）
english_meaning: Not behaving like a human; inhumane; outrageous; used to emphasize something extreme
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，常用來形容某事或某人過分、難以接受或殘忍，也可用作加強語氣（如「熱到唔系人噉品」表示非常熱）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe something or someone as excessive, inhumane, or outrageous. It can also be used to intensify a statement (e.g. "熱到唔系人噉品" = "so hot it's inhumane").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日熱到唔系人噉品，行幾步已經滿身汗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 jit6 dou3 m4 hai6 jan4 gam2 ban2, haang4 gei2 bou6 ji5 ging1 mun5 san1 hon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天热得不像人样，走几步就全身是汗。
examples.english_sentence: It's so hot today it's inhumane — after walking a few steps I'm already sweating all over.

cantonese: 唔系你嘅财，唔入你嘅袋
jyutping: m4 hai6 nei5 ge3 coi4, m4 jap6 nei5 ge3 doi2
mandarin_meaning: 不是你的錢／福分，不會進入你的口袋；不屬於你的東西得不到
english_meaning: If it's not yours, it won't end up in your pocket; you won't get what isn't meant for you
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，用來表示不屬於你的東西最終不會落到你手上，常用來安慰失去機會或財物的人，含有順其自然、不要強求的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying meaning that things not meant for you will not come to you. It is often used to console someone who lost an opportunity or possession, implying acceptance and 'what's meant to be will be'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我本來好想攞嗰份工，點知面試失敗，朋友安慰我話：'唔系你嘅财，唔入你嘅袋'。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bun2 loi4 hou2 soeng2 lo2 go2 fan6 gung1, dim2 zi1 min6 si3 sat1 baai6, pang4 jau5 on1 wai6 ngo5 waa6: 'm4 hai6 nei5 ge3 coi4, m4 jap6 nei5 ge3 doi2'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我本来很想得到那份工作，結果面試失敗，朋友安慰我說：「不是你的錢，不會進你的口袋」。
examples.english_sentence: I really wanted that job, but I failed the interview; my friend comforted me saying, 'If it's not yours, it won't go into your pocket.'

mandarin_meaning: 如果不是的話；要是不然的話；否則
english_meaning: if not; otherwise; unless
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示在某個條件不成立時的結果或替代情況，相當於「如果不是的話」或「否則」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese conditional phrase meaning "if not" or "otherwise," used to indicate an alternative outcome when a stated condition does not hold.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔知佢會唔會嚟，唔系嘅話我哋就先開始。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zi1 keoi5 wui5 m4 wui5 loi4, m4 hai6 ge3 waa6 ngo5 dei6 zau6 sin1 hoi1 ci2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不知道他會不會來，如果不是的話我們就先開始。
examples.english_sentence: I don't know if he'll come; if not, we'll start first.

mandarin_meaning: 不是小事；不可小覷
english_meaning: not a small matter; not to be underestimated; quite significant
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，字面上是「不是少的東西」，用來形容人或事重要、厲害或數量不少，不能輕視或掉以輕心。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "not a small thing." It describes a person or matter that is significant, formidable, or considerable in amount — not to be underestimated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔系嘢少，做咗十幾年老闆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 hai6 je5 siu2, zou6 zo2 sap6 gei2 nin4 lou5 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不是等閒之輩，做了十幾年老闆。
examples.english_sentence: He's not someone to be underestimated — he's been a boss for over ten years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢筆錢唔系嘢少，要諗清楚先簽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bat1 cin2 m4 hai6 je5 siu2, jiu3 nam2 cing1 co2 sin1 cim1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這筆錢不是小數目，要想清楚才簽字。
examples.english_sentence: This amount of money isn't small; think carefully before signing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你以為佢唔識？佢唔系嘢少，識好多嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji5 wai6 keoi5 m4 sik1? keoi5 m4 hai6 je5 siu2, sik1 hou2 do1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你以為他不懂？他可不是簡單人物，懂得很多東西。
examples.english_sentence: You think he doesn't know? He's not simple — he knows a lot.

mandarin_meaning: 不是這麼說 / 不是那樣說
english_meaning: That's not how you say it / That's not what I meant
explanation_mandarin: 用來糾正別人的說法或表示不同意，意思是「不是那樣說」或「不是這樣的情況」。通常出現在對方誤解或誤會時。
explanation_english: Used to correct someone's statement or to express disagreement; means 'that's not how it is' or 'that's not what I meant'. Often used when someone has misunderstood or misrepresented something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔系噉讲，你聽我講完先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hai6 gam2 gong2, nei5 teng1 ngo5 gong2 jyun4 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不是這樣說，你先聽我把話說完。
examples.english_sentence: That's not how it is — listen to me finish first.

mandarin_meaning: 不是就假的 / 要么是真的要么就是假的
english_meaning: If it's not (true), then it's fake; either it's real or it's fake (used to emphasize authenticity or express skepticism)
explanation_mandarin: 「唔系就假」是廣東話口語/俚語，用來表示對某事真偽的二分法判斷或表示懷疑與否定。字面意思是「不是（真的）就是假的」。
explanation_english: “唔系就假” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to express a binary judgment about authenticity or to voice skepticism/dismissal. Literally: "if it's not true then it's fake."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話嗰張相係真？唔系就假啦，你自己諗下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 go2 zoeng1 soeng2 hai6 zan1? m4 hai6 zau6 gaa2 laa1, nei5 zi6 gei2 lam2 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说那张照片是真的吗？不是就假的啦，你自己想想。
examples.english_sentence: He says that photo is real? If it's not, then it's fake — think about it yourself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話嗰件衫係名牌？唔系就假啦，價格又咁平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 go2 gin6 saam1 hai6 ming4 paai4? m4 hai6 zau6 gaa2 laa1, gaa3 gaak3 jau6 gam2 peng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说那件衣服是名牌？不是就假的啦，价格又这么便宜。
examples.english_sentence: You say that shirt is a designer brand? If not, then it's fake — the price is so low.

mandarin_meaning: 不是关于手脚（不是体力或动手的事）；通常表示需要动脑、按程序或受其他因素影响。
english_meaning: Not about hands and feet; not a physical/manual matter—often meaning it requires thinking, procedure, or other non-manual factors.
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语用法，表示某件事不是靠体力或动手就能解决，通常强调需要动脑、按程序或受其他原因影响。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to say that something is not solved by manual or physical action; it emphasizes that the matter requires mental effort, procedure, or other factors.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份工唔系手脚嘅工，係要動腦筋嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gung1 m4 hai6 sau2 goek3 ge3 gung1, hai6 jiu3 dung6 nou5 gan1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这份工作不是靠体力的活，是要动脑筋的。
examples.english_sentence: This job isn't about manual work; it requires thinking.

jyutping: m4 hai6 maang5 lung4 m4 gwo3 gong1
mandarin_meaning: 不是猛龍就不渡江；比喻能力不夠的人不要輕舉妄動，只有真正有實力的人才能完成艱難的任務。
english_meaning: If you're not a mighty dragon, don't try to cross the river; meaning don't attempt things beyond your ability — only the truly capable can take on certain difficult tasks.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來提醒人量力而為、不要逞強或冒險做超出自己能力範圍的事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb used to warn people to act within their abilities and not undertake tasks that exceed their capability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意唔係咁簡單，唔系猛龙唔过江，唔好亂嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3 m4 hai6 gam2 gaan2 daan1, m4 hai6 maang5 lung4 m4 gwo3 gong1, m4 hou2 lyun6 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這筆生意不簡單，沒實力的人別輕舉妄動，不要亂來。
examples.english_sentence: This deal isn't simple — if you're not up to it, don't act recklessly.

mandarin_meaning: 不合適／不妥當／不對勁
english_meaning: not right; inappropriate; something's off
explanation_mandarin: 「唔系路」是香港粵語口語，表示某事、某人或某種說法不合適、不妥當或不合常理，帶有批評或不讚同的語氣。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning something is not right, appropriate, or fitting — often used to criticize behavior, remarks, or appearance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣講真係唔係路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 gong2 zan1 hai6 m4 hai6 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣說真的很不合適。
examples.english_sentence: What you said is really inappropriate.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫著起身有啲唔係路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 zoek3 hei2 san1 jau5 di1 m4 hai6 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件衣服穿起來有點不合適/看起來怪怪的。
examples.english_sentence: This outfit looks kind of off / doesn't look right.

mandarin_meaning: 不要紧 / 没关系
english_meaning: It's not important; never mind; no problem
explanation_mandarin: 表示某事不重要或不必放在心上，常用来安慰对方或表示不用担心。为粤语口语表达，相当于“没关系/不要紧”。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that something is not important or not worth worrying about. Common colloquial Cantonese expression to reassure someone (equivalent to "never mind" or "it's okay").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔紧要，你已經做得好好喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 gan2 jiu3, nei5 ji5 ging1 zou6 dak1 hou2 hou2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 没关系，你已经做得很好了。
examples.english_sentence: It's okay, you've already done very well.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 遲到幾分鐘都唔紧要，但唔好成日遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ci4 dou3 gei2 fan1 zung1 dou1 m4 gan2 jiu3, daan6 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 迟到几分钟没关系，但不要总是迟到。
examples.english_sentence: Being a few minutes late is fine, but don't be late all the time.

mandarin_meaning: 不知不觉
english_meaning: unconsciously; without realizing; before one knows it
explanation_mandarin: 表示在没有注意或察觉的情况下发生或经过某事，常用于描述时间流逝或变化在不知不觉间发生。
explanation_english: Indicates that something happens without someone noticing or realizing it; commonly used to describe time passing or changes occurring subtly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺度做嘢，唔经唔觉已經做咗三個鐘頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 dou6 zou6 je5, m4 ging1 m4 gok3 ji5 ging1 zou6 zo2 saam1 go3 zung1 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在做事，不知不觉已经做了三个小时。
examples.english_sentence: I was working, and before I knew it I had already been working for three hours.

mandarin_meaning: 不招财／招不到财运
english_meaning: not attracting wealth; unlucky with money; doesn't bring in money
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，形容人、地方或事物不招財、帶不來財運，或在金錢方面運氣不好、難以積聚財富。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to describe a person, place, or thing that fails to attract wealth or good financial luck — i.e., unlucky with money or not bringing in income.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間舖頭開咗好耐，但係好少客，真係唔聚財。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 pou3 tau4 hoi1 zo2 hou2 noi6, daan6 hai6 hou2 siu2 haak3, zan1 hai6 m4 zeoi6 coi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間舖開了很久，但顧客很少，真的不聚財。
examples.english_sentence: That shop has been open for a long time, but very few customers come — it's really not bringing in money.

mandarin_meaning: 不出聲；不吭聲
english_meaning: to keep silent; not make a sound; quietly
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示不發出聲音或保持沉默。可用作命令（叫人不要說話）或描述某人/多人靜默的狀態。重複為「唔聲唔聲」可表示偷偷地、不張揚地。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to make no sound or remain silent. It can be used as a command (telling someone to be quiet) or to describe someone(s) being quiet. When reduplicated as "唔聲唔聲" it can mean doing something quietly or unobtrusively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開會嗰陣大家都唔聲，等老細講完先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 wui2 go2 zan6 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 seng1, dang2 lou5 sai3 gong2 jyun4 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开会的时候大家都不出声，等老板讲完再说。
examples.english_sentence: During the meeting everyone stayed silent and waited for the boss to finish speaking.

mandarin_meaning: 別得意/別自滿
english_meaning: don’t be smug / don’t be cocky / don’t show off
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語俚語，用來提醒或斥責對方不要得意、自滿或擺架子。語氣通常較為隨意，有時帶有半開玩笑或責備的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to tell someone not to be smug, self-satisfied, or showy. The tone is usually casual and can be teasing or reproachful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你贏咗一次就咁得意，唔好臭米气啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jeng4 zo2 jat1 ci3 zau6 gam2 dak1 ji3, m4 hou2 cau3 mai5 hei3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你贏了一次就這麼得意，別這麼自滿啦。
examples.english_sentence: You won once and you're already so pleased with yourself—don't be so smug.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都臭米气，成班朋友都覺得煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 cau3 mai5 hei3, sing4 baan1 pang4 jau5 dou1 gok3 dak1 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常自滿，整班朋友都覺得煩。
examples.english_sentence: He's always being smug; the whole friend group finds it annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 不擺架子／不自大
english_meaning: not arrogant; not showing off; humble
explanation_mandarin: 口語化的廣東話用語，用來形容一個人不擺架子、不自負、不愛炫耀。常在香港粵語中使用。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is not arrogant, does not show off, and is humble. Commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁臭米氣啦，大家都係朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 cau3 mai5 hei3 laa1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hai6 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別那麼擺架子啦，我們都是朋友。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so full of yourself; we're all friends.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗老闆，但佢好低調，完全唔臭米氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 lou5 baan2, daan6 keoi5 hou2 dai1 diu6, jyun4 cyun4 m4 cau3 mai5 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他當了老闆，但很低調，完全不擺架子。
examples.english_sentence: He became the boss, but he's very low-key and not at all arrogant.

mandarin_meaning: 不倒霉也要自找倒霉；自找麻煩
english_meaning: You're asking for trouble; bringing bad luck upon yourself
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容本來不會倒霉，但因為某些行為或決定而自己招來倒霉或麻煩，類似「自找麻煩」、「不倒霉也要自找倒霉」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to say someone who would not have been unlucky ends up causing their own bad luck or trouble — similar to 'asking for trouble' or 'bringing it on yourself.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢明明冇事做，偏偏去惹人，唔衰揾嚟衰啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ming4 ming4 mou5 si6 zou6, pin1 pin3 heoi3 je5 jan4, m4 seoi1 wan2 lai4 seoi1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他明明沒事做，偏偏去惹人，真是自找倒霉。
examples.english_sentence: He clearly had nothing to do but went and provoked people — he's just asking for trouble.

mandarin_meaning: 不只 / 不僅 / 不只是
english_meaning: not only; not merely; more than
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 副詞短語（表示範圍或程度超出單一事物）
explanation_mandarin: 「唔衹（止）」用於表示不僅限於某一情況或事物，常用於連接兩個並列的成分，相當於普通話的「不只/不僅/不只是」。可接名詞、動詞短語或子句，常與「仲／還／還有」連用。
explanation_english: “唔衹（止）” is used to indicate that something is not limited to one case or item — equivalent to Mandarin "不只/不僅" and English "not only". It can link two parallel elements and is often followed by words like "also" or "furthermore".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔衹識講廣東話，仲識講普通話同英文。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zi2 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2, zung6 sik1 gong2 pou2 tung1 waa2 tung4 jing1 man4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不只會說廣東話，還會說普通話和英文。
examples.english_sentence: He not only speaks Cantonese, but also Mandarin and English.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個問題唔衹影響一個部門，仲會影響成個公司。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 man6 tai4 m4 zi2 jing2 hoeng2 jat1 go3 bou6 mun4, zung6 wui5 jing2 hoeng2 sing4 go3 gung1 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個問題不只影響一個部門，還會影響整個公司。
examples.english_sentence: This problem not only affects one department, but could affect the whole company.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔衹係學生，仲係老師。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zi2 hai6 hok6 saang1, zung6 hai6 lou5 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不只是學生，還是老師。
examples.english_sentence: He is not only a student, but also a teacher.

mandarin_meaning: 無意中 / 不經意 / 不小心
english_meaning: unintentionally; inadvertently; accidentally
explanation_mandarin: 表示沒有意識到或不是故意做某件事，常用於口語，等同於「無意中」或「不經意」。
explanation_english: Indicates doing something without intending to or without awareness; a colloquial adverb meaning 'unintentionally' or 'inadvertently'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔覺意打翻杯水，啲文件全部濕晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gok3 ji3 daa2 faan1 bui1 seoi2, di1 man4 gin2 cyun4 bou6 sap1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不小心打翻了杯水，文件全部都湿了。
examples.english_sentence: I accidentally knocked over the cup of water and all the documents got wet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔覺意講漏咗佢嘅秘密。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 gok3 ji3 gong2 lau6 zo2 keoi5 ge3 bei3 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他無意中把他的秘密說漏了。
examples.english_sentence: He inadvertently let his secret slip.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 對唔住，我唔覺意遲到，唔好意思呀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: deoi3 m4 zyu6, ngo5 m4 gok3 ji3 ci4 dou3, m4 hou2 ji3 si1 aa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 對不起，我不小心遲到了，抱歉。
examples.english_sentence: Sorry, I unintentionally arrived late. My apologies.

mandarin_meaning: 沒發覺；沒注意到
english_meaning: without realizing; not noticing
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語用法，表示沒有察覺或不知不覺間發生某事。此詞常見於香港日常會話，有時也寫作「唔覺眼間」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning 'without noticing' or 'before one realizes'. Common in Hong Kong Cantonese; sometimes appears as '唔覺眼間'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔觉眼已經遲到咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gok3 ngaan5 ji5 ging1 ci4 dou3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我沒發覺已經遲到了。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't realize I was already late.

mandarin_meaning: 不想/不考虑/不费心思（不动脑筋）
english_meaning: don't think; not bothering to think; act without thinking; stop overthinking
explanation_mandarin: 口语粤语表达，字面意思为“不思考”。常用来表示不想费脑筋、不去考虑后果、随性或冲动行事，也可作劝说别人大可不必多想。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase literally meaning "not think." It is used to indicate not bothering to think, not considering consequences, acting impulsively, or telling someone not to overthink.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我細個嗰陣好唔諗嘢，成日衝動行事，依家學識冷靜啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 go2 zan6 hou2 m4 lam2 je5, sing4 jat6 cung1 dung6 hang4 si6, ji4 gaa1 hok6 sik1 laang5 zing6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小時候很不會思考，經常衝動行事，現在學會冷靜一些。
examples.english_sentence: When I was young I didn't think much and often acted on impulse; now I've learned to be a bit calmer.

mandarin_meaning: 這不是開玩笑的事 / 不能拿來開玩笑
english_meaning: not a laughing matter; no joke; not to be joked about
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞性短語（固定片語）
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示某事嚴肅或不能拿來開玩笑，常作評價性短語或感嘆用法，例如提醒別人別輕視或戲謔某情況。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that something is serious and not to be joked about. It functions as an evaluative phrase or exclamation to warn others not to treat the matter lightly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事唔講得笑，應該嚴肅處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 m4 gong2 dak1 siu3, jing1 goi1 jim4 suk1 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事不是鬧著玩的，應該嚴肅處理。
examples.english_sentence: This matter is no laughing matter; it should be handled seriously.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋唔好對佢講得笑，佢啱啱先失業。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 m4 hou2 deoi3 keoi5 gong2 dak1 siu3, keoi5 ngaam1 ngaam1 sin1 sat1 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們別拿他開玩笑，他剛剛失業。
examples.english_sentence: Let's not make fun of him; he just lost his job.

mandarin_meaning: 不懂得应付 / 不會處理（局面）
english_meaning: not know how to handle a situation; don't know what to do
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口語，意指在突發或尷尬的情況下不知道如何應對或處理，常用來形容沒經驗或不會變通的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone doesn't know how to cope with or handle a situation (often unexpected or awkward); used to describe inexperience or inability to respond appropriately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面試問到一啲突發問題，佢真係唔识驾步。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 si3 man6 dou3 jat1 di1 dat6 faat3 man6 tai4, keoi5 zan1 hai6 m4 sik1 gaa3 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面试被问到一些突发问题，他真的不知道怎么应付。
examples.english_sentence: In the interview they asked some unexpected questions; he really didn't know how to handle them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺派對上有人故意刺激你，如果你唔识驾步，好容易尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 paai3 deoi6 seong6 jau5 jan4 gu3 ji3 cik1 gei2 nei5, jyu4 gwo2 nei5 m4 sik1 gaa3 bou6, hou2 jung6 ji6 gaan1 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在派对上有人故意刺激你，如果你不懂应付，很容易尴尬。
examples.english_sentence: If someone deliberately provokes you at a party and you don't know how to respond, it can get awkward quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 不能说/不能讲（不可以提起或透露）
english_meaning: cannot be said / can't talk about it (not allowed to mention or disclose)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語（情態/助動用法）
explanation_mandarin: 「唔话得」是廣東話口語，表示某事不能說、不能透露或不應該提及，有時也用來表示某事不可行或不能接受。
explanation_english: “唔话得” is a Cantonese colloquial expression meaning something cannot be said, disclosed, or mentioned. It can also be used to indicate that something is unacceptable or not feasible.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事唔话得，唔好再提。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 m4 waa6 dak1, m4 hou2 zoi3 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事不能说，别再提了。
examples.english_sentence: This matter can't be discussed; don't bring it up again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司啲內部消息係唔话得嘅，要保密。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong1 si1 di1 noi6 bou6 siu1 sik1 hai6 m4 waa6 dak1 ge3, jiu3 bou2 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司的内部消息是不可以说的，要保密。
examples.english_sentence: The company's internal news can't be disclosed; it's confidential.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢想咁樣做？唔话得啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 gam2 joeng6 zou6? m4 waa6 dak1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他想那样做？不行！
examples.english_sentence: He wants to do that? No way!

mandarin_meaning: 谢谢 / 劳驾 / 请问（视语境而定）
english_meaning: thank you; excuse me; please (polite request) — depends on context
explanation_mandarin: 粤语常用的礼貌用语，根据语境可表示感谢（“谢谢”）、请求帮忙或引起注意（“劳驾/请问”）等。
explanation_english: A common Cantonese polite expression. Depending on context it is used to say thank you, to request assistance or attention (like 'excuse me' / 'please').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔該晒你幫我拎行李。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 goi1 saai3 nei5 bong1 ngo5 ling1 haang4 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 非常感谢你帮我拿行李。
examples.english_sentence: Thanks a lot for helping me carry my luggage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔該，洗手間喺邊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 goi1, sai2 sau2 gaan1 hai2 bin1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 请问，洗手间在哪里？
examples.english_sentence: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔該，畀我一杯咖啡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 goi1, bei2 ngo5 jat1 bui1 gaa3 fe1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 麻烦给我一杯咖啡。
examples.english_sentence: Could I have a cup of coffee, please?

mandarin_meaning: 先谢谢 / 麻烦你先（做某事）/ 我先走了（礼貌道别）
english_meaning: Thanks in advance / Please (do this first) / I'll go first (polite parting)
explanation_mandarin: 「唔该先」是廣東話的口語用法，通常用來表示事先致謝（類似“先謝謝”或“麻煩你先”），也可用作請對方先行處理某事或作為禮貌性道別（我先走了）。語氣較隨意，常見於香港日常會話。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to offer thanks in advance (like "thanks in advance" or "please do this first"). It can also be used as a polite way to say you'll go ahead/leave ("I'm off now"). It's informal and common in Hong Kong daily speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔該先，幫我影張相啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 goi1 sin1, bong1 ngo5 jing2 zoeng1 soeng2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 麻烦你先帮我拍一张照片。
examples.english_sentence: Could you please take a photo for me (thanks in advance).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我先走啦，唔該先！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sin1 zau2 laa1, m4 goi1 sin1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我先走了，謝謝（先）。
examples.english_sentence: I'm off now, thanks (bye).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 埋單，唔該先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maai4 daan1, m4 goi1 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 請結帳，謝謝。
examples.english_sentence: The bill please, thanks.

mandarin_meaning: 非常感謝／多謝（用於加強語氣的粵語感謝語）
english_meaning: Thanks a lot; thank you very much (an emphatic Cantonese thank-you)
explanation_mandarin: 「唔該晒」是粵語口語，為「唔該」的加強形式，用來表示較強烈或較客氣的感謝。有時亦可用作帶有輕微諷刺或強調語氣的用法，視語境而定。
explanation_english: “唔該晒” is a Cantonese colloquial expression, an intensified form of “唔該,” used to express stronger or more polite thanks. Depending on context and tone, it can be sincere or, occasionally, mildly sarcastic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔該晒，你幫我攞行李上車。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 goi1 saai3, nei5 bong1 ngo5 lo2 hang4 lei5 soeng5 ce1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 非常感謝，你幫我把行李放上車。
examples.english_sentence: Thanks a lot — you helped me put the luggage in the car.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你幫我整好部電話，唔該晒！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 bong1 ngo5 zing2 hou2 bou6 din6 waa2, m4 goi1 saai3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你幫我修好了手機，真的非常感謝！
examples.english_sentence: You fixed my phone — thanks a lot!

mandarin_meaning: 不吃亏 / 不赔本 / 不吃亏也不大赚（口语）
english_meaning: not lose out; not be at a loss; come out even (colloquial)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口语短语（形容词/动词短语）
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，表示在交易或处境中不会吃亏或处于不利，通常指至少不赔本或不吃亏。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to avoid losing out or being at a disadvantage—typically implying you at least won't lose money or be worse off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 買二送一，咁買就唔输蚀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maai5 ji6 sung3 jat1, gam2 maai5 zau6 m4 syu1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 买二送一，这样买就不亏。
examples.english_sentence: Buy two get one free — buying like that you're not losing out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊款減價，買返一件都唔输蚀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 fun2 gam2 gaa3, maai5 faan1 jat1 gin6 dou1 m4 syu1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 旧款降价，买回一件也不会吃亏。
examples.english_sentence: The old model is discounted; buying one back won't be a loss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我做呢單生意好小心，唔好賠錢，最緊要唔输蚀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zou6 ni1 daan1 saang1 ji3 hou2 siu2 sam1, m4 hou2 pui4 cin2, zeoi3 gan2 jiu3 m4 syu1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我做这一单生意很小心，不想赔钱，最重要的是不吃亏。
examples.english_sentence: I'm careful with this deal — I don't want to lose money; the key is not to come out worse off.

mandarin_meaning: 對某人冷淡、不理睬；與某人處於不和狀態
english_meaning: to give someone the cold shoulder; to ignore or be on unfriendly terms with someone
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指對某人不理、不搭理或冷落，通常用於雙方因誤會或爭執後處於不和狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to ignore someone, give them the cold shoulder, or refuse to communicate—often used when two people are not on speaking terms after a disagreement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢因為嗰件事同我唔通氣幾個月。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1 wai6 go2 gin6 si6 tung4 ngo5 m4 tung1 hei3 gei2 go3 jyut6。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他因為那件事跟我不和好幾個月。
examples.english_sentence: He hasn't been on speaking terms with me for several months because of that incident.

cantonese: 唔食咸魚口唔腥，唔做坏事心唔惊
jyutping: m4 sik6 haam4 jyu4 hau2 m4 sing1, m4 zou6 waai6 si6 sam1 m4 ging1
mandarin_meaning: 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门（不做坏事就不会心里害怕）
english_meaning: If you do nothing wrong, you have nothing to fear; an honest person has a clear conscience.
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是“不吃咸鱼嘴不会腥”，引申为“只要不做坏事，心里就不害怕”。用于表示问心无愧就不用担心别人或内心不安。
explanation_english: Literally: 'If you don't eat salted fish your mouth won't smell fishy.' Figuratively: 'If you don't do bad things your conscience won't trouble you.' Used to mean that an honest person who has done nothing wrong has nothing to fear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你放心做啦，唔食咸魚口唔腥，唔做坏事心唔惊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 fong3 sam1 zou6 laa1, m4 sik6 haam4 jyu4 hau2 m4 sing1, m4 zou6 waai6 si6 sam1 m4 ging1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你放心去做吧，不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门。
examples.english_sentence: Go ahead and do it—if you haven't done anything wrong, you have nothing to fear.

synonyms: 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门

jyutping: m4 sik6 gau2 juk6 lou1 gau2 zap1
mandarin_meaning: 表面上不直接参与肮脏或有争议的事情，却从中暗中获利；虚伪地回避责任但捞好处。
english_meaning: To avoid directly engaging in something dirty or controversial while secretly reaping its benefits; hypocritically profiting without getting one's hands dirty.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚语 / 动词短语（含贬义）
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，字面是“不吃狗肉但去捞狗汁”。用于形容那些表面上不沾手、不承担责任，实际却暗中牟利或占便宜的人或行为。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "don't eat dog meat but scoop the dog broth." It describes people who pretend not to be involved in dirty business but secretly profit from it — hypocritical opportunism.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢表面上話唔沾手，實際上係唔食狗肉捞狗汁，暗裏攞晒利益。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 biu2 min6 soeng6 waa6 m4 zim1 sau2, sat6 zai3 soeng6 hai6 m4 sik6 gau2 juk6 lou1 gau2 zap1, aam3 leoi5 lo2 saai3 lei6 jik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他表面上说不沾手，实际上是假装不直接涉入却暗中从中牟利。
examples.english_sentence: He claims to stay uninvolved, but in fact he's avoiding direct involvement while secretly reaping all the benefits.

mandarin_meaning: 不知不覺
english_meaning: before one knows it; unconsciously; without realizing
explanation_mandarin: 表示在不經意或未察覺的情況下發生或變化，相當於普通話的「不知不覺」或「不經意間」。
explanation_english: Used to indicate that something happens or changes without one noticing — similar to 'before one knows it' or 'unconsciously'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔驚唔覺，已經過咗兩年。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 ging1 m4 gok3, ji5 ging1 gwo3 zo2 loeng5 nin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不知不覺，已經過了兩年。
examples.english_sentence: Before I knew it, two years had already passed.

mandarin_meaning: 不介意；不在乎
english_meaning: don't mind; not care; indifferent
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示對某事不介意或不在乎，常用於日常對話中表示漠不關心或允許對方自行決定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning 'to not mind' or 'to not care'. Used in everyday speech to show indifference or to give permission for someone to decide.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔𠶧，你想點就點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gaai3, nei5 soeng2 dim2 zau6 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不在乎，你想怎麼做就怎麼做。
examples.english_sentence: I don't mind — do whatever you want.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對批評唔𠶧，照樣做佢嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 pei1 ping4 m4 gaai3, ziu3 joeng6 zou6 keoi5 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對批評不在乎，照樣做他的事。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't care about criticism and does his thing anyway.

mandarin_meaning: 不想耗費力氣／不願意勞動或費心做某事
english_meaning: don't want to bother / unwilling to put in the work or effort
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語（表達不願意/懶得做某事）
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，表示不想勞動、不願意花心思或費力去做某事；帶有懶或不屑的語氣，常用於日常對話或俚語語境。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning someone doesn't want to work or bother to do something. It conveys reluctance, laziness, or unwillingness and is commonly used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日瞓到中午，真係唔𪐀經（耕）去做家務。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 fan3 dou3 zung1 ng5, zan1 hai6 m4 soeng2 gaang1 heoi3 zou6 gaa1 mou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天睡到中午，真是不想費力去做家務。
examples.english_sentence: I slept until noon today — I really don't want to bother doing housework.

mandarin_meaning: 休息；喘息
english_meaning: to rest; to take a break; to catch one's breath
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语动词，表示休息、歇息或喘息，常见用法有“唞氣”、“唞下”等，带有短暂停顿或放松的意思。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to rest, take a break, or catch one's breath. Commonly used in phrases like “唞氣” or “唞下,” implying a short pause or relaxation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我攰，去唞下先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gui6, heoi3 tau2 haa5 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我累了，去休息一下先。
examples.english_sentence: I'm tired; I'll go rest for a bit first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好淨係係度唞，快啲返嚟幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 hai6 dou6 tau2, faai3 di1 faan1 lai4 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要只在那裡休息，快點回來幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just rest there — come back quickly and help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等陣我哋唞吓，再繼續開會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 zan6 ngo5 dei6 tau2 haa5, zoi3 gai3 zuk6 hoi1 wui2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等一下我們休息一下，再繼續開會。
examples.english_sentence: Let's take a short break and then continue the meeting.

mandarin_meaning: 歇一歇；乘凉
english_meaning: to take a breather / cool off; to relax for a short while
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，表示去乘凉或歇息一下，放松休息。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to rest or cool off for a short time — to take a breather and relax.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日好熱，去樹下唞涼下啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 hou2 jit6, heoi3 syu6 haa6 tau2 loeng4 haa5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天很热，去树下乘凉一下吧。
examples.english_sentence: It's very hot today — let's go sit under a tree and cool off.

mandarin_meaning: 廢話、胡說、無意義的閒聊
english_meaning: nonsense; rubbish; idle talk
explanation_mandarin: 「唥話」是廣東話的口語/俚語，用來形容無營養、沒意義或荒謬的話語，相當於普通話的「廢話」或「胡說」。通常帶有輕蔑或不耐煩的語氣。
explanation_english: “唥話” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to describe meaningless, pointless, or ridiculous talk — equivalent to Mandarin '廢話' or English 'nonsense'. It often carries a dismissive or impatient tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好講啲唥話，快啲做你應該做嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gong2 di1 long6 waa6, faai3 di1 zou6 nei5 jing1 goi1 zou6 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別說那些廢話，快點去做你該做的事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't talk that nonsense — hurry up and do what you should be doing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我真係冇心情聽你嘅唥話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 mou5 sam1 cing4 teng1 nei5 ge3 long6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我真沒心情聽你的廢話。
examples.english_sentence: I really don't feel like listening to your nonsense.

mandarin_meaning: 唬弄、嚇唬、虛張聲勢
english_meaning: to bluff, to intimidate or scare someone; to fool or show off
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，指用言語或行為嚇唬、唬弄別人或虛張聲勢，常帶貶義或諷刺意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term meaning to intimidate, bluff, or fool someone—often by boasting or pretending; usually derogatory or mocking in tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺街度吹得好勁，其實淨係想唬魆人啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 dou6 ceoi1 dak1 hou2 ging6, kei4 sat6 zing6 hai6 soeng2 fu2 seoi1 jan4 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天在街上吹噓，其實只是想唬弄別人。
examples.english_sentence: He brags on the street all the time; he's actually just trying to fool people.

mandarin_meaning: （比喻）做出大場面、賣弄或故意製造戲劇性場面以博取注意
english_meaning: to put on a big show; to make a scene; to show off or stage a spectacle to attract attention
explanation_mandarin: 原指唱戲曲的表演，口語中常用來比喻故意製造、誇張表現或賣弄以吸引他人注意或博取同情。
explanation_english: Originally referred to performing opera; colloquially it means to deliberately create a spectacle, behave exaggeratedly, or show off to attract attention or sympathy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺公司面前唱大戲，想博取上司注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gung1 si1 min6 cin4 coeng3 daai6 hei3, soeng2 bok3 ceoi2 soeng5 si1 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天在公司面前唱大戲，想博取上司注意。
examples.english_sentence: He always puts on a big show in front of the company to get his boss's attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街度大喊大叫，只係想唱大戲，根本冇真心幫忙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gaai1 dou6 daai6 haam3 daai6 giu3, zi2 hai6 soeng2 coeng3 daai6 hei3, gan1 bun2 mou5 zan1 sam1 bong1 mong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在街上大喊大叫，只是想唱大戲，根本沒有真心幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: He's shouting in the street just to make a scene; he's not really trying to help.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）小口啄食（橄欖），比喻隨意小口吃或只吃一點點
english_meaning: to nibble or peck at (food); colloquially, to pick at food or have a little snack
explanation_mandarin: 字面由「啄」（小口啄、咬）與「欖」（橄欖）組成。在香港口語中用來形容小口吃、隨便嚐幾口或只吃一點東西，有時帶玩笑或輕鬆語氣。
explanation_english: Literally 'peck peck olive' (啄 = peck, 欖 = olive). In Hong Kong colloquial speech it describes nibbling or taking small bites — eating only a little or casually snacking; often said in a light or joking tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔肚餓，就啄啄欖幾啖先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 tou5 ngo6, zau6 zoek3 zoek3 laam5 gei2 daam2 sin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不餓，就先啄幾口吧。
examples.english_sentence: I'm not hungry; I'll just nibble a few bites for now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日只係啄啄欖，唔好以為咁樣就夠飽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 zi2 hai6 zoek3 zoek3 laam5, m4 hou2 ji5 wai6 gam2 joeng6 gau3 baau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是只吃一點小東西，不要以為這樣就飽了。
examples.english_sentence: You keep just nibbling; don't think that will fill you up.

mandarin_meaning: 向巫覡請教、問事（如占卜、驅鬼、求神等）
english_meaning: to consult a shaman/medium (for divination, exorcism, or spirit-related matters)
explanation_mandarin: 「問覡」指向民間的巫覡（祭司、巫師或通靈者）詢問或求助，通常涉及占卜、驅邪、請神等宗教或迷信活動，語境多見於鄉村或傳統習俗中。
explanation_english: “問覡” means to consult a shaman/medium (a traditional spiritual practitioner) for matters such as divination, exorcism, or invoking spirits. It is rooted in folk-religious practices and traditional rituals.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話屋企出事，想請人嚟問覡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 uk1 kei2 ceot1 si6, soeng2 cing2 jan4 lai4 man6 gik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說家裡出了事，想請人來問覡。
examples.english_sentence: He said something happened at home and wants to hire someone to consult a shaman.

mandarin_meaning: 一口；吃一口；喂（人）
english_meaning: a bite; a mouthful; to take a bite; to feed someone a bite
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，「啗」常用作名詞表示一口、一啖的量，也可作動詞表示吃一口或給人吃。多見於口語或日常用語中。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '啗' refers to a bite or mouthful and can be used as a verb meaning to take a bite or feed someone a bite. It is commonly used in colloquial speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你試吓食一啗先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 si3 haa5 sik6 jat1 daam6 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你先试一下吃一口吧。
examples.english_sentence: Try taking a bite first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢碗湯咁正，飲一啗試吓啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wun2 tong1 gam2 zeng3, jam2 jat1 daam6 si3 haa5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这碗汤这么好，喝一口试试吧。
examples.english_sentence: This bowl of soup is great — take a sip to try it.

mandarin_meaning: （啗）一口、咬一口；（擔）負擔、擔載（兩字寫法在粵語口語中有時會互用或混淆）
english_meaning: (啗) a bite / a mouthful; (擔) to carry, to shoulder (note: the characters can be mixed in casual writing, but 啗/啖 commonly means 'mouthful')
explanation_mandarin: 「啗」常用於口語，表示吃一口或一口的份量（如「一啗」）；文字上有時見到用「擔」作代替，需視語境分辨（「擔」本字亦有“擔負、搬運”之義）。
explanation_english: 啗 (啖) commonly means a bite or a mouthful in Cantonese (e.g. "yat1 daam6" = one bite). The character 擔 has a different core meaning (to carry/shoulder), but casual writing/speaking may blur the characters—meaning should be determined from context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你食一啗試下啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 jat1 daam6 si3 haa5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你吃一口试试吧。
examples.english_sentence: Take a bite and try it.

mandarin_meaning: chuò（吮、啜饮；啜泣），表示小口吸飲或抽泣
english_meaning: to sip or suck (a small amount of liquid); also to sob/weep softly (as in '啜泣')
explanation_mandarin: 表示用嘴小口吸、吮或慢慢喝，也可用於描述抽泣、啜泣的動作。
explanation_english: A verb meaning to sip or suck small amounts (of drink), or to sob/weep softly (as in the compound '啜泣').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細細聲啜住杯咖啡，唔想畀人知佢唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 sai3 seng1 ceot3 zyu6 bui1 gaa3 fe1, m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 zi1 keoi5 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他小聲地啜着杯咖啡，不想讓人知道他不開心。
examples.english_sentence: He was quietly sipping his cup of coffee, not wanting people to know he was upset.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 深夜聽到樓上有啲人啜泣，聲音好心酸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sam1 je6 teng1 dou2 lau4 soeng6 jau5 di1 jan4 ceot3 zap1, seng1 jam1 hou2 sam1 syun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 深夜聽到樓上有人啜泣，聲音很心酸。
examples.english_sentence: Late at night I heard someone upstairs sobbing; the sound was heartbreaking.

mandarin_meaning: 拟声词，形容轻微的清嗓或咳嗽声，也可用于形容含糊、不太肯定的低声嘟囔
english_meaning: An onomatopoeic expression imitating a soft throat-clearing or light cough sound; can also describe a hesitant or muffled murmur
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 拟声词（可作名词或副词性用法）
partOfSpeech_english: onomatopoeia (used as a noun or adverbial/interjection)
explanation_mandarin: “啡啡聲”常见于粤语口语，是模仿轻微清嗓或咳嗽的声音。语境上也可表示说话含糊、犹豫或不愿直接说明时发出的低声声音。属于口语拟声用法，偏口语或俚语色彩。
explanation_english: “啡啡聲” is a Cantonese onomatopoeic, colloquial term that imitates a soft throat-clearing or light coughing sound. In context it can also indicate hesitant, muffled, or evasive murmuring. It is mainly used in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺會議入面啡啡聲，好似唔太投入。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 wui6 ji5 jap6 min6 fe1 fe1 sing1, hou2 ci5 m4 taai3 tau4 jap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在会议里面发出啡啡声，好像不太投入。
examples.english_sentence: He was making 'feh-feh' noises in the meeting, as if not very engaged.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友病咗，夜晚會發啡啡聲，要帶佢去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 beng6 zo2, je6 maan5 wui5 faat3 fe1 fe1 sing1, jiu3 daai3 keoi5 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友生病了，晚上会发出啡啡声，要带他去看医生。
examples.english_sentence: The kid is ill and makes 'feh-feh' noises at night; you should take him to the doctor.

mandarin_meaning: 啤酒箱；啤酒盒
english_meaning: beer crate / beer box
explanation_mandarin: 指用來裝啤酒的箱或盒，通常指成箱或多瓶（罐）包裝的啤酒容器。
explanation_english: Refers to a box or crate used to hold beer, typically meaning a packaged set of multiple bottles or cans.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 超市有賣啤盒，一盒有十二支啤酒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ciu1 si5 jau5 maai6 be1 hap6, jat1 hap6 jau5 sap6 ji6 zi1 be1 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 超市有賣啤酒箱，一箱有十二瓶啤酒。
examples.english_sentence: The supermarket sells beer crates; a crate has twelve bottles of beer.

mandarin_meaning: 嘈杂声；无意义的闲聊或唠叨
english_meaning: chatter; meaningless talk or noisy clamor
explanation_mandarin: 通常用來形容嘈雜、沒實質內容的談話或噪音，帶有貶義，指令人煩擾的嘈吵或閒聊。
explanation_english: Refers to noisy, meaningless chatter or clamor. Often used derogatorily to describe annoying, purposeless talk or noise.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係講啲啦啦聲，講返有用嘅建議啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 gong2 di1 laa1 laa1 seng1, gong2 faan1 jau5 jung6 ge3 gin3 ji3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只是說些沒意義的話，說點有用的建議吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just talk nonsense; give some useful suggestions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日聽到隔離樓傳嚟啲啦啦聲，好嘈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 teng1 dou3 gaak3 lei4 lau4 cyun4 lai4 di1 laa1 laa1 seng1, hou2 cou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 总是听到隔壁楼传来一些嘈杂声，很吵。
examples.english_sentence: I keep hearing noisy chatter from the neighboring building; it's very noisy.

mandarin_meaning: 按钮（按鈕）；引申：触发点、激怒某人的“按键”
english_meaning: button (literal); figuratively: a trigger or 'press someone's button' (to provoke)
explanation_mandarin: 「啪紐」字面上指會發出啪聲或可被按的紐/鈕（按鈕）。在口語或俚語中可用來比喻某個能觸發反應的地方或行為，即“觸發點/按到某人底線”。
explanation_english: Literally a button (one that might make a 'paak' sound). In Cantonese slang it can also be used figuratively as a trigger or the thing that provokes someone (to 'press someone's button').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 部相機個啪紐好易壞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou6 soeng1 gei1 go3 paak3 nau2 hou2 ji6 waai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這台相機的按鈕很容易壞。
examples.english_sentence: The camera's button breaks easily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好亂啪佢個紐，佢會嬲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lyun6 paak3 keoi5 go3 nau2, keoi5 wui5 nau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別亂按他的按鈕，他會生氣。
examples.english_sentence: Don't randomly press his button; he'll get angry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 一啪紐就開燈，好方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat1 paak3 nau2 zau6 hoi1 dang1, hou2 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一按按鈕就開燈，很方便。
examples.english_sentence: Press the button and the light turns on — very convenient.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）唠叨、啰嗦
english_meaning: nagging; long-winded; annoyingly talkative
explanation_mandarin: 「啰啋」為廣東話口語用詞，常用來描述一個人說話囉唆、愛唠叨或嘮叨不斷，等同於「啰唆」或「嘮叨」。主要在香港粵語口語中使用，帶有些許抱怨或嫌煩的語感。
explanation_english: “啰啋” is a colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe someone who is nagging, long-winded, or annoyingly talkative. It is equivalent to “啰唆/嘮叨” and often carries a tone of complaint or irritation in everyday Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日咁啰啋，真係好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gam2 lo1 so1, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天這樣唠叨，真煩。
examples.english_sentence: He/She keeps nagging like that all the time; it's really annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日對住我咁啰啋，我聽唔落！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 deoi3 zyu6 ngo5 gam2 lo1 so1, teng1 m4 lok6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別總是對我這麼唠叨，我聽不下去了！
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep nagging me like that; I can't listen anymore!

mandarin_meaning: 正好 / 剛好 / 合適
english_meaning: just right; just so; happens to be (exactly/right)
explanation_mandarin: 表示時間、數量或程度剛好，或表示某物剛合適；有時也表示碰巧（正好）。
explanation_english: Indicates that something is exactly right in timing, amount, or degree, or that something fits perfectly; can also mean 'happens to be' (by coincidence).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啱好佢嚟到，我哋可以開始。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngaam1 hou2 keoi5 lai4 dou3, ngo5 dei6 ho2 ji5 hoi1 ci2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 正好他/她到了，我們可以開始。
examples.english_sentence: He/she has just arrived, so we can start.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫啱好我個碼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 ngaam1 hou2 ngo5 go3 maa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件衣服剛好是我的尺寸。
examples.english_sentence: This shirt fits me perfectly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱好冇事，可以幫你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ngaam1 hou2 mou5 si6, ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我正好沒事，可以幫你。
examples.english_sentence: I'm free right now; I can help you.

mandarin_meaning: 正巧；恰好
english_meaning: by chance; coincidentally; as it happens
explanation_mandarin: 表示某件事正好發生或湊巧發生，常用於口語中。
explanation_english: Indicates that something happened by coincidence or just happened to be the case; commonly used in colloquial Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啱巧我今日都有一張多餘嘅飛，可以俾你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngaam1 haau2 ngo5 gam1 jat6 dou1 jau5 jat1 zoeng1 do1 jyu4 ge3 fei1, ho2 ji5 bei2 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 正巧我今天也有一张多余的票，可以给你。
examples.english_sentence: By chance, I also have an extra ticket today; I can give it to you.

mandarin_meaning: 合適、對胃口；恰到好處；（也可指）容易掌握要領、懂門道
