examples.english_sentence: Those two are always together; people call them 'twin chimneys'.

mandarin_meaning: 並排站立；（口語）也可指兩個相鄰的車站
english_meaning: to stand side-by-side; (colloquial) two adjacent stations
explanation_mandarin: 「孖站」是廣東話口語用法。常用來形容兩個人並肩站着、一起等候（例如在巴士站、排隊時）。在某些語境下，也可用來指兩個相鄰或相近的車站（例如步行距離很近的兩個地鐵站），帶有口語色彩。
explanation_english: “孖站” is Cantonese colloquial usage. It commonly describes two people standing side-by-side or waiting together (e.g., at a bus stop or in a queue). In some contexts it can also refer to two adjacent or very close stations (e.g., two MTR stations within walking distance). It is informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺巴士站孖站等車，唔好阻住人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 baa1 si6 zaam6 maa1 zaam6 dang2 ce1, m4 hou2 zo2 zyu6 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在巴士站並肩等車，別擋住別人。
examples.english_sentence: We're standing side-by-side at the bus stop waiting for the bus; don't block others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 中環同金鐘係孖站，行路好近。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zung1 waan4 tung4 gam1 zung1 hai6 maa1 zaam6, haang4 lou6 hou2 gan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 中環和金鐘可以說是相鄰的兩個站，步行很近。
examples.english_sentence: Central and Admiralty are like twin stations; they're very close on foot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢同個朋友孖站排隊買波鞋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tung4 go3 pang4 jau5 maa1 zaam6 paai4 deoi6 maai5 bo1 haai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他和朋友並肩排隊買運動鞋。
examples.english_sentence: He and his friend stood side-by-side in line to buy sneakers.

mandarin_meaning: 字纸篮（废纸篓），用于放废纸或草稿；也可比喻把不需要的文字或想法丢弃的地方
english_meaning: scrap-paper basket; a bin for discarded notes or drafts; figuratively, a place where unwanted writing or ideas are thrown away
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，指放置廢紙、草稿的籃子或容器。常用於學校或辦公室，也可作比喻，指被放棄或不被採納的文字、想法或草稿。
explanation_english: A colloquial term for a basket/container used to hold scrap paper or drafts. Common in schools or offices; can also be used metaphorically for discarded or rejected writing, ideas, or drafts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲唔要嘅草稿我擲咗入字紙籮啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 m4 jiu3 ge3 cou2 gok3 ngo5 zaak6 zo2 jap6 zi6 zi2 lo4 laa3
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些不要的草稿我已經丟進字紙籃了。
examples.english_sentence: I threw the unwanted drafts into the scrap-paper basket.

mandarin_meaning: 吝嗇；小氣
english_meaning: stingy; miserly; tightfisted
explanation_mandarin: 「孤寒鐸/孤寒度」是香港廣東話的俗語，用來形容一個人非常吝嗇、小氣。後綴的「鐸/度」為口語變體，強調程度或語氣，屬非正式用法。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning extremely stingy or miserly. The suffix 鐸 or 度 is a colloquial variant used to add emphasis. Informal and commonly used in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係孤寒鐸，連一蚊都唔肯俾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 gu1 hon4 dok6, lin4 jat1 man1 dou1 m4 hang2 bei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的是很吝嗇，連一塊錢都不肯給。
examples.english_sentence: He's really stingy; he won't even give a dollar.

mandarin_meaning: 爱说是非；指责或评判他人的对错
english_meaning: to nitpick or criticize others; to gossip/judge who's right and wrong
explanation_mandarin: 口语表达，用来形容喜欢评头论足、挑剔或指责别人是非的人，带有贬义。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who likes to judge, nitpick, or criticize others' right and wrong; carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鍾意學是學非，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zung1 ji3 hok6 si6 hok6 fei1, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是爱说是非，弄得大家不开心。
examples.english_sentence: He is always nitpicking and criticizing others, which makes everyone unhappy.

mandarin_meaning: （俗語、罵人用語）孫子／混蛋（粗俗）
english_meaning: a vulgar slang insult roughly meaning 'bastard' or 'little rascal' (lit. 'grandson')
explanation_mandarin: 「孫𤆵」是廣東話口語裡的罵人用語，字面上含有「孫子／孫輩」之意，但用作蔑稱或咒罵。此詞帶有強烈貶義與粗俗色彩，主要在香港粵語口語或網絡語境出現。字中使用的古字（𤆵）較罕見，在書寫上有時以「孫子」「孫仔」等更常見的字替代。
explanation_english: “孫𤆵” is a Cantonese colloquial insult. Literally referencing a 'grandson', it is used pejoratively like 'bastard' or 'little rascal'. The phrase is vulgar and commonly found in spoken Hong Kong Cantonese or online; the rare character 𤆵 is sometimes replaced by more common characters (e.g., 孫子).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你個孫𤆵又遲到喇，唔好再嚟借口啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 go3 syun1 gei1 jau6 ci4 dou3 laa3, m4 hou2 zoi3 lai4 ze3 hau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這個孫𤆵又遲到了，別再找藉口了。
examples.english_sentence: Your little bastard is late again — don't make excuses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁講佢，雖然佢係個孫𤆵，但都唔值得咁罵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 gong2 keoi5, seoi1 jin4 keoi5 hai6 go3 syun1 gei1, daan6 dou1 m4 zik1 dak1 gam2 maa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別那樣罵他，雖然他是個孫𤆵，但也不值得那麼罵。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say that about him. Even if he's a little bastard, he doesn't deserve that much abuse.

mandarin_meaning: 承擔／背負（責任、過失、包袱等）
english_meaning: to shoulder; to bear (responsibility, blame, burden)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，表示承擔或背負某種責任、過失或包袱，常用於指被迫或不得已承擔不屬於自己的責任。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to take on or shoulder a responsibility, blame, or burden—often implying being forced or unfairly made to bear something that may not be one's own.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司出事，我唔想孭戴責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ceot1 si6, ngo5 m4 soeng2 jip3 daai3 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司出了問題，我不想承擔責任。
examples.english_sentence: The company got into trouble; I don't want to take on the responsibility.

mandarin_meaning: 承担（一般为替他人）过错或责任；背黑锅、替人顶罪
english_meaning: to take the blame (often for someone else); to be made a scapegoat; to shoulder unwanted responsibility
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，表示替別人承擔過錯或責任，常含被冤枉或不情願的意思。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to take the blame for someone else or to be forced to accept blame; often implies being unfairly blamed or unwillingly taking responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想孭鑊，呢樣嘢唔係我做嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 nip1 wok6, ni1 joeng6 je5 m4 hai6 ngo5 zou6 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想替別人背黑鍋，這件事不是我做的。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to take the blame; I didn't do this.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日要孭鑊，成個部門出事佢就要孭鑊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 jiu3 nip1 wok6, sing4 go3 bou6 mun4 ceot1 si6 keoi5 zau6 jiu3 nip1 wok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常要替人背鍋，整個部門出問題就由他來承擔責任。
examples.english_sentence: He often has to take the blame; whenever the department has a problem, he ends up taking the fall.

mandarin_meaning: 學別人說閒話／學別人重複無營養的話
english_meaning: to imitate/parrot others' idle talk or gossip; to copy what others say without thinking
explanation_mandarin: 「學人口水溦」是廣東話口語，指模仿或重複別人的閒言閒語或無聊說話，帶有批評或貶義，暗示缺乏主見或盲目跟從。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to imitate or parrot someone else's idle chatter or gossip. It carries a mildly critical tone, implying lack of independent thought or blindly following others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咪成日學人口水溦啦，做嘢自己諗啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 mai4 sing4 jat6 hok6 jan4 hau2 seoi2 wai1 laa1, zou6 je5 zi6 gei2 lam2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別總是學別人說閒話了，做事自己想吧。
examples.english_sentence: Stop always copying other people's gossip; think for yourself when you work.

mandarin_meaning: 人云亦云；照搬别人的话，不加思考地重复或模仿
english_meaning: to parrot; to repeat others' words without independent thought; to mimic speech
explanation_mandarin: 指不加思考、机械地模仿或重复别人的话，常用来批评缺乏独立思考或盲从。
explanation_english: Refers to repeating or imitating what others say without thinking; often used to criticize a lack of independent thought or blind conformity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日學口學舌，冇自己意見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hok6 hau2 hok6 sit3, mou5 zi6 gei2 ji3 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是人云亦云，沒有自己的意見。
examples.english_sentence: He always parrots others and has no opinion of his own.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲學生只會學口學舌，唔肯自己思考。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 hok6 saang1 zi2 wui5 hok6 hau2 hok6 sit3, m4 hang2 zi6 gei2 si1 haau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些學生只會人云亦云，不肯獨立思考。
examples.english_sentence: Those students only parrot others and won't think independently.

mandarin_meaning: 懦弱／膽小鬼
english_meaning: coward; timid person; weakling
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞 / 形容詞（口語、貶義）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來形容一個人懦弱、膽小、不敢面對困難或挑戰。可作名詞（「佢係個孻尾」）或形容詞（「你好孻尾」），屬於非正式、帶貶義的用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term for someone who is cowardly or timid. It can be used as a noun ("He's a 孻尾") or an adjective ("You're so 孻尾"). Informal and derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日退縮，係個孻尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 teoi3 seok3, hai6 go3 naai6 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是退縮，是個懦弱的人。
examples.english_sentence: He always backs down; he's a coward.

cantonese: 宁可得罪君子，不可得罪小人
jyutping: ning4 ho2 dak1 zeoi6 gwan1 zi2, bat1 ho2 dak1 zeoi6 siu2 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 宁可得罪有德之人，也不要得罪心胸狭窄、爱记仇、会报复的小人。
english_meaning: Better to offend a virtuous/honorable person than to offend a petty, vindictive person.
explanation_mandarin: 意思是宁愿得罪品德高的人，也不要得罪容易记恨、会陷害或报复别人的小人，因为后者更可能给自己带来麻烦或不利后果。
explanation_english: The saying advises that it's preferable to offend an honorable person rather than a small-minded, vindictive one, since the latter are more likely to cause trouble, seek revenge, or harm you socially or professionally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做事好小心，寧可得罪君子，不可得罪小人，唔想惹到小人報復。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 hou2 siu2 sam1, ning4 ho2 dak1 zeoi6 gwan1 zi2, bat1 ho2 dak1 zeoi6 siu2 jan4, m4 soeng2 je5 dou3 siu2 jan4 bou3 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很小心，宁可得罪君子，不可得罪小人，不想招来小人的报复。
examples.english_sentence: He is very careful in his actions; he'd rather offend an honorable person than a petty one because he doesn't want to provoke a petty person's revenge.

cantonese: 宁愿隔篱车水，唔愿隔篱中举
jyutping: ning4 jyun6 gaak3 lei4 ce1 seoi2, m4 jyun6 gaak3 lei4 zung1 geoi2
mandarin_meaning: 宁愿隔着篱笆看到车水马龙，也不愿看到隔壁有人中举（取得显赫功名）
english_meaning: Would rather the neighbours' street be bustling than have someone next door achieve a great success — expresses preferring ordinary prosperity or being unwilling to see someone nearby outshine you.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粤语俗语，用来表达对邻里或身边人出人头地的忌妒或不愿被比下去的心态：宁可邻居平凡热闹，也不愿有人取得显赫地位（如中举）。含有小市民的妒忌或怕被比下去的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverbial saying that conveys envy or reluctance to see someone nearby achieve outstanding success. It implies a preference for neighbours to remain ordinary or busy rather than become notably successful — reflects petty jealousy or the desire not to be outshone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽成日講：寧願隔篱車水，唔願隔篱中举，佢唔想鄰居個仔贏過我哋個仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 gong2: ning4 jyun6 gaak3 lei4 ce1 seoi2, m4 jyun6 gaak3 lei4 zung1 geoi2, keoi5 m4 soeng2 leon4 geoi1 go3 zai2 jing4 gwo3 ngo5 dei6 go3 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我妈妈常说：宁愿隔篱车水，唔愿隔篱中举，她不希望邻居的孩子比我们的孩子更出人头地。
examples.english_sentence: My mother often says, 'I'd rather see the neighbours' street bustling than see someone next door succeed' — she doesn't want the neighbour's child to outshine ours.

synonyms: 寧願鄰居平凡，唔願佢出頭

cantonese: 宁教人打仔，莫教人分妻
jyutping: ning4 gaau3 jan4 daa2 zai2, mok6 gaau3 jan4 fan1 cai1
mandarin_meaning: 宁可让别人打孩子，也不要让别人拆散夫妻；比喻宁可吃小亏，不可遭受更大的损失或祸害。
english_meaning: Better to suffer a minor harm than a major one; literally 'better to let someone beat the child than let someone split the wife' — i.e. choose the lesser of two evils to protect the marriage or avoid a greater loss.
explanation_mandarin: 這是廣東話的俗語，字面意思是寧可受小的委屈，也不可讓人拆散夫妻。引申為在兩害相權時，要選擇較小的損失以保留更重要的事物（如家庭或婚姻）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb whose literal wording contrasts tolerating a lesser wrong with avoiding a greater calamity (preserving a marriage). It advises choosing the lesser of two evils to protect what matters more.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗保住婚姻，佢哋決定忍讓，寧教人打仔，莫教人分妻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 bou2 zyu6 fan1 jan1, keoi5 dei6 kyut3 ding6 jan2 joeng6, ning4 gaau3 jan4 daa2 zai2, mok6 gaau3 jan4 fan1 cai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了保住婚姻，他们决定忍让，宁可让别人打孩子，也不要让别人拆散夫妻。
examples.english_sentence: To preserve their marriage they decided to yield — better to suffer a small wrong than to have someone break up the marriage.

synonyms: 宁可吃小亏，不可遭大祸

cantonese: 宁欺白须公，莫欺鼻涕虫
jyutping: ning4 hei1 baak6 sou1 gung1, mok6 hei1 bei6 tai3 cung4
mandarin_meaning: 宁可欺负白胡子老人，也不要欺负流鼻涕的小孩（即不要欺负弱小或无助的人）
english_meaning: Don't bully or take advantage of the little ones/innocent; don't underestimate or mistreat the weak
explanation_mandarin: 这是句粤语俗语，用来劝诫或提醒人不要欺负小孩子或弱者，强调不要轻视或欺凌看似无助的人，因为他们可能有依靠或将来会反击。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb advising people not to bully children or the weak; it warns against underestimating or mistreating those who seem helpless, since they may have protectors or may retaliate later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日欺負細路，我就對佢講：「宁欺白须公，莫欺鼻涕虫」，唔好欺負小朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hei1 fu6 sai3 lou6, ngo5 zau6 deoi3 keoi5 gong2: "ning4 hei1 baak6 sou1 gung1, mok6 hei1 bei6 tai3 cung4", m4 hou2 hei1 fu6 siu2 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常欺负小孩，我就对他说：“宁欺白须公，莫欺鼻涕虫”，别欺负小朋友。
examples.english_sentence: He often bullies kids; I told him, '宁欺白须公，莫欺鼻涕虫' — don't bully children.

cantonese: 宁食开眉粥，唔食愁眉饭
jyutping: ning4 sik6 hoi1 mei4 zuk1, m4 sik6 cau4 mei4 faan6
mandarin_meaning: 寧可清貧而快樂，不願富有卻愁苦
english_meaning: Better to be poor but happy than rich but worried.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東俗語用「開眉粥」和「愁眉飯」作對比，意思是寧願生活清苦但心情愉快，也不要有錢卻心事重重、憂愁不安。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb that contrasts 'congee with open brows' and 'rice with worried brows' — it means one should prefer a simple life with happiness over wealth accompanied by anxiety.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做人最緊要開心，寧食開眉粥，唔食愁眉飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 jan4 zeoi3 gan2 jiu3 hoi1 sam1, ning4 sik6 hoi1 mei4 zuk1, m4 sik6 cau4 mei4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做人最重要的是開心，寧可生活簡樸快樂，也不要富有卻憂愁。
examples.english_sentence: What's most important is being happy — better to live simply and happily than to be wealthy but worried.

synonyms: 寧可清貧開心，不可富有愁苦

cantonese: 宁食飞天四两，唔食地上本斤
jyutping: ning4 sik6 fei1 tin1 sei3 loeng5, m4 sik6 dei6 soeng5 bun2 gan1
mandarin_meaning: 宁可接受小而正当的利益，也不接受看似更多但不正当或不光彩的收益。
english_meaning: Better to take a small, honest gain than a larger gain that is dishonorable or illicit.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東俗語用對比的方式表達一個道德取向：寧可接受少量但正當、清白的利益（比喻為「飛天四兩」），也不願意接受雖多但來源可疑、不光彩或不合道德的收益（比喻為「地上本斤」）。常用來勸人守規矩、重視清白。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb contrasts a small, legitimate gain with a larger but dishonorable one. It advises that one should prefer modest but honest earnings (the “four taels from the sky”) rather than bigger gains that are questionable or shameful (the “full catty on the ground”). It’s used to encourage integrity and avoid dirty money or illicit deals.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話寧食飛天四兩，唔食地上本斤，寧願收少少合法嘅佣金，都唔會做偷雞嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 ning4 sik6 fei1 tin1 sei3 loeng5, m4 sik6 dei6 soeng5 bun2 gan1, ning4 jyun6 sau1 siu2 siu2 hap6 faat3 ge3 jung4 gam1, dou1 m4 wui5 zou6 tau1 gai1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说宁可吃天上掉下来的四两，不吃地上本斤，宁愿收一点合法的佣金，也不会去做偷鸡摸狗的勾当。
examples.english_sentence: He says he'd rather take the four taels that fall from the sky than the full catty on the ground — he'd accept a small legitimate commission rather than doing sneaky, dishonest deals.

synonyms: 寧食飛來四兩，不食地上半斤
宁可清白无财，不要肮脏之财

jyutping: sau2 dak1 wan4 hoi1 gin3 jyut6 ming4
mandarin_meaning: 坚持忍耐，困境终会过去，最终会看到希望或好转。
english_meaning: Persevere through hardships and you will see the light; enduring difficulties will lead to improvement or success.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻只要忍耐堅持，經歷的困難會過去，情況會好轉，看到希望。
explanation_english: An expression meaning that if one endures and persists through hard times, the situation will eventually improve and hope will appear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 經歷咗咁多挫折，佢而家終於守得雲開見月明，事業有起色。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging1 lik6 zo2 gam2 do1 co3 zit3, keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zung1 jyu1 sau2 dak1 wan4 hoi1 gin3 jyut6 ming4, si6 jip6 jau5 hei2 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 经历了这么多挫折，他现在终于守得云开见月明，事业有起色。
examples.english_sentence: After going through so many setbacks, he has finally persevered and his career is starting to look up.

mandarin_meaning: 維持生計；謀生的手段（指有飯吃、有收入）
english_meaning: livelihood; means of making a living; bread-and-butter
explanation_mandarin: 「安樂茶飯」是廣東話俗語，指維持生活所需的收入或謀生手段，常用來表示為了糊口而做某事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression referring to the income or means needed to sustain one's life; commonly used to indicate doing something to earn a living.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我做呢份工只係為咗有安樂茶飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zou6 ni1 fan6 gung1 zi2 hai6 wai6 zo2 jau5 on1 lok6 caa4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我做這份工作只是為了能維持生計。
examples.english_sentence: I do this job just to have a livelihood.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗安樂茶飯，乜都肯做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 on1 lok6 caa4 faan6, mat1 dou1 hang2 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了維持生計，什麼都肯做。
examples.english_sentence: He'll do anything to make a living.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）把螺絲固定／把事情處理妥當（「定螺絲」的簡稱）
english_meaning: (colloq.) to tighten/secure a screw; (figurative) to make something secure or put matters in order (abbrev. of 'tighten the screw')
explanation_mandarin: 「定螺」多為口語用法，常作「定螺絲」的簡短說法。字面上指把螺絲鎖緊以固定物件；引申可指把事情處理穩妥、不留後患。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression, usually a shortened form of '定螺絲' (tighten the screw). Literally means to tighten a screw to secure something; figuratively it means to fix or secure a matter so nothing is left loose.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 張椅腳鬆咗，要定螺先穩陣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng1 ji2 goek3 sung1 zo2, jiu3 ding6 lo4 sin1 wan2 zan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 椅子腳鬆了，要把螺絲固定先穩當。
examples.english_sentence: The chair leg is loose; we need to tighten the screw first so it's stable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好細心，成件事都會定螺，唔會爛尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 sai3 sam1, sing4 gin6 si6 dou1 wui5 ding6 lo4, m4 wui5 laan6 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很細心，事情都會處理妥當，不會爛尾。
examples.english_sentence: He works carefully and always secures everything properly; nothing gets left unfinished.

mandarin_meaning: （疑似粤语地区口语/俚语）大致意思为“已成定局/已经决定、无法更改/非常肯定”，但该用语并非标准书面词汇，存在地区性和用法差异。
english_meaning: A regional/colloquial Cantonese phrase roughly meaning "already decided; a done deal; nothing can be changed," or "completely certain." It is not a widely documented standard idiom and is regionally used.
explanation_mandarin: “定過”在粤语里可解释为“已经决定/定下”，而“擡油”字面意义不明，可能为地区性加强调式的口语成分。合起来常用来表示事情已成定局、无法更改，或形容某人对某事非常肯定。由于该短语在正规词典中少见，具体来源与用法存在不同说法，应注意为方言/俚语用法。
explanation_english: “Ding gwo toi jau” combines "ding gwo" (already decided/past) with a regionally used particle/phrase "toi jau" whose literal meaning is unclear. Together it is used colloquially to indicate that something is a done deal or that someone is absolutely certain. The phrase is regional/slang and not widely recorded in standard references, so usage and nuance can vary by locality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲嘢已經講晒，嗰單交易已經定過擡油，冇得反悔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 je5 ji5 ging1 gong2 saai3, go2 daan1 gaau1 jik6 ji5 ging1 ding6 gwo3 toi4 jau4, mou5 dak1 faan2 fui2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 事情都已经谈妥，那笔交易已经定了，不能反悔。
examples.english_sentence: Everything's been agreed— that deal is already set in stone; no backing out.

mandarin_meaning: 确定；决定；（表示肯定）
english_meaning: to decide; to determine; definite; certainly
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 动词 / 形容词 / 副词
explanation_mandarin: 在粤语中，“定”（讀 ding6）可作动词表示“决定”（如“你定咗未？”），亦可表示肯定或确定（相当于“一定/肯定”）。用法灵活，常见于口语。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '定' (ding6) can mean 'to decide' when used as a verb, and can also express certainty ('definitely'). It is commonly used in colloquial speech to ask whether someone has made a decision or to state something is certain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你定咗未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ding6 zo2 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你决定了吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you decided yet?

mandarin_meaning: 确凿；确凿无疑
english_meaning: conclusive; irrefutable; indisputable
explanation_mandarin: 表示證據或說法非常確實、無可置疑。常用來形容結論或證據非常可靠、難以反駁。
explanation_english: Indicates that evidence or a statement is solid and beyond doubt. Used to describe conclusions or proof that are reliable and hard to refute.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份報告寫得實斧實凿，冇人可以反駁佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 se2 dak1 sat6 fu2 sat6 zaak6, mou5 jan4 ho2 ji5 faan2 bok3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这份报告写得确凿无疑，没人可以反驳它。
examples.english_sentence: This report is written with conclusive evidence; no one can refute it.

mandarin_meaning: 直率；坦率；说话直截了当
english_meaning: straightforward; blunt; frank
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，形容說話或為人直率、不拐彎抹角，講話坦白、直截了當。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone who is blunt or forthright in speech or manner—speaks plainly without beating around the bush.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢實牙實齒，唔會拐彎抹角。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 sat6 ngaa4 sat6 ci2, m4 wui5 gwaai2 waan1 mut6 gok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話直率，不拐彎抹角。
examples.english_sentence: He speaks bluntly and doesn't beat around the bush.

mandarin_meaning: 真的，沒有騙你
english_meaning: For real; I'm not lying to you
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俚語，用來強調說話的真實性或保證沒有欺騙，類似「真的、不是騙你的」。常見於香港日常對話或網絡用語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to emphasize that the speaker is telling the truth or giving a genuine assurance — similar to "for real" or "I'm not lying to you." Common in Hong Kong spoken and online usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你信唔信我？实食冇黐牙，我真係冇呃你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 seon3 m4 seon3 ngo5? sat6 sik6 mou5 ci1 ngaa4, ngo5 zan1 hai6 mou5 aak1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你信不信我？真的，我沒有騙你。
examples.english_sentence: Do you believe me? For real — I'm not lying to you.

mandarin_meaning: 家居环境 / 居家环境，指家庭内部或居住环境的状况
english_meaning: home environment; the living environment within a household
explanation_mandarin: 指家庭內部或居住環境的整體狀況，包括居住空間、衛生、設備及周邊環境等，會影響居住者的健康與生活品質。
explanation_english: Refers to the overall condition of the household living environment, including living space, hygiene, facilities and surrounding environment; it affects occupants' health and quality of life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 家居環境好重要，會影響小朋友嘅健康同情緒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaa1 geoi1 waan4 ging2 hou2 zung6 jiu3, wui5 jing2 hoeng2 siu2 pang4 jau5 ge3 gin6 hong1 tung4 cing4 seoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家居环境很重要，会影响小朋友的健康和情绪。
examples.english_sentence: The home environment is very important; it can affect children's health and emotions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗改善家居環境，我哋打算重新裝修廚房同浴室。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 goi2 sin6 gaa1 geoi1 waan4 ging2, ngo5 dei6 daa2 syun3 cung4 san1 zong1 sau1 cyu4 fong2 tung4 juk6 sat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了改善家居环境，我们打算重新装修厨房和浴室。
examples.english_sentence: To improve the home environment, we plan to renovate the kitchen and bathroom.

mandarin_meaning: 在家生孩子；在家分娩
english_meaning: to give birth at home; homebirth
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語表達，指在自己家裡分娩或在家生孩子，而不是到醫院產房生產。可用來描述計劃在家分娩或實際發生的情況。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to give birth at home (homebirth) — delivering a baby at one's residence rather than in a hospital. It can describe a planned homebirth or an actual event.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢老婆打算家生仔，唔想喺醫院分娩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lou5 po4 daa2 syun3 gaa1 saang1 zai2, m4 soeng2 hai6 ji1 jyun2 fan1 min5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老婆打算在家生孩子，不想在医院分娩。
examples.english_sentence: His wife plans to give birth at home; she doesn't want to deliver in a hospital.

mandarin_meaning: 不常见或不確定的詞語，可能是打字/聽寫錯誤，或地方口語、擬聲詞，沒有標準普通話對應
english_meaning: A rare or uncertain term—possibly a typo, mishearing, a dialectal expression, or an onomatopoeia; no established standard meaning in English
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 未知（非標準詞彙/可能不是詞）
partOfSpeech_english: unknown (non-standard/possibly not a real lexical item)
explanation_mandarin: 「宿亨亨」並非廣泛承認的標準廣東話詞彙。查無固定詞義，常見情況是作為網上用語、打字錯誤或地方口語。使用時應提示為不確定詞，並可詢問發話者原意。
explanation_english: “宿亨亨” is not a widely recognized standard Cantonese lexical item. It has no fixed meaning and may appear as an online nonce word, a typo, a regional/dialectal term, or an onomatopoeic expression. Treat it as uncertain and ask the speaker for clarification when encountered.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我見有人打「宿亨亨」，唔知係咪打錯字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gin3 jau5 jan4 daa2 'suk6 hang1 hang1', m4 zi1 hai6 mai6 daa2 co3 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我看到有人打「宿亨亨」，不知道是不是打錯字。
examples.english_sentence: I saw someone type "宿亨亨" and I don't know if it's a typo.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你聽過「宿亨亨」，可唔可以同我講下意思？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 teng1 gwo3 'suk6 hang1 hang1', ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 tung4 ngo5 gong2 haa5 ji3 si1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你聽過「宿亨亨」，可以跟我說一下意思嗎？
examples.english_sentence: If you've heard "宿亨亨", can you tell me what it means?

mandarin_meaning: 密密麻麻 / 擠得很緊密
english_meaning: densely packed; very crowded; tightly compacted
explanation_mandarin: 「密厔厔」為廣東話口語擬聲／疊字用法，用來形容物件、人群等排列得很緊密或場面非常擁擠。書寫上較少見，多見於口語或地域性說法。
explanation_english: “密厔厔” is a Cantonese colloquial reduplicative/onamatopoeic expression used to describe something (or a crowd) that is very densely packed or tightly compacted. It is primarily spoken and less often written.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個巴士上面人密厔厔，連位都冇得坐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 baa1 si2 soeng6 min6 jan4 mat6 zat6 zat6, lin4 wai2 dou1 mou5 dak1 co5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公共汽車上人密密麻麻，連座位都沒有得坐。
examples.english_sentence: The bus was packed tight — there wasn't even a seat to sit on.

jyutping: mat6 sat6 gu1 neoi5 gaa2 zing3 ging1
mandarin_meaning: 看似端庄實則虛偽或裝作正經的女生
english_meaning: a girl who pretends to be proper/respectable but is actually hypocritical or not as prim as she seems
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容表面裝作乖巧、端莊，但實際上虛偽或行為不正經的女孩，帶有貶義與調侃意味。
explanation_english: Used to describe a girl who puts on a prim/proper front but is actually hypocritical or not genuinely proper; carries a mocking or derogatory tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日扮乖，其實係密实姑娘假正经。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 baan6 gwaai1, kei4 sat6 hai6 mat6 sat6 gu1 neoi5 gaa2 zing3 ging1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她整天裝乖，其實是個假正經的姑娘。
examples.english_sentence: She acts well-behaved all the time, but in fact she's a girl who pretends to be proper.

mandarin_meaning: 结实/壮实的姑娘
english_meaning: a well-built/solid girl; a sturdy or curvy girl
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语/俚语，形容女孩子身材结实、不瘦、看起来有肉感或有肌肉感。视语境可为中性或褒义，有时也带调侃或轻微情色意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term describing a girl who is physically solid or well-built—not thin, often firm or fleshy. It can be neutral or complimentary, and in some contexts teasing or mildly sexual.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係一個密實姑娘，唔似啲好瘦嘅女仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jat1 go3 mat6 sat6 gu1 neoi5, m4 ci5 di1 hou2 sou3 ge3 neoi5 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她是一个结实的姑娘，不像那些很瘦的女孩。
examples.english_sentence: She's a well-built girl, not like those very thin girls.

mandarin_meaning: 暗中算计；暗自谋划（多含贬义）
english_meaning: secret scheming; hidden calculations or plots (usually pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 指在背后偷偷盘算、谋划，常用于形容为私利而暗中算计他人的行为。
explanation_english: Refers to secretly plotting or making covert calculations, often with negative connotations — describing someone who privately schemes for their own benefit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺公司度密底算盘，想爭上位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gung1 si1 dou6 mat6 dai2 syun3 pun4, soeng2 zeng1 soeng5 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在公司暗中打算计，想争夺升职。
examples.english_sentence: He is secretly scheming at the company, trying to get promoted.

jyutping: mat6 dai2 syun3 pun4, mou5 lau6 laat6
mandarin_meaning: 计划/算盘非常周密，没有漏洞
english_meaning: A plan or scheme so thorough that there are no loopholes; airtight plan
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人的計畫或算盤非常周詳、縝密，沒有可乘之機或破綻。常用於口語，既可讚賞周密，也可指小人算盡。
explanation_english: Describes a plan or calculation that is secretive and meticulous, leaving no loopholes. Used colloquially to say something is airtight—either praising careful planning or noting someone's cunning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇吓佢嗰個計劃，真係密底算盘，冇漏罅，拆唔穿㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5 keoi5 go2 go3 gai3 waak6, zan1 hai6 mat6 dai2 syun3 pun4, mou5 lau6 laat6, caak3 m4 cyun1 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看看他的那个计划，真是盘算得很周密，没有漏洞，拆不穿。
examples.english_sentence: Look at his plan—it's really airtight, no loopholes; you can't expose it.

mandarin_meaning: 非常機密；（也可指）非常親密（視語境而定）
english_meaning: extremely secret/confidential; (contextually) very close-knit or intimate
explanation_mandarin: 「密甚甚」為廣東話口語用法，用來強調某事或某種關係的保密性或緊密程度。常見於非正式語境，表示「非常機密」或「非常親密、關係密切」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to emphasize how secretive/confidential something is, or (depending on context) how close-knit/intimate a relationship is. Commonly used in informal speech as an intensifier.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個關係密甚甚，啲嘢都唔會同人講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 gwaan1 hai6 mat6 sam6 sam6, di1 je5 dou1 m4 wui5 tung4 jan4 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們兩個關係非常親密，事情都不會告訴別人。
examples.english_sentence: They are extremely close; they don't tell others about their matters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰份文件係機密，內容密甚甚，唔好亂傳出去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 fan6 man4 gin2 hai6 gei1 mat6, noi6 jung6 mat6 sam6 sam6, m4 hou2 lyun6 cyun4 ceot1 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那份文件是機密，內容非常保密，不要亂傳出去。
examples.english_sentence: That document is confidential; the contents are highly secret — don't circulate it.

mandarin_meaning: 偷偷吃、私下多吃別人的食物或佔便宜
english_meaning: to secretly eat (someone else's food) or help oneself to extra portions; to sneak snacks or freeload on food
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，指在別人不注意或不知情的情況下，暗中吃別人的食物或多吃一份，帶有佔便宜或偷偷摸摸的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to eat secretly or help yourself to extra portions (often someone else's food) without others knowing — implies sneaking or freeloading.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日密食當三番，食咗我杯奶茶都唔講一聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 mat6 sik6 dong3 saam1 faan1, sik6 zo2 ngo5 bui1 naai5 caa4 dou1 m4 gong2 jat1 sing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常偷偷吃東西，連我的奶茶都喝了不說一聲。
examples.english_sentence: He always sneaks food; he drank my milk tea without saying a word.

cantonese: 寒天饮冰水，点滴在心头
mandarin_meaning: 比喻恩将仇报、忘恩负义；对曾经帮助过自己的人冷酷无情，让对方感到一再受伤。
english_meaning: An idiom meaning to repay kindness with ingratitude; to treat someone who helped you coldly or hurt them repeatedly.
explanation_mandarin: 此句以形象比喻（寒天飲冰水），說明在不應該的情況下對他人冷漠或傷害，常用來斥責忘恩負義的行為。
explanation_english: This phrase uses a vivid metaphor (drinking ice water on a cold day) to describe treating someone coldly or harming them despite receiving their help; often used to criticize ungrateful behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁樣對待曾經幫過佢嘅人，真係寒天飲冰水，點滴在心頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 joeng6 deoi3 doi6 cang4 ging1 bong1 gwo3 keoi5 ge3 jan4, zan1 hai6 hon4_tin1_jam2_bing1_seoi2_dim2_dik1_zoi6_sam1_tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這樣對待曾經幫助過他的人，真是寒天飲冰水，點滴在心頭。
examples.english_sentence: Treating someone who once helped him like this is truly 'drinking ice water on a cold day' — ungrateful and hurtful.

mandarin_meaning: 非常寒冷；冷得發抖
english_meaning: very cold; freezing; shivering from the cold
explanation_mandarin: 口語疊字表達，用來強調天氣或身體感覺非常寒冷，帶有略微誇張或生動的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial reduplicative expression used to emphasize extreme coldness, often describing weather or the physical sensation of being freezing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日寒寒凍凍，我唔想出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 hon4 hon4 dung3 dung3, ngo5 m4 soeng2 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天很冷，我不想出門。
examples.english_sentence: It's very cold today; I don't want to go out.

mandarin_meaning: 起鸡皮疙瘩；毛发竖起
english_meaning: goosebumps; hairs standing on end
explanation_mandarin: 指因为寒冷、恐惧或震惊等原因导致皮肤出现小疙瘩、毛发竖起的现象（口语），相当于普通话的“起鸡皮疙瘩”。
explanation_english: Refers to the phenomenon where the skin forms small bumps and hairs stand on end due to cold, fear, or shock; colloquial equivalent of 'getting goosebumps'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到佢講嗰啲事我全身起寒毛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 dou3 keoi5 gong2 go2 di1 si6 ngo5 cyun4 san1 hei2 hon4 mou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听到他讲那件事，我全身起了鸡皮疙瘩。
examples.english_sentence: When I heard about that, I got goosebumps all over.

cantonese: 寒露打大风，十个田头九个空
jyutping: hon4 lou6 daa2 daai6 fung1, sap6 go3 tin4 tau4 gau2 go3 hung1
mandarin_meaning: 寒露时节刮大风，十个田头九个空（俗谚，指因寒露时的大风或突变天气导致庄稼受灾、收成严重减少）
english_meaning: A proverb saying that when strong winds come during the Cold Dew solar term, nine out of ten fields end up empty — i.e., sudden bad weather causes heavy crop losses; used figuratively for severe loss or poor harvest.
explanation_mandarin: 这是民间谚语，指在寒露节气遇到强风等恶劣天气，会造成庄稼受损、收成大减，常用来形容自然灾害导致的普遍损失或遭遇重创。
explanation_english: A folk proverb referring to strong winds during the Cold Dew solar term that ruin crops so most fields yield nothing. It warns of weather-caused crop failure and is used metaphorically for widespread or severe losses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年寒露嗰陣打大風，十個田頭九個空，啲莊稼都冇晒收成。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 hon4 lou6 go2 zan6 daa2 daai6 fung1, sap6 go3 tin4 tau4 gau2 go3 hung1, di1 zong1 gaa2 dou1 mou5 saai3 sau1 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年寒露那阵刮了大风，十个田头九个空，庄稼都没有收成。
examples.english_sentence: This year during Cold Dew there was a strong wind; nine out of ten fields were emptied and the crops failed.

cantonese: 寒露最怕风，霜降最怕雨
jyutping: hon4 lou6 zeoi3 paa3 fung1, song1 gong3 zeoi3 paa3 jyu5
mandarin_meaning: 这是一个农谚：寒露时节最怕刮风，霜降时节最怕下雨。
english_meaning: A farmers' proverb: during the Cold Dew solar term wind is most harmful, while during the Frost's Descent solar term rain is most harmful.
explanation_mandarin: 该谚语来源于农业经验，提醒人们在秋季两个节气里要注意不同的不利天气：寒露时风大会加速水分流失、影响作物与晾晒；霜降时多雨会增加湿害、延缓入霜并可能导致作物腐烂或收成受损。
explanation_english: This proverb comes from farming experience and warns which weather is most harmful during two autumn solar terms: during Cold Dew strong winds accelerate moisture loss and can damage crops or drying processes; during Frost's Descent rain increases humidity, delays freezing, and raises the risk of rot and crop loss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯喺田邊話：『寒露最怕风，霜降最怕雨』，所以大家收成要趁早。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 hai2 tin4 bin1 waa6: 'hon4 lou6 zeoi3 paa3 fung1, song1 gong3 zeoi3 paa3 jyu5', so2 ji5 daai6 gaa1 sau1 sing4 jiu3 can3 zou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 伯伯在田边说：‘寒露最怕风，霜降最怕雨’，所以大家要趁早收割。
examples.english_sentence: Grandpa said by the field, 'Cold Dew fears wind, Frost's Descent fears rain', so everyone should harvest early.

cantonese: 寒露过三朝，迟早一齐标
jyutping: hon4 lou6 gwo3 saam1 ziu1, ci4 zou2 jat1 cai4 biu1
mandarin_meaning: 寒露过三朝，迟早一齐标（意指到了适当的时间，事情或现象迟早会同时显现）
english_meaning: A Cantonese proverb meaning that once the right time (here referenced by the Cold Dew solar term) has passed, things will inevitably happen or become apparent — it's only a matter of time.
explanation_mandarin: 本句为粤语俗谚，用寒露（节气）作时间标志，表示在合适时节过后，相关的事物或征兆迟早会一同显现，含有“时机成熟，结果自会到来”的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folksaying that uses the Cold Dew solar term as a timing marker. It conveys that once the season/time is right, related events or signs will inevitably appear together — in other words, time will reveal the result.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔使太擔心，寒露過三朝，遲早一齊標。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 sai2 taai3 daam1 sam1, hon4 lou6 gwo3 saam1 ziu1, ci4 zou2 jat1 cai4 biu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不用太担心，寒露过三朝，迟早都会一起显现。
examples.english_sentence: Don't worry too much; after the Cold Dew for three mornings, sooner or later everything will come to light.

mandarin_meaning: 確鑿、沒有懷疑餘地（相當於「確鑿無疑」或「鐵證如山」）
english_meaning: indisputable, well-founded, concrete and undeniable
explanation_mandarin: 粵語成語，形容事實或證據非常確實、無可辯駁，也可用來形容說話非常肯定、有把握。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiom meaning that something (e.g. evidence or a statement) is very solid and indisputable; used to describe facts or claims that leave no room for doubt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢提供嘅證據實古實鑿，冇得反駁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tai4 gung1 ge3 zing3 geoi3 sat6 gu2 sat6 zaak3, mou5 dak1 faan2 bok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他提供的證據確鑿，無法反駁。
examples.english_sentence: The evidence he provided is indisputable; it cannot be refuted.

mandarin_meaning: 非常 / 極其
english_meaning: extremely; really; exceedingly (intensifier)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語中的程度副詞，用於形容詞或動詞前後以強調程度，表示「非常、極其」的意思，常見於香港口語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial intensifier (adverb) used to emphasize degree — meaning 'extremely' or 'really'. Common in Hong Kong spoken Cantonese and used to strengthen adjectives or verbs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅牛扒實極好食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 ngau4 paa4 sat6 gik6 hou2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間餐廳的牛排非常好吃。
examples.english_sentence: The steak at this restaurant is extremely delicious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢實極冇禮貌，真係惹人反感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 sat6 gik6 mou5 lai5 maau6, zan1 hai6 je5 jan4 faan2 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話非常沒禮貌，真的令人反感。
examples.english_sentence: He speaks extremely rudely; it really annoys people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試我真係實極攰，要訓覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 ngo5 zan1 hai6 sat6 gik6 gui6, jiu3 fan3 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次考試我真的非常累，要睡覺。
examples.english_sentence: I'm really extremely tired from this exam; I need to sleep.

mandarin_meaning: 寮屋的門口、臨時棚屋的出入口（口語）
english_meaning: the entrance/mouth of a shack or temporary hut (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 在粵語口語中，指寮屋、棚屋或臨時簡陋建築的門口或出入口，帶地方性與口語色彩。
explanation_english: In Cantonese colloquial usage, refers to the doorway or entrance of a shack, squatter hut, or other makeshift shelter; has a regional, informal tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你喺寮口等我啦，我快啲返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai2 liu4 hau2 dang2 ngo5 laa1, ngo5 faai3 di1 faan1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在寮口等我，我很快就回來。
examples.english_sentence: Wait for me at the entrance of the shack; I'll be back soon.

mandarin_meaning: 宝塔饼（直译：宝塔形状的饼，指一种传统点心/糕饼）
english_meaning: Baota cake / pagoda-shaped pastry (a traditional Chinese snack/pastry)
explanation_mandarin: 一種傳統糕點，名稱來自其外形類似寶塔。此類點心在廣府地區或廟會、街市的小吃中可見，質地多為酥脆或略帶甜味，配方與做法可能因地區而異。
explanation_english: A traditional pastry whose name comes from its pagoda-like shape. This snack can be found in Cantonese-speaking regions, at temple fairs or markets. Texture is often flaky or crisp and slightly sweet; recipes and preparation vary by locality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市入面有間舖專門賣寶塔餅，買嚟做茶點幾好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 jap6 min6 jau5 gaan1 pou3 zyun1 mun4 maai6 bou2 taap3 beng2, maai5 lai4 zou6 caa4 dim2 gei2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市场里面有一家店专门卖宝塔饼，买来当茶点很好。
examples.english_sentence: There's a shop in the market that specializes in baota cakes; they're nice to buy as tea-time snacks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 過年嗰陣，阿婆會整啲寶塔餅俾孫仔食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gwo3 nin4 go2 zan6, aa3 po4 wui5 zing2 di1 bou2 taap3 beng2 bei2 syun1 zai2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 过年时，奶奶会做一些宝塔饼给孙子吃。
examples.english_sentence: At New Year, grandma would make some baota cakes for the grandchildren.

jyutping: sau6 sing1 gung1 diu3 geng2, jim4 ming6 coeng4
mandarin_meaning: 字面意思是“寿星公上吊，嫌命太长”。常用来夸张地表示对生活或处境感到厌倦、受够了，甚至有“活得太久、想了結”的意绪（多为夸张或抱怨用法）。
english_meaning: Literally, "the God of Longevity hangs himself, complaining life is too long." Used hyperbolically to express being fed up with life or a situation — an exaggerated way to say one is tired of living or intolerant of continual suffering/annoyance.
explanation_mandarin: 口语化的俗语或俚语，用来形容对某种境况极度厌烦或受不了，带有夸张、幽默或抱怨的语气，不一定真有自杀意思，常用于宣泄不满。
explanation_english: A colloquial proverb/slang expression used to convey extreme annoyance or weariness with a situation. It is hyperbolic and often humorous or venting; it does not always indicate a literal wish to die.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日畀人罵，煩到佢都想話：寿星公吊颈，嫌命长。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 bei2 jan4 maa6, faan4 dou3 keoi5 dou1 soeng2 waa6: sau6 sing1 gung1 diu3 geng2, jim4 ming6 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常被人骂，烦到他都想说：寿星公吊颈，嫌命长。
examples.english_sentence: He's constantly being yelled at; he's so fed up he feels like saying, "The god of longevity would hang himself, complaining life is too long."

cantonese: 射人先射馬，擒贼先擒王
jyutping: se6 jan4 sin1 se6 maa5, kam4 caak3 sin1 kam4 wong4
mandarin_meaning: 要从关键处下手：要打败对手或捉拿贼人，先铲除或控制他们的依靠或头目。
english_meaning: Strike at the crucial point first: to defeat an opponent or capture criminals, first neutralize or seize their key support or leader.
explanation_mandarin: 这句谚语比喻办事要先从关键处下手。例如要瓦解一个组织，应先针对其核心人物或资源，而不是只做表面工作。
explanation_english: This proverb advises tackling the critical point first. For example, to dismantle an organization you should target its core people or resources rather than focusing on peripheral matters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 要整治呢個犯罪集團，射人先射馬，擒賊先擒王，先要捉到幕後老闆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jiu3 zing2 zi6 ni1 go3 faan6 zeoi6 zaap6 tyun4, se6 jan4 sin1 se6 maa5, kam4 caak3 sin1 kam4 wong4, sin1 jiu3 zuk1 dou3 muk6 hau6 lou5 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 要整治这个犯罪集团，应当射人先射马、擒贼先擒王，首先要抓到幕后老板。
examples.english_sentence: To take down this criminal group, follow 'shoot the horse before the man; capture the leader before the thieves' — first catch the boss behind the scenes.

mandarin_meaning: 将来 / 以后（將來）
english_meaning: in the future; later
explanation_mandarin: 表示未來的時間或情況，相當於普通話的“将来”或“以后”。在廣東話中為常用的口語說法。
explanation_english: Indicates a time or situation in the future. Equivalent to Mandarin 'jiānglái' or English 'in the future / later'. Commonly used in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 將嚟我會搬去英國讀書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng1 lai4 ngo5 wui5 bun1 heoi3 jing1 gwok3 duk6 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 将来我会搬去英国读书。
examples.english_sentence: In the future I will move to the UK to study.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你將嚟想做乜嘢工？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoeng1 lai4 soeng2 zou6 mat1 je5 gung1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你将来想做什么工作？
examples.english_sentence: What job do you want to do in the future?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司將嚟會有啲變動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 zoeng1 lai4 wui5 jau5 di1 bin3 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司将来会有一些变动。
examples.english_sentence: The company will have some changes in the future.

mandarin_meaning: 昨晚；昨天晚上
english_meaning: last night; yesterday evening
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示「昨晚」或「昨天晚上」。在香港口語中常見，語氣較隨意。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning "last night" or "yesterday evening." Commonly used in spoken Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 尋晚夜我去咗旺角食嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cam4 maan5 je6 ngo5 heoi3 zo2 wong6 gok3 sik6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚我去了旺角吃東西。
examples.english_sentence: Last night I went to Mong Kok to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 對證；核對、互相印證（核實或比對證據或說法）
english_meaning: to corroborate; to verify/cross-check (evidence or accounts); to match up
explanation_mandarin: 「對證」通常用來表示把不同的文件、證據或說法拿來互相核對或印證，確認是否一致或可信。
explanation_english: Used to indicate comparing documents, evidence, or accounts to verify or corroborate them—to check whether they match or are credible.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋要搵番啲文件嚟對證下先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 waan2 faan1 di1 man4 gin2 lai4 deoi3 zing3 haa5 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們要找回那些文件來對證一下。
examples.english_sentence: We need to find those documents to verify/corroborate them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘅時間同收據唔對證。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 ge3 si4 gaan3 tung4 sau1 geoi3 m4 deoi3 zing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說的時間和收據不相符（無法對證）。
examples.english_sentence: What he said about the time doesn't match the receipt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 兩個證人嘅講法可以互相對證，咁就可信啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: loeng5 go3 zing3 jan4 ge3 gong2 faat3 ho2 ji5 wu6 soeng1 deoi3 zing3, gam2 zau6 ho2 seon3 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 兩個證人的說法可以互相對證，這樣就比較可信。
examples.english_sentence: The two witnesses' accounts corroborate each other, so it's more credible.

mandarin_meaning: 面对鬼／徒劳地对某人说话（粤语俗语）
english_meaning: literally 'face ghosts'; colloquially: to talk to someone in vain / to speak to a person who won't listen
explanation_mandarin: 1) 字面意思：面对鬼魂。2) 俗语用法：指跟不听劝或固执的人讲道理是徒劳的，相当于“对牛弹琴”或“白费口舌”。
explanation_english: 1) Literal: to face ghosts. 2) Colloquial: to attempt to reason with someone who won't listen — a futile effort, similar to 'talking to a brick wall' or 'casting pearls before swine'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚一個人去墳場，我真係唔想對鬼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 jat1 go3 jan4 heoi3 fan4 coeng4, ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 soeng2 deoi3 gwai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚上一个人去墓地，我真的不想面对鬼。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to face ghosts by going to the cemetery alone at night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁死硬，同佢講道理根本係對鬼講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 sei2 ngaang6, tung4 keoi5 gong2 dou6 lei5 gan1 bun2 hai6 deoi3 gwai2 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他这么固执，跟他讲道理根本是在白费口舌。
examples.english_sentence: He's so stubborn; reasoning with him is just talking to a brick wall.

jyutping: siu2 tau1 bei2 gau2 ngaau5, am3 aa3 dai2
mandarin_meaning: 比喻做壞事的人遇到麻煩或被當場抓住時，裝作不知、裝啞巴以逃避責任或責備
english_meaning: A proverb/saying describing someone who, when caught or confronted for wrongdoing, pretends to be unaware or plays dumb to avoid blame or responsibility
explanation_mandarin: 此短語字面是「小偷被狗咬」，意指做壞事的人被揭發或遇到麻煩時，會裝作啞巴或不認，以圖迴避責任或責罵。
explanation_english: Literally 'the thief is bitten by a dog'; used to describe someone who, when exposed or in trouble, feigns ignorance or silence (plays dumb) to escape blame or consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啱啱見到佢偷嘢俾人捉到，之後就裝聾裝啞，真係小偷畀狗咬，暗哑抵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aam1 aam1 gin3 dou2 keoi5 tau1 je5 bei2 jan4 zuk1 dou3, zi1 hau6 zau6 zong1 lung4 zong1 aa3, zan1 hai6 siu2 tau1 bei2 gau2 ngaau5, am3 aa3 dai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剛剛看到他偷東西被人當場抓到，之後就裝聾作啞，真是「小偷畀狗咬，暗哑抵」。
examples.english_sentence: I just saw him stealing and getting caught; afterwards he pretended to be deaf and mute — classic 'thief bitten by a dog, plays dumb.'

mandarin_meaning: 小孩子不會耍詐或裝病，性情單純、天真無心機。
english_meaning: Children are innocent and incapable of deceit; they don't pretend to be ill or scheme.
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，用來形容小孩天真單純，不懂欺騙或裝腔作勢，說話或表現往往直接真誠。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression describing how children are innocent and guileless; they do not feign illness or deceive, and their words and actions are straightforward and sincere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢仲細，真係小兒無詐病，講咩就信咩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zung6 sai3, zan1 hai6 siu2 ji4 mou4 zaa3 beng6, gong2 me1 zau6 seon3 me1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他還小，是真的單純，不會耍詐，說什麼就信什麼。
examples.english_sentence: He's still young — truly innocent and not deceitful; he believes whatever he's told.

mandarin_meaning: 小儿科（医学科目：儿科）；比喻：指事情简单、幼稚或肤浅
english_meaning: Pediatrics; (figuratively) something trivial, childish, or superficial
partOfSpeech_english: noun (can be used figuratively as adjective)
explanation_mandarin: 本義是醫學上的兒科；口語中常用來比喻某事很簡單、幼稚或缺乏深度，帶貶義。
explanation_english: Literally the medical specialty of pediatrics. Colloquially used to describe something as trivial, childish, or lacking depth (pejorative).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺醫院做小兒科醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ji1 jyun2 zou6 siu2 ji4 fo1 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在醫院做小兒科醫生。
examples.english_sentence: He works as a pediatrician at the hospital.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你問嘅問題太小兒科，唔夠深度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 man6 ge3 man6 tai4 taai3 siu2 ji4 fo1, m4 gau3 sam1 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你問的问题太小儿科，不夠深度。
examples.english_sentence: The question you asked is too trivial/childish — not deep enough.

mandarin_meaning: 父親的弟弟（小叔、小叔子）
english_meaning: paternal younger uncle (father's younger brother)
explanation_mandarin: 指父親的弟弟，是一種親屬稱謂，可用來描述關係或稱呼對方。在粵語口語中也常以「小叔叔」稱呼。
explanation_english: Refers to the father's younger brother, a kinship term used to describe the relationship or address the person. In Cantonese spoken usage, '小叔叔' is also commonly used.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我爸爸有個小叔，成日會嚟我哋屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 baa4baa1 jau5 go3 siu2 suk1, seng4 jat6 wui5 lai4 ngo5dei6 uk1kei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我爸爸有个小叔，经常会来我们家。
examples.english_sentence: My dad has a younger brother; he often comes to our house.

jyutping: siu2 hon4 nyun5, daai6 hon4 mou4 dei6 zyun1
mandarin_meaning: 如果小寒時節較暖和，往往預示大寒會特別寒冷，難以躲避
english_meaning: If the 'Lesser Cold' period is unusually warm, it often foreshadows an especially severe 'Greater Cold'—very bitterly cold weather.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來形容天氣變化：若小寒時溫度偏高，通常意味接下來的大寒會特別嚴寒，提醒人們要做好禦寒準備。
explanation_english: A weather-related proverb: when the Lesser Cold period is unusually mild, it usually predicts that the upcoming Greater Cold will be particularly severe. It warns people to prepare for harsher cold.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年小寒暖，大寒無地鑽，聽講下個禮拜會凍到透骨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 siu2 hon4 nyun5, daai6 hon4 mou4 dei6 zyun1, teng1 gong2 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 wui5 dung3 dou3 tau3 gwat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年小寒暖，大寒无地钻，听说下个礼拜会冷得彻骨。
examples.english_sentence: This year the Lesser Cold was warm, but the Greater Cold is unbearably cold — I heard next week will be freezing to the bone.

mandarin_meaning: 小心就不会犯大错 / 小心谨慎就能避免严重错误
english_meaning: If you are careful, you won't make major mistakes; better safe than sorry.
explanation_mandarin: 表示只要小心谨慎，就不会犯严重的错误。常用作劝告或提醒注意。
explanation_english: Expresses that being careful prevents major mistakes. Commonly used as advice or a warning to be cautious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做呢份報告嘅時候要小心無大錯，數字要核實先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 ge3 si4 hau6 jiu3 siu2 sam1 mou4 daai6 co3, sou3 zi6 jiu3 hat6 sat6 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做这份报告的时候要小心无大错，数字要核实才行。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful when preparing this report so you don't make big mistakes; verify the numbers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出門前檢查好路線同帶定啲現金，旅行時小心無大錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 mun4 cin4 gim2 caa4 hou2 lou6 sin3 tung4 daai3 ding6 di1 jin6 gam1, leoi5 hang4 si4 siu2 sam1 mou4 daai6 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出门前检查好路线并带好些现金，旅行时小心就不会犯大错。
examples.english_sentence: Check your route and bring some cash before leaving; when traveling, being careful helps avoid big mistakes.

jyutping: siu2 sam1 sai2 dak1 maan6 nin4 syun4
mandarin_meaning: 谨慎行事可以保平安／长久
english_meaning: Better safe than sorry; acting cautiously ensures long-term safety
explanation_mandarin: 这句谚语意思是：做事要小心谨慎，这样才能避免危险并保持长久安全或顺利。
explanation_english: This proverb means that one should act carefully and cautiously to avoid danger and ensure long-term safety or success.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出門記住鎖門，小心驶得万年船。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 mun4 gei3 zyu6 so2 mun4, siu2 sam1 sai2 dak1 maan6 nin4 syun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出门记得锁门，小心驶得万年船。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to lock the door when you go out — better safe than sorry.

mandarin_meaning: 為小利斤斤計較、過分計較小事並擔心長期的得失
english_meaning: to be overly concerned with petty sums or petty matters; to quibble over small amounts and obsess about long-term tallying
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容為了很小的利益或零頭而反覆計較、過分在意，常帶貶義，類似“斤斤計較”或“為小失大”的一種表現（但不完全同義）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who fusses over trivial amounts or petty matters and worries about the long-term tally; derogatory connotation similar to being petty or overly nitpicky.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係小數怕長計，為咗幾蚊嘢可以計咁耐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 siu2 sou3 paa3 coeng4 gai3, wai6 zo2 gei2 man1 je5 ho2 ji5 gai3 gam2 noi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是小數怕長計，為了幾塊錢可以算這麼久。
examples.english_sentence: He's really petty — he can argue over a few dollars for ages.

cantonese: 小暑大暑未为暑，最热在立秋处暑
jyutping: siu2 syu2 daai6 syu2 mei6 wai6 syu2, zeoi3 jit6 zoi6 lap6 cau1 cyu3 syu2
mandarin_meaning: 小暑和大暑并非一年中最热的时候，最热通常在立秋和处暑前后。
english_meaning: 'Lesser Heat' and 'Greater Heat' are not necessarily the hottest periods; the hottest time often occurs around the solar terms 'Start of Autumn' and 'End of Heat'.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語指的是二十四節氣中的氣候現象：雖然有小暑、大暑，但最悶熱、最高溫的時段往往出現在立秋或處暑前後，反映出季節變化的延遲性。
explanation_english: This proverb refers to a climate pattern among the 24 solar terms: although there are 'Lesser Heat' and 'Greater Heat', the most intense heat often occurs around the 'Start of Autumn' and 'End of Heat', reflecting a lag in seasonal change.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆成日話：「小暑大暑未為暑，最熱在立秋處暑。」提醒我哋出門要帶水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 sing4 jat6 waa6: "siu2 syu2 daai6 syu2 mei6 wai6 syu2, zeoi3 jit6 zoi6 lap6 cau1 cyu3 syu2" tai4 jing6 ngo5 dei6 ceot1 mun4 jiu3 daai3 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶常說：「小暑大暑未为暑，最热在立秋处暑。」提醒我們外出要帶水。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma often says, 'Lesser Heat and Greater Heat aren't the hottest; the hottest is around the Start of Autumn and End of Heat,' reminding us to bring water when going out.

jyutping: siu2 cin2 m4 ceot1 daai6 cin2 m4 jap6
mandarin_meaning: 既不肯出小钱，也不愿意出大钱；形容非常吝啬或不愿意出钱参与
english_meaning: Refuses to spend even small amounts and won't put in large sums either; describes someone extremely stingy or unwilling to contribute money
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人很小氣，既不願意付出零碎的錢，也不願意在需要時付出較大的金錢，總之不肯出錢參與或幫忙。
explanation_english: Used to describe a person who is very stingy — unwilling to pay small sums and likewise unwilling to invest or contribute larger amounts; basically refuses to put up money or take part financially.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司搞個集資活動，阿明完全係小钱唔出大钱唔入，連一蚊都唔肯掏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gaau2 go3 zaap6 zi1 wun6 dung6, aa3 ming4 jyun4 cyun4 hai6 siu2 cin2 m4 ceot1 daai6 cin2 m4 jap6, lin4 jat1 man1 dou1 m4 hang2 tou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司搞集资活动，阿明完全是既不肯出小钱，也不肯出大钱，连一块钱都不愿掏。
examples.english_sentence: The company organized a fundraising activity, and Ah Ming was totally 'won't pay small, won't invest big' — he wouldn't even hand over one dollar.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講要慳錢，但係實際上係小钱唔出大钱唔入，朋友叫佢分擔都唔幫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 jiu3 haan1 cin2, daan6 hai6 sat6 zai3 soeng6 hai6 siu2 cin2 m4 ceot1 daai6 cin2 m4 jap6, pang4 jau5 giu3 keoi5 fan1 daam1 dou1 m4 bong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常說要省錢，但實際上是既不肯出小錢，也不肯出大錢，朋友叫他分擔也不幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks about saving money, but in reality he's 'won't pay small, won't invest big' — when friends ask him to share expenses he doesn't help.

cantonese: 小雪大雪未为雪，小寒大寒至系寒
jyutping: siu2 syut3 daai6 syut3 mei6 wai4 syut3, siu2 hon4 daai6 hon4 zi3 hai6 hon4
mandarin_meaning: 小雪、大雪还算不上真正的雪，只有小寒、大寒才是真正寒冷。
english_meaning: The solar terms 'Lesser Snow' and 'Greater Snow' don't necessarily mean it's truly snowy; it's during 'Lesser Cold' and 'Greater Cold' that it gets truly cold.
explanation_mandarin: 这句粤语谚语用二十四节气来描述气候变化：小雪、大雪只是标示降雪的节气，未必是最冷的时候；而小寒、大寒才是最寒冷的阶段。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb that uses solar terms to describe seasonal temperature: 'Lesser Snow' and 'Greater Snow' mark snowfall but aren't necessarily the coldest times; 'Lesser Cold' and 'Greater Cold' signify the truly coldest period.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講到冬天，阿媽成日都話：「小雪大雪未為雪，小寒大寒至系寒。」
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 dou3 dung1 tin1, aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 dou1 waa6: 'siu2 syut3 daai6 syut3 mei6 wai4 syut3, siu2 hon4 daai6 hon4 zi3 hai6 hon4.'
examples.mandarin_sentence: 说到冬天，妈妈常说：‘小雪大雪还算不上雪，只有小寒大寒才是真正的寒冷。’
examples.english_sentence: When we talk about winter, my mother always says, 'Lesser Snow and Greater Snow aren't really snowy; it's Lesser Cold and Greater Cold that are truly cold.'

mandarin_meaning: 指本來沒什麼權勢或能力的人被提升到有權勢的位置後變得傲慢、專橫或擺架子。
english_meaning: Refers to a small-time or insignificant person who, after being promoted to a position of authority, becomes arrogant, domineering, or puts on airs.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語用法，常用來形容本來無大本事或地位低微的人，一旦有了權力或地位就變得驕傲、擺架子或濫用權勢。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression used to describe someone of little ability or standing who, upon gaining power or position, becomes conceited, bossy, or abuses their new authority.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗部門經理之後就變晒樣，真係小鬼升城隍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 bou6 mun4 ging1 lei5 zi1 hau6 zau6 bin3 saai3 joeng6, zan1 hai6 siu2 gwai2 sing1 sing4 wong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他升任部門經理後就變了樣，真是小鬼升城隍。
examples.english_sentence: After he became the department manager he completely changed — truly a small-timer promoted to power.

jyutping: siu2 gwai2 m4 gin3 dak1 daai6 san4
mandarin_meaning: 別小看年輕人／小孩子也可能是高手。
english_meaning: Don't underestimate youngsters; someone young may actually be very skilled or an expert.
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話的口語說法，用來提醒或反駁別人不要小看年輕人或年紀小的人，表示他們也可能技術高強或有本事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to warn against underestimating younger people. It implies that a 'kid' (小鬼) isn't necessarily powerless — they can be highly capable or an expert.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好睇少佢，佢雖然細個，但小鬼唔見得大神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 tai2 siu2 keoi5, keoi5 seoi1 jin4 sai3 go3, daan6 siu2 gwai2 m4 gin3 dak1 daai6 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要小看他，他雖然年紀小，但小孩子也可能是高手。
examples.english_sentence: Don't underestimate him. Although he's young, a kid can still be a real expert.

mandarin_meaning: 小凤饼；一种小型的传统中式点心，通常外皮酥软、内馅偏甜，类似老婆饼或凤梨酥（不同地区叫法或配方可能有差异）
english_meaning: Small phoenix pastry; a small traditional Chinese pastry with a flaky crust and sweet filling, similar in style to a wife cake or pineapple cake (usage and filling vary by region).
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話中用來指一種小型中式餅點，外皮酥鬆、內餡多為甜味，可作茶點或禮餅。不同地方的配方或名稱可能會有差別。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, this refers to a small traditional pastry with a flaky crust and sweet filling, eaten as a snack or given as a gift. Recipes and exact names can vary by region.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺餅店買咗幾個小鳳餅，幾好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 beng2 dim3 maai5 zo2 gei2 go3 siu2 fung6 beng2, gei2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在餅店買了幾個小鳳餅，很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a few small phoenix pastries at the bakery — they're delicious.

mandarin_meaning: 缺乏膽量；膽小
english_meaning: cowardly; lacking courage; having no guts
explanation_mandarin: 口語粗俗用法，意思是缺乏勇氣、沒膽量，常用來嘲笑或責備別人膽小。此處的「膶」常被視為「膽」的變體或誤寫。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese slang (often coarse). It means lacking courage or having 'no guts' and is used to mock or scold someone for being cowardly. The character '膶' here is often a variant/misspelling of 膽 (daam2).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你少块膶啦，唔好成日咁驚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 siu2 faai3 daam2 laa1, m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 gam2 geng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你少點膽量吧，不要總是這麼膽小。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be such a coward; stop being so afraid all the time.

mandarin_meaning: 尖酸刻薄、不饒人
english_meaning: acerbic/mean and unrelenting; sharp-tongued and unsparing
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，形容一個人說話或態度尖刻、刻薄，而且不會遷就或饒人，讓人覺得不舒服或尷尬。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe someone whose words or attitude are sharp, cutting, and unsparing — they don't soften or go easy on others, often making people uncomfortable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好尖不甩，聽落真係唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 zim1 bat1 lat1, teng1 lok6 zan1 hai6 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話很尖酸刻薄，聽起來真的不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: He speaks very sharply and abrasively; it really makes you uncomfortable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面試官好尖不甩，問嗰啲問題令我好尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 si3 gun1 hou2 zim1 bat1 lat1, man6 go2 di1 man6 tai4 ling6 ngo5 hou2 gaam1 ngaap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面試官很苛刻，問的問題讓我很尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: The interviewer was harsh; the questions made me feel awkward.

mandarin_meaning: 尖嘴辣椒 / 尖椒（指外形细长、顶端尖的辣椒）
english_meaning: pointed chili pepper (a long, narrow chili with a pointed tip)
explanation_mandarin: 一种外形细长且顶端尖的辣椒品种，常用于中式烹饪中提味或做配菜。
explanation_english: A variety of chili pepper that is long and pointed at the tip; commonly used in Chinese cooking to add heat and flavor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺街市買咗啲尖嘴辣椒，今晚拌埋蒸魚用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gaai1 si5 maai5 zo2 di1 zim1 zeoi2 laat6 ziu1, gam1 maan5 bun6 maai4 zing1 jyu4 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在菜市场买了些尖嘴辣椒，今晚用来拌蒸鱼。
examples.english_sentence: I bought some pointed chilies at the market; I'll use them to season steamed fish tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 尖酸刻薄或愛講閒話的人
english_meaning: a sharp-tongued person; someone who is snarky, gossipy or overly critical
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話俚語，用來形容嘴巴尖刻、愛說別人閒話或喜歡挖苦他人的人，帶有貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who is sharp-tongued, gossipy, or inclined to make cutting remarks about others; pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好理佢，佢只係一個尖嘴雞，成日愛講人閒話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5, keoi5 zi2 hai6 jat1 go3 zim1 zeoi2 gai1, seng4 jat6 oi3 gong2 jan4 haan4 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別理他，他只是個尖嘴雞，總愛說人閒話。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pay attention to him — he's just a sharp-tongued person who always gossips about others.

mandarin_meaning: 尖狀的堆、錐形的堆積；（口語、少見用法）也可比喻突出的積壓或問題
english_meaning: a pointed/ conical heap; (rare/colloquial) figuratively, a prominent piled-up mass or accumulated problem
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（可作具體名詞或比喻用）
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指呈尖錐形的堆積物，例如沙堆或碎石堆。此詞在粵語中屬較少見或口語化的用法，亦可用作比喻，形容累積起來而突出的負擔或問題。
explanation_english: Literally refers to a heap shaped like a point or cone (e.g., a pile of sand or rubble). This term is relatively rare/colloquial in Cantonese and can also be used figuratively to describe an accumulation that sticks out as a burden or problem.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 工地度堆住一個尖堆，小朋友唔好近嗰度玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 dei6 dou6 deoi1 zyu6 jat1 go3 zim1 deoi1, siu2 pang4 jau5 m4 hou2 gan6 go2 dou6 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 工地上堆著一個尖尖的堆，小朋友不要靠近那裡玩。
examples.english_sentence: There's a pointed heap piled up at the construction site; children shouldn't play near it.

jyutping: ce2 jau5 so2 dyun2, cyun3 jau5 so2 coeng4
mandarin_meaning: 各有所长，各有优缺点
english_meaning: Everyone has strengths and weaknesses; each has their own merits and faults.
explanation_mandarin: 這句成語表示每個人都有優點和缺點，不必以偏概全，要看到他人的長處。
explanation_english: This idiom expresses that everyone has strengths and weaknesses; don’t judge someone solely on one shortcoming and overlook their merits.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好因為佢唔識做呢樣嘢就睇低佢，尺有所短，寸有所長。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jan1 wai6 keoi5 m4 sik1 zou6 ni1 joeng6 je5 zau6 tai2 dai1 keoi5, ce2 jau5 so2 dyun2, cyun3 jau5 so2 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要因为他不会做这件事就看低他，尺有所短，寸有所长。
examples.english_sentence: Don't look down on him just because he can't do this; everyone has strengths and weaknesses.

mandarin_meaning: 尽力而为；把能做的事情都做了
english_meaning: do everything one can; do one's best
explanation_mandarin: 表示尽自己所能去做事情，常与“听天命”连用，意为尽力而为，不强求结果。
explanation_english: Means to do everything one can; often used with phrases like 'leave the rest to fate.' It expresses making every effort without insisting on controlling the outcome.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我已經盡人事，唯有聽天命。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 zeon6 jan4 si6, wai4 jau5 teng1 tin1 ming6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我已经尽人事，唯有听天命。
examples.english_sentence: I've done everything I can; now it's up to fate.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺考試之前，盡人事就好，唔好太擔心結果。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 haau2 si3 zi1 cin4, zeon6 jan4 si6 zau6 hou2, m4 hou2 taai3 daam1 sam1 git3 gwo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在考试之前，尽人事就好，不要太担心结果。
examples.english_sentence: Before the exam, just do your best; don't worry too much about the outcome.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆話我哋盡人事，會再睇表現先至決定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 waa6 ngo5 dei6 zeon6 jan4 si6, wui5 zoi3 tai2 biu2 jin2 sin1 zi3 kyut3 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板说我们尽人事，会再看表现再决定。
examples.english_sentence: The boss said we should do our best; they will look at our performance and then decide.

mandarin_meaning: 把事情彻底弄糟/一团乱
english_meaning: to totally mess something up; a complete mess
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，字面为“尽（彻底）+地+一煲（一锅）”，用来形容事情被搞得彻底混乱或完全失败，也可指把关系/局面弄坏。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase literally 'completely into one pot'; used to describe a situation that's been thoroughly messed up or ruined—anything turned into a total mess or collapse.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次個項目真係盡地一煲，全部嘢都搞到散晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 go3 hong6 muk6 zan1 hai6 zeon6 dei6 jat1 bou1, cyun4 bou6 je5 dou1 gaau2 dou3 saan3 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次这个项目真是彻底乱成一锅粥，所有东西都被搞得一团糟。
examples.english_sentence: This project is a complete mess; everything has been messed up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁樣做，將啲關係盡地一煲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 joeng6 zou6, zoeng1 di1 gwaan1 hai6 zeon6 dei6 jat1 bou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他这样做，把关系完全弄砸了。
examples.english_sentence: By doing that, he completely ruined the relationship.

mandarin_meaning: 最後；終於
english_meaning: in the end; finally
explanation_mandarin: 「尾尾」是廣東話口語用法，表示事情的結尾或最後的結果，相當於普通話的「最後」「終於」。常用於日常對話中強調結局或最終情況。
explanation_english: "尾尾" is a Cantonese colloquial adverb used to indicate the ending or final outcome of an event, equivalent to Mandarin "最後/終於" or English "in the end/finally." It is commonly used in everyday speech to stress the final result.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我等咗個幾鐘，尾尾佢都冇嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dang2 zo2 go3 gei2 zung1, mei5 mei5 keoi5 dou1 mou5 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我等了好幾個小時，最後他還是沒來。
examples.english_sentence: I waited for several hours; in the end he still didn't come.

mandarin_meaning: 沒用、令人討厭或一無是處（粗俗貶義）
english_meaning: A vulgar slang insult meaning something or someone is useless, crappy, or worthless
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 貶義詞（名詞或形容詞用法）
explanation_mandarin: 粗俗的廣東話俗語，用來形容人或事物非常沒用、討厭或一無是處，屬於侮辱性用語，口語中常見於非正式場合。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang term used to label a person or thing as totally useless, awful, or worthless. It is insulting and used in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日遲到，真係尾尾屎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3, zan1 hai6 mei5 mei5 si2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是遲到，真是沒用透頂。
examples.english_sentence: He’s always late — he’s such a useless guy.

mandarin_meaning: 尾椎 / 尾骨（尾巴骨）
english_meaning: coccyx; tailbone
explanation_mandarin: 指脊柱最末端的小塊骨頭，即尾椎／尾骨，位於臀部上方，受傷或長時間坐姿會引起疼痛。
explanation_english: Refers to the small bone at the very end of the spine (the coccyx or tailbone), located above the buttocks; can be painful after injury or prolonged sitting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢跌親，尾膇好痛，行唔到路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dit3 can1, mei5 zeoi1 hou2 tung3, haang4 m4 dou3 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他跌倒了，尾椎很痛，走不了路。
examples.english_sentence: He fell and his tailbone hurts badly; he can't walk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 生產後好多媽媽尾膇會痛，要做康復運動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: saang1 caan2 hau6 hou2 do1 maa4 maa1 mei5 zeoi1 wui5 tung3, jiu3 zou6 hong1 fuk6 wan6 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 產後很多媽媽尾椎會疼，需要做康復運動。
examples.english_sentence: After childbirth many mothers experience tailbone pain and need rehabilitation exercises.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生話我尾膇冇事，只係坐得耐有啲痠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 waa6 ngo5 mei5 zeoi1 mou5 si6, zek3 hai6 co5 dak1 noi6 jau5 di1 syun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 醫生說我的尾椎沒事，只是坐久了有點酸。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor said my tailbone is fine; it's just sore from sitting too long.

mandarin_meaning: 尾巴；末端；結尾（亦可指時間上的末尾或剩餘部分）
english_meaning: tail; end; rear; the final part or remainder
explanation_mandarin: 表示物體的後端或結尾部分，也可引申為時間或事件的末尾、剩餘部分（如「年尾」「尾數」）；口語中亦可表示跟隨在後。
explanation_english: Refers to the rear or end part of an object; can be extended to mean the end of a time period or the remainder (e.g. 'year-end', 'balance'). In colloquial usage it can also mean to follow behind someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 隻貓有條長長嘅尾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zek3 maau1 jau5 tiu4 coeng4 coeng4 ge3 mei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那隻貓有一條長長的尾巴。
examples.english_sentence: The cat has a long tail.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家差唔多到年尾啦，我哋要交報表。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 caa1 m4 do1 dou3 nin4 mei5 laa3, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 gaau1 bou3 biu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在差不多到年尾了，我們要交報表。
examples.english_sentence: It's almost the end of the year; we need to submit the report.

mandarin_meaning: 笨蛋；傻瓜（粵語俚語，帶貶義）
english_meaning: idiot; fool (Cantonese slang, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「尾二」是粵語俗語，用來罵人或形容某人愚蠢、做事不聰明，語氣通常帶有貶義或不耐煩。
explanation_english: “尾二” is Cantonese slang used to insult or describe someone as stupid or doing foolish things. It is derogatory and often used with annoyance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你尾二㗎咩？點可以咁樣做？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 mei5 ji6 gaa3 me1? dim2 ho2 ji5 gam2 joeng6 zou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你是笨蛋嗎？怎麼可以這樣做？
examples.english_sentence: Are you an idiot? How could you do that?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做啲尾二嘢，真係好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zou6 di1 mei5 ji6 je5, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是做些蠢事，真的很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He always does stupid things; it's really annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好尾二啦，快啲決定啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 mei5 ji6 laa1, faai3 di1 kyut3 ding6 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別傻了，快點決定吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't be foolish — make a decision quickly!

mandarin_meaning: 以後；之後
english_meaning: later; afterwards; afterward
explanation_mandarin: 「尾後」是香港粵語口語用法，表示在某事之後或將來的時間，相當於普通話的「以後／之後」。
explanation_english: “mei5 hau6” is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial term meaning ‘later’ or ‘afterwards’, indicating a time following some event.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我尾後會還畀你啲錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mei5hau6 wui5 waan4 bei2 nei5 di1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我以後會把錢還給你。
examples.english_sentence: I'll pay you back later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做完功課尾後可以出嚟玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 jyun4 gung1 fo3 mei5hau6 ho2 ji5 ceot1 lai4 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做完作業後可以出來玩。
examples.english_sentence: You can come out to hang out after you finish your homework.

mandarin_meaning: 膽小鬼；懦夫（口語、罵人的俚語）
english_meaning: coward; scaredy‑cat (slang insult; literally 'pee‑shrimp', implying someone who is extremely timid)
explanation_mandarin: 「尿蝦」為廣東話口語俚語，用來罵人膽小或遇事容易驚慌失措。字面上把「尿」和「蝦」結合，有誇張、戲謔的貶義語氣，主要在香港粵語口語中使用，屬非正式且可能冒犯人的用詞。
explanation_english: “Niu6 haa1” is Cantonese slang used to insult someone as a coward or extremely timid person. Literally combining 'pee' and 'shrimp', it carries a mocking, derogatory tone. It is informal, chiefly used in Hong Kong Cantonese, and can be offensive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做尿蝦，出嚟試吓先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 niu6 haa1, ceot1 lai4 si3 haa5 sin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別當膽小鬼，出來試試看吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a coward; come out and give it a try.

mandarin_meaning: （口語/地區性）局裡的信件；也可指郵局寄來的信件或某個「局」發出的通知，具體含義視語境而定。
english_meaning: A colloquial/rare term possibly referring to a letter or notice from an office or the post office; exact meaning depends on context.
explanation_mandarin: 「局信」並非標準書面語，屬口語或地區性用法。可用來簡稱「郵局的信件」或指某個機構（局）發出的信件/通知。由於使用不廣，遇到時應根據上下文判斷具體含義。
explanation_english: “局信” is not a standard written term; it is colloquial and regionally used. It can be a shorthand for a letter from the post office or a notice issued by an office/department. Because it is uncommon, the precise meaning should be inferred from context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有冇收過局信？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 mou5 sau1 gwo3 guk6 seon3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有沒有收到局裡的信？
examples.english_sentence: Did you receive the letter from the office/post office?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂講，'局信'呢個詞好少人用，要睇埋上下文先知係邊個意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 gong2, 'guk6 seon3' ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 siu2 jan4 jung6, jiu3 tai2 maai4 soeng6 haa6 man4 sin1 zi1 hai6 bin1 go3 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別亂說，『局信』這個詞很少人用，要看語境才能知道是哪種意思。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say that lightly—'局信' is rarely used; you need context to know which meaning is intended.

mandarin_meaning: 處處設局／到處是圈套；總是設計詭計
english_meaning: everywhere are traps; constantly setting up schemes or tricks
explanation_mandarin: 香港口語，形容到處都是圈套或詭計，或形容某人總是設局、愛算計。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase describing situations full of traps or schemes, or a person who is always plotting or setting up tricks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家做嘢要小心，成日有局局角，唔好輕信人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 zou6 je5 jiu3 siu2 sam1, sing4 jat6 jau5 guk6 guk6 gok3, m4 hou2 hing1 seon3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在做事要小心，經常有各種陷阱，不要輕信別人。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful at work now; there are traps everywhere—don't trust people easily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日諗到啲局局角，搞到人好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 lam2 dou3 di1 guk6 guk6 gok3, gaau2 dou3 jan4 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是想出些詭計，讓人很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He's always coming up with schemes, which annoys people.

mandarin_meaning: 擺架子、裝腔作勢、有優越感或盛氣凌人
english_meaning: having an air of superiority; acting pretentious or high-handed
explanation_mandarin: 「局氣」用來形容一個人擺出高人一等、盛氣凌人或很有派頭、很講排場的態度或氣勢。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who puts on airs, acts superior or bossy, or behaves in a pretentious/stately manner.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好有局氣，講嘢成日擺架子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 jau5 guk6 hei3, gong2 je5 seng4 jat6 baai2 gaa3 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很有局氣，說話總是擺架子。
examples.english_sentence: He is very pretentious; he always speaks with an air of superiority.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁局氣啦，大家係同一隊，唔使扮高人一等。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 guk6 hei3 laa1, daai6 gaa1 hai6 tung4 jat1 deoi6, m4 sai2 baan6 gou1 jan4 jat1 dang2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別這麼擺架子，我們是一隊的，不用裝得高人一等。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so pretentious; we're on the same team, no need to act superior.

mandarin_meaning: 栽赃、诬陷
english_meaning: to frame someone; to falsely accuse
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示故意栽贓或誣陷別人，常見於香港粵語語境。由「屈」（誣陷、栽贓）與「質/厔」構成的俗語或俚語表達。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to mean framing or falsely accusing someone. Commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese; derived from 屈 (to frame) combined with 質/厔 as a slangive form.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔鍾意佢，就屈質佢偷嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zung1 ji3 keoi5, zau6 wat1 zat1 keoi5 tau1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不喜欢他，就诬陷他偷东西。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't like him, so he framed him for stealing.

mandarin_meaning: 栽贓、嫁禍於人
english_meaning: to frame someone; to pin the blame on others
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，指把自己的錯誤或責任推到別人身上，使他人代為承擔後果或受責備。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning to frame someone or shift blame onto another person so they take the consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做錯嘢，唔肯認，反而想屈尾龍畀同事頂佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 co3 je5, m4 hang2 jing6, faan2 ji4 soeng2 wat1 mei5 lung4 bei2 tung4 si6 deng2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做錯事不肯承認，反而想栽贓同事替他頂罪。
examples.english_sentence: He made a mistake and refuses to admit it; instead he tries to frame a colleague to take the blame for him.

mandarin_meaning: 被人栽贓、被誣陷（成為替罪羊／背黑鍋）
english_meaning: to be framed; to be set up; to be made the scapegoat
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指被人誣衊或栽贓，最終被推到承擔責任或後果，類似「背黑鍋」或「被嫁禍」。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to be framed or set up—made the scapegoat and forced to take the blame or consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 明明係佢搞錯，點解要我屈釘尾？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ming4 ming4 hai6 keoi5 gaau2 co3, dim2 gaai2 jiu3 ngo5 wat1 ding1 mei5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明明是他搞錯，為什麼要我背黑鍋？
examples.english_sentence: It was clearly his mistake—why am I being made the scapegoat?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲證據唔清楚，但公司最後屈釘尾畀咗我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 zing3 geoi3 m4 cing1 co2, daan6 gung1 si1 zeoi3 hau6 wat1 ding1 mei5 bei2 zo2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 證據不清楚，但公司最後把責任栽到我頭上了。
examples.english_sentence: The evidence was unclear, but the company ended up pinning the blame on me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好俾人屈釘尾，留底證據啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 wat1 ding1 mei5, lau4 dai2 zing3 geoi3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別讓人栽贓，留好證據吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let yourself be framed; keep the evidence.

mandarin_meaning: 不詳（此字形罕見或可能是誤寫），可能是「屋企」（家）的誤寫或方言變體
english_meaning: Unknown (the character is rare or possibly a misspelling); possibly intended as '屋企' (home)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 未知 / 名詞（若為「屋企」則為名詞）
partOfSpeech_english: unknown / noun (if intended as '屋企', noun)
explanation_mandarin: 詞條中的字「㖉」在常用字表中極為罕見，未能找到可靠詞典記載。很可能是手寫、印刷或輸入時的誤寫，常見的近義或口語詞為「屋企」（廣東話「家」）。在無更多語境下，應視為不確定詞形，建議提供原句上下文以便核實。
explanation_english: The character 㖉 is extremely rare and not attested in common Cantonese dictionaries; no reliable references were found. It may be a misspelling or variant of a common Cantonese word such as '屋企' (uk1 kei5 = home). Without more context it is unsafe to assign a definitive pronunciation or meaning. Provide the original sentence or context for accurate identification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 原文寫「屋㖉」，但我懷疑係寫錯，可能意思係「屋企」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyun4 man4 se2 "uk1 㖉" , daan6 ngo5 waai4 gei1 hai6 se2 co3 , ho2 nang4 ji3 si1 "uk1 kei5" .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 原文寫「屋㖉」，但我懷疑是寫錯，可能意思是「屋企」。
examples.english_sentence: The original text wrote '屋㖉', but I suspect it's a mistake and may mean '屋企' (home).

cantonese: 屋漏更兼連夜雨，船遲又遇頂頭風
jyutping: uk1 lau6 gang1 gim1 lin4 je6 jyu5, syun4 ci4 jau6 jyu6 ding2 tau4 fung1
mandarin_meaning: 與“禍不單行”或“屋漏偏逢連夜雨”意思相近，形容不幸或麻煩接二連三地發生。
english_meaning: Similar to "when it rains, it pours" — misfortunes or troubles come one after another; to make matters worse.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話字面上說屋頂在漏水時還遇上連夜下雨，船行得慢時又碰到頂頭風，用來比喻不順利的事接連發生，越來越糟糕。
explanation_english: Literally describes a leaking roof encountering night rain and a slow boat meeting headwinds — used to describe a sequence of misfortunes piling up, i.e. troubles coming one after another.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱俾公司炒，屋漏更兼連夜雨，返到屋企又發現水喉漏水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ngaam1 ngaam1 bei2 gung1 si1 caau2, uk1 lau6 gang1 gim1 lin4 je6 jyu5, faan1 dou3 uk1 kei5 jau6 faat3 jin6 seoi2 hau4 lau6 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛被公司解僱，屋漏更兼連夜雨，回到家又發現水管漏水。
examples.english_sentence: He was just fired from the company; misfortunes kept coming — when he got home he discovered a leaking pipe.

mandarin_meaning: 去你媽的 / 操你媽（粗俗的骂人话，用来表示愤怒或侮辱对方及其母亲）
english_meaning: Fuck your mother (vulgar insult used to express extreme anger or to insult someone)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話粗口，用來強烈表示憤怒、蔑視或侮辱對方，字面上是侮辱對方的母親，極具攻擊性，不宜在正式場合或禮貌對話中使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar expletive used to express intense anger, contempt, or to insult someone; literally insults the other person's mother. Extremely offensive and inappropriate in polite or formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屌那媽！佢又遲到，害我哋等咗成個鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: diu2 naa5 maa1! keoi5 jau6 ci4 dou3, hoi6 ngo5 dei6 dang2 zo2 sing4 go3 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去你媽的！他又遲到，害我們等了整整一個小時。
examples.english_sentence: Fuck your mother! He's late again and made us wait a whole hour.

mandarin_meaning: 废物；笨蛋；混蛋（粗俗，侮辱性用語）
english_meaning: shithead; useless person; idiot (vulgar insult)
explanation_mandarin: 「屎䍇」是香港廣東話的粗俗俚語，用來形容沒用、愚蠢或令人討厭的人，語氣帶有強烈貶抑和冒犯性，通常用於口語非正式場合。
