examples.mandarin_sentence: 我懒，通常都是懒人使长线，一次买足两个星期的菜。
examples.english_sentence: I'm lazy; I usually use the 'lazy person's' method — buying groceries for two weeks at once.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗慳時間，佢星期日煮好晒成個禮拜嘅飯放落雪櫃，真係懶人使長線。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 haan2 si4 gaan3, keoi5 sing1 kei4 jat6 zyu2 hou2 saai3 sing4 go3 lai5 baai3 ge3 faan6 fong3 lok6 syut3 gwai6, zan1 hai6 laan5 jan4 sai2 coeng4 sin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 为了省时间，他周日把一周的饭菜都做好放进冰箱，真是懒人使长线。
examples.english_sentence: To save time, he cooks the week's meals on Sunday and puts them in the fridge — truly a 'lazy person's' approach.

mandarin_meaning: 懶惰的人會帶來更多麻煩（比喻懶人會留下更多問題或爛攤子）
english_meaning: Literal: 'lazy people have more poop and pee' — a Cantonese saying meaning lazy people cause more mess or trouble, leaving extra work for others.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，用來形容懶惰的人常常不負責任或做事馬虎，結果會留下更多麻煩或需要別人善後。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying used to criticize laziness — lazy people often leave messes or problems that others must clean up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 懶人多屎尿—佢成日唔做嘢，最後總係要其他人幫手收爛攤子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: laan5 jan4 do1 si2 niu6 - keoi5 sing4 jat6 m4 zou6 je5，zeoi3 hau6 zung2 hai6 jiu3 kei4 taa1 jan4 bong1 sau2 sau1 laan6 taan1 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 懒人多屎尿——他总是不做事，最后总是要别人帮忙收拾烂摊子。
examples.english_sentence: Lazy people cause more mess—he never does his work, and in the end someone else always has to help clean up the mess.

mandarin_meaning: 偷懶敷衍的做法；馬虎的工夫
english_meaning: a lazy, half‑hearted way of doing something; shoddy/half-baked work
explanation_mandarin: 指做事偷懶、敷衍或偷工減料的方式，常帶貶義，用來形容工作或手藝不認真、不負責任。
explanation_english: Refers to doing things in a lazy, perfunctory, or cut‑corners manner. Usually derogatory; describes shoddy workmanship or half‑hearted effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好用懒佬工夫做呢份報告，老闆會睇得出嚟㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 jung6 laan5 lou2 gung1 fu1 zou6 ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3, lou5 baan2 wui5 tai2 dak1 ceot1 lai4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要用懒佬工夫做這份報告，老闆會看得出來。
examples.english_sentence: Don't do this report with lazy work — the boss will be able to tell.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢整梳化用懒佬工夫，做咗兩個禮拜就散晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing2 so1 faa3 jung6 laan5 lou2 gung1 fu1, zou6 zo2 loeng5 go3 lai5 baai3 zau6 saan3 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他修理沙發很偷工減料，做了兩個禮拜就壞掉了。
examples.english_sentence: He fixed the sofa sloppily; it fell apart after only two weeks.

mandarin_meaning: 懒到骨子里 / 懒得要命
english_meaning: extremely lazy; lazy to the bone
explanation_mandarin: 粤語俗語，形容人非常懒，懒到骨子里，常用于口語或俚語中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone is extremely lazy — literally 'lazy to the bone.' Used informally/slangily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢懒到出骨，成日都唔做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 laan5 dou3 ceot1 gwat1, seng4 jat6 dou1 m4 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他懒到骨子里，整天都不做事。
examples.english_sentence: He's lazy to the bone; he never does any work.

mandarin_meaning: 懒惰、爱睡觉的人（常作戏谑或亲昵称呼）
english_meaning: a lazy person who loves to sleep; 'lazybones' or 'sleepyhead' (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，字面意思为“懒得睡的猪”或“爱睡觉的猪”，用来形容很懒、喜欢睡懒觉的人，通常带有戏谑或亲昵的语气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term literally 'lazy-sleeping pig' used to describe someone lazy who loves to sleep; often used teasingly or affectionately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做懒瞓猪，快啲起身返工啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 laan5 fan3 zyu1, faai3 di1 hei2 san1 faan1 gung1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別做懒睡猪，快点起床去上班吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a lazy sleepyhead—hurry up and get up for work!

mandarin_meaning: 茫然掙扎、糊塗地掙扎或迷惘地掙扎
english_meaning: to struggle or flounder in a dazed/confused way; to make a half-hearted or confused struggle
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指在茫然、迷惘或不清楚情況下的掙扎或反抗，常帶有無助或慌張的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to struggle or resist in a dazed, confused, or flustered way — often implying helplessness or a half-hearted effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 俾人捉住嘅時候，佢懞掙咗幾下都冇用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 jan4 zuk1 zyu6 ge3 si4 hau6, keoi5 mung4 zaang1 zo2 gei2 haa6 dou1 mou5 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 被人抓住的時候，他茫然掙扎了幾下也沒用。
examples.english_sentence: When he was grabbed, his confused struggles for a few moments were useless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面試嗰陣佢有啲緊張，講嘢有啲懞掙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 si3 go2 zan6, keoi5 jau5 di1 gan2 zoeng1, gong2 je5 jau5 di1 mung4 zaang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面試的時候他有點緊張，說話有些茫然掙扎。
examples.english_sentence: During the interview he was a bit nervous and spoke in a somewhat flustered, confused way.

mandarin_meaning: 茫然、不知所措、愣住
english_meaning: to be stunned, bewildered, flummoxed; at a loss how to react
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語說法，形容因突發情況或對方說話而感到愣住、腦袋一片空白、不知道如何回應或處理。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to be dazed or stunned by something unexpected, leaving one at a loss and unsure how to respond.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢突然咁樣講，我真係懵上心口，唔知點回應。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dat6 jin4 gam2 joeng6 gong2, ngo5 zan1 hai6 mung6 soeng5 sam1 hau2, m4 zi1 dim2 wui4 jing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然這樣說，我真的愣住了，不知道怎麼回應。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly said that; I was completely stunned and didn't know how to respond.

mandarin_meaning: 罕见词汇，通常作为人名（如“怀枝”）；字面意为“怀抱的枝/枝条”
english_meaning: A rare/obscure term, most commonly seen as a personal name (e.g. 'Huaizhi'); literally 'cherished/embraced branch'
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（人名 / 專有名詞，罕見詞）
partOfSpeech_english: proper noun / noun (rare term, usually a personal name)
explanation_mandarin: “懷枝”並非廣泛使用的廣東話常用詞彙，較常見於漢語人名中。兩個字合在一起字面可解為“懷抱的枝條”或帶有懷念、珍惜之意，但作為詞語其用法罕見或屬人名用法。
explanation_english: “懷枝” is not a commonly used Cantonese lexical item; it most often appears as a Chinese personal name. Literally the characters convey 'a branch held/cherished', with connotations of cherishing or remembrance, but as a lexical item it is rare and mainly functions as a name.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我細妹叫懷枝，佢今年十九歲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3mui6 giu3 waai4 zi1, keoi5 gam1nin4 sap6 gau2 seoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我妹妹叫怀枝，她今年十九岁。
examples.english_sentence: My younger sister is called Huaizhi; she is nineteen this year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個詞好罕見，懷枝聽落更像係人名。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 hon2 gin3, waai4 zi1 teng1 lok6 gang3 zoeng6 hai6 jan4 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个词很罕见，怀枝听起来更像是人名。
examples.english_sentence: This term is very rare; 'Huaizhi' sounds more like a personal name.

mandarin_meaning: 歡喜（高興、愉快）
english_meaning: happy; joyful; pleased
explanation_mandarin: 表示高興、愉悅的心情。『懽』為古字或書面字，為『歡』的異體字，『懽喜』多見於粵語或文言用法，意思與「歡喜」「高興」相近。
explanation_english: Expresses a feeling of happiness or joy. The character 懽 is a classical/variant form of 歡, so 懽喜 corresponds to 歡喜 and means being pleased or joyful. Common in Cantonese and literary usages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 收到呢個消息，我真係好懽喜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sau1 dou3 ni1 go3 siu1 sik1, ngo5 zan1 hai6 hou2 fun1 hei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 收到這個消息，我真的很歡喜。
examples.english_sentence: When I received the news, I was really happy.

mandarin_meaning: 一輩子；終身；很長一段時間（粵語口語）
english_meaning: for a lifetime; the whole life; for a very long time (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，表示持續很長的時間或一輩子，常用作誇張或強調的說法。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese time expression meaning 'for a lifetime' or 'for a very long time'. Often used hyperbolically or to emphasize long duration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成世流流长都搵唔到份穩陣嘅工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 sai3 lau4 lau4 coeng4 dou1 waan2 m4 dou2 fan6 wan2 zan6 ge3 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一輩子都找不到一份穩定的工作。
examples.english_sentence: He never found a stable job his whole life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你唔努力，你成世流流长都係咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 m4 nou5 lik6, nei5 sing4 sai3 lau4 lau4 coeng4 dou1 hai6 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你不努力，你一輩子都會這樣下去。
examples.english_sentence: If you don't work hard, you'll be like this your whole life.

mandarin_meaning: 像隻雀一樣（形容驚慌、緊張或惶恐不安）
english_meaning: like a (small) bird — used as a simile to describe someone being skittish, startled, nervous, or jittery
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用法，字面是「成隻雀一樣」，通常用來形容一個人驚慌、緊張、易受驚或坐立不安的狀態，也可形容人動作輕快、急促。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese simile literally meaning "like a whole sparrow." It usually describes someone who is skittish, startled, very nervous, or fidgety; can also evoke quick, flustered movements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到巨響，驚到成隻雀噉跳咗起嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 dou3 geoi6 hoeng2, geng1 dou3 sing4 zek3 Zoek3 gam2 tiu3 zo2 hei2 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他聽到巨響，嚇得像隻雀一樣跳了起來。
examples.english_sentence: He heard a loud noise and jumped up like a startled bird.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面試前佢緊張到成隻雀噉講唔出嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 si5 cin4 keoi5 gan2 zoeng1 dou3 sing4 zek3 Zoek3 gam2 gong2 m4 ceot1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面試前他緊張得像隻雀一樣說不出話。
examples.english_sentence: Before the interview he was so nervous he couldn't speak.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲客人排隊等太耐，有啲人急到成隻雀噉走嚟走去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 haak3 jan4 paai4 deoi2 dang2 taai3 noi6, jau5 di1 jan4 gap1 dou3 sing4 zek3 Zoek3 gam2 zau2 lai4 zau2 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 客人在排隊等太久，有些人急得像隻雀一樣來回走動。
examples.english_sentence: The customers had been waiting in line too long; some people were pacing back and forth like anxious birds.

mandarin_meaning: 未查到；可能是罕見字詞、方言變體或錯字
english_meaning: Not found/unknown; likely a rare term, dialectal variant, or a typo
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 未知（可能為口語/俚語或非標準詞）
explanation_mandarin: 在主要粵語詞典與語料庫中未檢索到「戙厾企」的記錄。該組合可能為罕見或古字、地區性方言寫法、口語拼寫的創新詞，或原文打字錯誤。若需確定意思，建議提供來源語境或原始文本以便進一步辨析。
explanation_english: No entries for “戙厾企” are found in major Cantonese dictionaries or corpora. The string may be a rare/archaic character combination, a regional/dialectal variant, a nonce/slang coinage, or a typo. To determine its meaning more precisely, please provide the original context or source.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「戙厾企」呢個詞我查唔到，應該係罕見或錯字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ci4 ngo5 caa4 m4 dou3, jing1 goi1 hai6 hon2 gin3 waak6 co3 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: “戙厾企”这个词我查不到，应该是罕见或错字。
examples.english_sentence: I can't find the word “戙厾企”; it is probably rare or a typo.

mandarin_meaning: 洞（dòng）：孔、穴、凹陷、洞穴、漏洞
english_meaning: hole; cavity; opening; cave; loophole
explanation_mandarin: 表示物體上的孔、穴或凹陷。‘戙’為較少見或古字的異體字形式，與常用字『洞』意義相同。
explanation_english: Refers to a hole, cavity, or opening in an object or surface. '戙' is a less common or variant character equivalent in meaning to the standard character '洞'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 牆上有個戙（洞），要修補一下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: coeng4 soeng6 jau5 go3 dung6, jiu3 sau1 bou2 jat1 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 墙上有个洞，要修补一下。
examples.english_sentence: There is a hole in the wall; it needs to be repaired.

mandarin_meaning: （常见于「戮力同心」）齐心协力、共同努力
english_meaning: to combine efforts; to work together with concerted effort (often used in the phrase "戮力同心")
explanation_mandarin: 「戮力」常見於「戮力同心」，表示大家齊心協力、共同投入力量以完成某事或克服困難。
explanation_english: Often used in the phrase "戮力同心", meaning to unite efforts or work together vigorously toward a common goal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋要戮力同心完成呢個項目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 luk6 lik6 tung4 sam1 jyun4 sing4 ni1 go3 hong6 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们要戮力同心完成这个项目。
examples.english_sentence: We must work together with united effort to complete this project.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司全體要戮力，先可以渡過難關。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 cyun4 tai2 jiu3 luk6 lik6, sin1 ho2 ji5 dou6 gwo3 naan4 gwaan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司全体要戮力，才能渡过难关。
examples.english_sentence: The whole company must unite efforts to get through the difficult times.

mandarin_meaning: 扁圓形 (biǎn yuán xíng)：扁平的圓形或橢圓形，呈扁平的圓盤狀或橢圓狀
english_meaning: flattened-oval; oblate; a flattened circular or oval shape (disk-like or lenticular)
explanation_mandarin: 表示物體的形狀較為扁平，近似圓形或橢圓形，常用來描述石頭、果實或其他呈扁平圓盤狀的物件。
explanation_english: Describes a shape that is flattened and roughly circular or oval—used for objects that look like flat discs or lenticular/oblate forms (e.g., pebbles, seeds, certain fruits).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢塊鵝卵石係扁圓形，適合擺喺花園做裝飾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 faai3 ngo4 lyun5 sek6 hai6 bin2 jyun4 jing4, sik1 hap6 baai2 hai2 faa1 jyun4 zou6 zong1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這塊鵝卵石是扁圓形的，適合擺在花園做裝飾。
examples.english_sentence: This pebble is flattened-oval; it's suitable to place in the garden as a decoration.

jyutping: bin2 bei6 lou2 daai3 ngaan5 geng2, mou5 dak1 ding2
mandarin_meaning: 戴眼镜的塌鼻男子看起来非常吸引／無可匹敵（口語化的讚美或感嘆）
english_meaning: A flat‑nosed guy wearing glasses — unbeatable/looks great. A colloquial exclamation praising how glasses transform someone's appearance.
explanation_mandarin: 這句是香港廣東話的口語說法，字面是「扁鼻的男人戴上眼鏡，沒有人能比」，常用來表示戴眼鏡後某人變得特別好看或有型，語氣可誇張或帶玩笑、讚美意味；「扁鼻佬」帶點粗俗或戲謔成分，視語境可親切或冒犯。
explanation_english: This Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase literally reads “a flat‑nosed guy wearing glasses — unbeatable.” It’s used to say that putting on glasses has made someone unexpectedly attractive or stylish. The tone can be playful or admiring; note that 扁鼻佬 (flat‑nosed guy) is colloquial and can be mildly crude depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇吓阿強，扁鼻佬戴眼镜，冇得顶！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5 aa3 koeng4, bin2 bei6 lou2 daai3 ngaan5 geng2, mou5 dak1 ding2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看阿强，塌鼻子的男生戴上眼镜，真是没得比！
examples.english_sentence: Look at Ah Keung — a flat‑nosed guy wearing glasses, unbeatable!

cantonese: 扁鼻哥戴眼镜，你紧佢唔紧
jyutping: bin2 bei6 go1 daai3 ngaan5 geng3, nei5 gan2 keoi5 m4 gan2
mandarin_meaning: 就算塌鼻子的男生戴上眼鏡，你會喜歡他嗎？（用來戲謔或諷刺）
english_meaning: Even if the flat‑nosed guy puts on glasses, do you like him or not? (a teasing/rhetorical remark)
explanation_mandarin: 一個廣東話的戲謔性短語，用來反問或諷刺某人是否會因外表的微小改變而改變對別人的好感，通常帶有調侃、取笑或指出膚淺的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese teasing slang phrase used to rhetorically ask whether someone would change their attraction because of a small change in appearance. It usually carries a mocking or playful tone, pointing out superficiality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話啲朋友鍾意個男仔，其實就係扁鼻哥，戴眼鏡，你緊佢唔緊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 di1 pang4 jau5 zung1 ji3 go3 naam4 zai2, sat6 hai6 bin2 bei6 go1, daai3 ngaan5 geng3, nei5 gan2 keoi5 m4 gan2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說朋友喜歡那個男生，其實就是塌鼻哥，戴眼鏡，你會喜歡他嗎？
examples.english_sentence: He said his friend likes that guy — actually it's the flat‑nosed guy wearing glasses — do you like him or not?

mandarin_meaning: 手信；纪念品、伴手礼（旅行或探访时带回或带去给别人的礼物）
english_meaning: souvenir; gift (a present brought back or given to others, often after travel or visits)
explanation_mandarin: 「手信」在粤语中常指旅行或探訪時買來帶回或帶去給親友的小禮物或紀念品，有時亦泛指拜訪帶去的伴手禮。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '手信' refers to a souvenir or small gift brought back from a trip or brought along when visiting someone. It can also mean a local specialty given as a token.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我去旅行會買手信畀你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 heoi3 leoi5 hang4 wui5 maai5 sau2 seon3 bei2 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我去旅行會幫你買手信。
examples.english_sentence: I'll buy you a souvenir when I travel.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲係本地手信，好有名。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 hai6 bun2 dei6 sau2 seon3, hou2 jau5 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些是本地的手信，很有名。
examples.english_sentence: These are local souvenirs; they're very famous.

mandarin_meaning: 手工制造；手工製作（亦可寫作「手製」）
english_meaning: handmade; hand-crafted (not mass-produced)
explanation_mandarin: 在香港常用來表示以手工製作的東西，強調非工廠大量生產。亦見寫法「手製」。
explanation_english: Commonly used in Hong Kong to indicate something made by hand, emphasizing it is not mass-produced. Often written as "手製" (handmade).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲係手制月餅，唔係工廠大量生產嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 hai6 sau2 zai3 jyut6 beng2, m4 hai6 gung1 cong2 daai6 loeng6 saang1 caan2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些是手工製作的月餅，不是工廠大量生產的。
examples.english_sentence: These are handmade mooncakes, not mass-produced in a factory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢自己做手制肥皂賣，材料天然，收到好評。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi6 gei2 zou6 sau2 zai3 fei4 zou6 maai6, coi4 liu2 tin1 jin4, sau1 dou3 hou2 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他自己做手工肥皂賣，材料天然，收到好評。
examples.english_sentence: He makes handmade soap to sell; the ingredients are natural and it has received good reviews.

mandarin_meaning: 手部的力量；力气（常用于搬运、提举等需要用手的工作或动作）
english_meaning: hand strength; hand power; manual strength (physical strength of the hands used for lifting, carrying or manual work)
explanation_mandarin: 指手部或以手為主的肌肉力量，常用來形容搬運、提舉、握持等需要手部力氣的能力，也可泛指體力的一部分。
explanation_english: Refers to the strength of the hands or muscles used primarily by the hands. It is commonly used to describe the ability to lift, carry, grip or perform manual tasks, and can also refer generally to part of one's physical strength.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢手力好大，可以一個人搬兩袋米。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sau2 lik6 hou2 daai6, ho2 ji5 jat1 go3 jan4 baan1 loeng5 doi6 mai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他力气很大，一个人可以搬两袋米。
examples.english_sentence: He has strong hands (a lot of physical strength); he can carry two bags of rice by himself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做搬運工要有手力同持久力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 bun1 wan6 gung1 jiu3 jau5 sau2 lik6 tung4 ci4 gau3 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做搬运工需要有手部力量和耐力。
examples.english_sentence: Being a mover requires hand strength and endurance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲老人家手力弱，開罐頭都唔容易。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 lou5 jan4 gaa1 sau2 lik6 joek6, hoi1 gun3 tau4 dou1 m4 jung4 ji6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些老人家手部力量较弱，连开罐头都不容易。
examples.english_sentence: Some elderly people have weak hand strength; even opening a can isn't easy.

jyutping: sau2 gap6 ngaan5 faai3, ngaan5 maan6 syu1 saai3
mandarin_meaning: 手快眼快，反應快；眼睛慢或動作慢就會輸光、錯失良機
english_meaning: Be quick-handed and quick-eyed; have fast reactions — if you're slow you'll lose out or miss the opportunity
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來形容反應快、動作迅速的人；也可用作勸誡，提醒人要快一點，否則會輸或錯過機會。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying describes someone with quick reactions and fast hands; it can also be used as a warning to act quickly or you'll lose or miss the chance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 打麻雀嗰陣要手急眼快，慢咗就輸晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daa2 maa4 zoek3 go2 zan6 jiu3 sau2 gap6 ngaan5 faai3, maan6 zo2 zau6 syu1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 打麻将的时候要手快眼快，慢了就全输光了。
examples.english_sentence: When playing mahjong you need to be quick-handed and quick-eyed; if you're slow you'll lose everything.

mandarin_meaning: 指紋
english_meaning: fingerprint
explanation_mandarin: 指頭上的紋路，用於身份識別或作為法醫、偵查的證據。"手指屘"為廣東話口語用法，對應普通話的「指紋」。
explanation_english: The ridge patterns on a fingertip used for identification or as forensic evidence. "手指屘" is a Cantonese colloquial term corresponding to Mandarin "指紋" (fingerprint).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方喺現場搵到手指屘，經過比對之後鎖定咗疑犯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 hai2 jin6 coeng4 wan2 dou3 sau2 zi2 man4, ging1 gwo3 bei2 deoi3 zi1 hau6 so2 ding6 zo2 ji4 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方在現場發現了手指紋，經過比對後鎖定了嫌疑人。
examples.english_sentence: The police found a fingerprint at the scene; after comparison they identified the suspect.

mandarin_meaning: 手腳發抖、緊張不安
english_meaning: to be trembling all over; very nervous or jittery
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，形容因緊張、害怕或激動而手腳發抖、坐立不安。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone who is trembling or extremely jittery—usually from nervousness, fear, or excitement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試前我成日手揗脚震，唔知點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 cin4 ngo5 seng4 jat6 sau2 wan2 goek3 zan3, m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考試前我整天手腳發抖，不知道怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: Before the exam I was trembling all over all day and didn't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 范本；榜样；样本
english_meaning: model; example; template; pattern
explanation_mandarin: 指用作參考或模仿的範例或樣本，也可指可供效法的榜样。在書法或手工等領域常指示範用的樣張或範本。
explanation_english: Refers to a model, example, or template used for reference or imitation; can also mean someone or something that serves as an example. In contexts like calligraphy or crafts, it denotes a sample or exemplar sheet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要做個好手本畀細路睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 zou6 go3 hou2 sau2 bun2 bei2 sai3 lou6 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要给孩子做个好榜样。
examples.english_sentence: You should set a good example for the children.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老師畀咗幾張書法手本我哋練習。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 si1 bei2 zo2 gei2 zoeng1 syu1 faat3 sau2 bun2 ngo5 dei6 lin6 zaap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老师给了我们几张书法范本练习。
examples.english_sentence: The teacher gave us several calligraphy model sheets to practice.

mandarin_meaning: 小人物怎能与大人物抗衡？
english_meaning: How can a small fry go up against the big shot? (an underdog can't beat a much more powerful opponent)
explanation_mandarin: 表示實力或地位懸殊，弱勢一方無法與強大對手競爭或抗衡。
explanation_english: Expresses that the parties are mismatched in strength or status — the weaker side cannot compete with or overcome the much stronger opponent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢只係個小職員，手瓜點拗得过大髀，唔好自不量力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi2 hai6 go3 siu2 zik1 jyun4, sau2-gwaa1 dim2 aau3 dak1 gwo3 daai6-bei2, m4 hou2 zi6 bat1 loeng4 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只是個小職員，怎能與大人物抗衡，不要自不量力。
examples.english_sentence: He's just a junior employee; how can a small fry go up against a big shot? Don't overestimate yourself.

synonyms: 小人物怎能與大人物抗衡
small fry can't beat the big guy

mandarin_meaning: 手脚不灵活；动作笨拙/反应迟缓
english_meaning: clumsy; physically awkward; slow to act or uncoordinated
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，形容一個人動作不靈活、笨拙，或反應遲緩、辦事不利索。有時也可用來批評處事拖沓。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone is physically clumsy or awkward, or slow to react/inefficient in doing things. It can also criticize sluggishness in handling tasks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢手腳唔好，成日跌嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 sau2 goek3 m4 hou2, seng4 jat6 dit3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事手脚不灵活，总是把东西弄掉。
examples.english_sentence: He's clumsy when doing things and always drops stuff.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 救災嗰陣政府手腳唔好，救援嚟得太遲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau3 zoi1 go2 zan6 zing3 fu2 sau2 goek3 m4 hou2, gau3 wun6 lai4 dak1 taai3 ci4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 救灾时政府反应迟缓，救援来得太慢。
examples.english_sentence: During the disaster the government's response was slow; the rescue arrived too late.

mandarin_meaning: 手部發抖；手部震顫（如生理或病理原因），也可口語指因緊張或不穩而手抖
english_meaning: hand tremor; trembling hands (involuntary shaking of the hands) — can be medical or caused by nervousness/clumsiness
explanation_mandarin: 指手部不自主地發抖，既可指生理或病理的震顫（例如帕金森氏症或本態性震顫），也可口語化地指因緊張、手抖導致動作不穩或拍照模糊等情況。
explanation_english: Refers to involuntary shaking of the hands. It can denote a medical tremor (e.g. Parkinson's, essential tremor) or be used colloquially for shaky hands caused by nervousness, fatigue, or unsteady movement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢因為緊張，拍相嗰陣手震，張相都模糊咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1 wai6 gan2 zoeng1, paak3 soeng2 go2 zan6 sau2 zan3, zoeng1 soeng2 dou1 mo4 wu4 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他因為緊張，拍照時手抖，照片都模糊了。
examples.english_sentence: He was so nervous that his hands shook while taking the photo, and the picture came out blurry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老人家有病，成日手震，應該去睇醫生檢查下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jan4 gaa1 jau5 beng6, sing4 jat6 sau2 zan3, jing1 goi1 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1 gim2 caa4 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老人家有病，經常手抖，應該去看醫生檢查一下。
examples.english_sentence: The elderly person has an illness and often has hand tremors; they should see a doctor for a check-up.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見/疑似方言或錯寫）可能指「手擀麵／手拉麵」（手工製作的麵）或是個別地區的口語用法，需根據語境判斷
english_meaning: Rare/nonstandard term — possibly refers to hand-made noodles (hand-rolled or hand-pulled noodles) or a regional colloquialism; meaning depends on context
explanation_mandarin: 「手面」並非標準廣東話常見詞彙，書面或正式語境中罕見。根據語境，有時被用作「手擀麵」或「手拉麵」的簡略說法；也可能是某些地區或口語中的特殊用法或錯別字。建議遇到該詞時參考上下文或向說話者查詢其具體含義。
explanation_english: “手面” is not a common standard Cantonese term and is uncommon in written/standard usage. Depending on context it may be a shorthand or regional term for hand-made noodles (e.g., hand-rolled or hand-pulled noodles). It can also be a dialectal usage or a misspelling. Check context or ask the speaker for precise meaning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間小店話佢哋有自己整嘅手面，話好傳統。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 siu2 dim3 waa6 keoi5 dei6 jau5 zi6 gei2 zeng2 ge3 sau2 min6, waa6 hou2 cyun4 tung2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间小店说他们有自己做的手面，说很传统。
examples.english_sentence: This small shop says they make their own "手面" and that it's very traditional.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 其實我唔確定「手面」係咪手擀麵，聽上去像地方口語。
examples.jyutping_sentence: kei4 sat6 ngo5 m4 kok3 ding6 「sau2 min6」 hai6 mai6 sau2 gon2 min6, teng1 soeng5 heoi3 zoeng6 dei6 fong1 hau2 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 其实我不确定“手面”是不是手擀面，听起来像地方口语。
examples.english_sentence: I'm not sure whether "手面" means hand-rolled noodles; it sounds like a local colloquialism.

mandarin_meaning: 樣本；範本；示範用的範例或帖本（多指臨摹、學習用的樣本）
english_meaning: model; sample; template; copybook (especially a model or exemplar used for copying or learning)
explanation_mandarin: 「手本」通常指示範用的樣本或範例，例如書法臨摹用的帖本或工作上的模板。有時見到寫作「手首本」的變體，但最常用、正確的寫法為「手本」。
explanation_english: “手本” refers to a model, exemplar, or template—often a copybook or sample used for imitation or study. A rare variant spelling with 首 sometimes appears, but the standard form is 手本.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢照住手本寫字，寫得好靚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ziu3 zyu6 sau2 bun2 se2 zi6, se2 dak1 hou2 leng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他照著手本寫字，寫得很好看。
examples.english_sentence: He writes by copying the model; his handwriting looks very nice.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個手本可以俾我參考嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 sau2 bun2 ho2 ji5 bei2 ngo5 caam1 haau2 maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个手本可以给我参考吗？
examples.english_sentence: Can I refer to this sample/template?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老師俾咗一份手本畀我哋練習。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 si1 bei2 zo2 jat1 fan6 sau2 bun2 bei2 ngo5 dei6 lin6 zaap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老師給了我們一份手本練習。
examples.english_sentence: The teacher gave us a copybook to practice with.

mandarin_meaning: 拿手好戲／拿手本領（某人的專長、拿手之處）
english_meaning: one's specialty; signature act; forte; the thing someone does best
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指某人最擅長或最能顯示實力的表現或項目。常用於說某人在某情境下發揮拿手之處。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression referring to someone's signature act or forte — the performance or skill they are best known for or excel at. Often used when someone displays their strengths in a particular situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次呢場比賽，終於到佢出手本戲嘅時候。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 ni1 coeng4 bei2 coi3, zung1 jyu1 dou3 keoi5 ceot1 sau2 bun2 hei3 ge3 si4 hau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次比賽，終於輪到他發揮拿手本領的時候了。
examples.english_sentence: In this competition, it's finally his turn to show his specialty.

mandarin_meaning: 年紀輕或有才能但體質虛弱 / 身體虛弱
english_meaning: physically weak; frail (often used to describe someone who is young or otherwise fragile)
explanation_mandarin: 「才多身子弱」用來形容一個人身體虛弱、抵抗力差，常用於提醒對方要注意休息或避免劇烈活動。有時也帶有「年紀輕但體弱」的含意。
explanation_english: This phrase describes someone who is physically weak or frail, often implying they should rest or avoid strenuous activity. It can carry the nuance of being young but constitutionally frail.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢先十幾歲，才多身子弱，唔好叫佢做咁劇烈嘅運動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sin1 sap6 gei2 seoi3, coi4 do1 san1 zi2 joek6, m4 hou2 giu3 keoi5 zou6 gam2 kek6 lit6 ge3 wan6 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他才十几岁，身子弱，不要叫他做那麼劇烈的運動。
examples.english_sentence: He's only in his teens and is physically weak; don't make him do such strenuous exercise.

mandarin_meaning: 跳入水中；跳进水里去救人；（引申）出手帮忙、救急
english_meaning: to jump/dive into water; to jump in to rescue someone; (figurative) to step in to help or to bail someone out in an emergency
explanation_mandarin: 「扑水」字面上指跳入或撲向水中，常用於形容跳入水中救人或救援。引申用法為在緊急或危機時刻立即出手幫忙、代人頂手或把情況扳回來（類似「救火」）。這個詞在香港廣東話日常語境中既可作為字面動作，也常用作口語化的比喻。
explanation_english: Literally, "扑水" means to plunge or dive into water, often used to describe jumping into water to rescue someone. Figuratively, it means to step in quickly to help out in an emergency, cover for someone, or salvage a situation (similar to "putting out a fire"). In Hong Kong Cantonese it is used both for the literal action and as a colloquial metaphor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲小朋友唔識游水，見到佢跌咗落河，佢即刻扑水去救佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 siu2 pang4 jau5 m4 sik1 jau4 seoi2, gin3 dou3 keoi5 dit3 zo2 lok6 ho4, keoi5 zik1 hak1 pok3 seoi2 heoi3 gau3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友不會游泳，看到他跌進河裡，他立刻跳入水中去救他。
examples.english_sentence: The kid couldn't swim; when he saw him fall into the river, he immediately jumped into the water to save him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司啲截稿日期好緊迫，阿陳臨時請假，同事即刻扑水幫手，先完成咗個項目。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 di1 zit3 gou3 jat6 kei4 hou2 gan2 bik1, aa3 can4 lam4 si4 ceng2 gaa3, tung4 si6 zik1 hak1 pok3 seoi2 bong1 sau2, sin1 jyun4 sing4 zo2 go3 hong6 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司截稿日期很緊迫，阿陳臨時請假，同事立刻出面幫忙，才完成了那個項目。
examples.english_sentence: The company's submission deadline was tight and Ah Chan took leave at the last minute; colleagues immediately stepped in to help, and only then was the project finished.

mandarin_meaning: 没抢到（票）；扑空；错失机会
english_meaning: to miss out (especially on tickets); to fail to get something; to miss an opportunity
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，常见于香港，通常指在抢购票券或争取某个机会时没有成功，意为“扑空”或“错过”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term commonly used in Hong Kong meaning to miss out—especially failing to get tickets or losing an opportunity at the last moment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今次買演唱會飛扑飞咗，啲飛好快就賣晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ci3 maai5 jin2 coeng3 wui2 fei1 pok3 fei1 zo2, di1 fei1 hou2 faai3 zau6 maai6 saat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次买演唱会的票我没抢到，票很快就卖光了。
examples.english_sentence: I missed out on the concert tickets this time — they sold out very quickly.

jyutping: paa4 syun4 daa2 gu2 jat1 jan4 gim1
mandarin_meaning: 一個人同時擔任多項工作；身兼數職。
english_meaning: One person taking on multiple roles or jobs at the same time; to wear many hats.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，原意指一個人既要划船又要打鼓，比喻一個人要同時做多項工作或擔當多重職責，常用於人手不足或分工不明的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiom literally meaning 'one person both paddles the boat and beats the drum.' It figuratively describes someone who takes on multiple jobs or responsibilities at once — often used when staff are few or roles overlap.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間小公司人手少，大家都要扒船打鼓一人兼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 siu2 gung1 si1 jan4 sau2 siu2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 jiu3 paa4 syun4 daa2 gu2 jat1 jan4 gim1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這家公司人手不足，大家都得身兼數職。
examples.english_sentence: This small company is short-staffed; everyone has to wear multiple hats.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿明做埋會計又做埋出納，真係扒船打鼓一人兼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 ming4 zou6 maai4 wui6 gai3 jau6 zou6 maai4 ceot1 naap6, zan1 hai6 paa4 syun4 daa2 gu2 jat1 jan4 gim1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿明既做會計又做出納，真是身兼數職。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Ming handles both accounting and cashier work — he really wears many hats.

mandarin_meaning: 打架 / 吵架 / 找人麻煩
english_meaning: to pick a fight; to quarrel or brawl
explanation_mandarin: 「打仗仔」是廣東話口語/俚語，用來形容與人打架、吵架或惹事，常帶有輕蔑或戲謔語氣（有時指小規模的打鬥或爭吵）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to get into a fight, pick a quarrel, or cause trouble. Often used informally and can imply a minor scuffle or squabble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鍾意同人打仗仔，班人都唔鐘意理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zung1 ji3 tung4 jan4 daa2 zoeng3 zai2, baan1 jan4 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是喜歡找人吵架，大家都不喜歡理他。
examples.english_sentence: He always likes to pick fights with people; nobody likes to deal with him.

jyutping: daa2 dou3 dang2 dou1 mou5 dik1 mak6 seoi2
mandarin_meaning: 毫無用處、一文不值
english_meaning: completely useless; worthless; of no value
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語 / 形容詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，用來形容某人或某事完全沒用、毫無價值；字面上以「滴墨水」比喻一點價值或可寫之處也沒有。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang/idiomatic expression used to describe someone or something as utterly useless or worthless; literally implies there's not even a drop of ink (i.e. nothing of substance) to write about.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個計劃打倒掟都冇滴墨水，根本唔值得投資。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 gai3 waak6 daa2 dou3 dang2 dou1 mou5 dik1 mak6 seoi2, gan1 bun2 m4 zik1 dak1 tau4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的計劃完全沒用，根本不值得投資。
examples.english_sentence: His plan is completely useless — not worth investing in.

mandarin_meaning: 定做；製作
english_meaning: to make; to manufacture; to tailor-make (customize)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指按需要製作或訂製某物（亦有寫作「打製」或用字變體「掣」的情況）。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to make or manufacture something, often custom-made or tailored to specifications (variant forms/characters exist).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢幫我打制一件西裝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bong1 ngo5 daa2 zai3 jat1 gin6 sai1 zong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他幫我訂做了一件西裝。
examples.english_sentence: He had a suit tailor-made for me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 間公司專門打制高檔手錶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaan1 gung1 si1 zyun1 mun4 daa2 zai3 gou1 dong6 sau2 biu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那家公司專門製作高檔手錶。
examples.english_sentence: That company specializes in making high-end watches.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲電腦程式係打制出嚟㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 din6 nou5 cing4 sik1 hai6 daa2 zai3 ceot1 lai4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些電腦程式是定製出來的。
examples.english_sentence: Those computer programs are custom-made.

mandarin_meaning: 占卜（算命）的預言應驗了／算卦成真
english_meaning: a colloquial expression meaning a fortune-telling or prediction came true
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話表達，指去打卜或算命後，師父/算命的預測結果應驗或成真。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning that a fortune-telling or prediction has come true — the divination proved accurate.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿明上個月去打卜，師傅話佢會同Mary拍拖，結果真係打卜成。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 ming4 soeng6 go3 jyut6 heoi3 daa2 buk1, si1 fu6 waa6 keoi5 wui5 tung4 Mary paak3 to1, git3 gwo2 zan1 hai6 daa2 buk1 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿明上個月去算命，師父說他會和Mary交往，結果真的應驗了。
examples.english_sentence: A Ming went to have his fortune told last month; the fortuneteller said he'd start dating Mary, and it turned out to be true.

mandarin_meaning: 踢友谊赛 / 进行一场友谊赛
english_meaning: to play a friendly match (usually football); to play an exhibition game for practice or fun
explanation_mandarin: “打友谊波”是香港粤语的口语表达，字面上是“打（球）”＋“友谊（赛）”＋“波（球）”，通常指踢一场友谊赛／表演赛，常用于足球或其他球类的非正式比赛，侧重练习、磨合或娱乐性质。
explanation_english: “打友谊波” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang literally meaning ‘play a friendship ball’. It refers to playing a friendly/exhibition match (often football) — usually informal, for practice, team coordination or fun rather than competition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋星期日打友誼波，大家主要係練習同埋玩下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sing1 kei4 jat6 daa2 jau5 ji6 bo1, daai6 gaa1 zyu2 jiu3 hai6 lin6 zaap6 tung4 maai4 waan2 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们星期日踢友谊赛，大家主要是练习和玩一下。
examples.english_sentence: We played a friendly match on Sunday; everyone mainly practiced and had fun.

mandarin_meaning: 未查到通行词义；可能为错别字或罕见方言用语
english_meaning: No attested meaning; likely a typo, a very obscure/obsolete or nonstandard regional term
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 短語（非標準/疑似錯別字/罕見用語）
explanation_mandarin: 「打嘶餼」在主要粵語詞典與常見語料中均無明確條目。逐字拆解：打（做、擊）、嘶（表示嘶聲）、餼（古字，與贈送食物或祭祀食物有關）。整體看來不像現代粵語的常用詞，可能是打字錯誤或區域、家族性的罕見說法。若想表達常見粵語動詞，可考慮是否本意為「打嘢」「打噏」等常用口語詞。
explanation_english: There is no attested entry for "打嘶餼" in major Cantonese dictionaries or common corpora. Character-by-character: 打 (do/hit), 嘶 (hiss), 餼 (an archaic character related to giving food). As a whole it does not appear to be a standard modern Cantonese expression and is likely a typo, an extremely obscure/archaic form, or a localized/private usage. If you meant a common colloquial verb, consider alternatives such as "打嘢" or "打噏" depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我搵唔到「打嘶餼」嘅意思，可能係打錯字或者唔係通用嘅粵語詞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 wan2 m4 dou3 "daa2 si1 sik6" ge3 ji3si1, ho2 nang4 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6 waak6 ze2 m4 hai6 tung1 jung6 ge3 jyut6 jyu5 ci4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我找不到「打嘶餼」的意思，可能是打錯字或者不是通用的粵語詞。
examples.english_sentence: I can't find the meaning of "打嘶餼"; it might be a typo or not a commonly used Cantonese word.

mandarin_meaning: 作秀／表面功夫
english_meaning: to put on a show; a performative act for appearance's sake
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，通常指為了吸引注意或掩飾真實情況而做的表面性、演示性行為，類似「作秀」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to perform something mainly for show—an act meant to attract attention or hide reality rather than produce substantive results; akin to 'putting on a show.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰場辯論會好似淨係打國技，冇講實際政策。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 coeng4 bin6 leon6 wui2 hou2 ci5 zing6 hai6 daa2 gwok3 gei6, mou5 gong2 sat6 zai3 zing3 caak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那場辯論會好像只是作秀，沒有談及實際政策。
examples.english_sentence: That debate seemed like it was just putting on a show and didn't discuss concrete policies.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲宣傳淨係打國技，目的係掩飾成績差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 syun1 cyun4 zing6 hai6 daa2 gwok3 gei6, muk6 dik1 hai6 jim2 sik1 sing4 zik1 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的那些宣傳只是作秀，目的是掩蓋成績差。
examples.english_sentence: Their publicity is just for show; the aim is to cover up poor results.

jyutping: daa2 coeng4 daai6 fung1, zap1 faai3 syu6 jip6
mandarin_meaning: 虛張聲勢，做些無關緊要的小事；大張旗鼓卻沒實際用處
english_meaning: to make a big show or fuss but only do trivial, insignificant things; all show and no substance
explanation_mandarin: 形容人誇大其詞、裝腔作勢，但實際上只是做一些無關緊要或無實質效果的事情。
explanation_english: Describes someone who makes a lot of noise or shows off, but only performs trivial or pointless actions with no real effect.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度打场大风，执块树叶，做啲無謂嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 daa2 coeng4 daai6 fung1, zap1 faai3 syu6 jip6, zou6 di1 mou4 wai6 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在這裡大張旗鼓、做些無關緊要的事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make a big show and fuss over trivial things here.

mandarin_meaning: 光着脚；赤脚；（引申）生活简陋或贫穷
english_meaning: to go barefoot; (figuratively) to be poor or living in humble/rough conditions
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是光着脚走路或活动，通常指不穿鞋；在口语中也可引申指生活简陋、贫穷或条件艰苦。
explanation_english: Literally means to go or work barefoot (not wearing shoes). In colloquial use it can also imply poverty or living/working in rough, humble conditions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細個成日打大赤腳喺田度玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 go3 sing4 jat6 daa2 daai6 cek3 goek3 hai2 tin4 dou6 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他小时候经常光着脚在田里玩。
examples.english_sentence: When he was little he often played barefoot in the fields.

jyutping: daa2 jyun4 zaai1 m4 jiu3 wo4 soeng6
mandarin_meaning: 恩將仇報；得了好處之後不感恩、拋棄或嫌棄幫助自己的人
english_meaning: To take advantage of someone or accept their help and then discard or repudiate them; to be ungrateful after receiving benefits.
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容接受別人的幫助或好處後，反而嫌棄、拋棄或忘恩負義，不知感恩。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who, after receiving help or benefits, turns against or abandons the helper — essentially being ungrateful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢幫咗我咁多，最後打完斋唔要和尚，真係唔識做人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bong1 zo2 ngo5 gam2 do1, zeoi3 hau6 daa2 jyun4 zaai1 m4 jiu3 wo4 soeng6, zan1 hai6 m4 sik1 zou6 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他幫了我這麼多，最後卻恩將仇報，真沒良心。
examples.english_sentence: He helped me so much, but in the end he discarded me after getting what he wanted — really heartless.

mandarin_meaning: 打工的女孩／女工（指在服務業或低薪工作中的年輕女性）
english_meaning: a working girl; a female worker (often a young woman in low-paid or service jobs)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的口語詞，指從事打工（通常為服務業或相對低薪的工作）的女性，語氣可中性或帶有輕微貶義，視語境而定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term for a female worker, typically a young woman employed in low-paid or service-sector jobs. The tone can be neutral or mildly derogatory depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我個妹妹而家做打工妹，喺茶餐廳做侍應，成日都好忙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 mui6 mui6 ji4 gaa1 zou6 daa2 gung1 mui6, hai2 caa4 caan1 teng1 zou6 si6 jing3, sing4 jat6 dou1 hou2 mong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我妹妹現在做打工妹，在茶餐廳當服務員，每天都很忙。
examples.english_sentence: My younger sister is working as a 'daagong mui' — she works as a waitress in a cha chaan teng and is busy every day.

jyutping: daa2 dak1 gang1 je6 jau6 coeng4
mandarin_meaning: （玩/打/工作）越打越晚、持續越久；越晚越長時間地做某事（多指打機、應酬或通宵工作）
english_meaning: To keep doing something later into the night and for longer periods (often referring to gaming, socializing, or working late)
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，形容做某件事愈來愈晚開始、愈做愈久，常用於打機、通宵應酬或加班等情況，含有疲累或無節制的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial phrase describing doing something progressively later into the night and for longer durations. Commonly used for gaming, partying, or working overnight, often implying tiredness or lack of restraint.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 昨晚同朋友打機，打得更多夜又長，第二朝返工好攰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zok6 maan5 tung4 pang4 jau5 daa2 gei1, daa2 dak1 gang1 je6 jau6 coeng4, dai6 ji6 ziu1 faan1 gung1 hou2 gui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚和朋友打电玩，玩得更晚更久，第二天上班很累。
examples.english_sentence: Last night I played video games with friends, stayed up later and played much longer — I was really tired at work the next day.

mandarin_meaning: 打（別人的）手心；拍打手掌（常作為懲罰）
english_meaning: to slap someone's palm (often as a form of punishment)
explanation_mandarin: 指用手或尺等拍打別人的手掌，常用於管教小孩或作為輕微的體罰。
explanation_english: Refers to striking or slapping someone's palm (with the hand or a ruler), commonly used as a mild form of punishment or discipline, especially for children.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細佬唔聽話，阿媽就打佢手板。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 m4 ting1 waa6, aa3 maa1 zau6 daa2 keoi5 sau2 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 弟弟不聽話，媽媽就打他的手心。
examples.english_sentence: My younger brother was naughty, so mom slapped his palm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺學校做錯嘢，可能會被老師打手板。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 hok6 haau6 zou6 co3 je5, ho2 nang4 wui5 bei6 lou5 si1 daa2 sau2 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在學校做錯事，可能會被老師打手心。
examples.english_sentence: If you do something wrong at school, you might get your palm slapped by the teacher.

mandarin_meaning: 未見於常用詞典的詞彙；字面可譯為「打、拍、肋、赤」，可能為方言、俚語或個別創新用法，真實含義不明
english_meaning: Not attested in standard references; literally 'hit/clap rib/red'; possibly a dialectal expression, slang, or coined phrase with uncertain meaning
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 不確定（可能為俚語/俗語）
explanation_mandarin: 「打拍肋赤」在主要粵語詞典與資料庫中未能找到確切記錄。從字面上看由「打」「拍」「肋」「赤」四字組成，可能是口語或地區性用法，需具體語境才能判斷含義。若遇到此詞，建議向使用者查詢具體語境或來源。
explanation_english: This phrase is not found in major Cantonese references. Literally composed of the characters 'hit', 'pat/clap', 'rib', 'red', it may be a regional or colloquial expression whose meaning is unclear without context. If encountered, ask the speaker for context or source.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我聽過有人講「打拍肋赤」，但唔肯定佢係乜意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 teng1 gwo3 jau5 jan4 gong2 "daa2 paak3 lak6 cek3", daan6 m4 hang2 ding6 keoi5 hai6 mat1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我听过有人说“打拍肋赤”，但不确定它是什么意思。
examples.english_sentence: I've heard people say "打拍肋赤", but I'm not sure what it means.

jyutping: daa2 zaai1 hok6, dou6 jan4 sing1 sin1
mandarin_meaning: 假裝虔誠或作秀，用宗教/道德姿態博取讚賞或說教他人
english_meaning: To put on a show of piety or virtue — performative religiosity used to gain praise or moralize others
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容表面上做出修行或行善的樣子，實際上是作秀、虛偽地以宗教或道德立場來博取他人讚賞或教化別人。
explanation_english: Describes someone who pretends to be pious or righteous as a performance — hypocritically using religion or moral posturing to win approval or preach to others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺街度講佛，實際上係打斋鹤，度人升仙，淨係想攞人讚賞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 dou6 gong2 fat6, sat6 zai3 soeng6 hai6 daa2 zaai1 hok6, dou6 jan4 sing1 sin1, zing6 hai6 soeng2 lo2 jan4 zaan3 soeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在街上宣講佛法，實際上是假裝虔誠、打斋鹤、度人升仙，只是想博取別人的讚賞。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps preaching Buddhism on the street, but actually he's putting on a show of piety — performatively 'saving' people to look virtuous — just to get praise.

mandarin_meaning: 用斧头砍、劈（如伐木、劈柴）
english_meaning: to chop/split with an axe; to cut wood
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是用斧头进行砍、劈的动作（例如伐木、劈柴）。在廣東話中通常指實際的砍伐動作，較常用於描述體力勞動或伐木場景，並不普遍作為比喻。
explanation_english: Literal meaning: to swing an axe to chop or split something (e.g., logging, splitting firewood). In Cantonese it is typically used for the physical action of chopping and is commonly found in contexts describing manual labor or woodcutting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝佢去山度打斧頭，砍咗啲柴返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 keoi5 heoi3 saan1 dou6 daa2 fu2 tau4, ham2 zo2 di1 caai4 faan1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天早上去山上打斧头，砍了一些柴回来。
examples.english_sentence: He went up the mountain this morning to chop wood with an axe and came back with some firewood.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺工地要打斧頭劈開舊木板。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gung1 dei6 jiu3 daa2 fu2 tau4 pik1 hoi1 gau6 muk6 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在工地上要用斧头把旧木板劈开。
examples.english_sentence: He needs to use an axe to split the old wooden planks at the construction site.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）完全結束／搞掂；（口語）鬆弛、累倒或完全被打敗
english_meaning: (slang) completely finished/done; (colloquial) utterly exhausted or totally beaten
explanation_mandarin: 「打晒纈」是廣東話的口語／俚語，常用來表示某件事已經全部做完、收尾（相當於「搞掂晒」）；在不同語境下亦可表示人累到完全撐不住或被徹底打敗。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression. It commonly means that something is completely finished or wrapped up (similar to "all done"). Depending on context it can also describe a person who is utterly exhausted or has been completely defeated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝趕咗成晚報告，依家我打晒纈，要休息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 gon2 zo2 sing4 maan5 bou3 gou3, ji1 gaa1 ngo5 daa2 saai3 kit3, jiu3 jau1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上赶了整晚的报告，現在我累垮了，要休息。
examples.english_sentence: I spent the whole night rushing the report this morning; now I'm completely exhausted (打晒纈) and need to rest.

mandarin_meaning: 下棋/移動棋子；（比喻）成為棋子、被人利用
english_meaning: to play chess / move chess pieces; (figurative) to be a pawn, to be used by others
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指下棋、擺弄棋子；引申義指在某種局勢中只是被人操控或利用的角色（做棋子）。
explanation_english: Literally means to play chess or move chess pieces. Figuratively it can mean being a pawn — a person who is manipulated or used by others in a situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋下晝去公園打棋子啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 haa6 zau3 heoi3 gung1 jyun4 daa2 kei4 zi2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們下午去公園下棋吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go play chess in the park this afternoon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺呢單嘢入面淨係做緊個棋子，被人利用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ni1 daan1 je5 jap6 min6 zing6 hai6 zou6 gan2 go3 kei4 zi2, bei6 jan4 lei6 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在這件事裡只是個棋子，被人利用。
examples.english_sentence: He's just a pawn in this matter, being used by others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話唔想畀朋友當棋子，拒絕咗嗰個計劃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 m4 soeng2 bei2 pang4 jau5 dong3 kei4 zi2, geoi2 zeok6 zo2 go2 go3 gai3 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說不想被朋友當棋子，拒絕了那個計劃。
examples.english_sentence: He said he didn't want to be treated as a pawn by his friends, so he refused that plan.

mandarin_meaning: 横着过来；横躺着过来；（引申）横着挡路或不配合、顽固地阻拦
english_meaning: to come/lie across sideways; (figurative) to block, obstruct, or act uncooperatively by coming in sideways
explanation_mandarin: 原义指以横向的姿势过来或横着横躺，常用于描述某物或某人横向挡住通道。口语中也可引申为顽固、不配合、横蛮地阻拦。
explanation_english: Literally 'to come/lie across sideways' — used to describe something or someone positioned crosswise blocking a passage. Colloquially it can also mean to obstruct, be uncooperative, or behave stubbornly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 部貨車泊得唔好，打横嚟擋住條行車線。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou6 fo3 ce1 paak3 dak1 m4 hou2, daa2 waang4 lai4 dong2 zyu6 tiu4 hang4 ce1 sin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那輛貨車停得不好，橫着擋住了車道。
examples.english_sentence: The truck parked badly, lying across and blocking the lane.

mandarin_meaning: 即使已經沒有回旋餘地或時機已過，仍然為小利或瑣事討價還價/斤斤計較
english_meaning: To haggle or quibble over trivial matters or small savings when it's pointless or too late
explanation_mandarin: 形容在事情已無轉機或時機已過的情況下，仍然為小利或瑣事討價還價，顯得不合時宜或吝嗇。
explanation_english: Describes someone who continues to haggle or nitpick over trivial amounts or details when there is no point — appearing ungenerous or inappropriate.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件事已經決定咗，你而家仲打死狗講價做乜？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 si6 ji5 ging1 kyut3 ding6 zo2, nei5 ji4 gaa1 zung6 daa2 sei2 gau2 gong2 gaa3 zou6 mat1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 事情已經決定了，你現在還在打死狗講價做什麼？
examples.english_sentence: The matter has already been decided — what are you still haggling about?

jyutping: daa2 laan6 saa1 pun4 man6 dou3 niu6
mandarin_meaning: 穷追猛问、盘问到底，逼得对方招供或出丑（字面：盘问到对方尿裤子）
english_meaning: To interrogate or badger someone relentlessly until they crack/confess (literally 'break the sand tray and question until they pee').
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，形容不停、刻意地盤問或追問，把對方逼到承認或出丑。常帶誇張與粗俗色彩，屬口語或俚語用法。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to badger or interrogate someone mercilessly until they break or confess. The phrase is figurative and somewhat vulgar.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方打爛沙盤問到尿，終於逼到佢承認犯案。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 daa2 laan6 saa1 pun4 man6 dou3 niu6, zung1 jyu4 bik1 dou3 keoi5 sing4 jan4 faan6 on3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方穷追猛问，终于逼得他承认犯罪。
examples.english_sentence: The police grilled him relentlessly and finally forced him to admit the crime.

mandarin_meaning: 闲聊；聊天；闲谈
english_meaning: to chat idly; to gossip; to have a casual chat
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指與人閒談、閒聊或談論家長里短，通常含有打發時間或說閒話的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to chat idly or gossip — talking casually, often to pass time or discuss trivial matters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你哋喺度打牙兒，做緊嘢未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 hai2 dou6 daa2 ngaa4 ji4, zou6 gan2 je5 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你们在这里闲聊，还在工作吗？
examples.english_sentence: You guys are chatting here — are you working?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日同人打牙兒，乜嘢正經事都唔做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 tung4 jan4 daa2 ngaa4 ji4, mat1 je5 zing3 ging1 si6 dou1 m4 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是和别人闲聊，什么正经事都不做。
examples.english_sentence: He’s always chatting with people and doesn’t do any proper work.

mandarin_meaning: 闲聊；聊天；闲扯
english_meaning: to chat idly; to shoot the breeze; chit-chat
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，用來形容和人閒談、聊天、沒甚麼正經內容地閒扯，有時帶有打發時間的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to chat idly or shoot the breeze — to have an informal, often aimless conversation, typically for passing time or socializing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去茶餐廳打牙铰，傾下最近啲八卦啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 caa4 caan1 teng1 daa2 ngaa4 gaau1, king1 haa5 zeoi3 gan6 di1 baat3 gwaa3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去茶餐廳閒聊，聊聊最近的八卦吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the cha chaan teng tonight and have a chat about the latest gossip.

mandarin_meaning: 闲聊；聊天；聊天打发时间（粤语俗语）
english_meaning: to chat idly; to shoot the breeze; to have a casual chat (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「打牙骹（鉸）」是香港粵語俗語，意思是閒聊、吹水或隨便談天，多用於朋友或熟人之間聚會時打發時間或聊天。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang expression meaning to chat casually or gossip — to shoot the breeze. Often used when friends meet and pass the time talking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚冇嘢做，不如去茶餐廳打牙骹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 mou5 je5 zou6, bat1 jyu4 heoi3 caa4 caan1 teng1 daa2 ngaa4 gaau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚沒事，不如去茶餐廳聊聊天吧。
examples.english_sentence: Nothing to do tonight — let's go to the cha chaan teng and have a chat.

mandarin_meaning: 打弹珠；玩玻璃弹子
english_meaning: to play marbles (glass marbles)
explanation_mandarin: 指以玻璃彈子（彈珠）進行的兒童遊戲或玩耍，屬廣東話口語用法，常見於童年或街頭遊戲的情境。
explanation_english: Refers to the children's game of playing with glass marbles. A colloquial Cantonese expression often used in contexts of childhood or street play.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細個嘅時候我哋成日打玻子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 go3 ge3 si4 hau6 ngo5 dei6 sing4 jat6 daa2 bo1 zi2
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小时候我们经常打弹珠（玻璃弹子）。
examples.english_sentence: When we were kids we often played marbles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺街度見到幾個細路仔喺度打玻子，好有童年味道。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gaai1 dou6 gin3 dou2 gei2 go3 sai3 lou6 zai2 hai2 dou6 daa2 bo1 zi2
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在街上看到几个小孩在打玻子，充满童年气息。
examples.english_sentence: I saw some kids playing marbles on the street—it brought back childhood memories.

mandarin_meaning: 在政府或公營機構工作；做公職
english_meaning: to work for the government; to be a civil servant or be on the public payroll
explanation_mandarin: 口語或俚語用法，字面上有「替皇室（或政府）工作」之意，實指受僱於政府或公營機構，做比較穩定的行政或公職工作。視語境可帶玩笑或輕微貶義。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang phrase literally meaning 'to work for the royal house', used to mean being employed by the government or a public institution (i.e., working as a civil servant). It often implies steady, nine-to-five employment and can be teasing or mildly pejorative depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家打皇家工，朝九晚五，穩陣啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 daa2 wong4 gaa1 gung1, ziu1 gau2 maan5 ng5, wan2 zan6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在在政府工作，朝九晚五，比較穩定。
examples.english_sentence: He now works for the government, nine-to-five, which is relatively stable.

mandarin_meaning: 開玩笑；耍鬧；胡鬧
english_meaning: to joke around; to mess about; to tease/playfully fool around
explanation_mandarin: 「打皮」是廣東話俗語，表示耍鬧、開玩笑或不認真地胡鬧、取笑別人，語氣通常較隨意或調皮。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term meaning to joke around, mess about, or tease someone playfully. It implies playful, not-serious behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日打皮，依家係上課時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 daa2 pei4, ji4 gaa1 hai6 soeng5 fo3 si4 gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要老是開玩笑，現在是上課時間。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep fooling around; it's class time now.

mandarin_meaning: （正在）打、正在做某事（进行时）
english_meaning: to be doing something right now; doing/playing/hitting (progressive)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 动词短语（进行体/进行时）
explanation_mandarin: 由動詞「打」和助詞「緊」組成，表示動作正在進行或持續中。根據上下文可指打電話、打針、打機、打人等正在發生的動作，屬粵語口語常用表達。
explanation_english: Formed from the verb 打 plus the aspect particle 緊, indicating an action is currently in progress. Depending on context it can mean making a call, receiving an injection, playing games, hitting someone, etc. Common colloquial Cantonese usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家打緊電話，唔好理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 daa2 gan2 din6 waa2, m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在正在打电话，别理他。
examples.english_sentence: He's on the phone right now; don't bother him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我打緊機，等陣先傾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 daa2 gan2 gei1, dang2 zan6 sin1 king1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我正在打机，等一下再谈。
examples.english_sentence: I'm playing games right now; let's talk later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 病人而家打緊針，等佢好啲先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: beng6 jan4 ji4 gaa1 daa2 gan2 zan1, dang2 keoi5 hou2 di1 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 病人现在正在打针，等他好一点再说。
examples.english_sentence: The patient is receiving an injection now; wait until they feel better.

jyutping: daa2 lok6 mun4 ngaa4 daai3 hyut3 tan1
mandarin_meaning: 忍气吞声；含血忍受（被羞辱或吃亏却不反抗）
english_meaning: to swallow one's pride and endure humiliation; to grit one's teeth and accept a beating or loss without protest
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，字面意思是被打掉門牙帶着血吞下，形容遭受羞辱或損失但不反抗、忍氣吞聲。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally meaning 'knocked-out front teeth swallowed with blood.' It describes enduring humiliation or loss without resisting — swallowing pride and keeping silent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀人欺負，最後都係打落门牙带血吞唔出聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 hei1 fu6, zeoi6 hau6 dou1 hai6 daa2 lok6 mun4 ngaa4 daai3 hyut3 tan1 m4 ceot1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人欺负，最后还是忍气吞声，不出声反抗。
examples.english_sentence: He was bullied and in the end he swallowed his pride and didn't make a scene.

jyutping: daa2 se4 m4 sei2 bei2 se4 ngaau5
mandarin_meaning: 打蛇不死，反被蛇咬
english_meaning: If you don't finish off the snake when you hit it, it will bite you — i.e., failing to deal with a problem thoroughly will lead to trouble later.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻處理事情不徹底、留下隱患，最終可能招致更大的麻煩或損失。
explanation_english: A proverb meaning that if a problem is not dealt with thoroughly, the remaining issue can come back to cause trouble later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做事拖拖拉拉，打蛇唔死畀蛇咬，遲啲會出大事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 si6 to1 to1 laai1 laai1, daa2 se4 m4 sei2 bei2 se4 ngaau5, ci4 di1 wui5 ceot1 daai6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要做事拖拖拉拉，打蛇不死被蛇咬，遲早會出大問題。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be sloppy — if you don't finish the job properly, it will come back to bite you; sooner or later it'll cause big trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋唔可以淨係罰個人一次，如果唔徹底解決，打蛇唔死畀蛇咬，問題會再嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 m4 ho2 ji5 zing6 hai6 fat6 go3 jan4 jat1 ci3, jyu4 gwo2 m4 cit3 dai2 gaai2 kyut3, daa2 se4 m4 sei2 bei2 se4 ngaau5, man6 tai4 wui5 zoi3 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們不能只是處罰一個人，如果不徹底解決，打蛇不死會被蛇咬，問題會再發生。
examples.english_sentence: We can't just punish one person — if we don't solve it thoroughly, the problem will come back to bite us.

mandarin_meaning: 打蛇随棍上 / 乘势而上，趁机加入或扩大某种行为
english_meaning: to take advantage of the momentum; to seize the opportunity and join in or push something further (often 'jump on the bandwagon')
explanation_mandarin: 形容順著事態的發展採取行動，趁機加入、擴大或跟進某種行為；有時含有見風轉舵或跟風的意思。
explanation_english: Describes acting in line with a situation's momentum—seizing the opportunity to join in or press an advantage; can also imply going along with others or piling on.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到有人投訴，佢就打蛇随棍上，趁機講多兩句。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou2 jau5 jan4 tau4 sou3, keoi5 zau6 daa2 se4 ceoi4 gwan3 soeng6, can3 gei1 gong2 do1 loeng5 geoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到有人投诉，他就打蛇随棍上，趁机多说了两句。
examples.english_sentence: When he saw someone complaining, he jumped on the bandwagon and added a couple more comments.

mandarin_meaning: 吃火锅
english_meaning: to have/eat hot pot (hotpot)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，指大家围着一锅热汤边煮边吃各种食材，通常是聚餐或社交活动的一种形式，香港和广东地区常用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to eat hot pot together — a communal meal where people cook ingredients in a shared pot at the table. Commonly used in Hong Kong and Guangdong.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去你屋企打邊爐啦？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 nei5 uk1 kei2 daa2 bin1 lou4 laa1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去你家吃火锅吧？
examples.english_sentence: Shall we go to your place for hot pot tonight?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聖誕節通常會同屋企人打邊爐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing3 daan3 zit3 tung1 soeng4 wui5 tung4 uk1 kei2 jan4 daa2 bin1 lou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 圣诞节通常会和家人一起吃火锅。
examples.english_sentence: At Christmas we usually have hot pot with the family.

jyutping: daa2 bin1 lou4 m4 tung4 daa2 si2 kut3
mandarin_meaning: “打边炉唔同打屎窟”是粤语俗语/俚语，用来强调两件事完全不同、不能混为一谈，常带粗俗色彩，语境中有时也用来劝人不要胡闹或不认真对待。
english_meaning: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning 'having hotpot is not the same as digging a shit hole' — used figuratively to say two things are completely different or not comparable; often coarse and used to warn against messing around or conflating matters.
explanation_mandarin: 用于比喻兩件事物截然不同，不能相提並論；語氣粗俗，常用來提醒對方別把正式或認真的事當作玩鬧或隨便處理。
explanation_english: Used metaphorically to state that two things are entirely different and not comparable; it's a coarse expression often used to tell someone not to treat something serious as a joke or to stop messing around.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意要認真，打边炉唔同打屎窟，唔好亂嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 ji3 jiu3 jing6 zan1, daa2 bin1 lou4 m4 tung4 daa2 si2 kut3, m4 hou2 lyun6 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意要认真，打边炉和打屎窟不是一回事，别胡来。
examples.english_sentence: Do business seriously — having hotpot is not the same as messing around; don't fool around.

mandarin_meaning: 玩电子游戏 / 打游戏机
english_meaning: to play video games (on an arcade machine, console, computer, or mobile)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，指玩電子遊戲，可以包括街機、家用主機、電腦或手機遊戲。常用於日常談話，亦可縮短為「打機」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to play video games — including arcade machines, consoles, computers, or mobile games. Common in everyday speech and often shortened to "打機" (daa2 gei1).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋去商場打遊戲機啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 soeng1 coeng4 daa2 jau4 hei3 gei1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我们去商场玩电子游戏吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the mall to play video games tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日打遊戲機，唔太肯讀書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 daa2 jau4 hei3 gei1, m4 taai3 hang2 duk6 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是打游戏机，不太愿意读书。
examples.english_sentence: He always plays video games and isn't very willing to study.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路仔好鍾意去電玩店打遊戲機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 zai2 hou2 zung1 ji3 heoi3 din6 waan4 dim3 daa2 jau4 hei3 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子很喜欢去电玩店打游戏机。
examples.english_sentence: Kids love going to arcades to play video games.

jyutping: daa2 sing2 sap6 ji6 go3 zing1 san4
mandarin_meaning: 使某人徹底清醒或高度警覺（口語）
english_meaning: to jolt someone awake (figuratively); to make someone fully alert or highly vigilant
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，形容某件事或某人的言行使人從麻木、疏忽或散漫的狀態中被強烈喚醒，變得警覺或振作起來。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing something that shocks or prompts a person out of complacency or inattention, making them alert, vigilant, or energised.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰次差啲死嘅經歷，真係打醒咗我十二個精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 ci3 caa1 di1 sei2 ge3 ging1 lik6, zan1 hai6 daa2 sing2 zo2 ngo5 sap6 ji6 go3 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那次差點喪命的經歷，真的讓我徹底清醒過來／變得非常警覺。
examples.english_sentence: That near-death experience really jolted me awake and made me completely alert.

mandarin_meaning: 接種記錄卡；疫苗接種證明
english_meaning: vaccination card; immunization record
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俗稱，指用來記錄已接種疫苗或注射紀錄的紙卡或證明，常用於入學、醫療或官方查驗。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for the paper/card that records vaccinations or injections, used as proof for school enrollment, medical records, or official checks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你記唔記得帶埋打針紙去醫院？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gei3 m4 gei3 dak1 daai3 maai4 daa2 zam1 zi2 heoi3 ji1 jyun2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你記得帶上接種記錄卡去醫院嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Did you remember to bring your vaccination card to the hospital?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 入學要交打針紙，唔交可能入唔到學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jap6 hok6 jiu3 gaau1 daa2 zam1 zi2, m4 gaau1 ho2 nang4 jap6 m4 dou3 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 入學需要提交接種記錄卡，不交可能無法入學。
examples.english_sentence: Schools require vaccination records for enrollment; without them you might not be allowed to enroll.

mandarin_meaning: 敲鑼打鼓地招攬生意；大肆宣傳以吸引顧客
english_meaning: to drum up business; to loudly or showily solicit customers/attention
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指用嘈雜或誇張的方式招徠生意或吸引別人的注意，帶有較強的商業或宣傳意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to attract customers or attention by noisy or showy methods — essentially to drum up business or promote oneself loudly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日打鑼噉揾生意，成日大聲招呼客人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 daa2 lo4 gam2 wan2 sang1 ji3, sing4 jat6 daai6 sing1 ziu1 fu1 haak3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天敲鑼打鼓地招攬生意，經常大聲招呼客人。
examples.english_sentence: He’s always drumming up business, often loudly calling out to customers.

jyutping: daa2 zam1 sik6 wong4 lin4, tung3 fu2
mandarin_meaning: 打针吃黄连，很痛苦（比喻处境难受、受罪）
english_meaning: To get an injection and eat Huanglian (a very bitter herb) — very painful; to endure bitter suffering
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語把兩種令人不快或痛苦的經歷（打針與吃苦藥黃連）並列，用來形容身心受苦、處境難受或遭遇多重折磨，常見於廣東話口語中。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial saying pairs two unpleasant experiences (getting an injection and taking the very bitter herb Huanglian) to describe enduring severe or compounded suffering. It is used informally to express that someone is having a hard time or going through a painful ordeal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家要打針又要食嗰啲好苦嘅藥，真係打針食黃連，痛苦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 jiu3 daa2 zam1 jau6 jiu3 sik6 go2 di1 hou2 fu2 ge3 joek6, zan1 hai6 daa2 zam1 sik6 wong4 lin4, tung3 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在要打針還要吃那種很苦的藥，真是打針吃黃連，痛苦。
examples.english_sentence: Now I have to get an injection and also take that very bitter medicine — it's really painful.

mandarin_meaning: 大張旗鼓地招攬生意／賺錢
english_meaning: to drum up business or money in an ostentatious/noisy way; to solicit customers loudly
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，形容藉著熱鬧或大張旗鼓的方式招攬生意或吸引客人、賺錢，多含略帶批評或諷刺的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to solicit business or money by making a loud or showy display. It often carries a mildly critical or tongue-in-cheek tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間小店成日打锣噉揾生意，喺門口大聲招呼客人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 siu2 dim3 sing4 jat6 daa2 lo4 gam2 wan2 sang1 ji3, hai2 mun4 hau2 daai6 seng1 ziu1 fu1 haak3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間小店常常大張旗鼓地招攬生意，在門口大聲招呼客人。
examples.english_sentence: That little shop is always loudly drumming up business, calling out to customers at the entrance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日打锣噉揾錢，做啲實際啲嘅嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 daa2 lo4 gam2 wan2 cin2, zou6 di1 sat6 zai3 di1 ge3 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要總是大張旗鼓地賺錢，做些更實際的事吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always try to drum up money ostentatiously; do something more practical.

mandarin_meaning: 風雨交加 / 刮風下雨
english_meaning: to be battered by wind and rain (stormy weather); figuratively, to face hardships or adverse conditions
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，字面指刮風下雨、天氣惡劣；也可引申為遭遇艱難或困境。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally describing windy and rainy (stormy) weather. It can also be used figuratively to mean encountering difficulties or adversity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 就算打風打雨，我哋都要返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zau6 syun3 daa2 fung1 daa2 jyu5, ngo5 dei6 dou1 jiu3 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 即使刮風下雨，我們也要上班。
examples.english_sentence: Even if it's windy and rainy, we still have to go to work.

mandarin_meaning: 打风的时候 / 颱風期間
english_meaning: during a typhoon / while a typhoon warning is in effect
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指颱風來襲或颱風警告生效的那段時間，常用來描述在此期間應注意的行為或安排。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning the period when a typhoon is occurring or a typhoon signal is in force; used to talk about actions or arrangements during that time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 打風舊唔好出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daa2 fung1 gau6 m4 hou2 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 打风的时候不要外出。
examples.english_sentence: Don't go out during a typhoon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學校打風舊會提早放學。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 haau6 daa2 fung1 gau6 wui5 tai4 zou2 fong3 hok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有台风时学校会提前放学。
examples.english_sentence: When there's a typhoon, schools will dismiss early.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲舖頭打風舊會關門靜待天氣好返先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 pou3 tau4 daa2 fung1 gau6 wui5 gwaan1 mun4 zing6 doi6 tin1 hei3 hou2 faan1 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些店在打风时会关门，等天气好转再营业。
examples.english_sentence: Some shops close during a typhoon and wait for the weather to improve before reopening.

cantonese: 打风唔荡西，三日就翻归
jyutping: daa2 fung1 m4 dong6 sai1, saam1 jat6 zau6 faan1 gwai1
mandarin_meaning: 遇到风灾或困境不要慌张，过几天很快就会恢复正常。
english_meaning: When a storm or trouble hits, don't panic — things will return to normal within a few days.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東俗語。字面指遇到打風（颱風）時不要外出或驚慌，耐心等候，三天內情況通常會回復，延伸為遇事冷靜，短期內可望恢復原狀。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally referencing a typhoon: don’t rush or panic during the storm; if you wait it will typically settle in about three days. Figuratively it advises staying calm during difficulties because things often return to normal quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 雖然而家生意唔好，但阿叔成日話："打风唔荡西，三日就翻归。"
examples.jyutping_sentence: seoi1 jin4 ji4 gaa1 sang1 ji3 m4 hou2, daan6 aa3 suk1 sing4 jat6 waa6: "daa2 fung1 m4 dong6 sai1, saam1 jat6 zau6 faan1 gwai1."
examples.mandarin_sentence: 虽然现在生意不好，但叔叔常说：“遇到风灾不要慌，三天就会恢复。”
examples.english_sentence: Although business is bad now, my uncle often says, "Weather the storm — everything will be back to normal in three days."

mandarin_meaning: （口語、粗俗）以請吃飯為藉口與人發生性關係（推測性釋義，屬地區性俚語，含義可能有變化）
english_meaning: (colloquial, vulgar) to invite someone to a meal as a pretext for having sex (inferred; regional slang; meaning may vary)
explanation_mandarin: 『打饭炮』為非正式俚語，字面由「打飯」（請吃飯、吃飯）與「打炮」（粗俗語，發生性行為）組合。常見於口語或網絡用語，帶有性暗示與貶義。由於用法地區性強，實際含義或語感會隨語境改變，使用時需注意場合與對象。
explanation_english: '打饭炮' is an informal, vulgar slang phrase composed of '打飯' (to have/eat a meal together) and '打炮' (vulgar: to have sex). It typically refers to inviting someone to a meal as a pretext to have sex. Usage is regional and context-dependent; it carries sexual connotations and is coarse, so exercise caution when using it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話今晚請我食飯，但我懷疑佢係想打飯炮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 gam1 maan5 ceng2 ngo5 sik6 faan6, daan6 ngo5 waai4 ji4 keoi5 hai6 soeng2 daa2 faan6 paau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说今晚请我吃饭，但我怀疑他是想用吃饭为借口发生性关系。
examples.english_sentence: He said he'd treat me to dinner tonight, but I suspect he wants to use the meal as a pretext to have sex.

mandarin_meaning: 趁兴/趁着兴致做某事；一时兴起而为
english_meaning: To do something while in high spirits; to seize the moment of enthusiasm (often for a fun or impulsive action).
explanation_mandarin: 「打鼓趁兴」是粤语俗语，字面可理解为「在兴致高涨时打鼓」。引申为趁着一时的兴致或热闹气氛去做某事，通常是娱乐或冲动性动作，有时含有一时兴起的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to act while one is excited or in the mood. It suggests taking advantage of a moment of enthusiasm—often to do something fun or impulsive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚大家心情好，唔如打鼓趁兴去唱K啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 daai6 gaa1 sam1 cing4 hou2, m4 jyu4 daa2 gu2 can3 hing3 heoi3 coeng3 K laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚大家心情好，不如趁兴去唱K吧。
examples.english_sentence: Everyone's in a good mood tonight — let's seize the moment and go sing karaoke.

mandarin_meaning: 不詳（罕見粵語俗語/方言用語，含義未有可靠書面記載）
english_meaning: Unclear/rare Cantonese slang; meaning not well documented
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語/可能為動詞（不確定）
explanation_mandarin: 「打𦠹」是一個罕見或地域性較強的粵語詞彙/俗語。該字形（𦠹）屬於不常見的漢字擴展字，書面與詞義資料甚少。沒有可靠參考來源能夠準確說明其含義或讀音。若需確定含義，建議向熟悉該地區俗語的本地長者或語言學者查證。
explanation_english: “打𦠹” appears to be a rare or highly regional Cantonese slang term. The character 𦠹 is an uncommon extension character with little documented usage. There are no reliable references that clearly state its meaning or pronunciation. To determine its exact sense, consult native speakers from the relevant region or specialists in Cantonese dialects.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔識「打𦠹」呢個詞，可能係老一輩嘅俚語。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 sik1 "daa2 ??" ni1 go3 ci4, ho2 nang4 hai6 lou5 jat1 bui3 ge3 lei5 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不認識「打𦠹」這個詞，可能是老一輩的俚語。
examples.english_sentence: I don't know the term "打𦠹"; it might be an older generation's slang.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）大家都同意；連權威或所有人都答應（常用作誇張或諷刺）
english_meaning: Colloquial expression meaning everyone agrees; even the highest authority consents (often used hyperbolically or sarcastically)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面為「托塔（持塔者）都應承」，用來強調某事得到普遍同意或答應，有時帶誇張或諷刺語氣，表示「連最難說服的人也同意」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase literally meaning "even the pagoda-bearer agrees." It emphasizes unanimous acceptance or agreement (sometimes hyperbolic or sarcastic), implying that even the hardest-to-convince person has agreed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大家都話冇問題，托塔都应承晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 mou5 man6 tai4, tok3 taap3 dou1 jing3 sing4 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大家都說沒問題，連（最難說服的人）都答應了。
examples.english_sentence: Everyone says it's fine; even the hardest-to-convince person agreed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講得太離譜，邊個會咁易就托塔都应承？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 dak1 taai3 lei4 pou2, bin1 go3 wui5 gam2 ji6 zau6 tok3 taap3 dou1 jing3 sing4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說得太離譜，誰會那麼容易就答應？
examples.english_sentence: He's being ridiculous — who would agree that easily?

mandarin_meaning: 自大、得意忘形、驕傲放肆（口語、廣東話俚語）
english_meaning: to act arrogantly or overconfidently; to be cocky/presumptuous (colloquial Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 表示某人因自信或得意而做出過分自大或放肆的行為，多用於廣東話口語或俚語。
explanation_english: Indicates someone behaving overly confident or presumptuous because of pride or self-importance; a colloquial Cantonese slang term.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗一兩年就以為好叻，開始托大腳，結果被老闆鬧返。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 jat1 loeng5 nin4 zau6 ji5 wai4 hou2 lek1 hoi1 ci2 tok3 daai6 goek3 git3 gwo2 bei6 lou5 baan2 naau6 faan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做了一兩年就覺得很厲害，開始托大腳，結果被老闆責備。
examples.english_sentence: After working for a year or two he thought he was great and started acting cocky; as a result the boss scolded him.

mandarin_meaning: 托人/拜託某人幫忙
english_meaning: to ask someone to do a favor; to get someone to handle something for you
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語（俗語），表示請別人代為處理或幫忙，常見於香港非正式語境。有時帶有把事交給人、委託他人辦理的意思。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese slang used to mean asking someone to do a favor or entrusting a task to someone. Common in informal Hong Kong contexts and implies relying on another person to handle something for you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想親自去，搵阿明托𨳊佢幫手啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 can1 zi6 heoi3, wan2 aa3 ming4 tok3 zaap6 keoi5 bong1 sau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想親自去，找阿明托他幫忙吧。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to go in person; ask Ah Ming to help.

mandarin_meaning: （少見）捏、掐、夾住（用手指夾取或捏住）
english_meaning: (rare) to pinch; to clasp between the fingers; to squeeze or clamp
explanation_mandarin: 「扢」為一個較少見的漢字，在粵語口語中可用作動詞，表示用手指捏、夾或掐住某物。現代書面語中不常用，常被更常見的字如「夾」「掐」替代。
explanation_english: “扢” is a relatively rare character. In Cantonese usage it can function as a verb meaning to pinch, clamp, or hold something between the fingers. It is uncommon in modern written usage and is often replaced by more common words like "夾" or "掐."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好扢我嘅手啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ngaap1 ngo5 ge3 sau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要掐/捏我的手。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pinch my hand.

mandarin_meaning: 兩邊撈、兩面討好（從雙方獲利）
english_meaning: to play both sides / to double-dip (take advantage of both sides)
explanation_mandarin: 口語/俚語，用來形容同時從兩方撈好處或兩邊撈錢，通常帶有貶義，指人見利就向兩邊靠攏以獲取利益。
explanation_english: Colloquial slang meaning to take advantage of both sides or 'double-dip' — to profit from two parties at once. Often negative, implying opportunism or two-faced behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日執二摊，見到兩邊有利就兩邊攞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zap1 ji6 taan1, gin3 dou2 loeng5 bin1 jau5 lei6 zau6 loeng5 bin1 lo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是兩邊撈，看到哪一邊有利就從哪一邊撈好處。
examples.english_sentence: He always double-dips — whenever one side looks profitable he tries to get benefits from both.

mandarin_meaning: 被人說閒話/被人取笑、責備
english_meaning: to be gossiped about, made fun of, or criticised by others (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，指被別人說閒話、取笑或責備，帶有被動、受人評頭論足的意思。常用於日常口語中。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to be gossiped about, ridiculed, or criticised by others. It carries a passive sense of being talked about or picked on in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日遲到，畀同事執人口水溦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ci4 dou3, bei2 tung4 si6 zap1 jan4 hau2 seoi2 wai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是遲到，被同事說閒話/取笑。
examples.english_sentence: He's always late and gets gossiped about / made fun of by his colleagues.

mandarin_meaning: 抢男人的女人；介入他人感情关系的女人（贬义）
english_meaning: a woman who pursues or seduces men who are already in relationships; a man-stealer/homewrecker (pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗称，带贬义，用来形容经常追求或介入有伴侣的男人、破坏他人感情关系的女人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang, usually pejorative, for a woman who habitually pursues or seduces men who already have partners, often implying she breaks up relationships.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀人話係執仔婆，成日同有女朋友嘅男人曖昧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 waa6 hai6 zap1 zai2 po4, seng4 jat6 tung4 jau5 neoi5 pang4 jau5 ge3 naam4 jan4 oi3 mui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听说她是个小三，经常和有女朋友的男人暧昧。
examples.english_sentence: I heard she's a man-stealer; she often flirts with men who already have girlfriends.

mandarin_meaning: 當場抓到／當場逮個正著
english_meaning: to catch (someone) red-handed / to be caught in the act
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示在當場或正在做某事時被人發現或抓住，常用於描述被當場抓到做壞事或犯錯的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to be caught in the act or caught red-handed, typically used when someone is discovered doing something wrong or improper right at the scene.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個小偷喺舖頭入面偷嘢，畀店員執到正。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 siu2 tou1 hai2 pou3 tau2 jap6 min6 tau1 je5, bei2 dim3 jyun4 zap1 dou3 zeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小偷在店裡偷東西，被店員當場抓到。
examples.english_sentence: The thief stole things in the shop and was caught red-handed by the staff.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做錯嘢畀媽媽執到正，推都推唔甩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 co3 je5 bei2 maa4 maa1 zap1 dou3 zeng3, teoi1 dou1 teoi1 m4 lat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做錯事被媽媽當場抓到，想推卸也推不掉。
examples.english_sentence: He was caught in the act by his mom for doing something wrong; he couldn't shift the blame.

mandarin_meaning: 收拾行李走人；辞职或离开
english_meaning: to pack up and leave; to resign or walk away from a situation
explanation_mandarin: 口語或俚語，原指收拾包袱離開，現常用來表示辭職、離開某個地方或放棄某件事。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression literally meaning to pick up one's bundle and leave; commonly used to mean resigning, leaving a place, or giving up on something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今朝辭職，打算執包袱走人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ziu1 ci4 zik1, daa2 syun3 zaap1 baau1 fuk1 zau2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天早上辞职，打算收拾行李走人。
examples.english_sentence: He resigned this morning and plans to pack up and leave.

mandarin_meaning: 愛撿便宜、撿地上或他人遺失物品的人；形容占小便宜的人（俚語，貶義）
english_meaning: a person who picks up things from the ground or takes small advantages; a petty opportunist/scavenger (slang, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容那些喜歡撿地上東西或占小便宜、趁機獲利的人，帶有貶義。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang for someone who likes to pick up items from the ground or grab small advantages — essentially a petty opportunist or scavenger; derogatory in tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識執地仔，見到有便宜就攞，唔理啱唔啱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 zap1 dei6 zai2, gin3 dou2 jau5 bin6 ji4 zau6 lo2, m4 lei5 aam1 m4 aam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會撿小便宜，看到有便宜就拿，不管合不合理。
examples.english_sentence: He only picks up small gains — when he sees an opportunity he grabs it, not caring whether it's right.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺二手市場有啲人專執地仔，見到遺失嘅嘢就攞走。
