examples.english_sentence: What you're doing is cutting off your toe to avoid killing an insect — it's truly not worth the cost.

jyutping: dyun6 beng2 co4 tau4, mou5 zaa1 naa4
mandarin_meaning: 锄柄断了，没法拿/用；比喻没有办法、缺乏手段或无能为力
english_meaning: A hoe with a broken handle can't be wielded — literally unusable; figuratively, lacking means or ability, powerless to act
explanation_mandarin: 比喻缺乏工具、資源或能力，做不了事或無法發揮作用，常用於形容無能為力或沒有可用手段的情況。
explanation_english: Used figuratively to describe a situation where one lacks the tools, resources, or ability to do something — powerless or unable to act effectively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司想開新項目，但冇錢，真係斷柄鋤頭，冇揸拿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 soeng2 hoi1 san1 hong6 muk6, daan6 mou5 cin2, zan1 hai6 dyun6 beng2 co4 tau4, mou5 zaa1 naa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司想开展新项目，但没钱，真是断柄锄头，没办法（做）。
examples.english_sentence: The company wants to start a new project, but it has no money — it's really a hoe with a broken handle, unable to do anything.

jyutping: dyun6 sin3 saam1 jin4, mou5 dak1 daan6
mandarin_meaning: 字面：三弦断线，不能弹。引申：无可挽回、没办法、无能为力。
english_meaning: Literally 'a three-string instrument with broken strings can't be played.' Figuratively means hopeless, irreversible, or there's nothing that can be done.
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，原意指三弦断了就无法弹奏，常用来形容事情无法挽回、没有办法解决或无可奈何的处境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying: literally an instrument with broken strings cannot be played. Used to describe situations that are irreversible, hopeless, or beyond help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋交咗錯嘅合約，公司唔肯改，事情已經好麻煩，真係断线三弦，冇得弹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaau1 zo2 co3 ge3 hap6 joek3, gung1 si1 m4 hang2 goi2, si6 cing4 ji5 ging1 hou2 maa4 faan4, zan1 hai6 dyun6 sin3 saam1 jin4, mou5 dak1 daan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们签错了合同，公司不肯修改，事情已经很麻烦，真是无可挽回，没办法了。
examples.english_sentence: We signed the wrong contract and the company refuses to amend it; things are already a mess — it's hopeless, nothing can be done.

jyutping: dyun6 sin3 zi2 jiu6, mou4 hin1 mou4 gwaa3
mandarin_meaning: 像断了线的风筝/纸鸢一样，无牵无挂；形容人无拘无束、没有牵挂或束缚
english_meaning: Like a kite with a broken string — free and unencumbered; describing someone who is carefree, without ties or responsibilities
explanation_mandarin: “断线纸鹞”本为断了线的纸鸢，无法受控地飘走；引申为没有牵挂、自由自在或不受约束，有时也带有轻率、散漫的意味。
explanation_english: Literally a paper kite with a broken string that drifts away. Figuratively it describes someone who is free of ties or worries — carefree and unburdened; it can also imply being reckless or drifting without responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢辭職後到處旅行，真係断线纸鹞，無牵無挂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ci4 zik1 hau6 dou3 cyu3 leoi5 hang4, zan1 hai6 dyun6 sin3 zi2 jiu6, mou4 hin1 mou4 gwaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他辞职后到处旅行，真是断线的纸鸢，无牵无挂。
examples.english_sentence: He quit his job and travels around; he's like a kite with a broken string, without any ties or worries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做事好衝動，好似断线纸鹞，無牵無挂，成日都做啲出格嘅事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 hou2 cung1 dung6, hou2 ci5 dyun6 sin3 zi2 jiu6, mou4 hin1 mou4 gwaa3, sing4 jat6 dou1 zou6 di1 ceot1 gaak3 ge3 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很冲动，好像断线的纸鸢，无牵无挂，总是做些出格的事。
examples.english_sentence: He acts impulsively, like a kite with a broken string — carefree and irresponsible, always doing outrageous things.

mandarin_meaning: 看起來斯文的男子（常帶揶揄或貶義，指外表溫文但可能嬌弱、矯揉造作或沒用）
english_meaning: a 'refined' or 'soft' guy (Cantonese slang; often teasing or derogatory for a man who appears polite/gentle but may be seen as weak, effeminate, or pretentious)
explanation_mandarin: 「斯文崽」是香港粵語的俚語。字面上表示外表斯文、溫和的年輕男子，但語氣常帶揶揄或貶義，暗指對方可能不夠剛強、做事軟弱、矯情或假斯文；在特定語境下也可中性地形容有禮貌的人。
explanation_english: “斯文崽” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang. Literally someone who looks refined and gentle. The term is often used teasingly or derogatorily to imply the person is weak, effeminate, pretentious, or ineffectual — though in some contexts it can neutrally describe a polite, well-mannered man.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢睇落好似一個斯文崽，講嘢好溫柔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tai2 lok6 hou2 ci5 jat1 go3 si1 man4 zaai2, gong2 je5 hou2 wan1 jau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看起來像個斯文男子，說話很溫柔。
examples.english_sentence: He looks like a refined/soft guy and speaks very gently.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係因為佢係個斯文崽就以為佢唔掂，佢其實好叻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 jan1 wai6 keoi5 hai6 go3 si1 man4 zaai2 zau6 ji5 wai6 keoi5 m4 dim6, keoi5 kei4 sat6 hou2 lek1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別只是因為他是個斯文男子就以為他不行，他其實很厲害。
examples.english_sentence: Don't assume he's useless just because he's a 'soft'-looking guy — he's actually very capable.

mandarin_meaning: 新進門的嫂子／剛嫁入或剛搬入家中的媳婦
english_meaning: a new sister-in-law; a woman who has just married into or recently moved into the household (the brother's wife / daughter-in-law)
explanation_mandarin: 指剛嫁入或剛搬入家庭的嫂子（即兄長的妻子或媳婦），強調她是家庭的新成員，有時含有尚未適應新環境的意味。
explanation_english: Refers to a sister-in-law who has just married into the family or recently moved into the household (the older brother's wife/daughter-in-law). Emphasizes that she is a new member of the family and may not yet have adapted to the new environment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱有個新家嫂入咗我哋屋企，大家要好好招呼佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aam1 aam1 jau5 go3 san1 gaa1 sou2 jap6 zo2 ngo5 dei6 uk1 kei2, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 hou2 hou2 ziu1 fu6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我剛剛有個新家嫂搬進了我們家，大家要好好招待她。
examples.english_sentence: We just had a new sister-in-law move into our home; everyone should be sure to treat her well.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好同新家嫂鬧翻，佢仲未適應啲家務同人情世故。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 tung4 san1 gaa1 sou2 nau6 faan1, keoi5 zung6 mei6 sik1 jing3 di1 gaa1 mou6 tung4 jan4 cing4 sai3 gu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要和新嫂子吵架，她還沒適應家務和人情世故。
examples.english_sentence: Don't fall out with the new sister-in-law; she hasn't adjusted to the housework and family dynamics yet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做新家嫂有時幾辛苦，要學做家務、應付長輩同處理人際關係。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 san1 gaa1 sou2 jau5 si4 gei2 san1 fu2, jiu3 hok6 zou6 gaa1 mou6, jing3 fu6 zoeng2 bui6 tung4 cyu2 lei5 jan4 zai3 gwaan1 hai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 當新家嫂有時挺辛苦的，要學做家務、應付長輩並處理人際關係。
examples.english_sentence: Being a new sister-in-law can be tough; you often have to learn housework, deal with elders, and manage interpersonal relationships.

jyutping: san1 si2 haang1, saam1 jat6 hoeng1
mandarin_meaning: 新鮮感只持續很短的時間；新東西的熱度很快就過
english_meaning: A novelty that attracts attention only briefly; the initial excitement wears off quickly
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，字面意思是新的茅坑剛挖好時三天都有臭味，比喻新事物或新鮮感只會維持短暫的吸引力。
explanation_english: A colloquial saying that literally compares something new to a freshly dug latrine that 'smells' for three days — used to say that novelty or initial enthusiasm is short-lived.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲新嘢啱推出嗰陣好受歡迎，但往往都係新屎坑，三日香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 san1 je5 ngaam1 teoi1 ceot1 go2 zan6 hou2 sau6 fun1 jing4, daan6 wong5 wong5 dou1 hai6 san1 si2 haang1, saam1 jat6 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些新東西剛推出時很受歡迎，但往往只不過是新鮮感短暫。
examples.english_sentence: New things are very popular when first released, but they're often just a short-lived novelty.

mandarin_meaning: 相當於「新年快樂」或「新正如意」（粤語賀年用語）
english_meaning: A Cantonese New Year greeting meaning 'Happy New Year' or 'May the new year bring you what you wish'.
explanation_mandarin: 「新正」是廣東話的賀年口語，用於農曆新年時向人致意，通常是「新正如意」或「新年快樂」的簡略說法，屬祝賀語。
explanation_english: “新正” is a Cantonese New Year greeting used during the Lunar New Year. It is an informal abbreviation of phrases like '新正如意' and is equivalent to saying 'Happy New Year' or 'May your wishes come true.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 過年見面記得同長輩講聲「新正如意」或者簡單講「新正」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gwo3 nin4 gin3 min6 gei3 dak1 tung4 zoeng2 bui3 gong2 seng1 "san1 zing3 jyu4 ji3" waak6 ze2 gaan2 daan1 gong2 "san1 zing3".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 過年見面要跟長輩說「新正如意」或者簡稱「新正」。
examples.english_sentence: When meeting elders during Lunar New Year, say '新正如意' or simply '新正'.

mandarin_meaning: 新鲜出炉、刚刚做好或刚刚出现（常指食物或新闻）
english_meaning: freshly made / piping hot / brand-new; just out (can also mean 'hot off the press')
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，用來形容東西剛做好、剛出爐或非常新鮮且熱；亦可比喻消息或事物剛剛出現、很新很熱。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase used to describe something that is just made or released — fresh and still hot. It can also be used metaphorically for news or things that are 'hot off the press.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲蛋撻新鮮滾熱辣，啲皮好脆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 daan6 tat1 san1 sin1 gwan2 jit6 laat6, di1 pei4 hou2 ceoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些蛋挞刚出炉，外皮很酥脆。
examples.english_sentence: These egg tarts are piping hot and freshly made; the crust is very crispy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 條新聞係新鮮滾熱辣，大家都喺講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tiu4 san1 man4 hai6 san1 sin1 gwan2 jit6 laat6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hai2 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条新闻是刚发布的，大家都在讨论。
examples.english_sentence: This news item is hot off the press; everyone's talking about it.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）非常新、剛買/剛製成的
english_meaning: brand-new; fresh (just bought or just made)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語的重疊表達，用來強調某物非常新或剛買/剛弄好的狀態，相當於普通話的「全新/非常新鮮」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial reduplication used to emphasize that something is very new or just acquired/made. Equivalent to 'brand-new' or 'very fresh'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫係新𡃈𡃈，仲有張未拆嘅牌子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 hai6 san1 sin1 sin1, zung6 jau5 zoeng1 mei6 caak3 ge3 paai4 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件衣服是全新的，還有未拆的標籤。
examples.english_sentence: This shirt is brand-new; it still has the tag on.

mandarin_meaning: 方竹（竹子的一種或對某些竹類的俗稱，字面可理解為「方形的竹」）
english_meaning: a type of bamboo (literally 'square bamboo'); a local/colloquial name for certain bamboo species
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話裡，方竹通常指某些竹類的俗稱，字面意為「方形的竹」，有時用來指莖可能帶稜角或當地習慣稱呼的竹子，常用於籬笆、建材或取竹筍食用。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '方竹' commonly denotes a type of bamboo — literally 'square bamboo'. It is a local/colloquial name for certain bamboo species, sometimes referring to culms with angled cross-sections, and bamboo used for fences, construction, or edible shoots.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企後園種咗幾叢方竹，夏天涼快好多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 hau6 jyun4 zung3 zo2 gei2 cung4 fong1 zuk1, haa6 tin1 loeng4 faai3 hou2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡後院種了幾叢方竹，夏天涼快多了。
examples.english_sentence: We planted some clumps of square bamboo in the backyard; it gets much cooler in summer.

cantonese: 无了无休，立夏讲到立秋
jyutping: mou4 liu5 mou4 jau1, laap6 haa6 gong2 dou3 laap6 cau1
mandarin_meaning: 没完没了，从立夏一直说到立秋（形容说个没完、喋喋不休）
english_meaning: Endless (usually talking); to talk on and on for a very long time (literally 'from the start of summer until the start of autumn')
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人說話或事情持續不斷、沒完沒了，強調時間很長、纏綿不休。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone or something that goes on incessantly, especially talking that never seems to end — emphasizing a long, drawn-out duration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢無了無休，立夏講到立秋，聽到我頭都大埋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 mou4 liu5 mou4 jau1, laap6 haa6 gong2 dou3 laap6 cau1, teng1 dou3 ngo5 tau4 dou1 daai6 maai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他讲话没完没了，从立夏说到立秋，听得我头都大了。
examples.english_sentence: He talks endlessly, from the start of summer to the start of autumn — it's driving me crazy.

mandarin_meaning: 不计其数；非常多
english_meaning: countless; innumerable; a great many
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 数量短语 / 副词性短语
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示數量非常多，無法逐一計算，類似「成千上萬」「數不清」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to indicate a very large, uncountable number of items or instances — similar to "countless" or "a great many."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 超市入面餅乾款式無千無萬，真係揀唔切。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ciu1 si5 jap6 min6 beng2 gon1 fun2 sik1 mou4 cin1 mou4 maan6, zan1 hai6 gaan2 m4 cit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 超市裡餅乾的款式非常多，真不知道該怎麼選。
examples.english_sentence: There are countless types of cookies in the supermarket; I really can't choose.

jyutping: mou4 sing1 gau2, ngaau5 sei2 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 外表沉默但暗中会伤害或陷害别人的人（警告某人很危险、看似无害却会下毒手）
english_meaning: A person who appears quiet/unassuming but will secretly harm or betray others; a warning about someone who seems harmless but is dangerous.
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容外表沉默、低調，但暗地裡會傷人或下狠手的人；常用作警告或貶義。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who is outwardly quiet or low-key but will secretly hurt, betray, or cause trouble for others; often used as a warning or insult.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小心佢，佢係無聲狗，會咬死人嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 sam1 keoi5, keoi5 hai6 mou4 sing1 gau2, wui5 ngaau5 sei2 jan4 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小心他，他是个无声狗，会暗中伤人的。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful of him — he's a 'silent dog' who will secretly harm people.

mandarin_meaning: 没有头绪/没有领导或方向，事情难以成事
english_meaning: Unable to accomplish anything without a leader/plan; aimless or disorganized so nothing gets done
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一件事沒有頭緒、沒有主導或方向、缺乏組織，因而無法順利進行或完成。
explanation_english: Used to describe a situation that lacks a leader, direction, or coherent plan, so it cannot proceed or succeed; describes disorganized or aimless efforts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果大家都唔肯定方向，呢個計劃就无头安出脚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 hang2 ding6 fong1 hoeng3, ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 zau6 mou4 tau4 on1 ceot1 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果大家都不確定方向，這個計劃就沒有頭緒，做不成事。
examples.english_sentence: If nobody's clear about the direction, this plan will be aimless and won't get anywhere.

mandarin_meaning: 无情的人 / 冷血的人
english_meaning: a heartless person; someone cold-hearted or merciless (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，用来形容对别人冷酷、没有同情心或不留情面的人，语气可带玩笑或讽刺。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang for a person who is cold-hearted or merciless; used jokingly or sarcastically to describe someone who shows no sympathy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係無情雞，見到我有難都唔幫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 mou4 cing4 gai1, gin3 dou3 ngo5 jau5 naan6 dou1 m4 bong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個無情的人，看到我有難都不幫。
examples.english_sentence: He's such a heartless person — he didn't help me when I was in trouble.

mandarin_meaning: 随时、任何时候、一直不断
english_meaning: at any time; constantly; always
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示在任何時候、一直不間斷地發生或存在，常用於強調動作或狀態的持續性。
explanation_english: Used to indicate at any time or continuously; often emphasizes that an action or state occurs or persists without stopping.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢無時無候都掛住阿媽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou4 si4 mou4 hau6 dou1 gwaa3 zyu6 aa3 maa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他无时无刻都在想念妈妈。
examples.english_sentence: He misses his mother all the time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家啲手機，無時無候都可以聯絡到朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 di1 sau2 gei1, mou4 si4 mou4 hau6 dou1 ho2 ji5 lyun4 lok3 dou3 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在的手机让我们可以随时随地联系朋友。
examples.english_sentence: Nowadays phones let us contact friends at any time.

jyutping: mou4 zin1 mou4 sin3, san4 sin1 naan4 bin3
mandarin_meaning: 没有被褥和扇子，连神仙也难以保持不变；比喻缺乏基本生活必需或处境恶劣，连再有耐性或德行的人也难以保持冷静或原状。
english_meaning: Literally 'no blanket, no fan — even an immortal finds it hard to remain the same.' It means that without basic comforts or in very poor conditions, even the most patient or steadfast people will be affected.
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容缺乏生活必需、待遇恶劣或環境極差，會使人失去耐性或改變原本的態度與行為。
explanation_english: Used to describe situations where lack of basic necessities or very uncomfortable conditions can make people lose their patience or change their usual behavior — even those normally calm or virtuous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢排天氣咁熱，公司又冇冷氣，無氈無扇，神仙難變，啲人都頂唔順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 paai4 tin1 hei3 gam2 jit6, gung1 si1 jau6 mou5 laang5 hei3, mou4 zin1 mou4 sin3, san4 sin1 naan4 bin3, di1 jan4 dou1 ding2 m4 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近天氣這麼熱，公司又沒有冷氣，缺乏基本舒適，連再有耐心的人也難以忍受。
examples.english_sentence: It's been so hot and the office has no aircon — without basic comforts, even the most patient people can't stay calm; everyone is about to lose it.

mandarin_meaning: 电子烟／蒸汽烟（指无明火、以雾化产生气溶胶的吸烟装置）
english_meaning: Vape; electronic cigarette — a smokeless vaping device that produces aerosol rather than smoke
explanation_mandarin: 口语或俚语用法，常用于粤语圈，指无明火、以雾化方式产生可见气雾的电子烟装置。有时带戏谑或贬义。
explanation_english: Colloquial/slang term (Cantonese) for an electronic cigarette or vape — a device that creates aerosol rather than traditional smoke. Often used humorously or pejoratively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近買咗個無烟大炮，出街成日都抽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 maai5 zo2 go3 mou4 jin1 daai6 paau3, ceot1 gaai1 seng4 jat6 dou1 cau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近买了一个无烟大炮，出门经常在外面抽。
examples.english_sentence: He recently bought a vape and vapes outside all the time.

mandarin_meaning: 无缘无故惹上麻烦／无端发生的事
english_meaning: to get into unnecessary trouble; a needless or groundless incident
explanation_mandarin: 「无端白事」是粤语口语，意思是无缘无故惹上麻烦或无端发生的事。字面上“白事”原指丧事，但在口语中常被引申为不必要的事端或惹出的麻烦。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to be embroiled in trouble for no reason or an unnecessary incident. Literally 'a needless funeral matter' — '白事' originally refers to funerals but is used colloquially to mean unwanted trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想惹無端白事，遲啲再講啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 je5 mou4 dyun1 baak6 si6, ci4 di1 zoi3 gong2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想惹无端的麻烦，晚点再说吧。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to get into unnecessary trouble; let's talk later.

cantonese: 无酒三分醉，有酒十分癫
jyutping: mou4 zau2 saam1 fan1 zeoi3, jau5 zau2 sap6 fan1 din1
mandarin_meaning: 没喝酒也有点醉意，喝了酒就变得非常疯狂或失控。
english_meaning: Soberly slightly tipsy; when drinking, completely crazy — describes someone who is easily affected by alcohol and behaves erratically when drunk.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人平時就有些古怪或容易激動，沒喝酒也像醉了一樣；一旦喝酒就變得更瘋狂或失控。
explanation_english: A colloquial proverb describing a person who is already a bit unbalanced or excitable without alcohol, and becomes totally wild or out of control when they drink.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強平時都有啲古怪，真係無酒三分醉，有酒十分癲，大家飲嘢要小心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 ping4 si4 dou1 jau5 di1 gu2 gwaai3, zan1 hai6 mou4 zau2 saam1 fan1 zeoi3, jau5 zau2 sap6 fan1 din1, daai6 gaa1 jam2 je5 jiu3 siu2 sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强平时也有点古怪，真是无酒三分醉，有酒十分癫，大家喝酒要小心点。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Keung is already a bit odd — slightly tipsy even without drinking, and completely crazy when he drinks; be careful when drinking with him.

jyutping: jat6 ceot1 zou2, jyu5 lam4 nou5
mandarin_meaning: 事与愿违 / 计划赶不上变化
english_meaning: Things don't go as planned; expectations are often overturned; unlucky or unexpected setbacks.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻事情常常出乎意料，按計劃行事卻遇到突發狀況或倒霉事，表示無奈或感嘆。
explanation_english: A proverb used to say that things often turn out differently from what was planned — encountering unexpected problems or bad luck despite preparation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日特登早啲出門，點知一路塞車，又開始落雨，真係日出早，雨淋脑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 dak6 dang1 zou2 di1 ceot1 mun4, dim2 zi1 jat1 lou6 sak1 ce1, jau6 hoi1 ci2 lok6 jyu5, zan1 hai6 jat6 ceot1 zou2, jyu5 lam4 nou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天特意早出门，谁知道一路堵车，又开始下雨，真是事与愿违（或：日出早，雨淋脑）。
examples.english_sentence: I left early on purpose today, but there was traffic the whole way and then it started raining — just my luck.

cantonese: 日头唔讲人，夜晚唔讲神
jyutping: jat6 tau4 m4 gong2 jan4, je6 maan5 m4 gong2 san4
mandarin_meaning: 白天沒有人管，夜晚也沒有人顧忌神明（形容無法無天、混亂不受約束）
english_meaning: Literally: 'By day no one talks about people, by night no one talks about gods.' Idiomatically: describes a place or situation that is chaotic and lawless — no rules or restraints either day or night.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語用來形容某個地方或情況極度混亂、沒有人管束、無法無天，白天夜晚都沒有規矩可言。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb used to describe a situation or place that is extremely chaotic and unregulated — nobody enforces rules or morals either by day or by night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條街成日都好混亂，真係日头唔讲人，夜晚唔讲神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 gaai1 sing4 jat6 dou1 hou2 wan6 lyun6, zan1 hai6 jat6 tau4 m4 gong2 jan4, je6 maan5 m4 gong2 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条街一直很混乱，真是白天没人管，夜晚也不怕神明。
examples.english_sentence: This street is always chaotic; it's truly lawless both day and night.

mandarin_meaning: 日夜盼望；整天急切期待（某事发生）
english_meaning: to eagerly await something day and night; to long for something constantly
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示對某事非常期待、整天盼望，帶有急切和渴望的語氣。
explanation_english: Used to express eager, continual anticipation for something, implying impatience and strong desire.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我日望夜望佢返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat6 mong6 je6 mong6 keoi5 faan1 lei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我日夜盼望他回來。
examples.english_sentence: I've been eagerly awaiting his return day and night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 家長日望夜望學校快啲重開。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaa1 zoeng2 jat6 mong6 je6 mong6 hok6 haau6 faai3 di1 cung4 hoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家长日夜盼望學校盡快重新開放。
examples.english_sentence: Parents are eagerly awaiting the school's reopening.

cantonese: 日本味精，味之素（未知数）
jyutping: jat6 bun2 mei6 zing1, mei6 zi1 sou3 (mei6 zi1 sou3)
mandarin_meaning: 指日本產的味精（品牌味之素/Ajinomoto），同時與「未知數」諧音，是一個俚語/雙關語，用來戲稱某物或某人難以預料、效果不明或只是靠「調味」表面增色。
english_meaning: Refers to Japanese MSG (Ajinomoto); also a pun with the phrase "unknown quantity" (same pronunciation in Cantonese). Used slangily to joke that something or someone is uncertain, unpredictable, or only superficially adds "flavor".
explanation_mandarin: 此詞利用「味之素」和「未知數」在粵語的同音，既可指日本味精品牌，也可用來形容某事物或人是個未知數、效果難以預料或帶有人工增味的意味。
explanation_english: This phrase plays on the Cantonese homophone between 味之素 (Ajinomoto) and 未知數 (unknown quantity). It can literally refer to Japanese MSG but is often used jokingly to describe something/someone as an "unknown" or as artificially adding flavor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢包調味料係日本味精，味之素（未知数），唔知會唔會有副作用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 baau1 tiu4 mei6 liu6 hai6 jat6 bun2 mei6 zing1, mei6 zi1 sou3 (mei6 zi1 sou3), m4 zi1 wui5 m4 wui5 jau5 fuk6 zok3 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這包調味料是日本味精，味之素（未知數），不知道會不會有副作用。
examples.english_sentence: This packet of seasoning is Japanese MSG, Ajinomoto (unknown), not sure if it will have side effects.

cantonese: 日落有云盖，明日雨再来
jyutping: jat6 lok6 jau5 wan4 goi3, ming4 jat6 jyu5 zoi3 loi4
mandarin_meaning: 日落時若有雲遮，隔天可能會下雨（民間天氣諺語）
english_meaning: If clouds cover the sky at sunset, it often indicates rain the next day (folk weather proverb).
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句民間的天氣俗語，意思是：日落時天空若有雲，通常預示隔天會下雨。除了用來預測天氣，也可作比喻，提醒未來可能有不利情況。
explanation_english: A piece of folk weather lore meaning that cloud cover at sunset often signals rain the following day. It is used to predict weather and can also be used metaphorically to warn of trouble ahead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚日落有云盖，明日雨再来，出門記得帶把遮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jat6 lok6 jau5 wan4 goi3, ming4 jat6 jyu5 zoi3 loi4, ceot1 mun4 gei3 dak1 daai3 baa2 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚日落有云盖，明天会下雨，出门记得带把伞。
examples.english_sentence: There were clouds covering the sky at sunset tonight, so it will likely rain tomorrow—remember to bring an umbrella when you go out.

jyutping: jat6 fong4 je6 fong4, gaa1 zaak6 naan4 fong4
mandarin_meaning: 即使日夜防备，也难防范来自家里或内部的背叛或损害（家贼难防）。
english_meaning: Even with constant vigilance day and night, it's hard to guard against thieves or betrayal from within the household or organization; internal threats are the hardest to guard against.
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗语，意思是外面再怎麼防範也不如防範內部的人困難，常用來形容內部人員帶來的風險或背叛。
explanation_english: A proverb meaning that external vigilance may be effective, but it's difficult to prevent harm or betrayal from insiders — used to describe risks coming from within one's own family, group, or organization.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司入面出事，最驚係自己人作亂，真係日防夜防，家贼难防。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jap6 min6 ceot1 si6, zeoi3 ging1 hai6 zi6 gei2 jan4 zok3 lyun6, zan1 hai6 jat6 fong4 je6 fong4, gaa1 zaak6 naan4 fong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司里面出事，最怕是自己人作乱，真是日防夜防，家贼难防。
examples.english_sentence: When problems happen in the company, the worst thing is insiders causing trouble — it's really true that even if you guard day and night, internal thieves are the hardest to guard against.

mandarin_meaning: 天氣晴朗、陽光明媚（口語）
english_meaning: sunny; the sun is shining brightly (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 「日頭晟」是廣東話口語，表示白天陽光明亮、天氣晴朗，多用於描述天氣或日光充足的情況。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning the daytime is bright and sunny—used to describe clear, sunlit weather.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日日頭晟，出去散步啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 jat6 tau4 sing4, ceot1 heoi3 saan3 bou6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天天氣晴朗，出去散步吧。
examples.english_sentence: It's sunny today — let's go out for a walk.

mandarin_meaning: 最近；前陣子
english_meaning: recently; a short while ago; the other day
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示不久之前、前陣子。常見寫法為「早排」，「早牌」為同音的變體寫法，多見於非正式書寫或網絡用語。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese adverb meaning 'recently' or 'a short while ago'. Commonly written as "早排"; "早牌" is an alternative homophonic spelling used informally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我早排喺旺角見到佢，佢話換咗工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zo2 paai4 hai2 wong6 gok3 gin3 dou2 keoi5, keoi5 waa6 wun6 zo2 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我前陣子在旺角看到他，他說換了工作。
examples.english_sentence: I saw him in Mong Kok recently; he said he had changed jobs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 早排啲天氣好熱，依家就舒適啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zo2 paai4 di1 tin1 hei3 hou2 jit6, ji1 gaa1 zau6 syu1 sik1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 前陣子天氣很熱，現在就舒服一點。
examples.english_sentence: It was very hot a little while ago; now it's more comfortable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你早排點呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zo2 paai4 dim2 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你最近怎麼樣？
examples.english_sentence: How have you been lately?

cantonese: 早知灯系火，唔使盲摸摸
jyutping: zou2 zi1 dang1 hai6 fo2, m4 sai2 maang4 mo2 mo2
mandarin_meaning: 早知道（事情的真相/結果），就不用盲目摸索/白費力氣了。
english_meaning: If I had known earlier (what was really going on), I wouldn't have had to fumble around blindly or waste effort.
explanation_mandarin: 一句帶有懊悔或感嘆意味的俗語，表示如果早有資訊或早知道結果，就不用盲目行動、浪費時間或出錯。
explanation_english: A colloquial saying expressing regret or exasperation: if one had known earlier (the true situation), there would have been no need to act blindly, waste time, or make mistakes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你早啲話我知啦，早知灯系火，唔使盲摸摸等咁耐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou2 di1 gong2 ngo5 zi1 laa3, zou2 zi1 dang1 hai6 fo2, m4 sai2 maang4 mo2 mo2 dang2 gam2 noi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你早一点告诉我嘛，早知道就不用盲目等待那么久。
examples.english_sentence: You should have told me earlier — if I'd known, I wouldn't have had to wait around blindly for so long.

cantonese: 早知燈係火，唔使盲摸摸
jyutping: zou2 zi1 dang1 hai6 fo2, m4 sai2 maang4 mo2 mo2
mandarin_meaning: 要是早知道（就不用）盲目摸索／摸黑
english_meaning: If I'd known earlier, I wouldn't have had to fumble around blindly (hindsight: one wouldn't have wasted time or groped in the dark).
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，表示事後回想若早知道情況，就不用盲目摸索、浪費時間或犯錯。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying used to express that if one had known earlier, one wouldn't have had to fumble around blindly or make unnecessary mistakes — similar to 'hindsight is 20/20' or 'if only I'd known'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你早啲同我講，我就早知燈係火，唔使盲摸摸啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 zou2 di1 tung4 ngo5 gong2, ngo5 zau6 zou2 zi1 dang1 hai6 fo2, m4 sai2 maang4 mo2 mo2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你早点告诉我，我就早知道，不用盲目摸索了。
examples.english_sentence: If you'd told me earlier, I would have known and wouldn't have had to fumble around blindly.

synonyms: If only I'd known / Hindsight is 20/20

cantonese: 早禾望白撞，晚造望秋霖
jyutping: zou2 wo4 mong6 baak6 zong6, maan5 zou6 mong6 cau1 lam4
mandarin_meaning: 早種的禾作期待天氣晴好、早熟，晚種的則期待秋季降雨以利生長（農村關於播種時節和天氣希望的諺語）。
english_meaning: An agricultural proverb: early-sown crops hope for clear/dry weather and early maturation, while late-sown crops hope for autumn rains — a farmer's saying about timing and weather.
explanation_mandarin: 這句農諺反映農民依據播種時機對天氣的不同期待：早播的希望天氣適合早熟與收成，晚播的則希望秋季有雨以助生長。也引申為凡事要看時機與天時。
explanation_english: This farming proverb reflects farmers' different expectations of the weather depending on sowing time: early-sown crops need fair/dry conditions to mature early, while late-sown crops rely on autumn rains. It also implies that timing and weather (conditions) matter.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯話：「早禾望白撞，晚造望秋霖」，講緊種田要睇時令同天氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 waa6: "zou2 wo4 mong6 baak6 zong6, maan5 zou6 mong6 cau1 lam4", gong2 gan2 zung3 tin4 jiu3 tai2 si4 ling6 tung4 tin1 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿伯說：「早禾望白撞，晚造望秋霖」，在說種田要看時節和天氣。
examples.english_sentence: The old farmer said, 'Early-sown crops hope for clear weather; late-sown hope for autumn rains,' meaning farming depends on timing and the weather.

mandarin_meaning: 角落；隅；偏僻或不起眼的小地方（口語）
english_meaning: a nook/corner; a remote or out-of-the-way place; an obscure spot (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，指房間或空間裡的角落、隅或偏僻、不顯眼的小地方，也可泛指偏僻的地點。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for a corner, nook, or a small out-of-the-way/obscure place; can refer to a tucked-away or remote spot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲舊嘢堆晒喺房間嘅一個旮旯度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 gau6 je5 deoi1 saai3 hai2 fong2 gaan1 ge3 jat1 go3 gaa1 laa1 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些旧东西全堆在房间的一个旮旯里。
examples.english_sentence: The old stuff is all piled in a corner of the room.

mandarin_meaning: 角落；偏僻、隱蔽的地方
english_meaning: a nook or corner; a secluded, tucked-away spot
explanation_mandarin: 指房間或空間中的小角落，通常偏僻或不顯眼，也可泛指隱蔽的地方。
explanation_english: Refers to a small corner or nook in a room or space, often out-of-the-way or inconspicuous; can also mean any secluded spot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺櫃桶嘅旮旯角搵到一本舊相簿。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gwai6tung4 ge3 gaa1 laa1 gok3 wan2 dou3 jat1 bun2 gau6 soeng2 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在櫃子的旮旯角找到了一本舊相簿。
examples.english_sentence: I found an old photo album in a nook of the drawer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲細件嘢就擺喺屋企嘅旮旯角，唔想俾人見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 sai3 gin6 je5 zau6 baai2 hai2 uk1 kei5 ge3 gaa1 laa1 gok3, m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 gin3 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些小東西就放在家的旮旯角，不想讓人看到。
examples.english_sentence: These small items are tucked away in the corner of the house; I don't want people to see them.

cantonese: 旱天多雨色，闻雷洒几滴
jyutping: hon6 tin1 do1 jyu5 sik1, man4 leoi4 saa2 gei2 dik1
mandarin_meaning: 看起來有下雨的徵兆或有聲勢，但實際只下幾滴雨；比喻聲勢大或說得好，結果收效甚微。
english_meaning: Literally: 'In drought time it looks like rain, you hear thunder but only a few drops fall.' Used to describe great show or promises but little actual result — much noise, little effect.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容事情看似有希望或聲勢很大，但最後的成效很少或沒有實際結果。
explanation_english: Used to describe situations that appear promising or loud in rhetoric but produce very little tangible result.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋講得好有希望，但最後都係旱天多雨色，闻雷洒几滴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gong2 dou3 hou2 jau5 hei1 mong6, daan6 zeoi3 hau6 dou1 hai6 hon6 tin1 do1 jyu5 sik1, man4 leoi4 saa2 gei2 dik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们说得很有希望，但最后都只是雷声大、雨点小（旱天多雨色，闻雷洒几滴）。
examples.english_sentence: They sounded very promising, but in the end it was all show — thunder but only a few drops.

mandarin_meaning: 旱甕（比喻）
english_meaning: dry urn (figurative)
explanation_mandarin: 字面為乾燥無水的甕。常見用法為「在旱甕裡翻船」，比喻在自以為安全或沒問題的地方反而出差錯、遇到麻煩或失敗。
explanation_english: Literally a 'dry urn' or jar. Often used in the expression 'to overturn a boat in a dry urn' to mean unexpectedly getting into trouble or failing in a place where one thought they were safe.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好諗住唔會有人知道，做錯嘢好容易喺旱甕裡翻船。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lam2 zyu6 m4 wui5 jau5 jan4 zi1 dou3, zou6 co3 je5 hou2 jung6 ji6 hai2 hon6 wong6 leoi5 faan1 syun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要以為不會有人知道，做錯事很容易在自以為安全的地方出事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't assume no one will find out — making a mistake can easily get you into trouble where you thought you were safe.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語俚語）長期沒有性行為的人；常用以形容長期單身或缺乏性生活
english_meaning: Cantonese slang for someone who has gone a long time without sexual activity; chronically single or sexless (often used jokingly or derisively)
explanation_mandarin: 「旱芹」是廣東話俚語，字面上帶「乾、缺乏」的意思，用來指長時間沒有性經驗或性生活匱乏的人，常帶戲謔或嘲諷意味。
explanation_english: “旱芹” is a Cantonese slang term literally evoking dryness; it describes a person who has gone a long time without sexual experience or an active sex life. It is often used teasingly or mockingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講自己係旱芹，唔敢追女仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 zi6 gei2 hai6 hon4 kan4, m4 gam2 zeoi1 neoi5 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是说自己是旱芹，不敢追女生。
examples.english_sentence: He always says he's 'dry celery' and doesn't dare to pursue girls.

mandarin_meaning: 旱蕹（旱地栽培的蕹菜），即空心菜的一種或稱蕹菜
english_meaning: Land-grown water spinach (a type of water spinach/kangkong, also called morning glory)
explanation_mandarin: 旱蕹指的是蕹菜（又稱空心菜）在較乾燥或旱地栽培的變種或稱呼，常作蔬菜烹調使用。
explanation_english: ‘旱蕹’ refers to water spinach (kangkong/morning glory) grown on drier land; it is a vegetable commonly used in cooking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚食旱蕹炒蒜蓉啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 sik6 hon3 wing6 caau2 syun3 jung4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚吃蒜蓉炒旱蕹。
examples.english_sentence: We're having stir-fried land-grown water spinach with garlic tonight.

jyutping: si4 bat1 si4 (commonly si4 m4 si4)
mandarin_meaning: 不时；偶尔，时常发生但有间歇
english_meaning: from time to time; occasionally; now and then
explanation_mandarin: 表示某种行为或情况间歇性、偶尔发生，而非持续不断。粤语口语中更常用写法/说法为「時唔時」。
explanation_english: Indicates that something happens intermittently or occasionally rather than continuously. In Cantonese speech the common colloquial form is '時唔時' (si4 m4 si4).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢時唔時都打電話俾我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 si4 m4 si4 dou1 daa2 din6 waa6 bei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他时不时给我打电话。
examples.english_sentence: He calls me from time to time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近天氣唔穩定，時唔時落雨，要記得帶傘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 tin1 hei3 m4 wan5 ding6, si4 m4 si4 lok6 jyu5, jiu3 gei3 dak1 daai3 saan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近天气不稳定，时不时下雨，要记得带伞。
examples.english_sentence: The weather's unstable recently; it rains now and then, so remember to bring an umbrella.

mandarin_meaning: 时辰八字 / 生辰八字（用于算命，指出生的年、月、日、时所对应的干支）
english_meaning: birth time and 'eight characters' (the Four Pillars of Destiny used in Chinese astrology; the year, month, day and hour in sexagenary cycle); used for fortune-telling or to indicate exact birth time/details
explanation_mandarin: 「时辰八字」指根據中國傳統紀年法，用出生的年、月、日、時換算出的八個天干地支，常用於算命、擇日等，也可泛指具體的時間資料。
explanation_english: Refers to the 'eight characters' (the Four Pillars: year, month, day, hour in the sexagenary cycle) determined from a person's birth date and time; commonly used in fortune-telling, selecting auspicious dates, or more generally to mean specific timing details.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要唔要畀你嘅時辰八字畀師傅睇下？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 m4 jiu3 bei2 nei5 ge3 si4 san4 baat3 zi6 bei2 si1 fu1 tai2 haa5？
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要不要把你的时辰八字给师傅看看？
examples.english_sentence: Do you want to give your birth time/eight characters to the fortune-teller to have a look?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋結婚要拎埋時辰八字去擇日子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 git3 fan1 jiu3 ling1 maai4 si4 san4 baat3 zi6 heoi3 zaak6 jat6 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们结婚要把时辰八字拿去择日子。
examples.english_sentence: For our wedding we need to bring the birth times/eight characters to choose an auspicious date.

mandarin_meaning: 擺架子、裝腔作勢，顯得自以為是或傲慢
english_meaning: to put on airs; to act arrogant or pretentious
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，形容人在別人面前故意擺出高人一等或裝腔作勢的態度，帶有貶義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term used to describe someone who puts on airs or acts arrogantly/pretentiously in front of others; carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺人面前昂勾，令人好唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 jan4 min6 cin4 ngong4 gou1, ling6 jan4 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在別人面前擺架子，讓人很不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: He always puts on airs in front of others, which makes people uncomfortable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺度昂勾，大家傾下計就好啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 ngong4 gou1, daai6 gaa1 king1 haa5 gai2 zau6 hou2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要在這裡裝腔作勢，大家聊聊就好了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't act arrogant here; just chat together.

mandarin_meaning: 明目张胆；公然、厚颜无耻地在别人面前做某事
english_meaning: to do something brazenly or openly (right in front of others); blatant and shameless
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，形容在別人面前公然、明目張膽地做某些通常帶有負面含義的行為，含有囂張或厚顏無恥的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing doing something openly and shamelessly in front of others. It usually carries a negative connotation — brazen, blatant, or audacious behavior.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺我面前明剃眼眉偷嘢，都唔驚畀我見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ngo5 min6 cin4 ming4 tai3 ngaan5 mei4 tau1 je5, dou1 m4 geng1 bei2 ngo5 gin3 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他明目张胆在我面前偷东西，根本不怕被我看到。
examples.english_sentence: He brazenly stole something right in front of me, not afraid of being seen.

mandarin_meaning: 公開陷害／當眾陷害
english_meaning: to publicly frame (someone); to set someone up openly
explanation_mandarin: 「明框」是香港粵語的俗語，指公開或明目張膽地陷害、陷住某人，使其遭受指控或不利後果。通常帶有被動用法：被人明框（被公開陷害）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used in Hong Kong meaning to openly or blatantly frame someone. It often appears in passive constructions (to be publicly framed).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話有人要明框佢，佢好驚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 jau5 jan4 jiu3 ming4 kwaang1 keoi5, keoi5 hou2 geng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說有人要公開陷害他，他很害怕。
examples.english_sentence: He said someone wants to publicly frame him; he's very afraid.

mandarin_meaning: 头昏、精神不振、感到昏沉或迷糊
english_meaning: dazed; groggy; lethargic; feeling faint or stupefied
explanation_mandarin: 表示因疲倦、病痛、天氣或其他原因而感到頭腦不清醒、無精神或昏沉迷糊的狀態。
explanation_english: Describes a state of feeling mentally unclear, sluggish, or faint — often due to fatigue, illness, heat, or other causes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日成日覺得昏頓，唔想做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 seng4 jat6 gok3 dak1 fan1 deon6, m4 soeng2 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天一直觉得头昏脑胀，不想做事。
examples.english_sentence: I've been feeling groggy all day and don't feel like doing anything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 暑熱令佢覺得昏頓，要即刻補水同休息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: syu3 jit6 ling6 keoi5 gok3 dak1 fan1 deon6, jiu3 zik1 haak1 bou2 seoi2 tung4 jau1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 炎热让他感到头昏，要马上补水和休息。
examples.english_sentence: The heat made him feel dizzy and groggy; he needed to hydrate and rest immediately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我睇電腦睇耐咗，成個人好昏頓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tai2 din6 nou5 tai2 noi6 zo2, seng4 go3 jan4 hou2 fan1 deon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我看电脑看久了，整个人很昏沉。
examples.english_sentence: After looking at the computer for a long time, I feel very groggy.

mandarin_meaning: 轻易地把……说成/视为……
english_meaning: to readily/easily label or regard (someone/something) as ...
explanation_mandarin: 表示不经过充分了解就轻易把某人或某事称作某种身份或性质（常带贬义或草率判断）。
explanation_english: Indicates calling or considering someone/something as a particular identity or quality too easily or without sufficient evidence (often a hasty or negative judgment).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 社交媒體上好多人會易话为罪犯，但證據未完備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: se5 gaau1 mui4 tai2 seong6 hou2 do1 jan4 wui5 ji6 waa6 wai4 zeoi6 faan6, daan6 zing3 geoi3 mei6 jyun4 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在社交媒体上很多人会轻易就把别人说成罪犯，但证据不充分。
examples.english_sentence: On social media many people readily call others criminals, but the evidence isn't sufficient.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁易易话为失敗，試埋先知結果。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 ji6 ji6 waa6 wai4 sat1 baai6, si3 maai4 sin1 zi1 git3 gwo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要这么轻易就说是失败，先尝试了才知道结果。
examples.english_sentence: Don't so easily declare it a failure; try it first to know the outcome.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都會易话为我哋唔識做事，其實佢自己都有問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 dou1 wui5 ji6 waa6 wai4 ngo5 dei6 m4 sik1 zou6 si6, kei4 sat6 keoi5 zi6 gei2 dou1 jau5 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常轻易就说我们不懂做事，其实他自己也有问题。
examples.english_sentence: He often too readily says we don't know how to do things, but actually he himself has problems too.

mandarin_meaning: 很容易；輕而易舉（像借火一樣簡單）
english_meaning: very easy; a piece of cake
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語/口語（副詞短語，表示程度）
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用來形容某件事非常容易完成，類似「小菜一碟」或「易如反掌」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning something is very easy to do, similar to "a piece of cake" or "easy as pie."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次考試其實易過借火，你唔使咁緊張。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1-ci3 haau2-si3 kei4-sat6 ji6-gwo3 ze3-fo2, nei5 m4-sai2 gam2 gan2-zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次考试其实很容易，你不用那么紧张。
examples.english_sentence: This exam is actually very easy; you don't need to be so nervous.

mandarin_meaning: 比喻非常容易，輕而易舉
english_meaning: extremely easy; a piece of cake
explanation_mandarin: 「易過食生菜」是香港粵語口語俗語，用來形容某事非常容易，幾乎不用費勁就能完成。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquialism used to describe something that is extremely easy to do, almost effortless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份工作對佢嚟講易過食生菜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gung1 zok3 deoi3 keoi5 lai4 gong2 ji6 gwo3 sik6 saang1 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份工作對他來說非常容易。
examples.english_sentence: This job is extremely easy for him.

mandarin_meaning: （網絡口語，非標準）可能用來問「美國現在是星期幾？」或戲謔指「星期的美味點心/週末好東西」。
english_meaning: An informal/net-slang phrase. Often used to ask "what day of the week is it in the US?" (with 美 short for 美國), or jokingly to mean "week's tasty treats/pleasant weekend things."
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語 / 網絡用語（片語）
explanation_mandarin: 「星期美点」不是標準詞彙，屬於網絡俗語或玩笑說法。當「美」作為「美國」的簡稱時，可用來問美國當地的星期幾（即時區差異相關）；另一種較少見的創意用法是把「美點」（美味點心、好東西）與「星期」結合，表示週內或週末的美好事物。具體含義需視語境判斷。
explanation_english: “星期美点” is not a standard lexical item but an informal internet/slang expression. If 美 is short for 美國 (the U.S.), it can be used to ask what day of the week it is in the United States (time-zone context). Alternatively, as a playful coinage it can combine “星期” (week) with “美點” (tasty treats/good things) to refer to pleasant weekend treats or highlights. Meaning depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺帖文問「星期美點？」好似想知而家美國係星期幾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 tip3 man4 man6 "sing1 kei4 mei5 dim2?" hou2 ci5 soeng2 zi1 ji4 gaa1 mei5 gwok3 hai6 sing1 kei4 gei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在帖子裡問「星期美点？」，好像想知道美國現在是星期幾。
examples.english_sentence: He asked "星期美点?" in the post, which seems to be asking what day of the week it is right now in the United States.

mandarin_meaning: 惹眼 / 醒目（有時也指刺眼）
english_meaning: eye-catching; striking; (sometimes) glaring
explanation_mandarin: 表示某物或某人很吸引人注目、很醒目；在描述光線時也可表示刺眼、令人不舒服的亮光。
explanation_english: Describes something or someone that attracts visual attention (eye-catching, striking). In contexts about light it can mean glaring or harsh on the eyes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢件衫好映眼，好多人望住佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin6 saam1 hou2 jing3 ngaan5, hou2 do1 jan4 mong6 zyu6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的衣服很惹眼，很多人在看着他。
examples.english_sentence: His clothes are very eye-catching; many people are looking at him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢盞燈好映眼，我戴埋太陽眼鏡先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zaan2 dang1 hou2 jing3 ngaan5, ngo5 daai3 maai4 taai3 joeng4 ngaan5 geng2 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这盏灯很刺眼，我得戴上太阳镜才行。
examples.english_sentence: This lamp is very glaring; I need to put on sunglasses.

mandarin_meaning: 放映電影／播映電影
english_meaning: to screen/show a movie
explanation_mandarin: 表示在戲院、電視台或其他場所放映、播映電影。屬於動詞短語，可指正式上映或重播。
explanation_english: Means to screen or show a movie (in a cinema, on TV, etc.). A verb phrase referring to projecting or broadcasting a film.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 間戲院今晚會映電影，幾點開場？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaan1 hei3 jyun2 gam1 maan5 wui5 jing3 din6 jing2, gei2 dim2 hoi1 coeng4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那家電影院今晚會放映電影，幾點開場？
examples.english_sentence: The cinema will screen a movie tonight; what time does it start?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 電視台今晚會映電影，重溫經典老片。
examples.jyutping_sentence: din6 si6 toi4 gam1 maan5 wui5 jing3 din6 jing2 cung4 wan1 ging1 din2 lou5 pin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 電視台今晚會播映經典老片。
examples.english_sentence: The TV station will air a classic movie tonight.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）發春、性慾高漲或變得好色
english_meaning: slang for becoming sexually aroused; to be horny or act lecherously
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，用以形容產生性慾或變得好色、想追求異性。有時書寫時會見到變體字「膥」。常與「發」連用為「發春」。
explanation_english: A slang verb describing becoming sexually aroused or acting lecherously. Sometimes written with the variant character "膥". Often used as "發春" (to get horny).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家發春，行街成日望女仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 faat3 ceon1, haang4 gaai1 sing4 jat6 mong6 neoi5 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在發春，逛街時總是盯著女生看。
examples.english_sentence: He's horny right now; always staring at girls while out shopping.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好發春，尊重啲人啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 faat3 ceon1, zyun1 zung6 di1 jan4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要發春，要尊重一點人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't get horny—show some respect.

mandarin_meaning: 阴囊（俗称，男性外生殖器的一部分）
english_meaning: scrotum; (slang) balls/testicles (vulgar)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語粗俗俚語，指男性外生殖器的陰囊（俗稱“蛋蛋”或“睾丸”），常見於口語、玩笑或罵人時使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar slang term referring to the male scrotum (colloquially 'balls' or 'testicles'). Commonly used in spoken language, jokes, or coarse language.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小心啲，唔好畀人踢到春袋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 sam1 di1, m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 tek3 dou3 ceon1 doi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小心点，别让人踢到你的阴囊。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful, don't let anyone kick your scrotum.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 踢波嘅時候佢比人撞到春袋，好痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tek3 bo1 ge3 si4 hau6 keoi5 bei2 jan4 zong6 dou3 ceon1 doi6, hou2 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 踢球的时候他被人撞到阴囊，很痛。
examples.english_sentence: While playing football he got his scrotum hit and it hurt a lot.

cantonese: 春分日日暖，秋分夜夜寒
jyutping: ceon1 fan1 jat6 jat6 nyun5, cau1 fan1 je6 je6 hon4
mandarin_meaning: 春分過後白天日益變暖，秋分過後夜晚逐漸變冷
english_meaning: After the spring equinox it becomes warmer day by day; after the autumn equinox nights become colder night by night.
explanation_mandarin: 一句描述季節變化的俗語，指出春分之後白天天氣會逐日回暖，而秋分之後夜晚會逐夜轉冷。可用於字面上的天氣觀察，也可比喻事物隨時間逐漸改變。
explanation_english: A proverb describing seasonal shifts: after the spring equinox days warm up day by day, and after the autumn equinox nights cool down night by night. It can be used literally for weather or figuratively to note gradual change over time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 春分日日暖，秋分夜夜寒，所以朝早同夜晚出門要記得帶件外套。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceon1 fan1 jat6 jat6 nyun5, cau1 fan1 je6 je6 hon4, so2 ji5 ziu1 zou2 tung4 je6 maan5 ceot1 mun4 jiu3 gei3 dak1 daai3 gin6 ngoi6 tou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 春分日日暖，秋分夜夜寒，所以早晚出門要記得帶外套。
examples.english_sentence: After the spring equinox it gets warmer day by day and after the autumn equinox nights get colder, so remember to bring a jacket when going out in the morning or evening.

jyutping: ceon1 fan1 gwaa1, cing1 ming4 maa4
mandarin_meaning: 春分長瓜、清明長麻（關於節氣與作物生長的諺語）
english_meaning: A proverb: "At the Spring Equinox melons, at Qingming hemp" — refers to crops growing according to seasonal solar terms; used to say things should follow their natural timing.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語俗語，字面意思為「春分長瓜、清明長麻」，來源於農業對節氣與作物生長的觀察。用來說明事物有其時令與規律，提醒人們做事要順應天時，不可操之過急。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb referring to solar terms and crop growth. Literally "spring equinox (brings) melons; Qingming (brings) hemp." It reflects agricultural observations that crops grow at certain seasonal times and is used figuratively to advise that things have their proper timing and should not be rushed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯成日講：「春分瓜，清明麻」，佢想話農時重要，做嘢要順應時令。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 sing4 jat6 gong2: "ceon1 fan1 gwaa1, cing1 ming4 maa4", keoi5 soeng2 waa6 nung4 si4 zung6 jiu3, zou6 je5 jiu3 seon6 jing3 si4 ling6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 伯父常說：「春分長瓜、清明長麻」，意思是提醒農時重要，要順應時令。
examples.english_sentence: My uncle often says, "At the Spring Equinox melons, at Qingming hemp," meaning agricultural work follows the seasons and you should go along with the natural timing.

mandarin_meaning: （通常為日本女性名字）春的孩子；人名「春子」
english_meaning: A Japanese female given name meaning "child of spring" (Haruko). Not a common Cantonese lexical item.
explanation_mandarin: 「春子」多用作日本女性的名字，字面可解作「春天的孩子」。在粵語中這個組合通常只是人名，並非常見口語詞彙或俚語。
explanation_english: "春子" is commonly used as a Japanese feminine given name (Haruko), literally "child of spring." In Cantonese contexts it is generally treated as a personal name rather than a native Cantonese word or slang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 春子係我朋友，佢今日嚟咗我屋企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceon1 zi2 hai6 ngo5 pang4 jau5, keoi5 gam1 jat6 lai4 zo2 ngo5 uk1 kei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 春子是我的朋友，她今天來我家了。
examples.english_sentence: Haruko is my friend; she came to my house today.

cantonese: 春早迟耕种，春迟早早耕
jyutping: ceon1 zou2 ci4 gang1 zung3, ceon1 ci4 zou2 zou2 gang1
mandarin_meaning: 春天来得早就晚些耕种；春天来得晚就要早些耕种。意思是根据春季的早晚变化来调整耕作时间，强调随时机而变、灵活应对。
english_meaning: If spring arrives early, postpone planting; if spring arrives late, plant early. Advises adjusting planting times based on the arrival of spring — be flexible and adapt to seasonal timing.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語來自農事經驗，提醒人們要根據季節與天氣的變化靈活安排耕作時間；引申為遇事要因時制宜、隨機應變。
explanation_english: This proverb originates from farming experience: it reminds people to adjust cultivation timing according to seasonal/weather changes. By extension, it means to act according to the situation and be adaptable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯話：「春早迟耕种，春迟早早耕，要睇天氣安排。」
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 waa6: "ceon1 zou2 ci4 gang1 zung3, ceon1 ci4 zou2 zou2 gang1, jiu3 tai2 tin1 hei3 on1 paai4."
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老人說：「春天來得早就晚些耕種，春天來得晚就要早點耕種，要看天氣來安排。」
examples.english_sentence: Grandpa said, "If spring comes early, delay sowing; if spring comes late, sow early — arrange it according to the weather."

jyutping: ceon1 mou6 cing4, cau1 mou6 jyu5
mandarin_meaning: 春天有雾通常会放晴，秋天有雾通常会下雨；一句民间谚语。
english_meaning: A proverb saying that spring fog usually clears while autumn fog often leads to rain; used literally for weather prediction and metaphorically to say the same sign can mean different things at different times.
explanation_mandarin: 一句根据季节判断雾与天气变化的民间谚语：春季出现雾多转晴，秋季出现雾多转雨。引申为同一征兆在不同时间可能有不同的结果或含义。
explanation_english: A folk proverb based on seasonal weather patterns: fog in spring tends to clear, while fog in autumn often brings rain. Figuratively, it warns that the same sign can have different meanings or outcomes depending on the timing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老人家成日講：春雾晴，秋雾雨，見到霧應該留意係邊個季節。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jan4 gaa1 sing4 jat6 gong2: ceon1 mou6 cing4, cau1 mou6 jyu5, gin3 dou3 mou6 jing1 goi1 lau4 ji3 hai6 bin1 go3 gwai3 zit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老人家常说：春雾晴，秋雾雨，看到雾应该注意是哪个季节。
examples.english_sentence: Old people often say, 'Spring fog clears, autumn fog brings rain.' When you see fog you should pay attention to which season it is.

jyutping: ceon1 bin1 cau1 lei5 haa6 saam1 lei4
mandarin_meaning: 春季鳊鱼、秋季鲤鱼、夏季三黧（古代俗稱），列舉各季節盛產的魚；泛指物產或食物隨季節更替，各有時令。
english_meaning: Literally 'spring bian, autumn carp, summer san-li' — an old saying listing fish abundant in different seasons; generally means produce or food changes with the seasons and each season has its specialties.
explanation_mandarin: 一句舊時俗語，列舉不同季節常見或盛產的魚類，常用來說明物產、飲食或事物會隨季節變化，各有時令。
explanation_english: An old folk saying that lists fish commonly abundant in different seasons. It is used to point out that produce, food, or other things vary with the seasons and each season has its own specialties.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老漁夫話：春鳊秋鲤夏三黧，各有時令，唔使驚冇嘢食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jyu4 fu1 waa6: ceon1 bin1 cau1 lei5 haa6 saam1 lei4, gok3 jau5 si4 ling6, m4 sai2 ging1 mou5 je5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老渔夫说：春鳊秋鲤夏三黧，各有时令，不用担心没有吃的。
examples.english_sentence: The old fisherman said, 'spring bian, autumn carp, summer san-li' — each season has its specialties, so don't worry about lacking food.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見片語（來源不詳）；字面可譯為「昧着水的春牆」，可能比喻裝作不知或掩飾真相
english_meaning: A rare/obscure phrase (origin unclear); literally "obscure/hidden water spring wall" — possibly used figuratively to mean feigning ignorance or covering up the truth
explanation_mandarin: 「昧水春墙」並非廣泛使用的粵語俗語或成語，來源與典故不詳。根據字面拆解可作為比喻性說法，用來形容有人故意裝作不知道、掩飾事實或含混其詞。由於使用極少，應用時需註明為罕見或古舊用法。
explanation_english: "昧水春墙" is not a widely used Cantonese idiom; its origin is unclear. Based on the literal characters it can be interpreted metaphorically to describe someone feigning ignorance, hiding the truth, or being evasive. The phrase is very rare, so note its obscure/archaic character when using it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再昧水春墙，快啲承認啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi6 mui6 seoi2 ceon1 coeng4, faai3 di1 sing4 jing6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再裝作不知，快点承认吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pretend not to know anymore; admit it quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 随便闲聊的讨论区/聊天频道；随意、不认真
english_meaning: an off‑topic/casual chat area or platform; also describes a casual, don't‑care attitude
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話俚語，通常指網絡社群或群組中用來隨便閒聊、討論雜七雜八話題的版塊或頻道；也可用來形容談話或態度很隨便、不認真。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term typically referring to an off‑topic section or channel in an online group where people casually chat about anything; it can also describe a casual or unserious manner of speaking or attitude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個群入面有個是但台，大家喺度亂吹水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 kwan4 jap6 min6 jau5 go3 si6 daan6 toi4, daai6 gaa1 hai2 dou6 lyun6 ceoi1 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个群里面有一个“是但台”，大家在这里随便闲聊。
examples.english_sentence: This group has an 'is-daan-toi' (off‑topic) channel where people just casually chat.

cantonese: 是非成日有，唔听自然无
jyutping: si6 fei1 sing4 jat6 jau5, m4 teng1 zi6 jin4 mou4
mandarin_meaning: 是非每天都有，不去聽（別人的閒言閒語）自然就不會受到影響。
english_meaning: There will always be criticism and gossip; if you don't listen, they won't affect you.
explanation_mandarin: 用來勸人不要被是非或閒言閒語困擾，只要不去聽或理會，這些事就不會影響自己。
explanation_english: Used to advise someone not to be bothered by disputes or gossip — since such things are inevitable, ignoring them prevents them from affecting you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好理嗰啲閒言閒語，是非成日有，唔听自然无。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lei5 go2 di1 haan4 jin4 haan4 jyu5, si6 fei1 sing4 jat6 jau5, m4 teng1 zi6 jin4 mou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別理那些閒言閒語，是非天天都有，不聽自然就不會有影響。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pay attention to that gossip — disputes happen all the time; if you don't listen, they won't affect you.

mandarin_meaning: 时事文章；时评
english_meaning: current affairs article; topical commentary; opinion piece
explanation_mandarin: 指關於時事的文章或評論，通常出現在報章或專欄，討論當下的政治、社會或經濟議題。
explanation_english: Refers to an article or commentary about current affairs, typically appearing in newspapers or opinion columns, discussing contemporary political, social, or economic issues.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺報紙寫咗一篇時文，批評政府嘅政策。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 bou3 zi2 se2 zo2 jat1 pin1 si4 man4, pai1 ping4 zing3 fu2 ge3 zing3 caak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在报纸上写了一篇时事评论，批评政府的政策。
examples.english_sentence: He wrote a current affairs article in the newspaper criticizing the government's policy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今期嘅時文主題係房屋問題，講咗唔少數據同建議。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 kei4 ge3 si4 man4 zyu2 tai4 hai6 fong4 nguk1 man6 tai4, gong2 zo2 m4 siu2 sou3 geoi3 tung4 gin3 ji5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 本期的时文专题是住房问题，提到了不少数据和建议。
examples.english_sentence: This issue's topical article focuses on housing problems and mentions many data and recommendations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大家都應該多讀時文，咁先可以了解時事嘅來龍去脈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 gaa1 dou1 jing1 goi1 do1 duk6 si4 man4, gam2 sin1 ho2 ji5 liu5 gaai2 si4 si6 ge3 loi4 lung4 heoi3 mak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大家都应该多读时文，才能了解时事的来龙去脉。
examples.english_sentence: Everyone should read more topical articles so they can understand the background and context of current affairs.

mandarin_meaning: 間歇性症狀；偶發性的病徵或不適
english_meaning: intermittent symptom; a symptom or ailment that appears occasionally or periodically
explanation_mandarin: 「時症」常用來形容偶爾出現、不穩定或間歇發作的病徵或不適，強調不是持續性的病情，可能會時好時壞。
explanation_english: "時症" refers to symptoms or ailments that occur intermittently or occasionally rather than continuously. It emphasizes periodic or sporadic episodes of discomfort or signs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近成日有啲時症，頭暈同手震時有時無，應該去睇吓醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 sing4 jat6 jau5 di1 si4 zing3, tau4 wan4 tung4 sau2 zan3 si4 jau5 si4 mou5, jing1 goi1 heoi3 tai2 haa5 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近經常有些間歇性症狀，頭暈和手抖時有時沒有，應該去看看醫生。
examples.english_sentence: Lately he has been having intermittent symptoms — sometimes dizziness and hand tremors — he should see a doctor.

mandarin_meaning: 時不時愛找碴／愛挑起爭端（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: prone to pick fights or make trouble from time to time (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「時離吵拿」是粵語口語俚語，用來形容某人時常或偶爾愛找麻煩、愛挑起爭端或愛跟人爭吵。詞源非正式，常見於口語對話中。
explanation_english: “時離吵拿” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe someone who, from time to time, likes to cause trouble or pick fights. It’s informal and mainly used in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢時離吵拿，成日同人發生衝突，大家都好頭痕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 si4 lei4 caau2 naa4, sing4 jat6 tung4 jan4 faat3 saang1 cung1 dat6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hou2 tau4 hon4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他時不時愛找碴，經常和人發生衝突，大家都很頭痛。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is prone to picking fights from time to time and often gets into conflicts with others; everyone finds it frustrating.

cantonese: 晚来西北黑半天，纵唔落雨有风缠
jyutping: maan5 loi4 sai1 bak1 hak1 bun3 tin1 zung6 m4 lok6 jyu5 jau5 fung1 cin4
mandarin_meaning: 傍晚時分西北方向天色陰暗，雖然不一定下雨，但會刮風。
english_meaning: When the northwest sky darkens in the evening, even if it doesn't rain there will be persistent wind.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語民間諺語，用來根據天象預測天氣：傍晚西北方天色變暗，通常代表有冷鋒或風會來，雖然不一定會下雨，但容易刮風。
explanation_english: A Cantonese weather proverb used to predict conditions from the sky: if the northwest sky darkens in the evening, it often signals an approaching front or windy weather — even if it doesn't rain, wind is likely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老一輩成日講：晚來西北黑半天，縱唔落雨有風纏，出門記得帶外套。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jat1 bui3 sing4 jat6 gong2 maan5 loi4 sai1 bak1 hak1 bun3 tin1 zung6 m4 lok6 jyu5 jau5 fung1 cin4 ceot1 mun4 gei3 dak1 daai3 ngoi6 tou3
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老一輩常說：晚來西北黑半天，縱不下雨有風纏，出門記得帶外套。
examples.english_sentence: The older generation often says, 'When the northwest darkens in the evening, even if it doesn't rain there will be wind' — remember to take a jacket when going out.

cantonese: 晚霞行千里，西北火烧天
jyutping: maan5 haa4 hang4 cin1 lei5, sai1 bak1 fo2 siu1 tin1
mandarin_meaning: 晚霞蔓延千里，西北方向的天空被夕陽染成火紅。這句俗語描述壯麗的晚霞，傳統上常被用作觀天象的經驗談，晚霞通常被視為好天氣或適合遠行的徵兆。
english_meaning: The sunset glow stretches for miles and the northwest sky is burning red. This proverb describes a spectacular red sunset; in folk weather lore a red evening sky is often taken as a sign of fine weather and good conditions for travel.
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語俗語，形容晚霞非常壯觀並延伸很遠。民間氣象觀察認為晚霞一般預示天氣良好、適合出行；有時亦用作比喻前景廣闊或形勢顯眼。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folk saying describing a spectacular sunset that stretches far and lights the northwest sky red. Traditionally used in weather lore to indicate fair weather and suitability for travel; it can also be used figuratively to suggest a bright or far-reaching prospect.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日傍晚見到晚霞行千里，西北火燒天，聽日應該唔會落雨，可以去行山。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 bong6 maan5 gin3 dou2 maan5 haa4 hang4 cin1 lei5, sai1 bak1 fo2 siu1 tin1, ting1 jat6 jing1 goi1 m4 wui5 lok6 jyu5, ho2 ji5 heoi3 haang4 saan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天傍晚看到晚霞行千里，西北火烧天，明天應該不會下雨，可以去爬山。
examples.english_sentence: This evening I saw the sunset spread for miles and the northwest sky burning red; it probably won't rain tomorrow, so we can go hiking.

synonyms: 朝霞不出門，晚霞行千里

mandarin_meaning: 不是常見詞語；按字面可解作顏色暗沉或變質的肉，亦可能是書寫錯誤（如想寫「肥肉」）
english_meaning: Not an attested/common Cantonese word; literally could mean dark/decayed meat or be a typo (e.g. intended '肥肉', fatty meat)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（若按字面指肉類）／非標準用法
partOfSpeech_english: noun (if interpreted as referring to meat) / non-standard
explanation_mandarin: 「晦肉」在粵語中不是常見或標準的詞彙。按字面分析，『晦』有陰暗、黯淡之義，因此可臆測指顏色變暗或已變質的肉；另一種可能是書寫或聽寫錯誤，原意為「肥肉」等。使用時應注意該詞並非通行用法。
explanation_english: “晦肉” is not a commonly attested Cantonese term. Literally, 晦 means dim/dark, so it could be interpreted as meat that has darkened or gone bad; alternatively it may be a written/heard mistake for words like “肥肉” (fatty meat). It is non-standard, so use with caution.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「晦肉」唔係廣泛使用嘅粵語詞，通常唔會咁講。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 「wui6 juk6」 m4 hai6 gwong2 faan3 si6 jung6 ge3 jyut6 jyu5 ci4, tung1 soeng4 m4 wui5 gam2 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: “晦肉”不是广泛使用的粤语词，通常不会这样说。
examples.english_sentence: "晦肉" is not a widely used Cantonese word; people normally wouldn't say it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果係筆誤，可能想寫「肥肉」或者指變質嘅肉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 hai6 bat1 ng6, ho2 nang4 soeng2 se2 「fei4 juk6」 waak6 ze2 zi2 bin3 zat1 ge3 juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果是笔误，可能想写“肥肉”或者指变质的肉。
examples.english_sentence: If it's a typo, it may have intended “肥肉” (fatty meat) or refer to spoiled/altered meat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰塊晦肉有異味，唔好食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 faai3 wui6 juk6 jau5 ji6 mei6, m4 hou2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那塊“晦肉”有异味，不要吃。
examples.english_sentence: That piece of '晦肉' smells off; don't eat it.

cantonese: 晨早黑云栏住东，穿起蓑衣去做工
jyutping: san4 zou2 hak1 wan4 laan4 zyu6 dung1, cyun1 hei2 so1 ji1 heoi3 zou6 gung1
mandarin_meaning: 早上東邊出現烏雲，就穿上雨衣去上班（即見有下雨徵兆要帶雨具）
english_meaning: If dark clouds appear in the east early in the morning, put on a raincoat and go to work — a folk warning to prepare for rain.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語是民間的天氣經驗總結：早晨東邊出現黑雲通常預示會下雨，所以提醒人們上班前要穿雨衣或帶雨具。也可以引申為遇到不祥徵兆時要提早準備。
explanation_english: A folk-weather proverb: dark clouds in the east in the early morning usually mean rain is coming, so people should wear a raincoat or bring rain gear when going to work. It can also be used figuratively to warn to prepare when there are bad signs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 晨早黑云栏住东，穿起蓑衣去做工，記得帶把遮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san4 zou2 hak1 wan4 laan4 zyu6 dung1, cyun1 hei2 so1 ji1 heoi3 zou6 gung1, gei3 dak1 daai3 baa2 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 早上東邊出現烏雲，就穿上雨衣去上班，記得帶把傘。
examples.english_sentence: When dark clouds appear in the east early in the morning, put on a raincoat and go to work — remember to bring an umbrella.

mandarin_meaning: 容易頭暈／容易暈眩（口語、俚語）；也可指人精神恍惚、反應遲鈍
english_meaning: easily dizzy / light‑headed (slang); can also mean spacey or scatterbrained
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語或俚語，用來形容一個人容易感到頭暈（例如暈車、暈船）、頭腦不清楚或顯得精神恍惚、反應遲鈍。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term describing someone who easily feels dizzy (e.g. motion sickness) or who seems spacey/scatterbrained and not fully alert.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我坐巴士會暈精，成日要拎藥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 co5 baa1 si2 wui5 wan1 zing1, seng4 jat6 jiu3 ling1 joek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我坐公交車會暈車，經常要拿藥。
examples.english_sentence: I get motion sick on buses and often have to take medicine.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個暈精，乜嘢都驚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 wan1 zing1, mat1 je5 dou1 geng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個容易緊張／容易害怕的人，什麼都怕。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is such a nervous person—afraid of everything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 坐過山車嗰陣要小心，啲小朋友可能會暈精。
examples.jyutping_sentence: co5 gwo3 saan1 ce1 go2 zan6 jiu3 siu2 sam1, di1 siu2 pang4 jau5 ho2 nang4 wui5 wan1 zing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 坐過山車的時候要小心，小朋友可能會暈眩。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful on roller coasters; kids might get dizzy.

mandarin_meaning: 用來「暖場」或吸引人流的食物（俗稱暖場飯／免費招待小吃）
english_meaning: Food/snacks provided to 'warm up' an event or attract people (free samples or promotional food)
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱，用來在市集、活動或店舖等場合提供的免費小吃或試食，目的是活躍氣氛或吸引人流。此詞在口語中有時作暖場飯（暖場/暖房的變體）。
explanation_english: Colloquial term for free food or samples given at markets, events, or shops to warm up the venue, create atmosphere, or draw in crowds. Often used interchangeably with 暖場飯 in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次市集會擺啲暖房飯，免費畀人試食，想吸引多啲人入場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 si5 zaap6 wui5 baai2 di1 nyun5 fong4 faan6, min5 fai3 bei2 jan4 si3 sik6, soeng2 kap1 jan5 do1 di1 jan4 jap6 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次市集會擺一些暖場飯，免費讓人試吃，想吸引更多人入場。
examples.english_sentence: This market will put out some warm-up food—free samples for people to try—in order to attract more visitors.

mandarin_meaning: 暖洋洋 / 暖烘烘
english_meaning: pleasantly warm; warm and cozy
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語的擬聲詞／形容詞，用來形容令人感到舒適的溫暖感覺，常用於天氣、房間或身體的暖和感。與「暖烘烘」「暖洋洋」意思相近。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese onomatopoeic adjective describing a pleasant, cozy warmth. Commonly used for weather, rooms, or bodily warmth; similar in meaning to 'warm and cozy' or 'toasty'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝個天好暖翕翕，唔使着咁多衫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 go3 tin1 hou2 nyun5 hip3 hip3, m4 sai2 zoek3 gam2 do1 saam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今早天氣暖洋洋，不用穿那麼多衣服。
examples.english_sentence: This morning it's nice and warm; no need to wear so many clothes.

mandarin_meaning: 暗自不滿、悶悶地生氣或覺得委屈
english_meaning: to feel quietly resentful or bitter; to be silently annoyed or put out
explanation_mandarin: 粵語非正式用語，形容表面上說沒事或不表露情緒，但心裏其實不滿、悶住唔開心。
explanation_english: An informal Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who outwardly acts as if nothing's wrong but is secretly annoyed, hurt, or bitter.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話唔緊要，但其實係暗哑抵住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 m4 gan2 jiu3, daan6 kei4 sat6 hai6 am3 aa3 dai2 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说没事，但其实暗自不满。
examples.english_sentence: He says he's fine, but he's actually quietly resentful.

mandarin_meaning: 突然地；猛然間（口語）
english_meaning: suddenly; abruptly; all of a sudden (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「暴暴聲」是香港粵語口語用詞，表示某事或某個動作在沒有預告下迅速、突然地發生，常作副詞使用。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial expression meaning that something happens quickly and without warning; used as an adverb to indicate abruptness or suddenness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢暴暴聲走咗，冇同我講一聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bou6 bou6 seng1 zau2 zo2, mou5 tung4 ngo5 gong2 jat1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然走了，沒跟我說一聲。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly left without telling me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢暴暴聲話：「我唔做啦！」大家都愣咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bou6 bou6 seng1 waa6: "ngo5 m4 zou6 laa3!" daai6 gaa1 dou1 lung6 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然說：「我不做了！」大家都愣住了。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly said, "I'm not doing it!" and everyone was stunned.

mandarin_meaning: 光亮；日光（文言）
english_meaning: brightness; sunlight (literary/archaic)
explanation_mandarin: 「曀」為文言字，常用來表示光亮、日光或陽光的輝映，現代漢語中較少使用，多見於古文或詩詞。
explanation_english: A literary/archaic character meaning brightness or sunlight; used in classical texts and poetry to describe radiant light or sunshine.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「曀」呢個字好少用，多喺古文入面表示光亮或者日光。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 'jik6' ni1 go3 zi6 hou2 siu2 jung6, do1 hai6 gu2 man4 jap6 min6 biu2 si6 gwong1 loeng6 waak6 ze2 jat6 gwong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: “曀”这个字很少使用，多出现在古文中，表示光亮或日光。
examples.english_sentence: '曀' is a rarely used character, mostly appearing in classical texts to denote brightness or sunlight.

mandarin_meaning: 小聲、含糊或模糊地說話（低聲嘀咕、喃喃自語）
english_meaning: speaking softly or indistinctly; murmuring/whispering or muttering under one's breath
explanation_mandarin: 描述說話時聲音很小、含混或低沉，常用來形容細聲抱怨、嘀咕或輕聲交談。
explanation_english: Describes a manner of speaking with a very soft, muffled, or low voice — often used for murmuring, muttering, or quiet talk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿嫂喺屋企曉曉聲講嘢，聽唔清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 sou2 hai2 uk1 kei2 hiu2 hiu2 seng1 gong2 je5, teng1 m4 cing1 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 嫂子在家裡小聲地說話，聽不清楚。
examples.english_sentence: My sister‑in‑law was speaking softly at home; I couldn't hear clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 晒盐；用日晒（和风）使海水蒸发以制盐
english_meaning: to sun-dry salt; to produce salt by evaporating seawater in salt pans
explanation_mandarin: 指將海水或鹵水放在鹽田或平地上，利用太陽和風使水分蒸發，從而留下鹽的傳統製鹽方法。
explanation_english: Refers to the traditional method of producing salt by spreading seawater or brine in salt pans or on flat ground and using the sun and wind to evaporate the water, leaving the salt behind.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 以前有啲鹽田會曬鹽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji5 cin4 jau5 di1 jim4 tin4 wui5 saai3 jim4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 以前有些盐田会晒盐。
examples.english_sentence: In the past, some salt pans used to sun-dry salt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 曬鹽係傳統製鹽方法，利用太陽同風把海水蒸發。
examples.jyutping_sentence: saai3 jim4 hai6 cyun4 tung2 zai3 jim4 fong1 faat3, lei6 jung6 taai3 joeng4 tung4 fung1 baa2 hoi2 seoi2 zing1 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晒盐是传统制盐方法，利用太阳和风使海水蒸发。
examples.english_sentence: Sun-drying salt is a traditional method of producing salt, using sun and wind to evaporate seawater.

mandarin_meaning: （粤语俚语）讨厌又爱自夸或惹事的人；用作贬义称呼
english_meaning: Cantonese slang insult for an annoying, show-off or troublemaking person
explanation_mandarin: 「曳豬」是香港粤语俚语，用来骂人，通常指爱吹嘘、装腔作势、惹人厌或难搞的人。有时亦用于形容既嚣张又胆小的人。语气粗俗、不正式。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang insult. It refers to someone who is obnoxious, a show-off, or a troublemaker — often bragging or acting arrogant and annoying. The term is vulgar and informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日曳豬，成日吹水，真係好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 je5 zyu1, sing4 jat6 ceoi1 seoi2, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是曳豬，整天吹牛，真的很烦人。
examples.english_sentence: He’s always acting like a show-off — constantly bragging. He's really annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好曳豬，做人低調啲啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 je5 zyu1, zou6 jan4 dai1 diu6 di1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你别当曳豬，做人低调一点吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a '曳豬' — try to be more low-key.

mandarin_meaning: 书馆（图书馆）
english_meaning: library; book house
explanation_mandarin: 指收藏、借阅或供人阅读书籍的场所；在一些语境或古代用法中，也可指书院或藏书楼。
explanation_english: Refers to a place that houses, lends, or provides books for reading; in some contexts or historically it can mean a study hall or repository of books.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間社區書舘好多人借書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 se5 keoi1 syu1 gun2 hou2 do1 jan4 ze3 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間社區書館很多人借書。
examples.english_sentence: Many people borrow books from this community library.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 古時有書舘係學者教書研讀嘅地方。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 si4 jau5 syu1 gun2 hai6 hok6 ze2 gaau3 syu1 jin4 duk6 ge3 dei6 fong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 古時有書館是學者教書、研讀的地方。
examples.english_sentence: In ancient times, book houses served as places for scholars to teach and study.

cantonese: 曹操都有知心友，关公亦有对头人
jyutping: cou4 cou1 dou1 jau5 zi1 sam1 jau5, gwaan1 gung1 jik6 jau5 deoi3 tau4 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 即使是曹操也有知心朋友，关公也有对头（对手/敌人）。表示人人都有朋友和对手。
english_meaning: Even a powerful figure like Cao Cao has close confidants, and even a revered hero like Guan Yu has rivals — everyone has friends and foes.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用历史人物比喻，意思是即便是地位显赫或受人尊敬的人，也会有人支持和有人对抗。常用来提醒别人不要以为某人孤立无援或不可战胜。
explanation_english: This saying uses historical figures as examples to convey that even prominent or respected people have both confidants and adversaries. It's used to remind others not to assume someone is unsupported or invincible.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺政壇上，曹操都有知心友，關公亦有對頭人，唔好低估對手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 zing3 taan4 soeng5, cou4 cou1 dou1 jau5 zi1 sam1 jau5, gwaan1 gung1 jik6 jau5 deoi3 tau4 jan4, m4 hou2 dai1 gu3 deoi3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在政坛上，曹操都有知心朋友，关公也有对头，不要低估对手。
examples.english_sentence: In politics, even Cao Cao has close confidants and even Guan Yu has rivals — don't underestimate your opponents.

mandarin_meaning: 最多不過是 / 充其量只是
english_meaning: at most; only; at best
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用來表示某事的程度上限或弱化對某事的評價，意為“充其量不過是／頂多是”。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used to indicate an upper limit or to downplay something; means 'at most' or 'only'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢遲到，最多唔係十幾分鐘啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ci4 dou6, zeoi3 do1 m4 hai6 sap6 gei2 fan1 zung1 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他迟到，最多不过十几分钟而已。
examples.english_sentence: He's late; at most it's only about ten-odd minutes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔覺得佢做錯，最多唔係經驗唔夠啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gok3 dak1 keoi5 zou6 co3, zeoi3 do1 m4 hai6 ging1 jim6 m4 gau3 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不覺得他做錯了，充其量只是經驗不夠而已。
examples.english_sentence: I don't think he did anything wrong; at most it's just a lack of experience.

mandarin_meaning: 最后；在最末尾（括號中的「屘」為罕用或古字寫法）
english_meaning: at the very end; last (the character in parentheses '屘' is a rare/archaic variant)
explanation_mandarin: 表示位置或次序在最末端，常用於口語，用來指事情的最後階段、最後一個或最後到達。括號中的「屘」為罕見或古字寫法，口語一般寫作「最尾」。
explanation_english: Indicates position or order at the very end; commonly used in colloquial Cantonese to refer to the final stage, the last item, or arriving last. The character in parentheses ('屘') is a rare/archaic variant; spoken Cantonese typically uses '最尾'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最尾先嚟，結果冇位坐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 mei5 sin1 lei4, git3 gwo2 mou5 wai6 co5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最后才来，结果没有位置坐。
examples.english_sentence: He came at the very end, and as a result there were no seats left.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）最有面子 / 最光彩
english_meaning: most 'face' (most prestigious or gives the most face); very respectable/impressive (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「最面」為廣東話口語，常作「最有面」的縮略說法，用來表示某人或某事最有面子、最光彩、最體面。多見於香港口語或朋友間的非正式用法。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression, typically a clipped form of "最有面". It indicates that someone or something is the most 'face-giving' — prestigious, respectable, or impressive. Mostly used in informal Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日公司派佢上台領獎，真係最面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 gung1 si1 paai3 keoi5 soeng5 toi4 ling5 zoeng2, zan1 hai6 zeoi3 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天公司派他上台領獎，真是最有面子。
examples.english_sentence: The company sent him on stage to receive the award — it really gives him the most face.

mandarin_meaning: 会弹不会唱（会弹奏乐器但不会/不擅长唱歌；也可比喻擅长幕后或技术工作但不擅长表演/领衔）
english_meaning: Can play (an instrument) but can't sing; figuratively, good at the instrumental/technical/backstage part but not at singing/leading/performing
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，字面意思是「會彈奏樂器但不會唱歌」。日常也常用作比喻，指一個人擅長配合、技術性或幕後工作，但不適合或不擅長做主唱/領導/表演性角色。常見於香港口語語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning literally 'can play (an instrument) but can't sing.' It is used literally to describe someone who can play instruments but cannot sing, and figuratively to describe someone who is good at accompaniment, technical or behind-the-scenes work but not suited to lead or perform.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢識彈結他，但係會彈唔會唱，通常只做伴奏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sik1 daan6 git3taa1, daan6hai6 wui5 daan6 m4 wui5 coeng3, tung1 soeng4 zi2 zou6 bun6 zau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他會彈吉他，但會彈不會唱，通常只做伴奏。
examples.english_sentence: He can play the guitar but can't sing, so he usually only does accompaniment.

mandarin_meaning: 幹嘛擺出那麼大的架勢／為什麼那麼擺架子
english_meaning: Why put on that attitude? / What's with the big attitude?
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，用來質疑或抱怨對方為何表現得很有架子、擺出高姿態或過於正式／做作。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to question or complain about someone acting pretentious, putting on airs, or behaving with an unnecessary attitude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有乜咁架势？我只係幫手啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 mat1 gam2 gaa3 sai3? ngo5 zi2 hai6 bong1 sau2 ze2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你幹嘛那麼擺架子？我只是幫忙而已。
examples.english_sentence: Why are you putting on that attitude? I'm just helping.

mandarin_meaning: 有什麼就說什麼；儘管說
english_meaning: Say whatever you have to say; speak your mind; say it freely
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語短語 / 祈使語（片語）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語表達，用來鼓勵對方把心裡的話說出來（有什麼就說什麼），也可描述某人說話直率、不加修飾。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning 'say whatever (you have to say)' or 'speak your mind.' It can be used to encourage frankness or to describe someone who speaks bluntly or without restraint.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有乜話乜，唔使驚，講出嚟啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 mat1 waa6 mat1, m4 sai2 geng1, gong2 ceot1 lai4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有什麼就說什麼，不用怕，說出來吧。
examples.english_sentence: Say whatever you have to say, don't be afraid — say it out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日有乜話乜，講話好直接。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 jau5 mat1 waa6 mat1, gong2 waa6 hou2 zik6 zip3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常有什麼就說什麼，說話很直接。
examples.english_sentence: He often says whatever is on his mind; he speaks very directly.

cantonese: 有事钟无艳，无事夏迎春
jyutping: jau5 si6 zung1 mou4 jim6, mou4 si6 haa6 jing4 ceon1
mandarin_meaning: 有事钟无艳，无事夏迎春（指在需要幫助或遇到麻煩時，有用的人往往不在；沒事時，長得討人喜歡或不切實際的人卻出現）
english_meaning: When there's trouble, Zhong Wuyan isn't around; when there's nothing going on, Xia Yingchun shows up — i.e. the capable/helpful person is absent when needed, while the pretty/pleasant-but-useless one appears only when there's no need.
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東俗語，借兩個名字（鐘無艷、夏迎春）對比，表示在緊要關頭常常沒有實際幫助的人，而外表討喜或無實際幫助的人只在無事時出現。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb that contrasts two names (Zhong Wuyan and Xia Yingchun) to say that those who can really help are often absent in times of need, while those who are pleasant or merely decorative show up only when nothing important is happening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰陣時真係有事鍾無艷，無事夏迎春，大家都唔幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zan6 si4 zan1 hai6 jau5 si6 zung1 mou4 jim6, mou4 si6 haa6 jing4 ceon1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那時真是有事鐘無艷，無事夏迎春，大家都不幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: At that time it was exactly 'when there's trouble, Zhong Wuyan isn't there; when there's nothing, Xia Yingchun shows up' — nobody helped.

jyutping: jau5 bin6 ji4 m4 sai2 geng2
mandarin_meaning: 有便宜不用害羞／別客氣地佔便宜
english_meaning: If there's a bargain/benefit, don't hesitate to take it; help yourself
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，意思是遇到便宜或佔便宜的機會時，不用害羞或客氣，儘量去享受或拿取。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression telling someone not to be shy or hesitant about taking advantage of a bargain or benefit — essentially 'help yourself' when there's a deal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 超市今日減價，啲罐頭平好多，有便宜唔使颈，買幾罐落手啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ciu1 si5 gam1 jat6 gaam2 gaa3, di1 gun3 tau4 peng4 hou2 do1, jau5 bin6 ji4 m4 sai2 geng2, maai5 gei2 gun3 lok6 sau2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 超市今天打折，罐頭便宜很多，有便宜不用害羞，買幾罐吧。
