examples.english_sentence: The supermarket is on sale today; the cans are much cheaper — if there's a bargain, don't hesitate, buy a few.

mandarin_meaning: 你有没有搞错？/你在开玩笑吗？
english_meaning: Are you kidding me? / You've got to be kidding / Are you serious?
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感叹词 / 口语化疑问句
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示對某事或某人感到驚訝、不滿或難以置信，語氣通常較強烈且口語化，有時帶有冒犯意味。
explanation_english: Used to express surprise, disbelief, or annoyance at someone's action or statement. It is colloquial and often forceful; can sound rude depending on tone and context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 咁貴？有冇搞錯？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam2 gwai3? jau5 mou5 gaau2 co3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这么贵？你有没有搞错？
examples.english_sentence: This expensive? Are you kidding me?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你遲到三個鐘？有冇搞錯！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ci4 dou3 saam1 go3 zung1? jau5 mou5 gaau2 co3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你迟到三小时？你有没有搞错！
examples.english_sentence: You're three hours late? Are you serious!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司要我做埋啲份外工作，仲唔加人工，有冇搞錯！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jiu3 ngo5 zou6 maai4 di1 fan6 ngoi6 gung1 zok3, zung6 m4 gaa1 jan4 gung1, jau5 mou5 gaau2 co3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司要我做额外的工作，还不加工资，你有没有搞错！
examples.english_sentence: The company wants me to do extra work and still won't raise my pay — are you kidding me!

mandarin_meaning: 有多少；有幾多（書面/古風用法）
english_meaning: how many / how much (literary or rhetorical Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 用來詢問數量或程度，相當於口語的「有幾多」或現代漢語的「有多少」。在粵語中此詞帶有較多書面或文言色彩，有時用作修辭問句。
explanation_english: Asks about quantity or extent, equivalent to the colloquial '有幾多' or Mandarin '有多少'. In Cantonese it has a somewhat literary/archaic tone and can be used rhetorically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢箱餅乾有幾何，夠我哋分嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 soeng1 beng2 gon1 jau5 gei2 ho4, gau3 ngo5 dei6 fan1 maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這箱餅乾有多少，夠我們分嗎？
examples.english_sentence: How many cookies are in this box; are they enough for us to share?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你屋企有幾何人？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 uk1 kei2 jau5 gei2 ho4 jan4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你家裡有多少人？
examples.english_sentence: How many people are in your household?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 世間榮辱有幾何，名利不過雲煙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 gaan1 wing4 juk6 jau5 gei2 ho4, ming4 lei6 bat1 gwo3 wan4 jin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 世間的榮辱有多少，名利不過雲煙。
examples.english_sentence: How many honors and disgraces are there in the world? Fame and fortune are nothing but passing clouds.

mandarin_meaning: 能為自己加分；贏得好感或讚賞
english_meaning: to earn points/credit (with someone); to gain favor or make a good impression
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示某個行為或表現能為自己帶來好 impression 或增加好感、積分般的優勢。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning an action or behavior that 'earns you points' — i.e., gains favor, makes a good impression, or brings you advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁幫佢，真係好有分數。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 bong1 keoi5, zan1 hai6 hou2 jau5 fan1 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣幫他，真的很加分。
examples.english_sentence: Helping him like this really earns you points.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個舉動喺女朋友嚟講好有分數。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 geoi2 dung6 hai2 neoi5 pang4 jau5 lai4 gong2 hou2 jau5 fan1 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個舉動在女朋友眼中很加分。
examples.english_sentence: This gesture scores you big points with your girlfriend.

jyutping: jau5 gam2 ngaam1 dak1 gam2 kiu4
mandarin_meaning: 竟然這麼湊巧／真是太巧了
english_meaning: What a coincidence! / It's unbelievably coincidental
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，用來強調事情發生得非常湊巧或令人難以置信的巧合，帶有驚訝或無奈的語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to emphasize that something happened in an extremely coincidental or unlikely way, often conveying surprise or a bemused tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日喺地鐵站撞到阿Sam，有咁啱得咁跷！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 hai2 dei6 tit3 zaam6 zong6 dou3 aa3 Sam1, jau5 gam2 ngaam1 dak1 gam2 kiu4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天在地鐵站遇到阿Sam，真是太湊巧了！
examples.english_sentence: I bumped into Ah Sam at the MTR today — what a coincidence!

cantonese: 有咁大个头戴咁大顶帽
jyutping: jau5 gam2 daai6 go3 tau4 daai3 gam2 daai6 ding2 mou6
mandarin_meaning: 自以為了不起；擺架子、裝腔作勢
english_meaning: to put on airs; to act pretentious; who do you think you are?
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人自以為了不起、擺架子或誇耀自己，常帶責備或不滿的語氣。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone acting as if they are important, putting on airs or showing off; often said in a reproachful or dismissive tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢有咁大個頭戴咁大頂帽，成日擺架子，大家都唔鍾意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau5 gam2 daai6 go3 tau4 daai3 gam2 daai6 ding2 mou6, sing4 jat6 baai2 gaa3 zi2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他自以為了不起，總是擺架子，大家都不喜歡。
examples.english_sentence: He acts like he's so important and is always putting on airs; no one likes it.

cantonese: 有咁大条鱼打咁大个晕
jyutping: jau5 gam2 daai6 tiu4 jyu4 daa2 gam2 daai6 go3 wan1
mandarin_meaning: （口語）被嚇暈／被嚇到／驚呆了
english_meaning: Colloquial expression meaning to be extremely surprised, shocked or stunned (lit. 'there's such a big fish that causes such a big dizziness').
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語片語 / 感嘆短語
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，用來形容對某事感到非常驚訝或被嚇到，帶有誇張或幽默色彩。字面上提到一條很大的魚和很大的暈，但實際上是比喻驚訝或震驚。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial idiom used to describe being extremely surprised or shocked, often with an exaggerated or humorous tone. Literally mentions a very large fish and a big faint/dizziness, but is used figuratively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話自己贏咗大獎，大家都當場有咁大条鱼打咁大个晕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 jing4 zo2 daai6 zoeng2, daai6 gaa1 dou1 dong1 coeng4 jau5 gam2 daai6 tiu4 jyu4 daa2 gam2 daai6 go3 wan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說自己中了大獎，大家當場都嚇呆了。
examples.english_sentence: He said he won the big prize — everyone was stunned on the spot.

jyutping: jau5 gam2 hou2 dak1 gam2 hou2
mandarin_meaning: 既然那么好，那就算了/随它去（带有无奈或讽刺意味）
english_meaning: If it's really that good, fine — so be it (often resigned or sarcastic)
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示無奈、接受或帶有諷刺意味，通常在對方聲稱某事很好的時候說，意思是「既然那麼好，那就算了／隨它去」。
explanation_english: Used to express resignation, reluctant acceptance, or sarcasm when someone claims something is very good or someone gets special treatment; it means 'if it's that great, fine / so be it.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日攞特權，真係有咁好得咁好！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 lo2 dak6 kyun4, zan1 hai6 jau5 gam2 hou2 dak1 gam2 hou2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是占特權，真是——既然那麼好，那就算了！
examples.english_sentence: He always gets special privileges — well, if it's really that great, fine!

mandarin_meaning: 就只有這麼多；僅此而已
english_meaning: only this much; that's all there is; that's it
explanation_mandarin: 表示只有那麼多，沒有更多。常用於口語，帶有略為無奈或輕微淡化語氣，等同「就這麼多／只有這麼多」。
explanation_english: Indicates there is only that amount and no more. Used in colloquial speech, often with a slightly resigned or downplaying tone; equivalent to "that's all" or "only this much."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我袋入面而家得三十蚊，真係有啲咁多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 doi6 jap6 min6 ji4 gaa1 dak1 saam1 sap6 man1, zan1 hai6 jau5 di1 gam2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我包里現在只有三十元，真的是只有這麼多。
examples.english_sentence: There's only thirty dollars in my bag now — it's really just this much.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你問佢會幫幾多，佢話可以幫一半，但實際上有啲咁多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 man6 keoi5 wui5 bong1 gei2 do1, keoi5 waa6 ho2 ji5 bong1 jat1 bun3, daan6 sat6 zai3 soeng6 jau5 di1 gam2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你問他會幫多少，他說可以幫一半，但實際上只有這麼多。
examples.english_sentence: You asked how much he'd help; he said half, but in reality it's only this much.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）有東西到了；也可表示「有情況/有問題發生」
english_meaning: There is something that has arrived; (colloquially) something's up / something's going on
explanation_mandarin: 「有嘢到」在粵語中常用來表示某件東西（例如快遞、包裹）已經到達；在口語中也可用來表示察覺到異常情況或懷疑有問題（即「有事/有情況」）。語氣和語境決定具體含義。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "有嘢到" is often used to say that something (e.g. a delivery or package) has arrived. Colloquially it can also mean "something's up" or "there's a situation/problem," depending on tone and context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喂，快遞打嚟話有嘢到喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai3, faai3 dai6 daa2 lai4 waa6 jau5 je5 dou3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 喂，快递打电话来说东西到了。
examples.english_sentence: Hey, the courier called to say something has arrived.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢咁詭異，我覺得有嘢到喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 gam2 gwai2 jik6, ngo5 gok3 dak1 jau5 je5 dou3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说话很诡异，我觉得有情况/有问题发生了。
examples.english_sentence: He's talking oddly; I feel something's up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺屋企樓下有嘢到，要落去睇下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 uk1 kei2 lau4 haa6 jau5 je5 dou3, jiu3 lok6 heoi3 tai2 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家里楼下有东西到了，要下去看看。
examples.english_sentence: There's something that arrived downstairs at home; I need to go down and check.

jyutping: jau5 gam2 ngaam1 dak1 gam2 kiu4
mandarin_meaning: 竟然這麼湊巧 / 怎麼會這麼巧
english_meaning: What a coincidence; how unreasonably/remarkably coincidental (often with surprise or irony)
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示對事情發生得非常湊巧或恰好感到驚訝、無奈或帶有諷刺意味的口語表達。相當於「真是太湊巧了」或「怎麼會這麼巧」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to show surprise (or ironic resignation) at how coincidentally something occurred. Similar to "what a coincidence" or "as if it couldn't be more coincidental."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝落街，啱啱遇到舊同學，佢話有張多餘嘅飛送俾我，真係有噉啱得噉橋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 lok6 gaai1, ngaam1 ngaam1 jyu6 dou3 gau6 tung4 hok6, keoi5 waa6 jau5 zoeng1 do1 jyu4 ge3 fei1 sung3 bei2 ngo5, zan1 hai6 jau5 gam2 ngaam1 dak1 gam2 kiu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上出門時正好遇到舊同學，他說有一張多餘的票送給我，真是太湊巧了。
examples.english_sentence: This morning I ran into an old classmate who said he had an extra ticket and gave it to me — what a coincidence.

jyutping: jau5 tau4 wai1 mou5 mei5 zan3
mandarin_meaning: 虎头蛇尾 / 有頭無尾（開頭聲勢大但沒有後續或收尾）
english_meaning: Starts off with a lot of show or momentum but peters out; all sizzle and no steak
explanation_mandarin: 形容事情或人開頭做得很有聲勢或很誇張，但最後沒有後續或沒做好、草草收場。
explanation_english: Describes something or someone that begins with great show or momentum but lacks follow-through or a proper finish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個計劃聽落好吸引，但大家做咗幾個星期就停咗，真係有头威冇尾阵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 teng1 lok6 hou2 kap1 jan5, daan6 daai6 gaa1 zou6 zo2 gei2 go3 sing1 kei4 zau6 ting4 zo2, zan1 hai6 jau5 tau4 wai1 mou5 mei5 zan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个计划听起来很吸引，但大家做了几星期就停了，真是有头无尾。
examples.english_sentence: This project sounded attractive, but everyone stopped after a few weeks — really a flashy start with no finish.

mandarin_meaning: 有头有路（表示有条理、清晰有序；也可指体面、像样）
english_meaning: organized/coherent; presentable or proper
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容說話、做事有條理、頭緒分明、安排得當；有時也用來形容打扮或情況看起來體面、像樣。
explanation_english: Used to describe speaking or acting in an orderly, coherent way with clear structure; can also describe someone or something that looks presentable or proper.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢有頭有路，老細好放心交畀佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 jau5 tau4 jau5 lou6, lou5 sai3 hou2 fong3 sam1 gaau1 bei2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事有頭有路，老板很放心把工作交給他。
examples.english_sentence: He works in an organized way; the boss feels confident assigning tasks to him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次嘅報告寫得有頭有路，評審都話好有條理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 ge3 bou3 gou3 se2 dak1 jau5 tau4 jau5 lou6, ping4 sam2 dou1 waa6 hou2 jau5 tiu4 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次的報告寫得有頭有路，評審都說很有條理。
examples.english_sentence: This report is written coherently; the reviewers said it's very well-organized.

mandarin_meaning: 有面子；有排面；體面、有身份、有面子
english_meaning: to have prestige/face; to be respectable or presentable; to have social status
explanation_mandarin: 表示一個人或事物有體面、有排場或有社會地位，讓人覺得尊重或看得起；也可指外表或場面顯得堂堂正正。
explanation_english: Indicates that a person or thing is dignified, respectable, or shows social status—something that gives 'face' or looks impressive; can refer to both reputation and outward appearance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家做咗經理，好有頭有面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zou6 zo2 ging1 lei5, hou2 jau5 tau4 jau5 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在當了經理，很有面子。
examples.english_sentence: He's now a manager and looks very respectable.

jyutping: jau5 tau4 mou4 m4 zou6 laap6 lei6
mandarin_meaning: 有頭髮別自貶身份（俗語）
english_meaning: Don't demean yourself / Don't do something beneath your dignity (colloquial proverb)
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俗語，用來勸人不要做有損身份或自貶身價的事。字面意思是「既然有頭髮，就不要做像瘌痢（卑微、可恥）的東西」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial proverb advising someone not to demean themselves or do things beneath their dignity. Literally, 'if you have hair on your head, don't be a louse.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有頭毛唔做瘌痢，唔好為咗啲小錢屈低自己。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 tau4 mou4 m4 zou6 laap6 lei6, m4 hou2 wai6 zo2 di1 siu2 cin2 wat1 dai1 zi6 gei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有頭髮別自貶身份，不要為了那點小錢降低自己。
examples.english_sentence: Don't demean yourself — if you've got hair on your head, don't act like a louse; don't lower yourself for a little money.

jyutping: jau5 zi1 si3 mou5 sat6 zai3
mandarin_meaning: 華而不實 / 徒有其表
english_meaning: all show and no substance; style without substance
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容外表或表現看起來很有氣派或姿勢，但實際上缺乏內容或效果，沒有真實價值。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone or something that looks stylish or impressive on the surface but lacks real substance, practical value, or effectiveness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個報告好有姿勢，但實際上冇乜用，真係有姿勢冇實際。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 bou3 gou3 hou2 jau5 zi1 si3, daan6 sat6 zai3 soeng6 mou5 mat1 jung6, zan1 hai6 jau5 zi1 si3 mou5 sat6 zai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的報告很有表面功夫，但實際上沒什麼用，真是華而不實。
examples.english_sentence: His report looks impressive, but in reality it's hardly useful — really all style and no substance.

cantonese: 有尺莫量人短，有口要講人長
jyutping: jau5 cek3 mok6 loeng4 jan4 dyun2, jau5 hau2 jiu3 gong2 jan4 coeng4
mandarin_meaning: 不要用自己的尺子去度量别人的短处；既然有嘴，就多说别人的优点（不要一味挑剔，要多肯定别人）。
english_meaning: Don't use your own ruler to measure others' faults; if you speak, mention people's merits — an admonition not to nitpick or criticize others and to be more positive.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用比喻提醒人不要以自己的標準挑剔或放大別人的缺點，說話時應該多稱讚別人的長處，少責備。
explanation_english: A proverbial admonition: don't judge or nitpick others' shortcomings by your own standards; when you speak, highlight people's strengths rather than criticize them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做人唔好成日挑剔，記住有尺莫量人短，有口要講人長。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 jan4 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 tiu1 tik1, gei3 zyu6 jau5 cek3 mok6 loeng4 jan4 dyun2, jau5 hau2 jiu3 gong2 jan4 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做人不要总是挑剔，记住不要用尺子量人的短处，有嘴就多说别人的优点。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always be nitpicky; remember not to measure others' faults, and if you speak, say people's strengths.

jyutping: jau5 dak1 zan3, mou5 dak1 fan3
mandarin_meaning: 可以盡情玩樂/嗨，但會通宵不能睡覺
english_meaning: Can have a blast/party, but won't get any sleep
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，表示有機會盡情玩、狂歡或慶祝，通常會導致通宵或沒法好好睡覺。常用於談論派對、通宵慶祝或考後放鬆等情境，有時帶玩笑或誇張語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning there's an opportunity to party/have fun but as a result you won't get to sleep. It's used to talk about celebrations, all‑night parties, or occasions where staying up is expected; often said jokingly or hyperbolically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚有得震，冇得瞓都要去玩！
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jau5 dak1 zan3, mou5 dak1 fan3 dou1 jiu3 heoi3 waan2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚可以盡情玩，雖然沒得睡覺也要去玩！
examples.english_sentence: Tonight we can have a blast — even if we don't get any sleep, we're still going out!

cantonese: 有心唔怕迟，十月都系拜山时
jyutping: jau5 sam1 m4 paa3 ci4, sap6 jyut6 dou1 hai6 baai3 saan1 si4
mandarin_meaning: 只要有心，迟到也不成问题；什么时候去扫墓（拜山、祭祖）都可以，即使在十月也行。
english_meaning: If you have sincere intentions, it's never too late — you can pay respects at the grave anytime, even in October.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面意思是「有心不怕遲」，強調只要有心意，遲了也沒關係；「拜山」指掃墓、祭祖，帶有不拘時間、重視心意的文化含義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb meaning 'it's never too late if you're sincere.' '拜山' refers to visiting graves or ancestral rites; the phrase stresses intention over exact timing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢遲咗先到拜山，但有心唔怕遲，十月都係拜山時。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ci4 zo2 sin1 dou3 baai3 saan1, daan6 jau5 sam1 m4 paa3 ci4, sap6 jyut6 dou1 hai6 baai3 saan1 si4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他迟了才去扫墓，但只要有心，迟到也不怕，什么时候去扫墓都可以。
examples.english_sentence: He only went to visit the grave late, but if you're sincere it's never too late — you can pay your respects even in October.

cantonese: 有心开晏店，唔怕大肚廉
jyutping: jau5 sam1 hoi1 ngaan3 dim3, m4 paa3 daai6 tou5 lim4
mandarin_meaning: 有决心（去做某事）就不怕受人嘲笑或遇到困难；字面指想开晚间营业的店铺，就不怕被闲话。
english_meaning: If you're determined to do something, don't be afraid of ridicule or obstacles; literally, if you want to open a late-night shop, you won't fear people talking.
explanation_mandarin: 这句粤语俗语多用于鼓励或形容有心去做某事的人，意思是只要有心去做，就不应畏惧别人的议论或困难。原句字面与开晚间店铺有关，但常被引申为凡事有决心就不怕阻碍。属于香港粤语口语表达。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying used to encourage or describe someone determined to do something. It means that if you really want to do something, you shouldn't fear others' gossip or obstacles. Literally about opening a late-night shop, but commonly extended to any determined effort. It is a Hong Kong Cantonese expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話想辭職去做自己生意，我同佢講：有心开晏店，唔怕大肚廉，試下先啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 soeng2 ci4 zik1 heoi3 zou6 zi6 gei2 saang1 ji3, ngo5 tung4 keoi5 gong2: jau5 sam1 hoi1 ngaan3 dim3, m4 paa3 daai6 tou5 lim4, si3 haa5 sin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說想辭職去做自己的生意，我跟他說：有心開晏店，唔怕大肚廉，先試試看吧。
examples.english_sentence: He said he wants to quit and start his own business. I told him: if you're determined, don't fear people's talk — give it a try first.

cantonese: 有情饮水饱，无情食饭饥
jyutping: jau5 cing4 jam2 seoi2 baau2, mou4 cing4 sik6 faan6 gei1
mandarin_meaning: 有情饮水饱，无情食饭饥（俗语）
english_meaning: A proverb meaning that when there is love or affection, even little (e.g. just water) feels satisfying; without affection, even plentiful food cannot satisfy.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用對比表達感情的重要性：有愛情或關係融洽時，物質條件即使簡單也覺得滿足；若無情感支持，即使有食物物質也感到空虛、飢乏。
explanation_english: This proverb contrasts material needs and emotional bonds: with love or a close relationship, even the simplest provision (water) seems enough; without affection, even food leaves one feeling unsatisfied or emotionally hungry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋恩愛咁多年，真係印證咗：有情飲水飽，無情食飯飢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 jan1 oi3 gam2 do1 nin4, zan1 hai6 jan3 zing3 zo2: jau5 cing4 jam2 seoi2 baau2, mou4 cing4 sik6 faan6 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们相爱这么多年，真印证了：有情饮水饱，无情食饭饥。
examples.english_sentence: They've been in love for so many years — it really proves the saying: with love, even water satisfies; without it, even food leaves you hungry.

jyutping: jau5 chaau1 gaa1 mou5 fung1 gou3
mandarin_meaning: 遭到抄家/搜查但沒有官方封令或書面證明
english_meaning: Subjected to a raid/confiscation/search without any official warrant or written authorization
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容被抄家、搜查或被沒收財產，但沒有正式的封令、手續或書面證明，含有非法或程序不透明、被冤枉或被濫權的意思。
explanation_english: Used to describe being raided, searched, or having property confiscated without an official warrant or paperwork; implies lack of due process, illegality, or arbitrary action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講佢哋半夜嚟搜樓，真係有抄家冇封诰，連張紙都冇留低。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 keoi5 dei6 bun3 je6 lai4 sau1 lau4, zan1 hai6 jau5 chaau1 gaa1 mou5 fung1 gou3, lin4 zoeng1 zi2 dou1 mou5 lau4 dai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听说他们半夜来搜楼，确实是有抄家但没有封诰，连一张纸都没留下。
examples.english_sentence: I heard they came to search the building at midnight — it was really a raid without any official warrant; they didn't even leave any paperwork.

mandarin_meaning: 有辦法／有掌控能力
english_meaning: have the ability/means/control to handle something; be capable
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，表示有人有能力、辦法或掌控權，可以處理或搞定某事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning someone has the means, ability, or control to handle or resolve something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔使擔心，佢有揸拿，可以搞掂呢件事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 sai2 daam1 sam1, keoi5 jau5 zaa1 naa4, ho2 ji5 gaau2 dim6 ni1 gin6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不用擔心，他有辦法，可以搞定這件事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't worry, he has the means and can handle this.

mandarin_meaning: （口語/方言）有把握、佔優勢；有底氣（此詞多為「有數」或「有把握」的變體或誤寫）
english_meaning: To be confident; to have a sure advantage or good chance (colloquial/variant of 'jau5 sou3' / 'have a sure thing')
explanation_mandarin: 「有数为」在廣東話口語中通常表示對結果有把握、佔優勢或有底氣。這一寫法較少見，通常是「有數」或「有把握」的變體或誤寫，屬於非正式用法。
explanation_english: In Cantonese colloquial speech, "有数为" is used to indicate being confident, having the upper hand, or a sure advantage. This form is relatively uncommon and is likely a variant or nonstandard form of "有數" (jau5 sou3) or "having confidence"; it is informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次嗰場比賽我哋有数为，唔使太擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 go2 coeng4 bei2 coi3 ngo5 dei6 jau5 sou3 wai6, m4 sai2 taai3 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次那场比赛我们有把握，不用太担心。
examples.english_sentence: We have a good chance in that match; no need to worry too much.

mandarin_meaning: 有欢喜 / 感到高兴、愉快
english_meaning: to feel happy; to be pleased; to have joy
explanation_mandarin: 表示心裡感到高興、愉快，常用於口語，意為對某事或某人有喜悅的心情。
explanation_english: Expresses a feeling of happiness or pleasure. Used as a colloquial phrase meaning to be pleased or joyful about something or someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到你，我有歡喜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 nei5, ngo5 jau5 fun1 hei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 见到你，我很高兴。
examples.english_sentence: I'm happy to see you.

mandarin_meaning: 有精力但坐立不安；心裡焦躁、無法安定
english_meaning: restless; unable to settle down; agitated and fidgety
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語口語，形容一個人心神不寧、坐不定或焦急得安靜不下來。字面上可理解為“有氣（精力）但冇（沒有）定唞（安息）”。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial phrase describing someone who is restless or agitated and cannot calm down or sit still. Literally 'has energy but no rest'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢考試前成日行來行去，真係有氣冇定唞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haau2 si3 cin4 seng4 jat6 hang4 loi4 hang4 heoi3, zan1 hai6 jau5 hei3 mou5 ding6 tau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他考試前總是在來回走動，真是坐立不安。
examples.english_sentence: He kept pacing before the exam; he's really restless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等緊結果嗰陣，大家都好有氣冇定唞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 gan2 git3 gwo2 go2 zan6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hou2 jau5 hei3 mou5 ding6 tau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在等結果的時候，大家都很焦急、坐立不安。
examples.english_sentence: While waiting for the result, everyone was anxious and couldn't sit still.

jyutping: jau5 je4 saang1 mou5 naa5 gaau3
mandarin_meaning: 沒家教；沒禮貌；沒教養
english_meaning: ill-bred; lacking proper upbringing; rude and uncultured
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語／罵人說法，字面意思是「有父生沒有母教」，用來形容一個人沒受良好家教、行為粗魯或無禮。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang insult literally meaning 'born with a father but without a mother to teach' — used to describe someone who lacks proper upbringing and behaves rudely or uncivilized.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講粗口又唔尊重人，真係有爺生冇乸教。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 cou1 hau2 jau6 m4 zyun1 zung6 jan4, zan1 hai6 jau5 je4 saang1 mou5 naa5 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常說髒話又不尊重人，真是沒家教。
examples.english_sentence: He constantly swears and doesn't respect others — truly ill-bred.

mandarin_meaning: 有牌照／有資格；（口語）還要很久、需時很長
english_meaning: 1) licensed / certified; 2) (colloquial) a long time / it'll take a while
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞（亦可作副詞短語）
partOfSpeech_english: adjective (also used as an adverbial phrase)
explanation_mandarin: 「有牌／有排」在粵語有兩個常見用法：一是指持有牌照、合資格或官方認可（如「有牌師傅」）；二是口語用法（常寫作「有排」）表示「還要很久、需時很長」，用作描述時間長短。兩者讀音相同（jau5 paai4），在非正式書寫中常見用「牌」或「排」互換。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 有牌／有排 (jau5 paai4) has two common senses: (1) 'have a licence / be certified' — meaning officially permitted or qualified; (2) colloquial 'a long time' — indicating that something will take or last for quite a while. The two senses share pronunciation, and characters 牌 and 排 are sometimes interchanged in informal writing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係有牌嘅電工，做嘢好可靠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jau5 paai4 ge3 din6 gung1, zou6 je5 hou2 ho2 kaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是有牌照的電工，做事很可靠。
examples.english_sentence: He is a licensed electrician; his work is very reliable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有排等啦，唔好心急。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 paai4 dang2 laa1, m4 hou2 sam1 gap1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你還要等很久，別著急。
examples.english_sentence: You'll have to wait a long time; don't be impatient.

jyutping: jau5 wun2 waa6 wun2, jau5 dip6 waa6 dip6
mandarin_meaning: 实话实说；直言不讳，把事物按其本质称呼
english_meaning: Call things by their name; speak plainly and directly; be blunt and straightforward
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話俗語，意思是把事物或話按其本質稱呼、直截了當地說出來，不拐彎抹角或含糊其詞。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to call things by their proper names and speak directly—be blunt and straightforward rather than evasive or vague.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有嘢要講就有碗話碗、有碟話碟，唔好拐彎抹角。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 je5 jiu3 gong2 zau6 jau5 wun2 waa6 wun2, jau5 dip6 waa6 dip6, m4 hou2 gwaai2 waan1 mut3 gok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有事要說就直說，不要拐彎抹角。
examples.english_sentence: If you have something to say, say it straight—don't beat around the bush.

mandarin_meaning: 看起來有精神/有氣勢但缺乏實質力量或說服力；華而不實
english_meaning: appears impressive or spirited on the surface but lacks real strength, substance, or convincing power; all show and no substance
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容外表或說話看似有氣勢、精神，但實際上缺乏實質內容、力量或執行力，帶有嘲諷或負面評價的語感。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone or something that looks spirited or impressive externally but actually lacks real substance, power, or effectiveness; often used sarcastically or pejoratively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢寫嗰份建議書好有神冇气，字句華麗但冇實質內容。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 se2 go2 fan6 gin3 ji5 syu1 hou2 jau5 san4 mou5 hei3, zi6 geoi3 waa4 lai6 daan6 mou5 sat6 zat1 noi6 jung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他寫的那份建議書看起來很有文采，但沒有實質內容。
examples.english_sentence: The proposal he wrote looks impressive but lacks substance—flowery wording with no real content.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢成日有神冇气，表面講得好威，做起嘢又唔掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 sing4 jat6 jau5 san4 mou5 hei3, biu2 min6 gong2 dak1 hou2 wai1, zou6 hei2 je5 jau6 m4 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話總是外表很有氣勢，表面很厲害，但做事又做不好。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks like he's impressive, but when it comes to doing things he can't deliver.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個演員鏡頭有神冇气，面相有感染力但演技說服力不足。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 jin2 jyun4 geng2 tau4 jau5 san4 mou5 hei3, min6 soeng3 jau5 gam2 jauh6 lik6 daan6 jin2 gei6 syut3 fuk6 lik6 bat1 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那位演員鏡頭感覺有神，但演技缺乏說服力。
examples.english_sentence: That actor looks striking on camera, but his acting lacks convincing power.

mandarin_meaning: 反應慢；做事遲緩
english_meaning: slow to react or move; sluggish
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示某人反應或動作遲緩、跟不上節奏，常帶有輕微貶義或戲謔意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase meaning someone is slow to react or act, often unable to keep up; can be mildly derogatory or teasing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢好有站慢，成日跟唔切我哋嘅進度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 hou2 jau5 zaam6 maan6, sing4 jat6 gan1 m4 cit3 ngo5 dei6 ge3 zeon3 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很慢，經常趕不上我們的進度。
examples.english_sentence: He works slowly and often can't keep up with our schedule.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 打機嗰陣佢手腳好有站慢，成日俾人圍殺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daa2 gei1 go2 zan6 keoi5 sau2 goek3 hou2 jau5 zaam6 maan6, sing4 jat6 bei2 jan4 wai4 saat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 玩遊戲時他動作很慢，經常被人圍殺。
examples.english_sentence: When gaming he is slow to react and often gets surrounded and killed.

mandarin_meaning: 有紋理；（口語）有特色、有層次、很有質感
english_meaning: has texture/pattern; (colloquial) has character, depth, or stylish appeal
explanation_mandarin: 字面上可指物件表面有紋路或紋理；在香港粵語口語中常用來讚賞某人、某物或作品，表示有層次、特色或有質感、好看有看頭。
explanation_english: Literally describes surface texture or pattern. In Hong Kong Cantonese slang it is often used to praise a person, object, or work as having depth, character, distinctive details, or a stylish/appealing texture.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件外套好有紋路，睇落好有質感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 ngoi6 tou3 hou2 jau5 man4 lou6, tai2 lok6 hou2 jau5 zat1 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件外套很有纹路，看起来很有质感。
examples.english_sentence: This jacket has great texture; it looks very stylish/has a nice feel.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講故仔好有紋路，聽落好有層次。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 gu3 zai2 hou2 jau5 man4 lou6, teng1 lok6 hou2 jau5 cang4 ci3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她讲故事很有纹路，听起来很有层次。
examples.english_sentence: He/she tells stories with depth; they sound layered and interesting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個設計有紋路，顯得好有心思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 sit3 gai3 jau5 man4 lou6, hin2 dak1 hou2 jau5 sam1 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个设计很有纹路，显得很有心思。
examples.english_sentence: The design has a lot of texture/detail; it shows thoughtful effort.

mandarin_meaning: 有门路／有关系、有经验、有办法（在某个圈子或行业里能帮忙或解决问题）
english_meaning: To have connections, inside knowledge, or practical know-how — i.e. be well-connected or able to get things done.
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，表示某人在某个行业或圈子里有关系、有经验或有资源，能帮忙处理事情或提供便利。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning someone has connections, experience, or resources within a particular field — they know the way around and can make things happen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你去問佢啦，佢喺呢行真係好有纹有路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 heoi3 man6 keoi5 laa1, keoi5 hai2 ni1 hong4 zan1 hai6 hou2 jau5 man4 jau5 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你去问他吧，他在这一行真的很有门路／有人脉、很有办法。
examples.english_sentence: Go ask him — he really has connections in this line of work and can help.

jyutping: jau5 wu4 seoi1 zau6 hai6 lou5 dau6
mandarin_meaning: 有鬍子就是爸爸
english_meaning: If someone has a beard, they must be the dad (joking/stereotype)
explanation_mandarin: 這句是香港粵語的俚語或戲謔說法，字面意思是「只要有鬍須就判定是父親」，常用來揶揄或戲謔地以外表（例如鬍鬚）推斷身份。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang/joking expression literally meaning "if someone has a beard, they're the dad." It's used humorously or teasingly to stereotype or infer parenthood from facial hair.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到佢有胡须，有啲人就話「有胡须就系老豆」，好搞笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou2 keoi5 jau5 wu4 seoi1, jau5 di1 jan4 zau6 waa6 "jau5 wu4 seoi1 zau6 hai6 lou5 dau6", hou2 gaau2 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到他有鬍子，有些人就說「有鬍子就是爸爸」，很好笑。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing he has a beard, some people say "If he has a beard, he's the dad" — it's pretty funny.

cantonese: 有花自然香，唔使随处抰
jyutping: jau5 faa1 zi6 jin4 hoeng1, m4 sai2 ceoi4 cyu3 mut6
mandarin_meaning: 有本事自然會吸引人，不需要到處炫耀或到處塗抹（香水/妝容等）
english_meaning: If you have genuine quality (beauty, talent, etc.), it shows naturally — you don't need to show off or plaster it everywhere.
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東話俗語，用來表達有內在優勢或真本事的人不需要到處誇耀或刻意裝飾，天然會吸引別人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb advising modesty: true qualities (beauty, talent, virtue) show themselves naturally, so there's no need for ostentatious display or excessive embellishment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔使成日打扮，有花自然香，唔使随处抰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 sai2 sing4 jat6 daa2 baan6, jau5 faa1 zi6 jin4 hoeng1, m4 sai2 ceoi4 cyu3 mut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不需要天天打扮，有本事自然會吸引人，不用到處塗抹。
examples.english_sentence: You don't need to dress up all the time; if you have it naturally, it shows — no need to plaster it everywhere.

mandarin_meaning: 有想法／有潛力／值得一試
english_meaning: interesting; promising; worth considering or trying
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示某事或某主意很有意思、有創意或有發展潛力，值得考慮或嘗試。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning something is interesting, creative, or has potential — worth considering or trying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個計劃有諗頭，值得再傾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 jau5 lam2 tau4, zik1 dak1 zoi3 king1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个计划有想法，值得再讨论。
examples.english_sentence: This plan has potential; it's worth discussing further.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我覺得呢間餐廳有諗頭，啲菜好有創意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gok3 dak1 ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 jau5 lam2 tau4, di1 coi3 hou2 jau5 cong3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我觉得这家餐厅很有想法，菜很有创意。
examples.english_sentence: I think this restaurant is creative; the dishes are very inventive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講法有諗頭，不如試下落手做做睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 faat3 jau5 lam2 tau4, bat1 jyu4 si3 haa5 lok6 sau2 zou6 zou6 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你的说法有想法，不如试着动手做做看。
examples.english_sentence: Your idea is interesting; why not try putting it into practice?

jyutping: jau5 gai3 sik6 gai3, mou5 gai3 sik6 nai4
mandarin_meaning: 有辦法就用，沒辦法就算了／認命
english_meaning: If there's a way, use it; if there isn't, accept it or give up.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，表示遇到問題時：有辦法就採取行動；沒有辦法就只能接受現實或放棄。常用於口語場合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying meaning that if there is a solution or plan, go ahead and use it; if there isn't, accept the situation or give up. Commonly used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果真係有辦法，就去做；冇辦法就算喇——有计食计，冇计食泥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 zan1 hai6 jau5 baan6 faat3, zau6 heoi3 zou6; mou5 baan6 faat3 zau6 syun3 laa3 — jau5 gai3 sik6 gai3, mou5 gai3 sik6 nai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果真的有辦法，就去做；沒有辦法就算了——能做就做，做不到就認命。
examples.english_sentence: If there's really a way, go ahead and do it; if not, forget it — use a plan if you have one, otherwise accept it.

synonyms: 有辦法就做，冇辦法就算

jyutping: jau5 zaak6 sam1 mou5 zaak6 daam2
mandarin_meaning: 有賊心無賊膽（心里有坏念头但没有胆量去做）
english_meaning: Has the intent to do something wrong or daring but lacks the courage to follow through; all talk, no action.
explanation_mandarin: 形容某人心裏有壞念頭或想做壞事，但沒有膽量去付諸行動，常帶貶義。
explanation_english: Describes a person who secretly wants to do something mischievous or daring but does not have the courage to carry it out; often used disparagingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日諗住拎走公司啲錢，但係有賊心冇賊膽，最後冇做成。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 lam2 zyu6 ling1 zau2 gung1 si1 di1 cin2, daan6 hai6 jau5 zaak6 sam1 mou5 zaak6 daam2, zeoi3 hau6 mou5 zou6 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是想着拿公司的钱，但有賊心無賊膽，最后没做成。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps thinking about taking the company's money, but he has the intent without the courage, so in the end he never did it.

mandarin_meaning: 懷孕多久／懷孕幾個月？
english_meaning: How far along are (you) in pregnancy? / How many months pregnant are (you)?
explanation_mandarin: 「有身」在廣東話中表示懷孕，「幾」在此為口語省略用法，合起來常用來詢問懷孕多久或懷孕幾個月。屬於口語/俚語用法，通常用在熟人間的非正式提問。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 有身 means 'to be pregnant' and 幾 here is an informal/elliptical particle asking 'how' or 'how many'. Together, 有身幾 is a colloquial way to ask how far along someone is in pregnancy (e.g. how many months). It's informal and typically used among acquaintances.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家有身幾？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 jau5 san1 gei2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你現在懷孕多久了？
examples.english_sentence: How far along are you now?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講阿玲有身幾，唔知係咪真。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 aa3 ling4 jau5 san1 gei2, m4 zi1 hai6 mai6 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽說阿玲懷孕了，不知道是不是真的。
examples.english_sentence: I heard Ah Ling is pregnant; not sure if it's true.

cantonese: 有酒有肉亲兄弟，无柴无米做乜夫妻
jyutping: jau5 zau2 jau5 juk6 can1 hing1 dai6, mou5 caai4 mou5 mai5 zou6 mat1 fu1 cai1
mandarin_meaning: 指人们只在富足、热闹的时候互相依靠；遇到缺乏柴米等困难时就会抛弃对方，连夫妻关系也难以维持。
english_meaning: A proverb meaning people stick together in good times (plenty of food and drink) but abandon each other in hard times; relationships often depend on material conditions.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语用以形容拜金或见利忘义的现象：有钱有物时大家亲近，贫穷时人心易变，连夫妻也可能分离。
explanation_english: This saying criticizes fair-weather relationships: people are close when there is plenty but desert one another during hardship, even spouses may not stay together without basic resources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋只係有酒有肉親兄弟，無柴無米做乜夫妻，喺你困難嗰陣又走晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 zi2 hai6 jau5 zau2 jau5 juk6 can1 hing1 dai6, mou5 caai4 mou5 mai5 zou6 mat1 fu1 cai1, hai2 nei5 kwan3 naan4 go2 zan6 jau6 zau2 saat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们只是有酒有肉时才像亲兄弟，没柴没米时做什么夫妻，在你困难的时候就全都走了。
examples.english_sentence: They are only like brothers when there is food and drink; when there's no firewood or rice, how can they be spouses — when you have troubles they all leave.

cantonese: 有钱日日节，无钱日日歇
jyutping: jau5 cin4 jat6 jat6 zit3, mou4 cin4 jat6 jat6 hit3
mandarin_meaning: 有钱的人天天像过节，没钱的人天天辛苦
english_meaning: When you're rich every day feels like a holiday; when you're poor every day is a struggle
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，用來形容有錢人可以享受生活、無須操心，而沒錢的人則要天天勞苦或過得辛苦，帶有對社會不公平或生活差異的感慨。
explanation_english: A proverb that describes how wealthy people can enjoy life as if every day is a celebration, while poor people must toil every day; it expresses frustration at social or economic inequality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 香港人成日講：有钱日日节，无钱日日歇，目的係話有錢先可以輕鬆享受生活。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 jan4 sing4 jat6 gong2: jau5 cin4 jat6 jat6 zit3, mou4 cin4 jat6 jat6 hit3, muk6 dik1 hai6 waa6 jau5 cin4 sin1 ho2 ji5 hing1 sung1 hoeng2 sau6 sang1 wut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 香港人常说：有钱天天像过节，没钱天天辛苦，意思是有钱才可以轻松享受生活。
examples.english_sentence: People in Hong Kong often say: when you're rich every day feels like a holiday, when you're poor every day is a struggle — meaning only the wealthy can easily enjoy life.

cantonese: 有钱楼上楼，冇钱地下踎
jyutping: jau5 cin2 lau4 soeng6 lau4, mou5 cin2 dei6 haa6 ngaau4
mandarin_meaning: 有钱的人住上层/过得好，没钱的人只能在下面受窘/受苦
english_meaning: If you have money you go upstairs; if you don't, you squat downstairs — money determines one's social/status advantages, the rich live comfortably while the poor are left worse off.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗语 / 谚语 / 俚语
explanation_mandarin: 一句粤语俗语，用来形容社会资源和待遇随财富分配：有钱的人占优势（“上楼”），没钱的人处于劣势（“地下踎”）。常用于批评社会不公或描述现实的贫富差距。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying that describes how money determines one’s position or treatment: the rich get the better position ('go upstairs'), while the poor are left in worse conditions ('squat downstairs'). Used to comment on social inequality or harsh social realities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家啲樓價咁高，真係有錢樓上樓，冇錢地下踎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 di1 lau4 gaa3 gam2 gou1, zan1 hai6 jau5 cin2 lau4 soeng6 lau4, mou5 cin2 dei6 haa6 ngaau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在房价这么高，确实是有钱的人占优，没钱的人被甩在下面。
examples.english_sentence: With property prices so high, it's true: the rich get the good floors while the poor are left downstairs.

mandarin_meaning: 有時 / 有一陣子
english_meaning: sometimes; for a while
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，表示「有一段時間」或「有時候」，可指短暫的一段時間或偶爾發生的情況。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese adverb meaning 'for a while' or 'sometimes'. It indicates a short period or that something happens occasionally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有陣我都會唔知點算。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 zan6 ngo5 dou1 wui5 m4 zi1 dim2 syun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有時候我也會不知道怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: Sometimes I don't know what to do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢有陣會返工遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau5 zan6 wui5 faan1 gung1 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他有時會上班遲到。
examples.english_sentence: He sometimes arrives late to work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有陣會落雨，記住帶把遮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 zan6 wui5 lok6 jyu5, gei3 zyu6 daai3 baa2 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有時候會下雨，記得帶傘。
examples.english_sentence: It sometimes rains; remember to bring an umbrella.

mandarin_meaning: 已經有了大的麻煩或醜聞，就不再害怕流言或更多指責。
english_meaning: If someone already has a scandal or big problem, they no longer fear gossip or further exposure.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語或網絡用語，字面是「有雷就不怕風吹」，引申為如果已經被揭發或已有重大問題，就不再害怕別人的流言、批評或更多的麻煩，因為情況已經無可再壞。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial or internet phrase. Literally 'having thunder, not afraid of wind' — meaning once someone already has a scandal or big problem, they no longer fear gossip, rumours, or additional trouble because things cannot get much worse.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家佢已經有雷不怕风，外界講啲咩都影響唔到佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 keoi5 ji5 ging1 jau5 leoi4 bat1 paa3 fung1, ngoi6 gaai3 gong2 di1 me1 dou1 jing2 hoeng2 m4 dou3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在已經有了醜聞，所以不再害怕流言蜚語，外界說什麼都影響不了他。
examples.english_sentence: He already has a scandal now, so he's not afraid of the gossip — other people's comments don't affect him.

mandarin_meaning: 趁勢全力以赴／乘勢而為
english_meaning: to seize a favourable opportunity and go all out; to take full advantage of the momentum
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語／口語俚語 (動詞短語)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，指在有利時機或氣勢時盡最大努力、全力以赴去爭取或推進某事。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to make the most of a favourable situation or momentum and go all out to push something through or seize an opportunity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日有機會做大生意，我哋就要有风使尽𢃇，盡量搵多啲客。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 jau5 gei1 wui6 zou6 daai6 saang1 ji3, ngo5 dei6 zau6 jiu3 jau5 fung1 sai2 zeon6 gaap3, zeon6 loeng6 wan2 do1 di1 haak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天有機會做大生意，我們就要趁勢全力以赴，盡量爭取更多客戶。
examples.english_sentence: There’s an opportunity for big business today; we should seize the momentum and go all out to get more customers.

jyutping: jau5 gai1 m4 gwaan2 gwaan2 maa4 jing1
mandarin_meaning: （口語/俚語）對應該照顧或負責的事情漠不關心、敷衍了事；（亦有地區用法指多管閒事）
english_meaning: A colloquial/slang phrase describing someone who neglects duties or things they should take care of — irresponsible or careless; in some regional uses it can imply meddling in others' affairs.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語 / 俚語 短語
explanation_mandarin: 此短語屬香港粵語口語/俚語，字面上含「有雞」與「唔管」等詞，常用來形容對自己應負責的事置之不理、敷衍或不負責；不同地區或語境下也可能帶有「多管閒事」的含意。
explanation_english: This is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression. Literally containing words like "have a chicken" and "not manage," it's commonly used to describe someone who ignores responsibilities or is negligent; depending on regional usage it can also carry a nuance of meddling in others' business.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日有鸡唔管管麻鹰，屋企嘢都唔理，總之唔負責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jau5 gai1 m4 gwaan2 gwaan2 maa4 jing1, uk1 kei5 je5 dou1 m4 lei5, zung2 zi1 m4 fu6 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是有鸡唔管管麻鹰，家裡的事都不管，總之不負責任。
examples.english_sentence: He always '有鸡唔管管麻鹰' — he doesn't take care of things at home; in short, he's irresponsible.

mandarin_meaning: 不詳（疑為粵語地區性俚語／俗語，所用字罕見，主流詞典無收錄）
english_meaning: Unclear/obscure (appears to be a local Cantonese slang expression; characters are rare and not recorded in standard dictionaries)
explanation_mandarin: 「有𪐀㨢」所用的字（𪐀、㨢）均屬罕見字，未見於主要漢語或粵語詞典。此短語應為地區性或網路流行的粵語俚語，具體詞義和讀音在主流資料中無法確認。若在語境中出現，通常需向說話者查證其含義或用法。
explanation_english: The characters used in "有𪐀㨢" (𪐀, 㨢) are rare and not found in standard Chinese or Cantonese dictionaries. The phrase appears to be a localized or internet Cantonese slang expression; its exact meaning and pronunciation cannot be reliably determined from mainstream sources. When encountered, ask the speaker or community for clarification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺街市聽到有人講「有𪐀㨢」，唔知係乜意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gaai1 si5 teng1 dou3 jau5 jan4 gong2 "[pronunciation unknown]", m4 zi1 hai6 mat1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在街市聽到有人說「有𪐀㨢」，不知道是什麼意思。
examples.english_sentence: I heard someone say "有𪐀㨢" at the market; I don't know what it means.

jyutping: ziu1 zung1 jau5 jan4 hou2 zou6 si6
mandarin_meaning: 有后台好办事／有人在权力中心，事情容易办成
english_meaning: If you have someone inside (in authority) backing you, it's easy to get things done — i.e., having connections or a patron makes affairs easier
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容有背景或有人在當權位置幫助，事情就容易辦成，常帶有靠關係、走後門的含意。
explanation_english: A colloquial saying meaning that with influential backing or insider connections, tasks are easy to accomplish — often implying nepotism or influence-peddling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單生意搞掂咗，主要係因為朝中有人好做事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei1 daan1 sang1 ji3 gaau2 dim6 zo2, zyu2 jiu3 hai6 jan1 wai6 ziu1 zung1 jau5 jan4 hou2 zou6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这笔生意能办成，主要是因为朝中有人好办事。
examples.english_sentence: This deal got done mainly because they had someone in power helping — with connections it's easier to get things done.

cantonese: 朝出红云晚落雨，晚出红云晒街市
jyutping: ziu1 ceot1 hung4 wan4 maan5 lok6 jyu5, maan5 ceot1 hung4 wan4 saai3 gaai1 si5
mandarin_meaning: 早晨出现红云，晚上可能下雨；晚上出现红云，第二天会放晴（市场晒太阳）。
english_meaning: If red clouds appear in the morning, expect rain by evening; if red clouds appear in the evening, expect fair weather the next day.
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句粵語的天氣諺語，根據觀察紅色天空與天氣系統位置的關係來預測短期天氣：早上見紅雲通常表示天氣系統將帶來降雨；傍晚見紅雲通常表示翌日放晴。屬於民間經驗，並不保證百分百準確。
explanation_english: A Cantonese weather proverb based on folk observation: red clouds in the morning often indicate an approaching weather system that may bring rain by evening, whereas red clouds in the evening suggest that the following day will be fine. It's a traditional guideline, not a guaranteed forecast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆成日講：朝出紅雲晚落雨，晚出紅雲晒街市，聽佢講我就帶多把遮出門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 sing4 jat6 gong2: ziu1 ceot1 hung4 wan4 maan5 lok6 jyu5, maan5 ceot1 hung4 wan4 saai3 gaai1 si5, teng1 keoi5 gong2 zau6 daai3 do1 baa2 ze1 ceot1 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶常說：朝出紅雲晚落雨，晚出紅雲晒街市。我聽她的話就多帶把傘出門。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma always says, 'red clouds in the morning mean rain by evening; red clouds in the evening mean sunshine the next day.' I take an extra umbrella when she says that.

mandarin_meaning: 整天、從早到晚
english_meaning: from morning till night; day and night; constantly
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，表示一整天、從早到晚、經常持續發生的情況，相當於普通話的「整天／從早到晚」或「日日夜夜」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning all day long or from morning till night — used to indicate something happens constantly or repeatedly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢朝頭夜晚都喺公司加班，冇時間陪屋企人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ziu1 tau4 je6 maan5 dou1 hai2 gung1 si1 gaa1 baan1, mou5 si4 gaan3 pui4 uk1 kei5 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他朝朝晚上都在公司加班，沒時間陪家人。
examples.english_sentence: He works overtime at the company day and night and has no time to spend with his family.

mandarin_meaning: 早上；早晨
english_meaning: in the morning; morning time
explanation_mandarin: 表示早晨的時段，指一天之初的時間。口語中常用「朝早」較多，「朝時」較偏書面或古風用法。
explanation_english: Refers to the morning period of the day. It indicates the early part of the day. In colloquial Cantonese, "朝早" is more commonly used; "朝時" can sound more literary or old-fashioned.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我朝時要返工，八點半出門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ziu1 si4 jiu3 faan1 gung1, baat3 dim2 bun3 ceot1 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我早上要上班，八点半出门。
examples.english_sentence: I have to go to work in the morning; I leave at 8:30.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 朝時個街市好熱鬧，有好多新鮮菜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ziu1 si4 go3 gaai1 si5 hou2 jit6 naau6, jau5 hou2 do1 san1 sin1 coi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 早市很热闹，有很多新鲜蔬菜。
examples.english_sentence: The morning market is lively and has lots of fresh vegetables.

cantonese: 朝朝一碗粥，饿死医生一屋
jyutping: ziu1 ziu1 jat1 wun2 zuk1, ngo6 sei2 ji1 sang1 jat1 uk1
mandarin_meaning: 每天吃一碗粥（清淡飲食），就不容易生病，醫生會沒事可做。
english_meaning: If you eat a simple bowl of congee every day you won't get sick — the doctors would have nothing to do. (Saying that a plain, moderate diet keeps you healthy.)
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，強調清淡、規律的飲食有助於保健和少生病，從而使醫生減少診病機會。
explanation_english: A folk saying that emphasizes eating plain, regular food (like congee) helps keep you healthy and reduces the need for doctors.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆成日講：朝朝一碗粥，餓死醫生一屋，所以我哋盡量食清淡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 sing4 jat6 gong2: ziu1 ziu1 jat1 wun2 zuk1, ngo6 sei2 ji1 sang1 jat1 uk1, so2 ji5 ngo5 dei6 zeon6 loeng6 sik6 cing1 daam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶常說：每天吃一碗粥，醫生全家都會餓死，所以我們盡量吃清淡。
examples.english_sentence: My grandmother always says: 'Eat a bowl of congee every day and you'll starve all the doctors in the house,' so we try to eat lightly.

jyutping: ziu1 zung2 syu6 maan5 gwaai1 baan2
mandarin_meaning: 比喻做事反复无常或自我拆毁，缺乏耐性和长远眼光；把刚开始的努力毁掉，短视。
english_meaning: Literally "plant a tree in the morning and saw it into boards by evening" — an idiom describing short-sighted, self-defeating or inconsistent actions; lacking patience or long-term planning.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容做事沒有恆心或前後矛盾，剛做了事情又把成果毀掉，缺乏長遠規劃與耐性。
explanation_english: Used to criticize behavior that is inconsistent or self-defeating — starting something but destroying it before it can bear fruit; lacking patience and foresight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你成日朝种树晚鎅板，點會有長久嘅成績？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 sing4 jat6 ziu1 zung2 syu6 maan5 gwaai1 baan2, dim2 wui5 jau5 coeng4 gau2 ge3 sing4 zik1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你總是朝種樹、晚鎅板，怎麼會有長久的成效？
examples.english_sentence: If you keep planting trees in the morning and cutting them into boards by evening, how can you expect lasting results?

jyutping: ziu1 hung4 maan5 jyu5, maan5 hung4 saai3 po3 gu2
mandarin_meaning: 早上出現的彩虹常預示之後會下雨；晚間的彩虹則短暫或很快被陽光消散。比喻好景不長或表面現象不可靠，提醒人們不要太早高興或被表象迷惑。
english_meaning: A Cantonese proverb: a rainbow in the morning often signals rain later, while an evening rainbow is short‑lived or will be dispersed by the sun. Figuratively it warns that promising signs can be fleeting or misleading—don't celebrate too early.
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東諺語。字面上說明不同時間出現的彩虹和天氣變化的關係，延伸用法是形容好景不常或表象不能信賴，用來提醒不要太早高興或依賴初步跡象。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying that literally links the timing of rainbows to weather changes. Metaphorically it describes fleeting or deceptive appearances and cautions against premature celebration or trusting first impressions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個項目啱啱開始睇落好有希望，但老細話：朝虹晚雨，晚虹晒破鼓，唔好太早高興。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hong6 muk6 aam1 aam1 hoi1 ci2 tai2 lok6 hou2 jau5 hei1 mong6, daan6 lou5 sai3 waa6: ziu1 hung4 maan5 jyu5, maan5 hung4 saai3 po3 gu2, m4 hou2 taai3 zou2 gou1 hing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个项目刚开始看起来很有希望，但老板说：朝虹晚雨，晚虹晒破鼓，别太早高兴。
examples.english_sentence: This project looked promising at first, but the boss warned: 'a morning rainbow means rain later; an evening rainbow will be ruined by the sun' — don't celebrate too early.

mandarin_meaning: 朝建暮拆／一建一拆；反覆無常、缺乏連貫性
english_meaning: Constantly building and tearing down; repeatedly changing; lacking continuity; also describing fickleness or lack of perseverance
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容事情、工程或政策反覆不定、經常建了又拆、沒有持續性；亦可形容人做事反覆、沒有恆心。
explanation_english: Used to describe projects, policies, or situations that are repeatedly built and dismantled or frequently changed—i.e., lacking continuity. It can also refer to a person who is fickle or lacks perseverance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間公司做嘅項目成日朝行晩拆，員工都唔知幾時先會完成。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 gung1 si1 zou6 ge3 hong6 muk6 sing4 jat6 ziu1 haang4 maan5 caak3, jyun4 gung1 dou1 m4 zi1 gei2 si4 sin1 wui5 jyun4 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那家公司做的項目經常一建一拆，員工都不知道何時才能完成。
examples.english_sentence: That company's projects are constantly being built and torn down; the staff don't know when they'll ever be finished.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府嘅政策好似朝行晩拆，早時決定嘅又一改再改，商家好難計劃未來。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 ge3 zing3 caak3 hou2 ci5 ziu1 haang4 maan5 caak3, zou2 si4 kyut3 ding6 ge3 jau6 jat1 goi2 zoi3 goi2, soeng1 gaa1 hou2 naan4 gai3 waak6 mei6 loi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府的政策像是反覆無常，早先決定的又一改再改，商家難以規劃未來。
examples.english_sentence: The government's policies seem constantly changeable; earlier decisions are revised again and again, making it hard for businesses to plan for the future.

jyutping: ziu1 gin3 hau2, maan5 gin3 min6
mandarin_meaning: 早上只是打個招呼/說幾句話，真正見面或相處通常要到晚上；形容因忙碌而白天難以相聚
english_meaning: Only exchange greetings in the morning and meet in the evening; describes people (often couples/family) who are so busy that they have only brief contact during the day and see each other properly at night
explanation_mandarin: 一個口語俗語，用來形容因為工作或其他事情忙碌，白天只有簡短問候，真正一起相處或見面通常要到晚上才有時間。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression used to describe situations where people are so busy (e.g., with work) that they only exchange brief greetings in the morning and only have time to meet or spend time together in the evening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我同阿珍而家返工好忙，朝見口，晚見面啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 aa3 zan1 ji4 gaa1 faan1 gung1 hou2 mong4, ziu1 gin3 hau2, maan5 gin3 min6 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我和阿珍現在工作很忙，早上只是打個招呼，晚上才能見面。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Jan and I are really busy with work right now; we only exchange greetings in the morning and can meet properly in the evening.

synonyms: 白天匆匆打招呼，晚上才相聚

cantonese: 朝霓风，晚霓风，晏昼虹霓晒裂柱
jyutping: ziu1 ngai4 fung1, maan5 ngai4 fung1, aan3 zau3 hung4 ngai4 saai3 lit6 cyu5
mandarin_meaning: 民间谚语（观天俗语）：不同时间看到霓虹/晕圈会预示不同的天气变化；早晚出现霓虹常被认为意味着将有风，晌午看到虹霓则是极端日晒或异常天气的征兆（民间说法）。
english_meaning: A Cantonese weather proverb/folk saying: seeing rainbows/halos at different times predicts weather changes — rainbows/halos in the morning or evening are taken as signs of forthcoming wind; a midday rainbow/halo is regarded as a sign of intense sun or unusual weather (folk belief).
explanation_mandarin: 這句話屬於粵語的觀天民間說法，用來描述在不同時辰看到霓虹或日月晕圈時，對應的天氣徵兆。它反映了漁民或農村社群基於經驗形成的氣象觀察與預警方法，而非科學預報。
explanation_english: This is a Cantonese folk-weather proverb describing how seeing rainbows/halos at different times of day is taken as a sign of different weather changes. It reflects traditional observational meteorology used by communities (e.g. farmers, fishers) rather than a scientific forecast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我阿爺成日講：朝霓风，晚霓风，晏昼虹霓晒裂柱，話見到霓就要提防風勢同天氣變化。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3je5 sing4 jat6 gong2: ziu1 ngai4 fung1, maan5 ngai4 fung1, aan3 zau3 hung4 ngai4 saai3 lit6 cyu5, waa6 gin3 dou2 ngai4 zau6 jiu3 tai4 fong4 fung1 sai3 tung4 tin1 hei3 bin3 faa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我爷爷常说：朝霓风，晚霓风，晏昼虹霓晒裂柱，说看到霓（虹）就要提防风力和天气变化。
examples.english_sentence: My grandfather often says: '朝霓风，晚霓风，晏昼虹霓晒裂柱.' He says when you see a halo/rainbow you should watch for strong winds and changing weather.

jyutping: ziu1 haa4 jam1, maan5 haa4 cing4
mandarin_meaning: 早晨的霞光預示天氣將轉陰或下雨，傍晚的霞光則預示天氣會放晴。
english_meaning: A traditional weather proverb: a red sunrise (morning glow) often indicates clouds or rain ahead, while a red sunset (evening glow) usually signals fair weather.
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句觀察天象的民間諺語，根據日出日落時雲層與陽光的折射顏色判斷短期天氣變化：朝霞多為西風帶來雲雨，晚霞常代表即將無雲或風向利於放晴。
explanation_english: A folk-weather saying based on how sunlight and clouds interact at sunrise and sunset: red skies in the morning often mean clouds and possible rain are coming, while red skies in the evening usually mean clearer weather ahead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝見到朝霞陰，出門記得帶把遮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 gin3 dou3 ziu1 haa4 jam1, ceot1 mun4 gei3 dak1 daai3 baa2 zoek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今早看到朝霞陰，出門記得帶把雨傘。
examples.english_sentence: This morning I saw a red sunrise (morning glow) and expect rain, so remember to bring an umbrella when going out.

synonyms: 朝霞不出門，晚霞行千里

jyutping: ziu1 sik6 maan5 sai2, maan5 sik6 lou5 syu2 sai2
mandarin_meaning: 早吃晚洗，晚吃就被老鼠吃／比喻拖延處理導致損失
english_meaning: A proverb warning that delaying action (e.g. not cleaning up immediately) invites loss or allows others (or pests) to take advantage
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俗語，用來形容做事拖延、不即時處理，結果可能被人佔便宜或造成損失（比喻後果自負）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb used to describe procrastination or neglecting timely action; if you delay, you risk losing out or having others (or pests) take advantage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日朝食晚洗，做嘢拖拖拉拉，最後就俾人蝕底。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 ziu1 sik6 maan5 sai2, zou6 je5 to1 to1 laai1 laai1, zeoi3 hau6 zau6 bei2 jan4 sik1 dai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你總是朝食晚洗，做事拖拖拉拉，最後就被別人占便宜，吃虧。
examples.english_sentence: You always 'eat in the morning and wash at night' — procrastinating — your work drags on and in the end others take advantage and you lose out.

mandarin_meaning: 朦朦的光 / 朦胧的光，微弱或含糊的光線
english_meaning: a dim, hazy, or faint light; a soft, indistinct glow
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞 / 形容詞（表示光線的狀態）
explanation_mandarin: 「朦朦光」用來形容光線微弱、朦朧或看起來含糊不清的樣子，常用於描述天色、燈光或窗外光線的氛圍。
explanation_english: “朦朦光” describes light that is faint, hazy, or indistinct. It's commonly used to talk about the atmosphere of twilight, dim street lamps, or a soft glow coming through a window.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 天色開始轉黑，街上只係有啲朦朦光，行路要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tin1 sik1 hoi1 ci2 zyun3 hak1, gaai1 soeng6 zi2 hai6 jau5 di1 mung4 mung4 gwong1, haang4 lou6 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 天色开始变黑，街上只有朦朦的光，走路要小心。
examples.english_sentence: The sky was getting dark and there was only a faint, hazy light on the street—be careful walking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 朝早窗外有啲朦朦光，好有詩意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ziu1 sou3 coeng1 ngoi6 jau5 di1 mung4 mung4 gwong1, hou2 jau5 si1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 早上窗外有朦朦的光，很有诗意。
examples.english_sentence: In the morning there's a soft, hazy light outside the window; it's very poetic.

mandarin_meaning: 木頭公仔；比喻呆板、遲鈍或不善言談的人，也可指木製玩偶
english_meaning: wooden doll; figuratively, a person who is stiff, expressionless, slow-witted, or like a puppet
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，字面上指木製的玩偶；引申為形容一個人反應遲鈍、表情僵硬或不會主動說話，亦可帶有諷刺意味。
explanation_english: Colloquial term: literally a wooden doll; used metaphorically to describe someone who is stiff, expressionless, slow to react, or passive—sometimes used mockingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做事好慢，好似一個木头公仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 hou2 maan6, hou2 ci5 jat1 go3 muk6 tau4 gung1 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事很慢，好像一個木頭公仔。
examples.english_sentence: He works very slowly, like a wooden doll.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面試嗰陣，你唔好做個木头公仔，要主動講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 si5 go2 zan6, nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 go3 muk6 tau4 gung1 zai2, jiu3 zyu2 dung6 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面試的時候，你不要做個木頭公仔，要主動說話。
examples.english_sentence: During the interview, don't be a wooden doll; speak up proactively.

jyutping: muk6 gung1 paau4 syu6, zyun1 lei5 bat1 ping4
mandarin_meaning: 木匠刨樹，專門處理不平（比喻替受委屈或不公正的人出頭或平反）
english_meaning: Literal: a carpenter planes a tree, specializing in dealing with unevenness. Figurative: someone who habitually stands up for the wronged or takes it upon themselves to right injustices.
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語以木工刨平樹木的不平處作比喻，表示某人專門為不平之事出面，替受委屈的人說話或平反。亦可含中性或帶有稱讚替人仗義的意味。
explanation_english: This saying uses the image of a carpenter planing away uneven parts of wood to symbolize someone who specializes in addressing grievances — i.e., a person who stands up for the wronged or seeks to right injustices. It can be neutral or praise someone for being principled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到有人受欺負就會出手幫忙，真係木工刨樹，專理不平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 jau5 jan4 sau6 hei1 fu6 zau6 wui5 ceot1 sau2 bong1 mong4, zan1 hai6 muk6 gung1 paau4 syu6, zyun1 lei5 bat1 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到有人受欺負就會出手幫忙，真是木匠刨樹，專門為不平之事出頭。
examples.english_sentence: When he sees someone being bullied he steps in to help — he's really a 'carpenter planes trees, specializes in unfairness' (i.e., he always stands up for the wronged).

mandarin_meaning: 呆住、愣住或像被黏在沙發上一樣動彈不得（廣東話俚語）
english_meaning: to freeze/zone out or be glued to the sofa; to be stunned, motionless or expressionless (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「木梳化」是香港廣東話的口語/俚語，用來形容因為震驚、訝異、無奈或麻木而呆住、動彈不得或面無表情；也可指被某事弄得無力反應，像被黏在梳化（沙發）上。
explanation_english: “木梳化” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang meaning to freeze, go numb, or be glued to the sofa—i.e., to be stunned, motionless, or expressionless because of shock, surprise, helplessness, or numbness. It can describe being unable to react.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到果個消息，當場木梳化，面都冇表情。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 dou2 gwo2 go3 siu1 sik1, dong1 coeng4 muk6 so1 faa3, min6 dou1 mou5 biu2 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他聽到那個消息，當場呆住，面無表情。
examples.english_sentence: He heard the news and froze on the spot, expressionless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我一睇到嗰張相就木梳化，完全唔知點反應。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 tai2 dou3 go2 zoeng1 soeng2 zau6 muk6 so1 faa3, jyun4 cyun4 m4 zi1 dim2 faan2 jing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我一看到那張照片就愣住了，完全不知道怎麼反應。
examples.english_sentence: When I saw that photo I just froze; had no idea how to react.

mandarin_meaning: 木棉花（mù mián huā）
english_meaning: kapok flower; cotton tree flower (Bombax ceiba)
explanation_mandarin: 指木棉树的花，花色常为鲜红或橙红，常见于热带和亚热带地区。在粤语地区和华南一带常见，木棉（又称红棉）为广州等地区的象征之一。传统上木棉的绒毛也曾用作枕芯或填充物。
explanation_english: Refers to the flower of the kapok (cotton) tree, typically bright red or orange-red, common in tropical and subtropical regions. In southern China the kapok (also called red kapok) is a regional symbol (notably Guangzhou). Historically, its fibers were used as stuffing for pillows and cushions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 春天嘅時候，街邊嘅木棉花盛開，整條路都紅晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceon1 tin1 ge3 si4 hau6, gaai1 bin1 ge3 muk6 min4 faa1 sing4 hoi1, zing2 tiu4 lou6 dou1 hung4 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 春天的时候，街边的木棉花盛开，整条路都红了。
examples.english_sentence: In spring, the kapok flowers along the street bloom, turning the whole road red.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊時人會用木棉花嚟做枕芯，因為佢鬆軟又保暖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 si4 jan4 wui5 jung6 muk6 min4 faa1 lai4 zou6 zam2 sam1, jan1 wai6 keoi5 cung1 jyun5 jau6 bou2 nyun5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 过去人们会用木棉花来做枕芯，因为它松软又保暖。
examples.english_sentence: In the past, people used kapok fibers to stuff pillows because they are soft and insulating.

cantonese: 木棉花开透，寒风快快走
jyutping: muk6 min4 faa1 hoi1 tau3, hon4 fung1 faai3 faai3 zau2
mandarin_meaning: 木棉花盛开，寒风赶快离开（意指春天到来，寒冷结束）
english_meaning: The kapok trees are in full bloom, may the cold winds quickly go away (a poetic way to say spring has arrived and the cold is over)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 短語 / 詩句 / 俗語
explanation_mandarin: 這句話字面指木棉花盛開、寒風快走，常用作比喻春天來臨或艱難時期結束，帶有喜悅、盼望轉好的語氣，亦可見於口語或歌詞、詩句中。
explanation_english: Literally describes kapok trees in full bloom and the cold wind leaving; used metaphorically to signal the arrival of spring or the end of hard times. It carries a tone of joy and hopeful change and appears in speech, songs, or poetic lines.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 睇到街邊啲木棉花開透，心情就覺得春天嚟咗，寒風快快走啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tai2 dou3 gaai1bin1 di1 muk6 min4 faa1 hoi1 tau3, sam1 cing4 zau6 gok3 dak1 ceon1 tin1 lai4 zo2, hon4 fung1 faai3 faai3 zau2 laa1
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到街邊的木棉花全開了，我覺得春天來了，寒風快快走吧。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing the kapok trees in full bloom, I feel spring has come — may the cold wind leave quickly.

cantonese: 木棉花开透，筑基兼使牛
jyutping: muk6 min4 faa1 hoi1 tau3, zuk1 gei1 gim1 si2 ngau4
mandarin_meaning: 木棉花開了，開始打好基礎，並動用牛（耕作或勞力）
english_meaning: When the kapok (cotton tree) flowers fully bloom, lay the foundations and put oxen to work; i.e. the season/time is right to start major work.
explanation_mandarin: 此語字面指木棉花盛開時啟動筑基和使用牛力，實際用來表示時機成熟，適合開始大規模建設或從事重體力工作，也可比喻把握良機開始行動。
explanation_english: Literally refers to kapok trees blooming and starting foundation work while putting oxen to work. Figuratively it means the time is ripe to begin major projects or heavy work — seize the opportunity and get started.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家木棉花開透，築基兼使牛，係時候起工喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 muk6 min4 faa1 hoi1 tau3, zuk1 gei1 gim1 si2 ngau4, hai6 si4 hau6 hei2 gung1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在木棉花開了，開始築基並用牛，是時候開工了。
examples.english_sentence: Now the kapok flowers have bloomed and foundations are being laid with oxen working — it's time to get started.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）形容行為嬌柔、軟弱或娘娘腔的男人
english_meaning: (slang) a man who behaves effeminately, timidly, or like a 'sissy'
explanation_mandarin: 「木瓜公」是香港粵語俚語，用來貶義或戲稱某些男人行為嬌柔、缺乏魄力或帶有女性化特徵。有時亦指過度依賴母親或缺乏男子氣概的人。
explanation_english: “Mukgwaagung” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang, used pejoratively or jokingly to describe a man who behaves effeminately, timidly, or lacks backbone. It can also imply someone overly dependent or lacking traditionally masculine traits.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日唔敢做決定，成個木瓜公咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 m4 gam2 zou6 kyut3 ding6, sing4 go3 muk6 gwaa1 gung1 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他常常不敢做決定，完全像個木瓜公一樣。
examples.english_sentence: He often won't make decisions; he's totally like a 'mukgwaagung' (a sissy/timid man).

jyutping: muk6 saau1 gei1, dik1 seoi2 bat1 lau6
mandarin_meaning: 滴水不漏；周密無漏，萬無一失（帶有諷刺或誇張意味）
english_meaning: Watertight; foolproof; extremely thorough and without loopholes (sometimes ironic or exaggerated)
explanation_mandarin: 字面上把本應漏水的木筲箕與『滴水不漏』並列，帶有諷刺或誇張意味，用來形容安排或做事非常周詳、沒有破綻，也可用作戲謔。常與『滴水不漏』同義或用來強調嚴密程度。
explanation_english: Literally pairs a wooden sieve (which should leak) with 'no water drips', creating an ironic or emphatic expression. Used to describe something extremely thorough or airtight with no loopholes; can be complimentary or tongue-in-cheek.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份合約佢審得好仔細，真係木筲箕，滴水不漏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 hap6 joek3 keoi5 sam2 dak1 hou2 zai2 sai3, zan1 hai6 muk6 saau1 gei1, dik1 seoi2 bat1 lau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份合約他審得很仔細，真是滴水不漏。
examples.english_sentence: He reviewed this contract very carefully — it's truly watertight.

mandarin_meaning: 木薯（mùshǔ），又稱樹薯，為一種澱粉質塊根，常用作食材或製作木薯粉／木薯珍珠。
english_meaning: Cassava (tapioca root) — a starchy tuber used as food and to produce tapioca/tapioca pearls.
explanation_mandarin: 木藷（即木薯）是一種熱帶栽培的塊根作物，富含澱粉，可蒸煮食用，或加工成木薯粉、珍珠（粉圓）等食品原料。
explanation_english: Cassava is a starchy tropical tuber eaten cooked or processed into products such as tapioca flour and tapioca pearls.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗啲木藷，打算蒸嚟食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 di1 muk6 syu4, daa2 syun3 zing1 lei4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我買了些木薯，打算蒸來吃。
examples.english_sentence: I bought some cassava and plan to steam it to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 死記硬背的書/溫習資料
english_meaning: books/notes used for rote memorization; rote-learning materials
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱指為應付考試或背誦而機械重複閱讀、沒有理解的書或筆記，帶有貶義，強調死記硬背。
explanation_english: A colloquial, often pejorative term for books or notes used for rote memorization — material read mechanically to cram or recite without real understanding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日淨係睇啲木魚書，讀到連點應用都唔識。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zing6 hai6 tai2 di1 muk6 jyu4 syu1, duk6 dou3 lin6 dim2 jing3 jung6 dou1 m4 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天只看那些木魚書，讀到連如何應用都不會。
examples.english_sentence: He only reads those rote-learning books; he studies so mechanically he doesn't even know how to apply the knowledge.

cantonese: 未到六十六，唔好笑人手指曲
jyutping: mei6 dou3 luk6 sap6 luk6, m4 hou2 siu3 jan4 sau2 zi2 kuk1
mandarin_meaning: 自己還沒到六十六（比喻自己還沒具備資格或沒達到某種程度），不要嘲笑別人的缺點或毛病。
english_meaning: Don't laugh at others' faults when you yourself are not in a position to do so (i.e., you are not qualified or not free of faults).
explanation_mandarin: 這是一句廣東話的俗語，用來提醒人們在自己還不完美或沒資格評論別人之前，不要嘲笑或指責他人的缺點。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb advising people not to mock or judge others' shortcomings when they themselves are not free of faults or not qualified to do so.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你自己啲問題仲多，未到六十六，唔好笑人手指曲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zi6 gei2 di1 man6 tai4 zung6 do1, mei6 dou3 luk6 sap6 luk6, m4 hou2 siu3 jan4 sau2 zi2 kuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你自己的問題還很多，沒資格嘲笑別人的缺點。
examples.english_sentence: You still have many problems yourself; you have no right to mock others' faults.

mandarin_meaning: 還未完全釋放（情緒）或說開／解決
english_meaning: not yet fully vented/expressed or resolved; still unsettled
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示情緒、怨氣或問題還沒有完全發洩、說開或解決，仍然掛在心上。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning emotions, grievances, or issues have not been fully expressed, resolved, or let go; something remains unsettled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今朝同我吵完，仲未大透，大家都唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ziu1 tung4 ngo5 caau3 jyun4, zung6 mei6 daai6 tau3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天早上和我吵完架，還沒徹底把話說開，大家都不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: He argued with me this morning and hasn't fully cleared things up; everyone's uncomfortable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 報告交咗，但心入面啲問題仲未大透，要再查返資料。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou3 gou3 gaau1 zo2, daan6 sam1 jap6 min6 di1 man6 tai4 zung6 mei6 daai6 tau3, jiu3 zoi3 caa4 faan1 zi1 liu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 報告交了，但心裡的問題還沒完全釐清，需要再查資料。
examples.english_sentence: The report's submitted, but some issues in my mind remain unresolved; I need to check the data again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢失戀咗，幾個月都未大透，仲會喺夜晚諗返起佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sat1 lyun2 zo2, gei2 go3 jyut6 dou1 mei6 daai6 tau3, zung6 wui5 hai2 je6 maan5 lam2 faan1 hei2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他失戀了，幾個月都還沒徹底走出來，晚上還會想起對方。
examples.english_sentence: He broke up and for months hasn't fully gotten over it; he still thinks about them at night.

jyutping: mei6 hok6 hang4, sin1 hok6 zau2
mandarin_meaning: 还没学会走就学跑 / 没学会走就想跑
english_meaning: To try to run before one can walk; to get ahead of oneself; to attempt advanced tasks before mastering the basics
explanation_mandarin: 形容做事急於求成，還沒有掌握基礎就想做複雜或進階的事情，或做事太心急、操之過急。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is impatient and tries to do advanced things before mastering the basics; getting ahead of oneself or being overly hasty.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日未學行就先學走，做嘢太心急，結果成日出錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 mei6 hok6 hang4 zau6 sin1 hok6 zau2, zou6 je5 taai3 sam1 gap1, git3 gwo2 sing4 jat6 ceot1 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是还没学会走就想跑，做事太心急，结果总是出错。
examples.english_sentence: He always tries to run before he can walk; he's too impatient at work, and as a result he keeps making mistakes.

jyutping: mei6 gin3 gwo3 daai6 se4 o1 si2
mandarin_meaning: 沒見過世面／沒見過大世面（形容見識淺、經驗少）
english_meaning: haven't seen much of the world; inexperienced (colloquial/vulgar)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面為“沒見過大蛇拉屎”，用來形容一個人沒見過世面、見識淺或經驗不足，語氣通常帶有調侃或粗俗色彩。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "haven't seen a big snake poop." It is used to describe someone as inexperienced or naive (hasn't seen much of the world). The expression is colloquial and somewhat vulgar, often used jokingly or to tease.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係未見過大蛇屙屎，啲小事情都覺得好驚訝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 mei6 gin3 gwo3 daai6 se4 o1 si2, di1 siu2 si6 cing4 dou1 gok3 dak1 hou2 geng1 ngaa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的是沒見過世面，連小事都覺得很驚訝。
examples.english_sentence: He really hasn't seen much of the world; he gets surprised even by small things.

jyutping: mei6 gin3 gun1 fu2 sin1 daa2 saam1 baan2
mandarin_meaning: 還沒等到官府就先自行處罰／處理
english_meaning: To punish or take action before the authorities arrive; to take matters into one's own hands and act preemptively
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，字面意思是「還沒見到官府（官員）就先打三板」，用來形容在官方介入或審理前，當事人或民眾先自行處置、懲罰或草率行動。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally meaning "beat with three boards before the authorities arrive." It describes acting hastily or taking justice into one's own hands—punishing or dealing with a matter before official intervention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 村民發現有人偷糧，未見官府先打三板，自己捉咗人審問。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyun1man4 faat3jin6 jau5jan4 tau1 loeng4, mei6 gin3 gun1 fu2 sin1 daa2 saam1 baan2, zi6gei2 zuk1 zo2 jan4 sam2man6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 村民發現有人偷糧，還沒等官府就先自行處罰，把人抓來審問。
examples.english_sentence: When the villagers discovered someone stealing grain, before the authorities arrived they took matters into their own hands and brought the suspect in for questioning.

jyutping: mei6 gin3 gwo3 daai6 se4 o1 si2
mandarin_meaning: 沒見過世面 / 沒有經歷過大風大浪
english_meaning: haven't seen much of the world; inexperienced; naive
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人沒有見過世面、缺乏經驗或不懂世故，通常帶有嘲諷或戲謔意味。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who is inexperienced or naive—hasn't 'seen the world.' Often used teasingly or mockingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話自己好叻，其實未見過大蛇屙屎，經驗好少。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 hou2 lek1, kei4 sat6 mei6 gin3 gwo3 daai6 se4 o1 si2, ging1 jim6 hou2 siu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說自己很厲害，其實沒見過世面，經驗很少。
examples.english_sentence: He says he's very capable, but actually he hasn't seen much of the world and has very little experience.

cantonese: 未食五月粽，寒衣唔入笼
jyutping: mei6 sik6 ng5 jyut6 zung1, hon4 ji1 m4 jap6 lung4
mandarin_meaning: 端午没到，别把寒衣（冬衣）收起来；比喻不要操之过急或过早放下防备。
english_meaning: Don't put away your winter clothes before the Dragon Boat Festival; metaphorically, don't be premature or let down your guard too soon.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語字面意思是端午節（農曆五月）前不要收起寒衣，因為有可能還會回冷。引申意思是提醒人們不要太心急或過早放鬆警惕、收起準備。
explanation_english: Literally: don't store away cold-weather clothes before the Dragon Boat Festival (fifth lunar month), since cold snaps may still occur. Figuratively: a warning against acting prematurely or letting your guard down too early.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年氣候奇怪，未食五月粽，寒衣唔入笼，唔好咁快收冬衫喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 hei3 hau6 kei4 gwaai3, mei6 sik6 ng5 jyut6 zung1, hon4 ji1 m4 jap6 lung4, m4 hou2 gam2 faai3 sau1 dung1 saam1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年氣候反常，端午沒到，別把寒衣收起來，別那麼快收冬裝。
examples.english_sentence: The weather's been strange this year. Don't put away your winter clothes before the Dragon Boat Festival — don't pack away your winter wear so quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 罕见词语，可能为人名、店名或方言俚语，未见于主流辞典记录。
english_meaning: An obscure or rare term; possibly a personal name, shop name, or local slang with no wide dictionary record.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词（可能的专有名词或俗称）
partOfSpeech_english: noun (possible proper noun or colloquial name)
explanation_mandarin: 「末利花」在粤语语境中并非常见词条，沒有可靠的词典释义记录。根据文字形式，较常作为专有名或招牌名出现；在口语中也可能是地方性俚语或人名的音译。使用时应视为专有名词并根据上下文理解其确切含义。
explanation_english: “末利花” is not a common Cantonese entry and lacks authoritative dictionary definitions. Based on its form it is most likely used as a proper name (e.g., a shop or person) or a localized slang/transliteration. Treat it as a proper noun in context and infer specific meaning from surrounding context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我見到街上有一間叫末利花嘅小店。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gin3 dou2 gaai1 soeng5 jau5 jat1 gaan1 giu3 mut6 lei6 faa1 ge3 siu2 dim3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我看到街上有一家叫“末利花”的小店。
examples.english_sentence: I saw a small shop on the street called "末利花."

mandarin_meaning: 本地人不可小看／本地人有優勢和地緣熟悉度
english_meaning: Don't underestimate the locals; locals have an advantage or know the place well.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容本地人不可小看，因為他們熟悉當地的情況、人際關係或資源，具有優勢。
explanation_english: Used to say a local person should not be underestimated — they have an advantage because they know local conditions, relationships, or resources well.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係本地姜唔辣，地方嘅人情世故佢最識。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 bun2 dei6 goeng1 m4 laat6, dei6 fong1 ge3 jan4 cing4 sai3 gu3 keoi5 zeoi3 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是地道的本地人，別小看他，他最熟悉本地的人情世故。
examples.english_sentence: He's a local — don't underestimate him; he's the most familiar with local customs and ways.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果喺香港做生意，搵本地姜唔辣嘅夥伴會幫到手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 hai6 hoeng1 gong2 zou6 saang1 ji3, wan2 bun2 dei6 goeng1 m4 laat6 ge3 fo2 baan6 wui5 bong1 dou3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果在香港做生意，找懂本地情況的合作夥伴會有幫助。
examples.english_sentence: If you're doing business in Hong Kong, finding partners who know the local situation helps.

mandarin_meaning: 本地狀元（在本地或本校考試／比賽中名列第一的人）
english_meaning: local top scorer / local champion (the person who ranks first in local exams or competitions)
explanation_mandarin: 在香港口語中常用的短語，指在本地（例如本校或本地考試、比賽）名列第一的人。語氣可中性、讚賞，或在戲謔／諷刺語境中使用。
explanation_english: A colloquial Hong Kong phrase referring to someone who achieves first place locally (e.g., in a school or local exam/competition). It can be neutral or complimentary, and sometimes used jokingly or sarcastically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺我哋學校嘅公開考試拎咗第一，真係本地狀元。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ngo5 dei6 hok6 haau6 ge3 gung1 hoi1 haau2 si3 ling1 zo2 dai6 jat1, zan1 hai6 bun2 dei6 zong6 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在我們學校的公開考試拿了第一，真是本地狀元。
examples.english_sentence: He got first place in our school's public exam — truly a local top scorer.

mandarin_meaning: 本地妓女 / 本地賣淫者（貶義）
english_meaning: local prostitute / local hooker (derogatory slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面為「本地的雞」，用來指本地（如香港）從事性交易的女性，或帶有貶義地稱呼被認為有賣淫或行為不檢點的女性。屬冒犯性用語，應謹慎使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term literally meaning "local chicken," used to refer to local (e.g. Hong Kong) women who work as prostitutes, or derogatorily to describe women perceived as engaging in sex work or promiscuous behaviour. It is offensive and should be used with caution.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方喺夜場巡查時捉咗幾個本地雞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 hai2 je6 coeng4 ceon4 caa4 si4 zuk1 zo2 gei2 go3 bun2 dei6 gai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方在夜店巡查時抓了幾個本地妓女。
examples.english_sentence: The police arrested several local prostitutes during a nightclub patrol.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲人用「本地雞」嚟罵香港女性，聽落好侮辱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 jan4 jung6 "bun2 dei6 gai1" lai4 maa6 hoeng1 gong2 neoi5 jan4, teng1 lok6 hou2 mou6 juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些人用「本地妓女」來罵香港女性，聽起來很侮辱。
examples.english_sentence: Some people use 'local prostitute' to insult Hong Kong women; it sounds very insulting.

mandarin_meaning: 術／朮（1. 技術、手段；2. 中藥名：白朮/白術，拼音：báizhú）
english_meaning: 1) skill, technique, art; 2) Bai Zhu (Atractylodes), a traditional Chinese medicinal herb
explanation_mandarin: 「朮」為古字或「術」的異體字，常用於表示技藝、手段或方法；在中藥語境中指白朮（一種常用的中藥材，也寫作白術）。
explanation_english: A variant character of 術 used to mean skill, technique, or method. In medicinal contexts it refers to Bai Zhu (Atractylodes), a commonly used traditional Chinese herb.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗啲白朮去煲湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 di1 baak6 seot6 heoi3 bou1 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我買了些白朮來煲湯。
examples.english_sentence: I bought some Bai Zhu (Atractylodes) to make soup.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅醫朮好高明。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 ji1 seot6 hou2 gou1 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的醫術很高明。
examples.english_sentence: His medical skill is very impressive.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）某人或某事很假、虛偽/是假的
english_meaning: Colloquial dismissal meaning something or someone is fake/phony
explanation_mandarin: 「朱义盛，假嘢」常見於香港口語與網絡用語，用來嘲諷或否定某物或某人為假、虛偽或騙人。當中「朱义盛」多為戲謔性的人名代稱，搭配「假嘢」（假東西／假的）以加強貶義。來源多屬非正式語境或網絡流行語。
explanation_english: “朱义盛，假嘢” is a Hong Kong colloquial/slang expression used to mock or dismiss something as fake or phony. The name “朱义盛” functions as a joking or sarcastic personal label, and paired with “假嘢” (fake thing) emphasizes that the person or thing is not genuine. It is used in informal speech and online contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話嗰個名牌袋係真？朱义盛，假嘢！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 go2 go3 ming4 paai4 doi2 hai6 zan1? zyu1 ji6 sing4, gaa2 je5!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說那個名牌包是真的？完全是假貨！
examples.english_sentence: You say that designer bag is real? Totally fake!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講大話，大家都話佢係朱义盛，假嘢嚟㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 daai6 waa6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 keoi5 hai6 zyu1 ji6 sing4, gaa2 je5 lei4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是說謊，大家都說他很假/是個騙子。
examples.english_sentence: He lies all the time; everyone says he's 'Zhu Yisheng' — a phony.
