examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 gam2 lyun6, ngo5 lam2 laan6 baan2 fong4 jau5 ci3, m4 hou2 caap3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個計劃這麼混亂，我覺得可能有隱患，不要插手。
examples.english_sentence: This plan is such a mess — I think it's risky; better not get involved.

jyutping: laan6 saa1 dang1, dak1 go3 gaa3
mandarin_meaning: 名不副实/只是个摆设，没有实际用途
english_meaning: Just for show; merely a shell or decoration with no practical use
explanation_mandarin: 用于形容某物或某事只有外表或形式，实际上没有用处或没有价值，等同“华而不实”或“只是摆设”。
explanation_english: Used to describe something that is only for appearance or form and has no real use or value — equivalent to 'all show and no substance' or 'just for decoration'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個項目只係爛紗燈，得個架，冇實際用途。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hong6 muk6 zi2 hai6 laan6 saa1 dang1, dak1 go3 gaa3, mou5 sat6 zai3 jung6 tou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个项目只是个摆设，名不副实，没有实际用途。
examples.english_sentence: This project is just for show — all appearance and no practical use.

mandarin_meaning: 软弱或有破绽的人/事容易被欺负或利用
english_meaning: Literally 'rotten meat gets more pokes' — the weak or flawed attract more trouble or get picked on
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「爛肉會被多碰」，比喻軟弱、有缺陷或示弱的人/事容易招來欺負、針對或利用。
explanation_english: Literally 'rotten meat gets more poked.' Figuratively it means that those who are weak, vulnerable, or have flaws attract more trouble, exploitation, or bullying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日示弱，畀人見到就爛肉多碰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 si6 joek6, bei2 jan4 gin3 dou3 zau6 laan6 juk6 do1 pung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要总是示弱，被人看到就会招来更多欺负。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always show weakness; if people see that, you'll attract more trouble/be picked on.

jyutping: laan6 syun4 dou1 jau5 saam1 gan1 ding1
mandarin_meaning: 再破的船也有值得称道的地方；再差的东西也有优点
english_meaning: Even a rotten boat has three pounds of nails — even something or someone seemingly worthless has some redeeming quality.
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語諺語用來表示即使看似破爛或沒用的東西或人，也可能有可取之處或價值，常用來為人辯護或提醒別人不要完全否定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb meaning that even things or people that appear shabby or worthless can have some value or merit; used to defend someone or to remind others not to dismiss something completely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好睇少佢，烂船都有三斤钉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 tai2 siu2 keoi5, laan6 syun4 dou1 jau5 saam1 gan1 ding1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別小看他，再破的船也有三斤釘（意思是再差的東西也有優點）。
examples.english_sentence: Don't underestimate him — even a rotten boat has three pounds of nails (meaning even something poor has its merits).

mandarin_meaning: 破烂不堪；衣衫褴褛或状况很糟（形容人或事物很狼狈、凌乱）
english_meaning: in tatters; shabby or in a terrible/messy state (describing a person or situation looking battered, ragged, or chaotic)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，形容人衣著破爛、外表狼狽或事情、地方非常混亂、糟糕。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing someone or something that is shabby, in tatters, or in a very messy/bad condition; can refer to a person's battered appearance or a chaotic situation/place.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日返工俾人打，成個人烂身烂势，行得都唔穩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 faan1 gung1 bei2 jan4 daa2, sing4 go3 jan4 laan6 san1 laan6 sai3, haang4 dak1 dou1 m4 wan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天上班被人打，整個人烂身烂势，走路都不穩。
examples.english_sentence: He got beaten at work today; he's all battered and ragged and can't even walk steadily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企搞到烂身烂势，成堆嘢無收拾，真係好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 gaau2 dou3 laan6 san1 laan6 sai3, sing4 deoi1 je5 mou5 sau1 sap1, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡弄得烂身烂势，堆滿了東西沒整理，真讓人頭痛。
examples.english_sentence: The house is a mess — everything's piled up and not tidied; it's really annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 乌天黑地（wū tiān hēi dì）：形容非常黑暗，也可比喻情況陰暗或混亂
english_meaning: Pitch-black; extremely dark. Can also be used figuratively for a chaotic or ominous situation.
explanation_mandarin: 「烏天黑地」原指天與地一片漆黑，常用來形容夜色極暗；引申可形容局勢或環境陰暗、混亂、不清楚。
explanation_english: Originally describes the sky and ground being completely dark; commonly used to say it's very dark at night. Figuratively, it can describe a bleak, chaotic, or murky situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚真係烏天黑地，啲街燈又冇開，出街要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 zan1 hai6 wu1 tin1 hak1 dei6, di1 gaai1 dang1 jau6 mou5 hoi1, ceot1 gaai1 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚真是乌天黑地，路灯也没开，出门要小心。
examples.english_sentence: It's really pitch-black tonight; the streetlights aren't on, be careful going out.

mandarin_meaning: （罕用/疑為誤寫）可能是「無忌」的誤寫，字面上「烏」為黑或烏者，「忌」為忌諱；整體並非常用詞
english_meaning: (rare/likely a misspelling) possibly a misspelling of '無忌' (without inhibition); literally 'black' + 'taboo', but not an established term
explanation_mandarin: 「烏忌」並非標準或常見的廣東話詞彙，更多情況下可能是把「無忌」（不顧忌、無所顧忌）誤寫或誤聽。字面可拆為「烏」（黑、烏）與「忌」（忌諱），但沒有固定慣用義。
explanation_english: Not a standard or commonly used Cantonese word. It is likely a misspelling or mishearing of '無忌' (meaning 'without inhibition' or 'unconcerned about taboos'). Literally the characters read 'black' + 'taboo' but there is no established usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺網上見到一個詞叫做「烏忌」，好似係寫錯咗嘅「無忌」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 mong5soeng6 gin3dou2 jat1go3 ci4 giu3zou6 "wu1 gei3", hou2ci5 hai6 se2 co3 zo2 ge3 "mou4 gei3".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在網上看到一個詞叫做「烏忌」，好像是寫錯了的「無忌」。
examples.english_sentence: I saw a word '烏忌' online; it seems to be a misspelling of '無忌'.

mandarin_meaning: 一團糟；亂七八糟；非常混亂或骯髒
english_meaning: a mess; in utter disorder; chaotic; messed up
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，形容事物或場面很凌亂、混亂或被搞砸了，類似「一團糟」「亂七八糟」。常用於抱怨房間、文件或安排很亂。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing something messy, chaotic, or screwed up. Similar to "a mess" or "in shambles," often used to complain about disorderly rooms, documents, or plans.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好整到間房咁烏糟啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing2 dou3 gaan1 fong2 gam2 wu1 zou1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別把房間弄得這麼亂！
examples.english_sentence: Don't make the room such a mess!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲文件搞到一鑊烏糟，依家搵唔到份合約。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 man4 gin2 gaau2 dou3 jat1 wok6 wu1 zou1, ji1 gaa1 wan2 m4 dou2 fan6 hap6 joek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 文件弄得一塌糊塗，現在找不到那份合約。
examples.english_sentence: The documents are in a complete mess; now I can't find the contract.

mandarin_meaning: 板著臉的人；愛擺臭臉、臉色陰沉的人
english_meaning: a sulky/sullen person; a 'sourpuss' who often wears a gloomy expression
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容一個人臉色陰沉或經常擺臭臉，顯得不高興或悶悶不樂。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term describing someone who often looks sullen or sulky, showing a gloomy or displeased expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都係烏面貓，唔鍾意講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 hai6 wu1 min6 maau1, m4 zung1 ji3 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是擺臭臉，不喜歡說話。
examples.english_sentence: He's always sulking and doesn't like to talk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做烏面貓啦，大家傾下計開心啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: M4 hou2 zou6 wu1 min6 maau1 laa1, daai6 gaa1 king1 haa5 gai2 hoi1 sam1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別擺臭臉了，大家聊聊天開心一點。
examples.english_sentence: Don't sulk — let's chat and be a bit happier.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 初次見面佢有啲烏面貓，但其實好好人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Co1 ci3 gin3 min6 keoi5 jau5 di1 wu1 min6 maau1, daan6 kei4 sat6 hou2 hou2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 初次見面他有點板著臉，但其實人很好。
examples.english_sentence: At first meeting he looked a bit sullen, but he's actually very nice.

mandarin_meaning: 乌骨鸡（鸡的一种，皮肤、肉和骨呈暗色或黑色的家禽，常用于药膳和滋补料理）
english_meaning: silkie (black-boned) chicken — a breed of chicken with dark/black skin, flesh and bones, often used in Chinese medicinal soups and tonic dishes
explanation_mandarin: 烏骨雞是一種家禽，特徵是皮肉及骨頭多呈暗色或黑色，常見於中式藥膳或滋補湯中，因為被視為有補益作用。
explanation_english: A silkie (black-boned) chicken: a poultry breed characterized by dark or black skin, flesh and bones. Commonly used in Chinese medicinal cuisine and nourishing soups because of its perceived tonic properties.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚煲咗一隻烏骨雞，湯好補身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 bou1 zo2 jat1 zek3 wu1 gwat1 gai1, tong1 hou2 bou2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚煲了一只乌骨鸡，汤很补身。
examples.english_sentence: We cooked a silkie chicken tonight; the soup is very nourishing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 市面上賣嘅烏骨雞唔平，但通常用嚟煲藥膳比較抵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si5 min6 soeng6 maai6 ge3 wu1 gwat1 gai1 m4 peng4, daan6 tung1 soeng4 jung6 lai4 bou1 joek6 sim6 bei2 gaau3 dai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市面上卖的乌骨鸡不便宜，但通常用来煲药膳比较划算。
examples.english_sentence: Silkie chickens sold on the market aren't cheap, but they're usually worth buying for medicinal soups.

mandarin_meaning: 一种淡水魚，指鯇（鲩）等鯉科魚類的俗稱，常作食用魚
english_meaning: A freshwater fish (a type of carp, commonly referred to as huan/鲩); used as edible fish
explanation_mandarin: 「烏鯇」是對某些鯉科淡水魚的俗稱（對應字常見為鯇/鲩），在市集或菜場常見，常用作烹飪食材。
explanation_english: “烏鯇” is a colloquial name for certain freshwater carp (corresponding to the character 鯇/鲩). It is commonly sold in markets and used as a food fish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺街市買咗隻烏鯇，今晚蒸嚟食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gaai1 si5 maai5 zo2 zek3 wu1 waan4, gam1 maan5 zing1 lai4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在菜市場買了一條烏鯇，今晚蒸來吃。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a wuhuan (carp) at the market; I'll steam it for dinner tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 一種小型淡水魚，常指泥鰍或類似的底棲魚
english_meaning: a small freshwater fish (commonly refers to loach or similar bottom-dwelling fish)
explanation_mandarin: 烏鱅為廣東話中對某些小型淡水底棲魚的俗稱，常用於市場或鄉村口語，亦可用於烹飪（如煲湯、煎炸）。在不同地區可能指向泥鰍或近似種。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 烏鱅 is a colloquial name for certain small freshwater bottom-dwelling fish, often referring to loaches or similar species. The term is used in markets and rural speech and in cooking (e.g. for soups or frying). The exact species can vary by region.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條河入面有好多烏鱅，細路最鍾意捉嚟玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 ho4 jap6 min6 jau5 hou2 do1 wu1 beng1, sai3 lou6 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 zuk1 lai4 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這條河裡有很多烏鱅，孩子們最喜歡抓來玩。
examples.english_sentence: There are many loaches in this river; the kids love catching them to play.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽買咗幾條烏鱅返嚟煲湯，湯味道好鮮甜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 maai5 zo2 gei2 tiu4 wu1 beng1 faan1 lai4 bou1 tong1, tong1 mei6 dou6 hou2 sin1 tim4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽買了幾條烏鱅回來煲湯，湯味道很鮮甜。
examples.english_sentence: Mom bought a few loaches to make soup; the soup tasted very fresh and sweet.

mandarin_meaning: 漆黑、非常黑暗
english_meaning: very dark; pitch-black; blackish
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容顏色或環境非常黑暗、暗沉，看不清楚的樣子。
explanation_english: Describes something that is very dark or pitch-black, often implying poor visibility or a dingy black appearance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚個街道烏黢黢，乜都睇唔清。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 go3 gaai1 dou6 wu1 keoi1 keoi1, mat1 dou1 tai2 m4 cing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚上那條街黑漆漆的，什麼都看不清楚。
examples.english_sentence: The street was pitch-dark at night; you couldn't see anything clearly.

mandarin_meaning: 熱烘烘／暖烘烘（表示溫暖、剛出爐或悶熱的狀態）
english_meaning: warm; hot (often freshly baked/steamed) or warm and stuffy/muggy
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容東西剛出爐、還很溫暖，或形容環境悶熱、溫暖的感覺。例如麵包烘烘的表示剛出爐很暖；房間烘烘的表示悶熱。
explanation_english: Used to describe something that is warm (often just baked or steamed) or to describe a warm, stuffy atmosphere. For example, a bread can be 'hung1hung1' when it's freshly baked; a room can be 'hung1hung1' when it's muggy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個麵包仲烘烘㗎，好香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 min6baau1 zung6 hung1hung1 gaa3, hou2 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個麵包還熱烘烘的，很香。
examples.english_sentence: This bread is still warm and smells great.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日好焗，間屋好烘烘，開吓窗啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1jat6 hou2 guk6, gaan1 uk1 hou2 hung1hung1, hoi1 haa5 coeng1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天很悶，房間很熱烘烘，開開窗吧。
examples.english_sentence: It's stuffy today; the room is hot and muggy—open a window.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲餃子剛蒸好，仲烘烘㗎！
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 gaau2zi2 gong1 zeng1 hou2, zung6 hung1hung1 gaa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餃子剛蒸好，還熱乎乎的！
examples.english_sentence: The dumplings were just steamed; they're still piping hot!

cantonese: 烟通老鼠，人家发火就走
jyutping: jin1 tung1 lou5 syu2, jan4 gaa1 faat3 fo2 zau6 zau2
mandarin_meaning: 形容挑起事端或煽動別人，但一遇到麻煩或危險就逃走、撇清責任的人。
english_meaning: Describes someone who instigates trouble or encourages others to take risks but abandons them and runs away when things go wrong.
explanation_mandarin: 這句話用老鼠遇到火就跑的比喻，批評那些愛挑事、煽動別人但在事情惡化時立刻逃避責任的人。
explanation_english: The phrase uses the image of a mouse fleeing when a fire starts to criticize people who stir up trouble or egg others on, yet shirk responsibility and run when trouble arises.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日煽動人搞事，自己一有危險就走，真係煙通老鼠，人家發火就走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 sin1 dung6 jan4 gaau2 si6, zi6 gei2 jat1 jau5 ngai4 him2 zau6 zau2, zan1 hai6 jin1 tung1 lou5 syu2, jan4 gaa1 faat3 fo2 zau6 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是煽動別人鬧事，自己一有危險就跑，真是挑事卻落荒而逃的人。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps stirring people up to cause trouble, but when danger appears he runs away — truly an instigator who abandons others when things get serious.

mandarin_meaning: 留着旧情人/备胎（保留后路）
english_meaning: To keep someone as a backup (in a romantic context); to maintain an old relationship while starting a new one
explanation_mandarin: 俚语，字面为“烧（点）冷灶”，引申为在发展新感情的同时保留旧情人或将某人当作备胎、留后路。
explanation_english: Slang literally meaning 'to light a cold stove.' Figuratively it means to keep an ex or another romantic option on the back burner while pursuing a new relationship — i.e., to treat someone as a backup.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家同個新歡拍得好好，但其實仲燒緊冷灶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 tung4 go3 san1 fun1 paak3 dak1 hou2 hou2, daan6 kei4 sat6 zung6 siu1 gan2 laang5 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在和新欢相处得很好，但其实还在留着旧情人做备胎。
examples.english_sentence: He's getting along well with his new partner, but actually he's still keeping his ex as a backup.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再燒冷灶，對大家都唔公平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 siu1 laang5 zou6, deoi3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 gung1 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别再当备胎了，对大家都不公平。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep someone as a backup anymore; it's unfair to everyone.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）炒作、作秀，用誇張或刻意的舉動吸引他人注意
english_meaning: to put on a show; to stage a stunt or show off in order to attract attention
explanation_mandarin: 「烧台炮」是廣東話的俗語，指透過誇張或刻意的行為、表演或宣傳來吸引公眾或媒體的注意，相當於「作秀」或「炒作」。多用於批評公關、網紅或公眾人物刻意博取曝光的行為。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term meaning to stage a show or publicity stunt—behaving ostentatiously or provocatively to attract public or media attention. Often used to criticize PR moves, influencers, or public figures who seek exposure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲網紅成日喺度燒台炮，淨係為咗搏版面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 mong5 hung4 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 siu1 toi4 paau3, zing6 hai6 wai6 zo2 bok3 baan2 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些网红老是在那儿作秀，只是为了博取版面。
examples.english_sentence: Those influencers are always putting on a show just to get publicity.

jyutping: siu1 waai6 ngaa5, m4 jap6 dap6
mandarin_meaning: 坏到无法使用或无法修复（为“无法挽回”的俗语或口语表述）
english_meaning: Ruined or damaged beyond use/repair; beyond redemption (colloquial expression implying it's too late to fix).
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語/俗語（短語/成語用法）
explanation_mandarin: 用来形容物品或事情被破坏得无法使用或无法修复，带有“无法挽回、只好放弃或重新开始”的含义。
explanation_english: Used to describe something that has been damaged beyond use or repair, implying irreversibility and that one must give up or start over.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰件陶瓷喺燒製嘅時候失火，燒坏瓦，唔入沓，唯有重做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gin6 tou4ci4 hai2 siu1 zai3 ge3 si4hau6 sat1 fo2, siu1 waai6 ngaa5, m4 jap6 dap6, wai4 jau5 cung4 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那件陶瓷在烧制时失火，已经烧坏了，无法使用，只好重做。
examples.english_sentence: That ceramic piece caught fire during firing and was ruined — it's beyond use, so we have to redo it.

jyutping: siu1 seoi2 tong3 ngau4, wan2 gung1 zou6
mandarin_meaning: 閒着沒事做、做些無聊或無意義的事；（帶有責備語氣）叫人趕快去找份正經工作
english_meaning: idly doing trivial or pointless tasks; (pejorative) telling someone to go and find a real job
explanation_mandarin: 這句話常用於廣東話口語，帶有責備或不耐煩的語氣，意思是對方在浪費時間做無關緊要的事，或應該去找份正經工作。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to scold or mock someone for wasting time on trivial tasks; it suggests they should go and get a proper job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日喺度烧水劏牛，唔好淨係噉，快啲揾工做啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 siu1 seoi2 tong3 ngau4, m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 gam2, faai3 di1 wan2 gung1 zou6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你整天在那裡做些無聊的事，別只是這樣，快去找份工作吧。
examples.english_sentence: You're always doing trivial things there; don't just keep doing that, go find a job quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 別吵了；不用再爭論（別再爭執）
english_meaning: Don't argue / No need to make a fuss
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，用來制止爭吵或表示不想再討論某事，相當於「別吵了、不用爭論」。常用於叫人不要再爭執或別再插手無謂的爭論。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to tell people to stop arguing or fussing; similar to "don't argue" or "it's not worth arguing about." Often used to shut down or de‑escalate petty disputes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你哋唔好再講啦，烧猪耳，免炒！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 laa1, siu1 zyu1 ji5, min5 caau2!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你們別再說了，別吵了！
examples.english_sentence: You guys stop talking — don't argue!

cantonese: 热天热大众，冷天冷穷人
jyutping: jit6 tin1 jit6 daai6 zung3, laang5 tin1 laang5 kung4 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 好時候大多數人受益，困難時候窮人受苦（俗語）
english_meaning: When times are good most people benefit; when times are bad, the poor suffer.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用天氣的冷熱作比喻，表示在景氣或順境時，多數人都能得到好處；而在不景氣或困難時，窮人受到的影響和痛苦會更大。
explanation_english: This proverb uses hot and cold weather as a metaphor: in good times most people enjoy benefits, but in hard times the poor are the ones who suffer most.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家經濟好，真係熱天熱大眾；一旦衰退，就先至見到冷天冷窮人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 ging1 zai3 hou2, zan1 hai6 jit6 tin1 jit6 daai6 zung3; jat1 daan6 seoi1 teoi3, zau6 sin1 zi3 gin3 dou2 laang5 tin1 laang5 kung4 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在經濟好，真是「熱天熱大眾」；一旦衰退，才會看到「冷天冷窮人」。
examples.english_sentence: With the economy doing well now, it really fits 'when times are good most benefit'; once it declines you'll see 'when times are bad the poor suffer.'

synonyms: 好時大家受惠，難時窮人受苦
景氣時人人有份，蕭條時窮人更受影響

mandarin_meaning: 只在热闹、流行的时候感兴趣，过了热潮就不再关注（趋炎附势、见风使舵）
english_meaning: Only interested when something is popular; fair‑weather support or trend‑chasing — people who flock to what's hot and abandon it when it's cold
explanation_mandarin: 俗语，形容人对事物的兴趣随流行与否而变化：热的时候追捧，冷落的时候就撤离或不理会。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing people who show interest or support only when something is popular; they follow trends and lose interest when the fad fades.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家啲人好热饥冷饱，啲嘢一热就有人捧，唔红就即刻冇晒人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 di1 jan4 hou2 jit6 gei1 laang5 baau2, di1 je5 jat1 jit6 zau6 jau5 jan4 pung2, m4 hung4 zau6 zik1 hak1 mou5 saai3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在这些人很见风使舵，东西一火就有人追捧，不火了就马上没人了。
examples.english_sentence: People nowadays are fair‑weather — when something's trending everyone jumps on it, but once it cools off there's nobody left.

mandarin_meaning: 焖（mèn）；用小火慢煮、炖
english_meaning: to simmer; to stew; to braise slowly over low heat
explanation_mandarin: 「焅」為較少見或古字，用作「焖」的異體或近義字，指用小火或蓋上悶煮，使食材入味、軟嫩。
explanation_english: A rare/archaic form often treated as a variant of 焖 (to simmer). It means to cook slowly over low heat (stew/braise) so ingredients become tender and absorb flavor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢煲牛腩要焅足兩個鐘先入味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou1 ngau4 naam5 jiu3 mun4 zuk1 loeng5 go3 zung1 sin1 jap6 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这锅牛腩要焖足两个钟才入味。
examples.english_sentence: This pot of beef brisket needs to simmer for two hours to absorb the flavor.

mandarin_meaning: 烤翅、烤雞翅
english_meaning: baked/roasted (chicken) wings
explanation_mandarin: 指以焗、烤等方法烹調的翅類（通常指雞翅），常見於餐廳或小吃中。
explanation_english: Refers to wings (usually chicken wings) prepared by baking or roasting; a common dish served in restaurants or as a snack.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚食唔食焗翅呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 sik6 m4 sik6 guk6 ci3 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚吃不吃烤翅？
examples.english_sentence: Are we having baked wings tonight?

mandarin_meaning: 用熱悶或烘烤使熟（如焗飯）；也可指悶熱、感到悶焗
english_meaning: to bake or cook by enclosed heat (e.g. baked rice); also to feel stuffy/overheated
explanation_mandarin: 「焗」在粵語中常指用爐火或熱氣悶烤食物（如焗飯、焗魚等），另有口語用法指天氣或室內悶熱、不透氣，使人感到不舒服。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 焗 primarily means to bake or cook food with enclosed heat (e.g. baked dishes). Colloquially it also describes feeling stuffy or overheated in a place.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個焗飯好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 guk6 faan6 hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个焗饭很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: This baked rice is delicious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺間屋咁焗，我想開冷氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gaan1 uk1 gam2 guk6, ngo5 soeng2 hoi1 laang5 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在家里这么闷热，我想开空调。
examples.english_sentence: It's so stuffy at home; I want to turn on the AC.

synonyms: 悶 (mun6) - 悶熱、不透氣（口語）

mandarin_meaning: 感到悶熱、悶倦或悶悶不樂，像被悶住或無聊發悶
english_meaning: to feel stifled, stuffy, bored or pent-up; feeling oppressed by heat or confinement
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示因為天氣悶熱、空氣不流通或被限制在某處而感到不舒服、煩悶或無聊。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to feel stifled or bored — typically from heat, poor ventilation, or confinement; can describe physical stuffiness or mental boredom.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日咁焗悶，我想開窗透下氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 gam2 guk6 mun6, ngo5 soeng2 hoi1 coeng1 tau3 haa5 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天这么闷，我想开窗透透气。
examples.english_sentence: It's so stuffy today; I want to open a window to get some air.

mandarin_meaning: 悶熱
english_meaning: hot and stuffy; muggy; sultry
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容天氣或室內環境又悶又熱、缺乏通風，令人感到不舒服或窒息。
explanation_english: Describes weather or an indoor environment that is hot and stuffy (muggy), lacking ventilation and causing discomfort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日好焗熱，唔開冷氣真係頂唔順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 hou2 guk6 jit6, m4 hoi1 laang5 hei3 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天很悶熱，不開冷氣真的受不了。
examples.english_sentence: It's really muggy today; without the AC I can't stand it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果屋企冇風，室內好快會焗熱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 uk1 kei5 mou5 fung1, sat1 noi6 hou2 faai3 wui5 guk6 jit6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果家裡沒風，室內很快會悶熱。
examples.english_sentence: If there's no breeze at home, the room will quickly become stuffy and hot.

mandarin_meaning: 烤箱；（比喻）悶熱的地方或天氣
english_meaning: oven; (figurative) a very hot, stuffy place or weather like being in an oven
explanation_mandarin: 指用來烘烤食物的烤箱。引申為形容天氣或室內非常悶熱，好像置身於烤箱之中。
explanation_english: Refers to an oven used for baking. Figuratively used to describe very hot, stuffy weather or an indoor environment as if being inside an oven.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企買咗個新焗爐，可以整披薩同烤麵包。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 maai5 zo2 go3 san1 guk6 lou4, ho2 ji5 zing2 pei1 saat3 tung4 haau1 min6 baau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我家買了個新烤箱，可以用來做披薩和烤麵包。
examples.english_sentence: We bought a new oven at home — we can make pizza and bake bread.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日真係好焗，出街行幾步就流汗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 hou2 guk6, ceot1 gaai1 haang4 gei2 bou6 zau6 lau4 hon4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天真的很悶熱，出門走幾步就流汗。
examples.english_sentence: It's really muggy today — you start sweating after walking a few steps outside.

mandarin_meaning: 把食物放入有蓋的小盅內焗或燜的烹飪方法；用此方法製作的菜式
english_meaning: A cooking method (or dish) in which food is placed in a small lidded cup/bowl and baked/slow-cooked/steamed; the dish prepared that way
explanation_mandarin: 「焗盅」在粵語烹飪語境中指把材料放進有蓋的小盅內焗、燜或以微火烹調的做法，也可指以此法製成的單份菜或甜品（例如焗蛋盅）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese cooking, 'guk zung' refers to placing ingredients in a small lidded cup or bowl and baking/slow-cooking/steaming them; it also refers to the single-portion dish made this way (e.g. baked egg cup).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅焗盅好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 guk6 zung1 hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间餐厅的焗盅很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: The baked-cup dish at this restaurant is very tasty.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見俚語）可能指「無後」或「無後路」，即沒有後代或沒有後援/後路（來源不詳，屬口語、戲謔用法）
english_meaning: (rare slang) likely refers to 'no descendants' or 'no backup/no way out' — a jocular or colloquial expression; origin uncertain and usage is informal
explanation_mandarin: 「無后螺」在香港粵語中屬罕見或非標準的口語/俚語，字面上可拆作「無後」+「螺」，實際使用時多為戲謔或誇張說法，用來形容某人可能沒有後代，或比喻沒有後援、沒有後路。此詞來源不明，並非正式詞彙。
explanation_english: This term is a rare or nonstandard Cantonese slang. Literally composed of 'no descendants' plus 'snail/conch', it is typically used jokingly or hyperbolically to describe someone as having no offspring or, figuratively, having no backing/no way out. The origin is unclear and it is informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日咁亂嚟，唔小心將來可能真係無后螺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 gam2 lyun6 lai4, m4 siu2 sam1 zoeng1 loi4 ho2 nang4 zan1 hai6 mou4 hau6 lo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你總是這樣亂來，不小心將來可能真的會沒有後代（或沒有後援）。
examples.english_sentence: If you keep behaving recklessly like this, you might actually end up with no descendants (or no backup) in the future.

mandarin_meaning: 沒有結果 / 沒有結尾（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: having no conclusion or result; left unresolved (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「無尾羸」是香港粵語口語俚語，用來形容一件事或一個經過沒有結局、沒有交代或無法收尾，常帶有失望或無奈的語氣。屬於非正式用語，地區性較強。
explanation_english: “無尾羸” is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang expression used to describe something that ends without a conclusion or result — left hanging or unresolved. It usually conveys disappointment or frustration and is informal/regional.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋開會講咗幾次，最後竟然無尾羸，乜都冇決定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hoi1 wui6 gong2 zo2 gei2 ci3, zeoi6 hau6 ging2 jin4 mou4 mei5 leoi4, mat1 dou1 mou5 kyut3 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们开了几次会，最后竟然没有结果（無尾羸），什么都没决定。
examples.english_sentence: They held several meetings, and in the end it had no conclusion (was left unresolved); nothing was decided.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個工程做咗半年，突然無尾羸，全部功夫白費晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 gung1 cing4 zou6 zo2 bun3 nin4, dak6 jin4 mou4 mei5 leoi4, cyun4 bou6 gung1 fu1 baak6 fai3 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 工程做了半年，突然沒有結果（無尾羸），全部努力白費了。
examples.english_sentence: The project ran for half a year, then suddenly ended with no result (left unresolved), and all the effort was wasted.

mandarin_meaning: 不会输/必胜/没有输的可能
english_meaning: can't lose; a no-lose situation; guaranteed to win
explanation_mandarin: 表示某件事没有失败或输的可能，常用于非正式语境，带有自信或夸张的语气。
explanation_english: Expresses that there is no possibility of losing or failing; used informally, often with a confident or exaggerated tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋一齊做呢個計劃，基本上無得輸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 zou6 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6, gei1 bun2 soeng6 mou4 dak1 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们一起做这个计划，基本上不会输。
examples.english_sentence: If we do this plan together, it's basically a no-lose situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今場波佢哋有兩個王牌，真係無得輸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 coeng4 bou1 keoi5 dei6 jau5 loeng5 go3 wong4 paai4, zan1 hai6 mou4 dak1 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这场球赛他们有两张王牌，真的不会输。
examples.english_sentence: They've got two aces this match — they really can't lose.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次減價又送禮物，呢檔生意真係無得輸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 gaam2 gaa3 jau6 sung3 lai5 mat6, ni1 dong6 saang1 ji3 zan1 hai6 mou4 dak1 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次降价又送礼物，这笔生意真的不会亏。
examples.english_sentence: With the discounts and freebies this time, this deal is guaranteed — no way to lose.

mandarin_meaning: 无意中装载／无意中承担（可指上传文件或承担责任/负担）
english_meaning: to load/upload unintentionally; to unintentionally take on a burden/responsibility
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語/俚語，字面意思為「無心地裝載」。常用於描述不小心上傳檔案、載入資料，或比喻無意中承擔責任或負擔。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase literally meaning "unintentionally load." It is used to describe accidentally uploading files or loading data, and metaphorically to describe unintentionally taking on responsibilities or burdens.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔小心按錯，結果無心裝載咗啲檔案上去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 on3 co3, git3 gwo2 mou4 sam1 zong1 zoi6 zo2 di1 dong2 on6 soeng5 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不小心按错，结果无心上传了些文件。
examples.english_sentence: I accidentally clicked and ended up unintentionally uploading some files.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日幫人做嘢，久而久之無心裝載咗太多家務。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 bong1 jan4 zou6 je5, gau2 ji4 gau2 zi1 mou4 sam1 zong1 zoi6 zo2 taai3 do1 gaa1 mou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常帮别人做事，久而久之无意中承担了太多家务。
examples.english_sentence: He always helps others, and over time he unintentionally took on too many household chores.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個程式有錯，會令用戶無心裝載錯誤嘅資料。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 cing4 sik1 jau5 co3 ng6, wui5 ling6 jung6 wu6 mou4 sam1 zong1 zoi6 co3 ng6 ge3 zi1 liu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个程序有错误，会让用户无意中加载错误的数据。
examples.english_sentence: The program has a bug that can cause users to unintentionally load incorrect data.

mandarin_meaning: 平淡乏味、没有吸引力
english_meaning: insipid; dull; uninteresting; bland
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容事物很普通、沒特色或沒有吸引力，讓人覺得無聊、沒有意思。
explanation_english: Used to describe something ordinary, lacking distinctive features or appeal; makes people feel bored or uninterested.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部電影真係無聞無味，完全唔吸引。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 din6 jing2 zan1 hai6 mou4 man4 mou4 mei6, jyun4 cyun4 m4 kap1 jan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部电影真的很平淡乏味，完全没有吸引力。
examples.english_sentence: This movie is really dull and uninteresting; not appealing at all.

mandarin_meaning: （口语）不可能；没门；绝对不会
english_meaning: No way; impossible; absolutely not (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「無萬」为粤语中较罕见或非标准的口语/俚语表达，用作感叹或否定，表示「不可能」「没门」「绝对不会」。有时可能是「冇門/冇可能」的变体或笔误，并非正式书面用语，使用时带有强烈否定语气。
explanation_english: A rare/nonstandard Cantonese colloquial interjection used to express strong negation — "no way", "impossible", or "absolutely not." It may be a variant or typo of expressions like "冇門" or "冇可能" and is not common in formal usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話佢買到樓？無萬啦，你信佢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 keoi5 maai5 dou2 lau4? mou4 maan6 laa1, nei5 seon3 keoi5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说他买到房子？没可能啦，你信他？
examples.english_sentence: He says he bought a flat? No way — do you believe him?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話今晚會還晒錢？無萬㗎！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 gam1 maan5 wui5 waan4 saai3 cin2? mou4 maan6 gaa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说今晚会把钱都还？不可能啊！
examples.english_sentence: He says he'll pay all the money back tonight? No way!

mandarin_meaning: 沒有本事；沒有技術或辦法
english_meaning: no skill; inept; lacking ability or means
explanation_mandarin: 口語用來形容一個人沒有能力或技術，做事常常出錯或無法解決問題。
explanation_english: Colloquial term used to describe someone who lacks ability or skill, often makes mistakes, or cannot handle problems.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢無術，做嘢成日出錯，唔可靠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou4 seot6, zou6 je5 sing4 jat6 ceot1 co3, m4 ho2 kaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他沒本事，做事老是出錯，不可靠。
examples.english_sentence: He has no skill; he always makes mistakes at work and is unreliable.

mandarin_meaning: 没必要 / 不值得（别再做或别为此操心）
english_meaning: not worth it; pointless; don't bother
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用語，表示某事沒必要去做或沒必要為某事煩惱，常用來勸阻別人浪費時間或精力。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning something is unnecessary or pointless; used to discourage someone from wasting time or effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再嗌交啦，真係無謂𪃏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 aai3 gaau1 laa3, zan1 hai6 mou4 wai6 lo1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再吵了，真的沒必要。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep arguing; it's really not worth it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗佢啲小錯而生氣，真係無謂𪃏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 keoi5 di1 siu2 co3 ji4 saang1 hei3, zan1 hai6 mou4 wai6 lo1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了他的那些小錯而生氣，真沒必要。
examples.english_sentence: Getting angry over his small mistakes is really pointless.

mandarin_meaning: 沒有譜 / 不靠譜（不可靠、沒把握、不可預測）
english_meaning: unreliable / unpredictable / outlandish; used as slang to say someone or something is unreasonable or absurd
explanation_mandarin: 「無譜」是廣東話俚語，表示某人或某事沒有規律、沒把握、很不可靠或言行荒謬、不可預測。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang adjective meaning someone or something is without rules/plan — unpredictable, unreliable, unreasonable, or outrageous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次做嘢真係無譜，遲到仲唔講一聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 zou6 je5 zan1 hai6 mou4 pou2, ci4 dou3 zung6 m4 gong2 jat1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這次做事真是沒譜，遲到還不說一聲。
examples.english_sentence: He was really unreliable this time — he was late and didn't even say anything.

mandarin_meaning: 非標準詞彙，可能是誤寫或地區俚語，無確定義項
english_meaning: Not a standard term — likely a misspelling or regional slang with no established meaning
explanation_mandarin: 「無豚螺」並非常見的廣東話詞彙，沒有被廣泛記錄的固定含義。常見情況是誤寫、口語變體或地區性俚語，具體意思需視上下文而定。
explanation_english: “無豚螺” is not a commonly attested Cantonese word and has no established meaning. It is likely a misspelling, a colloquial variant, or a regional slang term — its meaning depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「無豚螺」唔係常用嘅詞，可能係寫錯或係地區俚語。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mou4 tyun4 lo4 m4 hai6 soeng4 jung6 ge3 ci4, ho2 nang4 hai6 se2 co3 waak6 hai6 dei6 keoi1 lei5 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「無豚螺」不是常用詞，可能是寫錯或是地區俚語。
examples.english_sentence: “無豚螺” is not a commonly used term; it might be a misspelling or regional slang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講嘅「無豚螺」係咩意思？我未聽過呢個用法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 ge3 'mou4 tyun4 lo4' hai6 me1 ji3 si6? ngo5 mei6 teng1 gwo3 ni1 go3 jung6 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說的「無豚螺」是什麼意思？我沒聽過這個用法。
examples.english_sentence: What do you mean by “無豚螺”? I haven't heard this usage before.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你想講「無啦啦」或者「莫名其妙」，就唔好用「無豚螺」，因為人可能唔明白。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 soeng2 gong2 'mou4 laa1 laa1' waak6 ze2 'mok6 ming4 kei4 miu6', zau6 m4 hou2 jung6 'mou4 tyun4 lo4', jan4 wai6 jan4 ho2 nang4 m4 ming4 baak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你想說「無啦啦」或「莫名其妙」，就不要用「無豚螺」，因為別人可能不明白。
examples.english_sentence: If you mean “out of the blue” or “for no reason,” don't use “無豚螺” — people might not understand.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）突然 / 忽然 / 無預警
english_meaning: suddenly; out of the blue; without warning (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，表示事情發生得很突然、沒有預兆。常用於口語對話，有時也寫作「無啦啦」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to indicate that something happened abruptly or without warning. Often used in spoken Cantonese and commonly written as "無啦啦".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢無𪐀𪐀冇通知就辭職喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou4 laa1 laa1 mou5 tung1 zi1 zau6 ci4 zik1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然沒通知就辭職了。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly quit without giving any notice.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我無𪐀𪐀收到佢嘅電話，好驚訝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mou4 laa1 laa1 sau1 dou3 keoi5 ge3 din6 waa2, hou2 ging1 ngaa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我突然接到他的電話，很驚訝。
examples.english_sentence: I got his call out of the blue and was surprised.

mandarin_meaning: 立刻、馬上（口語、帶有焦急或緊迫意味）
english_meaning: immediately; right away (colloquial, often with a sense of urgency or anxiety)
explanation_mandarin: 「焦即」為香港粵語口語用法的俗語，常用來表示因為緊張、焦急而迅速、立刻去做某事。語氣比一般「即刻」更帶急切或慌張的感覺。使用上屬非正式情境。
explanation_english: “焦即” is a colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese slang term used to indicate doing something immediately due to anxiety or urgency. It carries a more rushed or panicked tone than the neutral “immediately.” It is informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到爸爸入院嘅消息，焦即去咗醫院。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 dou3 baa4 baa1 jap6 jyun2 ge3 siu1 sik1, ziu1 zik1 heoi3 zo2 ji1 jyun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他聽到爸爸住院的消息，立刻去了醫院。
examples.english_sentence: When he heard his father was hospitalized, he immediately went to the hospital.

mandarin_meaning: 煎堆（炸芝麻球），一種用糯米粉或糯米漿油炸、外面裹芝麻的甜點或小吃
english_meaning: sesame ball (deep-fried glutinous rice ball coated with sesame seeds), a sweet snack/dessert
explanation_mandarin: 煎堆是廣東話常見的小吃，用糯米粉或糯米漿做成球形，油炸後外面裹上白芝麻，內餡常見有蓮蓉或紅豆等。常見於點心、街頭小吃以及節慶場合（如過年）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese/Chinese snack made from glutinous rice flour formed into a ball, deep-fried and coated with sesame seeds. Fillings may include lotus seed paste or sweet red bean. Served as dim sum, street food, or during festivals.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽咪買咗幾個熱騰騰嘅煎堆返嚟畀我食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa1 mi4 maai5 zo2 gei2 go3 jit6 tang4 tang4 ge3 zin1 deoi1 faan1 lai4 bei2 ngo5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽買了幾個熱騰騰的煎堆回來給我吃。
examples.english_sentence: Mom bought a few hot sesame balls and brought them home for me to eat.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）煎得焦了的鯽魚；（口語）比喻事情被弄糟、完全失敗（偶爾的比喻用法）
english_meaning: Literally: a crucian carp pan-fried until burnt. Colloquially/jokingly: something ruined or a complete mess.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞（食物）；亦可作口語比喻用的名詞/形容
explanation_mandarin: 指鯽魚在煎的過程中被煎得焦黑，通常用來描述烹飪失敗。口語中有時會把它用作比喻，形容事情被搞砸或徹底失敗（屬於戲謔或非正式用法）。
explanation_english: Refers to a crucian carp that has been pan-fried until burnt—i.e., an overcooked or ruined dish. Occasionally used colloquially as a humorous metaphor for something being completely messed up or failed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我唔小心煎焦鯽魚，成碟都食唔到啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 zin1 ziu1 zap1 jyu4, sing4 dip6 dou1 sik6 m4 dou2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我不小心把鯽魚煎焦了，整盤都吃不了了。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight I accidentally burned the crucian carp; the whole plate is inedible.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢次考試我準備不足，結果搞到煎焦鯽魚，分數好差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 ci3 haau2 si3 ngo5 zeon2 bei6 bat1 zuk1, git3 gwo2 gaau2 dou3 zin1 ziu1 zap1 jyu4, fan1 sou3 hou2 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次考试我准备不足，结果搞得一团糟，分数很差。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't prepare enough for this exam; it ended up a total mess and my score was very poor.

mandarin_meaning: 忙忙碌碌；忙來忙去
english_meaning: bustling about; being busy with many small tasks; fussing around
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，形容人為瑣碎的事情忙來忙去、奔波或處於忙碌狀態。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is busy fussing around, running about with many small tasks or being in a hectic state.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日煎煎炒炒，忙到冇時間訓覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zin1 zin1 caau2 caau2, mong4 dou3 mou5 si4 gaan3 fan3 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天忙忙碌碌，忙到沒有時間睡覺。
examples.english_sentence: He is busy all the time, so busy he doesn't even have time to sleep.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽喺屋企煎煎炒炒，準備晚飯俾大家。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 hai2 uk1 kei2 zin1 zin1 caau2 caau2, zeon2 bei6 maan5 faan6 bei2 daai6 gaa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽在家忙來忙去，準備晚飯給大家。
examples.english_sentence: Mom is bustling around at home, preparing dinner for everyone.

mandarin_meaning: 煎馅 / 煎制的餡料
english_meaning: pan-fried filling (the stuffing for pan-fried buns/dumplings/pancakes); (verb) to pan-fry the filling
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词 / 动词（视语境而定）
explanation_mandarin: 指經過煎制處理的餡料，常用於煎餃、煎包或各類煎製點心的內餡；亦可作動詞，表示把餡料煎熟或煎製使其入味和定型。
explanation_english: Refers to a filling that has been pan-fried, commonly used as the stuffing for pan-fried dumplings, buns, or pancakes; can also be used as a verb meaning to pan-fry the filling until cooked and flavored.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽整咗啲煎餡，準備今晚包餃子用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 zing2 zo2 di1 zin1 ham6, zeon2 bei6 gam1 maan5 baau1 gaau2 zi2 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈做了些煎馅，准备今晚包饺子用。
examples.english_sentence: Mom made some pan-fried filling to use for tonight's dumplings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲煎餡要即刻食，放耐咗會變硬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 zin1 ham6 jiu3 zik1 haak1 sik6, fong3 noi6 zo2 wui5 bin3 ngaang6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些煎馅要马上吃，放久了会变硬。
examples.english_sentence: These pan-fried fillings should be eaten right away; if left too long they'll become hard.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見/非標準）可能為「煎熬」的誤寫；字面上是烹飪中煎、加鹽的意思。
english_meaning: (rare/non-standard) possibly a misspelling of '煎熬' (to endure hardship); literally 'pan-fry salt' (to fry with salt).
explanation_mandarin: 「煎鹽」在現代粵語口語與書面語中極少見，沒有固定詞義或通行用法。多數情況下它可能是「煎熬」的誤寫或打字錯誤；若按字面解釋，則與烹飪（煎、加鹽）有關。
explanation_english: Not a common Cantonese term. There is no established meaning and it is likely a misspelling or typo of '煎熬' (to suffer/endure). Literally it would refer to frying/seasoning with salt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 好多時候網上見到「煎鹽」，但其實好大機會係打錯字，原本應該係「煎熬」。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hou2 do1 si4 hau6 mong5 seong6 gin3 dou2 'zin1 jim4', daan6 kei4 sat6 hou2 daai6 gei1 wui6 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6, jyun4 bun2 jing1 goi1 hai6 'zin1 ngou4'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 经常在网上看到「煎鹽」，但很可能是错别字，原本应为「煎熬」。
examples.english_sentence: You often see '煎鹽' online, but it's very likely a typo — the original should be '煎熬' (to endure).

mandarin_meaning: 烟缸；盛放烟灰和烟蒂的容器（為粵語口語或俗寫，常與「煙缸」通用）
english_meaning: Ashtray (a container for cigarette ash and butts) — colloquial/variant form used in Cantonese
explanation_mandarin: 「煙杠」為粵語口語或俗寫，指用來盛放煙灰和煙蒂的容器，相當於普通話的「煙缸」或「煙灰缸」。在香港口語中有時會見到「杠」字代替「缸」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term (variant spelling) for an ashtray — a receptacle for cigarette ash and butts. It is often used interchangeably with 煙缸 (yin1 gong1) in casual speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個煙杠放喺門口，唔好亂拋煙頭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 jin1 gong1 fong3 hai2 mun4 hau2, m4 hou2 lyun6 paau1 jin1 tau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 烟缸放在门口，不要乱扔烟头。
examples.english_sentence: The ashtray is at the doorway — don't throw cigarette butts around.

mandarin_meaning: 烟鬼（指抽烟成瘾的人；嗜烟者）
english_meaning: chain smoker; heavy smoker; someone addicted to smoking
explanation_mandarin: 「煙鬼」是粵語口語，通常帶有輕微貶義，用來形容對抽煙成癮、經常吸煙的人。
explanation_english: “煙鬼” is a Cantonese colloquial/slang term (often mildly pejorative) used to describe someone who is addicted to smoking or smokes heavily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個煙鬼，成日要食幾包煙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 jin1 gwai2, sing4 jat6 jiu3 sik6 gei2 baau1 jin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是个烟鬼，每天要抽好几包烟。
examples.english_sentence: He's a chain smoker; he smokes several packs a day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好畀細路見到大人做煙鬼，會影響佢哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bei2 sai3 lou6 gin3 dou2 daai6 jan4 zou6 jin1 gwai2, wui5 jing2 hoeng2 keoi5 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要让小孩看到大人在抽烟，会影响他们。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let children see adults smoking; it sets a bad example.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生話佢係個煙鬼，要戒煙，唔係對身體好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 waa6 keoi5 hai6 go3 jin1 gwai2, jiu3 gaai3 jin1, m4 hai6 deoi3 san1 tai2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 医生说他是个烟民，要戒烟，否则对身体不好。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor said he's a smoker and needs to quit; otherwise it's bad for his health.

mandarin_meaning: 制止、停止、抑制（相当于“制止/抑制/压制”）
english_meaning: to stop; to halt; to restrain; to suppress
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示使某事停止、限制或抑制某種行為或情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to stop, limit, or restrain an action or situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府煞制咗嗰個計劃，話唔夠資金。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 saat3 zai3 zo2 go2 go3 gai3 waak6, waa6 m4 gau3 zi1 gam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府制止了/停止了那个计划，说是资金不足。
examples.english_sentence: The government halted the project, saying there wasn't enough funding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司出咗通知，要煞制員工加班。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ceot1 zo2 tung1 zi1, jiu3 saat3 zai3 jyun4 gung1 gaa1 baan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司发出通知，要限制/停止员工加班。
examples.english_sentence: The company issued a notice to stop employees from working overtime.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘗試煞制自己唔好發脾氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng4 si3 saat3 zai3 zi6 gei2 m4 hou2 faat3 pei4 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他试图控制自己不要发脾气。
examples.english_sentence: He tried to restrain himself from losing his temper.

mandarin_meaning: 煞气（凶狠、威胁的气势；有时指不吉利或令人不舒服的气氛）
english_meaning: a menacing or aggressive aura; fierce/hostile look; ominous or intimidating vibe
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，指某人或某物散發出凶狠、具威脅性或不友善的氣勢；也可用來形容場所或氛圍顯得不吉利或讓人不舒服。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term describing someone or something that gives off a fierce, threatening, or unfriendly vibe; can also describe a place or atmosphere that feels ominous or unlucky.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一出場就好有煞氣，令到對手都驚縮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 ceot1 coeng4 zau6 hou2 jau5 saat3 hei3, ling6 dou3 deoi3 sau2 dou1 ging1 suk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一出場就很有煞氣，讓對手都嚇得退縮。
examples.english_sentence: He gave off such a menacing aura as soon as he appeared that his opponents were intimidated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間屋有啲煞氣，好似唔太吉利。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 uk1 jau5 di1 saat3 hei3, hou2 ci5 m4 taai3 gat1 lei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間屋有點煞氣，好像不太吉利。
examples.english_sentence: This house feels a bit ominous, like it's not very lucky.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂挑佢，佢而家好煞氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 tiu1 keoi5, keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hou2 saat3 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別亂惹他，他現在很有煞氣。
examples.english_sentence: Don't provoke him — he's looking very fierce right now.

mandarin_meaning: 把某人彻底打败或羞辱、把人搞得非常惨
english_meaning: to completely thrash, humiliate, or utterly trounce someone
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，字面上有“把狗头煮熟”的夸张意味，用來形容把對方彻底打败、羞辱或弄得一塌糊涂。语气较粗俗，用于口语或熟人之间的非正式场合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally evoking 'cooking a dog's head'—used figuratively to say someone was utterly defeated, humiliated, or soundly trounced. It's coarse and informal, typical in colloquial speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺比賽度畀人煠熟狗頭，輸到唔知點算。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 bei2 coi3 dou6 bei2 jan4 zaak3 suk6 gau2 tau4, syu1 dou3 m4 zi1 dim2 syun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在比赛中被人彻底打败，输得很惨。
examples.english_sentence: He got completely trounced in the match and lost badly.

mandarin_meaning: 煤气罐 / 液化气罐
english_meaning: gas cylinder; LPG canister
explanation_mandarin: 指裝液化石油氣或煤氣的金屬氣罐，常用於家庭煮食或熱水器供氣。注意存放和使用安全，避免漏氣或陽光直射。
explanation_english: A metal cylinder that contains liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) or town gas, commonly used for household cooking or water heaters. Handle and store with care to avoid leaks or exposure to direct sunlight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企啲煤氣罐用晒，要買多一罐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 di1 mui4 hei3 gun3 jung6 saai3, jiu3 maai5 do1 jat1 gun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡的煤氣罐用完了，要再買一罐。
examples.english_sentence: The gas cylinder at home is used up; we need to buy another one.

mandarin_meaning: 照着处方或指示办事；按规定或上级指示机械地执行（含按部就班、无弹性之意）
english_meaning: to follow instructions or orders exactly; to do things mechanically/by the book (follow a prescription or orders to the letter)
explanation_mandarin: 原指照处方配药，引申为严格按指示或规定去做，常带有机械、缺乏灵活性的含义。
explanation_english: Originally meant to fill a prescription exactly; figuratively means to carry out instructions or rules strictly and mechanically, often implying a lack of flexibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老板叫我照单执药，乜都唔可以自作主张。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 giu3 ngo5 ziu3 daan1 zap1 joek6, mat1 dou1 m4 ho2 ji5 zi6 zok3 zyu2 zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板叫我照单执药，什么都不可以擅自决定。
examples.english_sentence: The boss told me to follow orders to the letter; I can't make my own decisions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生話要照单执药，啲藥要準時食，唔好自己停藥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 waa6 jiu3 ziu3 daan1 zap1 joek6, di1 joek6 jiu3 zeon2 si4 sik6, m4 hou2 zi6 gei2 ting4 joek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 医生说要照单执药，药要按时服用，不可擅自停药。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor said to follow the prescription exactly; take the medicine on time and don't stop it on your own.

mandarin_meaning: 照本宣科；拘泥於固定做法，缺乏靈活變通
english_meaning: To follow a fixed pattern or instructions rigidly (often blindly), without adapting — usually resulting in a poor outcome or failure.
explanation_mandarin: 「照板煮糊」是廣東話慣用語，字面意為按著板子照樣煮，最後煮成糊狀。引申指拘泥按部就班或機械照做，缺乏靈活性或變通，往往導致效果不好或出錯。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiom literally meaning 'follow the mold and cook it into a mess.' It describes doing something mechanically or rigidly according to a set pattern or instructions, without flexibility — often leading to mistakes or unsatisfactory results.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好照板煮糊，遇到情況要靈活處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ziu3 baan2 zyu2 wu4, jyu6 dou3 cing4 fong3 jiu3 ling4 wut6 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要照本宣科，遇到情況要靈活處理。
examples.english_sentence: Don't follow the script blindly; be flexible and handle situations adaptively.

mandarin_meaning: 八卦新闻 / 花边新闻 / 耸人听闻的琐碎报道
english_meaning: tabloid/gossip news; sensational or trivial news stories meant to attract attention
explanation_mandarin: 指以吸引眼球或談資為目的的耸人听闻、琐碎或夸大其詞的新聞或傳聞，常用來形容小報、娛樂新聞或網絡謠言。
explanation_english: Refers to sensational, trivial, or gossip-driven news stories intended to attract attention—often used to describe tabloid pieces, entertainment gossip, or rumour-filled social media posts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日睇啲煲水新聞，嗰啲好多都係誇張嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 tai2 di1 bou1 seoi2 san1 man4, go2 di1 hou2 do1 dou1 hai6 kwaa1 zoeng1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要老是看那些煲水新聞，很多都是誇張的。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep reading those tabloid gossip pieces; a lot of them are exaggerated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 社交網成日充斥住煲水新聞，大家要小心分辨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: se5 gaau1 mong5 sing4 jat6 cung1 cik1 zyu6 bou1 seoi2 san1 man4, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 siu2 sam1 fan1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 社交網上經常充斥著煲水新聞，大家要小心分辨。
examples.english_sentence: Social media is often filled with tabloid gossip; people should be careful to tell fact from rumour.

mandarin_meaning: 长时间打电话聊天
english_meaning: to chat on the phone for a long time; to keep someone on the phone for ages
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗语，字面意思是“煲电话粥”，用来形容两人打电话聊很久，常用于情侣或关系亲密的人之间。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquialism literally meaning 'to cook telephone porridge.' It describes spending a long time talking on the phone, often used for lovers or close friends.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我同佢煲電話粥煲咗成晚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 bou1 din6 waa2 zuk1 bou1 zo2 sing4 maan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我和他/她打了整晚的电话聊得很久。
examples.english_sentence: I chatted on the phone with him/her for the whole evening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋成日煲電話粥，好似好熟絡。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 sing4 jat6 bou1 din6 waa2 zuk1, hou2 ci5 hou2 suk6 lok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们经常长时间打电话，好像关系很亲密。
examples.english_sentence: They often spend ages talking on the phone; they seem very close.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家上班時間，唔好喺度煲電話粥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 soeng5 baan1 si4 gaan3, m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 bou1 din6 waa2 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在是上班时间，不要在这里长时间打电话。
examples.english_sentence: It's work time now — don't be on the phone for ages here.

mandarin_meaning: 抽菸／吸菸
english_meaning: to smoke (a cigarette); to have a smoke/take a smoke break
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指抽菸或出去抽菸、休息時抽一支或幾支菸。常用於香港口語中，與「抽菸」「食煙」同義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to smoke (a cigarette) or to go out for a smoke/break. Common in Hong Kong speech and synonymous with 'to smoke'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我出去煲菸一陣，你等陣再傾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ceot1 heoi3 bou1 jin1 jat1 zan6, nei5 dang2 zan6 zoi3 king1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我要出去抽菸一下，你等一下再談。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going out for a smoke for a bit; wait and we'll talk later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都喺樓梯口煲菸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 hai2 lau4 tai1 hau2 bou1 jin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是在樓梯口抽菸。
examples.english_sentence: He always smokes at the stairwell.

mandarin_meaning: 焖；燜（用小火慢煮，使食物入味或保持温热）
english_meaning: to braise; to simmer; to keep food warm (slow-cook over low heat)
explanation_mandarin: 煴為罕用字，常作燜的變體，指用小火慢煮或悶煮，使食物入味或保持溫熱的烹調方法，常見於廣東、香港方言語境中描述烹飪方式。
explanation_english: 煴 is a rare/archaic form often used as a variant of 燜 (to braise/simmer). It denotes a cooking method of slow-cooking over low heat to make food flavorful or to keep it warm; used in Cantonese-speaking contexts to describe this cooking style.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 條魚煴咗好耐，入味晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tiu4 jyu4 mun4 zo2 hou2 noi6, jap6 mei6 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条鱼焖了很久，很入味。
examples.english_sentence: The fish has been braised for a long time and is very flavorful.

mandarin_meaning: 煽動（也可指扇火助燃，與「煽火/扇火」意思相近）
english_meaning: to incite / to stir up (figurative); to fan the flames / to stoke a fire (literal)
explanation_mandarin: 「煴火」在口語中常作「煽火」的變體，用於比喻時指煽動、挑起事端；也可作字面意思，指用風或加入可燃物使火勢增大。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 煴火 is often a variant of 煽火. Figuratively it means to incite or stir up trouble; literally it can mean to fan or stoke a fire to make it burn stronger.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺社交媒體上煴火，想挑起事端。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 se5 gaau1 mui4 tai2 soeng6 sin1 fo2, soeng2 tiu1 hei2 si6 dyun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常在社交媒體上煽動，想挑起事端。
examples.english_sentence: He often incites people on social media, trying to stir up trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽咪落啲枯枝去煴火，令火大啲方便煲嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 mi4 lok6 di1 fu1 zik1 heoi3 sin1 fo2, ling6 fo2 daai6 di1 fong1 bin6 bou1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽放一些枯枝去扇火，讓火大一些方便煮東西。
examples.english_sentence: Mom put some dry twigs to fan the fire, making it burn hotter so it's easier to cook.

mandarin_meaning: （不明／非標準詞語）
english_meaning: Unknown — not an attested standard Cantonese word (possibly a typo, rare/obsolete characters, or invented slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「煿炑」並非常見或標準的粵語詞彙。這兩個字均屬罕用字或非通行字形，查閱常用粵語詞典與語料未能找到可靠詞義。很可能是打字錯誤、個人自創詞或區域／行話用字，若在語境中出現應以上下文判斷其含義或向使用者求證。
explanation_english: “煿炑” is not a recognized standard Cantonese word. Both characters are rare or nonstandard and there is no reliable attested meaning in common Cantonese references. It is likely a typo, a coinage, or a very obscure/regional term. Interpretations should rely on context or confirmation from the speaker/writer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我睇唔明「煿炑」係乜嘢意思，可能係打錯字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tai2 m4 ming4 「煿炑」 hai6 mat1 je5 ji3 si1, ho2 nang4 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我看不懂「煿炑」是什么意思，可能是打错字。
examples.english_sentence: I don't understand what '煿炑' means; it might be a typo.

mandarin_meaning: 闷燃、微热或略有余温（古字，常用于文言）
english_meaning: to smolder; to give off gentle heat; to be warm (archaic/literary)
explanation_mandarin: 「熅」为古字，本义与火相关，指闷燃或有余温，现代汉语不常用，多见于文言或古籍中，也可表示微弱的热或光。
explanation_english: A literary/archaic character related to fire meaning to smolder, to emit gentle heat, or to retain warmth. Rare in modern usage and mainly found in classical texts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 炭堆仲熅住，唔好行咁近。
examples.jyutping_sentence: taan3 deoi1 zung6 wan4 zyu6, m4 hou2 haang4 gam2 gan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 炭堆还在闷燃，别走那么近。
examples.english_sentence: The pile of charcoal is still smoldering; don't get so close.

mandarin_meaning: 脾氣粗暴、愛發脾氣或喜歡責罵別人的女人（帶貶義）
english_meaning: a quarrelsome, bossy or nasty woman who often scolds or bullies others (pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 俗稱，用來形容性格兇惡、愛責備或苛刻對待他人的女性，常帶貶義，屬口語或俚語用法。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang term for a woman with a rough, hostile or bullying temperament who often scolds or mistreats others; pejorative and informal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰位鄰居成日鬧人，大家都話佢係個熊人婆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 wai2 leon4 geoi1 seng4 jat6 naau6 jan4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 keoi5 hai6 go3 hung4 jan4 po4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那位鄰居總是責罵別人，大家都說她是個熊人婆。
examples.english_sentence: That neighbor is always scolding people; everyone says she's a 'bear-woman' (a nasty, bossy woman).

mandarin_meaning: 找熟人頂罪/讓熟人替自己承擔錯誤或責任
english_meaning: to get an acquaintance to take the fall; to have someone you know take the blame
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，指讓認識的人替自己承擔錯誤或責任，通常帶有利用熟人或推卸責任的負面含義。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to arrange for an acquaintance to take responsibility or blame for a mistake; often implies exploiting connections or shirking responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做錯嘢，竟然搵熟人買爛鑊，根本唔負責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 co3 je5, ging2 jin4 wan2 suk6 jan4 maai5 laan6 wok6, gan1 bun2 zan1 hai6 m4 fu6 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做錯事，竟然找熟人頂罪，根本不負責任。
examples.english_sentence: He messed up and actually got an acquaintance to take the fall — that's totally irresponsible.

mandarin_meaning: （香港粵語俚語）指經常做蠢事、行為幼稚或令人覺得愚蠢的人（帶貶義）
english_meaning: Hong Kong Cantonese slang for a person who habitually acts foolishly or behaves in a stupid/childish way (derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「熟膠」為香港粵語俗語，通常用來形容某人老是做蠢事或行為幼稚，語氣帶貶義或嘲諷。常用於口語和網絡用語中。
explanation_english: “熟膠” is HK Cantonese slang used to describe someone who repeatedly does foolish things or behaves childishly. It carries a derogatory or mocking tone and is commonly used in spoken and online contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你又唔聽人講，真係熟膠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau6 m4 teng1 jan4 gong2, zan1 hai6 suk6 gaau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你又不听别人说，真是个老蠢蛋。
examples.english_sentence: You won't listen again — you're such a habitual fool.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢次次都做啲熟膠嘢，大家都唔想理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ci3 ci3 dou1 zou6 di1 suk6 gaau1 je5, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 soeng2 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他每次都做蠢事，大家都不想理他。
examples.english_sentence: He always does stupid things; nobody wants to bother with him.

mandarin_meaning: 熟門熟路 (shú mén shú lù)
english_meaning: to be very familiar with a route, place, task, or procedure; to know the ropes
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語 / 形容詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 形容對某地、某條路或某項工作、流程非常熟悉，知道該怎麼做或該怎麼走。
explanation_english: Describes being highly familiar with a place, route, job or procedure — knowing exactly what to do or where to go.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條街我熟行熟路，十幾年住喺附近。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 gaai1 ngo5 suk6 haang4 suk6 lou6, sap6 gei2 nin4 zyu6 hai2 fu6 gan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這條街我熟門熟路，十幾年住在附近。
examples.english_sentence: I'm very familiar with this street — I've lived nearby for over ten years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做呢份工做咗好耐，對呢啲工序熟行熟路，唔使我教。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 ni1 fan6 gung1 zou6 zo2 hou2 noi6, deoi3 ni1 di1 gung1 ceoi4 suk6 haang4 suk6 lou6, m4 sai2 ngo5 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做這份工作做了很久，對這些工序熟門熟路，不用我教。
examples.english_sentence: He's been doing this job for a long time; he's familiar with these procedures and doesn't need me to teach him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 去嗰個市場買餸我熟行熟路，可以帶你去最平嗰間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: heoi3 go2 go3 si5 coeng4 maai5 sung3 ngo5 suk6 haang4 suk6 lou6, ho2 ji5 daai3 nei5 heoi3 zeoi3 peng4 go2 gaan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去那個市場買菜我很熟門熟路，可以帶你去最便宜的那家。
examples.english_sentence: I'm familiar with that market; I can take you to the cheapest stall.

cantonese: 熟读王叔和，不如临症多
jyutping: suk6 duk6 wong4 suk1 wo4, bat1 jyu4 lam4 zing3 do1
mandarin_meaning: 与其熟读王叔和，不如多看临床病例；强调实践经验胜于书本知识。
english_meaning: Reading (the works of) Wang Shuhe thoroughly is not as good as treating/seeing many cases — practical experience is more valuable than book knowledge.
explanation_mandarin: 此俗语以古代名医王叔和为例，说明临床实践和接触病例比单纯读书更能提高医术；可引申为实践胜于理论的道理。
explanation_english: This proverb references the ancient physician Wang Shuhe to say that clinical practice and seeing many cases improve medical skill more than merely reading books; broadly, it means practice beats theory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做醫生嗰陣，熟讀王叔和，不如臨症多，實戰經驗最緊要。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 ji1 sang1 go2 zan6, suk6 duk6 wong4 suk1 wo4, bat1 jyu4 lam4 zing3 do1, sat6 zin3 ging1 jim6 zeoi3 gan2 jiu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 当做医生的时候，与其熟读王叔和，不如多看临床病例，实践经验最重要。
examples.english_sentence: When working as a doctor, reading Wang Shuhe thoroughly is not as good as seeing many cases — hands-on experience matters most.

synonyms: 纸上谈兵不如亲身经验

mandarin_meaning: 耗時間胡鬧/傻乎乎地閒混
english_meaning: to waste time messing around or acting silly (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「熬水膠」是香港粵語俚語，用來形容無所事事、耗時間地胡鬧或傻氣地閒混，常帶貶義，指浪費時間或不做正經事。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase meaning to idle about, mess around, or act foolishly for a long time. It usually carries a negative sense of wasting time or not doing anything productive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度熬水膠，快啲做返你份嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 ngou4 seoi2 gaau1, faai3 di1 zou6 faan1 nei5 fan6 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在這裡瞎混，快點把你的工作做回來。
examples.english_sentence: Stop messing around here and get back to your work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識喺網上熬水膠，唔做實事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 hai2 mong5 soeng6 ngou4 seoi2 gaau1, m4 zou6 sat6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會在網上胡鬧，做不成正事。
examples.english_sentence: He only messes around online and doesn't do anything productive.

mandarin_meaning: 痱子（汗疹、热疹）
english_meaning: heat rash; prickly heat (miliaria)
explanation_mandarin: 因高温或出汗导致汗腺或汗管堵塞，皮肤出现红色小疹、瘙痒或刺痛的皮肤问题，常见于婴幼儿和炎热潮湿环境下。
explanation_english: A skin condition caused by blocked sweat ducts due to heat or excessive sweating, producing small red bumps and itching or a prickling sensation; common in infants and hot, humid conditions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天咁熱，個BB出咗好多熱痱，我哋要幫佢搽藥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 gam2 jit6, go3 BB ceot1 zo2 hou2 do1 jit6 fai3, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 bong1 keoi5 caat3 joek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天这么热，宝宝长了很多痱子，我们要帮他擦药。
examples.english_sentence: It's so hot in summer; the baby has developed many heat rashes; we need to apply medicine.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出汗之後要即刻沖涼，免得出熱痱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 hon6 zi1 hau6 jiu3 zik1 hak1 cung1 loeng4, min5 dak1 ceot1 jit6 fai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出汗之后要立刻洗澡，免得长痱子。
examples.english_sentence: After sweating, shower immediately to avoid getting heat rash.

mandarin_meaning: 性急、暴躁、容易發脾氣（口語）
english_meaning: short-tempered; irritable; easily annoyed (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，形容人脾氣急躁、容易生氣或不耐煩。亦有時寫作「熱積」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term describing someone who is hot-tempered or easily annoyed. Sometimes written with the alternate character "積".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近成日好熱癪，啲小事都頂唔順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 sing4 jat6 hou2 jit6 zik1, di1 siu2 si6 dou1 ding2 m4 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近很急躁，小事都受不了。
examples.english_sentence: He's been very short-tempered lately; even small things set him off.

mandarin_meaning: 灯芯 (dēng xīn)：油灯或蜡烛等的灯芯；也可指用于做灯芯的植物（灯心草）
english_meaning: lamp wick; the wick of an oil lamp or candle; also the plant (rush) used as a wick
explanation_mandarin: 指油灯、蜡烛等裝置中用來吸油並持續燃燒的芯，也可指用于制作灯芯的植物，例如灯心草。
explanation_english: Refers to the wick used in oil lamps or candles that draws fuel and maintains the flame; can also mean the plant (rush) traditionally used to make wicks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企冇電嘅時候，我哋會用燈心點燈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 mou5 din6 ge3 si4 hau6, ngo5 dei6 wui5 jung6 dang1 sam1 dim2 dang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡沒電的時候，我們會用灯芯點燈。
examples.english_sentence: When there's no electricity at home, we light lamps using a wick.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 傳統蠟燭嘅燈心要用純棉，燃燒先會穩定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyun4 tung2 laat6 zuk1 ge3 dang1 sam1 jiu3 jung6 seon4 min4, jin4 siu1 sin1 wui5 wan2 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 传统蜡烛的灯芯要用纯棉，燃烧才会稳定。
examples.english_sentence: Traditional candles' wicks should be made of pure cotton for stable burning.

mandarin_meaning: 生活費；家用
english_meaning: basic household expenses; living costs (lit. 'lamp oil and candles')
explanation_mandarin: 原指點燈用的油和火燭，比喻日常生活支出或家用開銷。
explanation_english: Originally refers to oil and candles for lighting; metaphorically used for daily living expenses or household costs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家生活咁貴，連燈油火燭都唔夠錢應付。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 sang1 wut6 gam2 gwai3, lin4 dang1 jau4 fo2 zuk1 dou1 m4 gau3 cin2 jing3 fu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在生活這麼貴，連燈油火燭都不夠錢應付。
examples.english_sentence: Living is so expensive now that there's not even enough money to cover basic household expenses.

mandarin_meaning: 燈盞（小燈、燈杯或舊式油燈的燈具）
english_meaning: a small lamp or lamp cup (e.g. a small table lamp or the glass/cup of an oil lamp)
explanation_mandarin: 指小型的照明器具或燈杯，在粵語中常用來稱呼一盞燈或舊式油燈的燈盞部分。
explanation_english: Refers to a small lighting device or the lamp cup (the glass/container of a lamp); in Cantonese it's commonly used to refer to a single lamp or the lamp part of an old oil lamp.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 枱上擺咗一盞燈盞，光度好柔和。
examples.jyutping_sentence: toi4 soeng6 baai2 zo2 jat1 zaan2 dang1zaam2, gwong1 dou6 hou2 jau4 wo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 桌上擺了一盞燈盞，光線很柔和。
examples.english_sentence: There is a small lamp on the table; the light is very soft.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 村入面啲古老燈盞都用油嚟照明。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyun1 jap6 min6 di1 gu2 lou5 dang1zaam2 dou1 jung6 jau4 lai4 ziu3 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 村子裡面的古老燈盞都用油來照明。
examples.english_sentence: The old lamps in the village are all lit with oil.

mandarin_meaning: 灯筒（燈具的圓筒形外殼或燈罩）
english_meaning: lamphousing / cylindrical lampshade (the tubular housing or shade of a light fixture)
explanation_mandarin: 指燈具的圓筒形外殼或燈罩，用來保護燈泡或改變光線分布。在粵語中也可指某些圓柱形的燈具部件。
explanation_english: Refers to the cylindrical housing or shade of a light fixture that protects the bulb or shapes the light. In Cantonese it is used for tube-like lamp components.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢盞燈嘅燈筒好舊，要換番個新嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zaan2 dang1 ge3 dang1tung2 hou2 gau6, jiu3 wun6 faan1 go3 san1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這盞燈的燈筒很舊，要換一個新的。
examples.english_sentence: The lampshade of this light is very old; we need to replace it with a new one.

mandarin_meaning: 燉（燉煮）
english_meaning: to stew; to simmer; slow-cook
explanation_mandarin: 表示用文火長時間煮，通常指燉湯或燉菜，使食材軟爛入味。
explanation_english: Refers to cooking slowly over low heat (stewing/simmering), typically for soups or braised dishes to make ingredients tender and flavorful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽今晚燖咗一鍋雞湯，攞嚟熱返食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 gam1 maan5 deon6 zo2 jat1 wo1 gai1 tong1, lo2 lai4 jit6 faan1 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽今晚燉了一鍋雞湯，拿去加熱吃吧。
examples.english_sentence: Mom stewed a pot of chicken soup tonight — heat some up and eat.

mandarin_meaning: 脸红；感到尴尬或羞愧
english_meaning: to blush/feel embarrassed or ashamed; to be humiliated (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「燶起块面」是廣東話口語/俚語，字面含義與「臉被燒起來」類似，實際用來形容因為尷尬、羞愧或被當眾揭露而臉紅、難堪或丟臉的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression literally suggesting one’s face has been 'burned up' — used to describe blushing, feeling embarrassed, ashamed, or humiliated (often because of being exposed or scolded in public).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰次俾老闆當住責罵，我即刻燶起块面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 ci3 bei2 lou5 baan2 dong3 zyu6 zaak3 maa6, ngo5 zik1 hak1 nong4 hei2 faai3 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那次被老板当着众人责骂，我立刻脸红了/很尴尬。
examples.english_sentence: When the boss scolded me in front of everyone that time, I immediately blushed and felt embarrassed.

mandarin_meaning: 裂开；爆裂；（比喻）破裂、瓦解
english_meaning: to burst/split open; (figuratively) to break apart or fall apart
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，表示物體因內壓或外力而裂開、爆裂；也可比喻關係、計劃、局勢等突然破裂或瓦解。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning that something splits or bursts open due to pressure or force; can also be used figuratively for relationships, plans, or situations that suddenly break down.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個氣球爆㿭咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 hei3 kau4 baau3 cek3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 气球爆裂了。
examples.english_sentence: The balloon burst.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋嘅關係終於爆㿭，大家都唔講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 ge3 gwaan1 hai6 zung1 jyu1 baau3 cek3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们的关系终于破裂了，大家都不说话。
examples.english_sentence: Their relationship finally broke down; everyone stopped speaking.

mandarin_meaning: 挑起打架／惹事（口語）
english_meaning: to start a fight; to pick a fight (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「爆仗」是粵語口語，指在公眾場合或私人場合挑起爭執或打鬥，帶有挑釁或惹事的意思，常見於香港街頭或社交語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term meaning to start a fight or pick a quarrel, often implying provocation or causing trouble; commonly used in Hong Kong informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺夜店度爆仗，搞到大家都唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 je6 dim3 dou6 baau3 zoeng6, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在夜店惹事打架，弄得大家都不開心。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps starting fights at the club, making everyone unhappy.

mandarin_meaning: 惹上大麻烦／出大乱子
english_meaning: to get into big trouble; for a situation to go disastrously wrong
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，字面是“爆大镬”，用来形容惹上严重的麻烦或事情变得一发不可收拾。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally 'explode a big wok'; used to describe getting into serious trouble or a situation turning into a major mess.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果呢件事畀老細知道，肯定會爆大镬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 ni1 gin6 si6 bei2 lou5 sai3 zi1 dou6, hang2 ding6 wui5 baau3 daai6 wok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果这件事被老板知道，肯定会惹上大麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: If the boss finds out about this, we'll definitely be in big trouble.

mandarin_meaning: 被夾住／被擠得很緊（口語）
english_meaning: to be squeezed/pinned tightly (colloquial slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「爆夾」是香港粵語口語用法，形容被兩邊擠、夾住或擠得非常緊，帶有誇張語氣。有時用來形容在人多的地方被擠壓或被物件夾到的情況。
explanation_english: “爆夾” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang used to describe being tightly squeezed or pinned between things or people. It carries an emphatic/colloquial tone and is used for situations like being crushed in a crowd or getting pinched between objects.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 巴士太多人，我畀人擠到爆夾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baa1 si2 taai3 do1 jan4, ngo5 bei2 jan4 zai1 dou3 baau3 gaap3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公交車太多人，我被擠得很緊／被夾住了。
examples.english_sentence: The bus was so crowded I was squeezed tight / got stuck between people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 搬嘢嗰陣，兩件傢俬夾到我隻手，差啲爆夾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bun1 je5 go2 zan6, loeng5 gin6 gaa1 si1 gaap3 dou3 ngo5 zek3 sau2, caa1 di1 baau3 gaap3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 搬東西時兩件家具夾到我的手，差點被夾得很嚴重。
examples.english_sentence: While moving stuff the two pieces of furniture pinched my hand — I almost got badly pinched.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）用爆頭（headshot）方式擊殺對方的頭號人物；比喻性地對對手的關鍵人物或重要資源造成致命打擊。
english_meaning: A slang expression meaning to headshot/kill the opponent's ace/top player; figuratively, to deliver a decisive blow that destroys a rival's key person or asset.
explanation_mandarin: 常見於電子遊戲或口語比喻中，指以一次致命的爆頭（或關鍵一擊）除掉對方最重要的角色或利器，從而扭轉局勢。
explanation_english: Common in gaming and colloquial speech; refers to taking out the opponent's most important player with a headshot (or a single decisive strike), or metaphorically destroying a rival's key asset to change the situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 昨晚打機嗰陣，我用狙擊槍一發就爆咗對面個頭牌，隊友即刻鬆晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zok6 maan5 daa2 gei1 go2 zan6, ngo5 jung6 geoi1 gik1 coeng1 jat1 faat3 zau6 baau3 zo2 deoi3 min6 go3 tau4 paai4, deoi6 jau5 zik1 hak1 sung1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚打遊戲的時候，我用狙擊槍一槍就爆掉了對方的頭牌，隊友立刻鬆了一口氣。
examples.english_sentence: Last night while gaming, I headshot the opponent's ace with a single shot, and my teammates immediately relaxed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司入面佢一單醜聞就爆咗對手嘅頭牌，生意即刻衰落。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jap6 min6 keoi5 jat1 daan1 cau2 man4 zau6 baau3 zo2 deoi3 sau2 ge3 tau4 paai4, sang1 ji3 zik1 hak1 seoi1 lok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司內他一宗醜聞就擊垮了對手的頭牌，生意立刻衰落。
examples.english_sentence: Within the company, his scandal knocked out the rival's top figure and business immediately declined.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）表示對某事或某人感到非常糟糕、無奈或不滿，類似「真爛／太差勁了」；此詞屬非正式或粗俗用語，具強烈感嘆或貶義色彩
english_meaning: (slang) an informal/expletive expression used to convey strong frustration, contempt, or that something is lousy/terrible; nonstandard and coarse
explanation_mandarin: 「爛個唔」屬廣東話口語中較罕見或粗俗的感嘆用語，字面上並無嚴格語法結構，多用來表達對事物或人的不滿、輕蔑或無奈。具體含義及語氣視語境而定，常等同於「真爛、太差勁了、可惡」。不適合在正式或禮貌場合使用。
explanation_english: "爛個唔" is a Cantonese colloquial/expletive expression (relatively rare and coarse). It doesn't have a strict literal grammar but is used to express strong dissatisfaction, contempt, or frustration toward something or someone. Depending on context it roughly equals "that's rotten/terrible" or "damn it." Avoid in formal or polite settings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 爛個唔！啲嘢又壞喇！
examples.jyutping_sentence: laan6 go3 m4! di1 je5 jau6 waai6 laa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 真糟糕！東西又壞了！
examples.english_sentence: Damn it! The thing broke again!

mandarin_meaning: 裝聰明／賣弄聰明（帶諷刺語氣）
english_meaning: to pretend to be clever or show off (sarcastic; mocking someone who is actually incompetent)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來諷刺或嘲笑某人愛裝聰明、賣弄，但實際能力不足。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used sarcastically to mock someone who is showing off or pretending to be smart while actually lacking ability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再爛叻嚦啦，你根本唔識做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 laan6 lek1 lik6 laa1, nei5 gan1 bun2 m4 sik1 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再裝聰明了，你根本不會做。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep pretending to be clever — you don't actually know how to do it.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）廢物、無用的人
english_meaning: Derogatory slang meaning a useless, lazy or passive person (literally 'rotten corpse')
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，字面上是「爛屍」，用來侮辱或形容一個懶惰、無所作為、不負責任或毫無用處的人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang insult literally meaning 'rotten corpse'. Used to describe someone who is lazy, useless, passive, or shirks responsibility. It is derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日都唔做嘢，淨係喺度當爛尸，咁點得？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 dou1 m4 zou6 je5, zing6 hai6 hai2 dou6 dong3 laan6 si1, gam2 dim2 dak1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你整天都不做事，只是在那裡當個廢物，這樣怎麼行？
examples.english_sentence: You do nothing all day and just stand there like a useless person — how is that acceptable?

mandarin_meaning: 爛仔／壞蛋；行為惡劣或討人厭的人（粵語罵人用語）
english_meaning: a rotten brat; a scoundrel; a despicable or irresponsible person (pejorative, colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「爛崽」是粵語的貶義俗語，用來罵人，表示對方行為不良、討厭或不負責任。可用於指年輕人或成年人，帶有強烈不滿或輕蔑的語氣。
explanation_english: “爛崽” is a Cantonese pejorative slang term used to insult someone as a rotten brat or scoundrel — implying bad behavior, annoying or irresponsible conduct. It is colloquial and often expresses strong disapproval.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係條爛崽，成日唔做嘢，淨係識搵理由。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 tiu4 laan6 zai2, seng4 jat6 m4 zou6 je5, zing6 hai6 sik1 wan2 lei5 jau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個爛崽，整天不做事，只會找理由。
examples.english_sentence: He's such a rotten brat — never works and only comes up with excuses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁樣叫人爛崽，太過份。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 joeng6 giu3 jan4 laan6 zai2, taai3 gwo3 fan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那樣叫人爛崽，太過分了。
examples.english_sentence: Don't call someone a 'raan zai' like that — that's going too far.

mandarin_meaning: 沒救的人／一團糟／一個無用的人
english_meaning: a hopeless case; a useless person; a complete mess
explanation_mandarin: 爛湴泥為廣東話俚語，用來形容人懶散、沒用或無可救藥，也可用來形容事情一塌糊塗、很爛。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang used to describe a person who is lazy, useless, or hopeless; can also describe something that's a complete mess or in a bad state.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日咁懶惰，真係一個爛湴泥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gam2 laan5-do6, zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 laan6-baan6-nai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天這麼懶，真的是個沒救的人。
examples.english_sentence: He's always so lazy — he's really a hopeless case.

mandarin_meaning: 爛掉的番茄；亦指電影評論網站「Rotten Tomatoes」或用來形容作品評價很差
english_meaning: rotten tomato (literal); also refers to the review site 'Rotten Tomatoes' or used figuratively to mean something (e.g., a film) is rated very poorly
explanation_mandarin: 本詞本義為腐爛的番茄。現代用法除了指實物外，常作為電影評論聚合網站「Rotten Tomatoes」的中文名稱，亦可用來形容某作品或表現評價很差。
explanation_english: Literally a rotten tomato. Besides the literal meaning, it commonly denotes the review aggregator 'Rotten Tomatoes' in Chinese and is used figuratively to say a work or performance has very poor reviews or quality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢箱番茄有幾個爛番茄，要唔要我幫你挑下？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 soeng1 faan1 ke2 jau5 gei2 go3 laan6 faan1 ke2, jiu3 m4 jiu3 ngo5 bong1 nei5 tiu1 haa5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這箱番茄有幾個爛掉了，要不要我幫你挑一下？
examples.english_sentence: There are a few rotten tomatoes in this box — do you want me to pick them out for you?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇過爛番茄嘅評分未？呢套戲得咁低分。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 gwo3 laan6 faan1 ke2 ge3 ping4 fan1 mei6? ni1 tou3 hei3 dak1 gam2 dai1 fan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看過爛番茄的評分了嗎？這部戲只有這麼低的分數。
examples.english_sentence: Have you checked the Rotten Tomatoes score? This film only has such a low rating.

mandarin_meaning: 睡得很沉；睡過頭
english_meaning: to sleep very deeply; to oversleep (sleep like a log)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語說法，表示睡得又沉又熟，或睡過頭。有時會用『睏』字作變體（在部分用法中讀作 kwan3）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to sleep very deeply or to oversleep. The character 睏 is sometimes used as a variant (pronounced kwan3 in some contexts).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝爛瞓，結果遲到咗公司。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 laan6 fan3, git3 gwo2 ci4 dou3 zo2 gung1 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上睡過頭，結果上班遲到了。
examples.english_sentence: I overslept this morning and ended up being late for work.

jyutping: laan6 syun4 dou1 zung6 jau5 saam1 gan1 deng1
mandarin_meaning: 烂船也有三斤钉
english_meaning: Even a rotten boat still has value / even something (or someone) seemingly useless still has some use or advantage
explanation_mandarin: 比喻即使是看起來很差或沒用的人或物，也仍有一點價值或用處，不能完全否定。
explanation_english: A proverb meaning that even things or people that seem worthless still have some value or usefulness; don't dismiss them completely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢雖然唔係好叻，但爛船都仲有三斤釘，起碼都仲有啲用處。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 jin4 m4 hai6 hou2 lak1, daan6 laan6 syun4 dou1 zung6 jau5 saam1 gan1 deng1, hei2 maa5 dou1 zung6 jau5 di1 jung6 cyu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他雖然不是很厲害，但烂船也有三斤钉，起碼還有點用處。
examples.english_sentence: He's not very capable, but even a rotten boat has three catties of nails — at least he's somewhat useful.

jyutping: laan6 geoi1 geoi1 (鮓鮓: zaa2 zaa2)
mandarin_meaning: 破爛、不整潔、凌亂（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: shabby, tatty, messy; in a state of disrepair (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的俗語/俚語，用來形容衣物、地方或人看起來很破舊、凌亂、不整潔。有時帶輕視或揶揄的語氣。不同地區或語境可能會以「鮓鮓」等寫法或發音代替。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang term used to describe something or someone as shabby, tatty, or extremely messy. It often carries a slightly derogatory or teasing tone. Regional spellings or pronunciations (e.g. 鮓鮓) may vary.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間屋入面亂到爛苴苴，唔好叫人入嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 uk1 jap6 min6 lyun6 dou3 laan6 geoi1 geoi1, m4 hou2 giu3 jan4 jap6 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間屋裡亂得一團糟，不要讓人進來。
examples.english_sentence: This room is a complete mess — don't let people come in.

mandarin_meaning: 烂糊糊 / 破烂不堪
