mandarin_meaning: （两人）亲密无间、形影不离（字面：碗碟碰在一起都会发出声音）
english_meaning: So close/intimate that even their bowls and plates make noise when they touch; inseparable
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 短語 / 俗語（描述關係）
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容兩個人關係非常親密、經常一起出現或形影不離；字面意思是連碗碟碰埋也會有聲，借以強調親密程度。
explanation_english: Used to describe two people who are extremely close or inseparable; literally 'even bowls and plates make noise when they touch,' emphasizing the closeness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個碗碟碰埋都有聲，成日一齊出入。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 wun2 dip6 pung3 maai4 dou1 jau5 sing1, sing4 jat6 jat1 cai4 ceot1 jap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们两个人亲密得连碗碟碰在一起都会有声音，整天都在一起。
examples.english_sentence: Those two are so close that even their bowls and plates make noise when they touch; they're always together.

mandarin_meaning: 飯碗；謀生的方式或收入來源
english_meaning: livelihood; the job or means by which one earns a living (bread and butter)
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，'碗頭飯' 指靠某份工作或行業維持生計的飯碗，泛指謀生的方式或主要收入來源。
explanation_english: '碗頭飯' in Cantonese refers to the job or work that provides one's livelihood — the means of earning a living or main source of income.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家搵碗頭飯都唔容易。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 wan2 waan2 tau4 faan6 dou1 m4 jung4 ji6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在找飯碗／謀生的工作都不容易。
examples.english_sentence: It's not easy to find a way to make a living nowadays.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗保住碗頭飯，日日朝九晚五返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 bou2 zyu6 waan2 tau4 faan6, jat6 jat6 ziu1 gau2 maan5 ng5 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他為了保住飯碗，每天朝九晚五上班。
examples.english_sentence: He works 9-to-5 every day to keep his job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好為咗碗頭飯而放棄自己嘅理想。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 wai6 zo2 waan2 tau4 faan6 ji4 fong3 hei3 zi6 gei2 ge3 lei5 soeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要為了飯碗而放棄自己的理想。
examples.english_sentence: Don't give up your ideals just for the sake of a paycheque.

mandarin_meaning: 碧玉间（bì yù jiān）：字面为“碧玉般的房间/闺房”；常作诗意或书面用法，也可作店名、楼阁等专有名号。
english_meaning: Biyu Room (literally "jade-like room"): a poetic/literary term for an elegant chamber or boudoir; also used as a proper name for shops or halls.
explanation_mandarin: 「碧玉間」偏向文言或诗意用法，字面上指像碧玉般雅致的房间、闺房或楼阁。现代粤语口语不常见，常见于诗词、店名或古典风格的场所命名。
explanation_english: The term is chiefly literary/poetic, literally meaning a chamber as beautiful as jade. It usually refers to an elegant boudoir or pavilion and can appear as a proper name for shops or venues. It is not commonly used in everyday Cantonese conversation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間舖頭叫「碧玉間」，入面擺設好有古典氣息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 pou3 tau2 giu3 "bik1 juk6 gaan1", jap6 min6 baai2 cit3 hou2 jau5 gu2 din2 hei3 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家店叫做“碧玉间”，里面布置很有古典气息。
examples.english_sentence: This shop is called "Biyu Room"; the interior has a strong classical atmosphere.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 詩人喺詩入面寫到「碧玉間」，形容伊人喺度梳妝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 jan4 hai2 si1 jap6 min6 se2 dou3 "bik1 juk6 gaan1", jing4 joeng4 ji1 jan4 hai2 dou6 sou1 zong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 诗人在诗里写到“碧玉间”，形容佳人在那里梳妆。
examples.english_sentence: A poet wrote about the "Biyu Room" in a poem to describe a lady dressing there.

jyutping: bik1 juk6 gaan1 wong4 gam1 zuk1
mandarin_meaning: 碧玉間黃金竹 (字面：碧綠如玉的物體間夾雜著金黃色的竹子)，為書面或詩詞式的描寫，用來形容圖案或景物色彩華美、對比鮮明
english_meaning: Literary/poetic phrase literally 'green jade interspersed with golden bamboo'; used to describe a richly ornamented motif or an elegant, striking contrast of colors
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 短語（書面/詩詞用法，描述性）
explanation_mandarin: 這是一個偏書面或詩詞化的短語，字面意思為碧綠如玉的色彩中夾雜著金黃色的竹子。通常用來形容工藝品、布料、山水或園林等的圖案與景色華美、色彩對比鮮明，不常用於口語日常會話。
explanation_english: A literary/poetic descriptive phrase meaning literally 'green jade interspersed with golden bamboo.' It is used to describe ornate decorative patterns or elegant scenery with striking color contrasts. It is mainly literary and not common in everyday spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件瓷器上面畫住碧玉間黃金竹，睇落好華貴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 ci4 hei3 soeng6 min6 waa6 zyu6 bik1 juk6 gaan1 wong4 gam1 zuk1, tai2 lok6 hou2 waa4 gwai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件瓷器上畫著碧玉間黃金竹，看起來很華貴。
examples.english_sentence: This piece of porcelain is painted with a motif of green jade interspersed with golden bamboo; it looks very luxurious.

mandarin_meaning: （互相）碰到、相撞；（比喻）正面冲突、碰面
english_meaning: to bump into each other; to collide head-on; to run into; (figuratively) to clash or meet unexpectedly
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，原指兩個物體或人頭部相撞或迎面相遇，引申為意見、利益等正面衝突或意外碰到某人。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression that literally means two people or objects bump heads or collide; extended to mean running into someone unexpectedly or clashing (e.g., in opinions or interests).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我同阿明喺商場入面碰埋頭，真係無諗過會撞到佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 aa3 ming4 hai2 soeng1 coeng4 jap6 min6 pung3 maai4 tau4, zan1 hai6 mou4 lam2 gwo3 wui5 zong6 dou3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我和阿明在商场里碰到，真没想到会遇到他。
examples.english_sentence: I ran into Ah Ming at the mall; I really didn't expect to bump into him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 兩部車喺十字路口碰埋頭，交通一度癱瘓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: loeng5 bou6 ce1 hai2 sap6 zi6 lou6 hau2 pung3 maai4 tau4, gaau1 tung1 jat1 dou6 taan1 wun6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 两辆车在十字路口迎面相撞，交通一度瘫痪。
examples.english_sentence: Two cars collided head-on at the intersection, causing traffic to be paralyzed for a while.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋喺會議上碰埋頭，最後搞到冇共識。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai2 wui6 ji5 soeng6 pung3 maai4 tau4, zeoi3 hau6 gaau2 dou3 mou5 gung6 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们在会议上正面冲突，最后搞得没有共识。
examples.english_sentence: They butted heads in the meeting and ended up with no agreement.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見字，無固定或常見的現代漢語詞義或讀音
english_meaning: A rare/obscure Chinese character with no widely attested modern meaning or pronunciation
explanation_mandarin: 「磌」為生僻漢字，現代資料與用法稀少，通常不出現在日常書寫或口語中。不同古籍或字典中可能有不同標註或註解，但沒有穩定的現代詞義與讀音標準。
explanation_english: “磌” is an obscure character rarely used in modern Chinese. It has no widely established contemporary meaning or pronunciation; references may vary between classical sources and dictionaries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 字「磌」係一個好罕見嘅字，平時好少見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zi6 '（讀音不詳）' hai6 jat1 go3 hou2 hon2 gin3 ge3 zi6, ping4 si4 hou2 siu2 gin3 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 字“磌”是一个很罕见的字，平时很少见到。
examples.english_sentence: The character "磌" is a very rare character and is seldom seen in everyday use.

mandarin_meaning: 切磚刀（用于切割砖块或瓷砖的工具）
english_meaning: brick chisel / tile cutter (a tool used to cut bricks or tiles)
explanation_mandarin: 一種手工工具，用來切割或修整磚塊、瓷磚，常見於砌磚、鋪地或裝修的建築工地上。
explanation_english: A handheld tool used to cut or trim bricks and tiles, commonly found on construction sites for masonry, tiling, and renovation work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 師傅用磚刀切磚，幾準確又快。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 fu2 jung6 zyun1 dou1 cit3 zyun1, gei2 zeon2 kok3 jau6 faai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 师傅用砖刀切砖，很准确又快。
examples.english_sentence: The worker used a brick chisel to cut the bricks — it's accurate and fast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 砌磚牆要準備好磚刀同埋其他工具。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cai3 zyun1 coeng4 jiu3 zeon2 bei6 hou2 zyun1 dou1 tung4 maai4 kei4 taa1 gung1 geoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 砌砖墙要准备好砖刀和其他工具。
examples.english_sentence: To build a brick wall you need to have a brick chisel and other tools ready.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見漢字，現代漢語中無固定或常見的意義與用法
english_meaning: rare/obscure Chinese character with no established modern Cantonese meaning or usage
explanation_mandarin: 「磢」為罕見或古字，現代粵語與普通話資料中沒有一致或常見的詞義與詞性。此字可能出現在古籍、地名或人名中，但在日常語言與口語中並不使用。查詢需參考專門的字典或古籍資料。
explanation_english: The character "磢" is rare or archaic. It has no consistent or commonly attested meaning or part of speech in modern Cantonese or Mandarin. It may appear in historical texts, place names, or personal names, but it is not used in everyday speech. Consult specialist character dictionaries or historical sources for more information.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「磢」好罕見，平時唔會用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 '磢' hou2 hon2 gin3, ping4 si4 m4 wui5 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字「磢」很罕见，平时不会使用。
examples.english_sentence: The character "磢" is rare and not used in everyday language.

mandarin_meaning: 磨蹭、拖延、耗時間（口語）
english_meaning: to dawdle; to procrastinate; to stall and waste time (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，通常指人拖拖拉拉、磨蹭、不快去做事或浪費時間。有時帶有責備語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to dawdle or procrastinate — to stall, mess around, or waste time. Often used reproachfully.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日喺度磨𠺪，啲嘢做唔做好都拖拖拉拉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 mo4 daai2, di1 je5 zou6 m4 zou6 hou2 dou1 to1 to1 laai1 laai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是在那裡磨蹭，事情做得不好，總是拖拖拉拉。
examples.english_sentence: You always dawdle there — your work isn't done well and you're always dragging your feet.

mandarin_meaning: 礼多人不怪（意思是多礼貌不会招人指责，宁可多礼也不要失礼）
english_meaning: Being overly polite is not a problem; it's better to be courteous than rude.
explanation_mandarin: 表示即使舉止看起來過於客氣或繁禮，也不會被人覺得奇怪或責怪，強調寧可多禮以示尊重。
explanation_english: Expresses that excessive politeness is not frowned upon; it's better to show more courtesy than risk being impolite.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 初次見面見到長輩，講多兩句客套話都好，禮多人不怪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: co1 ci3 gin3 min6 gin3 dou2 coeng4 bui3, gong2 do1 loeng5 geoi3 haak3 tou3 waa6 dou1 hou2, lai5 do1 jan4 bat1 gwaai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 第一次见面遇到长辈，多说几句客套话没关系，礼多人不怪。
examples.english_sentence: When meeting elders for the first time, it's fine to say a few polite phrases — being overly polite isn't a problem.

jyutping: san4 zyu2 paai4 dou1 wui5 waak6
mandarin_meaning: 連祖先的牌位都會（受驚／發生反應）；用來誇張地形容事情非常荒謬或令人震驚
english_meaning: Even the ancestral tablet would 'waak' — a hyperbolic Cantonese slang phrase meaning something is so outrageous/shocking that even the ancestral tablet would react; used to emphasize absurdity or shock
explanation_mandarin: 短語由「神主牌」（祖先牌位）和「都會喐」組成。「喐」在這裡帶有擬聲或誇張意味，並非正式漢語詞彙。整句用作誇張性的說法，表示某事非常離譜、令人震驚或不可思議。
explanation_english: The phrase combines "神主牌" (ancestral tablet) with "都會喐" (an onomatopoeic/exaggerated reaction). "喐" here is colloquial and not a standard dictionary word; the whole expression is a hyperbolic Cantonese slang line used to stress that something is extremely absurd, shocking, or unbelievable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嗰樣做法真係無厘頭，神主牌都会喐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go2 joeng6 zou6 faat3 zan1 hai6 mou4 lei4 tau4, san4 zyu2 paai4 dou1 wui5 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他那種做法真是莫名其妙，連神主牌都會喐。
examples.english_sentence: His way of doing things is really nonsensical — it's so absurd that even the ancestral tablet would 'react'.

synonyms: 誇張到連祖先都會覺得離譜

jyutping: san4 sin1 si2, m4 cau3 mai5 hei3
mandarin_meaning: 名不副實，虛有其表，一點價值也沒有
english_meaning: all show and no substance; completely worthless despite grand name
explanation_mandarin: 廣東俚語，用來嘲諷某物或某人看似高級或有價值，但實際上一文不值、名不副實。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to mock something or someone that appears grand or valuable but is actually worthless or all show and no substance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰件賣緊嘅古董根本係仿冒，神仙屎，唔臭米氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gin6 maai6 gan2 ge3 gu2 dung2 gan1 bun2 hai6 fong2 mou6, san4 sin1 si2, m4 cau3 mai5 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那件在賣的古董根本是仿製品，名不副實，一點價值都沒有。
examples.english_sentence: That 'antique' they're selling is a fake — all show and no value.

jyutping: san4 sin1 fong3 pei3, fei1 tung4 faan4 hoeng2
mandarin_meaning: （帶諷刺）指某種說法或自誇荒謬、誇大、不可信，字面上是「神仙放屁」，後半句「非同凡響」是諷刺性的強調
english_meaning: An ironic/sarcastic Cantonese phrase used to call something absurd, exaggerated or unbelievable; literally "gods fart — not ordinary sound."
explanation_mandarin: 這句是粵語口語/俚語，常帶諷刺或貶義，當某人誇大其詞、說法荒謬或不可置信時使用。表面字義荒誕，實際用於否定或嘲弄。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese/slang expression, often sarcastic or derogatory, used to describe claims that are absurd, exaggerated or not credible. The literal imagery is humorous and ironic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嗰啲數據係神仙放屁，非同凡響，根本唔可信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 go2 di1 sou3 geoi3 hai6 san4 sin1 fong3 pei3, fei1 tung4 faan4 hoeng2, gan1 bun2 m4 ho2 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說那些數據簡直胡說八道、荒謬至極，根本不可信。
examples.english_sentence: What he said about the data is complete nonsense and absurd — utterly unbelievable.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）非常走運或幸運的人或情況，常用於描述在賭博、抽獎或其他機會性活動中屢次獲勝或中獎。
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang term meaning extremely lucky (often describing someone who repeatedly wins in gambling, lotteries, or other chance-based events).
explanation_mandarin: 「神仙腳」是香港粵語口語俚語，用來形容某人特別走運、好彩，尤其在賭博、抽獎、打麻將等以機會為主的活動中屢次得利，帶有誇張的戲謔意味。
explanation_english: "神仙腳" is Hong Kong Cantonese slang used to describe someone exceptionally lucky—especially in chance-based activities like gambling, lotteries, or mahjong—often said with a joking or exaggerated tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打麻將真係有神仙腳，成日贏錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 maa4 zoeng1 zan1 hai6 jau5 san4 sin1 goek3, sing4 jat6 jing4 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他打麻將真的很走運，總是贏錢。
examples.english_sentence: He's really lucky at mahjong; he always wins money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次抽獎我竟然中咗，真係有神仙腳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 cau1 zoeng2 ngo5 ging2 jin4 zung3 zo2, zan1 hai6 jau5 san4 sin1 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次抽獎我竟然中了，真是走運。
examples.english_sentence: I actually won the raffle this time — I'm really lucky.

mandarin_meaning: 运气极好，好像有神仙帮忙才能赢/获胜
english_meaning: Extremely lucky (as if aided by gods/immortals); won or succeeded against the odds
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容某人非常幸運或出人意表地贏/成功，彷彿有神仙相助。常用於驚訝或稱讚對方運氣或機緣特別好。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who is extremely lucky or wins in an unbelievable way, as if helped by deities. Used to express astonishment or to praise someone's extraordinary luck or fortune.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚賽馬嗰場，隻冷門馬竟然第一個過終點，真係神仙贏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 coi3 maa5 go2 coeng4, zek3 laang5 mun4 maa5 ging2 jin4 dai6 jat1 go3 gwo3 zung1 dim2, zan1 hai6 san4 sin1 jing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚那場賽馬，冷門馬竟然第一個衝線，真是運氣好到不像話（神仙贏）。
examples.english_sentence: In tonight's horse race, the long-shot actually finished first — what unbelievable luck (like the gods helped).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嗰次考試分數比我高，我都唔知佢點樣做到，簡直神仙贏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go2 ci3 haau2 si3 fan1 sou3 bei2 ngo5 gou1, ngo5 dou1 m4 zi1 keoi5 dim2 joeng6 zou6 dou6, gaan2 zik6 san4 sin1 jing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他那次考試分數比我高，我都不知道他怎麼做到，簡直運氣好得不像話（神仙贏）。
examples.english_sentence: He scored higher than me on that exam — I have no idea how he managed it; it's like he had divine luck.

cantonese: 神仙過鐵橋，穩陣又穩陣
jyutping: san4 sin1 gwo3 tit3 kiu4, wan2 zan6 jau6 wan2 zan6
mandarin_meaning: 形容非常穩妥、非常可靠、穩如泰山
english_meaning: describes something extremely steady, rock-solid, or completely reliable
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語，用來形容人或事非常穩固、不會出差錯或出問題，類似「穩若泰山」或「十拿九穩」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to say someone or something is extremely steady or fail-safe — similar to 'rock-solid' or 'as good as guaranteed.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次投標我哋做好準備，神仙過鐵橋，穩陣又穩陣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 tau4 biu1 ngo5 dei6 zou6 hou2 zeon2 bei6, san4 sin1 gwo3 tit3 kiu4, wan2 zan6 jau6 wan2 zan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次投标我们准备充分，稳若泰山，非常稳妥。
examples.english_sentence: For this bid we prepared thoroughly — rock-solid and totally safe.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打波嗰陣，動作穩晒，真係神仙過鐵橋，穩陣又穩陣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 bo1 go2 zan6, dung6 zok3 wan2 saai3, zan1 hai6 san4 sin1 gwo3 tit3 kiu4, wan2 zan6 jau6 wan2 zan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他打球的时候动作非常稳定，真是稳若泰山。
examples.english_sentence: When he plays, his moves are rock-solid — really steady as can be.

jyutping: san4 jau6 hai6 keoi5, gwai2 jau6 hai6 keoi5
mandarin_meaning: 什麼事都怪到他/他被當成所有事的元兇（帶有諷刺或埋怨意味）
english_meaning: Used to say someone is blamed or held responsible for everything; he's accused of being behind everything (often sarcastic).
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人被過度指責或被當成所有問題的罪魁，語氣常帶埋怨或諷刺。
explanation_english: A colloquial phrase used to describe a person who is blamed for everything or treated as the cause of all problems; often carries a tone of complaint or sarcasm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日出事，樣樣都話係佢，神又係佢，鬼又係佢，真係煩死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 ceot1 si6, joeng6 joeng6 dou1 waa6 hai6 keoi5, san4 jau6 hai6 keoi5, gwai2 jau6 hai6 keoi5, zan1 hai6 faan4 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老是出事，什麼都說是他的錯，總把他當成元兇，真讓人煩惱。
examples.english_sentence: Things keep going wrong and they say it's all his fault — they blame him for everything. It's really annoying.

jyutping: san4 jau6 hai6 keoi5, gwai2 jau6 hai6 keoi5
mandarin_meaning: 凡事都歸在同一個人頭上；什麼事都說是他（的功勞或錯誤）
english_meaning: Everything is attributed to the same person; it's always him — everything gets credited or blamed on that person
explanation_mandarin: 一個廣東話的口語表達，用來形容凡事都牽涉到或要歸咎於同一個人，無論是好事還是壞事，都說是他的緣故。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe situations where everything is linked to or blamed on the same person — whether for credit or fault, that person is held responsible.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺公司入面，乜嘢事都話係阿強，真係神又系佢，鬼又系佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gung1 si1 jap6 min6, mat1 je5 si6 dou1 waa6 hai6 aa3 koeng4, zan1 hai6 san4 jau6 hai6 keoi5, gwai2 jau6 hai6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在公司裡，什麼事都說是阿強，真是什麼事都和他有關／都要怪他。
examples.english_sentence: At the company, everything is said to be Ah Keung's fault (or credit); it's always him for everything.

mandarin_meaning: 比喻被冷落、擱置或長期無人理會（字面是擺在神台上的桔子被陰乾）
english_meaning: To be neglected or shelved for a long time (literally: the altar orange left to dry in the shade)
explanation_mandarin: 原指擺在神台上的桔子被放置到陰乾，用來比喻某事物被長期擱置、沒有人理會或被冷落。
explanation_english: Originally refers to oranges placed on an altar left to dry in the shade. Metaphorically used to describe something that has been left unattended, shelved, or neglected for a long time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲計劃擺咗咁耐，已經係神台桔，陰干啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 gai3 waak6 baai2 zo2 gam2 noi6, ji5 ging1 hai6 san4 toi4 gwat1 jam1 gon1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些計劃擺了那麼久，已經像擺在神台上的桔子一樣陰乾了。
examples.english_sentence: Those projects have been shelved for so long they're like oranges on the altar left to dry.

jyutping: san4 toi4 maau1 si2, san4 zang1 gwai2 jim3
mandarin_meaning: 被所有人憎惡、人人厭惡（非常討厭、令人唾棄）
english_meaning: Detested by everyone; universally loathed; utterly despised.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語或俚語，形容某人或某事物極其討厭、被大家嫌惡與排斥，幾乎無人喜歡或接受。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiomatic/slang expression describing someone or something that is extremely disliked or despised by everyone — universally hated or rejected.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗件事，搞到大家都神台猫屎，神憎鬼厌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 zou6 zo2 gin6 si6, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 san4 toi4 maau1 si2, san4 zang1 gwai2 jim3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做了一件事，搞得大家都對他又恨又厭。
examples.english_sentence: He did something that made everyone utterly despise him.

cantonese: 神臺貓屎 - 人憎鬼厭
jyutping: san4 toi4 maau1 sai2 - jan4 zang1 gwai2 jim3
mandarin_meaning: 人見人嫌；人人厭惡
english_meaning: Universally disliked; detested by everyone
explanation_mandarin: 口語化的粵語表達，用來形容某人或某事物被所有人厭惡、討厭，帶有強烈負面評價與排斥意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe a person or thing that is hated or disliked by everyone; carries a strong negative, off-putting sense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做咗啲嘢得罪晒人，依家成條街啲人都話佢神臺貓屎，人憎鬼厭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 zo2 di1 je5 dak1 zeoi6 saai3 jan4, ji4 gaa1 sing4 tiu4 gaai1 di1 jan4 dou1 waa6 keoi5 san4 toi4 maau1 sai2, jan4 zang1 gwai2 jim3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做了得罪大家的事，現在整條街的人都說他人見人嫌、人人厭惡。
examples.english_sentence: He did things that offended people; now everyone on the street says he's universally disliked.

cantonese: 祭灶鲤鱼，瞌埋双眼乱噏
jyutping: zai3 zou6 lei5 jyu4, hap6 maai4 soeng1 ngaan5 lyun6 aap3
mandarin_meaning: 打瞌睡或醉酒時眼睛半閉、胡言亂語；形容人半醒半醉或恍惚時亂說話
english_meaning: To babble incoherently with eyes half-closed (often when sleepy or drunk); to mutter nonsense in a half-asleep or intoxicated state
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面有押韻成分，常用來形容一個人在瞌睡、半醉或恍惚時眼睛闔住／半闔、說出很多沒邏輯或胡亂的話。語氣偏口語、帶幽默或輕微譏諷。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression (rhyming phrase) used to describe someone who, when half-asleep or drunk, has their eyes half-closed and speaks nonsense. It's informal and often used humorously or with mild derision.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一醉就祭灶鲤鱼，瞌埋雙眼亂噏，乜都講得出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 zeoi3 zau6 zai3 zou6 lei5 jyu4, hap6 maai4 soeng1 ngaan5 lyun6 aap3, mat1 dou1 gong2 dak1 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一醉就瞌着眼睛胡言亂語，什麼都說得出。
examples.english_sentence: When he gets drunk he mumbles with his eyes half-closed, babbling nonsense — he can say anything.

jyutping: bing2 san4 dou1 mou5 geoi3 zan1
mandarin_meaning: 連一句真話都沒有
english_meaning: Not a single true word (completely untruthful)
explanation_mandarin: 表示某人說的話完全不可信，一句真話也沒有，常用於口語或批評對方不誠實或誇大其詞。
explanation_english: Used to say that someone's words are completely untrustworthy — not a single true statement. Commonly used colloquially to criticize someone as dishonest or full of hot air.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日吹水，禀神都冇句真，唔好信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ceoi1 seoi2, bing2 san4 dou1 mou5 geoi3 zan1, m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是吹牛，連一句真話都沒有，別相信他。
examples.english_sentence: He always brags; not a single true word — don't trust him.

mandarin_meaning: 等一下 / 等一會兒（口語）
english_meaning: wait a moment / wait a bit (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「禁等」為粵語口語短語，常見於香港說法。「禁」在此作副詞用，帶有「稍微、一會兒」的意思，與「等」結合成「等一下、等一陣」的意思。屬非正式用法。
explanation_english: “禁等” is a colloquial Cantonese phrase. Here 「禁」 functions as an adverb meaning ‘a little / for a moment’, combined with 「等」 (‘wait’) to mean ‘wait a moment’. It is informal and commonly used in speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你禁等我一陣，好嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 dang2 ngo5 jat1 zan6, hou2 maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你等我一下，好嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Wait for me a moment, ok?

mandarin_meaning: 祭祀用的酒（用來祭拜祖先或神靈的供品）
english_meaning: sacrificial/offering wine (wine used for ancestral or deity offerings)
explanation_mandarin: 「禡酒」指在祭祀、拜祭祖先或神明時所用作供品的酒，屬於傳統禮俗中的祭品之一。用法偏正式或書面，某些方言或古文中較常見。
explanation_english: “禡酒” refers to wine used as an offering in rituals — wine presented when performing ancestral or deity worship. It is a traditional ceremonial offering term, more common in formal/archival or dialectal usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 拜山之前記得帶禡酒同水果去供奉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baai3 saan1 zi1 cin4 gei3 dak1 daai3 maa6 zau2 tung4 seoi2 gwo2 heoi3 gung1 fung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上山祭祖之前記得帶祭酒和水果去供奉。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to bring offering wine and fruit to present before the ancestral worship on the hill.

mandarin_meaning: 相差甚远；远远不够（与事实或目标差距很大）
english_meaning: to be a long way off; to be far from the truth or target
explanation_mandarin: 表示与事实、标准或目标相差很远，通常用于口语，带有夸张语气。
explanation_english: Expresses that something is far off from the truth, standard, or target; commonly used colloquially with an exaggerated tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你話佢會考第一名？離天隔丈遠喇！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 waa6 keoi5 wui5 haau2 dai6 jat1 ming4? lei4 tin1 gaak3 zoeng6 jyun5 laa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你说他会考第一名？差得远呢！
examples.english_sentence: You say he'll get first place? That's nowhere near true!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件貨嘅質素同網上所講離天隔丈遠，唔好信嗰啲廣告。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 fo3 ge3 zat1 sou3 tung4 mong5 soeng6 so2 gong2 lei4 tin1 gaak3 zoeng6 jyun5, m4 hou2 seon3 go2 di1 gwong2 gou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件货的质量和网上所说差得很远，别信那些广告。
examples.english_sentence: The quality of this item is nothing like what was claimed online — don't trust those ads.

mandarin_meaning: 形容杂乱、凌乱、不成体统
english_meaning: chaotic; in disorder; messy
explanation_mandarin: 「离行离迾」是廣東話口語用語，形容事物散亂、雜亂無章或不整齊，有時帶有輕微誇張或嘲諷的語氣。此詞較為口語或方言色彩，書面上不常見。
explanation_english: “离行离迾” is a Cantonese colloquial expression describing something scattered, disorderly, or messy. It often carries a slightly exaggerated or humorous/derogatory tone. The term is chiefly oral and dialectal rather than formal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間屋入面亂到离行离迾，一啲都收唔掂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 uk1 jap6 min6 lyun6 dou3 lei4 haang4 lei4 loeng6, jat1 di1 dou1 sau1 m4 dim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間屋子裡亂得離行離迾，一點也收不完。
examples.english_sentence: This room is a complete mess — it's chaotic, and I can't tidy any of it.

mandarin_meaning: 關押禽獸的牢籠或場所（多為古語或書面用法）；亦可比喻囚禁或限制。
english_meaning: A pen or cage for confining birds and animals (archaic/literary usage); can also be used metaphorically for confinement or restriction.
explanation_mandarin: “禽牢”由“禽”（禽鳥、禽獸）和“牢”（牢籠、監禁處）組成，原指關押禽獸的籠子或場所。此詞現代口語中較少見，常見於古文、書面或描述性的語境，也可用作比喻，表示被限制或囚禁。
explanation_english: Formed from 禽 (birds/animals) and 牢 (cage/prison), it originally refers to a cage or place for keeping birds and animals. The term is now rare in everyday speech and appears mainly in literary or historical contexts; it can also be used metaphorically to mean being confined or restricted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 古時農莊會用禽牢關住啲雞同鴨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 si4 nung4 zong1 wui5 jung6 kam4 lo4 gwaan1 zyu6 di1 gai1 tung4 aap3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 古時農莊會用禽牢關住雞和鴨。
examples.english_sentence: In old farms they would use a pen (禽牢) to confine chickens and ducks.

mandarin_meaning: 字面為「禽鳥與蟾蜍」，古文用語；引申可指卑劣、下賤或禽獸般的人（屬古雅或貶義用法）
english_meaning: Literally 'birds and toads' (classical/literary term); figuratively used to describe a vile, despicable, or beastly person (archaic/pejorative)
explanation_mandarin: 「禽蜍」原為動物名的並列，見於古文或書面語中，有時用來比喻品行卑劣或下賤的人。現代口語中較為少見，帶有文言或貶義色彩。
explanation_english: Originally a compound naming animals (birds and toads) found in classical or literary Chinese. It is sometimes used metaphorically to condemn someone as vile or base. It is relatively rare in modern spoken language and carries an archaic/pejorative tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日利用啲無助嘅人，實在係禽蜍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 lei6 jung6 di1 mou4 zo6 ge3 jan4, sat6 zoi6 hai6 kam4 co4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常利用那些无助的人，实在是禽蜍。
examples.english_sentence: He often takes advantage of helpless people; he's truly despicable.

mandarin_meaning: （非正式用語）網路俚語/罕見詞彙，無固定或廣泛承認的含義，可能為拼音化或圈內用語
english_meaning: (slang/neologism) an informal/rare online term with no widely agreed meaning; possibly a phonetic/in-group expression
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 感嘆詞或名詞（視語境）
explanation_mandarin: 「禾叉」在香港粵語圈中屬於較新或罕見的網路俚語，並無被廣泛收錄的固定意義。常見於留言或社交平台，可能是某些圈子內的戲稱、拼音化詞或打字用語。具體意思需視上下文判斷。
explanation_english: “禾叉” is a relatively new or rare Cantonese online slang term without a widely recorded, fixed meaning. It appears on comments and social platforms and may be an in-group joke, phonetic rendering, or typographical slang. Its specific sense depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我見到有人打「禾叉」喺留言，唔知道佢哋係講緊乜嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gin3 dou2 jau5 jan4 daa2 "wo4 caa1" hai2 lau4 jin4, m4 zi1 dou3 keoi5 dei6 hai6 gong2 gan2 mat1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我看到有人在留言裡打「禾叉」，不確定他們在說什麼。
examples.english_sentence: I saw someone type "禾叉" in the comments; I'm not sure what they mean.

cantonese: 禾怕寒露风，人怕老来穷
jyutping: wo4 paa3 hon4 lou6 fung1, jan4 paa3 lou5 loi4 kung4
mandarin_meaning: 犁地的庄稼怕秋天的寒露和风，人则害怕年老时陷入贫穷（要未雨绸缪、早做打算）。
english_meaning: As crops fear the cold autumn winds, people fear being poor in old age — a proverb advising to prepare early and save for the future.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用農作物怕寒露風來比喻人們擔心年老時沒有錢，提醒大家要早作打算、儲蓄備老。
explanation_english: This proverb compares crops fearing cold autumn winds to people fearing poverty in old age; it urges early planning and saving for retirement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯成日講：「禾怕寒露风，人怕老来穷」，所以佢一直努力储蓄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 sing4 jat6 gong2: 'wo4 paa3 hon4 lou6 fung1, jan4 paa3 lou5 loi4 kung4', so2 ji5 keoi5 jat1 zik6 nou5 lik6 co5 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿伯常說：「禾怕寒露風，人怕老來窮」，所以他一直努力攢錢。
examples.english_sentence: Grandpa often says, 'As crops fear the cold autumn winds, people fear being poor in old age,' so he has been saving diligently.

jyutping: wo4 caat3 dit3 lok6 zeng2, caa1 dou3 dai2
mandarin_meaning: 既然已經陷入或開始了某件事，就徹底做到底；亦可用來形容一旦陷入困境就難以脫身。
english_meaning: Once you're in (or have started), go all the way; also used to describe being stuck in a predicament with little chance of escape. (Similar to "in for a penny, in for a pound" or "see it through to the end".)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語。字面上像說叉子跌入井裡，叉到底，表示既然已經落手做了，就要做到底；有時亦用來形容一旦陷入麻煩就難以脫身。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying. Literally suggests a fork that falls into a well and reaches the bottom — meaning once you're involved, carry it through to the end; it can also describe being trapped in a difficult situation and unable to get out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司已經投咗咁多資金，既然咁就禾汊跌落井，杈到底，唔好半途而廢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ji5 ging1 tau4 zo2 gam2 do1 zi1 gam1, gei3 jin4 gam2 zau6 wo4 caat3 dit3 lok6 zeng2, caa1 dou3 dai2, m4 hou2 bun3 tou4 ji4 fai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司已經投入了這麼多資金，既然如此就做到底，不要半途而廢。
examples.english_sentence: The company has already invested so much capital; since that's the case, go all the way and don't give up halfway.

synonyms: in for a penny, in for a pound

jyutping: 未知（此詞罕見，字形與讀音均不確定）
mandarin_meaning: 外表光鮮但無實質；華而不實（字面意為把珍珠掛在稻秆上，喻價值與載體不相稱）
english_meaning: All show and no substance; superficially decorated or mismatched — literally like hanging pearls on a rice stalk
explanation_mandarin: 此為粵語俗語性表達（字形罕見），用以形容外表漂亮或裝飾華麗但內在空虛、不相配或無實際價值。字面意象為把珍珠掛在禾秆上，暗指前後不相稱或徒有其表。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression (rare/obscure) used to describe something that looks flashy or well-decorated but lacks real substance or is mismatched. The literal image—putting pearls on a rice stalk—suggests an inappropriate or superficial adornment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個project淨係講到好靚，落手做嘅嘢又唔多，真係禾秆𢫏珍珠。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他那個專案只是講得漂亮，實際做的又不多，真是外表光鮮而無實質。
examples.english_sentence: His project only sounds impressive on paper but little work was done — it's really all show and no substance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套衫配咗啲名貴配飾都仲係禾秆𢫏珍珠，唔合適。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這套衣服搭配了昂貴的配飾還是顯得不協調、徒有其表。
examples.english_sentence: Even with expensive accessories, this outfit still looks mismatched and superficial.

mandarin_meaning: 稻苗；準備插秧的幼苗（通常指水田裡的稻苗）
english_meaning: rice seedlings; young rice plants grown for transplanting into paddy fields
explanation_mandarin: 指在育秧田或苗圃裡長成、準備移栽到水田中的稻苗。
explanation_english: Refers to young rice plants grown in nurseries or seedbeds that are ready to be transplanted into paddy fields.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 農夫喺田度插禾秧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nung4 fu1 hai2 tin4 dou6 caap3 ho4 joeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 農夫在田裡插秧。
examples.english_sentence: The farmers are transplanting rice seedlings in the field.

jyutping: wo4 cou2 cyun1 zam1, m4 gwo3 dak1 ngaan5
mandarin_meaning: 看不下去；难以让人接受（不堪入目/无法通过审美）
english_meaning: So unattractive, inappropriate, or poorly put together that one can't bear to look; intolerable; doesn't pass muster.
explanation_mandarin: 形容某物外表、搭配或品質太差、離譜，使人無法接受或看下去，常用於口語場景。
explanation_english: Describes something whose appearance, combination, or quality is so poor or mismatched that people can't accept it or bear to look; used colloquially.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢件衫配得咁離譜，禾草穿针，唔过得眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin6 saam1 pui3 dak1 gam2 lei4 pou2, wo4 cou2 cyun1 zam1, m4 gwo3 dak1 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他把衣服搭配得太離譜，真是看不下去。
examples.english_sentence: He matched his clothes so badly — it's unbearable to look at.

mandarin_meaning: 稻田蝦／田蝦（淡水小蝦，常作食材）
english_meaning: rice-field shrimp / freshwater shrimp (small shrimp commonly used as food)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語中對生活於稻田或淡水環境的小型蝦類的稱呼，常見於華南及農村地區，常用作烹飪食材，也可稱為「田蝦」或「稻田蝦」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese term for small shrimp found in rice paddies or freshwater habitats. Common in southern China and rural areas, these shrimp are often used as a cooking ingredient; also called 'rice-field shrimp' or 'freshwater shrimp.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺魚市場買咗啲禾蝦，今晚用嚟炒飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 jyu4 si5 coeng4 maai5 zo2 di1 wo4 haa1, gam1 maan5 jung6 lai4 caau2 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在魚市買了些稻田蝦，今晚用來炒飯。
examples.english_sentence: We bought some rice-field shrimp at the fish market; we'll use them to make fried rice tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 小人物、小事物；比喻微不足道的人或事（廣東話俚語）
english_meaning: small fry; an insignificant person or thing (Cantonese slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「禾蝦蜢」是香港廣東話的俗稱或俚語，字面上由幾種小生物組合而成，用來比喻渺小、微不足道或不重要的人或事，語氣可帶輕視或不屑。
explanation_english: “禾蝦蜢” is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial/slang term. Literally composed of small creatures, it’s used metaphorically for someone or something insignificant or unimportant, often with a dismissive tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好理啲禾蝦蜢嘢，專心做返你自己嘅嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lei5 di1 wo4 haa1 maang5 je5, zyun1 sam1 zou6 faan1 nei5 zi6 ge3 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要理會那些小人物的事，專心做自己的事情吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't bother with those small fry; focus on your own business.

mandarin_meaning: 穀物、谷物、糧食（指稻、麥等農作物的總稱）
english_meaning: grains; cereals; crops (collective term for cereal crops like rice and wheat)
explanation_mandarin: 「禾谷」為文言或書面用語，泛指稻、麥等穀類作物或穀物總稱，常用於農業或古典文獻中。
explanation_english: A somewhat literary term referring to cereal crops or grains (such as rice and wheat). Used as a collective noun in agricultural contexts or classical texts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 農夫收成咗好多禾谷，今年收成唔錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nung4 fu1 sau1 sing4 zo2 hou2 do1 wo4 guk1, gam1 nin4 sau1 sing4 m4 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 農夫收了很多穀物，今年收成不錯。
examples.english_sentence: The farmer harvested a lot of grain; the harvest this year is pretty good.

mandarin_meaning: 未確認（可能為錯字或罕見字）
english_meaning: Unconfirmed (possibly a typo or an extremely rare/obsolete character)
explanation_mandarin: “禾鈒”一詞在常用粵語詞典與現代中文語料中未見確切記載。鈒字極為罕見或可能為輸入/印刷錯誤。若為錯別字，可能原意為“禾穗”“禾稈”等與穀物相關的詞，或只是兩個字並列的非詞組標記。此詞未有固定詞性或常用釋義。
explanation_english: The term “禾鈒” is not attested in major Cantonese dictionaries or modern Chinese corpora. The character 鈒 is extremely rare or may be a typographical/input error. If it is a mistake, the intended word might be something like “禾穗” (ear of grain) or “禾稈” (rice stalk). There is no established part of speech or standard meaning for this form.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「禾鈒」唔係一個常用字，可能係打錯字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wo4 ? m4 hai6 jat1 go3 soeng4 jung6 zi6, ho2 nang4 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: “禾鈒”不是常用字，可能是打錯字。
examples.english_sentence: '禾鈒' is not a commonly used character/term; it may be a typo.

mandarin_meaning: 年輕／沒經驗的人；菜鳥
english_meaning: a young or inexperienced person; a rookie/greenhorn (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，用來形容年輕或經驗不足的人，根據語境可帶有輕微貶義或中性意味。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang for someone young and inexperienced. Depending on context it can be mildly derogatory or neutral.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱返工，仲係個禾青，咩都唔識做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aap3 aap3 faan1 gung1, zung6 hai6 go3 wo4 cing1, me1 dou1 m4 sik1 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛剛開始上班，還是個菜鳥，什麼都不會做。
examples.english_sentence: He just started working; he's still a rookie and doesn't know how to do anything.

mandarin_meaning: 多到連雞都吃厭（比喻供過於求或過於充裕以致不受重視）
english_meaning: So abundant that even chickens are tired of the grain (metaphor for oversupply or something so common people become indifferent)
explanation_mandarin: 原指農作物豐收到連雞都吃膩了，用來形容某物過多、供過於求或普及到令人不再珍惜。
explanation_english: Originally refers to such a bountiful harvest that even chickens get tired of the grain; used metaphorically to describe an oversupply or such abundance that people no longer value it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年稻穀咁多，真係禾黄鸡厌谷，價錢跌晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 dou6 guk1 gam2 do1, zan1 hai6 wo4 wong4 gai1 jim6 guk1, gaa3 cim4 dit3 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年稻谷這麼多，真是多到連雞都吃厭，價格都跌光了。
examples.english_sentence: This year's rice harvest is so large—there's so much grain even the chickens are sick of it; prices have collapsed.

jyutping: sau3 coi4 sau2 gan1 - baau1 syu1 (syu1)
mandarin_meaning: 「包書（輸）」：認輸、替人承擔輸賠或故意輸掉（口語、俚語）；「秀才手巾」為俗稱，常帶有戲謔意味，形容須屈服或認輸的用法。
english_meaning: "bao-shu (lose)": to concede/accept a loss, to take the loss for someone (colloquial/slang). "sau coi sau gan" (literally 'scholar's handkerchief') is a jocular tag associated with yielding/surrender.
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話口語中，「包書」常用於打麻將、賭博或比賽等語境，表示替別人承擔輸賠或故意認輸以了結局面。前面的「秀才手巾」為俗稱或戲稱，用來形容需要示弱、認輸的狀態，帶有幽默或貶抑色彩，屬地區性俚語。
explanation_english: In Cantonese colloquial usage, "baau1 syu1" (包書) appears in contexts like mahjong, gambling, or contests to mean shouldering the loss for someone else or deliberately conceding. The prefatory tag "sau3 coi4 sau2 gan1" (literally "scholar's handkerchief") is a jocular label implying surrender or accepting defeat. This is regional slang with humorous or mildly pejorative tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 打麻將嗰陣，佢俾人叫去包書，最後輸晒所有錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daa2 maa4 zoeng1 go2 zan6, keoi5 bei2 jan4 giu3 heoi3 baau1 syu1, zeoi3 hau6 syu1 saai3 so2 jau5 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 打麻将的时候，他被叫去包书，最后把所有钱都输光了。
examples.english_sentence: While playing mahjong, he was asked to "bao-shu" (take the loss), and in the end he lost all his money.

jyutping: sau3 coi4 sau2 gan1, baau1 syu1 (syu1)
mandarin_meaning: 形容只會裝模作樣、外表像書生但沒有真本事，常帶有嘲諷意味，暗指表面功夫多、實際能力差，最後輸掉或失敗。
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang/idiom used to mock someone who puts on a scholarly or pretentious appearance but lacks real ability — all show and no substance; likely to fail or lose.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語 / 俚語（成語性質）
explanation_mandarin: 「秀才手巾，包書（輸）」是一句粵語俗語，用來形容那些外表裝作書生、耍些書卷氣或做表面功夫，但實際上沒有真才實學，最後往往吃虧或失敗。語中以「書」與「輸」諧音，帶有嘲諷與雙關。
explanation_english: This Cantonese saying ridicules people who affect a scholarly air (like a 'scholar with a handkerchief wrapping books') but lack real skills. The phrase plays on the homophone of 'book' and 'lose' in Cantonese, carrying a mocking, double-meaning tone: showy yet likely to lose.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識得扮秀才手巾、包書（輸），實際上冇真本事，做事成日出錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 dak1 baan6 sau3 coi4, sau2 gan1, baau1 syu1 (syu1), sat6 zai3 soeng6 mou5 zan1 bun2 si6, zou6 si6 sing4 jat6 ceot1 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會裝出書生樣子、做做表面功夫，實際上沒有真本事，做事老是出錯。
examples.english_sentence: He only puts on a scholarly act and does surface-level stuff; in reality he has no real ability and keeps making mistakes.

jyutping: sau3 coi4 kap1 ngaan5 fan3, zam2 zyu6 syu1
mandarin_meaning: 比喻學習或做事時打盹、鬆懈，容易失敗／吃虧
english_meaning: Literally 'the scholar dozes off, resting his head on a book (book/lose)'; an idiom warning that dozing off or being lax while studying/working leads to failure — criticizes complacency or laziness.
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俗語用形象的畫面：讀書人打瞌睡、枕著書。句中利用「書」和「輸」同音的雙關，指出因為懶散、不專心而導致失敗或吃虧，常用來提醒學生或責備敷衍了事的人。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb paints the image of a scholar dozing with his head on a book. It plays on the homophone between 'book' (syu1) and 'lose' (syu1) to imply that being lax or inattentive while studying or working will lead to failure. It's used to warn students or criticize complacency and half‑hearted effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做『秀才瞌眼瞓，枕住書』，讀書要專心先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 'sau3 coi4 kap1 ngaan5 fan3, zam2 zyu6 syu1', duk6 syu1 jiu3 zyun1 sam1 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別做『秀才打瞌睡、枕著書』，讀書要專心才行。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a 'scholar who dozes off with his head on a book' — study attentively if you want to succeed.

mandarin_meaning: 私下聚會 / 非法或未登記的私人聚會（有時含非法賭博或未經許可的活動）
english_meaning: a private/secret gathering — an unofficial meeting or event, sometimes implying illicit activities (e.g., illegal gambling or unlicensed events)
explanation_mandarin: 「私夥局」是粵語俗語，指私下舉辦的聚會或活動，通常規模較小且不公開，有時暗含非法或未獲許可的性質，例如私下賭局或無牌經營的聚會。
explanation_english: “私夥局” is Cantonese slang for a private, unofficial gathering. It often refers to small, secretive meetups and can imply illicit or unlicensed activities, such as clandestine gambling sessions or unregulated events.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大家唔好去佢哋嗰個私夥局，聽講有賭博成份，好危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 gaa1 m4 hou2 heoi3 keoi5 dei6 go2 go3 si1 fo2 guk6, teng1 gong2 jau5 dou2 bok3 sing4 fan6, hou2 ngai4 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大家不要去他们那个私夥局，听说有赌博成分，很危险。
examples.english_sentence: Don't go to their private gathering — I heard there's gambling involved; it's dangerous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲人會喺屋企搞私夥局，食飯飲嘢，唔想公開。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 jan4 wui5 hai2 uk1 kei2 gaau2 si1 fo2 guk6, sik6 faan6 jam2 je5, m4 soeng2 gung1 hoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些人会在家里办私夥局，吃饭喝酒，不想公开。
examples.english_sentence: Some people hold private get-togethers at home to eat and drink, and they don't want it publicized.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方收到舉報，有間茶餐廳暗地裡辦私夥局，已經去調查。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging2 fong1 sau1 dou3 geoi2 bou3, jau5 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 am3 dei6 leoi5 baan6 si1 fo2 guk6, ji5 ging1 heoi3 diu6 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方接到举报，有间茶餐厅暗中举办私夥局，已经在调查。
examples.english_sentence: The police received a tip-off that a cha chaan teng was secretly hosting private gatherings; they're investigating.

cantonese: 秋分天气白，唔忧冇饭喫
jyutping: cau1 fan1 tin1 hei3 baak6, m4 jau1 mou5 faan6 sik6
mandarin_meaning: 秋分天晴，不用担心没饭吃
english_meaning: If the sky is clear at the autumnal equinox, you don't need to worry about having no food (a bright sign of a good harvest).
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東俗諺，意思是秋分時若天氣晴朗、天空明亮，通常預示收成良好，因此不用擔心缺糧或沒飯吃。常用於預測農業收成或安慰他人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese folk proverb meaning that clear/bright weather at the autumnal equinox is taken as a sign of a good harvest, so there's no need to worry about food shortages. It's used to predict harvest outcomes or to reassure people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家係秋分，天氣白，唔忧冇饭喫，農田嘅收成應該會好啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 hai6 cau1 fan1, tin1 hei3 baak6, m4 jau1 mou5 faan6 sik6, nung4 tin4 ge3 sau1 sing4 jing1 goi1 wui5 hou2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在是秋分，天气晴朗，不用担心没饭吃，田里的收成应该会好一些。
examples.english_sentence: It's the autumnal equinox and the sky is clear — no need to worry about going hungry; the fields' harvest should be better.

jyutping: cau1 hau6 sin3, mou5 jan4 hau2
mandarin_meaning: 事后抱怨或发难已无用、无人理会
english_meaning: Complaining or protesting after the opportunity has passed is useless; nobody will respond
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，形容等到事情已经结束或时机过去才抱怨、发难，通常已经没有效果或没人理会。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying meaning that complaining or trying to settle scores after the event is futile — by then it's too late and no one will respond.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家先發現問題，秋后扇，冇人吼啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 sin1 faat3 jin6 man6 tai4, cau1 hau6 sin3, mou5 jan4 hau2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你现在才发现问题，事后抱怨也没人理会。
examples.english_sentence: You only discovered the problem now; complaining afterward won't get anyone's attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等到比人走咗先嚟罵，秋后扇，冇人吼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 dou3 bei2 jan4 zau2 zo2 sin1 lai4 maa6, cau1 hau6 sin3, mou5 jan4 hau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等到人已经走了才来骂，事后抱怨没人搭理。
examples.english_sentence: If you wait until they've already left to scold, it's too late — nobody will reply.

mandarin_meaning: 秋天的茄子（秋季上市的茄子）
english_meaning: autumn eggplant; eggplant in season in autumn
explanation_mandarin: 指在秋季成熟或上市的茄子，常用於描述當季食材的風味或品質。
explanation_english: Refers to eggplants that mature or are harvested in autumn; used to describe seasonal produce and its taste or quality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家係秋天，啲秋茄好甜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 hai6 cau1 tin1, di1 cau1 ke4 hou2 tim4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在是秋天，秋茄很甜。
examples.english_sentence: It's autumn now; autumn eggplants are very sweet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗一斤秋茄嚟煮晚飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 jat1 gan1 cau1 ke4 lai4 zyu2 maan5 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我买了一斤秋茄来做晚饭。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a catty of autumn eggplants to cook for dinner.

jyutping: cau1 fung1 hei2, saam1 se4 fei4
mandarin_meaning: 秋风一起，蛇就变肥了（谚语）
english_meaning: When the autumn wind rises, snakes grow fat (proverb)
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語俗語，字面意思是秋風一吹，蛇會變肥。描述季節性生態現象：秋季動物吃得飽、為過冬儲備能量。也可用作比喻，指某些事物在特定時節趁勢興旺或更容易出現（例如害獸或問題在有利季節更活躍）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally meaning 'when the autumn wind rises, snakes grow fat.' It comments on a seasonal natural phenomenon—animals fatten up in autumn to prepare for winter. Figuratively it can warn that certain things (or problems) thrive when conditions favor them, or note a period of abundance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 秋風起，三蛇肥，去行山要小心啲，唔好亂摸草叢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cau1 fung1 hei2, saam1 se4 fei4, heoi3 haang4 saan1 jiu3 siu2 sam1 di1, m4 hou2 lyun6 mo2 cou2 cung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 秋风一起，蛇就会长得很胖，去爬山要小心点，不要乱摸草丛。
examples.english_sentence: When the autumn wind starts, snakes get fat — be careful when hiking and don't touch the bushes.

mandarin_meaning: 古代的一種穀物（類似黍、稷），亦見於地名（如秭歸）
english_meaning: an ancient type of grain/millet (similar to shu or ji); also appears in place names (e.g. Zigui)
explanation_mandarin: 「秭」本為禾本科作物名，古籍中用以指某類黍稷；現多見於地名，如湖北的「秭歸」。
explanation_english: The character originally names a type of cereal (a kind of millet) in ancient texts; today it is often seen in place names such as Zigui (秭歸).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 秭歸係湖北一個縣，喺長江邊有名。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zi2 gwai1 hai6 wu1 buk6 jat1 go3 jyun2, hai2 coeng4 gong1 bin1 jau5 meng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 秭归是湖北的一个县，位于长江边很有名。
examples.english_sentence: Zigui is a county in Hubei, famous for being on the Yangtze River.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 古代人可能種秭嚟做主食，類似其他黍稷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 doi6 jan4 ho2 nang4 zung6 zi2 lai4 zou6 zyu2 sik6, leoi6 ci5 kei4 taa1 syu2 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 古代人可能种秭来做主食，类似其他黍稷。
examples.english_sentence: In ancient times people may have grown 'zi' millet as a staple, similar to other cereals like shu or ji.

mandarin_meaning: 挤挤挨挨 / 紧挨在一起
english_meaning: squeezed together; huddled up; packed closely
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，用來形容人或物緊挨在一起、擠在一處或聚集得很密集。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression describing people or things packed closely together or huddled up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 地鐵上啲人積積埋埋，好難企得舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dei6 tit3 soeng5 di1 jan4 zik1 zik1 maai4 maai4, hou2 naan4 kei5 dak1 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 地铁上人挤挤挨挨，很难站得舒服。
examples.english_sentence: On the subway people were squeezed together; it's hard to stand comfortably.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路哋積積埋埋坐喺一張長椅上睇書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 dei6 zik1 zik1 maai4 maai4 co5 hai2 jat1 zoeng1 coeng4 ji2 soeng6 tai2 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子挤挤挨挨坐在一张长椅上看书。
examples.english_sentence: The kids sat huddled together on one long bench reading.

jyutping: cing1 fu1 jan4 siu2, dak1 sat1 jan4 do1
mandarin_meaning: 表面上只點名或牽涉少數人，但實際上牽涉到很多人的得失或利益。
english_meaning: Although only a few people are named or addressed, many people's gains and losses (or interests) are affected.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來提醒：看似只關係少數人的決定或稱呼，實際上可能會影響到更多人的利益或感受，應該顧及更廣的影響範圍。
explanation_english: This proverb warns that a decision or recognition that appears to involve only a few people can actually affect many others' interests or feelings; it advises considering the wider impact.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司淨係表揚幾個人，結果其他人唔開心，正所謂『稱呼人少，得失人多』。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1si1 zing6hai6 biu2joeng4 gei2 go3 jan4, git3gwo2 kei4taa1 jan4 m4 hoi1sam1, zing3 so2 wai6 "cing1 fu1 jan4 siu2, dak1 sat1 jan4 do1".
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司只表扬几个人，结果其他人不开心，正所谓“称呼人少，得失人多”。
examples.english_sentence: The company only praised a few people, and as a result others felt unhappy — as the saying goes, 'fewer are named, but more gain or lose.'

cantonese: 程咬金三十六路板斧，出齐
jyutping: cing4 ngaau5 gam1 saam1 sap6 luk6 lou6 baan2 fu2, ceot1 cai4
mandarin_meaning: 把所有的招数都使出来；拿出全部本领。
english_meaning: To show all one's tricks or techniques; to pull out all the stops.
explanation_mandarin: 源自关于程咬金的传说，‘三十六路板斧’指各式招法，‘出齐’即全部使出。用来形容在关键时刻把所有招数或本领都拿出来使，或把所有手段一次性展示出来。
explanation_english: Derived from folklore about Cheng Yaojin; 'thirty-six tricks' refers to many moves and 'come out all' means to use them all. It describes pulling out every trick or showing all one's skills, especially at a crucial moment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今場比賽好似將程咬金三十六路板斧都出齊喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 coeng4 bei2 coi3 hou2 ci5 zoeng1 cing4 ngaau5 gam1 saam1 sap6 luk6 lou6 dou1 ceot1 cai4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他这场比赛好像把程咬金三十六路板斧都使出来了。
examples.english_sentence: In this match he seemed to pull out all thirty-six of Cheng Yaojin's tricks.

mandarin_meaning: 點算錢；清點、核對現金或款項
english_meaning: to count/check money; to verify cash or payments
explanation_mandarin: 「稽錢」是廣東話口語，指清點、核對現金或款項，通常用於收銀、結算或查賬的情境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to count, check, or audit cash/payments; commonly used when verifying amounts at a register or during settlement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 店員喺收銀櫃台度稽錢，確保無錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dim3 jyun4 hai2 sau1 ngan4 gwai6 toi4 dou6 gai1 cin2, kok3 bou2 mou5 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 店員在收銀台點算錢，確保沒有錯誤。
examples.english_sentence: The cashier counted the money at the register to make sure there were no mistakes.

mandarin_meaning: 默默積德、行善而不張揚（積累隱性的功德）
english_meaning: to accumulate merit or good deeds quietly/without seeking recognition; to build up 'hidden' merit
explanation_mandarin: 指在背後或不張揚地做善事、積累功德，通常帶有為將來或他人留福的含義。
explanation_english: A Cantonese idiom meaning to perform good deeds quietly and accrue merit without publicity; often implies building up blessings or karmic credit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢平時幫人做嘢唔張揚，真係積陰功。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ping4 si4 bong1 jan4 zou6 je5 m4 zoeng1 joeng4, zan1 hai6 zik1 jam1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他平時幫人做事不張揚，真是在積陰功。
examples.english_sentence: He helps others quietly without showing off — he's truly accumulating merit in secret.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽話做好事唔使張揚，積陰功自然會有回報。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 waa6 zou6 hou2 si6 m4 sai2 zoeng1 joeng4, zik1 jam1 gung1 zi6 jin4 wui5 jau5 wui4 bou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽說做好事不必張揚，積陰功自然會有回報。
examples.english_sentence: My mother says you don't need to publicize doing good — accumulating hidden merit will naturally bring rewards.

cantonese: 穷人一条牛，性命在上头
jyutping: hung4 jan4 jat1 tiu4 ngau4, sing3 ming6 zoi6 soeng6 tau4
mandarin_meaning: 窮人只有一頭牛，性命（生計）完全依賴它
english_meaning: For a poor person, a single cow represents their whole livelihood; their life depends on it.
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用形象的說法表達窮人只有一樣重要的財產或生計來源，因此必須特別珍惜和保護，暗含生活依賴單一資源的脆弱。
explanation_english: This proverb uses a vivid image to say that a poor person may have only one important asset or source of livelihood, so they must cherish and protect it. It implies the vulnerability of relying on a single resource.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯聽到就話：「穷人一条牛，性命在上头。」佢意思係話窮人淨係得嗰樣嘢，生活全靠佢，唔可以亂嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 teng1 dou3 zau6 waa6: hung4 jan4 jat1 tiu4 ngau4, sing3 ming6 zoi6 soeng6 tau4. keoi5 ji3 si1 hai6 waa6 hung4 jan4 zing6 hai6 dak1 go2 joeng6 je5, saang1 wut6 cyun4 kou3 keoi5, m4 ho2 ji5 lyun6 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老伯聽了說：「窮人一條牛，性命在上頭。」他的意思是窮人只有那一樣家當，生活全靠它，不能輕易放棄。
examples.english_sentence: The old man said, 'For a poor person, a single cow is everything; their life depends on it.' He meant that if a poor person only has that one asset, their livelihood relies on it and they must protect it.

mandarin_meaning: 窮到極點／窮得要命（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: extremely poor; so broke you can't afford basic necessities (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，形容非常窮、窮到無法解決基本生活開支或陷入困境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression describing being extremely poor or broke to the point of being unable to afford basic needs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家真係窮到燶，連飯都買唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 zan1 hai6 kung4 dou3 laan6, lin4 faan6 dou1 maai5 m4 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在真的窮到極點，連飯都買不到。
examples.english_sentence: I'm so broke right now I can't even afford a meal.

mandarin_meaning: （口語、罕見）放鬆、閒適、無憂無慮
english_meaning: (colloquial, rare) to chill; to relax and be at peace; to have free, worry‑free time
explanation_mandarin: 「空康寧」並非標準書面用語，屬口語或新創用法。字面上可拆為「空」（空閒）與「康寧」（安康、寧靜），合起來可理解為「閒著、放鬆並保持安寧」，用來表示想休息、歇息或悠閒地過一段時間。
explanation_english: "空康寧" is not a standard written term but a colloquial/rare coinage. Literally combining "空" (free/idle) and "康寧" (health/peace), it conveys the idea of having leisure and peaceful relaxation. It’s used to mean wanting to chill, rest, or take a peaceful break.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家我想空康寧一下，唔想見人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gaa1 ngo5 soeng2 hung1 hong1 ning4 jat1 haa6, m4 soeng2 gin3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在我想放鬆一下，不想見人。
examples.english_sentence: I want to chill for a bit; I don't want to see anyone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 放假就好好空康寧，唔好成日出去走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fong3 gaa3 zau6 hou2 hou2 hung1 hong1 ning4, m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 ceot1 heoi3 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 放假的時候就好好放鬆，不要整天到處跑。
examples.english_sentence: On holiday, really relax — don't be out and about all the time.

mandarin_meaning: 空洞的外殼；表面光鮮但沒有實質內容（俚語、口語用法，詞語較罕見或地區性）
english_meaning: an empty shell; superficial; all show and no substance (slang/colloquial; rare or regionally used)
explanation_mandarin: 「空框唥」並非標準書面詞彙，常用於粵語口語或俚語語境，用來形容某事物只有外表的框架或形式，缺乏實際內容或作用。此詞較罕見或屬地區性用語，具貶義。
explanation_english: “空框唥” is not a standard literary term; used in Cantonese colloquial/slang contexts to describe something that has only an outward frame or form but lacks substantive content or function. The term is relatively rare or region-specific and carries a derogatory sense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嗰個計劃好似一個空框唥，冇乜實際可行性。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go2 go3 gai3waak6 hou2 ci5 jat1 go3 hung1 kwaang1 laang6, mou5 mat1 sat6zat1 ho2 hang4 sing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的那個計劃像個空框唥，沒有什麼實際可行性。
examples.english_sentence: His plan is like an empty shell — it has little real feasibility.

cantonese: 空棺材出殡，木（目）中无人
jyutping: hung1 gwaan1 coi4 ceot1 ban3, muk6 zung1 mou4 jan4
mandarin_meaning: 徒有虛表、沒有實質內容且自以為是；目中無人
english_meaning: All show and no substance; arrogant and contemptuous of others
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俗語/成語，作形容詞或謂語短語
explanation_mandarin: 這句話把「空棺材出殡」比喻為徒有外表、沒有實質內容的排場，「目中無人（木中無人）」表示目中沒有人、看不起別人。合起來用來形容人虛有其表又自以為是、瞧不起他人。
explanation_english: The phrase uses “an empty coffin sent off” to suggest a showy but hollow display, while “muk6 zung1 mou4 jan4” (目中無人) means seeing no one — i.e., looking down on others. Together they describe someone who is all show, lacking substance, and arrogantly contemptuous of others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日好自大，簡直係空棺材出殡，目中無人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hou2 zi6 daai6, gaan2 zik6 hai6 hung1 gwaan1 coi4 ceot1 ban3, muk6 zung1 mou4 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天很自大，簡直是徒有虛名、目中無人。
examples.english_sentence: He's always so arrogant — basically all show and no substance, looking down on everyone.

mandarin_meaning: 被放到柜子/抽屉的底层，比喻被搁置、被忽视或被冷落
english_meaning: To be put at the bottom of a drawer — figuratively to be shelved, neglected, or ignored
explanation_mandarin: 俗語或俚語用法，原意把東西放到櫃桶底部，延伸義指某事或某人被擱置、不被重視或暫時無法推行。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression. Literally to put something at the bottom of a drawer; figuratively it means a matter or person has been shelved, neglected, or put aside and not acted on.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份計劃已經畀老細穿柜桶底，暫時冇得做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gai3 waak6 ji5 ging1 bei2 lou5 sai3 cyun1 gwai6 tung4 dai2, zaam6 si4 mou5 dak1 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个计划已经被老板搁置在抽屉底下，暂时没法执行。
examples.english_sentence: This project has been shelved by the boss and can't be carried out for now.

mandarin_meaning: 装死／躲避责任（俚语，口语用法）
english_meaning: to play dead; to shirk responsibility / feign ignorance (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 此詞為廣東話口語俚語，字面上為「穿（戴）田螺」，用來形容遇到問題或責任時故意裝作不理會、逃避或假裝無辜。此用法較口語化，帶有輕微貶義，部分地區或群體可能較少使用或視為地方俚語。
explanation_english: This is a Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "to wear a snail." Figuratively it describes deliberately playing dead, shirking responsibility, or feigning ignorance when faced with a problem. It's informal, mildly pejorative, and may be regionally or socially restricted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢遇到問題就成日穿𡰪田螺，唔肯面對。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jyu6 dou3 man6 tai4 zau6 sing4 jat6 cyun1 laan6 tin4 lo4, m4 hang2 min6 deoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他遇到问题就经常穿𡰪田螺，不肯面对。
examples.english_sentence: Whenever he faces a problem he always 'plays dead' and refuses to face it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再穿𡰪田螺啦，快啲幫手做！
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 cyun1 laan6 tin4 lo4 laa1, faai3 di1 bong1 sau2 zou6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再穿𡰪田螺了，快點幫忙做！
examples.english_sentence: Stop shirking and help out quickly!

mandarin_meaning: 窒息；使人感到悶塞、不舒服；（口語）令人尷尬或窘迫
english_meaning: to choke/suffocate; to feel stifled or suffocated; (colloquial) to feel awkward or uncomfortable
explanation_mandarin: 「窒」可指物理上窒息或呼吸受阻，也可用作口語，形容令人感到悶、尷尬或不自在，或事物阻滯不通。
explanation_english: “窒” can mean physical suffocation or obstruction of breathing. Colloquially it describes feeling stifled, uncomfortable, awkward, or that something is blocked/stalled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢被濃煙嗰陣窒到呼吸唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei6 nung4 jin1 go2 zan6 zat1 dou3 fu1 kap1 m4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被濃煙嗆到，窒息得不能呼吸。
examples.english_sentence: He was choked by the thick smoke and couldn't breathe.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個冷場真係好窒，大家都唔知講乜好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 laang5 coeng4 zan1 hai6 hou2 zat1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zi1 gong2 mat1 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這場冷場真的讓人覺得窒悶，大家都不知道說什麼好。
examples.english_sentence: This awkward silence is really suffocating; nobody knows what to say.

mandarin_meaning: 窈（yǎo）：深邃、幽靜；常見於「窈窕」一詞，表示秀麗、婀娜
english_meaning: An archaic/literary adjective meaning deep or secluded; appears in the compound '窈窕' meaning graceful/slim
explanation_mandarin: 古漢語用字，常見於「窈窕」，本義指幽深、隱秘，引申為纖秀、優雅的樣子。
explanation_english: An archaic literary character often seen in the compound '窈窕'. Its original sense is deep/secluded and it is extended to mean slender/graceful in classical phrases.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢睇落窈窕，行路姿態好優雅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tai2 lok6 jiu2 tiu2, haang4 lou6 zi1 taai3 hou2 jau1 ngaa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她看起來窈窕，走路姿態很優雅。
examples.english_sentence: She looks graceful; her gait is very elegant.

cantonese: 窗外吹喇叭，鸣（名）声在外
jyutping: coeng1 ngoi6 ceoi1 laa3 baa1, ming4 sing1 zoi6 ngoi6
mandarin_meaning: 把事情或吹嘘之事在外面宣扬；私事或內部情況被傳出去／聲名外傳
english_meaning: To blow a horn outside the window; figuratively, to make something public or to let boasting/private matters be exposed so that reputation/noise spreads outside
explanation_mandarin: 比喻把本該在內部處理或不宜公開的事情宣揚出去，或指張揚、吹噓以致名聲傳開。
explanation_english: A proverb-like expression meaning to publicize something that should remain private, or to boast/show off so that news or reputation spreads beyond where it should.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲係我哋屋企嘅私事，唔好喺街度講，免得窗外吹喇叭，名聲在外。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 hai6 ngo5 dei6 uk1 kei2 ge3 si1 si6, m4 hou2 hai2 gaai1 dou6 gong2, min5 dak1 coeng1 ngoi6 ceoi1 laa3 baa1, ming4 sing1 zoi6 ngoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些是我们家的私事，不要在街上说，免得传出去，名声在外。
examples.english_sentence: This is a private family matter; don't talk about it in public, or it will get out and people will know about it.

mandarin_meaning: 突然／忽然
english_meaning: suddenly; abruptly
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示事情在沒有預警下突然發生或變化，多用於廣東話日常對話中。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese adverb meaning that something happens abruptly or without warning; commonly used in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢窟忽走咗，冇同我講一聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kut3 fat1 zau2 zo2, mou5 tung4 ngo5 gong2 jat1 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然走了，沒跟我說一聲。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly left without telling me.

mandarin_meaning: 縫隙；裂縫；漏洞
english_meaning: a crack, gap, crevice; a loophole or small opening
explanation_mandarin: 指小的縫隙、裂縫或漏洞。既可用於具體的物理裂縫，也可引申為制度、文件或說話中的漏洞或可乘之機。
explanation_english: Refers to a small gap, crack, crevice, or loophole. It can be used literally for physical cracks or figuratively for vulnerabilities or loopholes in rules, contracts, or statements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 牆有啲窿罅，要補一補先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: coeng4 jau5 di1 lung4 hat6, jiu3 bou2 jat1 bou2 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 牆上有些裂縫，要先補一補。
examples.english_sentence: There are some cracks in the wall; we need to patch them up first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 條合約有啲窿罅，律師話要改。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tiu4 hap6 joek3 jau5 di1 lung4 hat6, leot6 si1 waa6 jiu3 goi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 合同有一些漏洞，律師說要修改。
examples.english_sentence: The contract has some loopholes; the lawyer says it needs revision.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺我講嘢嗰度搵窿罅推卸責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 ngo5 gong2 je5 go2 dou6 wan2 lung4 hat6 teoi1 se6 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在我說的話裡面找漏洞推卸責任。
examples.english_sentence: Don't look for loopholes in what I said to avoid taking responsibility.

mandarin_meaning: 巧妙；靈巧、巧智
english_meaning: ingenious; clever; skillful
explanation_mandarin: 表示方法或主意十分巧妙、靈活、有技巧，常用來稱讚解決問題或處理事務的手段或想法。
explanation_english: Describes a method, idea, or approach that is very clever, ingenious, or skillful; often used to praise an effective or artful way of solving a problem.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢諗法真係竅妙，解決問題好有一套。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lam2 faat3 zan1 hai6 hiu3 miu6, gaai2 kyut3 man6 tai4 hou2 jau5 jat1 tou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他想法真巧妙，解決問題很有一套。
examples.english_sentence: His way of thinking is really ingenious; he's very good at solving problems.

mandarin_meaning: 字面為「灶上的蝦」。粵語俚語（地區性、用法較少見），通常用來指在廚房忙碌、幫手做雜務的人；有時也用作對小巧、靈活或在家庭裡負責煮食者的戲稱。具體含義視語境而定，並非標準普通話詞彙。
english_meaning: Literally "stove shrimp." A regional Cantonese slang term (rare/colloquial). Often jokingly refers to someone who is constantly busy in the kitchen or a small/fidgety person who helps with cooking/household chores. Meaning depends on context.
explanation_mandarin: 「竈蝦」為粵語口語、地區性用語，字面是「灶/爐上的蝦」。在日常語境中多用來形容常在廚房忙碌或幫手做雜務的人，有時帶戲謔或親暱的語氣。此詞較少見且非正式。
explanation_english: A colloquial, regionally used Cantonese term literally meaning "stove/shrine shrimp." In everyday use it usually nicknames someone who is always busy in the kitchen or helps with small household/cooking tasks. Usage is informal, joking or affectionate, and relatively rare.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日自告奮勇落廚，屋企人都笑佢係竈蝦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zi6 gou3 fan5 jung5 lok6 ceoi4, uk1 kei2 jan4 dou1 siu3 keoi5 hai6 zou6 haa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是主動下廚，家人都笑他是「竈蝦」。
examples.english_sentence: He always volunteers to cook; the family teases him as a "stove shrimp."

mandarin_meaning: （罕見/疑義）字面為「灶馬」，可能指廚房相關的事物或職位，現代粵語中已罕見或無明確用法。
english_meaning: (rare/uncertain) Literally 'stove/oven horse'; possibly refers to a kitchen-related object or role; obsolete or not attested in contemporary Cantonese.
explanation_mandarin: 「竈馬」為罕見或古舊詞彙，字面由「竈/灶」與「馬」組成。現代粵語資料中缺乏清晰例證，可能為方言或舊時對某種廚房用具、位置或幫手的稱呼。若需精確語義，應查閱地方志或古籍資料以求考證。
explanation_english: A rare or archaic term composed of '竈' (stove/kitchen) and '馬' (horse). There are few or no clear attestations in modern Cantonese; it may once have referred to a kitchen implement, a role, or an assistant. For a precise meaning consult local dialect records or historical sources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺舊書入面見過「竈馬」呢個詞，但唔清楚係乜意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gau6 syu1 jap6 min6 gin3 gwo3 "zou6 maa5" ni1 go3 ci4, daan6 m4 cing1 co2 hai6 mat1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在舊書裡見過「竈馬」這個詞，但不清楚是什麼意思。
examples.english_sentence: I saw the term "竈馬" in an old book, but I don't know what it means.

mandarin_meaning: （香港俚語）在立交橋或高架路上搶道、亂插隊或以危險方式駕駛，帶有炫耀或招搖的含義
english_meaning: Hong Kong slang for cutting across lanes or hogging an interchange/overpass; reckless or show-off driving behavior on flyovers
explanation_mandarin: 「立交撟」為香港口語俗語，字面由「立交（橋）」和「撟」組成，用來形容在立交橋或高架路上以魯莽、搶道或炫耀方式行車，往往會造成危險或阻塞交通。屬非正式、地區性用語。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong colloquial/slang term combining 'interchange/overpass' with a verb-like element; it describes cutting across lanes, hogging an interchange, or driving recklessly/showing off on flyovers. It is informal and region-specific.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺立交撟啦，咁樣好危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 lap6 gaau1 giu1 laa1, gam2 joeng6 hou2 ngai4 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在立交上搶道，這樣很危險。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cut across on the overpass; that's dangerous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 有啲車成日喺立交撟，搞到成條路塞車。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jau5 di1 ce1 seng4 jat6 hai2 lap6 gaau1 giu1, gaau2 dou3 seng4 tiu4 lou6 sak1 ce1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有些車經常在立交橋上搶道，造成整條路塞車。
examples.english_sentence: Some cars often cut across on the interchange, causing the whole road to jam.

cantonese: 立冬过三朝，田上冇青苗
jyutping: laap6 dung1 gwo3 saam1 ziu1, tin4 soeng5 mou5 cing1 miu4
mandarin_meaning: 立冬过了三朝，田里还没有青苗（谚语），意思是耕种过晚或错过时机，可能颗粒无收。
english_meaning: If by three mornings after the Start of Winter there are no green seedlings in the fields (proverb): sowing or starting too late leads to crop failure — a warning about missing the right timing.
explanation_mandarin: 这句俗语来自农业经验：若到立冬后仍无苗，说明播种太晚或管理有问题，今季可能收成不好。引申为比喻错过最佳时机就很难有好结果。
explanation_english: A farming proverb: if there are no seedlings shortly after the Start of Winter, sowing was too late and the crop will likely fail. Figuratively it warns that missing the right timing makes success unlikely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿伯話：立冬過三朝，田上冇青苗，今季可能冇得收成喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3 waa6: laap6 dung1 gwo3 saam1 ziu1, tin4 soeng5 mou5 cing1 miu4, gam1 gwai3 ho2 nang4 mou5 dak1 sau1 sing4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 伯父说：立冬过三朝，田上没有青苗，今年可能没有收成了。
examples.english_sentence: The old farmer said, 'If by three mornings after the Start of Winter there are no seedlings in the fields, this season may have no harvest.'

mandarin_meaning: 下定决定 / 心肠坚定且真诚
english_meaning: to make a firm resolve; to be sincere and resolute
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 动词短语 / 形容词短语
explanation_mandarin: 表示下定决心、态度坚定或对人真诚、认真的心态，常用來形容某人決意去做某事或說話待人真誠。
explanation_english: Indicates making a firm resolve or having a sincere, resolute heart. Often used to say someone has decided to act seriously or speaks/behaves from the heart.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢終於立实心肠，要開始認真讀書喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zung1 jyu1 laap6 sat6 sam1 coeng4, jiu3 hoi1 ci2 jing6 zan1 duk6 syu1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他终于下定决心，要开始认真读书了。
examples.english_sentence: He finally made up his mind and is going to start studying seriously.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好講大話，立实心肠同佢講真嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gong2 daai6 waa6, laap6 sat6 sam1 coeng4 tung4 keoi5 gong2 zan1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你别说谎，真心对他讲实话。
examples.english_sentence: Don't lie — be sincere and tell him the truth.

mandarin_meaning: 立刻；马上；立即
english_meaning: immediately; right away; at once; promptly
explanation_mandarin: 香港廣東話的口語表達，重複「立」來加強語氣，表示馬上、立刻做某事，帶有緊迫或強調的意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese expression that duplicates '立' for emphasis. It functions as an adverb meaning to do something immediately or right away, often conveying urgency.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到火，大家要立時立緊走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 fo2, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 laap6 si4 laap6 gan2 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到火的時候，大家要立刻離開。
examples.english_sentence: If you see a fire, everyone should leave immediately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上司話要嗰份報告，你今晚整好，立時立緊交俾佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 si1 waa6 jiu3 go2 fan6 bou3 gou3, nei5 gam1 maan5 zing2 hou2, laap6 si4 laap6 gan2 gaau1 bei2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上司說要那份報告，你今晚做好，立刻交給他。
examples.english_sentence: The boss said he needs the report; finish it tonight and hand it to him right away.

mandarin_meaning: 立刻 / 馬上
english_meaning: immediately; right away
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示馬上、立刻發生或要做某事，相當於普通話的「立刻／馬上」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese adverb meaning immediately or right away; used to indicate that something happens or should be done at once.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等陣，我立时间返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 zan6, ngo5 lap6 si4 gaan1 faan1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等一下，我立刻回來。
examples.english_sentence: Wait a moment, I'll be back right away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到消息就立时间走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 siu1 sik1 zau6 lap6 si4 gaan1 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一聽到消息就立刻走了。
examples.english_sentence: He left immediately when he heard the news.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果有咩事，立时间話我知。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 jau5 me1 si6, lap6 si4 gaan1 waa6 ngo5 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果有什麼事，立刻告訴我。
examples.english_sentence: If anything happens, tell me immediately.

mandarin_meaning: 雜七雜八；零亂、雜亂
english_meaning: all sorts of things; miscellaneous; messy or cluttered
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，形容各種零散或雜亂的東西混在一起，或種類繁多、雜亂無序。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase describing a disorderly mix of various small items or an assortment of miscellaneous things; can be used to mean 'all sorts of' or to indicate clutter/untidiness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個櫃入面擺滿咗立立雜雜嘅嘢，搵唔到想要嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gwai6 jap6 min6 baai2 mun5 zo2 laap6 laap6 zaap6 zaap6 ge3 je5, wan2 m4 dou2 soeng2 jiu3 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個櫃子裡擺滿了雜七雜八的東西，找不到想要的。
examples.english_sentence: This cabinet is full of all sorts of miscellaneous things; I can't find what I want.

mandarin_meaning: 引用篇章或段落以證明或說明某觀點（偏書面或文言用語）
english_meaning: To cite passages or excerpts (from texts) to illustrate or support a point; chiefly a formal or literary usage.
explanation_mandarin: 指從書籍或文章中舉出章節、段落或句子作為證據或說明，語體偏正式或文言，常見於學術或古文書寫中。
explanation_english: Refers to citing chapters, passages, or sentences from texts as evidence or illustration. Usage is typically formal or literary, often found in academic writing or classical texts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢章舉經典文獻，想說服評審。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoeng1 geoi2 ging1 din2 man4 hin3, soeng2 syut3 fuk6 ping4 sam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他章举经典文献，想说服评审。
examples.english_sentence: He cites classical literature to try to persuade the reviewers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 教授喺論文入面章舉多個古代案例作比較分析。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaau3 sau6 hai2 leon6 man4 jap6 min6 zoeng1 geoi2 do1 go3 gu2 doi6 on3 lai6 zok3 bei2 gaau3 fan1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 教授在论文里面章举多个古代案例作比较分析。
examples.english_sentence: The professor cites several ancient cases in the paper for comparative analysis.

mandarin_meaning: 孩子氣的話；幼稚、不成熟的言論（字面：小孩的嘴）
english_meaning: Childish words; naive or immature remarks (literally: child's mouth)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，通常用來形容某些言論幼稚、天真或缺乏經驗，含貶義或戲謔成分。字面意思為「小孩的嘴」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe remarks that are childish, naive, or inexperienced; often slightly pejorative or teasing. Literally means 'a child's mouth.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好聽佢講啲童子口，佢都未試過做呢啲嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 teng1 keoi5 gong2 di1 tung4 zi2 hau2, keoi5 dou1 mei6 si3 gwo3 zou6 ni1 di1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別聽他說那些孩子氣的話，他也沒試過做這些事情。
examples.english_sentence: Don't listen to what he says — those are childish remarks; he hasn't done these things before.

jyutping: zuk1 si1 dang1 lung4, sam1 ngaan5 do1
mandarin_meaning: 形容人心思多、愛算計或狡猾多疑
english_meaning: Describes someone who is crafty, scheming, overly suspicious or full of tricks
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，用來形容一個人心思多、喜歡算計或城府深，帶有貶義，提醒別太相信或靠近此人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to describe a person who is full of schemes, overly cautious or sly. It is mildly pejorative and warns others not to trust or rely on that person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好理佢，佢成日竹絲燈籠，心眼多，唔好信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lei5 keoi5, keoi5 sing4 jat6 zuk1 si1 dang1 lung4, sam1 ngaan5 do1, m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別理他，他總是心思多、愛算計，別相信他。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pay attention to him; he's always scheming and full of tricks—don't trust him.

cantonese: 竹树尾曱甴，又想风流身又餲
jyutping: zuk1 syu6 mei5 gap3 zaa6, jau6 soeng2 fung1 lau4 san1 jau6 ngo6
mandarin_meaning: 形容身份卑微或窮困卻還想打扮風流、追求享受的人。
english_meaning: Describes a person of low status or poor means who nevertheless wants to act suave or pursue romantic/luxurious pleasures — someone who aspires beyond their condition.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語把人比作躲在竹樹底下的曱甴（蟑螂），用來嘲諷那些地位或條件不好，卻還想打扮風流、享受生活或追求高姿態的人。
explanation_english: This Cantonese colloquial saying likens someone to a cockroach hiding under bamboo/trees — used to mock people who are poor or low-status but still try to appear fashionable, flirtatious, or living beyond their means.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢無錢無勢，仲想搵女仔拍拖，真係竹树尾曱甴，又想风流身又餲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou4 cin2 mou4 sai3, zung6 soeng2 wan2 neoi5 zai2 paak3 to1, zan1 hai6 zuk1 syu6 mei5 gap3 zaa6, jau6 soeng2 fung1 lau4 san1 jau6 ngo6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他沒錢沒勢，還想追女生，真是竹樹尾曱甴，又想風流身又餓。
examples.english_sentence: He has no money or status but still wants to chase girls — truly like a cockroach under the bamboo, wanting to be flashy while starving.

jyutping: zuk1 syu6 mei5 ngaat6 zaak6, taan3 fung1 loeng4
mandarin_meaning: 形容人在將面臨麻煩或危險時，仍裝作若無其事、怡然自得或漠視問題
english_meaning: Describes someone who remains carefree or complacent while trouble or danger is imminent; acting oblivious or unconcerned.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語以「曱甴」（蟑螂）比喻處於不利或將受懲罰的處境，卻依然在樹下享受涼風，形容人對即將來臨的問題漠不關心或自得其樂。
explanation_english: This Cantonese slang uses a cockroach under a tree enjoying the cool breeze as an image: someone facing imminent trouble or danger yet acting nonchalant and complacent, ignoring the looming problem.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家公司話會裁員，阿強仲係竹樹尾曱甴，叹風涼，完全冇諗過點應付。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 gung1 si1 waa6 wui5 coi4 jyun4, aa3 koeng4 zung6 hai6 zuk1 syu6 mei5 ngaat6 zaak6, taan3 fung1 loeng4, jyun4 cyun4 mou5 nam2 gwo3 dim2 jing3 fu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在公司說要裁員，阿強還若無其事、怡然自得，完全沒想過要怎麼應對。
examples.english_sentence: The company says it will lay people off, but Ah Keung is still acting carefree, totally unprepared for how to deal with it.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見）竹製的小器具／小棍，可能是方言或古稱，具體用途因地而異，常與撐船或農務用具相關
english_meaning: (rare/obsolete) a small bamboo implement/tool — a dialectal or archaic term; usage varies but often refers to a bamboo pole or small bamboo tool (e.g. for poling a boat or farm work)
explanation_mandarin: 「竹笡」屬於罕見或方言詞彙，字面由「竹」與以竹為形的字構成。現代資料中使用不多，文獻或口語裡有時用來指稱竹製的小棍、小桿或小器具，可能與撐船、撥水或簡單農務器具有關。由於地域差異，確切含義會有所不同。
explanation_english: The term is rare and largely dialectal or archaic. Literally composed of the bamboo radical character, it appears infrequently in modern sources. When used, it typically denotes a small bamboo stick, pole, or implement — for example a tool for poling a boat or simple agricultural tasks. Exact meaning may vary by region.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿公屋企仲留住一把竹笡，話係以前撐船用嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 gung1 uk1 kei2 zung6 lau4 zyu6 jat1 baa2 zuk1 gaap3, waa6 hai6 ji5 cin4 caang1 syun4 jung6 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿公家裡還留著一把竹笡，說是以前撐船用的。
examples.english_sentence: My grandfather still keeps a bamboo 'zuk gaap' — he said it was used long ago to pole boats.

mandarin_meaning: 竹篱、竹笆（用竹子编成的篱笆、簾子或竹席）
english_meaning: bamboo fence/screen or bamboo matting made of bamboo slats
explanation_mandarin: 指用竹子或竹片編成的籬笆、簾子或鋪地/遮陽的竹片結構，常用於家庭或臨時圍蔽、遮蔽。
explanation_english: Refers to a fence, screen, or mat made from bamboo slats. Commonly used as a household fence, privacy screen, or sun/wind shield.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企門口裝咗道竹笪，擋風又遮陽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 mun4 hau2 zong1 zo2 dou6 zuk1 daap6, dong2 fung1 jau6 ze1 joeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家門口裝了一道竹笪，擋風又遮陽。
examples.english_sentence: They put up a bamboo screen at the house entrance; it blocks wind and sun.

mandarin_meaning: 竹节（竹子的节环）；也可指事物的节段、节点或比喻为有节奏、分段的结构
english_meaning: bamboo node/joint (the raised ring between bamboo segments); can also mean a segmented/node-like structure or metaphorically a rhythm/cadence
explanation_mandarin: 指竹子上每節的節環（外凸的部分），把竹子分成一節一節；引申為任何有節段、節點或有節奏感的結構。
explanation_english: Refers to the ring-like joint on bamboo that separates its segments; by extension, it denotes any segmented structure or a sense of rhythm/cadence.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢支竹有好多竹節，唔容易折斷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 zuk1 jau5 hou2 do1 zuk1 zit3, m4 jung4 ji6 zit3 dyun6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這根竹子有很多竹節，不容易折斷。
examples.english_sentence: This bamboo has many nodes; it's not easy to break.

mandarin_meaning: 竹节虾（常指螳螂虾/虾蛄，一种甲壳类海鲜）
english_meaning: bamboo-jointed shrimp (commonly refers to mantis shrimp; a type of crustacean eaten as seafood)
explanation_mandarin: 一种常见於粤港的甲壳类海鲜，体节明显，俗称螳螂虾或虾蛄，常用于清蒸、白灼或炒食。
explanation_english: A type of crustacean commonly found and eaten in Cantonese cuisine; characterized by distinct body segments (hence 'bamboo-jointed'). Often refers to mantis shrimp (also called 'haa1 gu1' in Cantonese) and is usually steamed, boiled, or stir-fried.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺街市見到新鮮嘅竹節蝦，好大隻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gaai1 si5 gin3 dou3 san1 sin1 ge3 juk1 zit3 haa1, hou2 daai6 zek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在菜市场看到新鲜的竹节虾，很大只。
examples.english_sentence: I saw fresh bamboo-jointed shrimp at the market; they were very large.

mandarin_meaning: 竹编并批荡的传统墙面工艺
english_meaning: bamboo lathing and plastering (traditional wall construction technique)
explanation_mandarin: 指以竹條編成格子作為牆面或內牆基底，然後進行批蕩（抹灰）處理的傳統建築做法，常見於粵語地區的舊屋或鄉村建築，現在較少見。
explanation_english: Refers to a traditional building method where bamboo strips are woven into a lattice as the base for walls and then plastered over. Common in older houses in Cantonese-speaking regions; now less common.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 間舊屋嘅牆係用竹織批蕩整成，保溫又透氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaan1 gau6 uk1 ge3 coeng4 hai6 jung6 zuk1 zik1 pei1 dong6 zing2 seng4, bou2 wan1 jau6 tau3 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間舊屋的牆是用竹織批蕩做成的，保溫又透氣。
examples.english_sentence: The old house's walls are made with bamboo lathing and plastering, which keeps them insulated and breathable.

jyutping: zuk1 zik1 aap3, mou5 sam1 gon1
mandarin_meaning: （俚語）沒良心、沒同情心、冷血
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang insult meaning 'heartless' or 'without conscience'; describes someone unfeeling or cruel.
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語／俚語，用來指責某人冷漠或無良心。前半句『竹织鸭』為口語化的強調或戲謔成分，整句合起來帶有貶義。來源帶有俗語與押韻成分，非正式用語。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase used as an insult to call someone heartless, unfeeling, or lacking conscience. The first part '竹织鸭' functions as a colloquial/dismissive intensifier; the phrase is informal and derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢明明知我有難，仲唔幫，真係竹织鸭，冇心肝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ming4 ming4 zi1 ngo5 jau5 naan4, zung6 m4 bong1, zan1 hai6 zuk1 zik1 aap3, mou5 sam1 gon1.
